Multi-buffer / differing-name (BORROW forms) DONE in 6aa7afd9/238e1388 (slice 4): forward layout-flow inference extended to ref Vec[E] / mut ref Vec[E] params (param_is_layout_carrying peels one ref/mut-ref), so multiple SoA buffers of one element type flow through shared by-ref helpers regardless of param name, each a distinct monomorph (total$data_soa_grid vs total$data_soa_coll). A borrow param keeps its pointer ABI (active_param_soa_layout guarded to by-value only); compile_mono_function's prologue registers a SoA borrow param in ref_params so the access paths deref the slot once (without it: pointer bytes read as the SoA struct -> garbage len -> SIGTRAP); ref_params is now save/restored around both mono entry points. Tests: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_soa_by_ref_param_caller_different_name + ::test_e2e_soa_two_buffers_through_one_ref_helper_distinct_monos + ::test_e2e_soa_mut_ref_push_across_function + tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_soa_mut_ref_fill_borrow_no_leak_or_double_free (Linux-LSan-clean). Origin-only soa_layouts cutover DONE in db584a09/8ad88b24 (slice 5): the access-path trigger now reads a per-binding LayoutId value carrier (binding_layouts, seeded at the binding site by seed_binding_site_layout) instead of re-deriving SoA-ness from the binding name against soa_layouts at each use; active_layout_id consults layout_subst then binding_layouts with no soa_layouts fallback, so soa_layouts is origin-only (catalogue + LayoutId->shape + binding-site name-match). The redundant name-keyed by-value param ABI (soa_value_param_layout) is retired: the base symbol lowers every Vec[E] param AoS and a SoA arg routes to a mono regardless of param name, fixing the footgun where a base param merely sharing a name with a layout block lowered SoA on the name alone (an AoS arg then marshalled a 3-field struct into a 4-field slot). Cross-group disjointness audited: the borrow checker is layout-agnostic (codegen containment), groups partition fields, so cross-group borrows are already-disjoint field places -- no new fact needed. Tests: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_soa_layout_named_param_base_is_aos_mono_is_soa + tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_soa_layout_named_param_base_aos_and_mono_soa_no_leak. Slice 6 (Slipstream full-SoA PROOF) DONE in b9138d30: examples/slipstream/src/sim.kara's carried LBM grid (plus per-substep coll/next) is a layout block split into two cache groups; the per-band chunks stay AoS (they cross the generic TaskHandle[Vec[LbmNode]] join). The native oracle's milestone framebuffer checksums are byte-identical AoS<->SoA (1582897806 / 793640938 / 680974524) and the browser flagship runs on SoA in real headless Chrome (verify_browser.mjs PASS). The proof surfaced and fixed FIVE more cross-function gaps (all in the compiler, no demo-side workarounds): (1) with_capacity SoA constructor -- the presize pass rewrites a counted-loop-filled Vec.new() into Vec.with_capacity(n) (init_grid/fan_collide shape) and the SoA let path matched only Vec.new, so the rewritten binding kept the AoS slot under an SoA layout; is_vec_with_capacity_call routes it to compile_soa_new. (2) Returned-local base-symbol clash -- a builder whose returned local is named after a layout block (init_grid's grid) name-matched its body SoA while the AoS-return base symbol returned the 3-field Vec; soa_return_locals suppresses the origin name-match for a returned local (its layout is the return mono's). (3) SoA reassignment grid = substep(grid,..) -- the carried-grid per-frame double-buffer had no backward-mono path on the assignment arm (only the let arm); compile_soa_assign_from_call parks the return layout, frees the OLD groups (by-value param is caller-retains), stores the new SoA header (Linux-LSan clean, no double-free/leak). (4) Tail-CALL SoA-return propagation -- a SoA-returning fn whose body ENDS IN a layout-returning call (substep's fan_stream(coll,..)) returned AoS while its signature was SoA; compile_tail_final_expr flows the return layout to the tail call. (5) SoA across a coroutine suspend (browser render loop's grid carried across frames.recv()) -- collect soa_layouts + pre-populate fn_asts BEFORE the state-machine emission (the poll-fn body's SoA-return inference reads both), size an SoA persisted local's state-struct field as the 4-field struct, and type an SoA binding's par-block/auto-par return slot SoA (infer_let_binding_llvm_type). Tests: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_soa_{counted_loop_fill_returned,returned_local_name_matches_layout,reassign_carried_buffer,tail_call_soa_return} + tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_soa_reassign_carried_buffer_no_leak_or_double_free. Gates: codegen E2E 1696/0, par_codegen 34/0, coro_e2e 122/0, Linux-LSan soa 12/0. FOLLOW-ONS (separate features, never miscompile -- degrade to AoS or unbuilt): branch-leaf/multi-return SoA returns degrade to AoS (spike §8); the whole-element SoA index-store grid[i] = E{..} is unbuilt even single-function (push + mut-ref field write-back + field-level vec[i].field= via B-2026-06-20-7 all work; the whole-element scatter is the gap). The field-level SoA index-store blocker is FIXED (B-2026-06-20-7). See docs/spikes/per-layout-monomorphization.md. FOLLOW-ONS (2026-06-20, commits c74752f6 + 3ccab359): (1) whole-element SoA index-store grid[i]=E{...} — compile_soa_index_store scatters the RHS element's fields into each group buffer at [i] (the push-at-len decomposition, bounds-checked, no growth; deref a ref/mut-ref param slot for cross-function scatter); pre-fix it fell into compile_vec_index_store and wrote whole AoS elements over one group's narrower stride (silent heap-buffer-overflow). 3 codegen E2E (single-fn, mut-ref cross-fn, cold-group) + 1 ASAN overflow guard. POD elements only (the whole SoA subsystem assumes POD; heap-field elements stay an orthogonal gap). (2) branch-leaf / multi-return SoA returns — soa_return_local_names now recursively collects EVERY bare-identifier return site (each explicit return <id>; in any branch/loop/nested block except closures, plus every tail leaf of a branch-bearing tail if c {a} else {b}), so each return value lowers SoA against the patched signature; pre-fix multi-site returns were a hard LLVM 'return type does not match' verify failure (NOT the silent AoS degrade the spike assumed). Early-return move-out uses a branch-safe runtime cap=0 sentinel (neutralize_moved_soa_groups_slot), not the tail path's compile-time FreeSoaGroups frame removal — the early-return frame is shared with the fall-through path where the local is not returned and must still be freed (branch-buried-move footgun). 3 codegen E2E + 2 ASAN/LSan (early-return fall-through, branch-leaf tails — both paths). Native Slipstream oracle byte-identical post-change (1582897806/793640938/680974524); full codegen 1713, par 34, coro 122, SoA LSan 15 all green.
title: SoA `layout` blocks did not cross function boundaries — passing a SoA-laid-out Vec[E] to another function miscompiled. The layout makes the binding-site a 4-field SoA value {g0_ptr,...,len,cap} (soa_layouts is a name-keyed codegen map), but a callee's `Vec[E]` parameter is always compiled with the default AoS {ptr,len,cap} representation, and the SoA access paths GEP the param's slot alloca directly. By-VALUE: caller loads the 4-field SoA and passes it to a 3-field AoS param -> LLVM 'Call parameter type does not match function signature' verification failure (loud). By-REF (`ref Vec[E]`): the slot alloca holds a POINTER to the caller's SoA struct, but compile_soa_index_read / compile_soa_method GEP'd the alloca as if it were the struct -> reads the pointer's bytes as group-ptrs/len -> garbage len (e.g. 1073741824) -> SIGTRAP (exit 133). A SILENT miscompile. AoS (no layout block) is correct; single-function SoA (push/index/field/len all within the declaring fn) is correct. Surfaced by the Slipstream LBM dogfood (examples/slipstream): its kernel splits the grid across `ref Vec[LbmNode]` helpers (collide_band/stream_band/velocities/render_fb), so it could not use SoA at all -- exactly the 'SoA layout' capability the roster bills it on. PARTIAL FIX: the by-REF READ path now works. compile_soa_index_read (collections.rs) and compile_soa_method (exprs.rs) compute a `soa_struct_ptr` that derefs the slot alloca once when the binding is a `ref`/`mut ref` param (self.ref_params), so the callee operates on the caller's existing SoA struct; a by-value/`let` binding's slot already IS the struct (no deref). Now working cross-function: .len(), whole-element index read (`let e = es[i]`), and direct indexed field access (`es[i].y`, which routes through compile_soa_index_read). Regression: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_soa_by_ref_param_read_across_function (sum 21 via a `ref Vec[E]` helper; was SIGTRAP). All 1670 codegen tests pass, fmt+clippy clean. REMAINING (ABI-level follow-on, not yet done): by-VALUE SoA params (callee signature must be the SoA struct type + call must marshal the SoA value + param prologue) and SoA RETURN values; plus the name-keyed model fits multi-buffer kernels (grid/coll/next) awkwardly -- the fuller design is per-layout monomorphization (design.md Feature 1, P1.5/Phase 11).

Passing a bare named `fn` as a first-class `Fn(...)` value miscompiles. `fn apply(f: Fn(i64)->i64, x: i64) -> i64 { f(x) }` called as `apply(doubler, 21)` (doubler a named fn) parses + type-checks fine, but codegen lowers `TypeKind::FnType` to the default `i64` (types_lowering.rs llvm_type_for_type_expr falls through) while a bare fn name lowers to a raw `ptr` (exprs.rs free-fn-as-value), so the higher-order call fails LLVM module verification: 'Call parameter type does not match function signature! ptr @doubler ... call i64 @apply(ptr @doubler, i64 21)'. Only the special-cased `Server.serve(handler)` dispatch works today (landed 2026-05-09, commit 60ce3a4); the general `Fn`-typed-parameter path is unsupported and was untracked. Workaround: wrap in a closure (`apply(|x| doubler(x), 21)`), which builds the {fn_ptr,env} fat pointer. Fix = lower FnType to the closure fat-pointer struct {ptr,ptr} and reify a bare fn name into {ptr, null-env} at Fn-typed arg sites (or have the Fn ABI accept a raw ptr). Surfaced writing the `#[inline(always)]`-through-fn-value IR test for the codegen-hint-attrs slice (phase-8-stdlib-floor.md line 775); the attribute itself emits correctly regardless of call shape, so only the indirect-call test is blocked. FIXED 2026-06-21 (79f1de14): lower `FnType` to the `{fn_ptr,env_ptr}` closure fat pointer (types_lowering.rs FnType arm — was the 8-byte i64 fall-through); register a `Fn`-typed parameter in closure_fn_types via the env-first closure_abi_fn_type so a body call `f(x)` routes through compile_closure_call as an indirect call (functions.rs); and reify a bare fn name at a `Fn`-typed arg site into `{trampoline, null env}` through a memoized, env-ignoring forwarder `__karac_fnval_<name>` (reify_named_fn_as_fn_value, call_dispatch.rs) so a plain free fn (no env param) conforms to the env-first ABI. Trampoline signature and the param's indirect-call type are both built from the same annotation, so they agree. A closure LITERAL into a `Fn(...)` param now works too (already a fat pointer; no reify). Tests: tests/codegen.rs fn_value_named_fn_as_fn_typed_param_runs / fn_value_fn_typed_param_multiarg_and_float_run / fn_value_named_fn_reused_across_call_sites (one memoized trampoline) / fn_value_closure_literal_into_fn_typed_param_run / test_ir_fn_value_named_fn_reified_trampoline; leak gate tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_named_fn_value_heap_arg_no_leak (heap String arg through the trampoline freed once — green on the Linux ASAN+LSan harness).

Four allocating String->String methods were unrecognized (Tier-B B1): `trim()` / `to_lowercase()` / `to_uppercase()` (no-arg -> String) and `replace(from, to)` (two String args -> String). FIXED complete across all three backends with FULL UNICODE semantics matching Rust's str stdlib exactly — `to_lowercase`/`to_uppercase` are Unicode case maps that can CHANGE byte length (`straße`.to_uppercase() == `STRASSE`), `trim` strips Unicode whitespace, `replace` is byte-substring. Typechecker (stdlib_seq.rs infer_str_method): arg-shape validation + String result. Interpreter (method_call_seq.rs try_eval_seq_method): direct Rust `s.trim().to_string()` / `s.to_lowercase()` / `s.to_uppercase()` / `s.replace(from,to)`. NOTE the interpreter `replace` arm is String-guarded and the vector handler (try_eval_vector_method, SIMD `Vector.replace`) runs BEFORE the seq handler, so a Vector receiver never reaches the new String arm. CODEGEN: new runtime helpers in runtime/src/clone.rs — `karac_string_{to_lowercase,to_uppercase,trim}(data, len, *mut out_len) -> ptr` and `karac_string_replace(data, len, from, from_len, to, to_len, *mut out_len) -> ptr`, each computing the result via the SAME Rust stdlib call as the interpreter (so the two backends are bit-identical on Unicode without shipping Unicode tables into codegen) and returning a fresh NUL-terminated `{ptr, out_len, out_len}` (cap==len) buffer (null+0 for empty, the karac_string_slice convention). codegen.rs declares the 4 externs; vec_method.rs adds the dispatch arms (load receiver {data,len}, extract arg {ptr,len} pairs, call helper with an out_len alloca, build the String aggregate via the shared build_string_xform_result helper). The result is freed exactly once by the existing String scope-cleanup registration (same path as repeat/slice). Decision: full Unicode (not an ASCII-only shortcut) — an ASCII `to_lowercase` would be a silent correctness footgun on non-ASCII AND would diverge from the interpreter's Rust-Unicode result. trim allocates an OWNED copy rather than returning a borrowed view (a String-view story is a future optimization). Tests: tests/interpreter.rs test_string_trim_replace_case_interpreter; tests/codegen.rs e2e_string_trim_replace_case_codegen (A/B parity incl. ß->SS and Unicode é); tests/typechecker.rs string_trim_replace_case_return_string / string_trim_rejects_arguments / string_replace_rejects_non_string_arg; tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_string_trim_replace_case_no_leak_no_double_free (macOS ASAN double-free/UAF + Linux LSan leak gate via scripts/lsan-local.sh, 36-byte payload, 1000x loop -> 143000).

`Vec.binary_search(x)` / `Slice.binary_search(x) -> Option[i64]` were typecheck- and interpreter-complete but had NO codegen — `karac build` failed loudly ('Vec/String method binary_search is not yet supported in codegen' / 'no handler for slice method binary_search'). Tier-B B2. FIXED in codegen for integer (any width, signed + unsigned) and String element types; float/struct/other element types emit an honest 'not yet supported under karac build; works under karac run' diagnostic (the interpreter handles them via value_compare). The search REPLICATES Rust's CURRENT branchless `slice::binary_search_by` EXACTLY (narrow-to-base: size=len,base=0; while size>1 { half=size/2; mid=base+half; base = cmp(v[mid],x)>0 ? base : mid; size-=half } then cmp(v[base],x)==0 ? Some(base):None) — NOT the textbook return-on-first-equal variant, which picks a DIFFERENT index among DUPLICATE keys; since the interpreter calls std's binary_search_by, codegen had to match it bit-for-bit (verified: [1,2,2,2,2,3,4].binary_search(2) == 4, [5,5,5,5].binary_search(5) == 3 on both backends). The 3-way element compare (emit_binary_search_cmp, src/codegen/vec_method.rs) is pure data-flow (no basic blocks): integers widen to i64 (zext for uN, sext for iN — matching the interpreter's signed i64 value_compare where uint values are non-negative i64) then signed 3-way via selects; String elements route through the existing karac_string_cmp runtime fn (byte-lexicographic, == Rust String Ord, no archive rebuild). Shared compile_binary_search helper drives BOTH the Vec arm (3-field {ptr,len,cap} header, compile_vec_method) and the Slice arm (2-field {ptr,len} header, the slice dispatch in method_call.rs); element type name recovered via var_elem_type_exprs (vec_elem_type_name). A fresh-owned String needle temp is freed once (free_fresh_owned_str_arg); the receiver's elements are read-only (never freed). Tests: tests/codegen.rs e2e_vec_binary_search_codegen (A/B parity: Vec i64/u8/String + Slice + empty + duplicates); tests/interpreter.rs test_vec_binary_search_duplicates_and_widths (pins std's duplicate-index reference); tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_vec_binary_search_string_needle_no_leak_no_double_free (fresh-needle free path, macOS ASAN + Linux LSan, 36-byte payloads).

fix: 90db12cb
title: String `==`/`!=` codegen memcmp'd `l_len` bytes from BOTH operand pointers UNCONDITIONALLY (compile_string_binop, BinOp::Eq|NotEq in src/codegen/expr_ops.rs), so when the left operand is LONGER than the right it read past the end of the shorter RIGHT buffer — a heap-buffer-overflow (ASAN-caught; a latent out-of-bounds read in release, mostly masked because libc memcmp short-circuits at the first differing byte, so it only actually overruns when the operands share a prefix at least as long as the shorter buffer, e.g. "OnceFnHandler" vs "OnceFn"). The Lt/Gt arm already clamped to min_len; only the equality arm used raw l_len. Surfaced during phase-12 self-hosting slice 3a: the parser's `current_ident_matches` borrow-matches a String payload out of an indexed place (`self.tokens[self.pos].token`) and compares it against a short keyword (`dup_str(n) == "Fn"` / `"OnceFn"`); a type name longer than the keyword overran the keyword literal's buffer. ORIGINALLY MIS-ATTRIBUTED to a double-free of the borrowed enum payload (the slice-3a writeup's 'latent codegen double-free on a repeated indexed-enum-payload borrow-match'); investigation showed the borrow-match is SOUND — the indexed enum scrutinee is deep-cloned by clone_borrowed_index_field_enum_scrutinee (#38), so the bound payload owns an independent buffer freed exactly once, and equal-length comparisons of any peek/move count are ASAN-clean. The real, reproducible defect is this `==` overread; the real multi-file buggy parser was ASAN-dirty before and is clean after, with NO second error behind the overread. FIX: clamp the equality memcmp span to min(l_len, r_len) (mirrors the Lt/Gt arm). Memory-safe and semantics-preserving — the existing `len_eq && data_eq` AND already forces unequal-length operands to compare false, and when lengths match min_len == l_len == r_len (identical to the prior code). Regression: tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_string_eq_mismatched_len_no_overread_in_indexed_payload_match — a multi-variant enum whose String payload is borrow-matched out of a struct-owned Vec element and compared against shorter, prefix-sharing literals; verified it fails (heap-buffer-overflow READ) on the pre-fix l_len memcmp and passes after. Green: memory_sanitizer 299, codegen 1684, selfhost_parser + selfhost_lexer.

No ordered key->value map existed (Tier-B B3) — only `SortedSet` (ordered set) and `Map` (insertion-order hash map). Added `SortedMap[K: Ord, V]`, the B-tree-backed key->value sibling of `SortedSet`, full across typecheck + interpreter; codegen is interpreter-only + honest Err (same v1 status as SortedSet, which also has no B-tree runtime). NEW Value::SortedMap(BTreeMap<OrdValue, Value>) keyed by the existing OrdValue (value_compare ordering, == SortedSet). Registration: prelude.rs PRELUDE_TYPES + STDLIB_SOURCES bake of runtime/stdlib/sorted_map.kara (struct SortedMap[=K,=V]{}) + stub_generics 2-param; resolver scope-0 picks it up via PRELUDE_TYPES. Methods (typechecker stdlib_map.rs infer_sorted_map_method, K:Ord bound via type_supports_ord; interpreter across method_call_seq/map/set): core map surface len/is_empty/contains_key/get->Option[V]/get_or->V/insert->Option[V](old)/remove->Option[V]/keys->Vec[K]/values->Vec[V]/entries->Vec[(K,V)]/merge(last-writer-wins)/clear, PLUS the ordered queries min/max->Option[(K,V)], floor(k)/ceiling(k)->Option[(K,V)] (largest key<=k / smallest key>=k via BTreeMap::range cursor), range(lo,hi)->Vec[(K,V)] (INCLUSIVE [lo,hi], inverted bounds yield empty). keys/values/entries and `for pair in m` iterate ascending key order. Dispatch wired through the existing Map/Set/SortedSet handler chain (set handler: clear/min/max/range/floor/ceiling on &obj; map handler: get_or/keys/values/entries/merge/insert/remove on owned clone; seq handler: len/is_empty/get/contains_key/clone). Support sites mirrored from SortedSet/Map: value.rs (PartialEq/Display/debug_fmt/variant_name), helpers.rs (value_compare lexicographic over (k,v) pairs + discriminant 14), exec.rs deep_clone_value explicit arm (collection VALUES get fresh storage, not aliased Arc), eval_expr/method_call_iter (for-loop + .iter() yield (k,v) tuples), env_build Item=(K,V), derives Clone/Display/Debug, types iterator_item/clone_self, effectchecker+ownership (insert/remove/clear/merge=MutRef seed allocates(Heap); reads=ImmRef), alloc_rejection, fallible_alloc. CODEGEN (interpreter-only): SortedMap.new() is intercepted in call_dispatch.rs compile_call with an honest 'SortedMap is interpreter-only in v1 ... Run under karac run, or use Map[K,V]' Err (every SortedMap program must construct before use, so the constructor gate gives ONE clean message instead of a downstream 'no handler for method' codegen-bug fall-through that SortedSet still emits); types_lowering/declarations/clone_drop/entry_chains/param_own add SortedMap alongside SortedSet so param/return lowering + try_clone never ICE. NO new runtime symbol, NO archive rebuild (BTreeMap lives in the interpreter only). Decision: full ordered API incl. floor/ceiling/range (user-requested) over a min/max-only minimal set. No memory_sanitizer test — interpreter-only means no AOT binary to ASAN. Tests: tests/interpreter.rs 12 (test_sorted_map_*: new/len, insert/get/contains, remove, ordered iteration, min/max + empty, floor/ceiling, range incl. inverted, get_or, string keys sorted, clone independence + clear, merge last-writer-wins); tests/typechecker.rs 16 (return types of every method, SortedMap[K,V] annotation, K:Ord bound rejection on a non-derived distinct type, unknown-method NoMethodFound); tests/codegen.rs test_sorted_map_codegen_rejected_interpreter_only (build fails loud with the interpreter-only message).

fix: FIXED in 38fb0b57 via a new compile_soa_field_store (collections.rs): locate the field's owning group + its within-group position, then address group_buf[index] by THAT group's sub-struct stride and GEP the field slot (the store-side mirror of compile_soa_index_read's group addressing — same ref-param deref, same bounds check, same coerce_to_struct_field_ty). compile_field_store (expr_ops.rs) routes an indexed SoA object here FIRST (gated on active_soa_layout), ahead of the indexed-shared / nested-plain-struct branches that caused the bug. Compound assignment `bodies[i].field += expr` composes for free (read via compile_soa_index_read, store via the new path). Tests: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_soa_field_index_store_strided (cross-group write+read, 164 — a dropped index-1 store gives 161.5) + tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_soa_field_index_store_no_overflow (field scatter across both groups, 20x loop — the old OOB store trips ASAN). ROOT CAUSE: compile_field_store had no SoA branch, so `bodies[i].x = expr` fell into the nested-plain-struct path which treats the SoA struct as a contiguous AoS element — it read the SoA header's field-0 pointer as the data base and strided by the FULL element size. Index 0 coincidentally hit group-0 slot 0; index >= 1 wrote PAST the group buffer (a silent heap overflow), so the store was dropped. Repro (single function, no call boundary): struct Body { x: f64, vx: f64, health: f64 }; layout bodies: Vec[Body] { group pos { x } group vel { vx } group hp { health } }; push two elements, then `bodies[0].x = 7.0; bodies[1].x = 9.0; println(bodies[0].x + bodies[1].x)`. Codegen (SoA) prints 17; the AoS interpreter oracle prints 16. The field-level SoA index-store writes element index 0 correctly but the store at index 1 lands at neither slot 1 nor slot 0 (read-back of bodies[0].x is still 7, bodies[1].x is still its original 10) -- the per-group destination address is computed wrong for index >= 1 (likely a missing index*elem_stride term / wrong group base, mirroring nothing like compile_soa_index_read's correct read addressing), so non-zero-index field scatters are effectively dropped. Pure cross-group READS (bodies[i].x + bodies[i].health) are correct (covered by existing tests). PRE-EXISTING: the base compiler at 6296b9ae miscompiles it byte-identically, so it is NOT introduced by per-layout-mono slice 5 (db584a09, which only swapped the layout value carrier). Independent of the borrow checker (a codegen address-arithmetic fault, not an aliasing-fact gap; surfaced while auditing cross-group disjointness for the e.position += e.velocity idiom). Same family as the unbuilt whole-element index-store grid[i] = E{..} (still open). UNBLOCKS B-2026-06-19-14 slice 6 (Slipstream's LBM kernel scatters field updates by index).
title: Field-level SoA index-store `vec[i].field = expr` is dropped for index >= 1 -- the per-group destination address is not strided by the element index, so only element 0 stores correctly (codegen 17 vs AoS-oracle 16 on a 2-element repro). Single-function; no call boundary involved. Surfaced during the per-layout-mono slice-5 cross-group disjointness audit while probing the field-scatter write idiom.

Tier-D D1: `Map.entry(k).or_insert(d)` write-through (the `mut ref V` contract, design.md § Entry[K,V]) was broken in BOTH backends — the flagship counter `*m.entry(k).or_insert(0) += 1` produced WRONG output under `karac run` (a=0 b=0 c=0) and a hard codegen error under `karac build` ('Binary op Add: left operand PointerType'). Root causes + fixes across both backends, A/B verified, Linux-LSan clean. INTERPRETER (2f0a7de1): `or_insert`/`or_insert_with` returned a DETACHED CLONE of the value, so scalar write-through silently dropped (heap Vec values only worked by accident via Arc-shared element storage). Fix: new `Value::MapSlotRef{map_var, key}` — a genuine place-ref into the live Map slot. `or_insert`/`or_insert_with` insert-if-absent then return it; `Env::get` resolves it to the slot value (auto-deref) and `Env::set` writes through to the slot, the SAME get/set choke-point treatment as `SharedCell`, so `*r += 1`, `r += 1` (deref-elided), `*r = v`, and `.push(x)` (Arc-shared elem) all land in the map. The bare-chain `*m.entry(k).or_insert(d) += 1` writes through via assign_to_place (Deref of a non-identifier yielding a MapSlotRef) + the Deref read resolves it in eval_unary; a MapSlotRef method receiver resolves to the slot value. Map SLOTS never hold a ref (only a local binding / chain-temp), so all map reads stay pristine (no collapse needed). Exhaustive arms: value.rs Display/variant_name (PartialEq + value_compare + deep_clone use catch-alls). CODEGEN (45089125): three gaps. (1) `*m.entry(k).or_insert(d) += rhs`: the entry chain lowers to a slot pointer WITH insert side effects, so compile it EXACTLY once then load/apply/store back through it (CompoundAssign + Assign deref cases in stmts.rs via `entry_chain_or_insert_map_name`). Previously `compile_expr(Deref(chain))` returned the raw pointer → binop PointerType error. (2) Two-step `let r = m.entry(k).or_insert(d); *r += 1`: bind `r` to the slot pointer + tag in NEW `entry_slot_ref_vars` (codegen analog of MapSlotRef; saved/restored across mono like ref_params, cleared per-fn) so `*r` reads / `*r += 1` / `r += 1` / `*r = v` write through (exprs.rs Deref read + stmts.rs assign/compound via `entry_slot_ref_target`/`entry_slot_ref_ptr`). Also closed a value-represented mut-ref deref-store: `*v += 1` in an `and_modify` closure SILENTLY dropped before (the `match target.kind` had no Deref(Identifier) arm); the canonical `v += 1` form already worked. (3) `Map.get_or(k, default)` was UNIMPLEMENTED in codegen ('not yet implemented'); lowered as a keyed lookup with a phi between the stored value and the default. The hit path returns an OWNED copy (deep-clone for String/Vec/struct V via emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr; rc_inc for shared V; load for scalar) because `get_or -> V` (owned), not a borrow — a raw alias double-freed (exit 133) with the map's drop at the caller's scope exit. KEY-TEMP LEAK (200b689c, caught by the Linux LSan gate — macOS ASAN misses reachable leaks): `karac_map_entry` bit-copies the key header into the bucket ONLY on the vacant insert (adopting the buffer); on the occupied path it keeps the existing key, so a fresh-owned-temp key (`m.entry(w.to_string())`) is orphaned — the counter leaked one key buffer per REPEATED key. `get_or` (any lookup) never stores its key. Fix: free the fresh-temp key when the runtime did not adopt it — entry chain frees conditionally on `occupied` (unconditionally for the `and_modify` lookup-only variant), `get_or` frees after the lookup; both via `free_fresh_owned_str_arg` (no-ops on borrowed cap==0 / non-Vec-String / non-fresh-temp). Moved-binding + place-expr keys on the no-adopt path remain a broader PRE-EXISTING map-key-ownership gap shared by get/insert (out of scope). Tests: interpreter 4 (direct counter, two-step mut-ref, per-key-Vec push, snapshot-not-ref); codegen 3 (direct counter, two-step mut-ref, get_or hit/default); memory_sanitizer 2 (entry counter + heap-valued get_or owned-copy, ≥36-byte payloads). Suites green: interpreter 976, codegen 1697, typechecker 1739, effectchecker 373, memory_sanitizer 304 (macOS ASAN) + Linux LSan map gate 27. NO new runtime symbol, NO archive rebuild.

fix: c7b72bd4
title: Map-key NO-ADOPT ownership residual (the broader gap B-2026-06-20-8 deferred): the fresh-temp-only key free missed every non-fresh-temp owned key on a map's no-adopt path. `karac_map_entry` ADOPTS the key's {ptr,len,cap} buffer (bit-copies the header into the bucket) ONLY on the VACANT insert; the `and_modify` lookup variant, `get`/`get_or`/`remove`/`contains_key`, and `insert` on the EXISTS path never adopt. Three distinct bugs, one root cause (entry adopting like `insert` but not running insert's consume-site dance), confirmed via the Linux LSan gate (macOS ASAN misses the leaks but caught the entry vacant double-free). (1) ENTRY DOUBLE-FREE + occupied leak: a moved local binding / owned param / place key into `m.entry(k)` DOUBLE-FREED on the VACANT path (map adopts the buffer AND the un-suppressed source binding's scope-exit free releases the same buffer -- entry, unlike insert, never suppressed the source) and LEAKED on the OCCUPIED path (the B-2026-06-20-8 free was gated to fresh temps via expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp, so an Identifier/place key was untouched). Fix (entry_chains.rs emit_entry_chain): mirror Map.insert's key consume-site dance -- suppress_fstr_acc_if_moved_out + maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg (deep-copy an owned String/Vec PARAM key so the bucket owns a private buffer; the caller still frees the original under the by-value header ABI) + suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg (zero a moved local binding's cap so its scope-exit free skips the adopted buffer); then free the key buffer on the NO-ADOPT branch (occupied for or_insert / always for the and_modify lookup variant), now UNGATED -- a vec-struct compile-time gate restricts the emitted free-diamond to String/Vec keys and the cap>0 runtime guard no-ops on a borrowed view / rodata literal. key_val is loaded before the suppress so the bucket still receives the owned (cap>0) header. (2) get/remove/contains_key FRESH-TEMP key leak: each looks the key up and never stores it, but only `get_or` freed its fresh-temp key -- so `m.get(w.to_string())` / remove / contains_key leaked one buffer per call. Fix: add free_fresh_owned_str_arg(&args[0].value, key_val) after the lookup in get / remove / contains_key (moved bindings are covered by their own un-suppressed source free, so the fresh-temp gate is correct here). (3) insert EXISTS-path key leak: insert suppresses the key source and adopts on a FRESH insert, but on the EXISTS (duplicate-key) path karac_map_insert_old keeps the bucket's existing key and never adopts the incoming one -- so the suppressed source's buffer is orphaned (one buffer per duplicate insert). Fix (maps.rs insert arm): free the owned incoming key (key_val, Some only on the non-borrowed path) on the existed (Some(old)) branch. Refactor: extracted the cap>0-guarded {ptr,len,cap} free out of free_fresh_owned_str_arg into the reusable, compile-time-gate-free free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap (runtime.rs); free_fresh_owned_str_arg keeps its fresh-temp expression gate and delegates the actual free -- behavior-preserving for all existing callers. NO runtime change, NO archive rebuild, NO interpreter change (the interpreter is GC-by-Value-clone; A/B output is byte-identical -- verified live: counter 3/2/1, get 3, entry +10 -> 12, contains_key has-cherry, identical under karac run and the codegen binary). Tests: 10 LSan regression tests in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs (entry moved-binding vacant no-double-free + occupied no-leak, entry owned-param vacant+occupied, entry and_modify moved-binding, get moved-binding + get fresh-temp, remove/contains fresh-temp [remove targets an ABSENT key on purpose -- see below], insert moved-binding-dup + owned-param-dup, insert duplicate heap-value discarded). All 24 map asan tests pass the Linux LSan gate; full worktree gate 314 passed / 3 failed where the 3 are PRE-EXISTING non-map leaks unrelated to this change (asan_owned_struct_option_shared_field_captured_from_builder_no_uaf, asan_single_field_struct_option_payload_sizing_no_bad_access, asan_string_eq_mismatched_len_no_overread_in_indexed_payload_match -- confirmed failing on clean main; from the recent selfhost codegen slices, invisible to the macOS post-landing run that has no LeakSanitizer). clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean, fmt clean. KNOWN OPEN (distinct, tracked separately): a present-key `remove` of a HEAP key tombstones the bucket WITHOUT freeing its STORED key (and the bool karac_map_remove variant also leaks the stored value) -- karac_map_free_with_drop_vec only frees OCCUPIED slots, so tombstoned buffers are orphaned. A full fix needs a drop-flag ABI on karac_map_remove_old (the runtime can't tell a heap key from a scalar one) + an archive rebuild -- out of scope for this codegen-only PR.

fix: Completes the map-key-ownership class B-2026-06-20-9 (c7b72bd4) started — that fix handled the key ARGUMENT (incoming, no-adopt); this handles the key/value already STORED in the bucket. A present-key remove of a HEAP key tombstones the bucket, but karac_map_free_with_drop_vec only walks OCCUPIED slots, so the tombstoned {ptr,len,cap} String/Vec key buffer is orphaned at map drop (Linux-LSan-only; macOS ASAN misses reachable leaks). FIXED via a drop-flag ABI on the runtime remove entry points + codegen threading the key's heap-ness through. RUNTIME (runtime/src/map.rs): karac_map_remove_old(map,key,out_old_val) gained drop_key: i32 — on a present-key tombstone it frees the bucket's STORED key when drop_key!=0 (heap {ptr,len,cap}) and cap>0; it NEVER frees the value, which is MOVED OUT to the caller via out_old_val (the returned Some(old) owns it — freeing it would double-free). The bool karac_map_remove(map,key) gained drop_key: i32, drop_val: i32 and frees BOTH stored halves (it discards both; the presence boolean carries no payload) — kept correct for the exported ABI even though codegen does not wire it (Map.remove/Set.remove lower to remove_old). Extracted the cap>0-guarded {ptr,len,cap} free into KaracMap::free_heap_field + free_stored_key/free_stored_val helpers and routed karac_map_free_with_drop_vec's live-slot walk through them (behavior-preserving dedup). CODEGEN: bumped the karac_map_remove_old declaration to 4 params (src/codegen.rs) and passed drop_key=llvm_ty_is_vec_struct(key_ty) at BOTH call sites — Map.remove (src/codegen/maps.rs) and Set.remove (src/codegen/collections.rs; elem_ty is the set's key, Set lowers to Map[T,()] so there is no value half). The Map.remove arm's existing incoming-key free (free_fresh_owned_str_arg, B-2026-06-20-9) is unchanged and complementary: it releases the key ARGUMENT on the no-adopt path; the new drop_key releases the STORED key the bucket adopted at insert. NO interpreter change (GC-by-Value-clone; A/B byte-identical). This MODIFIES an existing symbol's signature, so the prebuilt staticlib archives were REBUILT in the worktree (lean->min->full), not copied. TESTS: 2 LSan regression tests in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs (>=36-byte keys per the LSan-reachability rule) — asan_map_remove_present_heap_key_no_leak (Map[String,i64].remove(present)->Some; stored String key freed) and asan_map_remove_present_heap_key_and_vec_value_no_leak (Map[String,Vec[i64]].remove(present)->Some(vec): stored String key freed AND Vec value moved out + freed exactly once by the match-arm, NOT double-freed). NEGATIVE CONTROL: disabling the remove_old key free makes both tests FAIL under the Linux LSan gate (44 / 42 bytes leaked, exactly 1 allocation each = the stored key buffer; the value-test's single-alloc leak confirms the moved-out Vec is not leaked). GATES (worktree): fmt clean; clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm -D warnings clean; runtime unit tests 261; codegen 1700; macOS memory_sanitizer 319; Linux LSan gate 316 passed / 3 failed where the 3 are the PRE-EXISTING non-map leaks documented in B-2026-06-20-9 (asan_owned_struct_option_shared_field_captured_from_builder_no_uaf, asan_single_field_struct_option_payload_sizing_no_bad_access, asan_string_eq_mismatched_len_no_overread_in_indexed_payload_match — confirmed failing on clean main, unrelated to maps); all 39 map LSan tests green incl. the 2 new ones. KNOWN OPEN (distinct, out of scope): Set.remove of a heap element still leaks the INCOMING element — the B-2026-06-20-9 incoming-key class was never applied to Set (collections.rs has no free_fresh_owned_str_arg); flagged for a follow-up slice.
title: Present-key Map.remove / Set.remove of a HEAP key leaks the bucket's STORED key buffer (and the bool karac_map_remove variant leaks the stored value too). The present-key remove tombstones the bucket, but karac_map_free_with_drop_vec only walks OCCUPIED slots, so the tombstoned {ptr,len,cap} String/Vec key buffer is orphaned at map drop. Distinct from the INCOMING-key no-adopt class (B-2026-06-20-9, c7b72bd4) which handled the key ARGUMENT; this is the key/value already STORED in the bucket. Needs a runtime drop-flag ABI (the runtime cannot tell a heap key from a scalar — only codegen knows) + an archive rebuild, not a codegen-only change. Completes the map-key-ownership class B-2026-06-20-9 started. Linux-LSan-only (macOS ASAN misses reachable leaks).

Two codegen gaps surfaced by the bespoke word-frequency kata's `keys().sort()` ordered-report idiom over a `Map[String,_]`. (1) `Vec[String].sort()` was INTEGER-ONLY in codegen (errored 'Vec.sort() supports only integer element types; use sort_by(...)'); only the bare default-order `sort()` for ints had a comparator thunk. Fix (vec_method.rs): a new `emit_default_sort_thunk_string` builds the (ctx,*a,*b)->i64 comparator that loads each `{ptr,len,cap}` String header and calls the existing `karac_string_cmp` byte-lexicographic runtime fn (the same comparator `Vec.binary_search` and the String-key `sort_by` path already use); the `sort` arm picks it when `vec_elem_type_name(var) == "String"` (a Vec[T] element can't reach it — Vec is not Ord, so the typechecker only admits `.sort()` on String among heap `{ptr,len,cap}` shapes). Integer sort unchanged. (2) `Map.keys()/values()/entries()` SHALLOW-copied heap key/value halves into the result Vec, which is drop-tracked as OWNING its elements — so the result Vec's scope-exit drop and the map's own drop freed the same `{ptr,len,cap}` buffer (double-free). It crashed `Map[String,_].keys()` outright (SIGTRAP before any read; buffered stdout lost). Fix (maps.rs compile_map_keys_values_entries): deep-clone each heap half into the result buffer via `emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr` (the same owned-copy contract as `Map.get_or` — deep for String/Vec/struct, memcpy for scalar, pointer-copy for shared), through a new `kvg_emit_half` helper; the key TypeExpr comes from `map_key_type_exprs`, the value from `var_elem_type_exprs` (both populated for annotated maps). Falls back to the prior shallow load+store when a half's TypeExpr side-table entry is absent (inferred maps with no recorded K/V TypeExpr) — correct for scalars, regression-free otherwise. Interpreter was already correct (GC-by-Value-clone); A/B byte-identical. Tests: codegen E2E (vec string sort; keys-sorted report exercising BOTH fixes; values/entries owned-copy content) + memory_sanitizer (keys/values/entries deep-copy no double-free, macOS ASAN + Linux LSan). clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm + fmt clean. NO new runtime symbol (karac_string_cmp / karac_vec_sort_by / karac_clone_* all pre-exist), NO archive rebuild. RELATED OPEN (kata still blocked on it, tracked separately): the flagship `for w in words { *m.entry(w).or_insert(0) += 1 }` DOUBLE-FREES when the key is a MOVED FOR-LOOP ELEMENT — `push(w)` from a loop works, `entry(w)` does not, despite the entry chain running the identical consume-site suppress as push (B-2026-06-20-9). Distinct from the local-binding entry case (which passes). The kata uses `entry(w.to_string())` until that lands. Also a minor type-inference follow-up: an un-annotated `let keys = m.keys()` doesn't propagate the String element type to the `.sort()` gate (annotate `let keys: Vec[String]` meanwhile).

fix: efeb9dbf. Completes the Set side of the map/set key-ownership class: B-2026-06-20-9 (c7b72bd4) fixed the INCOMING key for Map's no-adopt paths but never applied it to Set (collections.rs had ZERO free_fresh_owned_str_arg calls), and B-2026-06-20-10 (a1b59c5e) fixed only the Set STORED element on a present-key remove. This handles the remaining gap — the INCOMING element ARGUMENT on Set's no-adopt paths. Set lowers to Map[T, ()], so the three element-taking arms in src/codegen/collections.rs call karac_map_remove_old / karac_map_contains / karac_map_insert_old; each leaked the incoming element buffer (Linux-LSan-only; macOS ASAN misses reachable leaks). (1) Set.remove and (2) Set.contains are lookup-only and never retain the incoming element — added free_fresh_owned_str_arg(&args[0].value, elem_val) after the runtime call (mirrors Map.remove / Map.contains_key from B-2026-06-20-9; no-ops on a moved binding via its own un-suppressed source free, on a borrowed cap==0 view, and on a non-Vec-String element). Set.remove's incoming free is a DISTINCT buffer from the STORED element freed by the existing drop_key flag (B-2026-06-20-10): the present-key remove test leaks exactly ONE buffer pre-fix (the incoming), confirming drop_key already frees the stored one. (3) Set.insert lowers to karac_map_insert_old, which ADOPTS the element only on the VACANT insert; on the EXISTS (duplicate) path it keeps the bucket's existing element and never adopts the incoming one, while the insert arm's consume-site dance (suppress_fstr_acc_if_moved_out + maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg + suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg) already either suppressed a moved source's scope-exit free or made a private defensive copy of an owned-param element — so the incoming {ptr,len,cap} buffer is orphaned. Fix: free it on the EXISTS branch ONLY (mirror Map.insert's exists-path free), via a conditional-branch diamond guarded by the `existed` bool calling free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap(elem_val); on the vacant branch the bucket adopted the buffer, so a free there would double-free. A vec-struct compile-time gate (llvm_ty_is_vec_struct(elem_ty)) restricts the diamond to heap (Set[String]/Set[Vec[T]]) elements; the cap>0 runtime guard inside free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap no-ops on a borrowed view / rodata literal. Audited ALL Set.* arms: len/is_empty/clear take no element; union/intersection/difference take another SET HANDLE (borrowed, not an owned element buffer) — only insert/contains/remove take an owned element. Reuses the existing free_fresh_owned_str_arg / free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap helpers (runtime.rs) — no duplicated cap>0 {ptr,len,cap} free logic. NO runtime/ABI change, NO archive rebuild, NO interpreter change (interpreter is GC-by-Value-clone; A/B output byte-identical). TESTS: 4 LSan regression tests in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs (>=36-byte elements per the LSan-reachability rule, since LSan misses short still-reachable String/Vec buffers) — asan_set_remove_present_fresh_temp_element_no_leak (Set[String].remove(present): STORED element freed by drop_key + INCOMING fresh temp freed by this fix, two distinct buffers), asan_set_contains_present_fresh_temp_element_no_leak (Set[String].contains(present) fresh temp), asan_set_insert_moved_binding_duplicate_element_no_leak (Set[String].insert dup moved binding -> exists-branch free), asan_set_remove_absent_fresh_temp_vec_element_no_leak (Set[Vec[i64]].remove(absent) fresh-temp Vec from a helper fn, >=48-byte data buffer; uses an EXPLICIT MISS because Set[Vec] does not dedupe equal-contents vecs — a pre-existing Set/Vec hash-eq gap, out of scope — so the lookup-only incoming free is isolated without depending on content equality). NEGATIVE CONTROL: stashing only collections.rs (fix reverted, tests kept) makes all 4 new tests FAIL under the Linux LSan gate with EXACTLY ONE leaked allocation each (39 / 40 / 64 / 39 bytes = the incoming element buffer; the present-remove test's single 39-byte leak confirms the stored element is NOT leaked); restoring the fix makes all 4 pass. GATES (worktree): fmt clean; clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm -D warnings clean; macOS codegen 1707; macOS memory_sanitizer 325 passed / 1 ignored (incl. the 4 new); Linux LSan gate `set` filter 15 passed / 0 failed (incl. the 4 new). The 3 PRE-EXISTING non-map/non-set LSan leaks documented in B-2026-06-20-9/-10 (asan_owned_struct_option_shared_field_captured_from_builder_no_uaf, asan_single_field_struct_option_payload_sizing_no_bad_access, asan_string_eq_mismatched_len_no_overread_in_indexed_payload_match) are unaffected (not in the `set` filter; macOS ASAN does not surface them). Completes the map/set key-ownership class B-2026-06-20-9 / B-2026-06-20-10 started.
title: Set INCOMING-element NO-ADOPT leak: Set.remove(x) / Set.contains(x) / Set.insert(x) of a HEAP element (Set[String], Set[Vec[T]]) leaked the incoming element buffer when the argument is a fresh-owned temp (s.remove("x".to_string())) or a moved binding on a no-adopt path. The B-2026-06-20-9 incoming-key class fixed for Map was never applied to Set (collections.rs had zero free_fresh_owned_str_arg calls); B-2026-06-20-10 fixed only the Set STORED element on a present-key remove. Codegen-only (Set lowers to Map[T,()], arms call karac_map_remove_old / karac_map_contains / karac_map_insert_old); no runtime/ABI change, no archive rebuild. Linux-LSan-only (macOS ASAN misses reachable leaks). Completes the map/set key-ownership class B-2026-06-20-9 / B-2026-06-20-10 started.

Heap `for`-loop element BORROW consumed by a retaining sink double-freed in codegen (A/B mismatch on the flagship counter idiom). `for w in vec` over a Vec is BORROW-iteration: the loop binds `w` to an ALIAS of `data[i]` (a plain header load, compile_for_vec_var) and the source Vec RETAINS ownership — it is usable after the loop (`for w in words {..}; words.len()` works, prints the full count). So a consume site that RETAINS `w` — `m.entry(w)`, `v.push(w)`, `m.insert(w, ..)` — bit-copied `w`'s `{ptr,len,cap}` into the sink, and BOTH the sink's drop and the source Vec's scope-exit drop freed the same buffer (double-free; SIGTRAP, buffered stdout lost). The interpreter clones values freely (GC-by-Value-clone), so it produced the right answer — this was a silent A/B divergence on the canonical histogram `for w in words { *m.entry(w).or_insert(0) += 1 }` (codegen crashed; interp printed the counts). Earlier mis-diagnosed as entry-specific (B-2026-06-20-11 RELATED note) because the `push(w)` control used STRING LITERAL elements (cap==0 rodata — no heap to double-free); with `.to_string()` heap elements, push/insert double-free identically. So it is general to all retaining-consume sites, not entry. FIX (codegen, no runtime change): a new `for_loop_borrow_vars` set marks heap (String/Vec) for-loop element bindings — `register_for_loop_bindings` adds a Binding (and the k/v of `for (k,v) in m`) when the element landed in `vec_elem_types` (the {ptr,len,cap} shapes) via the new `mark_for_loop_borrow_if_heap`. `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` treats membership the SAME as `owned_vecstr_params`: it deep-copies the borrowed element (`emit_vecstr_defensive_copy`) so the sink owns a private buffer while the source Vec keeps freeing its own elements — exactly the owned-param model, one level in (the source retains the scope-exit free in both). The consume sites (Vec.push/push_back, Map.insert key+value, the entry-chain key from B-2026-06-20-9) already call that helper, so they are fixed by the gate change alone; read-only loop bodies never call it, so they are untouched (no extra clone). A later `let` of the same name clears stale membership in the binding-registration block (shadow guard) so a fresh owned binding reusing a loop var name is not wrongly copied (the copy pairs with a source-suppress → would orphan the fresh String; LSan-only). Cleared per-function alongside `owned_vecstr_params`; NOT mono-saved (parity with owned_vecstr_params, which also relies on the per-fn clear). A/B verified byte-identical: the canonical word-frequency kata (histogram via `for w in words { *freq.entry(w)... }`, ascending report) now matches under `karac run` and `karac build`. Tests: 3 LSan regression tests in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs (entry counter with repeated keys + words-live-after; push+insert; shadow-rebind no-leak), macOS ASAN + Linux LSan green; clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm + fmt clean. RELATED MINOR OPEN (type-inference, not memory): an un-annotated `let keys = m.keys()` does not propagate the String element type to the `Vec.sort()` codegen gate (annotate `let keys: Vec[String]` meanwhile) — the kata annotates the binding. Separate from this ownership fix.

Three PRE-EXISTING leaks the Linux-LSan gate (scripts/lsan-local.sh) flags but the macOS post-landing ASAN run misses (Apple clang has no LeakSanitizer), surfaced by the phase-12 self-host render slices and confirmed failing on clean main. NOT introduced by the B-2026-06-20-9 map-key fix (all three are non-map). (1) SHARED-ENUM String/Vec payload MOVE-OUT double-free (suppress_shared_enum_payload_move_out, control_flow_match.rs). `match e { S(s) => s }` over `shared enum E { S(String) }` (the render_expr/get shape, returned) only zeroed the LOCAL binding's cap on move-out via the tail-move logic -- the RC box's payload words still pointed at the moved-out buffer, so the box's `__karac_rc_drop_<E>` (whose Vec/String arm frees cap>0) re-freed it after the caller already freed the returned String: a double-free (macOS ASAN catches it; the nested tests-1/2 form only LEAKED because the boxed-struct-drop gap below masked it -- the inner box's drop never ran). Fix: the shared sibling of the existing suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup_at, which explicitly bails on layout.is_shared. For each consumed EnumDropKind::VecOrString field, zero its payload words IN THE BOX (heap index start_word+2, mirroring emit_shared_enum_rc_drop_fn) so the box rc-drop skips the buffer the binding now owns. Gated to owned (non-borrow) shared scrutinees; shared-handle (rc-managed) and NestedStruct payloads are untouched. (2) SHARED-ENUM BOXED-struct payload rc-drop gap (emit_shared_enum_field_drop boxed arm + emit_nested_struct_shared_rc_decs_ex, synth_drop.rs). A struct payload wider than its allotted payload-area words is heap-boxed at construction (coerce_to_payload_words, `out.len() > num_words`: e.g. `struct Block { tail: Option[Expr] }` used as `Expr.Blk(Block)` -- the Option field hits the enum-in-enum carve-out, undersizing the area while Block is 4 words), but the rc-drop's struct arm ALWAYS read the payload INLINE -- GEP'ing the box-POINTER word as the struct's first field (a garbage tag, so the recursion skipped) and never freeing the box. It leaked the enumbox container PLUS every heap child reachable through it (the Block's inner Option[shared Expr] box -- tests #48 88+80B and #49 32+40B). Fix: recompute the SAME `llvm_type_word_count(struct) > num_words` predicate the pack/unpack sites use, and on boxed: inttoptr word 0 -> heap struct, walk it, then free the box. The walk passes nested_buffer_free=Some(false) (a new param replacing the old recurse bool): the boxed struct's DIRECT Vec/String buffers + shared/Option[shared] children are reclaimed, but a NESTED heap struct FIELD (`IfNode.then_block: Block`) is recursed to rc-dec ONLY its RC children -- because that nested struct may be MOVED OUT by the match binding (`let tb = nd.then_block`), whose own __karac_drop_struct_<S> value-drop frees its BUFFERS but does NOT rc-dec its shared children. Re-freeing those buffers through the box walk was a double-free (regressed tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_shared_enum_payload_with_nested_heap_struct_field -> empty output: a SIGSEGV at the scope-exit drop lost the buffered stdout); skipping the children was a leak. Some(false) splits them: buffers to the move-out owner, RC children to the box -- no double-free, no stranded child. RESIDUAL BOUNDED LEAK (documented v1, never corruption): a NEVER-moved-out nested heap struct's own Vec/String buffer inside a boxed payload is not reclaimed (the box walk leaves nested buffers to a move-out owner that, in that case, does not exist); none of the suite hits this. (3) METHOD-CALL fresh String/Vec temp arg leak (compile_method_call, method_call.rs). A fresh String/Vec produced by a Call/MethodCall and passed DIRECTLY by value to a USER method (`lx.ident_matches("Fn".to_string())`) had no consuming binding, and an owned by-value Vec/String param is NOT freed by the callee (it lands in owned_vecstr_params for retaining-consume deep-copy, never a callee-side track_vec_var) -- so the temp orphaned, leaking one buffer per call. The free-fn compile_call arg loop already materializes such args into a caller-scope __owned_tmp with a scope-exit free (the #20 is_fresh_heap_call_arg arm + the bare-shared __owned_arg_tmp arm); the method arg loop was missing it. Fix: mirror both arms verbatim after track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg, with the same guards (expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp / inline-temp-vec-index, llvm_ty_is_vec_struct, !rhs_stages_fstr_acc). Built-in consuming methods (push/insert/entry.or_insert) are special-cased BEFORE this generic user-method dispatch, so they are unaffected (verified: or_insert(Vec.new()) emits no __owned_tmp). Tests: tests/codegen.rs +3 IR-shape (shared_enum_string_payload_moveout_zeros_box_cap; shared_enum_boxed_struct_payload_rc_drop_unboxes_and_frees; method_call_fresh_string_temp_arg_materialized); tests/memory_sanitizer.rs +2 E2E (asan_shared_enum_string_payload_moveout_no_double_free -- the minimal move-out double-free that no prior test isolated, all existing shared-enum tests extract only scalar/shared-handle payloads; asan_shared_enum_boxed_struct_payload_moveout_no_double_free -- the boxed-struct nested-move-out, LSan-clean). The 3 target tests (asan_owned_struct_option_shared_field_captured_from_builder_no_uaf, asan_single_field_struct_option_payload_sizing_no_bad_access, asan_string_eq_mismatched_len_no_overread_in_indexed_payload_match) now LSan-green. Suites: codegen 1703, memory_sanitizer 319, par_codegen 122 (macOS ASAN); full scripts/lsan-local.sh green except the pre-existing flake below; fmt + clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean. NO runtime change, NO archive rebuild, NO interpreter change. KNOWN OPEN (PRE-EXISTING, distinct, NOT this change): asan_match_arm_vec_binding_freed_on_arm_exit SEGVs INTERMITTENTLY under Linux LSan (__aarch64_cas1_acq_rel, addr 0xff..f1) -- a seed-dependent (codegen HashMap-order) heap corruption in `Map.remove` of a heap VALUE (Vec[i64]) moved out into a match binding, the VALUE side of the map-remove ownership class (the stored-KEY side was fixed in B-2026-06-20-10/a1b59c5e, which deliberately never frees the moved-out value). Confirmed reproducing on CLEAN primary main under LSan when run ALONE; passes on most seeds, including the full post-rebase gate run that landed this change (330 passed / 0 failed). The map codegen is untouched by this change; a deterministic fix is a separate follow-up.

fix: ddc625ad. TWO Vec-specific root causes, both fixed. (1) TYPECHECKER (src/typechecker/derives.rs): the built-in `Vec` is registered in env.structs with NO derived traits, so `type_supports_hash`/`type_supports_eq` fell through to the generic `Type::Named` lookup and reported `Vec` as un-Hash/un-Eq -- a HARD ERROR in the codegen (`karac build`) path (so `Set[Vec[T]]` did not even compile) but only a non-fatal WARNING in the interpreter (`karac run`) path (interpreter is GC-by-Value-clone and dedupes via structural `Value::Array` eq, so it printed the right answer). Fix: a dedicated `Type::Named { name: "Vec", args } if args.len()==1` arm in BOTH predicates, placed BEFORE the generic Named struct/enum lookup, that recurses into the element (`Vec[T]` is Hash/Eq by content iff `T` is) -- mirrors the existing `Type::Array`/`Type::Slice`/`Type::Vector` recursion and `type_supports_display`'s explicit `"Vec"` arm. `Set[Vec[f64]]` stays correctly REJECTED (f64 is not Eq -- IEEE-754 NaN!=NaN). (2) CODEGEN (src/codegen/synth.rs): even past that gate, a `Vec[T]` element/key routed through the `emit_hash_fn_for_type`/`emit_eq_fn_for_type` byte-loop FALLBACK, which hashes/compares the {ptr,len,cap} HEADER (pointer identity), so two equal-contents vecs land in different buckets and never collapse. (String elements always deduped via the `type_name=="String"` byte-walk arm, masking the gap.) Fix: a `Vec` dispatch arm in `emit_hash_fn_for_type_expr`/`emit_eq_fn_for_type_expr` (before the user-struct arm) that, for a `TypeKind::Path` head "Vec" with a `GenericArg::Type` arg, calls the new `emit_hash_fn_for_vec`/`emit_eq_fn_for_vec`; absent the arg it falls back to the header byte-loop. `emit_hash_fn_for_vec` emits `karac_hash_Vec_<elem>(*const Vec)->i64`: loads {data,len} from the {ptr,len,cap} header, seeds the FxHash state with `len` (length is part of the digest, matching Rust's `Hash for [T]`; rotate_left(0,5)=0 collapses mix(0,len) to len*SEED), then folds each per-element hash (`emit_hash_fn_for_type_expr(elem)`, recurses for Vec[String]/Vec[Vec[_]]) via the same rotate-5/xor/mul tail-mix the tuple/struct combiners use. `emit_eq_fn_for_vec` emits `karac_eq_Vec_<elem>(*const Vec,*const Vec)->i1`: compare lengths, then each element via the per-element eq fn, short-circuit false on first mismatch. CRITICAL naming: keyed on the element-aware `karac_hash_Vec_<elem>`/`karac_eq_Vec_<elem>` (via `display_mangle_te`) NOT the shallow `mangled_type_name` "Vec" -- otherwise distinct element types would share one now-content-dependent body; the dispatcher's early cache check (keyed on shallow "Vec") simply misses for Vec and the real dedup happens inside the new fns. Empty vecs: len 0 -> no element loop, hash 0, eq true (data ptr loaded but never dereferenced -> no NULL deref). `cap` is NOT read (a Vec's value identity is len+contents, not capacity). NO runtime/ABI change, NO archive rebuild, NO interpreter change (A/B byte-identical). Fixes `Map[Vec[T], _]` keys and Vec-field-bearing struct/tuple keys for free (all route through the same dispatchers). Vec-ONLY on BOTH sides (not VecDeque): the codegen content path is keyed on a Path head "Vec", so admitting VecDeque in the typechecker without a matching codegen path would re-create the A/B divergence one layer down -- keeping both sides Vec-only stays in lockstep. The fix ALSO opens a previously-UNREACHABLE ownership path: once two equal-contents vecs collapse, the second insert takes `karac_map_insert_old`'s EXISTS branch, whose incoming-element free (B-2026-06-20-12) now actually fires -- covered by a new LSan regression. TESTS: 3 codegen E2E (tests/codegen.rs: test_e2e_set_vec_dedup_by_content [dedup + distinct-stay-separate + contains/remove + same-prefix-diff-length non-equality], test_e2e_set_string_dedup_companion, test_e2e_map_vec_key_dedup_by_content); 2 typechecker (tests/typechecker.rs: test_set_and_map_accept_vec_element_when_inner_hash_eq, test_set_rejects_vec_element_when_inner_not_hash_eq); 1 LSan (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs: asan_set_vec_duplicate_element_dedup_no_leak_no_double_free, >=48-byte buffer per the LSan-reachability rule). Stale-comment fixup on asan_set_remove_absent_fresh_temp_vec_element_no_leak (its "Set[Vec] does not dedupe" parenthetical). GATES (worktree): fmt clean; clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm -D warnings clean; typechecker 1741; codegen 1710 (incl. 3 new); macOS memory_sanitizer 329 passed/1 ignored (incl. new); Linux LSan gate `set` filter 16 passed/0 failed (incl. new dedup test). Determinism verified across 6 codegen rebuilds (no HashMap-order nondeterminism). Closes the SEPARATE Set/Vec hash-eq gap noted while writing B-2026-06-20-12 (efeb9dbf).
title: Set[Vec[T]] (and Map[Vec[T], _]) did not deduplicate equal-CONTENTS vecs -- two equal vecs inserted as distinct elements (len()==2 instead of 1), an A/B divergence vs the interpreter (which dedupes via structural Value::Array eq). A `Set` has HashSet value semantics, so this is a correctness bug. Two Vec-specific causes: (1) the built-in `Vec` is registered with no derived traits so type_supports_hash/eq reported it un-Hash/un-Eq -- a hard ERROR in the codegen path (Set[Vec[T]] never compiled) but only a warning in the interpreter path; (2) past that gate, codegen's Vec element hash/eq used the byte-loop fallback over the {ptr,len,cap} HEADER (pointer identity) instead of walking the contents. String elements always deduped (byte-walk arm), masking the gap. Discovered while writing the B-2026-06-20-12 Set incoming-element leak tests (efeb9dbf); the leak fix is unrelated and already landed -- this is the separate functional dedup gap flagged there.

fix: 1ee2b64d
title: Auto-par (statement-level) RACED a map-mutating loop against a later read of the same map under the DEFAULT `karac build` — a silent wrong-answer/crash. The word-frequency kata's `for w in words { *freq.entry(w).or_insert(0) += 1 }` histogram loop and the subsequent `freq.keys()` were placed in the SAME parallel_group (`--concurrency-report`: "no data or effect dependencies"), so `freq.keys()` ran concurrently while the loop was still mutating `freq` — a read-after-write race on the map (mutex panics, garbled output). `karac run` (interpreter) and `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build` were both correct, so it was a silent A/B mismatch on the flagship counter idiom. ROOT CAUSE (src/concurrency.rs): the dual-analysis dependency graph builds per-statement reads/writes sets. `collect_assign_target_defines` (the write-target place-root resolver) matched only `Identifier` / `SelfValue` / `FieldAccess` / `Index` — it had NO arm for a `Unary{Deref}` or a `MethodCall` target, so a `*<place> = …` / `*<place> += …` whose place is a method chain recorded NO write. The CompoundAssign `*freq.entry(w).or_insert(0) += 1` therefore contributed zero writes; the `for`-loop's writes set (collected from the body via collect_block_inner_writes -> collect_assign_target_defines) omitted `freq`; the loop statement looked write-free; and the parallelizer saw no write-vs-read conflict with `freq.keys()` -> grouped -> raced. FIX: `collect_assign_target_defines` now recurses a `Unary{op: Deref}` target into its operand and a `MethodCall` place target into its receiver, so a write through a deref/method-chain roots at the underlying container — `*m.entry(k).or_insert(d) += 1` records writes(m), `*v.get_mut(i) = x` records writes(v). For a plain `*ref += …` on a mut-ref local it records the binding (the pointee's owner), which is conservative — it may over-serialize but NEVER under-serializes, the only safe direction for the parallel-safety gate. Reads were already captured (collect_block_reads routes CompoundAssign/Assign targets through the general collect_expr_reads, which recurses MethodCall/Unary). After the fix the racy loop+keys() parallel_group no longer forms (`--concurrency-report` shows only the two genuinely-independent groups), and the DEFAULT auto-par build of the word-frequency kata is A/B byte-identical to `karac run`. Tests: tests/concurrency.rs unit (a map-mutating loop is not co-grouped with a later `m.keys()` read) + tests/par_codegen.rs E2E (auto-par histogram-then-keys, deterministic sorted output — exercises the whole word-frequency cascade: moved-loop-element copy B-2026-06-20-13, keys deep-copy + String sort B-2026-06-20-11, and this serialization). Full concurrency unit suite 100, clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm + fmt clean. NO runtime change, NO archive rebuild. FOURTH and final gap surfaced by the bespoke word-frequency kata (after B-2026-06-20-9 entry/get/insert no-adopt, -11 sort+keys deep-copy, -13 moved-loop-element copy); the kata now runs A/B-clean under run + default build + KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0.

title: Follow-up on the KNOWN-OPEN value-side `Map.remove` SEGV that B-2026-06-20-14 logged for asan_match_arm_vec_binding_freed_on_arm_exit (intermittent __aarch64_cas1_acq_rel crash at addr 0xff..f1 under Linux LSan, attributed to a seed-flavoured heap corruption in `Map.remove` of a heap VALUE moved into a match binding). CONCLUSION: does NOT reproduce on current main (886c2a2f); no latent codegen bug found; closed with permanent regression coverage rather than a code change. Evidence: (1) the emitted IR for the exact `match bucket.remove(k) { Some(indices) => indices.len() }` over `Map[i64,Vec[i64]]` is single-owner and provably correct -- `karac_map_remove_old(.., drop_key=0)` bitwise-moves the value out into the `Some` payload words and tombstones the slot WITHOUT freeing it; the arm reconstructs `{ptr,len,cap}` into `indices` and frees its data buffer EXACTLY ONCE under a `cap>0` guard; the scope-exit `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec(handle, key=0, val=1)` walks only OCCUPIED slots, all of which are tombstoned by then -> no double-free, no leak, no UAF. (2) The path has NO HashMap-order-dependent decision (drop_key and the val-is-vec free flag are pure type predicates; the per-arm cleanup frame is an ordered Vec with a single FreeVecBuffer; no shared types are involved, so the shared-heap-type-collision nondeterminism class does not apply) -- the single-function IR is therefore structurally seed-invariant, so the dumped IR is representative of every seed. (3) ~2680 REAL Linux arm64 ASAN+LSan runs across fresh per-process HashMap seeds (the original test plus three new churn stress variants), 0 failures, with a verified positive control (a deliberate 12345-byte C leak IS reported by the same container's LSan, and karac emits direct malloc/free so ASAN tracks the kara heap). ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS for the original transient symptom: a stale-archive ABI mismatch during the B-2026-06-20-10/a1b59c5e `drop_key` rollout -- codegen emitting the 4-arg `karac_map_remove_old` call against a not-yet-rebuilt 3-arg archive in the SHARED kara-lsan-target docker volume (the documented stale-karac-after-rebase footgun), so the 4th arg landed in a register the old body sometimes clobbered -> seed/layout-flavoured corruption that vanishes once all archives are rebuilt consistently. The earlier 'reproducing when run ALONE' observation is consistent with a single contaminated build, not a code defect. ADDED (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs, +3 E2E churn guards that exhaust the ASAN quarantine so any real value-side double-free/UAF surfaces as live-chunk corruption, not a benign quarantined catch): asan_map_remove_vec_value_moveout_under_churn (Vec[i64], 200 keys x 20 generations x 20 iters), asan_map_remove_vec_value_indexed_readback (reads every element of the moved-out Vec inside the arm before free), asan_map_remove_string_key_vec_value_both_heap_halves (heap String key drop_key=1 + heap Vec value move-out, both halves freed once). Suites: memory_sanitizer 337 passed/0 failed (macOS ASAN) + full scripts/lsan-local.sh value-path loop green; codegen unchanged-count green; fmt + clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean. NO src/ change, NO runtime change, NO archive ABI change.

fix: b83e11fc
title: SoA layout elements with String/Vec heap fields leaked across push/store/cleanup (front-end rejected them entirely). Lifted the resolver gate for String + Vec[POD] element fields (Map/Set/VecDeque/Sorted*/Vec[heap]/shared still rejected) and added per-element heap-field drops across the whole SoA write/drop lifecycle. Synthesized a per-layout __karac_soa_drop_<layout>(*mut SoaStruct) (emit_soa_drop_fn, cached in soa_drop_fns) that loops live elements [0,len) and frees each heap group's String/Vec buffers via emit_aggregate_heap_field_frees (recursing nested tuples/structs); None for a POD layout so that path stays byte-identical (Slipstream native oracle held). The drop fn is carried on CleanupAction::FreeSoaGroups / SlotOwnership::Soa and invoked inside the cap>0 guard BEFORE the group buffers are freed, at scope-exit cleanup, carried-grid reassignment (emit_free_soa_groups_inline), and single-element whole-element/field-store drop-old (emit_soa_drop_element_at). Move-in double-frees suppressed: a named owned struct moved into push / grid[i]= is cap-zeroed (zero_struct_move_caps), and an f-string into grid[i].name= has its accumulator's FreeVecBuffer neutralized. pop/remove unchanged (scatter-read moves the element out; decremented len excludes the vacated slot). Verified on the Linux LSan gate (21/21 SoA tests, ≥36-byte payloads ×20 frames). RESIDUAL: reading a heap SoA field back as a method receiver / index base (grid[i].name.len(), grid[i].data[k]) needs the field's address (the per-field read materialize-then-extracts a non-addressable SSA value — correct only as a direct value like println(grid[i].name)); and whole-element let e=grid[i] aliases the buffer (the same latent hazard AoS Vec[Struct] already carries). The SoA heap-field READ-back is the next slice.
