fix: fcc2c925
title: First-class fn value bound to a LOCAL first miscompiled — sibling of B-2026-06-20-1 (which only closed the direct bare-fn-name argument case). `let f = doubler; apply(f, 21)` (and the `let f: Fn(i64)->i64 = doubler;` annotated form) failed LLVM module verification ('Call parameter type does not match function signature! ... load ptr ... call ... @apply(ptr, i64)'), because the free-fn-name-as-value path (exprs.rs Identifier arm) produced a raw `ptr` and the local was never registered in closure_fn_types — so the local held an 8-byte raw fn ptr while the `Fn(...)` parameter slot is the 16-byte {fn_ptr,env_ptr} fat pointer. WORSE: a direct call through such a local, `let f: Fn(i64)->i64 = doubler; f(21)`, compiled clean but SILENTLY RETURNED 0 (the unregistered name fell through compile_call's unknown-callee branch), a wrong-output miscompile rather than a verifier error. FIXED 2026-06-21 (fcc2c925): in compile_stmt's `let <name> = <bare fn name>` arm, reify the fn name into a {trampoline, null env} closure fat pointer and register the local in closure_fn_types, so both `apply(f, x)` (pass to a Fn-typed param) and `f(x)` (direct call through the local) work for annotated and inferred bindings; the fat pointer's env is null and the trampoline is a module global, so the binding owns no heap (early return, no scope cleanup). Refactor for one trampoline definition per fn: reify_named_fn_value is the shared core (argument-site + let-binding paths), emit_fn_value_trampoline derives its env-first signature from the TARGET fn's own LLVM signature (not a Fn annotation) so the single memoized __karac_fnval_<name> stays consistent, and a side-effect-free name_resolves_to_free_fn mirrors compile_expr's Identifier resolution precedence (const-subst/local/module-let/unit-enum-variant/top-level-const all shadow a free fn) via membership tables only — never try_load_module_binding/try_unit_enum_variant, which emit IR. Typechecker already accepts both forms (verified). Tests: tests/codegen.rs fn_value_let_bound_named_fn_passed_and_called / fn_value_let_and_arg_reify_share_one_trampoline (memoization) / test_ir_inline_always_through_fn_value_compiles (un-defers the codegen-hint-attrs indirect-call IR test that waited on B-2026-06-20-1); leak gate tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_let_bound_fn_value_heap_arg_no_leak (heap String through a let-bound fn value freed once — green on the Linux ASAN+LSan harness). RESIDUAL (next slice): returning a `Fn(...)` value (-> Fn(...)), storing one in a struct field / Vec[Fn()], and the `karac run` interpreter path for fn values are still unaddressed.

First-class fn values in return / struct-field / Vec[Fn] positions miscompiled — the remaining non-arg, non-let positions after B-2026-06-20-1/-06-21-1. A `fn` returning a `Fn(...)` value (`fn pick() -> Fn(i64)->i64 { doubler }`) failed verification ('Function return type does not match operand type of return inst! ret ptr @doubler / {ptr,ptr}') because the bare fn name in return-tail position emitted a raw ptr vs the {fn_ptr,env_ptr} return slot; a fn value stored in a struct field (`H { f: doubler }`) or Vec element (`v.push(doubler)`) stored a raw ptr into a fat-pointer slot and the call back through it silently returned 0. FIXED 2026-06-21 (98731b72): make the bare-fn-name-as-value lower to the {trampoline, null env} closure fat pointer at the ONE free-fn-as-value source — the Identifier arm of compile_expr (src/codegen/exprs.rs) — instead of a raw ptr. That single change fixes every value position at once (return tail, struct-field init, Vec element, let RHS); Server.serve resolves its handler name independently (resolve_free_fn_for_handler_arg) so its raw-fn-ptr FFI ABI is untouched (whole codegen suite 1736/0 confirms no regression). Call side: new let_binding_fn_value_type registers a fn-value `let` binding in closure_fn_types so `f(x)` is an indirect call — signature recovered from an explicit `Fn(...)` annotation, a bare free-fn-name RHS, or a call whose callee's declared return type is `Fn(...)` (so `let f = pick()` works un-annotated). env_first_fn_type factors the shared env-first signature build; the compile_stmt let arm routes through let_binding_fn_value_type (replacing the bare-name-only special case from B-2026-06-21-1). Interpreter (`karac run`) ALREADY handled fn values as args/let/return — verified, added regression cover (tests/interpreter.rs fn_value_passed_to_param/let_bound_then_called/returned_then_called) rather than a fix; closes the third 'residual' item from B-2026-06-21-1 as a non-bug. Tests: tests/codegen.rs fn_value_returned_then_called / fn_value_returned_passed_directly / fn_value_struct_field_annotated_extraction / fn_value_vec_element_annotated_extraction; leak gate tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_returned_fn_value_heap_arg_no_leak (heap String through a returned fn value freed once — green on Linux ASAN+LSan). RESIDUAL: un-annotated extraction of a fn value from a struct field / Vec element (`let g = h.f;` without `: Fn(..)`) still falls through to the unknown-callee path — needs per-field/per-element fn-type tracking; explicit `let g: Fn(..) = h.f` is the workaround. [CLOSED by B-2026-06-21-3.]

Un-annotated first-class fn-value extraction from a struct field / Vec element miscompiled — the last residual of B-2026-06-21-2. `let g = h.f;` / `let g = v[0];` (no `: Fn(..)` annotation) reading a `Fn(..)`-typed struct field or `Vec` element bound `g` to the correct fat pointer, but `g` was never registered in closure_fn_types because its signature wasn't recoverable from the RHS shape (field-read / index, unlike a bare fn name or a call-with-declared-Fn-return), so `g(x)` fell through compile_call's unknown-callee branch and SILENTLY RETURNED 0. Workaround was an explicit `let g: Fn(..) = h.f`. FIXED 2026-06-21 (7010bc86) with the architecturally-general mechanism (typechecker → lowering side-table → codegen), recovering the signature from the typechecker rather than the RHS shape: (1) typechecker type_to_type_expr (src/typechecker/patterns.rs) now maps Type::Function / Type::OnceFunction to a TypeKind::FnType (was the Error fallback) so a fn value's signature round-trips to a TypeExpr; (2) the lowering pass (src/lowering.rs) populates a new Program.fn_value_typed_exprs span table — for every Fn(..)/OnceFn(..)-typed expression (borrow-unwrapped), its FnType TypeExpr — a sibling of string_typed_exprs/tensor_typed_exprs; (3) codegen let_binding_fn_value_type (src/codegen/closures.rs) consults fn_value_typed_exprs as a general fallback after the annotation / bare-name / call-return cases, so ANY inferred fn-value binding (field read, index, method call, …) registers closure_fn_types and dispatches indirectly. closure_abi_fn_type now maps a unit return to void for ABI consistency with the env-first trampoline. Tests: tests/codegen.rs fn_value_struct_field_unannotated_extraction / fn_value_vec_element_unannotated_extraction. Full typechecker 1741/0, closures 14/0, interpreter 979/0, codegen 1738/0, memory_sanitizer 347/0 (macOS ASAN), clippy + fmt clean. No new heap/drop logic (fn values are heap-free; the heap-arg-forwarding path was LSan-validated in B-2026-06-21-1/-2), so no dedicated LSan run for this slice. First-class named-fn values are now complete across arg / let / return / struct-field / Vec positions, annotated or inferred, in both karac build and karac run.

Map.new()/SortedMap.new() did not back-propagate K/V from insert/get, so an un-annotated map field/binding failed `karac check` though it ran fine. `Map.new()` mints the receiver as `Map[?K, ?V]` (two fresh typevars), but the insert/get/contains_key/get_or/remove arms of infer_map_method (src/typechecker/stdlib_map.rs) only ran `check_assignable(?K, ConcreteK)` — never unifying the argument type into the slot typevar the way Vec.new()+push does. So `let mut m = Map.new(); m.insert("a", 1); let s = S { m: m }` (S.m: Map[String,i64]) reported a spurious `expected '?T0', found 'String'` at the insert AND a `Map<String,i64>` vs `Map<?T0,?T1>` mismatch at the struct literal, because K/V stayed unsolved and the inferred `Map[?K,?V]` then clashed with the annotated field. Annotating `let mut m: Map[String,i64] = Map.new()` was the only workaround — proving it was pure inference. Surfaced building protobuf `map<K,V>` support (runs correctly; only the user-facing map construction tripped check). FIXED 2026-06-22 (387c9346): a new check_map_slot_arg helper unifies the slot type with the inferred argument type (unify_types) BEFORE resolving the slot and running check_assignable — mirroring the Vec.new()+push element-type pinning. Applied to BOTH infer_map_method and infer_sorted_map_method (identical latent bug); get/insert/remove/get_or also resolve V through the substitutions in their return type so a sibling insert that pinned V surfaces it (e.g. `m.get(k)` returns `Option[i64]`, not `Option[?V]`). Pinning does not erase real checks: once the first insert pins V=i64, a later `insert("b", "oops")` is still a clean `expected 'i64', found 'String'` TypeMismatch. Tests: tests/typechecker.rs test_map_new_insert_infers_field_type / test_map_new_get_pins_key_and_resolves_value / test_map_new_insert_conflicting_value_type_rejected / test_sorted_map_new_insert_infers_field_type; codegen E2E tests/codegen.rs e2e_unannotated_map_new_insert_infers_field_type (full inference→codegen→runtime). Full non-llvm suite green, codegen map subset 99/0, clippy + fmt clean.

fix: be2ef68e
title: An ESCAPING capturing closure silently miscompiles (dangling stack environment) — soundness hole surfaced finishing first-class fn values (B-2026-06-20-1..B-2026-06-21-3). A closure that captures a local and then outlives its defining frame — returned (`fn make(k: i64) -> Fn(i64)->i64 { |x| x + k }`), or stored in a struct field / Vec / global that escapes — reads its captures from freed stack memory after the frame returns. Repro: `fn make(k){ |x| x + k }; let f = make(10); println(f(5))` typechecks with 0 errors and `karac build` prints -1 (garbage) instead of 15; it is a WRONG-OUTPUT miscompile, not a verifier error or a diagnostic. Root cause: compile_closure (src/codegen/closures.rs) builds the env as a stack alloca in the OUTER fn frame (`create_entry_alloca(outer_fn, "__closure_env", ..)`) and the fat pointer's env slot points at it; there is NO heap allocation, NO escape analysis, and NO closure-env drop machinery anywhere today (a non-escaping closure is fine because the frame is still live when it's called, which is why all existing closure tests — same-frame `let f = |x| x+base; f(5)` — pass). Non-capturing escaping closures are safe (null env). The interpreter (`karac run`) is unaffected (tree-walk closures own their captured environment). FIX = the heap-closure-environment epic (tracked in phase-7-codegen.md as a sequenced plan): heap-allocate an escaping closure's env, drop POD then heap (String/Vec) captures at the owning value's scope exit, handle a closure value copied to multiple owners (RC env or strict move + move-out suppression), and add escape analysis so non-escaping closures keep the cheap stack env. Interim-safety option (if a slice can't land): reject a not-yet-supported escaping capturing closure with a clear `not yet supported` diagnostic so no silent miscompile remains. Until fixed, the workaround is to not return / store a capturing closure (pass it down by `Fn(..)` parameter instead, which keeps the defining frame live — already supported). PROGRESS — Slice 0 of the epic landed 2026-06-22 (ab6ff88b): reject_escaping_capturing_closure (a pure-AST pre-check at the top of compile_function) now turns the silent miscompile into an honest `error[E_ESCAPING_CLOSURE_NOT_YET]` for the common TAIL-position escape — a capturing-closure literal, or an identifier bound to one, in the function's tail / return (recursing through block/if/match tails). Sound programs are untouched (non-capturing closures, same-frame use, pass-down-by-Fn-param all still compile — full codegen suite 1743/0). Slice 0 EXTENDED 2026-06-22 (c006ccda): the guard now also covers an explicit mid-body `return <capturing closure>` (collect_outer_return_values walks every `return` not inside a nested closure) and a capturing closure returned inside an aggregate literal (`return H { f: |x| x+k }` / `return (clo, 1)` / `return [clo]`, via aggregate-literal recursion in tail_escapes_capturing_closure). Both walkers are non-exhaustive on purpose — a missed container only UNDER-collects, never falsely rejects (full codegen 1746/0). STAYS OPEN: the feature itself (actually returning a capturing closure) is unimplemented, and ONE narrower silent-miscompile residual remains — a capturing closure stored into a LOCAL struct/Vec that is then returned via an identifier (`let h = H{f:|x|x+k}; return h`), which needs container-escape tracking (the escape-analysis slice). Severity stays high until that residual is guarded or the heap-env feature lands. SLICE 1 WIP on branch clo-rc1 (commit bcf8472c, NOT merged — unsound, do not merge): the RC heap-env CORE is built and proven — a capturing closure that is a function's direct tail gets a reference-counted heap env (emit_rc_alloc {i64 refcount, env}; body GEPs past the refcount), the owning `let f = make()` binding frees it via a new CleanupAction::FreeClosureEnv (RC-dec, free-at-0, null-guarded), driven by compute_fns_returning_heap_env + current_fn_heap_closure_spans; the demonstrated repro `let f = make(21); println(f(21))` compiles and prints 42 (test heap_env_returned_capturing_closure_runs). BLOCKER (remaining ~80%): the comprehensive misuse guard — a heap-env binding that escapes again (`let f = make(); return f` UAF, copy `let g = f`, store, pass-as-arg) and an UNBOUND `make()` (leak) are NOT yet rejected, so the branch is unsound. A sound guard needs an EXHAUSTIVE 'f only ever a call callee' walker (refs_in_expr is unusable — lossy `_ => {}`, 33/~40 ExprKinds, a missed kind = a missed escape = UAF); cleaner end-state is inc-on-copy RC (fold in the shared-ownership slice) so nothing needs rejecting. Then ASAN + LSan gate. SLICE 0 RESIDUAL CLOSED 2026-06-22 (3829b1de): the STAYS-OPEN residual above — a capturing closure stored into a LOCAL aggregate then returned via an identifier (`let h = H{f:|x|x+k}; h`, and the identifier chain `let g=|x|x+k; let h=H{f:g}; h`) — is now GUARDED; both built+ran printing garbage (0 / -1) before and now emit error[E_ESCAPING_CLOSURE_NOT_YET]. reject_escaping_capturing_closure's capturing_vars builder now runs in SOURCE ORDER and reuses tail_escapes_capturing_closure as the `does this RHS produce a capturing closure` predicate (direct closure / aggregate literal / identifier chain), mirroring the ownership pass's collect_closure_let_bindings shapes (closure_escape.rs) — that pass fires only on REF captures (a dangling borrow), so the OWN-capture escape it soundly admits but codegen's stack env cannot yet support is exactly what this guard catches; tail_escapes_capturing_closure also gained the prefix Vec/Map/Repeat-literal + struct ..spread arms for parity with the ownership walker. One-sided as before (codegen 1750/0, par_codegen 123/0, memory_sanitizer 347 passed +1 ign /0). Tests: tests/codegen.rs escaping_capturing_closure_local_struct_then_return_is_rejected, escaping_capturing_closure_local_identifier_chain_is_rejected, non_capturing_closure_local_struct_then_return_still_ok. STILL SILENT (now the only known escaping-closure residual; deferred to the escape-analysis slice — the same field-access class the ownership pass also defers in collect_escape_target): a returned field projection `return h.f` still builds+runs with garbage (-1); guarding it soundly needs struct-shape/projection info to avoid over-rejecting the sound `return h.non_closure_field`. fix field stays empty — the feature is still unimplemented and that residual remains; severity stays high. The element slot holds an inline closure fat ptr — exactly the shape the Vec's DYNAMIC element drop loop (__karac_vec_elem_closure_env_drop) frees at scope exit, and that loop is REFCOUNT-AWARE (dec + free at zero), so a shared env co-owned by v[i] and a binding source is freed once. CODEGEN (new try_compile_heap_env_vec_elem_reassign, called from the Assign Index-target arm ahead of the generic compile_index_store) follows the RC setter rule (retain new -> store -> release old): compute the element ptr, save its CURRENT fat, inc the new env on a binding copy (a fresh `make(j)` carries its +1), store, then RC-drop the saved old env via the shared emit_heap_closure_env_dec/_inc helpers. So v[i]'s old env is freed once at the reassignment, the new env once by the drop loop at scope exit, and on a copy the source `g` stays a live co-owner. Position-agnostic (top-level, branch, loop), works over a DYNAMIC index, sibling element untouched. GUARD: is_heap_env_reassign now also sanctions an Index target whose root is a heap-env Vec[Fn] owner (heap_env_vec_owners), alongside the bare-binding and struct-field targets, in both Assign arms. Verified: move-to-fresh / copy+reuse / multi-element / loop / dynamic-index runs -> 25/206/73/35/300; converted the Vec-element rejection test to passing; 3 ASAN tests (copy, move-to-fresh, 50-iteration dynamic-index loop) macOS ASAN + Linux LSan clean. A/B across default auto-par, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, and the interpreter oracle. codegen 1903/0, par_codegen 123/0, memory_sanitizer 403/0. ===== EPIC CLOSED (status -> fixed). Every heap-env closure place is now supported: RETURN (bare tail / top-level return, branch-leaf), STORE (struct field / tuple / array / Vec element), COPY/MOVE (struct/tuple/array owner COPY, Vec owner MOVE, binding copy), ESCAPE (aggregate / container move-out + caller adopt), by-value ARG-PASS BORROW (binding + struct/tuple/array/Vec owner to a borrows-only callee), and REASSIGNMENT (binding g=f/g=make, struct field r.f=.., Vec element v[i]=..). The original soundness hole — an escaping capturing closure reading a freed stack env — is fully resolved: escaping closures get an RC heap env box, every owner/use site is RC-accounted (inc on copy, dec/free at scope exit, move-out neutralize + caller adopt on escape, drop-old on reassign), and the misuse guard over-rejects (never miscompiles) any not-yet-modeled shape. =====

`--bindings component` (the wasm_wasi default) emitted NON-reproducible component bytes — three builds of identical source produced three DIFFERENT SHA256 at the SAME byte length; `--bindings none` (core module) was always byte-identical. NOT HashMap/iteration-order (the initial hypothesis): a `cmp -l` of two captured cores showed exactly 2 differing bytes, both inside the `name` custom section — `...\x04name\x00! karac_9013_filter_core.core.wasm` vs `...9066...`; `wasm-tools component new` is itself deterministic on fixed input, and the embedded-WIT text is already deterministic (collect_host_fns/collect_wasm_exports iterate `program.items` in source order). Root cause: the embedded-component build links the C-ABI core module to a process-unique SCRATCH file named `karac_<pid>_<stem>.core.wasm` (single-file, src/cli.rs) / `karac_proj_<pid>_<pkg>.core.wasm` (project), and wasm-ld bakes that basename verbatim into the module-name subsection of the wasm `name` section; `wasm-tools component embed`/`component new` then carry it into the final component. Two builds = two processes = two pids → the component differed in exactly the pid digits (same length whenever the pids share a digit width, different bytes always). `--bindings none` was immune because it links straight to the stable `<stem>.wasm` output path (no pid). FIXED by linking the core module under a source-DERIVED basename (`<stem>.core.wasm`) inside a process-unique DIRECTORY — new `componentize::link_core_scratch(stem)` reuses `scratch_dir()` (pid+counter) for the enclosing dir, so parallel builds stay collision-free on disk while the embedded module name — and thus the whole component — is byte-identical run to run; both link sites (single-file + project) and their cleanup (remove the scratch dir, not just the file) updated. Side benefit: the shipped artifact no longer leaks an internal temp path into its name section. Regression: tests/cli.rs `wasm_wasi_component_is_byte_reproducible` builds the same source twice in two distinct processes and asserts byte-identical components (an export drives the WIT embed leg too); a manual 3x build now yields a single SHA. Surfaced via the bench/wasm_size size receipt (the Kāra component brotli figure jittered ~0.2% run-to-run).

fix: 4feed3b1
title: Calling a closure stored in a struct field silently returns 0 under `karac build` — `(h.f)(arg)` miscompiles (codegen-only; `karac run` is CORRECT). A closure value (the {fn_ptr, env_ptr} fat pointer) stored in a struct field and invoked through a parenthesized field-access callee — `struct H { f: Fn(i64)->i64 }  let h = H { f: |x| x * 2 };  (h.f)(21)` — typechecks and `karac build` links+runs, but the call evaluates to 0 instead of invoking the closure. Reproduced SAME-FRAME and NON-CAPTURING, so it is independent of the B-2026-06-22-2 escaping-stack-env hole — a distinct closure-call-DISPATCH gap. Confirmed divergence: the same program under `karac run` (tree-walk interpreter) prints the correct 42; only the LLVM backend returns 0. Root-cause hypothesis: compile_closure_call (src/codegen/closures.rs ~L1057) lowers an indirect closure call ONLY when the callee is a NAMED identifier present in closure_fn_types (`match self.closure_fn_types.get(name) { Some(t) => .., None => return Ok(i64 const 0) }`); a FieldAccess callee (and presumably index / tuple-index / call-result place-expressions yielding a closure value) never reaches the fat-pointer extract+indirect-call path, so it falls through to the None const-0 stub. Notably NO existing codegen test RUNS a closure call through a struct field — the only `(x.f)(..)` snippets in tests/codegen.rs are expect_err escape-rejection tests that never execute the program, so the gap was invisible. FIX: generalize closure-call lowering to accept a closure VALUE produced by any expression (field access, index, tuple-index, parenthesized expr, call result) — evaluate it to the {fn_ptr, env_ptr} fat pointer and emit the env-first indirect call — and add E2E tests that actually RUN `(h.f)(arg)` and a Vec[Fn]-index call, asserting parity with `karac run`. Severity high: silent WRONG-OUTPUT, not a diagnostic.

DataFrame.select fresh Vec[String] arg leaked its heap buffer (48 bytes) — `select` is dispatched by try_compile_dataframe_method, which returns early from compile_method_call BEFORE the generic owned-temp argument loop, so a fresh-owned `cols` arg (a Vec[String] literal `df.select(["b", "a"])` — lowered to PrefixCollectionLiteral, which compile_vec_prefix_literal mallocs a real {ptr,len,cap} buffer for — or a fresh call result like other.column_names()) had no consuming binding; select only READS it (names copied in via df_copy_name), so its 48-byte buffer (+ heap element strings) leaked once per call. Pre-existing on main since the phase-11 slice 2c DataFrame codegen (481d6bb6); invisible to local macOS ASAN (no LeakSanitizer), caught only by the Linux LSan gate (asan_dataframe_column_names_select_clean, 48 byte(s) in 1 allocation). FIX: route the arg through the same materialize_owned_temp chokepoint the generic method / free-fn arg loop uses — a FreeVecBuffer (element-type-aware via owned_temp_drops, cap>0-guarded) drains it at scope exit — gated to the fresh forms (expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp || PrefixCollectionLiteral) plus llvm_ty_is_vec_struct, so an identifier/field/index alias (its own binding cleanup) is never double-freed. Mirrors insert's fresh-temp column free. Linux LSan memory_sanitizer 377/0.

fix: a6c92f5b
title: Scalar integer-indexing a BORROWED nested collection inferred Type::Error, so a `let row = m[i]` binding (where `m: ref Vec[Vec[i64]]` / `mut ref Slice[T]`) recorded NO surface/element type and codegen later failed with "no handler for method 'len' on variable 'row'" under `karac build` (`karac run`/interpreter was CORRECT; an explicit `let row: Vec[i64] = m[i]` annotation, and the direct double-index forms `m[i][j]` / the nested-index parallel-assignment swap `m[i][j], m[j][i] = m[j][i], m[i][j]`, all worked — only the let-bound-row form broke). Root cause in infer_expr's ExprKind::Index arm (src/typechecker/exprs.rs): the FINAL scalar-index `match &obj_ty` handled Array / Slice / Vector / Vec but had NO Type::Ref/MutRef arm, so a borrowed container fell to `_ => Type::Error` — even though the RANGE-index path (`m[a..b]`) and the Tensor/Column arms just above already peel Ref/MutRef. The Error type propagated silently (no diagnostic), bind_pattern_types recorded nothing for the binding, and method dispatch fell through in codegen. FIX: add a Type::Ref(inner)|Type::MutRef(inner) arm to the scalar-index match that peels one borrow and extracts the inner Array/Slice/Vector/Vec element (mirroring the range path; the Vector arm also records vector_method_receivers), bringing scalar integer indexing of a borrowed collection in line with the rest. Surfaced by kata #48 Rotate Image's matrix display iterating rows of a `ref`-passed Vec[Vec[i64]] (`let row = m[i]; row.len()`). E2E regression: codegen.rs ref_param_nested_vec_row_binding_dispatches + mut_ref_param_nested_vec_row_binding_dispatches. Suites green: typechecker 1040, interpreter 1824, codegen 1909, ASAN 408; clippy/fmt clean.

Printing a `char` that crosses a CALL-RETURN SSA boundary formatted the i32 scalar as its integer codepoint under `karac build` (LLVM codegen) instead of the UTF-8 glyph — `println(f())` for `fn f() -> char { 'A' }` emitted `65`, not `A`; `karac run` (interpreter) was CORRECT, so a run/build divergence. Also hit `println(f"{f()}")` (f-string interpolation of a call) and `println(b.get())` for a method `fn get(self) -> char` (printed `77`, not `M`). NOT triggered by char literals, char-typed identifiers, Vec[char] index reads, `String.push(char)`, or a `let c = pick(); println(c)` binding (the untyped-let type-expr recovery already records `c: char`). Root cause: codegen's print / f-string char arm gates on `expr_is_char` (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs), which had arms for CharLit / Identifier (via var_type_names) / Index (element TypeExpr) / a `.clone()`-only MethodCall / FieldAccess, but NO free-function `Call` arm and no general `MethodCall` arm — so a call result fell through to `_ => false` and the value (char lowers to i32) hit the generic `%lld` integer path. The sibling `expr_is_unsigned_int` already carried exactly these two arms (added 2026-06-06 for the `println(u8_fn())` sign-extension bug, 200 printed as -56). FIX: add to `expr_is_char` a free-fn `Call` arm keyed on `fn_return_type_names[name] == "char"` and generalize the `MethodCall` arm to resolve the receiver's type name and look up the impl method's declared return type under the synth `Type.method` key (keeping the `.clone()` receiver-recursion special case) — a mirror of the unsigned-int arms; this restores the source `char` type across the call-return boundary for both the direct-print and f-string paths. E2E regression: codegen.rs test_e2e_println_char_call_return (direct free-fn return, f-string call interpolation, method return, multibyte 3-byte UTF-8 return, plus the already-working let-bound form as a non-regression guard), asserting glyph parity with `karac run`. Read-only predicate change — no drop/ownership/alloc path touched, so no LSan exposure. Suites green: full codegen E2E 1916, codegen `char` filter 28 incl. the new E2E; clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm and cargo fmt --all --check clean.

fix: f82feef2
title: `s[i]` (scalar integer index) on a `String` inferred Type::Error SILENTLY in infer_expr's ExprKind::Index final `match &obj_ty` (the `_ => Type::Error` arm had no Type::Str case and recorded NO diagnostic), so the program typechecked, reached the tree-walk interpreter, and hit `unreachable!` on the (Value::String, Value::Int) operand pair (src/interpreter/eval_expr.rs:605) — an internal-error PANIC instead of the newcomer-friendly compile error the spec mandates (design.md § Character type: UTF-8 is variable-width, so `[]` would hide an O(n) scan). Minimal repro `fn main() { let s = "hello"; println(s[0]); }` panicked under `karac run`. ROOT CAUSE: the scalar-index match handled Array/Slice/Vector/Vec (+ a Ref/MutRef peel arm from B-2026-06-29-2) but never String, and String isn't a sequence element type, so it fell to the silent `_ => Type::Error`. FIX: detect `Type::Str` (peeling ref/mut-ref) in the Index arm AFTER the range-index path — so `s[a..b]` String slicing (→ fresh String) is untouched — emit the spec diagnostic ('String does not support indexing with []' + O(n) rationale + `s.char_at(i)` / `s.bytes()[i]` help) and return Type::Error. New `TypeErrorKind::StringNotIndexable` (E0268) is marked is_run_fatal() so `karac run`'s lenient script path ABORTS with error[typecheck] (exit 1) rather than downgrading to warning[typecheck] and tripping the same interpreter `unreachable!` — mirrors the invalid-cast run-fatal family (B-2026-06-13-15); `karac check`/`build` already rejected via the has_type_errors gate. The two alternatives the diagnostic points at keep working (separate paths): `s.char_at(i)` (method call → Option[char]) and `s.bytes()[i]` (Slice[u8] index). Regression: tests/typechecker.rs::{test_string_scalar_index_rejected_with_newcomer_diagnostic asserting the full diagnostic body, test_string_char_at_and_bytes_index_still_work}; codegen string suite (16 incl. bytes-index / char_at / slice) green under --features llvm.

fix: a0f77cbb
title: Reassigning a non-`mut` field of a `shared`/`par struct` was unchecked at compile time — `karac build` silently accepted the write (exit 0) while `karac run`'s interpreter caught it only as a runtime error (`write_shared_struct_field` defense-in-depth guard). Root cause: the typechecker had no shared-field write-permission rule and `StructInfo` dropped per-field `is_mut`. FIXED (a0f77cbb): new `SharedFieldNotMut` typecheck kind (run-fatal, E0269) rejects the write on run/check/build, mirroring the interpreter's rule (assignable iff `f.is_mut` OR the field is an interior-mutable `Atomic[T]`/`Mutex[T]`); carried via a new `StructInfo.mut_fields` set, gated on the immediate assignment LHS through the already-captured `is_lhs` in `infer_field_access`. Surfaced verifying book examples. Tests: tests/typechecker.rs shared_struct_non_mut_field_reassign_rejected / _mut_field_reassign_accepted / _atomic_field_reassign_accepted / par_struct_non_mut_field_reassign_rejected / plain_struct_field_reassign_not_gated / shared_field_not_mut_is_run_fatal.

fix: a0f77cbb
title: Iterating a shared-borrowed `Vec` of a Copy scalar bound the element `ref i64`, not auto-deref'd in arithmetic — `for x in row` over a `ref Vec[i64]` (the inner loop of a `ref Vec[Vec[i64]]`): `karac run` emitted `warning: expected 'i64', found 'ref i64'` and computed the right answer, while `karac build` HARD-errored `error[typecheck]: expected 'i64', found 'ref i64'` on `total + x` (build stricter than run). Root cause: `element_type_of` re-wrapped a borrowed collection's element in the same borrow form, so a nested `ref Vec[Vec[i64]]` yielded `ref i64` at the innermost element (unlike `Slice[i64]`, which yields `i64`). FIXED (a0f77cbb): the shared-`Type::Ref` arm now binds a Copy-scalar element BY VALUE (`i64` — copying a scalar out of a shared borrow is not a move), matching `Slice[i64]` and the `Str`->`char` peel; the `mut ref` arm is untouched so in-place element mutation keeps `mut ref T`, and non-scalar elements (`ref Vec`, `ref String`) stay borrowed to preserve the move-out-of-borrow rejection. Surfaced verifying book examples. Tests: tests/typechecker.rs for_loop_borrowed_nested_vec_scalar_element_usable_in_arithmetic / _triple_nested / _vec_of_string_element_stays_borrowed; tests/codegen.rs + tests/interpreter.rs for_loop_borrowed_nested_vec_scalar_autoderefs (run/build agreement -> 10).

Atomic[T] op arity diverged between `karac run` and `karac build`: the implicit-ordering form (`c.count.fetch_add(1)` / `c.count.load()`) ran fine under the interpreter (which ignores the absent MemoryOrdering) but failed `karac build` with 'codegen: Atomic.fetch_add takes (value, MemoryOrdering), got 1 args'. The spec defines NO implicit-ordering form — every atomic op is declared with an explicit ordering (deferred.md § Atomic Operations: load(ord), store(val,ord), fetch_*/swap(val,ord), compare_exchange(old,new,succ,fail)) — so the fix requires the ordering on BOTH surfaces (option b, explicit-over-magic). Shipped example examples/mend/examples/concurrent_emails/solution.kara used the 1-arg form, so it ran but did not build. ROOT CAUSE: typechecker infer_method_call special-cased only compare_exchange; load/store/fetch_*/swap fell through to the silent Type::Error arm with NO arity check, so the implicit form passed typecheck; codegen's compile_atomic_method DID require the ordering, hence the split. FIX: (1) new run-fatal TypeErrorKind::AtomicMissingOrdering (E0270) + a typechecker arm that requires the ordering on load (1 arg) / store+RMW (2 args) for Atomic receivers and models the real return type (T for load/RMW, Unit for store) instead of Type::Error; run-fatal so `karac run`'s lenient script path aborts rather than downgrade-and-run, matching build. (2) interpreter backstop in method_call_optres.rs (load/store/fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange) — REQUIRED because a field access through a `ref`/`mut ref` struct param types as Type::Error (fields.rs), so `c.count.fetch_add(1)` on a `ref Counter` slips past typecheck; the guard makes `karac run` reject it too, matching codegen. (3) solution.kara + its canned_responses.json / notes.md / .cast demo mirrors moved to the explicit MemoryOrdering.Relaxed form. Regression: typechecker.rs test_atomic_op_missing_ordering_rejected (asserts kind + run-fatal) / test_atomic_op_with_explicit_ordering_typechecks; interpreter.rs test_atomic_fetch_add_load_explicit_agrees_with_codegen (prints 3) / test_atomic_implicit_ordering_rejected_by_interpreter; par_codegen.rs test_e2e_atomic_fetch_add_load_explicit (prints 3, interpreter parity) / test_atomic_implicit_ordering_rejected_by_codegen. examples/ all build under karac build. Sibling of the same-day B-2026-06-30-3/-4 run/build unifications.

Iterating a `mut ref Vec` of a Copy scalar bound the element `mut ref i64`, not auto-deref'd in arithmetic — the mutable-borrow sibling of B-2026-06-30-4. `for x in xs { x = x * 2; }` over a `mut ref Vec[i64]`: `karac check`/`build` HARD-errored `error[typecheck]: arithmetic operator requires numeric type, found 'mut ref i64'` while `karac run` warned-and-proceeded (and the `x = x * 2` write silently no-op'd) — a run/build divergence. Root cause: `element_type_of`'s `Type::MutRef` arm bound the bare-`for` loop variable as `mut ref i64`, which arithmetic does not auto-deref. But design.md § Iteration (line 2739) makes bare `for x in c` desugar to `c.iter()` — it borrows and yields `ref T` REGARDLESS of the collection's own borrow form (line 2758 reaffirms); mutable iteration is the explicit `.iter_mut()` path, not bare `for`. So the `MutRef` arm was mistyping a read-only shared element as `mut ref`. FIXED (cc002702): mirror the B-2026-06-30-4 shared-`Type::Ref` arm — a Copy scalar element binds BY VALUE (`i64`), aggregates (`mut ref Vec`, `mut ref String`, structs) keep the borrow form so the move-out-of-borrow rejection is preserved. This unifies check/run/build (loop var is `i64`, arithmetic works) and keeps the type HONEST: the element is read-only, so `x = x * 2` is a plain local reassignment that does NOT reach the Vec (bare `for` never mutates — use `xs[i] = ...` over `0..xs.len()`, or the future `.iter_mut()`), consistent across all surfaces. NOT a rejection: `x = x * 2; total = total + x` (reassign-and-use of the by-value loop local) is a legitimate working pattern computing 14; a hard error on loop-var assignment would wrongly reject it. (Renumbered from -5, concurrently claimed on main by the unrelated Atomic-ordering divergence 12c2346f.) Tests: tests/typechecker.rs (mut-ref scalar arithmetic, reassign-and-use, triple-nested, aggregate `mut ref Vec[String]` stays borrowed); tests/interpreter.rs + tests/codegen.rs (run/build agreement — repro prints 3/4 consistently, reassign-and-use computes 14 on both surfaces). fmt + clippy --all-targets clean (native + llvm); codegen E2E + memory_sanitizer green.

A for-loop over a struct FIELD's Vec accessed through `self` inside an impl method (`for s in self.items.iter()`) silently iterated ZERO times under `karac build` while the interpreter (`karac run`) iterated correctly — a SILENT miscompile (wrong output, no error). `self.items.len()` returned the correct count (field Vec intact); only the for-loop over the field was broken. ROOT CAUSE: `try_compile_for_field_iter` (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs) hand-rolled its own receiver-pointer/field-GEP resolution that (1) matched only `Identifier`/`Index`, never `self` (which parses as `ExprKind::SelfValue`), so the self-field iterable fell through to the for-dispatcher's silent `_ =>` skip; (2) even when matched used `slot.ptr` directly — one indirection short for a `ref self` receiver (the alloca holds a pointer-TO-struct); (3) for shared structs single-loaded `slot.ptr` (short for a `ref self` handle) and hardcoded the header-shifted GEP layout (wrong for Phase-D headerless shared structs). FIX (948a758b): delegate to the canonical `lower_field_access_ptr` (the same field-place resolver the method-call field-receiver path uses), which handles owned vs `ref` bindings vs shared handles and the Phase-D layout uniformly, so the for-loop and method paths can no longer drift; `self` is normalised to a synthetic `Identifier("self")` in the for-loop CALLER (mirrors `compile_method_call`'s `self.field.method()` normalisation), NOT by teaching the resolver about `SelfValue` — the resolver deliberately leaves a bare `SelfValue` at `Ok(None)` to preserve the atomic-on-self method path (`self.count.fetch_add(..)`), and a for-loop source is unambiguously a collection field (atomics are never iterable). Both `.iter()` and bare `for s in self.items` forms route through the same helper, so both are fixed together, on plain and shared structs. Verified byte-identical `karac run` vs `karac build` (default auto-par + AUTO_PAR=0): plain 201, shared 119; atomic-on-self unchanged (3); Linux LSan clean. Discovered while implementing owned-temp slice 3j; independent pre-existing method-body-lowering bug. Tests: tests/codegen.rs test_e2e_for_self_field_vec_iter_in_impl_method / _shared_struct / test_ir_for_self_field_vec_iter_emits_loop_body; tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_for_self_field_vec_iter_no_double_free / asan_for_shared_self_field_vec_iter_no_double_free. OUT OF SCOPE (separate pre-existing HARD-error gaps, not silent): owned-`self` method dispatch on a variable receiver, and `self.items[i].method()` indexed-receiver method dispatch.

`TaskGroup.new()` / `tg.spawn(closure)` / `handle.join()` / `tg.cancel()` and the free `spawn(closure)` compiled and ran under `karac build` (codegen lowers them to `karac_runtime_taskgroup_*` / real work-pool tasks) but had NO tree-walk-interpreter evaluation rule, so `karac run` DIVERGED: `TaskGroup.new` hit the generic "accepted by the typechecker but not wired in the tree-walk interpreter — please report this" internal error, and free `spawn(closure)` panicked as "variable 'spawn' not found" (unresolved identifier reaching the eval_expr Identifier arm). A run/build divergence of the same class as the Atomic-ordering split B-2026-06-30-5 (12c2346f). ROOT CAUSE: the interpreter's builtin dispatch had arms for `Atomic.new` / `Mutex.new` / `collect_all` / `par {}` but none for the structured-concurrency surface declared in runtime/stdlib/task_group.kara. FIX (b11459e1): give the interpreter real evaluation rules, following the established convention that concurrency primitives run sequentially/eagerly in the tree-walk host (collect_all / collect_all_vec; real OS threads via thread::scope are reserved for lexically-scoped `par {}`). Two Value variants — `TaskGroup` (stateless marker — the group carries no live task state because children run eagerly) and `TaskHandle(Box<Value>)` (carries the child's already-computed result), each with Display + variant_name arms; a `TaskGroup.new` associated-call arm (sibling of `Atomic.new`) returns the marker; a `spawn` builtin-identifier arm + shared `eval_spawn_closure` run the closure eagerly at the spawn site and box the result into a `TaskHandle` (a panicking child dominates via pending_cf — fail-fast parity with par {} / collect_all); receiver-typed method dispatch routes `TaskGroup.spawn` (run child, return handle), `TaskGroup.cancel` (no-op — children already ran), and `TaskHandle.join` (deliver the boxed result), gated on the concrete receiver value so they never shadow `Command.spawn` / `String.join`. The join-at-spawn model is observably identical to the parallel codegen for the order-independent fan-out/join shape the `ScopeLocal` rules permit (a handle cannot escape its spawning scope, so cross-task communication is confined to shared Atomic/Mutex cells whose interpreter models are already thread-safe); it deliberately does NOT model programs that observe shared mutable state BETWEEN spawn and the group's drop barrier (those read a racy, unsynchronized value under codegen too). Verified byte-identical `karac run` == `karac build`: 60 for the explicit-join fan-out (worker(10)+worker(20)) and 42 for free spawn/join. Tests: tests/interpreter.rs test_taskgroup_spawn_join_agrees_with_codegen / test_free_spawn_join_agrees_with_codegen + codegen E2E twins tests/par_codegen.rs test_e2e_taskgroup_spawn_join / test_e2e_free_spawn_join (all assert the same output). OUT OF SCOPE: genuinely-parallel deferred execution in the interpreter — the tree-walk host holds program/typecheck_result as borrows that cannot cross into a 'static thread::spawn, so `par {}` gets real threads only via its lexical thread::scope.

Arithmetic on a `mut ref`/`ref` numeric SCALAR did not auto-deref, so `x = x + 1i64` where `x: mut ref i64` diverged: `karac check`/`build` HARD-errored `error[typecheck]: arithmetic operator requires numeric type, found 'mut ref i64'` while `karac run` warned-and-applied (the interpreter mutates through the borrow, printing 11) — a check/build ↔ run divergence. The scalar-parameter sibling of B-2026-06-30-6 (which fixed `mut ref Vec` ELEMENT typing under iteration; this fixes a `mut ref` scalar used DIRECTLY in `a = a + b`). NOTE `x += 1i64` already typechecked — `StmtKind::CompoundAssign` is checked as `infer_expr(target); infer_expr(value)` and never builds the `x + 1` binary, so only the explicit `x = x + 1` (desugared Assign with a Binary RHS) hit the arithmetic arm. ROOT CAUSE: the `BinOp::Add|Sub|Mul|Div|Mod` arm of `infer_binary` (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs) tests `is_numeric(&left_ty)`, which is false for `Type::MutRef(i64)` / `Type::Ref(i64)`; it never read through the borrow, though design.md § "Compound assignment on `mut ref` lvalues" (:5306) mandates read-through (`a = a + b` on a `mut ref T` lvalue desugars to `*a = *a + b`, so the RHS reads `*a`), and comparison ops already strip borrows via `strip_refs_for_compare`. FIX (6f00795b): add `deref_numeric_scalar` — peel a single `ref`/`mut ref` off a NUMERIC-scalar operand — and apply it to both operands in the arithmetic arm BEFORE Q4 literal promotion, so an unsuffixed literal (`x + 1`) still promotes to the pointee type and records its span (a borrow left un-stripped makes `is_numeric` false, skipping promotion and risking a codegen literal-width mismatch). The result type is the bare scalar `T`. Gated on a numeric pointee, so a non-numeric borrow (`mut ref bool`) still reaches the "requires numeric type" diagnostic (reporting the original type). Exposed a co-fixed pre-existing codegen silent miscompile, B-2026-06-30-10. (IDs -9/-10: originally minted -7/-8, which collided with the self-field-for-iter and TaskGroup/spawn fixes that landed concurrently on main.) Tests: tests/typechecker.rs (implicit assign, unsuffixed-literal promotion, `ref` read-through, float, non-numeric-still-errors); tests/interpreter.rs + tests/codegen.rs (run/build agreement, all print 11). fmt + clippy --all-targets clean (native + llvm); typechecker, interpreter, codegen, memory_sanitizer green.

Mutating a `mut ref` numeric-SCALAR parameter via an identifier target (`x = x + 1` / `x += 1`) did NOT propagate to the caller in built binaries — a SILENT miscompile: `karac build` printed the un-mutated value (10) while `karac run` / the interpreter printed 11. Independent of and PRE-EXISTING relative to B-2026-06-30-9: `x += 1i64` already typechecked, so any program mutating a `mut ref` scalar param via `+=`/`=` silently no-op'd on the caller in shipped binaries; the explicit `x = x + 1` form was merely masked by -9's typecheck rejection until it was fixed, which surfaced this. ROOT CAUSE: a `mut ref T` scalar param is POINTER-represented — `inner_type_of_ref` registers it in `ref_params` and its entry alloca holds the borrow POINTER (load_variable derefs on read; get_data_ptr loads the pointer). But the identifier-target store in both `StmtKind::Assign` (the generic `build_store(slot.ptr, val)` fallthrough) and `StmtKind::CompoundAssign` (src/codegen/stmts.rs) wrote into `slot.ptr` — the alloca holding the POINTER — clobbering the borrow pointer with the integer value instead of writing THROUGH it, so the caller's storage was never updated. FIX (6f00795b): in both arms, when the identifier is a numeric-scalar `ref_param`, store the width-coerced value THROUGH `get_data_ptr(name)` (which loads the borrow pointer) and return early. Scalar-only (int/float pointee): Vec/String/struct `mut ref` mutate via methods / field stores that already deref through `get_data_ptr`, and routing their whole-value moves here would bypass the heap move-tracking (eager-free / move-suppression) below. Verified byte-identical `karac run` vs `karac build`: implicit-assign 11, compound-assign 11, narrow `mut ref i32` 42, `ref i64` read-through 11. Tests: tests/codegen.rs mut_ref_scalar_param_{implicit_assign,compound_assign,narrow_int_assign}_through_e2e + ref_scalar_param_read_through_arithmetic_e2e; tests/interpreter.rs run/build-parity peers. memory_sanitizer green (scalar stores — no heap alloc/free surface). fmt + clippy --all-targets clean (native + llvm).

fix: 18e1b6ca
title: A user program that redefined ONE always-injected stdlib type (`struct Response`, exported by `runtime/stdlib/http.kara`) lost the WHOLE module: `Server.serve(addr, handler)` / `Server.serve_tls(...)` HARD-errored `no associated function 'serve' on type 'Server'` (TypeErrorKind::NoMethodFound) at typecheck, taking down the entire tests/http_server.rs serve / serve_tls / http2 suite (18 of 25 tests; the 7 serve_static tests survived only because they don't define `struct Response`). `karac build` (and the codegen test harness's `karac::typecheck`) rejected it hard; `karac run` downgraded the same error to a non-fatal `warning[typecheck]` and then failed later at the interpreter, so the two surfaces disagreed. ROOT CAUSE (git-bisected to f6d9873f, the phase-12 #34 stdlib-collision fix): `register_baked_stdlib` (src/typechecker/env_build.rs) implemented the collision-skip at MODULE granularity — when the user program redefined any struct/enum a baked module exports, the ENTIRE module was dropped from env injection. #34's target (the self-host `struct Parser` vs std.cli's `Parser`, so `Parser.new(tokens)` resolves to the user impl) was met, but the hammer was far too wide: redefining a single common type name (`Response`) also dropped its sibling exports (`Server`, `Request`, `HttpError`, `impl Server`, `impl Request`), so `Server.serve` no longer resolved via the `env.impls` associated-fn lookup in expr_ops.rs. FIX: make the collision-skip per-ITEM instead of per-module — drop only the redefined `struct`/`enum` and any impl block whose target type is that name; keep all sibling types, their impls, and free functions always-injected. This still satisfies #34 (the user's `struct Parser` + `impl Parser` become the sole `Parser` surface — std.cli's `struct Parser` AND `impl Parser` are both dropped, so `Parser.new` binds to the user impl, which is exactly why dropping the type WITHOUT its impls was unsafe and the per-item filter drops both) without amputating the rest of the module. A kept sibling impl whose signature names the redefined type now references the USER's type through the shared env — identical to the pre-f6d9873f shadowing behavior, and only sites that actually call such a sibling are affected (those were already the user's to reconcile). NOT one of the two same-day suspects (489825fa codegen / 12c2346f atomic) that predated the report — both are codegen/atomic-only and structurally cannot emit a typecheck NoMethodFound; the bisect over c119c1f6..d280af49 (1074 commits) pinned the real culprit at f6d9873f (2026-06-18). The `compiling_stdlib` gate (a stdlib module self-compiling must not skip itself) is unchanged. Tests: tests/typechecker.rs test_redefining_one_stdlib_type_keeps_sibling_module_items (redefine `Response`, assert `Server.serve` / `serve_tls` resolve and `req.path()` still works); the full tests/http_server.rs suite (25 passed / 0 failed, was 7/18); #34 guard test_e2e_user_struct_shadows_always_injected_stdlib_type still green. fmt + clippy --all --all-targets clean; cargo test + cargo test --features llvm green.

`String.sorted()` — characters sorted ascending into a fresh String, the canonical anagram key — was interpreter-only: `karac build` HARD-errored `codegen failed: Vec/String method 'sorted' is not yet supported in codegen` while `karac run` computed it via `chars().sort_unstable()`, a run/build divergence for a general-purpose String method. Surfaced authoring kata leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams (the sorted-string anagram key `word.sorted()`; the index-map grouping — `Map[String,i64]` key→group-index + `Vec[Vec[String]]` with `groups[i].push(word)` in-place element mutation — and the count-signature sibling key all ALREADY lowered, probed under both surfaces first). FIX (a00a2f58): a `karac_string_sorted(data, len, *mut out_len) -> ptr` runtime helper (runtime/src/clone.rs) mirroring the interpreter char-sort byte-for-byte — sorts by Unicode SCALAR value, not raw byte, so both backends agree on multi-byte input, not just the kata's ASCII. Wired through codegen identically to the sibling `karac_string_{trim,to_lowercase,to_uppercase}` xforms via `build_string_xform_result`; the new method arm is guarded on `string_vars.contains(var_name)` so a String receiver routes to the helper while `Vec[T].sorted()` still falls through to the catch-all UNCHANGED (the same String-vs-Vec disambiguation the `push` arm uses). New runtime symbol → rebuilt lean+full native archives (runtime-archive-rebuild-dance) + reinstalled to ~/.local. Tests: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_string_sorted_codegen (literal + identifier receiver, non-mutating receiver, empty string, anagram equality); tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_string_sorted_no_leak_no_double_free (fresh buffer freed exactly once, 36-byte payload ×1000). fmt + clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean; string/sort codegen (230) + interpreter sorted (31) suites green; Vec.sorted() unchanged. Both kata solvers (sorted-key ★ + count-signature) A/B-identical to the Python oracle across karac run, karac build (default auto-par), and KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0.

fix: 1cf09cb6
title: `String.cmp(other) -> Ordering` — the method form of the `<`/`>` operators — was rejected at typecheck (`error[typecheck]: no method 'cmp' on type 'String'`) under `karac check`/`build`, while `karac run` merely emitted the same as a `warning[typecheck]` and then executed it — a run/check divergence. `impl Ord for String` (cmp/lt/le/gt/ge) + `impl Eq for String` ARE registered in env_build.rs (String is in `eq_ord_targets`), but String's method dispatch (`infer_str_method`, reached because `obj_ty == Type::Str` routes there unconditionally) is a CLOSED hardcoded list whose unknown-method arm calls `require_known_method` — which hard-errors without ever consulting the registered trait impl. So `s.cmp(t)` was unreachable via method syntax even though the operators and the `Vec[String].sort`/`binary_search` byte-order (karac_string_cmp) already existed. Integer/char `.cmp` resolve fine (they fall through to the impl-table lookup, not a closed dispatcher). FIX (1cf09cb6): (a) typecheck — added a `cmp` arm to `infer_str_method` returning `Ordering` and validating exactly one String-like arg; (b) codegen — added a String branch to the `.cmp` lowering in method_call.rs (extract each operand's {ptr,len}, call the existing karac_string_cmp which returns -1/0/+1, map to the Ordering tag via `tag = cmp + 1` since Less=0/Equal=1/Greater=2), guarded on `inferred_receiver_type(object) == Some("String")` so a user struct's derived-Ord `.cmp` still falls through unchanged; (c) NO new runtime symbol (karac_string_cmp pre-existed). The interpreter already computed String.cmp via `value_compare` — but see B-2026-06-30-14, which fixing this exposed. Tests: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_string_cmp_codegen; tests/interpreter.rs::test_match_bare_ordering_variant_from_cmp. Surfaced authoring kata leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams (probing `sort_by(|a,b| a.cmp(b))` comparators).

fix: 1cf09cb6
title: SILENT interpreter miscompile: `match x.cmp(y) { Less => .., Equal => .., Greater => .. }` with BARE (unqualified) Ordering variant patterns ALWAYS took the first arm — `karac run` returned Less for EVERY comparison (both int AND String `.cmp`) while `karac build` (codegen) was correct. A run/build divergence that silently produced wrong results, pre-existing on main and independent of B-2026-06-30-13 (int cmp was already typecheck-valid); fixing -13 (String.cmp method) merely exposed it for String too. ROOT CAUSE: the interpreter's pattern matcher (pattern_match.rs `PatternKind::Binding`) classifies a bare PascalCase identifier as a unit-variant pattern only when `self.env.get(name)` returns a unit `EnumVariant` value — the mechanism user-enum unit variants rely on — otherwise it is a catch-all binding that matches anything. `register_items` (interpreter.rs) registered the built-in `Ordering` (and `MemoryOrdering`) variants under their QUALIFIED names only (`"Ordering.Less"`), so `env.get("Less")` was None and bare `Less` fell through to the always-true binding, making the first arm win. The qualified `Ordering.Less` pattern and `sort_by(|a,b| a.cmp(b))` (which reads the Ordering value directly, no match) both worked, which is why the bug hid. FIX (1cf09cb6): bind BOTH the qualified and the bare names for Ordering + MemoryOrdering, mirroring user-enum registration (PascalCase, so no collision with snake_case value bindings per Kāra's case-class invariant). Tests: tests/interpreter.rs::test_match_bare_ordering_variant_from_cmp (int + String, correct arms). Interpreter (1055) + user-enum bare matching unaffected. Surfaced authoring kata leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams while adding String.cmp.

`Vec.sort()` on a non-integer / non-String element type (e.g. `Vec[Vec[String]]`) runs under `karac run` (the interpreter's `value_compare` handles nested Vecs lexicographically) but errors under `karac build`: `codegen failed: Vec.sort() in codegen supports integer and String element types; use sort_by(|a, b| a.cmp(b)) for other element types` (src/codegen/vec_method.rs sort arm). A run/build divergence (honest error, not silent). The suggested workaround itself is incomplete for nested Vecs: after B-2026-06-30-13 `String.cmp` works, but there is no `Vec[T].cmp` method, so `outer.sort_by(|a,b| a.cmp(b))` on `Vec[Vec[String]]` does not typecheck either. FIX DIRECTION: emit a comparator thunk for the general element type in the `sort`/`sort_by` codegen path — recursively compare nested Vec/other Ord element types the way the interpreter's `value_compare` does (lexicographic for Vec, karac_string_cmp for String leaves). Surfaced authoring kata leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams (canonicalising the output by sorting the groups; the kata itself does NOT need it — it uses an index-map first-appearance order — so this is tracked, not blocking). NOT fixed inline: heavier codegen slice than the String.sorted/String.cmp gaps the kata drove. FIXED 463fa826 along the sketched direction: recursive `i64 karac_cmp_<T>(ptr,ptr)` comparator family (scalars by declared signedness, floats partial-order NaN=Equal, String via karac_string_cmp, Vec/VecDeque lexicographic-then-length, tuples per-field) wrapped into the karac_vec_sort_by thunk ABI; unordered elements (user structs) keep a loud sort_by-directing error. TWO STALE PREMISES corrected while fixing: (1) the interpreter did NOT handle nested Vecs — value_compare had no Value::Array arm, so nested sorts were a silent NO-OP (Equal fallback + stable sort = insertion order preserved); Array + Slice lexicographic arms added. (2) Floats were also unsupported in codegen sort (now covered by the family).

Tensor element-wise negation `-t` lowered to `0.0 - x` (fsub with a zero LHS) instead of a true IEEE `fneg`, so a `0.0` element negated to `+0.0` under `karac build` while `karac run` (interpreter `eval_unary` computes `-f`) yields `-0.0` — printed as `0` vs `-0`, a silent run-vs-build divergence at exactly the signed-zero edge (all non-zero elements agree; NumPy also fnegs: `-np.array([0.0])` is `[-0.]`). Int tensor neg was unaffected (`0 - x` via compile_binop_typed IS the correct checked form there). Found probing the S3 element-wise-map unification (docs/spikes/reduce-elementwise-trait-unification.md): the shared emitter made the two surfaces' neg postures directly comparable. FIX: MapKernelOp::Neg in src/codegen/kernel.rs emits build_float_neg for float elements (checked `0 - x` kept for ints); compile_tensor_neg routes through it (Unary+Neg) instead of Binop(Sub)+zero-scalar. Regression: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_tensor_neg_signed_zero (A/B: `-0` on both surfaces).

Column element-wise negation `-c` on an `i64` column lowered to a bare wrapping `ineg` (build_int_neg), so a slot holding `i64::MIN` silently wrapped back to `i64::MIN` under `karac build` while `karac run` traps with `integer overflow` (interpreter `eval_unary` uses `checked_neg`) — a missed-trap miscompile: Kara's checked-arithmetic posture requires the overflow trap, and Tensor's `-t` (0 - x via compile_binop_typed) already trapped, so the two container surfaces disagreed with each other AND with the interpreter. Float column neg (fneg) was already correct. Found probing the S3 element-wise-map unification alongside B-2026-07-01-1. FIX: the shared MapKernelOp::Neg emits checked `0 - x` via compile_binop_typed for int elements (fneg kept for floats); Column `-c` routes through it instead of NegNative. Regression: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_column_neg_i64_min_traps. Narrow-int columns (i32 etc.) now trap at their own width on neg, which still diverges from the interpreter's width-lax i64 evaluation — that pre-existing class is tracked separately as B-2026-07-01-3.

Interpreter narrow-int width laxity for Column/Tensor element-wise ops: the interpreter stores every integer element as Value::Int(i64) and evaluates element-wise arithmetic at i64 width, so a `Column[i32]` op that overflows i32 does NOT trap under `karac run` and produces an out-of-range value — probe: `Column[i32]` holding `2147483647`, `c + 1` prints `2147483648` under `karac run` while `karac build` traps `integer overflow` (codegen computes at the element's LLVM width via compile_binop_typed, which is the correct checked-at-i32 semantics). A run-vs-build divergence class covering ALL narrow-int (i8/i16/i32/u*) element-wise ops and likely element-typed reductions (sum folds at i64 in the interpreter vs elem-width in codegen's emit_reduce_fold) on Column and Tensor. Found probing the S3 element-wise-map unification (docs/spikes/reduce-elementwise-trait-unification.md). FIX DIRECTION: the interpreter needs element-width-aware arithmetic for container elements — either wrap/trap at the declared element width in the shared map_binop_slots/eval_binary path (threading the element TypeExpr through the container ops), or normalize+bounds-check on element store. Related to the receiver-width class in receiver-width-recovery-for-scalar-methods. FIXED 2026-07-02 (1078e747): narrow_oob now peels Column[T]/Tensor[T, S] recorded types down to their element before the width check — a single peel covers all 4 element-wise container paths (map_binop_slots funnels them through eval_binary with the container binop's span). Column[i32] + 1 on INT_MAX traps 'integer overflow' under karac run, matching build; in-range narrow ops (incl. u8) unchanged; reductions were already interp-correct via the S5 checked folds. Probing this fix unearthed the far bigger codegen literal-packing bug B-2026-07-02-6. Regressions: tests/interpreter.rs::test_column_narrow_element_binop_{overflow_traps,in_range_ok}, tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_narrow_column_elemwise_overflow_traps.

fix: c6aa55c6
title: karac test panicked the interpreter ("internal error: entered unreachable code: variable not found; should be caught by resolver", src/interpreter/eval_expr.rs) on any test body calling a name imported from a sibling module — the per-test execution Program was built from ONLY the test module's own items (m.items.clone() in cmd_test), so the imported item resolved and typechecked at the tree level (Resolver/TypeChecker::with_tree) but its body was absent at execution; the JIT path had the same gap (missing symbol at compile). Cross-package dep imports in tests would have hit it identically. Minimal repro: src/util.kara `pub fn triple(...)`, main_test.kara `import util.triple; test { triple(4) }` → panic, exit 101. FIX: cmd_test now executes every test against the karac-run-style merged super-program (build_super_program_for_run — all modules concatenated, imports dropped, gated-stdlib expansions appended), resolved+typechecked once for the whole suite; execution-equivalent to what karac build/run already concatenate, so no new collision constraint. The tree-wide per-module compile pass (imports, visibility, module scoping) still gates first. Regression: tests/cli.rs::test_test_cross_module_import_executes + test_xpkg_test_runner_imports_path_dep_items.

fix: c6aa55c6
title: Test-companion merge tripped E0101 'already defined in this scope' when the _test.kara file re-declared an import its production sibling already has — the natural pattern, since each file states its own imports and a companion imports the same helpers the code under test uses (e.g. both main.kara and main_test.kara `import mathx.double;`). build_program_tree's merge_test_companions arm concatenated both files' Item::Import decls verbatim, so the merged module bound the name twice. FIX (src/module.rs merge arm): exact re-imports — same module path, same source name, same alias — are deduped from the companion's items/imports at merge time; a same-binding import from a DIFFERENT path or source name is kept and still errors as the genuine conflict it is. Regression: tests/cli.rs::test_test_companion_reimport_dedup_keeps_genuine_conflicts (conflict kept) + test_xpkg_test_runner_imports_path_dep_items (dedup exercised — fixture imports the same dep items in both files).

Enum-variant Drop-typed temporary passed directly as a call argument never ran its user drop body — the Call arm of track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg registered only the payload-walking EnumDrop (nothing at all for a heap-free enum), and unit-variant (Path) / struct-variant (StructLiteral) temps weren't matched at all. consume(Sig.A(1)) / consume(Sig.B) / consume(Sig.C{x}) where Sig: Drop leaked the drop side effect once per call; let-bound args were fine (the flagged carry-forward inside fixed B-2026-06-10). Fix mirrors the let-path: key on enum_name_of_expr over the three fresh-temp shapes (Identifier excluded — bindings own their drop) and register the karac_drop_<E> wrapper when drop_method_keys has the enum and it isn't shared; UserDrop + EnumDrop are complementary for enums (the wrapper's struct-synthesis half no-ops on enum names) so the heap-payload walk keeps its own registration. LSan-clean (Linux docker gate, fresh compile, ≥36-byte payload).

fix: dcd819d8
title: Fn-call-RETURNED Drop-typed temporary passed directly as a call argument skips the user drop body for BOTH structs and enums — consume_g(make_guard()) / consume_s(make_sig()) where make_* returns a Drop-implementing value print nothing (probe fnret.kara 2026-07-01, one silent skip per call). track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg keys on constructor SHAPES (struct literal / enum-variant Call-Path-StructLiteral); a plain fn call returning the type matches none of them (enum_name_of_expr's Call arm resolves variant ctors only). Closing it needs fn_return_type_names-driven detection PLUS passthrough-chain analysis (g(make()) where g returns its arg — registering both temps would double-drop; see fresh_arg_bare_shared_heap_type's passthrough guard for the pattern). Distinct from fixed B-2026-07-01-6 (constructor temps). FIXED dcd819d8 exactly along the sketched lines: fn_return_type_names-driven detection (a new fnret arm in track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg registering UserDrop + enum payload walk; interp twin via user_fn_return_type_name in run_fresh_temp_arg_drops) PLUS the passthrough analysis as shared syntactic ast::fn_returns_param (any bare-param return site => skip the caller-side arg-temp registration; a mint(g)->Guard returning a FRESH value keeps both drops). Probing exposed the predicted double-drop ALREADY SHIPPING: let x = pass(Guard{id:7}) fired the user body twice on BOTH surfaces (B-2026-07-01-6's ctor-temp registration + the binding drop) — the guard fixes that too. Discarded statement position (make();) covered on both surfaces as well (try_track_discarded_user_drop_temp / the interp stmt-expr discard hook). 8-probe matrix: 7 shapes output-identical across surfaces, mint count-parity, heap-carrying combined probe identical with zero leaks.

Interpreter never runs user impl Drop for value enums in ANY position — let-bound, inline temp arg, or scope exit (probe enumdrop.kara 2026-07-01: karac run prints zero drops where karac build prints one per value; struct let-bindings DO fire under the interpreter, so this is enum-specific). Additionally the interpreter misses the struct INLINE-TEMP call-arg case (interp twin of fixed-in-codegen B-2026-06-10: consume(Guard{id:7}) silent under run, fires under build). A run-vs-build A/B divergence class for RAII-style code: any kata/program observing enum Drop side effects (or struct temp-arg Drop) behaves differently across surfaces. Fix belongs in the interpreter's drop machinery (struct Drop dispatch exists; enums need the same hook, plus temp-arg ownership at call sites). FIXED d6f2e665: drop_target gained the Value::EnumVariant arm (drop_method_keys keeps builtin enums inert); both move suppressors (tail-expr, let-rebind) accept EnumVariant in tandem; run_fresh_temp_arg_drops in eval_call runs the user body on struct-literal/enum-ctor/unit-variant temp args after the call returns (the interp twin of codegen's B-2026-07-01-6 shapes; Identifier args stay with the caller binding's NLL drop, shared types with rc). 14-probe A/B: drop-COUNT parity everywhere; remaining ORDER differences are the sanctioned NLL-vs-scope-exit timing (interp implements design.md § Drop ordering NLL endpoints, codegen drops at scope exit). Joint both-surface gaps noted, no divergence: Vec[DropEnum] element user-drop bodies, and fn-RETURNED temp args (open B-2026-07-01-7).

SILENT miscompile: Stats.* over an integer slice bit-reinterpreted the i64 buffer as f64 under `karac build` — `Stats.sum(vec![3, 1, 2])` printed denormal garbage (~1.5e-323) while `karac run` printed 6. The permissive numeric coercion admitted Vec[i64] (and every other numeric element) against the baked `Slice[f64]` signatures, the interpreter value-coerced each element, and codegen's try_compile_stats_call read the raw buffer at f64 unconditionally — no error anywhere, just wrong numbers. FIX (S5, the non-f64 element axis of the reduce-kernel spike): (a) typechecker `infer_stats_call` intercept (expr_call.rs) types the whole Stats surface from the argument's element — i64 gets element-typed rules (sum/prod -> i64 CHECKED folds that trap on overflow, min/max -> Option[i64], sort -> Vec[i64], argmin/argmax/argsort exact-i64 compares, float statistics promote to f64), f64 keeps the existing table, and any OTHER numeric element (i32/u8/f32/...) is now a hard typecheck error (width-faithful evaluation on both surfaces is blocked on the interpreter width-laxity class B-2026-07-01-3); (b) the element kind is recorded in a new stats_elem_types side-table (TypeChecker -> lowering -> Program -> codegen, the channel_elem_types plumbing) so codegen reads the buffer at the right element type; (c) interpreter int-mode reads the STATIC element type from expr_types (so an EMPTY Vec[i64] still gets the integer identities sum=0/prod=1, not the float -0.0/1.0) and funnels through the new reduce_i64 in src/reduce_kernel.rs; (d) codegen int paths reuse the shared kernel emitters (emit_reduce_fold int seeds, emit_sum_f64_and_count/emit_variance_from over an i64 access, emit_reduce_minmax/argminmax int predicates, emit_sort_scratch's new SortKey::IntValue/IndexIntoInt exact-integer sorts). Exact above 2^53 on both surfaces (9007199254740993 round-trips). Tests: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_stats_i64_full_surface / _exact_above_2_pow_53_and_empty_identities / _sum_overflow_traps; tests/interpreter.rs::test_stats_i64_* (5); tests/typechecker.rs::test_stats_i64_* + narrow-elem rejection (4); reduce_kernel unit tests (4).

Stats.* arguments MOVE the slice: `let v: Vec[f64] = ...; Stats.sum(v); Stats.mean(v)` is rejected by the ownership checker ('value v moved here, used again here') even though the runtime semantics never consume the argument (the codegen module doc explicitly documents 'the slice is a borrow' and only frees fresh-temp args). Root cause: Kara declares parameter modes on the callee (`ref` = borrow, bare = move; call sites never write `ref`), and runtime/stdlib/stats.kara declares `xs: Slice[f64]` WITHOUT `ref` — so every Stats call consumes its vec under `karac check`/`build`, making two statistics over one dataset impossible without cloning. The whole codegen test suite masks this because the run_program harness never gates on ownership errors (tests/codegen.rs run_program_capturing_inner computes ownershipcheck only to feed codegen's RC-fallback surface — test_e2e_stats_empty_slice passes v FOUR times and stays green while `karac check` rejects the same program). NOT Stats-specific in mechanism (any bare Slice/Vec param moves — that part is the language design), but the stdlib signature contradicts both the documented borrow semantics and obvious usage. FIX DIRECTION: declare the stats.kara params `ref` (audit interpreter/codegen arg handling + the fresh-temp free gate first: a `ref` param changes the ownership pass's view, and materialize_owned_temp on a fresh literal arg must still fire), or give `Slice[T]` params borrow mode by default as the type's design intent; and consider making the codegen harness surface ownership errors so the suite stops masking this class. FIXED 1fd799b7: all 13 stats.kara params declared `ref Slice[f64]`, AND the root enabler — collect_callee_param_modes/collect_method_param_modes walked only the USER program's items, so NO baked-stdlib signature's declared mode ever reached the ownership pass's call-arg classification (the whole baked surface was consume-default); both collectors now walk STDLIB_PROGRAMS first with user entries overriding. Probed: 13-fn reuse over one dataset, borrow-mutate-borrow, fresh temp args (freed via ref-rvalue materialization), i64 elements — check-clean, interp/codegen matched, zero leaks. The harness-masking half (run_program harness never gates on ownership errors, so the codegen suite stayed green on programs karac check rejects) remains a test-infra follow-up — not fixed here.

*const Foo / *mut Foo for an opaque foreign type (unsafe extern "C" { type Foo; }) incorrectly fired E_OPAQUE_TYPE_REQUIRES_INDIRECTION — the canonical C opaque-handle FFI shape (fn use_foo(p: *const Foo)) was rejected outright. The slice-1b indirection walker (lower_type_expr_inner) flipped parent_is_ref=true only through TypeKind::Ref/MutRef; when raw-pointer surface syntax later landed with the strict-provenance slices, TypeKind::Pointer still passed false — exactly the regression the phase-5 line-306 carry-forward predicted (its 'no regression risk today, raw pointers don't parse' note had gone stale; verified-all-surfaces rule caught it). Fix: Pointer arm passes parent_is_ref=true (raw pointers are sized regardless of pointee, like references); diagnostic hint gains the *const/*mut FFI spelling; generic args still reset the flag so *const Vec[Foo] (Foo by-value inside Vec) keeps rejecting. NOTE: commit message says B-2026-07-01-9 — renumbered to -11 post-merge after a parallel-agent id collision (the ledger's -9 is the Stats.* bit-reinterpret bug).

fix: be3ddf6e
title: Map.get payload MOVED OUT of the borrow-bound match arm double-frees against the map's stored value — `let s = match m.get(k) { Some(x) => x, None => f"none" }; println(s)` on a plain Map[i64, String] exits 133 TODAY (probe p9_string_moveout.ka 2026-07-01; interpreter prints fine — value semantics copy). The scrutinee is borrow-classified (scrutinee_is_borrow_call), so `x` correctly registers no cleanup, but the arm-tail move hands the ALIASED bit-copy to the let binding, which tracks it as an owned String — both the binding's FreeVecBuffer and the map's drop_val=1 walk free the same buffer. Same class for struct values with the slice-3r per-value drop armed (`match m.get(k) { Some(h) => h }`). The fix is a deep-clone (or reject) when a borrow-mode pattern binding is moved out of the arm — the map retains ownership, so the escapee needs its own copy; mirrors the 3q loop-element consume-from-copy discipline but at the arm-tail move site. Pre-existing before slice 3r (not introduced by it). FIXED slice 3s (be3ddf6e): deep-clone at the borrow-mode bind when the arm moves the name (exhaustive conservative escape walker; read-only arms stay clone-free), plus if-let/while-let/let-else borrow-call flag parity (read-only if-let over Map.get crashed too) and the missing if-let then-tail move suppression (owned v.pop() tails crashed). Residual alias: destructuring payload patterns (Some((a,b)), Some(H{f})) and VecDeque payloads.

Struct-pattern destructure of Option/Result payloads (`Some(Holder { name, id })`) was wholly UNIMPLEMENTED in codegen while the interpreter handled it — every shape failed ("Undefined variable" for direct uses, "no handler for method" for method calls on a destructured field) across match/if-let/while-let, named bindings, fresh temps (v.pop()), and Map.get scrutinees. pattern_payload_word_count/pattern_payload_llvm_type defaulted a PatternKind::Struct sub-pattern to ONE word, so reconstruct_payload_value bound the raw tag-adjacent word and bind_pattern_values' plain-struct arm's StructValue guard silently no-op'd. Fix (slice 3t, 51d562bb): Struct-pattern arms in the three helpers + the 1-word binding_is_struct gate; then two OWNERSHIP legs the probes surfaced — (a) the named-binding BoxedEnumDrop inner walk double-freed CONSUMED fields against the destructured bindings' own cleanup (LLVM DCE'd the malloc/free pair when the payload was unobserved, so len()-only probes were vacuously green — observe payloads in probes), fixed by per-field cap-zero inside the box (suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure, all four bind sites, unbound fields stay box-owned; and (b) an ESCAPING destructured field over a Map.get borrow scrutinee aliased the bucket (exit 133), fixed by extending the 3s clone fixup to field granularity. Residual alias: tuple-payload destructure field escape over Map.get; deeper nested sub-patterns.

fix: d84e8de4
title: Option/Result STRUCT payloads as container elements leaked in both widths: Vec[Option[Holder]] (payload wider than Option's 3-word inline area → heap-BOXED per element) leaked box + interior per element (LSan-red, 336B/3 iters), and Vec[Result[Holder, i64]] (payload FITS Result's 5-word area → INLINE) leaked the struct's heap fields — the 3p/3q element-drop gates admitted only inline String/Vec {ptr,len,cap} overlay payloads. Inline struct/enum payloads needed only a gate (the emitters' in-place GEP path is layout-correct: all-i64 words overlay the LLVM aggregate); boxed payloads got a width-keyed debox branch (load w0, null-guard, inner drop, free box) in emit_option/result_drop_fn. Same fix inherits to Map values (3r selection) and deeper nesting (te_recursive_drop_fully_supported). Two interactions closed with it: for-loop element bindings over such Vecs marked as borrows (3q machinery), and moved boxed bindings (v.push(o), m.insert(k,o)) disarmed by nulling the box word — variant-agnostic, branch-safe, rides BoxedEnumDrop's null-guard. Sibling fixed in the same slice (leg A): Some((a,b)) => a over m.get(k) crashed exit 133 — the 3s escaping-borrow clone extended to tuple payload destructures and whole-tuple bindings. Residuals: whole-tuple NON-tail consume may leak its clone (crash→leak downgrade); VecDeque payloads still excluded (no clone/drop arms).

Drop-surface tail bundle (slice 3v, four legs, all probe-red): (1) VecDeque never admitted by the recursive drop/clone gates despite sharing Vec's linear {ptr,len,cap} layout — Vec[VecDeque[String]] and Vec[Option[VecDeque[String]]] leaked their strings; routed through the Vec arms at both dispatchers + the element/payload/clone gates. (2) `let s = v.get_unchecked(i)` bound a shallow element alias with an OWNED track — exit-133 double-free at the two scope exits; now deep-clones like `let s = v[i]` (clone_owned_vec_index_element get_unchecked arm). (3) The Tuple-typed BINDING payload reconstruction assumed single-word elements and insertvalue'd a raw i64 into a {ptr,i64,i64} slot — `Some(x)` binding an (String,i64) payload failed module verification from ANY source (Map.get, Vec.pop, plain bindings); rebuilt via #44's word-correct reconstruct_struct_from_words. (4) 3u's whole-tuple escape clone was untracked (non-tail consume leaked it); tracking it surfaced str-spelling sites 4-6 of the 3p trap: type_expr_has_drop_heap classified inferred-spelled tuples as HEAPLESS (every tuple-drop-synthesis consumer silently no-op'd — a wide latent class), emit_tuple_elem_drops' String arm, and its move-suppression dual zero_tuple_elem_cap_at (fixed in tandem; drop/suppress asymmetry is a double-free). Lesson standing: EVERY "String"-keyed TypeExpr gate in codegen must match both spellings; grep for '"Vec" | "VecDeque" | "String"' patterns when touching drop machinery.
