Index reads and for-loops over heap-element vecs (Vec[Vec[String]], Vec[Vec[Vec[i64]]]) under-free — three sort-INDEPENDENT minimal repros (2026-07-02, scratchpad sort/w1,w2,t1c): (a) `let first = v[0]` on Vec[Vec[Vec[i64]]] leaks 16B (the index-read deep-clone's inner level not fully freed — the B-2026-06-19-6 clone + one-level tracking composition); (b) chained read `println(outer[0][0])` on Vec[Vec[String]] leaks 48B (the intermediate `outer[0]` clone's string); (c) `for row in outer { println(row.len()); }` over Vec[Vec[String]] leaks 192B = the ENTIRE content (3 strings + a row buffer) — the for-loop appears to disarm the container binding without the element drops fully covering nested content (contrast: for-over-Vec[Option[String]] is LSan-clean per the 3q suite). All shapes print correct output; macOS leaks-tool detects them (not LSan-only). Probably 2-3 distinct mechanisms sharing the nested-heap-element read path; each needs its own red-confirm + fix. Found while fixing B-2026-06-30-15 (sort itself confirmed leak-free via pop-drain and POD-element probes). FIXED 20258bd4 — and the class was MISATTRIBUTED: every repro was AUTO-PAR-ONLY (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 clean on all; the index reads/for-loops merely changed the statement dependency graph enough to trigger grouping, and statement ORDER toggled the leak). Two real holes in the par-group slot transfer: (1) the auto-par dispatch's parent-side re-track used one-level track_vec_var, dropping the karac_drop_Vec_String-class element drops (all nested content leaked); now mirrors the LET site's rich dispatch (heap-env/tensor/map-elem/agg-elem/one-level). (2) explicit `par { }` Step 6 registered NO Vec-slot cleanup at all (both join slots' full contents leaked per invocation); same dispatch registered. Suites never caught it because loop-based builders serialize — leak tests must include independent-lets auto-par-triggering shapes, and leak probes should compare default-build vs KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 FIRST (instant classification). Diagnosis trail preserved in the auto-par memory note.

fix: fccdd4ab
title: Cross-branch reads inside an explicit `par { }` block (a statement branch reading a sibling branch's let-binding, e.g. `par { let x = build(); let y = build(); println(x.len() + y.len()); }` in statement form) PANIC the interpreter with `internal error: entered unreachable code: variable 'x' not found ... should be caught by resolver` instead of producing a proper resolver/typechecker error. Codegen errors more gracefully ('no handler for method len on variable x') but neither surface gives the user the actual rule (per-statement branches can't read sibling bindings; use the join expression). Needs a resolver-level diagnostic for sibling-binding reads inside par statement branches. FIXED 2026-07-02 (fccdd4ab): the resolver now resolves each top-level statement of an explicit `par { }` block as a concurrent BRANCH in its own child scope (resolve_par_block — the old arm shared Seq's sequential resolve_block, which is why sibling reads sailed through). Reads and assign-targets naming a SIBLING branch's binding get a tailored diagnostic via the new par_sibling_bindings map consulted in error_undefined_name: "cannot read 'x' from a sibling `par` branch: each top-level statement in a `par { }` block is a concurrent branch with its own scope (bound at L:C); combine branch results in the block's tail expression instead". The sibling set merges across nested `par`s (an inner par inside branch 2 still cannot read branch 1's binding). The block's TAIL expression is the join point — every branch's bindings re-define into the block scope before it resolves, so tuple joins `(p, q)`, outer-binding reads inside branches, and branch-internal shadowing keep resolving. Both surfaces now emit the identical error[resolve] and refuse to execute (was: interp panic + ungraceful codegen error). Probing surfaced a SEPARATE pre-existing codegen gap at the par join — opened as B-2026-07-02-31. Regressions: tests/resolver.rs::test_par_{sibling_branch_read_rejected,sibling_branch_assign_rejected,nested_par_still_sees_outer_siblings_as_illegal,tail_expression_sees_all_branch_bindings}.

Narrow-element collection LITERALS packed i64/f64 behind a narrow-typed context at EVERY sink: the literal compilers derived the element LLVM type from the first compiled item (int literal = i64), so `let v: Vec[i32] = [10, 20, 30]`, by-value/ref/Slice call args, method args, struct fields, and return position all stored wide-packed buffers that every read reinterpreted at the narrow stride — silent wrong answers (`v[2]` read element 1's low half; iteration summed garbage; Column.from_vec's memcpy propagated it — Column[i32].sum() = 30 not 60, Column[i8] = 1 not 6; `let v: Vec[f64] = [1, 2, 3]` read back denormal garbage from int BITS in double slots). Bare `[v; n]` at a Vec-typed arg sink additionally failed module verification (stack [N x T] array vs the {ptr,i64,i64} Vec ABI). FIX (three layers): (1) typechecker check-mode re-records a collection literal admitted against a scalar-element Vec/VecDeque/ref-Vec/Slice context at its CONTEXTUAL type (record-only — acceptance semantics untouched; Slice contexts record Vec[elem] since the literal materializes as a Vec); (2) codegen literal compilers consume the width via the existing pending_let_elem_type carrier (annotated lets, Column.from_vec inline args) plus a new span-record fallback (literal_span_elem_hint over enum_inst_type_exprs), coercing each element via coerce_literal_elem_to_type (trunc/sext + the int→float sitofp leg); (3) bare repeat literals whose span record says Vec route through build_vec_filled. FOLLOW-ON leak (caught by the new ASAN test on Linux LSan only — macOS missed it via reachable stack slots, the known LSan-reachability caveat, and it PRE-EXISTED for array-literal args): by-value Vec params are caller-retains (callee emits no free — verified in IR), so a fresh collection-literal arg's heap buffer orphaned once per call; the fresh-heap materialization gates in compile_call/compile_method_call now admit collection-literal args, and collection_literal_slice_parts queues the backing-buffer free for Slice-param borrows. 19-probe A/B matrix all-match (interp / default auto-par build / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0). Regressions: tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_narrow_literal_{vec_packs_at_annotated_width,all_sinks_pack_contextual_width}, tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_narrow_literal_arg_sink_buffers.

fix: d984ddfc
title: Out-of-range integer literals are silently admitted at narrow int contexts: `let x: i8 = 200` typechecks and both surfaces print 200 (the permissive let-coercion class — the value is stored wide); `let v: Vec[i8] = [200]` typechecks and DIVERGES — interp prints 200 (Value::Int kept wide) while build prints -56 (B-2026-07-02-6's literal packing truncates into the honest i8 buffer; pre-fix build read the wide buffer's low byte, also -56, so the divergence is long-standing, not introduced). `let a: Array[i8, 1] = [200]` prints 200 on both (array elements stored wide — its own width dishonesty). FIX DIRECTION: reject integer literals that do not fit the contextual narrow int range at check-mode (scalar and collection-element positions alike — the Rust literal-out-of-range rule); that also makes the 200-vs--56 divergence unrepresentable. Related: the numeric-coercion-permissive class (let-binding coercion widens AND narrows i64<->f64). FIXED 2026-07-02 (d984ddfc): typechecker literal-range validation at three sites sharing check_int_literal_fits (i128 math) — (1) SUFFIXED literals validate against their own suffix at synthesis (`300u8` errors anywhere; negated `-128i8` validates the NEGATED value in the Unary arm and span-suppresses the positive-operand check so bare `128i8` stays an error); (2) UNSUFFIXED bare/negated literals validate against the contextual narrow type in check-mode (annotated lets, fn args, struct fields, returns; `ref T` peels); (3) the B-2026-07-02-6 Vec-context collection-literal arm validates direct integer-literal elements (that arm synthesizes elements so site 2 never sees them; Array-expected literals get it free via per-element check_expr). Negative-into-unsigned gets a dedicated message — `let x: u8 = -1` was the worst divergence (run -1 vs build 18446744073709551615); `f(70000)` vs an i16 param, suffixed `300u8`, struct fields, repeat values, and return position all also silently diverged pre-fix. Probed 18 shapes: all rejected identically on both surfaces now; boundary values (255u8/-128i8/i16-i32 extremes/large u64) locked green by test. RESIDUALS: match PATTERN literals (`200` against an i8 scrutinee — consistent unreachable-arm behavior on both surfaces, no divergence) and generic-inference sinks (`Column.from_vec([300])` with Column[u8] — the literal unifies against a metavar before solving; still diverges 300 vs 44 via honest narrow packing; needs post-solve literal validation). `-9223372036854775808` stays a consistent pre-existing parse error (no unary-minus lexer special-case). Regressions: tests/typechecker.rs::test_int_literal_{out_of_range_rejected_at_narrow_contexts,boundaries_still_admitted}.

SILENT data corruption in DEFAULT auto-par builds: `Vec.sort()`/`sort_by`/`sort_by_key`/`reverse`/`pop`/`remove` were invisible to the auto-parallelizer's write-dependency gate — `method_effects_imply_receiver_mutation` (src/concurrency.rs) found no `.{method}` effect key because the effectchecker's builtin seed table only seeded the push/insert families. A `v.sort()` co-grouped with a later read of `v` raced the runtime's permute-back against the read (NON-DETERMINISTIC duplicated/lost elements: a 2-element Vec[String] section printed `omega,omega` on ~25% of runs; 9 distinct outputs over 25 runs of a 4-section program); `v.pop()`/`v.remove(i)` followed by `v.len()` read a stale pre-mutation {ptr,len,cap} branch-capture copy 100% DETERMINISTICALLY (printed the un-popped len every run). Distinct from B-2026-07-02-4 (par-group slot CLEANUP leaks) — this is missed SERIALIZATION; same class as B-2026-06-20-16 (map entry writes) and the VecDeque.push/pop seeds from the Map+VecDeque coexistence fix. FIX: seed the six method keys `allocates(Heap)` in the builtin table — accurate for the reorder family (runtime sort paths allocate index/scratch buffers, `karac_vec_reverse` a tmp element), over-approximate for pop/remove matching the VecDeque.pop_* precedent. The gate matches on the `.{method}` name suffix, so the `Vec.`-qualified seeds also serialize `Map.remove`/`Set.remove`/VecDeque `.pop()`. RESIDUAL: any future builtin mutating method must be seeded or it silently races — `clear`/`insert`/`truncate`/`dedup`/`retain` are not yet in codegen (honest 'not yet supported' errors) so nothing else is exposed today; when one lands, seed it in the same block. E2E regression test drives all three shapes under the default auto-par build (tests/par_codegen.rs test_e2e_auto_par_sort_and_pop_serialize_against_reads).

fix: 3c8cd55b
title: `String.cmp(other)` on a NON-identifier receiver — a string LITERAL (`"abd".cmp("abc")`) or an INDEX into a Vec[String] (`v[0].cmp(v[1])`) — typechecked and ran correctly but FAILED `karac build`: `codegen failed: Vec/String method 'cmp' is not yet supported in codegen`. A run/build divergence, and an incomplete-fix follow-on to B-2026-06-30-13 (which shipped String.cmp codegen but guarded the branch on `inferred_receiver_type(object) == Some("String")`, a lookup that resolves only NAMED receivers via var_type_names — a literal / index / field receiver has no var-name, so it fell through to the loud catch-all). Surfaced by a post-reinstall smoke test using `("abd").cmp("abc")`. FIX (3c8cd55b): guard the String branch on the operand LAYOUT (`l.get_type() == vec_struct_type()`, the String {ptr,len,cap} header) instead of the receiver name. Sound because the typechecker admits `.cmp` only on int/char/bool/String; int/char/bool compile to IntValue (handled by the earlier arm), floats are excluded from Ord (NaN), and user-struct `.cmp` is typecheck-rejected — so ANY {ptr,len,cap}-shaped struct pair reaching this arm is a String, for every receiver shape (identifier/local/param already worked; literal + index now join them). Test: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_string_cmp_nonident_receiver_codegen; e2e_string_cmp_codegen still green. fmt + clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean.

Explicit closure capture-mode prefix (`own`/`ref`/`mut ref`, design.md Rule 2½) was IGNORED by the closure-escape check: `own |x| x + k` returned from a function still fired E0508 RefCaptureEscapesScope, even though an own-capture escape is the design-blessed CLEAN escape (Rule 2 sub-case (i) — captures move into the closure, no borrow to outlive). Root cause: the Rule 2½ prefix pinning (disjoint-capture slice 5) was applied to the per-PATH map `closure_capture_path_modes` but never to the per-NAME `closure_captures` map, which is the one `check_closure_ref_capture_escapes` reads — so the escape check always saw the body-usage-inferred Ref mode. Meant there was NO check-clean spelling for an escaping capturing closure at all (`karac check` rejected the entire shipped heap-env feature surface in every spelling, while build/run execute it correctly). FIXED e092e041: pin `captures` to the declared mode before the insert (ownership/expr_check.rs), mirroring the existing path-map pinning. Bare (inferred) ref-capture escapes still reject per Rule 2 sub-case (iv). Surfaced by the new E2E ownership gate (this slice) flushing 88 heap_env_* tests; probed via own_probe.kara.

`println(s); println(s)` (or any later use of a printed heap value: `println(c); println(c.len())`) was rejected by `karac check` as a use-after-move — printing CONSUMED its argument. Root cause: the print family (print/println/eprint/eprintln) are typechecker/codegen intrinsics with no declared signature in the user program OR the baked stdlib, so collect_callee_param_modes had no entry and call args fell through to the conservative consume-everything default. Contradicts design.md § Display ('borrows the receiver — the same value can appear in multiple {} slots without being consumed') and both execution surfaces (interp + codegen never consume the arg). Same class as B-2026-07-01-10 (Stats bare-Slice params) — a read-only stdlib surface whose signature/classification says consume. FIXED e092e041: intrinsic Ref-mode entries for the four print fns inserted at the head of collect_callee_param_modes (stdlib/user definitions still override), plus `s: ref String` on the baked Stdout/Stderr print/println methods in runtime/stdlib/io.kara. Cured ~20 E2E reds (string push/concat/display/shadow corpus). Full llvm suites + LSan-lane green — no RC-fallback or codegen behavior shift observed.

`for x in v { .. } println(v.len())` was rejected by `karac check` as a use-after-move of `v` ('moved' at the for-loop header). Root cause: use_classifier.rs walked the For iterable in Mode::Consuming, while design.md § Iterable is explicit — 'The collection is always borrowed — `for` never consumes it. To consume a collection while iterating, call .into_iter() explicitly.' The legacy state-machine walker (ownership/expr_check.rs) already walked it as reading; only the predicate-pipeline classifier consumed, so the UAM predicate fired. FIXED e092e041: For iterable walks Mode::Reading; a consuming iterable sub-expression (v.into_iter()) still classifies itself via the method-receiver walk. Cured the vec_macro_literal/vec_repeat_literal/unsigned_vec_elem/for_loop_string_elem E2E reds.

Comparison operators CONSUME their operands under `karac check`: `if a == b {..} if a == c {..}` on String flags `a` as moved at the first comparison; `a < b` / `a > b` same; and `==` on a user struct consumes the operands EVEN WHEN the resolved PartialEq/Eq impls declare `ref self, other: ref Self`. Both use_classifier.rs and ownership/expr_check.rs walk ExprKind::Binary operands as reads, so the consume comes from the lowered/dispatched eq path (typechecker method lowering or the desugared eq call's receiver/arg classification) — not the Binary arm itself; root not yet isolated. Design is unambiguous (partial_eq.kara: `fn eq(ref self, other: ref Self)`; comparisons borrow). Hits completely natural code — the http_server serve-handler tests iterate headers with `for (k, v) in hdrs { if k == "x-test-echo" {..} if k == "host" {..} }` and the second `k ==` is a use-after-move. Runtime semantics unaffected (interp + codegen never consume; `karac build`/`run` execute correctly) — check-surface only. Grandfathered: test_e2e_string_equality, test_e2e_string_ordering, test_e2e_user_impl_eq_drives_equality, test_server_serve_handler_iterates_headers, test_server_serve_handler_reads_query_param (tests/common/mod.rs OWNERSHIP_GATE_GRANDFATHERED — remove on fix).

Binding a NAMED FUNCTION as a value treats the fn item as affine: `let g = doubler; let h = doubler;` flags `doubler` moved at the first let and use-after-move at the second; likewise `apply(doubler, 10); apply(doubler, 11)` (two call-arg uses). A fn item has no captures and is a plain code pointer — freely duplicable per design.md § First-Class Functions ('User.validate is an unbound function value — no capture'; only closures capturing owned non-Copy values are once-callable). Check-surface only (build/run fine). Grandfathered: fn_value_let_bound_named_fn_passed_and_called, fn_value_named_fn_reused_across_call_sites (remove on fix).

A field- or tuple-path USE consumes the WHOLE root binding: `Add(b) => eval(b.left) + eval(b.right)` flags `b` moved-whole at the first field-path call arg (b.right is then a use-after-move); `match t.0 {..} match t.1 {..}` over a tuple does the same for projections; struct-field iterables (`for a in c.args` then c.callee) likewise. No partial-move tracking for direct place paths — call-arg and match-scrutinee place classification keys the root binding — contradicting the disjoint-place philosophy the borrow checker and closure disjoint-capture (Rule 2¼) already implement. Dominant red class in the ASAN shared-enum drop corpus (match-arm payload struct `b` with two+ Expr fields consumed field-by-field — the natural recursive-eval shape every tree-walking program uses). Check-surface only (build/run + drop behavior correct; the corpus pins that). Grandfathered (remove on fix): test_e2e_struct_wrapped_recursive_shared_enum_tree, test_e2e_vec_of_struct_with_shared_and_option_field, asan_collect_all_heterogeneous_tuple_no_uaf, asan_match_byvalue_shared_enum_* (3), asan_shared_enum_recursive_struct_payload_string_freed_no_leak, asan_struct_nested_enum_leaf/with_direct_enum_field (2), asan_struct_wrapped_* (6), asan_vec_of_shared_enum_elements_freed_no_leak.

`with_provider[Metric](p, || ..); println(p.n)` is rejected — the provider VALUE arg is classified as consumed, so the post-pop use of `p` is a use-after-move. But the documented semantics of the with_provider E2E pin is exactly 'mut ref self mutation VISIBLE AFTER pop' — the value is borrowed by the provider frame, not consumed. with_provider is a typechecker special form whose generic call shape does not route through collect_callee_param_modes (an intrinsic [Ref, Own] entry for the bare name was added in e092e041 but does not match the `with_provider[Effect](..)` callee form), so the args fall to the consume default. Fix direction: classify the special form's value slot as a borrow where its call is lowered/classified. Grandfathered: test_with_provider_e2e_mut_ref_self_mutation_visible_after_pop (remove on fix).

A `ref Column[i64]` parameter SILENTLY produces no output under codegen: `fn fst(c: ref Column[i64], i: i64) -> i64 { match c[i] { Some(v) => v, None => -999 } }` called as fst(a, 0) — `karac check` clean, interpreter prints the right values, but the AOT binary prints NOTHING and exits 0 (probed refcol_probe.kara on clean main d811565c via the primary llvm karac — pre-existing, not introduced by the gate slice). Bare (consuming) Column params work on both surfaces; only the ref form mis-lowers, presumably the builtin-container method/index paths don't deref the ref param (same family as the receiver-width/ref-param deref gotchas in the Column/DataFrame codegen notes). Surfaced attempting the check-clean rewrite of test_e2e_column_3vl_arithmetic (helper reuse over Columns requires ref params after B-2026-07-01-10's precedent). The test keeps bare params and is grandfathered past the ownership gate until this lands (remove on fix).

`ref Slice[i64]` + `unsafe { xs.get_unchecked(i) }` MISCOMPILES: the AOT binary prints the slice header words instead of elements (probed refslice_probe.kara: expected 10/20/30, got 4340063264/3/4 = data-pointer/len/garbage) — get_unchecked indexes the {ptr,len,cap} struct itself rather than dereferencing the ref param to reach the buffer. `karac check` clean, interpreter correct; pre-existing on clean main d811565c (probed via the primary llvm karac). Plain `xs[i]` on `ref Slice` params is fine (Stats corpus, B-2026-07-01-10) — the unsafe get_unchecked lowering is missing the ref-param deref. Surfaced attempting the check-clean rewrite of test_e2e_slice_get_unchecked_in_bounds_returns_element; that test keeps the bare Slice param and is grandfathered past the ownership gate until this lands (remove on fix).

Struct method named like a seq builtin (first/last/get_unchecked) silently returned Unit — try_eval_seq_method receiver-shape arms swallowed non-seq receivers instead of falling through to the impl-block path; b.first() on a trait impl printed (). Fixed: try_eval_impl_method extracted and called early for Struct/SharedStruct receivers + the three swallow arms return None. Residual: user ENUM receivers with builtin-named methods still reach the seq arms.

Generic-mono param surface unimplemented: a Fn(...)-typed param was never in closure_fn_types so f(x) fell to the unknown-callee const-0 placeholder (apply[T](x,f)->T silently returned 0 under build); for-loops over Vec params silently compiled to NOTHING; xs.len() failed loudly. Fixed: mono prologue mirrors compile_function's param registration (closure_abi_fn_type, register_var_from_type_expr under active type_subst, owned_vecstr_params, unconditional ref_params) + the direct-call site passes pointers for ref-mode args.

Un-annotated closure param vs declared-Fn ABI mismatch: params fell back to i64 (pending_closure_param_hints was never set anywhere), so |a| f"{a}!" against Fn(String)->String compiled as (ptr,i64)->i64 while call sites dispatched the declared-Fn ABI — String's pointer word printed as an integer. Fixed: typechecker records the closure literal's resolved Fn type at its span (flows via fn_value_typed_exprs); compile_closure types un-annotated params from it and registers String/Vec params in the semantic side-tables.

let-annotation elem hint leaked into call-argument collection literals: pending_let_elem_type covers the whole RHS (needed by Vec.with_capacity lowering) and used to beat the literal's own span-recorded type, so let s: String = tail_str(vec![100,200,300]) packed the arg elements as i8 and printed 100100100. No generics involved. Fixed: literal_span_elem_hint's per-span type (enum_inst_type_exprs) now wins; span-less literals still fall through to the ambient hint.

Browser playground 100% broken: run_on_interp_thread (the Windows fat-stack fix) lifted EVERY interpreter run onto a fresh 16MB spawn_scoped thread; wasm32-unknown-unknown spawn returns Err(Unsupported) and the .expect trapped every playground run() — even fn main(){println("ctrl")} — as 'failed to spawn interpreter thread'. Found by the A2a-2.2-fu headless-Chrome probe (phase-5-diagnostics line 642); the compile-only check predating the fat-stack fix couldn't see it. Fixed: cfg(target_arch=wasm32) variant runs the closure inline on the caller's stack.

Second universal playground trap + the program-triggered wasm trap class: Interpreter::new seeded xorshift via SystemTime::now(), which panics 'time not implemented' on wasm32 — every run() still trapped after B-2026-07-02-29's fix. Fixed with a fixed golden-ratio seed (deterministic playground RandomSource). Same slice guarded the rest of the sys/unsupported class reachable from playground programs: sleep_ms thread::sleep → no-op pause (arg still evaluated), par{} thread::scope → sequential_mode defaults true on wasm (FIFO-deterministic, matches the seq_scheduler wasm codegen story), Clock.now + RateLimiter.try_acquire → runtime diagnostics instead of module traps. Verified in headless Chrome: control/sleep/par/clock probes green.

Explicit `par { }` blocks whose branches read an OUTER (pre-par) binding, or whose branch RHS contains a nested block expression, fail codegen at the join with 'Undefined variable' while `karac run` executes them correctly — a loud run-vs-build divergence (build refuses; no miscompiled output). Repros (2026-07-02, scratchpad pardiag/p4,p7 — identical on clean main, so pre-existing, surfaced while fixing B-2026-07-02-5): (a) `let base = 100; let total = par { let x = base + 1; let y = base + 2; x + y };` -> build: codegen failed: Undefined variable 'x' (run prints 203); (b) `let t = par { let x = 1; let y = { let x = 10; x + 1 }; x + y };` -> Undefined variable 'y' (run prints 12). The plain shapes work (tuple join `(p, q)` of bare-call branches and a direct `x.len() + y.len()` tail both build), so the explicit-par lowering loses branch bindings only when a branch body is more than a bare call chain — likely the branch classifier / return-slot collection (compute_return_slots in par_blocks.rs) drops branches it cannot slot and the tail then references a binding no slot carries. FIX DIRECTION: make the explicit-par lowering's binding collection cover arbitrary branch statement shapes, or serialize unsupported branches (with the design-mandated note[par_serialized]) instead of failing the join.

Every use of the fully-wired #[profile(P1, ...)] attribute emitted a bogus error[E_UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE] alongside the real profile diagnostics: 'profile' was never added to RECOGNIZED_BARE_ATTRIBUTES in src/attribute_validator.rs when the attribute shipped 2026-05-18 (parser scan_profile_attr -> Function.profile_compat, resolver placement/name validation, effectchecker/profile_compat.rs enforcement; phase-5-diagnostics.md line 510) — so karac check failed even on profile-compatible functions and the attribute was unusable under the check gate. Repro: #[profile(embedded)] fn f() -> Vec[i64] { Vec.new() } -> both the correct E_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE_EFFECT and the bogus unknown-attribute error. Fixed: allowlist entry (comment points at the checklist item), attr_slice2_profile_attribute_recognised regression pin, and the missing appendix-d book entry (A/B-verified on run + llvm build).

fix: 84fb2a6b
title: Interpreter had no ExprKind::OffsetOf arm: karac run panicked 'not yet implemented: unhandled expr' on any offset_of[T](field.path) while karac build printed the offset (typechecker+codegen shipped, interp never got the arm). Fixed with an AST-driven layout engine (src/interpreter/layout_query.rs) mirroring llvm_type_for_type_expr/llvm_type_for_name arm-for-arm: natural-alignment struct walks, String/Vec 24-byte {ptr,len,cap}, Slice 16, opaque heap handles ptr, enums {i64 tag, i64 x payload-words}, shared types ptr, Array/Vector/Atomic/Mutex/tuple/union, seeded builtin enum layouts, unknown-name i64 fall-through; nested paths chain like compile_offset_of. A/B byte-identical run-vs-build on 30 probes (mixed-alignment padding, heap/enum fields, 3-level nesting). eval_expr's match is now exhaustive — a future ExprKind fails at compile time, not via runtime todo!.

fix: 84fb2a6b
title: Sibling gap found probing B-2026-07-02-33: size_of[T]()/align_of[T]() had no interpreter intercept — the Call(Index(Ident,T)) parse shape fell through to variable lookup and panicked 'internal error: variable size_of not found; should be caught by resolver' under karac run (build compiled fine, printed 16/8). Fixed via the same layout engine (eval_layout_query = alloc size / ABI alignment of the lowered type, mirroring compile_layout_query_intrinsic) intercepted in eval_call ahead of normal dispatch, both parse shapes. The typecheck-invalid nested-generic shape size_of[Vec[i64]]() (E_LAYOUT_QUERY_TYPE_ARG_REQUIRED) now degrades to a clean runtime error under run's tolerate-typecheck-errors design instead of panicking. A/B identical on 13 probes.

A read-only owned bare-`T` param reused across call sites is flagged use-after-move by `karac check` (`fn peek(s: Span) -> i64 { s.off }` then `let x = peek(r); let y = peek(r);`). RESOLVED as correct-by-design, NOT a checker change: per design.md a bare-`T` param is OWNED (the caller loses ownership) and ownership modes are DECLARED at the signature, not inferred — so the second `peek(r)` genuinely is a move-after-move and the diagnostic is right. The two shared-enum-drop asan corpus programs were the defect: their read-only `peek` helper now takes `ref` (it only reads a field), making the reuse a legal borrow; both un-grandfathered and pass the strict ownership gate (runtime drop behavior unchanged). Considered but rejected: whole-program inferred-`ref`-mode call-arg classification — that would contradict design.md's declared-modes rule.

fix: 479ff4bf
title: Same-scope shadowing re-`let` shared the CFG binding identity of the binding it shadows: after `let x = "..."; let y = x; let x = 99;`, reading the NEW x (`println(x)`) was flagged 'value x moved here, used again here' — karac check false-rejected legal rebind-after-move (UseKind::Define is deliberately not a reassign-kill, so the old binding's consume paired with the new binding's reads), and sibling-scope name reuse could pair as a spurious RC witness. The REPL hard-failed the same shape since its cell pipeline gates on ownershipcheck (surfaced by B-2026-07-02-37's post-shadow replay). Fixed with per-shadow alpha-rename frames in the CFG builder (@shN — same device as @armN/@forN/@cuN, stripped by demangle_binding): a let/let-uninit/let-else that re-binds a visible name (params seeded via build_cfg_with_classification's new param_names arg; every introduction tracked in seen_names) renames subsequent uses until the ENCLOSING block's lowering completes (lower_block truncates the rename stack after fall-through defer emission), so an inner-block shadow pops at block end and a genuine use-after-move of the outer binding after the block still fires.

REPL sessions deterministically bricked by re-binding a persistent let: `let x = 99;` after `let x = "...";` pruned the earlier binder's replay slice (prune_shadowed_lets) while later persistent lets (`let y = x;`) — or the re-binding cell's own RHS (`let x = x + 1;`) — still referenced it, so every cell from the re-bind onward failed 'resolve error: undefined name x' (identical with/without KARAC_REPL_JIT; the failed cell's new binder was never captured, so the session never recovered). Fixed: prune_shadowed_lets -> clear_rebound_let_snapshots — ALL binders stay in persistent_lets (same-scope shadowing is legal Kara; the replay now matches the :save export program exactly) and only the stale value snapshot clears; the interpreter's snapshot override map re-keyed from binding NAME to the binder-pattern SPAN of each name's LAST top-level let (install_let_snapshot_overrides, shared by the cell pipeline and %show) so earlier shadows re-run their recorded RHS in submission order and pattern lets replayed between two binders read historically correct values; the lljit prototype's snapshot classification got the same last-binder gate (an earlier binder must not load the final — possibly differently-typed — global mid-sequence). Depends on B-2026-07-02-36: the post-shadow synthetic is exactly the rebind-after-move shape that predicate false-flagged.

fix: 1fecbb0f
title: Residual of B-2026-07-02-31: an explicit `par { }` branch whose `let` RHS is a METHOD CALL (`let x = base.abs()`) or an INDEX (`let x = v[0]`) still fails codegen at the join with 'Undefined variable' while `karac run` executes correctly (same run-vs-build divergence; build refuses, no miscompiled output). B-31 (24b1c9f4/ec5c9f20) made `infer_expr_llvm_type` (src/codegen/stmts.rs) cover lowered operator dispatch, block/if/match-expr RHS, and identifier/literal/bare-call RHS, but it conservatively returns None for MethodCall/Index/FieldAccess — sizing those needs impl-return-type / Vec-element-type lookup at that point. Fix direction: extend infer_expr_llvm_type to resolve method-return and index-element types (or thread the typechecker's inferred type through to the par return-slot sizer). Spawned as background task task_6b663d84.

Generic monos leaked every non-tensor name-keyed var side-table across nested compiles AND same-LLVM-shape handle instantiations shared one mono. Only tensor_var_infos was save/restored around compile_mono_function, so after B-2026-07-02-11's full-registration prologue mono #1's 'c -> Column[i64]' entry survived into mono #2 where 'c' was a Tensor param — the Column intercept compiled a column reduce over a tensor handle (SIGSEGV; probed report[C: MyReduce[i64]] instantiated at Column then Tensor). Independently, infer_type_args sees only LLVM value types (a Column and a Tensor arg are both `ptr`) so the two instantiations mangled to the SAME symbol and shared one body. Fixed: SavedVarSideTables swaps all 17 name-keyed tables around both mono wrappers (+ column/tensor/dataframe_var_infos join compile_function's per-fn clear — the same latent leak existed across top-level fns); mono_handle_param_infos threads the arg spans' column/tensor_typed_exprs records into a mangle axis ($c_col_i64 / $c_ten_i64_4) and the mono prologue's registration.

Bound trait-args never substituted in method dispatch through a generic bound: fn grand[C: MyReduce[i64]](c: ref C) -> i64 { c.total() } failed check with "expected 'i64', found 'T'" — dispatch_trait_assoc_fn substituted only Self, so a parameterized bound's method signature kept the trait's raw TypeParam. Fixed: trait_bound_arg_subs binds the bound's generic args to the trait's declared params (find_trait_def: user program then baked stdlib; args lowered in the enclosing generic scope so C: MyReduce[U] works) and dispatch_trait_assoc_fn seeds them into subs + scope. Prerequisite for the S6a stdlib Reduce[T] trait.

Vec[T]-param generic monos never bind T — two element-type instantiations SHARE one mono and the second silently returns garbage under `karac build`: fn head[T](v: ref Vec[T]) -> T { v[0] } called with Vec[i64] then Vec[f64] prints 7 then 4612811918334230528 (2.5's f64 bits as i64); interpreter correct. unify_type_expr only binds BARE Path(T) params against the whole LLVM type (the container-generic-args arm is a TODO) and a Vec's {ptr,len,cap} LLVM shape is element-erased, so the subst has no T entry, the mangle gets no suffix, and the prologue's register_var_from_type_expr falls back to i64 elems. Same family as the S6a handle-instantiation collision (fixed via mono_handle_param_infos, B-2026-07-02-39) but needs general TypeExpr-level mono type args — an S6b prerequisite (trait-method monomorphization needs the same substitution machinery). Probed p8_vec_elem_mono_collision.kara.

fix: ee1fd78e
title: FIXED (ee1fd78e): a PARAMETERIZED bound never compared its trait ARGS against the matched impl. `fn spread[C: Reduce[i64]](c: ref C)` called with a Column[f64] (which impls Reduce[f64], NOT Reduce[i64]) PASSED `karac check` (bound satisfaction matched the trait NAME only), ran with silently wrong types (a double result flowing through the i64-typed signature), and only codegen module verification died loud (ret double vs i64). FIX: ImplInfo now records the impl's trait_args (the [T] in `impl[T] Reduce[T] for Column[T]`) plus target_generic_args (the target's args WITH params, since target_args collapses to empty for a generic impl); discharge_type_bounds (src/typechecker/exprs.rs), on a bound carrying generic args, computes the impl's CONCRETE trait args via env.impl_concrete_trait_args (structurally bind the impl params from the receiver's args, substitute through trait_args) and compares them against the bound's requested args (lowered with the fn's params in scope + solved). Rejects only a fully-concrete-vs-fully-concrete mismatch; an unsolved/still-parametric arg on either side is skipped so `C: Reduce[T]` and a matching Reduce[i64] are never false-rejected. Message: 'Column<f64> implements Reduce[f64], not Reduce[i64]'. Tests: typechecker parameterized_trait_bound_args_checked_against_impl + parameterized_trait_bound_matching_accepted. Probed p10_bound_arg_mismatch.kara during S6a.

fix: 0ceda7ab
title: f64.to_bits()/to_bits32() and the inverse i64.bits_as_f64()/bits_as_f32() had an interpreter + typechecker implementation but NO codegen arm, so a program that round-tripped an f64 through its bit pattern ran under `karac run` yet failed `karac build` with "no handler for method 'to_bits'" — a run/build divergence. Surfaced by the LeetCode #50 Pow(x, n) benchmark, whose diffable cross-language sink sum-folds each result's raw f64 bits into an integer. Fixed: lowered to pure LLVM bitcasts (no runtime helper, no allocation, no new C symbol) — to_bits bitcast f64->i64; to_bits32 fptrunc->f32, bitcast->i32, zext->i64; bits_as_* width-normalize the receiver then bitcast to the float. Mirrors the interpreter arm byte-for-byte incl. the sign-bit-only -0.0 pattern. Regression: e2e_float_to_bits_codegen.

fix: f6e35b1c
title: A method declared `-> Self` was broken end-to-end under `karac build` for EVERY form (inherent method, trait impl, static constructor); `karac run` masked it by executing past the typecheck warning, and selfhost/examples never exercise `-> Self` under build (0 occurrences), so the gap was latent. Three legs: (1) TYPECHECK — a `Self` return-type annotation lowers to `Named{"Self"}` (or `TypeParam("Self")` when "Self" is an in-scope generic), and the body's concrete tail type is not assignable to it, so `check_function` rejected valid code with "expected 'Self', found 'W'". (2) CODEGEN PROTOTYPE — `llvm_return_type` hit the unknown-name `i64` fall-through for `Self`, so a struct-returning `-> Self` fn's LLVM type mismatched its aggregate `ret` (module-verify hard failure). (3) CALL-SITE TYPING — the value-receiver method-call return type substituted only the impl's generics, leaving `Self` unresolved, so `a.m()` typed as `Self` and downstream field reads returned 0 (silent miscompile). FIXED (f6e35b1c): items.rs `resolve_self_in_type` resolves `Self` in the lowered return type to the concrete impl target inside `check_function` (identity for a trait default body); helpers.rs `rewrite_self_in_type_expr` rewrites `Self` in the synthesized impl-method's return type before prototype build; expr_method_call.rs resolves `Self` in the method-call return type + params to the concrete receiver. Tests: typechecker `method_self_return_type_resolves_to_impl_target`, codegen e2e `e2e_method_self_return_struct_lowers_and_reads_fields`. Suites green: typechecker 1859 / interpreter 1082 / codegen 1978. Surfaced probing narrow-width x trait machinery. Two follow-ons it EXPOSED are tracked separately: B-2026-07-03-3 (chained aggregate-return field read) and B-2026-07-03-4 (auto-par static `-> Self` result).

fix: 839beaea
title: PRE-EXISTING codegen miscompile (independent of Self; surfaced while fixing B-2026-07-03-2): a chained `expr.method().field` where the method returns an AGGREGATE (struct) reads the wrong value (0) under `karac build`, while the let-bound form `let b = expr.method(); b.field` is correct, and `karac run` (interp) is correct. Confirmed with a CONCRETE return type (`impl W { fn m(self) -> W { W{v:self.v+1} } }`; `a.m().v` -> 0 vs bound -> 2), so it is not `Self`-specific. A SCALAR (i64) chained return is fine (`a.inc()` where inc -> i64 works), so the bug is specific to a method-call temporary of aggregate shape consumed immediately by field access — the temporary's struct slot is not materialized/addressed before the field GEP. Repro: struct W{v:i64}; impl W{fn m(self)->W{W{v:self.v+1}}}; fn main(){let a=W{v:1}; println(a.m().v);} -> build prints 0, run prints 2. Workaround: bind the call result to a local first. Fix likely in the method-call-result field-access path (materialize the aggregate temp to an alloca before the field offset load). FIXED (839beaea): added MethodCall/Call arms to type_name_of_expr (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs) resolving a call's static return-type name via fn_return_type_names (impl methods keyed by qualified Type.method; free/2-seg-Path calls by callee), so field_index_for locates the field and compile_field_access emits an extractvalue instead of the i64 0 placeholder. Receiver resolved recursively (deeper chains a.m().n, mk(x).field work); non-struct returns degrade to prior behavior. Tests: codegen e2e e2e_chained_call_struct_field_access (scalar/heap-String/multi-field/double-chain/free-fn), memory_sanitizer asan_chained_call_struct_heap_field_no_leak (heap-field temp loop; Linux ASan+LSan clean, macOS ASan clean). codegen 1985+, all suites green; fmt+clippy clean.

fix: db020ee6
title: FIXED (db020ee6, side effect of B-2026-07-03-11): Auto-par-only miscompile newly reachable after B-2026-07-03-2 enabled `-> Self` builds: a STATIC associated fn returning `-> Self`, bound to a local and then used as a method receiver, produces the wrong value (0) under the DEFAULT auto-par build, while the sequential build (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0) and interp are correct — and `--concurrency-report` says 'no parallelization opportunities detected', so the divergence is from an auto-par-path codegen decision, NOT from forming a par group. Tightly scoped: the INSTANCE `-> Self` result feeding a method is fine under auto-par, and a CONCRETE static return (`make() -> W`) feeding a method is fine — only the static `make() -> Self` source triggers it. Repro: struct W{v:i64}; trait Dbl{fn twice(self)->Self;} impl W{fn make()->Self{W{v:7}}} impl Dbl for W{fn twice(self)->Self{W{v:self.v+self.v}}} fn main(){let c=W.make(); let d=c.twice(); println(d.v);} -> auto-par build 0, seq build 14, run 14. Likely the auto-par path re-derives the static-assoc `-> Self` call result type from the original (unrewritten, `Self`) method AST rather than the concrete target, mis-materializing the binding's slot. Guarded out of the B-2026-07-03-2 e2e regression test (twice() is called on a literal-bound receiver there). FIX ATTRIBUTION: the binding `let c = W.make()` (static assoc `-> Self`) mis-materialized its slot via the HashMap-order struct reverse-lookup in stmts.rs; B-11 (db020ee6) hardened that path (record_var_type_name central name-subst resolution + a MethodCall ast_hint arm resolving via type_name_of_expr), which also corrected this static-Call binding. Verified: repro yields 0 at db020ee6^ (8a11959d) and 14 at db020ee6 through concurrency_analyze. Regression guard: test_e2e_auto_par_static_self_assoc_fn_receiver (par_codegen.rs). NOTE: trigger is KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1 (or the concurrency_analyze compile path), not the plain default build.

User-defined trait impls on PRIMITIVE integer types are unsupported end-to-end despite being an intended feature (design.md shows `impl Pod for u8`, `impl From[i32] for i64`; env_build.rs references `impl Eq for u8`; a typechecker test asserts `i64` would satisfy a bound if `impl Tr for i64` existed). For `impl Tr for <int> { fn m(self) -> ... { self + ... } }`: (1) `check_impl_block` builds the self type as `Type::Named{name:"u8"}` by hand (items.rs ~1808) instead of lowering the target, so inside the method body `self` is not recognized as numeric — `self + self` errors "arithmetic operator requires numeric type, found 'u8'" for EVERY width incl i64; (2) the method is never registered on the primitive — the call site errors "no method 'm' on type 'u8'" (and a generic bound `fn f[T: Tr](x:T)` reports "`u8` does not implement `Tr`"). Under `karac run` only `impl Tr for i64` accidentally dispatches (runtime int values are i64-typed, matching the i64-keyed impl); every narrow width (u8/u16/u32/i8/i16/i32) AND u64 fail at runtime with "method 'm' not found on type 'i64' (no interpreter dispatch arm)" because the value's runtime type is width-erased to i64 while the impl is keyed on the declared narrow width. Under `karac build` all widths fail at typecheck. Repro: trait Dbl{fn dbl(self)->Self;} impl Dbl for u8{fn dbl(self)->Self{self+self}} fn main(){let a:u8=10; println(a.dbl());}. Fix spans typecheck (lower the impl target so a primitive self is numeric + register methods for primitive impl targets) + interp dispatch (key user primitive-impl dispatch on the declared width, not the erased i64). Depends on B-2026-07-03-2's `Self`-return resolution for the `-> Self` shape. FIX ae7c9525 (DIRECT-call scope): (1) check_impl_block lowers the target and uses the lowered primitive Type as self_type so the body's self is numeric; (2) env_add_impl registers a primitive target under its canonical name (method_callee_type_name) instead of the `_ => return` fall-through; (3) the typecheck method-call arm routes a numeric-primitive receiver with a real impl candidate into normal impl-table dispatch (was poisoning to Type::Error), and the interpreter recovers the DECLARED receiver type from method_callee_types (value type is width-erased to i64/f64). Verified interp/seq/auto-par across all 8 scalar widths with distinguishing per-width impls incl `-> Self`. The generic-BOUND form now typechecks but mis-dispatches at runtime — see B-2026-07-03-24. REGRESSION (introduced by this fix in ae7c9525, missed by a concurrent-load-raced suite run; repaired in d15c8372): registering baked primitive impls made find_methods_with_args('i32',[],'cmp') non-empty, so the routing sent builtin comparison/cast methods (a.cmp(b)) into impl-table dispatch where the baked (self,other) signature mis-counts arity ('expects 2 arguments, found 1') — broke 4 typechecker Ord/PartialOrd tests. Fix: builtin value methods (cmp/eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge/cast) stay on their dedicated backend path, never routed.

SILENT DATA LOSS / no-op: the interpreter's `value_compare` (src/interpreter/helpers.rs) has NO arm for `Value::Struct` or `Value::EnumVariant`, so two struct (or two enum) values fall to the `_ => value_discriminant(a).cmp(&value_discriminant(b))` fallback where BOTH map to the catch-all discriminant 8 -> always Ordering::Equal. Consequences over ordered containers / sort on struct (and enum) element/key types, ALL silent-wrong under `karac run`: `SortedSet[Struct]` and `SortedMap[Struct,_]` COLLAPSE distinct keys to one (insert 3 distinct structs -> len()==1 — data loss; n11/n13), `Vec[Struct].sort()`/`sorted()` are NO-OPs that return the input order unchanged (n7: prints 3 1 2), and `min`/`max` over a Vec[Struct] are wrong. Hash-based `Set[Struct]`/`Map[Struct,_]` are UNAFFECTED (they route through derived Hash+Eq, not value_compare — n12 dedups correctly). Exactly the class FIXED for nested Vec in B-2026-06-30-15 (whose fix worked because Vec elements carry inherent order); Struct/EnumVariant are the remaining missing arms. ARCHITECTURAL wrinkle blocking a one-line arm: `value_compare` is a free fn AND backs `OrdValue::cmp`, which BTreeMap calls deep inside insert with no interpreter/type-registry access, so it cannot see struct FIELD or enum VARIANT declaration order — a naive alphabetical-field / variant-name comparison fixes the data loss but yields a WRONG order (e.g. enum Priority{Low,Med,High} would sort alphabetically High<Low<Med, and struct{last,first} would order by first). Correct fix: embed declaration order into the Struct/EnumVariant Value (or compute an ordering key with type info at SortedSet/SortedMap insert + sort call sites, where the interpreter IS in scope) so both value_compare and OrdValue reflect derived-Ord semantics. Surfaced probing narrow-width x trait (derive(Ord) on struct{i8,u8}); NOT width-specific — reproduces with i64 fields. Repros: n7 (sort no-op), n11 (SortedSet len 1), n13 (SortedMap len 1). FIXED (1b1a843b): added `Value::Struct` and `Value::EnumVariant` arms to value_compare (src/interpreter/helpers.rs) + `compare_field_maps`/`compare_enum_data` helpers. Structs order by type name then fields in sorted-field-name order; enums by enum name then variant name then payload. Both are proper total orders consistent with Value::eq, so distinct values no longer collapse in the OrdValue-keyed BTreeMap (SortedSet/SortedMap counts preserved, Vec[struct].sort() orders, min/max correct). Same class/shape as the nested-Vec fix B-2026-06-30-15. Order is alphabetical (NOT derived-Ord declaration order — value_compare has no type-registry access); that affects only observed sort/iteration SEQUENCE, never membership/dedup/count, and is tracked as B-2026-07-03-12. Test: interpreter test_struct_and_enum_ordering_no_dataloss_and_sorts. interpreter 1085 + all non-llvm green; fmt+clippy(incl llvm) clean.

Codegen side of the derived-Ord-struct ordering surface is unimplemented but fails LOUD (not silent, unlike its interp sibling B-2026-07-03-6): `Vec[Struct].sort()` errors 'Vec.sort() in codegen supports integer, String, float, tuple, and nested-Vec element types; use sort_by(|a,b| ...) for other element types'; `SortedSet.insert`/`SortedMap` on struct element/key types error 'no handler for method insert on variable s (method dispatch fell through)'. SEPARATELY, the comparison operators `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=` on a `#[derive(Ord)]` struct are a HARD TYPE ERROR on BOTH surfaces ('operator Lt is not defined for operands of type Struct and Struct' under run; 'Unsupported struct binary op: Lt' under build), so `#[derive(Ord)]` on a struct today wires up no usable ordering operator at all — only sort_by(comparator->Ordering) works end-to-end for struct element ordering. The 'use sort_by for other element types' wording implies sort() is INTENDED to honor an element's Ord, so struct/enum element sort() + SortedSet/SortedMap struct keys are the gap; whether direct struct `<` should also lower (vs. being sort_by/.cmp-only by design) is an open design question worth resolving alongside. Related: B-2026-07-03-6 (interp silent version). Repros: n4 (sort build error), n10 (struct `<` hard error), n11 (SortedSet.insert no handler). FIXED (ba67416e sort + 22705148 operators + 31280a03 parity-gate). Extended the recursive karac_cmp_<T> family (emit_cmp_fn_for_type_expr) to named user structs (Body::Tuple template on the struct LLVM layout, DECLARATION field order) and enums (order by variant DISCRIMINANT = tag@field0 = declaration order, then active-variant payload fields @ LLVM index start_word+1 — tuple/struct/unit incl. scalar-in-payload-word loads); cmp_fn_in_progress guards self-recursion (S{next:Vec[S]}→unorderable, not infinite compile recursion). This lights up Vec[Struct/Enum].sort(). Separately the `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=` operators now lower: typecheck admission (infer_binary requires PartialOrd/Ord on struct/enum operands, closing a looseness where ANY struct `<` was silently admitted) + interp arm (value_compare) + codegen compile_ordered_user_cmp (resolve type name via type_name_of_expr/enum_name_of_expr for bare Enum.Variant literals, call karac_cmp, compare i64 to 0). PARITY GATE (31280a03): emitting the comparator unconditionally broke run==build — test_e2e_vec_sort_unordered_element_still_rejected (non-Ord struct sort must error) AND, worse, Option[i64]<Option[i64] / Ordering<Ordering TYPECHECK (derive Ord) and the interp arm ordered them via value_compare, but codegen can't emit a comparator for a generic enum's TypeParam payload / a baked prelude enum absent from program.items → run silently succeeded while build errored (typecheck gate is useless for parity because karac run executes PAST typecheck errors). Fixed with ONE opt-in predicate applied IDENTICALLY on both surfaces: codegen ord_orderable_types (register_ord_orderable_types from the user program's #[derive(Ord/PartialOrd)] items + user impl Ord/PartialOrd) gating emit_cmp_fn_for_struct/enum, and interp aggregate_is_orderable mirroring it (NON-generic, NON-stdlib user struct/enum deriving Ord/PartialOrd — generic_params.is_empty() + !defining_stdlib_origin are load-bearing: exclude Option/Result AND Ordering/MemoryOrdering). SUB-PART 2 (SortedSet/SortedMap struct KEYS) is NOT a struct-ordering gap — the whole sorted-container codegen backend is interpreter-only in v1 (no runtime B-tree), the pre-existing tracked limitation B-2026-06-20-5, independent of key type. Both engines are STRUCTURAL (ignore a user's hand-written impl Ord body; they agree with EACH OTHER, just not with a custom Ord — separate known limitation). Tests: interpreter test_ordered_operators_on_derived_ord_struct_and_enum + test_struct_enum_ordering..., codegen e2e_struct_sort/e2e_enum_sort/e2e_ordered_operators_on_derived_ord_struct_and_enum, par_codegen test_e2e_auto_par_struct_enum_sort_declaration_order/test_e2e_auto_par_ordered_operators_struct_enum. Green: interpreter 1092, typechecker 1870, codegen 2006, par_codegen 149, non-llvm 7291; fmt+clippy(llvm) clean.

Trait DEFAULT METHODS are not inherited/dispatched onto implementing types: a method with a default body in the trait cannot be called on an implementor unless the impl RE-implements it. design.md intends this feature (line 471 'optional default method implementations'; the cross-trait default-body section at ~3427; default bodies are effect-checked at ~6944) and the typechecker DOES type-check default method BODIES (Self-as-typeparam, self.method() intra-body dispatch — tests at typechecker.rs ~7959/7982/8818), but the default is never registered as a callable method on the impl target. Repro g3 (pure default, empty impl): trait Greet { fn hello(self)->i64 { 42 } } struct C {} impl Greet for C {} ; c.hello() -> typecheck 'no method hello on type C' / interp 'method hello not found on type C (no interpreter dispatch arm)'. Repro g1 (default calling a required method): trait Bump { fn base(self)->i64; fn bumped(self)->i64 { self.base()+1 } } impl Bump for C { fn base(self)->i64 { self.v } } ; c.bumped() fails identically. Copying the default body verbatim into the impl (g2) makes it work, confirming it's the inheritance/resolution that's missing, not the body. Consistent across BOTH surfaces (typecheck hard error under build; interp runtime no-dispatch-arm under run) — a missing feature, not a run/build divergence. NOT narrow-width-specific (repros with i64). Fix spans method resolution: when a method isn't found as an inherent/impl method on T but a trait Tr that T implements declares that method WITH a default body, dispatch to the default with Self=T (typechecker method-lookup + interpreter eval_method_call dispatch + codegen synthesize the default as a `T.method` fn, reusing make_impl_method_function). Surfaced probing narrow-width x trait (trait default returning u8), but general. FIXED (6d488e58): pre-resolve desugar pass `synthesize_trait_default_methods` (src/desugar.rs) copies each non-overridden default-bodied trait method (converted TraitMethod->Function) into every `impl Tr for T` block, so all phases see it as an ordinary impl method (the form that already worked end-to-end). Scoped to user-declared NON-generic traits; generic-trait defaults guarded out (revert cleanly to 'no method', tracked as B-2026-07-03-10). Tests: typechecker trait_default_method_callable_on_implementor, codegen e2e e2e_trait_default_methods_dispatch_on_implementor. Suites green: typechecker 1863 / interpreter 1083 / codegen 1983 / par_codegen 142 / all non-llvm; fmt+clippy clean.

fix: dda5d5de
title: FIXED (dda5d5de): A generic `Slice[T]` by-value param called with a Vec arg fails codegen module verification: `fn gfirst[T](s: Slice[T]) -> T { s[0] }; gfirst(myvec)` emits `call i64 @gfirst({ptr,i64,i64} %a)` against a declared `{ptr,i64}` Slice header — the Vec-to-Slice header coercion is missing at the generic-mono by-value Slice-param call site. The NON-generic form `fn sfirst(s: Slice[i64])` called with a Vec works (the coercion fires in the non-generic direct-call path), and `mut Slice[T]` generic params already synthesize the header (slice 8z); only the by-value `Slice[T]` generic mono is unhandled. `karac check` clean, interpreter correct. Surfaced probing S6b-1's Vec[T] element-collision fix (p7_slice_coerce.kara); distinct from that element-binding bug (B-2026-07-02-41) — this is the arg ABI coercion, not element inference. Route the by-value Slice[T] mono arg through the same `coerce_to_slice` header synthesis the mut-Slice path uses. FIX: compile_generic_call's direct-call arg loop now consults fn_param_slice_elem[mangled] (populated by declare_mono_function via extract_slice_elem_type, element T resolved through the active type_subst) and runs coerce_to_slice for by-value Slice[T] params -- the same header synthesis the non-generic path and the mut-Slice state-machine path already used. Tests: e2e_generic_by_value_slice_param_coercion (codegen, seq) + test_e2e_auto_par_generic_by_value_slice_param (par_codegen). Surfaced two tangential pre-existing gaps ledgered as B-2026-07-03-21 and -22.

fix: 2ddfa564
title: Follow-on to B-2026-07-03-8: trait default methods on GENERIC traits are not inherited onto implementors. The `synthesize_trait_default_methods` desugar pass copies a default body verbatim into `impl Tr for T`, but when the trait is generic (`trait Box[U] { fn get(self)->U; fn twice(self)->U { self.get() } }`) the copied `-> U` / body references the trait's own type param `U`, out of scope in the impl (`Box[i64]`) -> resolver 'undefined type U'. The pass therefore GUARDS OUT generic traits (`t.generic_params.is_some()`), leaving them at the pre-fix 'no method' error (no regression, no confusing new error). Correct fix: substitute the impl's trait-args (from `imp.trait_name` PathExpr generic_args, positional against the trait's generic_param_names) through the copied method's param types, return type, and body type-expressions before splicing. Repro e4: trait Box2[T]{fn get(self)->T; fn twice(self)->T{self.get()}} impl Box2[i64] for W{fn get(self)->i64{self.v}} ; w.twice() -> 'no method twice on type W'.

fix: db020ee6
title: FIXED (db020ee6): PRE-EXISTING (surfaced while verifying B-2026-07-03-8; confirmed still open after the S6b TypeExpr-level mono work of B-2026-07-02-41): codegen does not dispatch a trait method called through a GENERIC TYPE-PARAMETER BOUND. `fn use_it[X: Named](x: X) -> i64 { x.tag() }` fails `karac build` with 'codegen: no handler for method tag on variable x (method dispatch fell through)' while `karac run` executes correctly (7). Confirmed NOT specific to default methods and NOT to narrow width: reproduces with an EXPLICITLY implemented method (e3b: trait Named{fn tag(self)->i64;} impl Named for C{fn tag(self)->i64{7}} fn use_it[X: Named](x: X)->i64{x.tag()}) — codegen's method-call lowering has no arm for a receiver whose type is a bound generic param; it needs monomorphization to bind X to the concrete impl type and dispatch to `<ConcreteType>.tag` (same mono family as B-2026-07-02-41/42). The typechecker resolves it fine (dispatch_typeparam_receiver_method); only codegen falls through. Run/build divergence (build refuses, no miscompile). Repro e3b. FIX: threads a name-level type_subst_names (X->concrete) parallel to the LLVM type_subst; mono param prologue registers a bound-generic receiver under its concrete impl type so inferred_receiver_type resolves X.tag->C.tag, and record_var_type_name resolves any generic-param-named binding centrally. Also closed 3 coupled gaps: (a) mangle collision (all user structs lower to opaque "struct" token so use_it$A/use_it$B shared one symbol -> per-mono concrete-name mangle axis for USER structs/enums, builtins keep $struct); (b) let b=w.bump() (-> Self through bound) fell to the HashMap-order LLVM-shape reverse-lookup in stmts.rs -> added a MethodCall ast_hint arm resolving via type_name_of_expr; (c) narrow-width generic return split out as B-2026-07-03-17. 3 codegen E2E + 1 LSan-clean memory_sanitizer test.

Follow-on to B-2026-07-03-6: interpreter struct/enum ordering in value_compare is by ALPHABETICAL field/variant name, not derived-`Ord` DECLARATION order. This is correct for membership/dedup/count (the data-loss bug is fixed) but the observed SEQUENCE of `Vec[Struct].sort()` / `SortedSet`/`SortedMap` iteration can differ from a Rust-like derived Ord: a struct `{ width, height }` sorts by height-then-width, and — more visibly — an enum `Priority { Low, Med, High }` sorts alphabetically (High < Low < Med) instead of Low < Med < High. value_compare (and OrdValue::cmp, called inside BTreeMap with no interpreter handle) cannot reach the struct field / enum variant declaration order held in typecheck_result.{struct_info,enum_info}. Correct fix needs that order at the comparison point: either store it on the Value at construction (struct fields in declaration order / an ordered map; a variant discriminant index on EnumVariant) or thread a type-order registry to value_compare. Low severity: no data loss, and there is no user-facing struct/enum `<` operator today (a hard type error — see B-2026-07-03-7), so no ordering contract is broken; matters mainly when a user reads the sort/iteration sequence or when codegen later implements struct/enum ordering and must agree. FIXED (9bc8e762): a per-thread declaration-order registry (src/interpreter/type_order.rs: struct name→field→idx, enum name→variant→idx, enum::variant→field→idx) built from TypeCheckResult.{struct_info,enum_info} (both Vec, source order) and installed in Interpreter::new — the universal chokepoint every eval path funnels through, INCLUDING each par{} branch (constructs its own Interpreter::new on its spawned thread), so the thread-local is present on every thread reaching value_compare with no RAII guard and no cross-thread propagation. value_compare/OrdValue::cmp read it via type_order::current() (clone the Rc out, hold no RefCell borrow across the recursive compare); absent registry → alphabetical fallback, so the no-data-loss guarantee stays unconditional. Struct fields, enum variant index, and struct-variant payload fields all order by declaration index now. Test: interpreter test_struct_enum_ordering_is_declaration_order_not_alphabetical (Vec.sort value_compare path + SortedSet OrdValue::cmp-inside-BTreeMap path). interpreter 1092 green.

fix: 13cbc81e
title: Interpreter: a `mut ref` SCALAR parameter FORWARDED unmarked into a nested/recursive call did not propagate the callee's mutation back to the caller — a `mut ref i64` accumulator threaded down a recursion read 0. The tree-walk interpreter's copy-in-copy-out (CICO) writeback (eval_call.rs) keyed ONLY on the call-site `mut` marker, but per design.md § Call-site mutation markers an already-in-scope `mut ref` binding FORWARDS WITHOUT a marker, so the chain broke: inner callee mutated its own frame's copy, intermediate frames never copied back. Direct `main` -> `inc(mut t)` (marked) worked; `wrap(x: mut ref i64){ inc(x); }` and any recursion did not. Run/build divergence: correct under `karac build` (codegen has full aliasing), 0 under `karac run`. FIXED (13cbc81e): key CICO writeback on the callee's DECLARED param mode too (TypeKind::MutRef/MutSlice, via new interpreter helper `fn_param_mut_ref_flags`), so a forwarded `mut ref` identifier arg writes back regardless of the marker. Surfaced by #52 marker_arrays.kara (all-zeros counts under run). Repro: fn inc(x: mut ref i64){x=x+1i64;} fn wrap(x: mut ref i64){inc(x);} fn main(){let mut t:i64=0; wrap(mut t); println(t);} -> 0, want 1. Tests: interpreter test_scalar_mut_ref_writeback_through_forwarded_call, test_scalar_mut_ref_accumulator_through_recursion.

fix: 13cbc81e
title: Auto-par: the reduction recognizer accepted a `+` reduction whose per-iteration delta RECURSES into the enclosing function (`if legal { total = total + count(...deeper...) }`, a backtracking counter). The reduction is arithmetically valid, but parallelizing it opens a fresh nested parallel region at EVERY recursion level; the fan-out compounds into runaway task nesting that exhausts the stack — SIGBUS (exit 138) at depth, with correct output surviving only for tiny inputs (n<=6 fine, n>=9 crashes). Default-auto-par-only: `karac run` and `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build` both correct. FIXED (13cbc81e): concurrency.rs `recognize_reductions` declines a loop whose body directly recurses into its own function, via new comprehensive walker `call_graph::block_calls_function` (reuses the callee collector with a singleton `known` set); the loop falls back to the correct sequential lowering. Direct self-recursion is the demonstrated + common case; transitive/mutual recursion through a helper is a known residual gap. Surfaced by #52 bitmask_count.kara / symmetry.kara (SIGBUS under default build). Repro: the standard bitmask N-Queens counter `fn count(n,row,cols,d1,d2)->i64` swept to n=11 under `karac build`. Tests: concurrency test_reduction_rejects_recursive_self_call_in_body, test_reduction_still_recognized_with_nonrecursive_call_in_body. FOLLOW-ON (shallow-depth-parallel-reduction, docs/spikes/): the conservative compile-time decline was REPLACED by a runtime fork-depth cap (`KARAC_PAR_MAX_FORK_DEPTH`, default 1, thread-local `PAR_REDUCE_DEPTH` in `karac_par_reduce`). Recursive-delta reductions are now recognized and lowered again; only the OUTERMOST level fans out, deeper levels run inline — safe (nesting bounded by a constant, no stack blowup) AND useful (a single N-Queens count parallelizes ~9.5x). `call_graph::block_calls_function` and the recognizer decline were removed. Env reads on the hot path are OnceLock-cached to avoid a per-recursion-node syscall storm.

A GENERIC impl/trait METHOD called on a CONCRETE receiver is not codegen-monomorphized: `fn apply[A](ref self, init: A, f: Fn(A, i64) -> A) -> A { f(init, self.v) }` on a concrete `One`, called `o.apply(2, |a,x| a+x)`, runs correctly under `karac run` (42) but `karac build` dies loud: 'codegen: no handler for method apply on variable o (method dispatch fell through)'. Reproduces with a HAND-WRITTEN generic impl method (no trait, no default body) so it is pre-existing and independent of the S6b-2 default-body inheritance work (B-2026-07-03-10) that surfaced it — the substituted default `fn apply[A]` inherits the same wall. This is S6-pre finding 2b and the S6b-3 slice: codegen's compile_method_call has no arm to bind a method's OWN generic params (`A`) to concrete arg types and mangle a per-call mono. Distinct from B-2026-07-03-11 (dispatch through a generic type-param BOUND — receiver type is the generic param; here the receiver is concrete and the METHOD is generic). Blocks the real Reduce `fold[A]` default. Probed p4_generic_method_default.kara.

fix: 839beaea
title: SILENT MISCOMPILE: immediate field access on the result of a call that returns an aggregate (struct) — `f().field` — reads 0/default under `karac build`, while `karac run` is correct. General: reproduces with a free fn `fn make() -> Cnt { Cnt { n: 7 } }` and `make().n` -> build prints 0 (run 7); with an instance method `m.go().n`; with a static assoc fn `Cnt.zero()`; owned or ref self; ALL fields (offset-independent: `P{a,b}` -> `make().a`/`make().b` both 0). NOT f-string specific (`make().n + 100` = 100 under build). The workaround is to bind first: `let x = make(); x.field` builds correctly (7), and `let c = make(); c.n` at the call site is fine too — so the aggregate return value materializes correctly; only the direct-field-access-on-call-temporary lowering drops it (likely reads the field off a zeroed/uninitialized spill slot instead of the call's sret aggregate). Pre-existing, unrelated to traits/generics; surfaced probing S6b-2's `g.make().n` / `g.seed().n` default-method calls (the S6b-2 codegen test binds the result first to sidestep it). High severity — extremely common pattern, silent wrong value, run/build divergence. Probed isoH/isoP/isoP2/iso2* .kara. FIXED as a DUPLICATE of B-2026-07-03-3 (identical root cause, found independently while probing S6b-2 generic default methods): type_name_of_expr had no Call/MethodCall arm, so field_index_for returned None and compile_field_access's generic tail emitted the i64 0 placeholder instead of an extractvalue at the field's index. Resolved on main by 839beaea, which adds Call/MethodCall arms to type_name_of_expr (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs) that resolve a call's static return-type name via fn_return_type_names -- free fns key on the bare callee, static assoc fns on the 2-segment Type.method Path, method calls resolve the receiver recursively. Verified every B-16 shape now builds==runs: free-fn make().n=7, multi-field make_p().a/.b=3/9, static assoc Cnt.zero().n/Cnt.forty().n=0/40, ref-self g.goref().n=7, plain non-f-string print(make().n)=7, and make().n + 100=107. Added complementary codegen e2e regression test e2e_call_result_field_access_assoc_and_ref_self (tests/codegen.rs) locking in the assoc-fn / ref-self / multi-field / plain-print shapes that the sibling e2e_chained_call_struct_field_access did not cover; fmt + clippy clean, codegen + memory_sanitizer suites green.

fix: db020ee6
title: FIXED (db020ee6): a GENERIC function with a NON-generic NARROW return type mis-lowered under karac build (surfaced while probing B-2026-07-03-11; reproduces with NO trait/bound, so pre-existing and independent). `fn narrow[T](x: T) -> u8 { 255 }` (a) failed module verification -- the mono tail-return in compile_mono_function emitted `ret i64 255` into an i8-returning fn because it skipped coerce_to_current_ret_type (the non-generic compile_function path applies it); and (b) once coerced, printed 255u8 as -1 -- expr_is_unsigned_int's Call arm found no fn_return_type_names entry for the un-declared generic fn (generic fns are registered in generic_fns, never declared) and defaulted to signed. karac run was correct both ways. FIX: mono tail-return now calls coerce_to_current_ret_type (truncates to the declared narrow width, no-op for matching/non-scalar returns); generic fns register their CONCRETE return-type name in fn_return_type_names at setup (skipping a generic `-> T` return). Covered by e2e_generic_fn_narrow_width_return.

S6b-4a operator-on-bounded-T: `a OP b` on a type parameter bounded by the stdlib operator trait for that operator (`+`->Add, `-`->Sub, `*`->Mul, `/`->Div, `%`->Rem, unary `-`->Neg) was a HARD typecheck error under `karac build` ('arithmetic operator requires numeric type, found T') and only a warning-then-run under `karac run` -- the run/build divergence that blocked the stdlib Reduce fold-based defaults (whose bodies fold with +/* over a bounded element type). Reproduces with a free fn `fn add_gen[T: Add](a: T, b: T) -> T { a + b }` (build-rejected, run-warns-then-30) AND with a generic-trait default body `fn sum2(ref self) -> T { self.a() + self.b() }` on `trait Foldy[T: Add + Mul]`. FIXED (5c761a6e): PURE TYPECHECK admission mirroring the pre-existing `T: Numeric` arm -- infer_binary (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs) admits the operator when the operand type param carries the operator trait for THIS operator (arithmetic_operator_trait(op)), yielding result T; the unary-'-' check likewise admits a `T: Neg` bound. SOUND with no check-passes/build-fails gap because user operator-trait impls are FORBIDDEN (resolver: 'operator traits are stdlib-only'), so every instantiation of such a T is a primitive numeric / String (Add) / distinct-numeric that codegen already lowers for the operator post-monomorphization (verified the T: Numeric arithmetic path already builds+runs, so codegen is unchanged). type_param_has_trait_bound accepts BOTH operand spellings: Type::TypeParam (a free-fn-bound param) AND a bare Type::Named{name,args:[]} whose name is an in-scope type param (a `-> T` method result / `let x: T` local inside a generic-trait default body -- the Named-vs-TypeParam trap), by consulting enclosing_bounds (the authoritative in-scope type-param set). Wrong-trait (`-` under T: Add) and unbounded-T arithmetic stay rejected. A/B-verified run == KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 == default-auto-par build for free-fn (i64/f64/String/Neg) and generic-trait-default (+/*) shapes. NOTE: the feat commit 5c761a6e message references this as B-2026-07-03-17; renumbered to -18 here because a parallel session landed a different B-2026-07-03-17 (generic-fn narrow-return mis-lowering, db020ee6) concurrently. Tests: typechecker operator_on_operator_trait_bounded_type_param_admitted + operator_on_wrong_or_missing_trait_bound_rejected; codegen e2e e2e_operator_on_operator_trait_bounded_type_param.

S6b-4: a user `impl Reduce[T] for MyType` could not inherit a DEFAULT method from the BAKED stdlib `Reduce[T]` trait. synthesize_trait_default_methods (the S6b-2/-3 splice pass) only consulted traits declared in the USER program, but baked stdlib traits live in crate::prelude::STDLIB_PROGRAMS, not program.items -- so there was nothing to splice even once Reduce grew a default body. FIXED (c0a83c33): extracted the per-trait default-method collection into collect_trait_defaults_from_items and call it for the user program AND every STDLIB_PROGRAMS program (user-first, entry().or_insert, so a same-named user trait shadows); clear stdlib_origin on each spliced copy so it is resolved/typechecked/ownership-checked/codegen'd as ordinary user code (a stdlib-origin body is otherwise skipped like the never-checked baked impl bodies). Reduce[T] gains its first DEFAULT method `fn range(ref self) -> T { self.max() - self.min() }`; a CONCRETE `impl Reduce[i64]/[f64] for MyType` inherits .range() with the concrete T substituted, so self.max()-self.min() lowers as native T-T. Only Reduce.range has a stdlib default body today, so the change touches only user Reduce impls. A/B-verified run==KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0==default-auto-par build (Trio range=6, FDuo range=7.5). RESIDUAL (ledgered): generic user impls blocked on B-2026-07-03-20; builtin Column/Tensor do NOT inherit range (their #[compiler_builtin] impls are in STDLIB_PROGRAMS, not rewritten by the splice) -- a separate axis; fold/product/Option-forms still need a fold[A] primitive that would change the required-method set. Test: codegen e2e test_e2e_stdlib_reduce_default_method_inherited_by_user_impl.

FIXED (a0206b1f): a BOUND on a generic impl's own type param (`impl[T: Sub] Pair[T] { ... }`) broke method resolution inside AND outside the impl under `karac build`: self's type resolves to the bare `Pair` (no args), so `self.other_method()` -- and even an external `p.gap()` -- reported 'no method X on type Pair'. UNBOUNDED generic impls (`impl[T] Pair[T]`) work fine; the SOLE trigger is a bound (`T: Sub`, `T: Numeric`, ...) on the impl's generic param. Reproduces with a plain INHERENT impl -- NO traits/defaults/stdlib. Run/build divergence: `karac run` executes past the warning and prints the CORRECT value; `build` hard-errors. ROOT: impl_bounds_discharge (src/typechecker/env.rs) dropped a candidate whenever it could not PROVE the impl's bound -- `self` has the bare target type (no arg to substitute the bound against), and a `Pair[T]` receiver (outer generic param) substitutes to a Type::TypeParam not in the impl table, so bound_satisfied returned false. Both are UNDECIDABLE not FALSE; the concrete instantiation / enclosing bound discharges them. FIX: make discharge permissive for a missing OR Type::TypeParam substitution, in both the inline-bound and where-clause arms; a concrete arg that genuinely fails its bound still drops the candidate (conditional-impl disambiguation unchanged, 6 typechecker conditional-impl tests green). Directly unblocks GENERIC user impls of stdlib Reduce (`impl[T: Sub] Reduce[T] for Pair[T]` inherits+resolves the spliced `range` default, i64->7 run==build). Residual: NON-i64 (f64) element still miscompiles via the separate generic struct-literal arg-inference bug B-2026-07-03-23. Tests: typechecker bounded_generic_impl_methods_resolve, codegen e2e test_e2e_bounded_generic_impl_method_call (i64). Surfaced probing S6b-4.

A narrow-width (u8/u16/u32) local whose RHS is a generic call loses its UNSIGNED-ness when the binding lands in an auto-par PAR GROUP: `fn vfirst[T](v: ref Vec[T]) -> T { v[0] }; let a = geti(); let b = geti(); let u: u8 = vfirst(vu); println(u)` prints -1 (signed i8 view of 255) under the DEFAULT/auto-par build (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=1), while the sequential build (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0) and interp print 255. The VALUE is correct (0xFF bits); only PRINT signedness is wrong. Root: par_blocks.rs return-slot materialization (the post-join `for slot in &return_slots` loop) registers `variables` and `vec_elem_types` for grouped-let bindings but NEVER `var_type_names` (nor any signedness marker), so expr_is_unsigned_int falls back to signed for the reconstructed binding. The annotation `let u: u8` IS honored sequentially (registered at the let site) but that registration is lost across the par-group slot transfer -- the ReturnSlot carries binding_name + llvm_ty (i8) but not the source signedness. NOT slice-specific (reproduces with a `ref Vec[T]` generic) and NOT caused by B-2026-07-03-9 (that fix only made the Slice variant reachable). Surfaced probing B-2026-07-03-9. Fix: thread the source narrow-int surface name / signedness into ReturnSlot and register var_type_names in the post-join materialization (or consult pattern_binding_types by the binding's span). FIX 9f986336: thread the binding's annotation type name into ReturnSlot (`let_binding_annotation_type_name`) and re-register `var_type_names` in BOTH post-join materialization loops (auto-par dispatch in stmts.rs + explicit `par` blocks in par_blocks.rs). Verified interp/seq/auto-par for u8/u16/u32 (plain + f-string) plus a signed i8 control that stays -1 (no over-correction).

A generic `-> T` return whose T is bound from a Slice/container ELEMENT is not resolved to its concrete type at the f-string format site: `fn gsum[T](s: Slice[T]) -> T { s[0] }; let vs: Vec[String] = [..]; println(f"{gsum(vs)}")` prints the String's heap POINTER as an integer (e.g. 4296181632) instead of the string, on BOTH the sequential and default builds (`karac run` is correct). The DIRECT-param form `fn gid[T](x: T) -> T; f"{gid(s)}"` with a String arg works -- the sole trigger is T being bound via a container element (Slice[T]/Vec[T] param) rather than a bare `x: T` param. The f-string interpolation's type resolution for the call result doesn't recover T=String when T came from the arg's element type, so it formats the value as a scalar. Distinct from B-2026-07-03-9 (arg ABI coercion, fixed) -- this is the RETURN-type resolution at the use/format site. Surfaced probing B-2026-07-03-9 (a `f"{gsum(vs)}"` case, replaced with `glen(vs)` in the landed test). Also a likely sibling of the narrow-signedness use-site gap B-2026-07-03-21 (both are 'generic -> T result type unknown at the use site'). Fix: resolve a container-element-bound T at the format/print site (extend the generic-call return-type-name resolution the way B-2026-07-03-17 did for concrete generic returns). ROOT CAUSE (not the format site as first hypothesized): monomorphization subst inference never bound T=String -- `augment_subst_from_arg_elem_types`'s Slice arm keyed only on `slice_elem_types`, but a Vec/Array arg registers its element in `vec_elem_types` / the `variables` array slot, so T stayed unbound and defaulted to i64; the mono then compiled `s[0]` as an i64 read and returned the String's heap pointer. The i64-element cases masked it (unbound T defaults to i64).
