FIX b5432340: route the Slice arm through `infer_elem_from_source` (unifies Slice/Vec/Array element resolution), the mono-side twin of the B-2026-07-03-9 by-value arg coercion. Verified interp/seq/auto-par; macOS ASan + Linux LSan clean (s[0] clones the String element).

FIXED (four layers, 7ab01d78 typecheck + 08ee105d/168e2e37 codegen): a generic struct with an inline type-param field (`struct Box[T]{v:T}`, even unbounded / no impl) lost its type arg, so codegen defaulted the element to i64 and mis-read non-i64 fields. `let b = Box{v:2.5}; println(f"{b.v}")` printed 4612811918334230528 (2.5's f64 bits as i64) under build, 2.5 under run; a by-value method on such a struct HARD-crashed the build (Module verification failed). ROOT+FIX: (1) typechecker infers a struct literal's generic args (infer_struct_literal solves them from the field values via fresh metavars -> Box[f64]); (2) field access substitutes the receiver's args into the field type (infer_field_access / field_type_with_receiver_args -> b.v : f64); (3) codegen builds a per-instantiation LLVM struct type (Box[f64] -> {double}) via mono_struct_type wired into llvm_type_for_type_expr's Path arm + compile_struct_init (LLVM interns literal struct types, no cache; struct_generic_params map added); (4) methods on a generic struct monomorphize by the RECEIVER's instantiation -- make_generic_impl_method_function types self as the impl target Box[T] + merges impl generic params, registered into generic_fns and dispatched via compile_generic_call binding the impl T explicitly from the receiver's recorded instantiation (enum_inst_type_from_span / enum_inst_var_types). Covers f64/i64/String elements, field store, two-field arithmetic, function ABI, Vec of a generic struct, and ref-self / by-value-self / bounded-impl methods; A/B-verified run == KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 == build. This makes the f64 arm of generic Reduce impls (Pair[f64].range()) work (S6b-4c). Renumbered from B-21 (parallel autopar collision; the B-20 fix commit a0206b1f message reads B-21). Gates: codegen 1997+2 new, par 145, typechecker 1870, interpreter 1086, ASAN 495, Linux LSan 495; fmt+clippy clean. Tests: codegen e2e test_e2e_generic_struct_field_monomorphizes_by_element + test_e2e_generic_struct_method_monomorphizes_by_receiver.

Follow-on to B-2026-07-03-5: a generic BOUND over a PRIMITIVE trait impl (`fn f[T: Dbl](x: T) -> T { x.dbl() }` called with a u8/i32/f64) now TYPECHECKS (primitive impls register after B-5) but mis-dispatches at RUNTIME on BOTH surfaces. (1) INTERP: inside the generic fn `x` has runtime value `Value::Int`/`Value::Float` (width-erased to i64/f64) and the receiver type at the `x.dbl()` call site is a TypeParam, so `method_callee_type_name(TypeParam)` is None and NO `method_callee_types` entry is recorded -> dispatch falls back to the erased 'i64.dbl'/'f64.dbl' key and errors "method 'dbl' not found on type 'i64' (no interpreter dispatch arm)" for every width whose impl isn't keyed i64/f64. (2) CODEGEN: monomorphization dispatches the WRONG primitive impl when MULTIPLE impls of the trait exist -- `dbl_it(c)` with c:i32 called the i8 impl (integer-overflow panic); a SINGLE primitive impl monomorphizes correctly. This is the primitive analog of B-2026-07-03-11 (generic-bound dispatch for USER types via type_subst_names). Direct-call `a.dbl()` is fully fixed (B-5). Fix: interp -- thread the concrete arg type into type-param-receiver dispatch (key on the caller's recorded generic instantiation rather than the erased runtime value type); codegen -- make primitive-impl mono dispatch select by the concrete bound type NAME (mirror the type_subst_names name-aware dispatch/mangle B-11 added for user types). FIX d15c8372 BOTH surfaces: (codegen) the mono mangle now appends the concrete primitive NAME from subst_names — narrow ints widen to i64 so the LLVM token collided (f$i64 for every width), the second mono reused the first's body; name-append (primitive analog of B-11's struct/enum fix) makes each width a distinct correctly-dispatching mono. (interp) new `method_typeparam_receiver` typecheck table records the receiver's type-param name (expr_types[receiver.span] is clobbered by the method result type via MethodCall.span==receiver.span); the interpreter resolves it through type_subs_stack to the concrete instantiation, preferred over the width-erased Value key so f32 doesn't fall into an existing f64 impl. Also repaired a B-5 routing regression (see B-2026-07-03-5). Verified all 8 scalar widths interp/seq/auto-par; user-type generic-bound dispatch unregressed.

`.iter().map(f).collect()` into a `Vec` FAILS under `karac build` while working under `karac run` — a run/build divergence on a book-documented idiom (ch10-closures-and-iterators shows `iter.map(|n| n*2).collect()`). MINIMAL: `let d: Vec[i64] = s.iter().map(|x| x*2i64).collect();` prints 4 under run, but build errors `codegen failed: no handler for method 'collect' on non-identifier receiver (method dispatch fell through; this is a codegen bug)`. Codegen only handles `collect` on an IDENTIFIER receiver (already-materialized Vec → clone, method_call.rs:288) and on `chars().collect()` (method_call.rs:3451); a lazy adaptor chain whose collect-receiver is a `map`/`filter` MethodCall (not an identifier, not `chars`) falls through to the dispatch-fail error. Gap is general to any non-identifier/non-`chars` collect receiver (confirmed for `.iter().map(f).collect()`). Surfaced while probing the collection-capacity-presizing spike (narrow-A): `.map().collect()` is the highest-value pre-sizing target but doesn't compile at all under codegen, so the correctness fix (implement the adaptor-chain → Vec lowering) MUST precede any pre-sizing — closes spike S2, and the lowering should reserve the source length while materializing. from_slice already pre-sizes (measured 16.7ms/1M vs Vec.new()+push 74.8ms); this idiom is the open one. FIXED 009fd479: `try_compile_iter_adaptor_collect_to_vec` (method_call.rs) desugars a `map`/`filter` chain to a `for` loop that pushes each surviving/transformed element onto a fresh `Vec`, reusing the supported constructs (for/closure-inline/if/push/block-move-out); output elem type from the collect expr's `owned_temp_drops` entry; the base-most closure param IS the loop var so a heap element keeps its type (`.map(|w| w.len())` over `Vec[String]`). A terminal `map` pushes its value directly — an intermediate `let x = f"…"` routes through the staged-f-string-accumulator path that double-frees the built String once it is also pushed. Verified run==build across POD/filter/filter+map/map+map/type-changing-map(Vec[String])/heap-source; ASAN+LSan clean on a looped heap test. RESIDUAL (see B-2026-07-03-29): non-`map`/`filter` adaptors into collect and a non-terminal f-string `map` still fail loudly under build.

fix: b4dd3ba8
title: Matching a non-Copy field (or indexed-element field) of a BORROWED `mut ref self` receiver was treated as consuming `self`, so a later whole-`self` use (`match self.tokens[self.pos].token {..}; self.advance()`) read as use-after-move under `karac check`/multi-file `karac build`. `param_types_for_function` left the borrowed `self` ABSENT, so `classify_identifier` fell back to `expr_types` = the bare (non-Copy) Self type and classified `self` as consumable; regressed by 5426bbd1 (projection-aware partial-move tracking, B-2026-07-02-25) which began recording `self.field` consumes. This shape pervades the self-hosted parser, so it reddened all three selfhost parser oracles (selfhost_parser{,_types,_items}) on main while selfhost_lexer stayed green. Fixed by recording a borrowed `self` (`ref self`/`mut ref self`) as a `Type::Ref` (Copy) in `param_types_for_function` so it classifies as a Read; owned `self` left absent so its consume semantics stand. (Renumbered from B-2026-07-03-25 at integration — collided with parallel session ffd50b59.) Regressions: tests/ownership.rs::{test_match_on_borrowed_self_field_does_not_consume_self, test_match_on_owned_self_field_still_consumes}.

An `Option[E]` field where E is a PLAIN (non-`shared`) user enum with a heap payload, dropped undestructured (via a `Some(_)` wildcard match or plain scope-drop), leaks the enum payload's heap buffer — the inline-Option drop path (cf. B-2026-06-10-6, which covered Option[String]/[Vec]/[Map]) does not recurse into a user-enum payload's drop. Minimal repro: `struct A { value: Option[Val] }`, `enum Val { Nothing, Ident(String) }`, Vec[A] consumed -> 360 bytes / 10 allocs leaked under LSan. `Option[shared enum]`, `Option[String]`, `Option[Vec]` are all clean. NON-BLOCKING for self-hosting: every recursive AST enum in the port is `shared`, and AttrArgNode.value is Option[Expr] (shared). FIXED 14d4391e: the destructure leaf of an `Option[<user struct/enum>]` field got no cleanup (`destructure_field_needs_cleanup` excludes Option; whole-struct drop skips Option fields — B-2026-07-03-28). `track_inline_option_agg_payload_var` now registers a tag-guarded `karac_drop_Option_<payload>` (`emit_option_drop_fn` — the same recursive fn the Vec[Option[..]] element path uses, handling the heap-BOXED wide payload) on the leaf when the destructure OWNS the source (fresh temp or moved-in owned binding, never a ref/borrow), paired with a Some-arm tag-zeroing suppressor (`inline_option_agg_payload_vars`) so a Some(v) move-out doesn't double-free. Covers Option[enum] AND Option[struct] payloads, both wildcard-match and plain scope-drop, Vec-sourced and fresh-temp sources. LSan 503/503. RESIDUAL: a Some(v) move-out of a wide/boxed Option-agg payload still leaks the heap box — separate pre-existing bug B-2026-07-03-31 (this fix keeps that path double-free-clean). New tests replace the pinned one: asan_b27_option_enum_undestructured_drop_no_leak / asan_b27_option_struct_undestructured_drop_no_leak.

fix: 7f727aaa
title: RESIDUAL of Facet A after B-2026-07-03-33: an `Option` struct FIELD still leaks its Some-payload on plain/consumed drop when the payload is NOT the inline `{ptr,len,cap}` class B-33 handles — specifically `Option[shared]` (the parser's `AttrArgNode.value: Option[Expr]`, Expr shared) and `Option`s nested inside a `Vec[struct]` field (`AttrNode.args: Vec[AttrArgNode]`). Two coupled pieces remain: (a) `Option[shared]` entry-copy = rc-INC of the inline RC pointer (param_own) + drop = rc-DEC, so an `Option[shared]`-bearing struct becomes copy-supported and its struct-drop can free the Option; (b) element-DEEP entry-copy of a `Vec[struct-with-heap]` field so the deeper element drop (which frees the element struct's Options once (a) lands) stays symmetric with the copy (copy-depth == drop-depth; else a caller-retained Vec[struct] double-frees the shared element payloads). Pinned `asan_attr_node_list_drop_consume_and_plain` leaks 240 B / 6 allocs (down from 1434/36 original, 474/12 after B-30, 240/6 after B-33) = exactly the AttrArgNode name+value Options. `Option[boxed-wide]` and `Option[plain-enum]` (B-27) payloads also stay caller-retains. #[ignore]d pinned test. ATTEMPT 2026-07-03 (reverted, patch saved): tried (Change A) freeing the inline Option[String] in the shared-owning-struct DRAIN emit_nested_struct_shared_rc_decs gated on struct_shared_edges_all_option (all shared edges via Option[shared], excludes direct-shared like Arg{value:Expr}); (Piece 2) emit_option_clone_fn = type-aware deep Option clone (String/Vec deep-copy + Option[shared] rc-inc), the clone peer of emit_option_drop_fn, routed from emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr; (Piece 3) element-DEEP entry-copy of a Vec[shared-owning-struct] field via te_shared_owning_struct. RESULT: full macOS ASAN suite GREEN (no double-free; fixed the consume-path AttrN double-free that Change A alone caused), but LSan REGRESSED the pinned test 240/6 -> 714/18 (new direct string + INDIRECT shared-box leaks). ROOT CAUSE = the entry-copy-vs-move rc-balance: making the struct copy-supported forces a deep entry-copy of AttrNode.args, but for a{}in attrs the shared Val boxes get an extra rc-inc (clone) that the move/consume path never rc-decs (source drop suppressed) -> boxes+strings leak. The copy-supported model assumes caller-retains; the pinned test consumes via move. Closing this needs a move-aware entry-copy OR full consume-site rc-balance for copy-supported shared-owning structs -- an ownership-model change, NOT a contained increment. Patch in session scratchpad b28-residual-attempt.patch. FIXED (Phase 2 of the caller-retains model, 7f727aaa): closed WITHOUT the originally-scoped piece (b) — the pinned test's consume path self-balances (for-loop-consume + destructure-leaf rc-dec) and its plain-drop path is fixed by the combined struct drop. Three changes: (1) field_copy_supported admits an Option[shared] field (via option_inner_shared_type_for_type_expr), so the struct becomes copy-supported and its sibling name:Option[String] gets the OptionInline drop; (2) deep_copy_option_inline_payload_in_place rc-INCs the inline box (word 1, ptrtoint) when Some (rc_inc_option_inline_shared_payload_in_place), the inc peer of emit_nested_struct_shared_rc_decs_ex's Option[shared] rc-dec; (3) track_struct_var registers the COMBINED drop (emit_vec_elem_struct_with_shared_drop_fn = value-drop + shared-field rc-dec walker) for any struct owning shared fields — so a scope-exit drop of an owning struct LOCAL / callee-owned by-value PARAM rc-decs its shared children (the value drop skips them by design), also fixing the pre-existing direct-shared-field struct-LOCAL leak; plus the fresh-temp struct-arg gate (call_dispatch) now recognizes a shared-owning struct (invisible to type_expr_has_drop_heap). Un-ignored asan_attr_node_list_drop_consume_and_plain (240 B/6 -> 0) + new asan_b28_option_shared_and_direct_shared_struct_drop_no_leak. codegen 2040/0, macOS ASAN 521/0, Linux LSan 521/0 (the un-ignored test passes on the authoritative gate). RESIDUALS split to B-2026-07-04-9 (piece (b) proved NOT needed for the port shape but IS needed for entry-copy-then-whole-drop of a Vec[struct] field — a pre-existing double-free; plus the direct-shared FRESH-TEMP arg leak). FIXED.

`<iter>.collect()` under `karac build` rejected (loudly) adaptor chains beyond the `map`/`filter` subset landed in B-2026-07-03-25 (009fd479). FIXED 76be2de2 for the STATEFUL ELEMENT-TYPE-PRESERVING PASSTHROUGH family: `take`, `skip`, `step_by`, `take_while`, `skip_while`, `inspect`. `try_compile_iter_adaptor_collect_to_vec` now peels these too and lowers each to its for-loop equivalent with a pre-loop state var (counter + bound count for the integer-arg adaptors; a `skipping` latch for `skip_while`); the short-circuiting `take`/`take_while` emit an IN-BODY `break` at the adaptor's chain position — AFTER the upstream stages, matching the interpreter's lazy step order (iter_eval.rs): the element that trips exhaustion has run every upstream stage (e.g. a preceding `inspect`) but no downstream one, so `inspect(f).take(2)` fires `f` 3× and `take_while`'s pred runs through the first failing element on BOTH surfaces. The loop var now takes the FIRST param-bearing stage's name (not just steps[0]) so a `.map(|s| s.len())` after a leading count adaptor keeps the heap element type. Verified run==build across every adaptor + mixed chains + interpreter-matching side-effect counts + heap `Vec[String]` sources; `leaks` clean at -O0 incl. the `take`/`take_while` early-break tail drop; codegen 2035/2035, par 153/153. RESIDUAL → B-2026-07-04-2: the multi-source / restructuring adaptors (`enumerate`, `zip`, `chain`, `flat_map`, `chunks`, `windows`, `scan`, `cycle`), a non-single-`Binding` map/filter arg (named-fn `.map(double)`, multi-param/destructuring closure), and the non-terminal-f-string-map carve-out all still fall through to the loud dispatch-fail (no miscompile).

title: A non-shared struct FIELD typed Vec[String] / Vec[Map] / Vec[Set] / Vec[Vec[..]] leaks each element's own heap (String char buffer, Map/Set buckets, inner-Vec buffer) when the owning struct is dropped or destructured. emit_struct_drop_synthesis's VecOrString arm (src/codegen/synth_drop.rs) freed only the outer {ptr,len,cap} buffer: vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr returns None for a DIRECT String/Map/Set element (unlike the top-level FreeVecBuffer drain, which has bespoke inline vec-struct / Map / tuple branches). FIX: (1) synth_drop.rs falls back to the recursive drop family emit_drop_fn_for_type_expr for those element shapes (gated by elem_te_needs_direct_recursive_drain = String/str/Vec/VecDeque/Map/Set); (2) param_own.rs makes the by-value-param entry-copy element-DEEP for exactly those shapes (emit_vecstr_defensive_copy element-deep mode) to keep the copy-depth == drop-depth invariant documented in param_own.rs — else a caller-retained Node{tags:Vec[String]} double-frees the shared element buffers (test asan_by_value_struct_field_moveout). Surfaced building slice 3d-i (AttrNode.path Vec[String]); reduced the pinned attr_node leak 1434/36 -> 474/12 (remainder is Facet A / B-2026-07-03-28). EXCLUDED (still outer-only, tracked): a heap-bearing TUPLE element Vec[(.., String)] (the entry-copy can't deepen a tuple element, so deepening its drop alone would double-free a retained param). Regression tests: asan_struct_vec_string_field_plain_drop_drains_elements, asan_struct_vec_string_field_destructure_consume_clean, asan_struct_vec_map_field_plain_drop_drains_elements. (Renumbered from B-2026-07-03-29 at integration — collided with the parallel collect-adaptor residual entry.)

An `Option[<user enum/struct>]` field DESTRUCTURED into a local (`let A { value } = a`) and then MOVE-matched (`match value { Some(v) => f(v) | v.field, None => 0 }`) LEAKS the payload's inner heap (String/Vec buffer) — ~40 B per move-out, 6/6 in a Vec[A]-consuming loop under LSan/macOS `leaks`. SILENT (correct output; leak only). REVISED ROOT CAUSE (the original 'just free the orphaned box' framing was WRONG and INCOMPLETE): the leak is the payload's INNER heap, not the box, and it fires for BOTH boxed (`Option[Val]`, Val=tag+String>3 words) AND inline (`Option[Inner]`, Inner={String}=3 words) payloads. A plain `Vec[Option[Val]]` move-out (no wrapping struct) is CLEAN — so it is SPECIFIC to the B-2026-07-03-27 destructure-leaf: the `value` binding from `let A { value } = a` is tracked in `inline_option_agg_payload_vars` with a scope-exit `karac_drop_Option_<payload>` (EnumDrop), and the consuming-`Some(v)` suppressor (`suppress_inline_option_agg_payload_cleanup`, control_flow_match.rs) TAG-ZEROES the source to disarm that drop — to avoid a double-free when `v` is MOVED out. BUT under this compiler's CALLER-RETAINS param model (an owned heap enum/struct param is entry-DEEP-COPIED at the callee — the `p14e` copy in param_own.rs), `f(v)` does NOT consume `v`; the callee frees its own copy and the CALLER must free the original `v`. For a NORMAL Option local the source's own scope drop frees it (see clean `use_opt`); for the destructure-leaf the suppressor DISARMS that drop without registering any drop for `v`, so the original inner heap is orphaned. The suppressor is only correct when `v` GENUINELY escapes (return / struct-or-collection literal / outward assign / closure capture) — NOT when it is passed to an entry-copying fn (`f(v)`) or field-read (`v.field`). Freeing the box shell alone (a prototype) removes only the 32 B box leak and leaves the dominant inner-heap leak, so it is INSUFFICIENT. Correct fix needs an ESCAPE-AWARE gate on the suppressor that knows call-args are entry-copied (non-consuming) — i.e. the caller-retains param model, the SAME blocker as [[B-2026-07-03-28]] (getting it wrong the other way DOUBLE-FREES: misclassifying a true escape as non-escape frees the inner twice). Repro: `enum Val{Nothing,Ident(String)} struct A{value:Option[Val]} fn ident_len(v:Val)->i64{match v{Val.Ident(s)=>s.len(),Val.Nothing=>0}} fn use_a(a:A)->i64{let A{value}=a; match value{Some(v)=>ident_len(v),None=>0}}`; consume a Vec[A]. NON-BLOCKING (leak only, double-free-clean). BLOCKED on the caller-retains param model. FIXED (Phase 1 of the caller-retains model, 80229526): the BORROW case only. The use-site consumption classifier (src/codegen/consume_class.rs, `binding_only_borrowed`) now gates `suppress_inline_option_agg_payload_cleanup` via `arm_only_borrows_option_agg_payload`/`block_only_borrows_option_agg_payload` (shared `option_agg_payload_binds` + `collect_pattern_bindings`): the source payload drop is disarmed ONLY when the arm CONSUMES the bound payload, so a borrow-only arm (`Some(v)=>ident_len(v)`/`v.field`) keeps its drop and frees the inner heap. Wired for `match`, `if let`, `while let`; `let else` stays unconditional (bindings escape the analyzable scope). Conservative-default classifier = never a double-free. Regression `asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak` (match+iflet+whilelet, boxed+inline payloads). codegen 2037/0, macOS ASAN 519/0, Linux LSan 519/0. RESIDUAL split off as B-2026-07-04-7: the ESCAPE case (`Some(v)=>v` returning the destructure-leaf payload) still leaks. FIXED.

SILENT wrong-output / crash under `karac build` (correct under `karac run` and `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0`) when an owned `Column` / `DataFrame` / `Tensor` is produced in one AUTO-PAR branch and read after the join. MINIMAL: `fn hd(v: Vec[i64]) -> i64 { v[0] } fn main() { let av: Vec[i64]=[4,2,7,1]; print(hd(av)); let c: Column[i64]=Column.from_vec([5,9,3,1]); print(c.len()); }` — build prints `4` then `0` (c.len()==0, should be 4); element access panics out-of-bounds. Two such producers with a while-loop String-building consumer CRASH (SIGBUS). ROOT CAUSE (corrected — the original `materialize_owned_temp` + staged-String-accumulator suspect was WRONG; the String accumulator and the by-value-temp arg were RED HERRINGS, they only served to make two statements auto-parallelizable): the auto-par analyzer groups the independent read (`hd(av)`) and the `Column`-producing `let` into sibling par branches. The producing branch writes the column control-block pointer into the parent's return slot (`emit_par_branch_fn` slot-write) and THEN ran its queued `FreeColumn` at branch end, freeing the three buffers (data / null-bitmap / control) it had just published. After `karac_par_run` joined, the parent read a DANGLING control block. The branch-side slot-source suppression already TRANSFERRED Map/File/Enum/Struct/User/SoA handle cleanups to the parent via `SlotOwnership` (publish-and-forget: remove the branch action, parent re-registers against its own alloca) — `FreeColumn` / `FreeDataFrame` / `FreeTensor` were simply missing from that retain loop AND from `register_slot_ownership`. FIX (52a454c3): added the three `SlotOwnership` variants + retain-loop transfer arms + parent re-registration, mirroring the existing owned-handle transfers; honored by both parent rebind sites (compile_par_block Step 6 + auto-par dispatch in stmts.rs). AFFECTED every Column/DataFrame/Tensor produced in an auto-par branch and consumed after the join (silent since the codegen E2E harness passes `None` concurrency and never fires auto-par). Regression: par_codegen run==build parity + memory_sanitizer full-pipeline ASAN/LSan (UAF + leak); full LSan suite 507/507. (Renumbered from B-2026-07-03-31 at integration.)

Facet A step 1 (FIXED): a struct FIELD typed `Option[String]` / `Option[Vec[..]]` (inline `{ptr,len,cap}` payload) leaked its `Some` payload when the struct was PLAIN-dropped or consumed (a `Vec[A]` element, a scope-exit drop). emit_struct_drop_synthesis deliberately excluded Option fields, and a prior prototype double-freed because Option-bearing structs were caller-retains (param_own bailed on Option). FIX makes such structs CALLEE-OWNED: (1) param_own.rs field_copy_supported now admits an inline-payload Option, and deep_copy_option_inline_payload_in_place duplicates the Some buffer type-aware off the field TypeExpr (element-deep for a Vec[String] payload, mirroring emit_option_drop_fn); (2) emit_struct_drop_synthesis frees Option fields via a new `OptionInline` FieldDrop, GATED on aggregate_param_copy_supported_struct(struct) = the same predicate that makes the struct entry-copied, so copy == drop and there is never a caller-retains shallow-shared instance to double-free; (3) destructure (finish_owned_struct_destructure), match (suppress_destructured_struct_pattern_cleanup), whole-struct move (zero_struct_move_caps), and field-access move-out (zero_struct_field_move_cap) all neutralize the moved Option by zeroing its tag to None (new zero_option_field_tag_at), and the destructure leaf tracks its own inline-Option cleanup. Verified LSan-clean (no leak) + ASAN-clean (no double-free) on plain-drop, destructure+match-consume, destructure-unused, and field-move-out; full memory_sanitizer suite green (no regressions). Reduced the pinned attr_node leak 474/12 -> 240/6 (AttrNode.string_value fixed; AttrArgNode Options are the residual B-2026-07-03-28). Regression tests: asan_option_field_{plain_drop_freed, destructure_match_consume_clean, destructure_unused_freed, moveout_clean}.

A Tensor declared with a NARROW numeric element type (i8/i16/i32, u8/u16/u32, f32) and built via `Tensor.from([...])` stores its elements at 8 bytes each, but every reader strides at the annotated narrow width (`tensor_elem_size` → 4 for i32/f32), so element reads land on the wrong bytes — SILENT wrong output under `karac build`, correct under `karac run`. MINIMAL (build-only, silent): `fn main() { let t: Tensor[i32,[4]] = Tensor.from([40,10,30,20]); print(t[0]); print(t[1]); print(t[2]); print(t[3]); print(t.sum()); }` — build prints `40 0 10 0` and sum `50` (reading [40,0,10,0]); run prints `40 10 30 20` and sum `100`. Root: the `Tensor.from` literal lowering writes i64/f64 8-byte values into the data buffer regardless of the narrow annotation, while `t[i]`, `t.sum()`, and all C-order readers GEP at `tensor_elem_size(elem)` (native narrow width) — an 8-byte-write / 4-byte-read stride mismatch (classic `0 0 10 40`-after-sort signature). AFFECTS all narrow-element tensor ops under build (indexing, sum/mean/prod, map/fold/zip, and — the surfacing case — sorted/argsort, which are therefore kept i64/f64-only under `karac build` and reject narrow elements LOUDLY; Column, which stores elements at native width, is unaffected and DID gain full-width sorted/argsort in this slice). PRE-EXISTING and independent of the sort work (reproduces with plain `t[i]` / `t.sum()`, code the S6c slices never touched). FIX likely at the `Tensor.from` element-store lowering (narrow the literal to `elem` before storing, OR store 8-byte uniformly and widen `tensor_elem_size` to 8 for all numeric elems + narrow on read-out). Unblocks the widened tensor sorted/argsort path (the kernel widening helpers `sort_widen_value`/`sort_build_vec_from_keys`/`sort_widen_data_buffer` already exist and handle every width — they are wired for Column and ready for Tensor once storage is correct). FIXED 98ae6e12: `compile_tensor_from` now threads the declared element type via `pending_let_tensor_info` (rank-guarded; unannotated falls back to the leaf width) and coerces each leaf with `coerce_scalar_to_type` before the store, so the write stride matches every reader's `tensor_elem_size(info.elem)`. Regression covers i32/i16/u8/u32/f32 reads + reductions, negative sign-extension on read-back, a 2-D narrow tensor, and the i64/f64 no-op widths. The widened tensor sorted/argsort follow-on (narrow elements still rejected loudly there) is now UNBLOCKED but not wired in this fix. (Renumbered from B-2026-07-03-34 at integration — collided with the FIXED reduce.rs modulo-BCE-preflight entry; the fix commit 98ae6e12 predates the renumber and references the old id.) FOLLOW-ON COMPLETION (9cce1610): the 98ae6e12 fix coerced `Tensor.from` leaves but left three gaps — (a) `Tensor.full`'s fill was stored uncoerced (an f32 `full([2], 2.5)` read back 0.0); (b) an integer literal in a FLOAT tensor (`Tensor[f64] = Tensor.from([1,2,3])`) needs int->float `sitofp`, which `coerce_scalar_to_type` omits; (c) `Tensor.mean` over an f32 tensor failed module verification (`fdiv f32, f64`). Fixed all three (shared `coerce_scalar_to_tensor_elem` helper for from+full incl. sitofp; the mean fold fpext's the f32 sum to f64) AND lifted the S6c tensor sorted/argsort narrow-width rejection — they now sort every numeric width via the widened scratch sort (only u64 rejected). Regression: codegen `test_e2e_tensor_narrow_element_storage_and_ops` + `test_e2e_tensor_sorted_argsort_narrow_widths` + reworked `_narrow_width_rejected_loudly`; interpreter `tensor_narrow_element_storage_and_sort_reduction`; memory_sanitizer `asan_tensor_sorted_argsort_narrow_widths_no_leak`.

SILENT seq-vs-auto-par divergence that CRASHES: a valid program panics `vec index out of bounds` under the DEFAULT `karac build` (auto-par on) while `karac run` and `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` are correct. TRIGGER: a reduction body indexes a captured fixed-size `Array[N x T]` by a modulo of the loop var. MINIMAL: `fn f(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a*100i64+b } fn main() { let m: i64=4i64; let atab: Array[i64,4]=[10,20,30,40]; let btab: Array[i64,4]=[1,2,3,4]; let mut total=0i64; let mut k=0i64; while k<100000i64 { let idx=k%m; total=total+f(atab[idx],btab[idx]); k=k+1i64; } println(total); }` -> build traps, run/seq print 250250000. ROOT CAUSE: a follow-on to the by-pointer array capture B-2026-06-15-3 (c3050fc8). The auto-par reduction worker's modulo bounds-check-elision preflight (`emit_modulo_bce_preflight`) is a Vec-ONLY optimization: it loads `{ptr,len,cap}` field 1 as the runtime length to prove `captured[k % upper]` in-bounds once at entry. But a by-pointer array capture has NO header -- its VarSlot points straight at the inline elements -- so `build_struct_gep({ptr,i64,i64}, ptr %atab, 1)` reads element[1] as the bogus "length" and the `len < upper` check traps on garbage (`btab=[1,2,3,4]` -> element[1]=2 < upper 4 -> false panic). The per-iter access itself was already a correct static-N `[N x T]` check; only the hoisted preflight was wrong. Constant-index array access and `Vec[i64]` tables (real runtime length) were both fine, which is why the seq lane and non-modulo shapes never showed it. FIX (99617752): `find_modulo_hoistable_bounds` drops any bound whose captured base has an ArrayType VarSlot -- arrays carry a compile-time-constant length, so the per-iter static-N bounds check suffices; only Vec captures get the preflight + BCE elision. Regression: par_codegen IR-pin (worker has no `bce.len` / `vec index out of bounds`, keeps `getelementptr [4 x i64]`) + e2e (250250000). par_codegen 155 + codegen 2029 + memory_sanitizer 511 green; clippy + fmt clean.

A `Vec[…]` literal (`compile_vec_prefix_literal`) whose element is an f-string (`Vec[f"…"]`) or an identifier String/Vec (`let a=…; Vec[a]`) DOUBLE-FREED the element buffer: heap-use-after-free when the element is read, SIGTRAP/exit 133 double-free at the Vec's drop. FIXED 3c96c8e9. ROOT CAUSE: the Vec-literal element loop bit-copied each value into the heap buffer but — unlike `compile_tuple` — never suppressed the element's OWN scope-exit cleanup, so both that cleanup and the Vec's owner freed the same pointer. An f-string element's accumulator queues a FreeVecBuffer via `track_vec_var` (exprs.rs InterpolatedStringLit arm); an identifier String/Vec carries its binding cleanup. FIX: mirror `compile_tuple`'s move-aware per-element suppression — `suppress_fstr_acc_if_moved_out` (called right after each element's compile_expr, while `last_fstr_acc` still holds THIS element's acc — the single slot is overwritten by the next element) + `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg` + the Map move-suppress for identifier elements; all no-op for fresh temps (`.to_string()`/`.clone()`) and POD. NOTE: the original entry's 'single-element / return-only' narrowing was a TESTING ARTIFACT — the earlier multi-element probes only read `.len()` (a freed element buffer isn't touched by a length read) so the UAF didn't manifest; reading an element exposes it for ANY count, in `main` or via `return`. Verified run==build + leak/double-free-clean (macOS ASAN + `leaks` -O0 + Linux LeakSanitizer) across f-string/identifier/to_string/clone/mixed elements; regression test `asan_single_element_fstring_vec_return_no_double_free`. Surfaced writing B-2026-07-03-29's leak test.

OPEN. HEAP-ZIP LEG FIXED 84e64cf (2026-07-07) + GENERAL heap-index-read-into-owning-sink double-free fixed same commit. Root finding: reading a heap element by index from a named Vec (`v[i]`, element String/Vec/…) and moving it into an OWNING sink — tuple literal `(v[i],…)`, `push(v[i])`, struct field `{f: v[i]}`, owned call arg, return — shallow-aliased the container's element buffer (compile_vec_index only loads the {ptr,len,cap} header), so BOTH the container's element-drop and the sink's owner freed it (double-free, exit 133). This was a real miscompile even in HAND-WRITTEN code (`(a[i],b[i])`, `d.push(a[i])`), not just the synthetic collect lowerings; the `let s = v[i]` binding path already deep-cloned via clone_owned_vec_index_element, so the fix routes heap index-reads through that SAME clone at the shared owning-sink hook maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg (scoped to a named-Vec, non-range, non-trivially-copyable index; source left intact -> distinct buffers). That closes the earlier 'synthetic-AST span-type limitation' framing: the clone keys on codegen's own var_elem_type_exprs, NOT typechecker spans, so it fires for synthetic index-reads too. With it, the zip lowering now admits a HEAP element pair when both `.iter()` bases are clone-eligible named Vecs (else keeps bailing loud). Verified run==build + LSan-clean over Vec[String] pairs and hand-written tuple/push/struct-field index-reads; regressions e2e_iter_adaptor_zip_heap_collect_codegen + e2e_heap_vec_index_read_into_owning_sinks (codegen), asan_b04_2_zip_heap_collect_no_leak + asan_heap_vec_index_read_into_sinks_no_double_free (memory_sanitizer). STILL OPEN: chunks/windows (blocked on the DISTINCT synthetic-move gap — `acc.push(chunk); chunk = Vec.new()` reassignment-drop suppression needs typechecker move analysis the synthetic AST lacks; the index-read clone only covers the inner `chunk.push(v[j])`), zip/chain/flat_map sides carrying their OWN adaptors, scan (unreliable under run), cycle (unbounded), and sub-part 3 (non-terminal f-string map). CHUNKS/WINDOWS RE-PROBED (2026-07-07, post heap-index-read fix 84e64cf): the picture is now finer than the earlier 'move-into-aggregate' framing. A nested-loop lowering with a FRESH per-iteration sub-Vec binding (`while start<len { let mut chunk=Vec.new(); while j<end&&j<len { chunk.push(base[j]); j+=1 }; acc.push(chunk); start+=step }`) is the right shape and AVOIDS the old `chunk=Vec.new()` reassignment double-free. Its two sub-frees are now individually sound: `chunk.push(base[j])` deep-clones the heap element (84e64cf) and `acc.push(chunk)` move-suppresses a FRESH nested Vec[String] — both verified ASAN-clean in isolation (minimal `outer.push(inner)` with cloned index-reads, and a SINGLE-chunk `chunks(2)` over a 2-elem Vec[String], both LSan-clean). BUT a MULTI-iteration chunks (>=2 outer iters) double-frees a CLONED String under ASAN (exit 23) while `karac run` and -O2 AOT mask it. Bisected: single outer iteration clean, two+ iterations crash -> the fault is the synthetic while-body's per-iteration `let mut chunk` reusing one entry-block alloca across iterations, so the move-suppression (cap=0 on the slot at acc.push) interacts wrong with the next iteration's re-init / the accumulated scope-exit cleanups on the shared slot (the sub-Vec's element Strings get freed by BOTH the stale per-iteration cleanup and acc's recursive drop). This is a SYNTHETIC-lowering scope-drain issue (a loop-local heap binding whose alloca is reused and whose cleanup isn't drained per-iteration in the generated AST), NOT the ownership move gap and NOT the index-read clone. The chunks/windows lowering was implemented + reverted this session (won't ship the double-free); a follow-on needs the per-iteration loop-body cleanup drain for the synthetic fresh binding (or a distinct alloca per iteration). Windows shares the identical shape (step=1, full-window cutoff `start+n<=len`) and the identical blocker. STILL OPEN. MAJOR PROGRESS 2026-07-07 (chunks/windows c8a915d, nested-index e06cb55, chain-adaptor-sides e9b08dd; heap-zip 84e64cf earlier this session). (1) CHUNKS/WINDOWS FIXED c8a915d: `<base>.iter().chunks(n)/.windows(n).collect()` -> Vec[Vec[E]] now lowers. The blocker was NOT the ownership move gap as previously recorded — it was that the synthetic AST bypasses the ownership checker, so a consume-then-reuse loop-local binding (`let chunk;..;acc.push(chunk)`) never got the RC fallback the checker inserts for hand-written code. Fix builds each chunk as a FRESH temp via an inline block tail-return (`acc.push({ let mut c=Vec.new(); while.. { c.push(base[j]) }; c })`) — the mk()-fresh-temp pattern inlined — which compile_block_with_frame's tail-cleanup suppression transfers cleanly; base[j] deep-clones. (An in-place `acc.push(empty); acc[idx].push(base[j])` alternative double-freed a clone on acc realloc; the fresh-temp block-return is the sound shape.) (2) NESTED-INDEX BIND FIXED e06cb55 (adjacent bug found here): `let x = m[i][j]` over Vec[Vec[String]] aliased the innermost buffer (clone_owned_vec_index_element only handled a bare Identifier object); generalized to peel one Vec layer per index level (vec_index_elem_type_expr). (3) CHAIN ADAPTOR-CARRYING SIDES FIXED e9b08dd: `a.iter().map(f).chain(b.iter())` / `a.chain(b.iter().filter(g))` recursively collect each side and merge into a shared acc. REMAINING RESIDUALS: (i) ZIP/FLAT_MAP adaptor-carrying sides (chain done; zip needs per-side pre-collect with distinct Vec[EA]/Vec[EB] owned_temp_drops entries, flat_map is nested — both niche); (ii) non-terminal f-string map (`map(|x| f"..").filter(..)`) — needs the poisoned staged-accumulator (B-2026-07-03-25), a separate hard bug; (iii) SCAN — WON'T-DO: broken under `karac run` itself (returns 0/garbage), no oracle; (iv) CYCLE — WON'T-DO: unbounded. All residuals loud-fail cleanly (never a miscompile). The common multi-source adaptor (chain) and the chunks/windows/zip terminal collects are DONE. ZIP ADAPTOR-CARRYING SIDES FIXED 7ecacf7 (2026-07-07): `a.iter().map(f).zip(b.iter())` / `a.iter().zip(b.iter().filter(g))` pre-collect each side to a typed temp and reuse the identity zip (result Vec[(EA,EB)] decomposed to type the temps; sub-collect result types registered under usize::MAX-based synthetic spans). Both multi-source adaptors with adaptor-carrying sides are now done (chain e9b08dd + zip 7ecacf7). UPDATED remaining residuals: (i) FLAT_MAP adaptor-carrying sides — the outer element type isn't derivable from the flattened result type (unlike zip's tuple), and an adaptor-carrying INNER needs per-element sub-pipelines; niche, deferred; (ii) non-terminal f-string map — a genuinely RARE shape needing either the poisoned-staged-accumulator fix (B-2026-07-03-25) or a collect-split at the f-string map; deferred; (iii) SCAN (won't-do, broken under run); (iv) CYCLE (won't-do, unbounded). Every common adaptor and multi-source shape now lowers; all residuals loud-fail cleanly (never a miscompile).
resolution: FIXED (collect surface fully closed 2026-07-07). Every iterator-adaptor `.collect()` shape now lowers under `karac build` at run==build parity, LSan-clean. Fix SHAs this session: heap-index-read-into-sink + heap-zip 84e64cf; chunks/windows c8a915d (fresh-temp block-return — the real blocker was the synthetic AST bypassing the ownership RC fallback, NOT a move-into-aggregate gap); nested-index bind m[i][j] e06cb55; chain adaptor-carrying sides e9b08dd (recursive collect + merge); zip adaptor-carrying sides 7ecacf7 (pre-collect + identity zip, synthetic-span typing); non-terminal f-string map c37ecb8 (split at the f-string map so it becomes terminal); flat_map adaptor-carrying outer c37ecb8 (pre-collect outer, identity flat_map); cycle+take 0f4016a (repeat-until-n with empty-source guard); scan 9230632 (running accumulator, extract the Some(..) inner tuple directly). Earlier sub-parts (enumerate, map/filter, named-fn, destructuring closure, identity/range/into_iter, chain/zip/flat_map identity) landed previously. TWO documented NON-implementable edges remain, both loud-fail cleanly (never a miscompile), neither an open bug: (1) a BARE `cycle().collect()` with no bounding `take` is unbounded/non-terminating — a semantic non-starter (only `cycle().take(n)` is collectable); (2) a scan body that conditionally returns `None` (rare — the common unconditional `Some((new,out))` is covered) bails, since resolving the Option in post-typecheck synthetic AST is fragile. NOTE: the earlier ledger claim that `scan` is 'broken under run' was WRONG — it works under run with the correct `|acc, x| -> Option[(A,U)]` signature (the mis-test used a bare `acc+x` body). Regressions: e2e_iter_adaptor_* + asan_b04_2_* across every adaptor (tests/codegen.rs, tests/memory_sanitizer.rs).

title: An inline tuple `(…, x)` whose heap component `x` is a FOR-LOOP element variable, moved into a `Vec` (`for x in w.iter() { v.push((i, x)) }`), DOUBLE-FREED the heap component under `karac build` (exit 133/134); `karac run` correct. FIXED 210eb93b. ROOT: codegen iterates a Vec IN PLACE (the `.iter()` peel makes borrow==owned iteration), so the loop var `x` bit-copies (ALIASES) the source Vec's element buffer; `compile_tuple` then bit-copied that alias into the tuple, and BOTH the source's scope-exit free and the pushed Vec's element drop released it. `compile_tuple` ran the two suppression helpers per element but — unlike every OTHER consume site (`v.push(x)`, struct-literal fields, call args, map inserts, let-bindings) — NOT `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg`, which deep-copies a RETAINING source (`for_loop_borrow_vars` / `owned_vecstr_params`) so the consumer owns a private buffer while the source keeps its free. Adding that one call fixes it (no-op for fresh temps / plain owned locals — handled by the existing suppression). Also unblocks TERMINAL heap `enumerate().collect()` (B-2026-07-04-2). Regression: `asan_for_loop_var_into_tuple_push_no_double_free` (macOS ASAN + Linux LSan). DISTINCT from B-2026-07-04-1 (element's OWN cleanup in a literal) — this is the for-loop VAR's aliased buffer on tuple move-out.

A NON-terminal heap `enumerate` in `<iter>.collect()` whose `(i64, <heap>)` tuple flows downstream miscompiled (garbage/crash). PARTIAL FIX aa24fb0c: `enumerate().map(|p| …)` now works — the desugar binds the tuple DIRECTLY to the map's param (single owning binding, no aliasing `let p = __ietup` copy), the loop-var search STOPS at enumerate so the source-element name can't collide with that param, and `map` pushes a TRANSFORMED value by unconditional move. Verified leak/double-free-clean (macOS ASAN 517, Linux LSan 517) incl. `map(|p| p.1)` / POD-producing map / `skip().enumerate().map` over LOCAL heap sources. STILL OPEN: a heap `enumerate` followed by `filter`/`take_while`/`skip_while`/`inspect` (a CONDITIONAL WHOLE-tuple move `if pred { push(p) }` whose synthetic binding is not move-suppressed → double-free), or a SECOND downstream stage (`enumerate().filter().map()`, `enumerate().take().map()` — the tuple reaches a param stage only after a non-param stage / is re-bound), stays GATED to the loud dispatch-fail (allowed heap shapes: terminal / `take` / `skip` whole-tuple push, and single-terminal `map`). POD tuples are always fine. Fixing the rest needs the synthetic downstream tuple binding to MOVE (suppress the source) rather than bit-copy-alias. OPEN (residual). UPDATE 2026-07-05 (FIXED 39a1ca46): all remaining downstream shapes lowered. The `Enumerate` build_body arm now binds the tuple to the FIRST downstream param-bearing stage's param, searching PAST the value-preserving passthrough adaptors (`take`/`skip`/`step_by`) — so `enumerate().take(n).map(|p| p.1)` (case D) binds the tuple DIRECTLY to the map param instead of a synthetic `__ietup` that the map's `let p = __ietup` bit-copied (the double-free). The caller's two-shape gate is replaced by a copy-free SIMULATION of the desugar's name/tuple threading: a heap enumerate is ADMITTED unless a whole-tuple COPY (`let X = <tuple>`) survives — a LATER param stage whose name differs from the tuple binding, or a NON-terminal `map` returning the whole tuple (`|p| p`, `|p| (…)`); those exotic residuals stay GATED to the loud dispatch-fail (never a miscompile), tracked as B-2026-07-05-1. Newly clean: `enumerate()` + `filter`/`take_while`/`skip_while`/`inspect` (conditional whole-tuple push), `enumerate().filter().take()`, and `map(|p| p.1)` past a `take`/`skip`/`filter`. Verified run==build + macOS ASAN 527/0 + Linux LSan 4/0 (enumerate class, fresh `Compiling karac`) + codegen 2053/0, fmt+clippy clean; regressions asan_b04_4_heap_enumerate_conditional_tuple_collect_no_double_free + asan_b04_4_heap_enumerate_downstream_map_collect_no_double_free + extended e2e_iter_adaptor_collect_enumerate_codegen. Sibling residuals under B-2026-07-04-2: multi-source adaptors (zip/chain/…), the multi-param/destructuring closure `enumerate().map(|(i,x)| …)`, and a non-terminal `map` whose body calls a METHOD on the mapped param (`enumerate().map(|p| p.1).filter(|s| s.len()>3)` — the PRE-EXISTING non-enumerate `map().filter()` gap, not this bug). FIXED.

A `<iter>.collect()` chain whose SOURCE is a FRESH-TEMP call result (`mk().iter().enumerate().collect()`, not a named local) read and dropped the source `Vec[String]` buffer at the WRONG element stride, freeing garbage (`pointer being freed was not allocated` — SIGABRT at -O0 / SIGTRAP exit-133 at -O2; `karac run` correct). Crashes even with NO index-read (a bare `.len()` still traps at scope-exit drop) — the earlier “index-read required / exit 134” framing was an artifact of a stale installed `karac`. ROOT (NOT a scope-exit race, as first guessed): the collect desugar's `for __ice in mk().iter()` peels `.iter()` and recurses into `try_compile_for_vec_value`, which resolved the loop element type from `owned_temp_drops` at the iterable span — but the whole method-call chain (`mk`, `mk()`, `.iter()`, `.enumerate()`, `.collect()`) SHARES the base callee's span (a known method-chain span collision), so `expr_types`/`owned_temp_drops` at that key hold the OUTERMOST result `Vec[(i64,String)]` (the last insert wins), not the source `Vec[String]`. The for-loop then read elements at the wider `(i64,String)` stride (32B) over a 24B `String` buffer and dropped the materialized temp the same way → garbage free. A LOCAL-binding source (`let w=…; w.iter()`) took the identifier path and was unaffected; `enumerate().map(|p| p.1)` (non-tuple output) happened to survive. FIX: `try_compile_for_vec_value` now consults `temp_recv_elem_types` (the receiver's ELEMENT type, recorded span-keyed by the typechecker for `.iter()`/`.into_iter()` fresh-temp peels — collision-immune) BEFORE `owned_temp_drops`; a non-peel Vec-value iterable (`t.iter_axis(n)`) has no element-table entry and still uses `owned_temp_drops`, so the reorder is a pure fix with no regression. Regressions: `e2e_iter_adaptor_collect_fresh_temp_source_codegen` + `asan_fresh_temp_source_enumerate_collect_no_double_free` (macOS ASAN + Linux LSan 518/0). RESIDUAL (separate, pre-existing, low): a PLAIN `.iter().collect()` with NO map/filter/enumerate adaptor loud-fails (`method 'iter' not supported` / `no handler for 'collect' on non-identifier receiver`) for both fresh-temp and local sources — identity collect, tracked under B-2026-07-04-2.

The natural rolling-DP inner scan `dp[c] = dp[c] + dp[c - 1]` over a `Vec[i64]` (kata #62 Unique Paths) ran ~3.1x slower than clang -O3 / rustc -O (316ms vs 102ms, K=1M seq bench): karac emitted THREE bounds-checked accesses per cell (read dp[c], read dp[c-1], write dp[c]) and — blocked by those checks — LLVM could not forward the just-written dp[c-1] into a register. The ENTIRE ~216ms gap was the per-cell bounds checks: with all of them off the bench runs 105ms ≈ clang's 102ms (LLVM does the store-to-load forwarding itself once the checks clear), so no separate load-forwarding work was needed. ROOT: the existing split-check elision (control_flow_bce.rs) only fires when a guard names `v.len()` directly or via a `let n = v.len()` alias, but the rolling-DP guard is `while c < cols` where `cols` is not spelled `dp.len()` yet EQUALS it (`dp` was filled to exactly `cols` elements by a counted `while j < cols` from 0 and never resized). FIX b5d18320, two parts: (1) bce_length_pin.rs — a fail-closed whole-function AST analysis records a length pin `cols == dp.len()` only when a soundness scan proves it holds from the fill loop to end-of-function (counter starts 0, steps +1, one unconditional push, `dp` untouched before the fill and only index-read/`.len()` after, `cols` never rewritten after); compile_while activates each pin when it finishes emitting the matching fill loop (live only lexically after), and resolve_len_origin consults the pins so `while c < cols` yields UpperBound{c, dp}. (2) index_bounds_already_proven extended from bare-identifier indices to `i ± k` (k a non-neg literal): `i - k` keeps the upper proof (i-k < i < len) so `dp[c-1]` elides its upper check; residual `< 0` checks fold against the loop's existing monotone `assume(i >= init)`. RESULT: kata #62 bench 316ms → 113ms (3.0x, TIED with rustc -O, within 7% of clang -O3); run==build==python preserved; adversarial shapes (bound reassigned after fill, non-zero counter, co-indexed shorter vec) still PANIC — the elision does not fire when unsound. Tests: 15 analysis unit tests + 3 E2E (positive + two must-panic negatives); codegen E2E (2037) and ASAN memory-sanitizer (518) green. Follow-ups (safe, not done): `for i in 0..b` fill form, push-only prelude seed, non-bare bound expressions.

The ESCAPE-side sibling of B-2026-07-03-31 (which fixed the BORROW side): RETURNING (or otherwise genuinely moving OUT) a `Some(v)`-bound payload from an `Option[<agg>]` DESTRUCTURE-LEAF (`let A { value } = a; match value { Some(v) => v, None => Val.Nothing }`) leaks the payload's inner heap (~48 B/String, 6/6 in a Vec[A]-consuming loop under macOS `leaks`; also `karac run`-correct, leak only). The consuming suppressor CORRECTLY disarms the destructure-leaf source's `karac_drop_Option` here (v really escapes), but the escaped value's ownership is not established on the RETURN path, so the downstream binding (`let g = get(a)`) never frees it. SPECIFIC to the destructure-leaf: returning `Some(v)=>v` from a PLAIN `Option[Val]` local/param is CLEAN (0 leaks) — so it is the `inline_option_agg_payload_vars` destructure-leaf path, not a general return-Option-payload leak. PRE-EXISTING (repros on main before and after B-2026-07-03-31). Found probing the B-31 fix's consuming cases (C1/C2). Likely resolved by completing the caller-retains model (the move-out/escape must transfer the payload's inner-heap ownership to the returned value). NON-BLOCKING (leak only, double-free-clean). See [[B-2026-07-03-31]], [[caller-retains-model-spike-phase0]]. REFINED DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-04, probing this entry): the 'escape/return-path' framing is INCOMPLETE — the leak is NOT escape-specific. Minimal ZERO-escape repro: `struct A { value: Option[Val] }` (Val = enum with Ident(String)); `let items: Vec[A] = build(); items.len()` (build + drop, NO get/return/consume) LEAKS 112 B / 2 objs per elem (String + boxed enum). ROOT CAUSE: `emit_struct_drop_synthesis(A)` emits NO drop for an `Option[<heap enum/struct>]` field — every field-classification pass leaves it None (the `EnumField` pass skips Option; the `OptionInline` pass is gated to String/Vec payloads AND copy-supported structs) — so `emit_struct_drop_synthesis(A)` returns None and `type_expr_has_drop_heap(A)` is false (the `Option => false` arm at synth_drop.rs ~1701), hence `Vec[A]` teardown skips the element walk entirely (bare `free(data)`, no per-element drop). THRESHOLD (all single-push build+drop): only `struct { Option[heap-enum/struct] }` leaks; `Vec[Option[Val]]`, `Vec[Val]`, `struct { value: Val }` (direct enum field), `struct { name: String }` are ALL CLEAN — the payload drop machinery already exists (`vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr(Option[Val])` emits `karac_drop_Option_Val` via `option_payload_struct_or_enum_drop_ok` + `emit_option_drop_fn`, inline + boxed); the gap is purely the struct-FIELD drop-synthesis wiring + the `type_expr_has_drop_heap` Option arm. COPY SIDE IS MANDATORY (proven empirically): a drop-only experiment (recurse `type_expr_has_drop_heap` into the Option payload + a copy-support-UNGATED `OptionInline` for plain-enum/struct payloads via `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr`) makes the zero-escape and plain-local-source cases CLEAN, but converts EVERY by-value-pass-of-an-ALIAS case (`for a in build() { let g = get(a) }`, `get(items[0])`) into a DOUBLE-FREE (exit 133): the callee-borrow move-out neutralizer `zero_option_field_tag_at` zeroes only the callee's local param header, NOT the aliased Vec element, so the Vec teardown and the escaped `g` free the same payload twice. Safe fix therefore needs `A` to be COPY-SUPPORTED (so a by-value `get(a)` entry-copies rather than borrow-shares) — `field_copy_supported`'s Option arm + `deep_copy_option_inline_payload_in_place` must admit a plain-enum/struct payload, which requires NEW boxed-Option-payload deep-copy machinery (Option[Val] BOXES its 4-word payload; the general `emit_clone_fn` Option path is shallow/WRONG per [[caller-retains-model-spike-phase0]] B-04-9(a)) plus the alias-source neutralization. CONFIRMS the original hunch: caller-retains model completion, NOT a contained fix; do NOT re-attempt drop-only (exit-133 double-free). OPEN. FIXED e56cc298 (2026-07-04) — the 'caller-retains model completion' framing OVERSTATED the scope; the real fix was THREE coupled halves (copy-depth == drop-depth), no model rewrite: (1) field_copy_supported's Option arm admits a non-shared struct/enum payload (option_payload_struct_or_enum_copyable — struct payloads need recursive copy-support, enum payloads mirror the existing direct-enum-field trust), making the owning struct callee-owned; (2) deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place — the box-aware copy peer of emit_option_drop_fn's boxed/inline branch (BOXED when LLVM word count > 3 per coerce_to_payload_words: malloc a fresh box, shallow-copy the payload in, deep-copy its heap in place, store the new ptr; inline: deep-copy in place). NOT emit_clone_fn (shallow for Option); (3) the OptionInline struct-drop pass broadens to that payload class (the drop fn from vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr already handled inline+boxed Option payloads). Plus the destructure-leaf branch (let A { value } = a) now zeros the callee-owned SOURCE's Option tag (zero_struct_field_move_cap) on move-out — its 'struct drop NEVER frees an Option field' invariant no longer holds, so without it the source struct-drop's new OptionInline free double-freed against the B-27 leaf drop (the exit-133 the 'do NOT re-attempt drop-only' warning predicted — resolved by pairing the drop with copy-support AND source-tag neutralization). Gates: macOS ASAN 526/0 (no double-free/UAF), Linux LSan 526/0 (no leak), fmt+clippy. Test asan_b04_7_option_heap_enum_struct_field_drop_no_leak. Residual (pre-existing, split to B-2026-07-04-17): for-loop-element-ESCAPE (`for a in vec { let x = a }` / field-move into a fresh struct literal) double-frees for ANY Vec[heap-struct] — this fix makes Option[heap-enum] structs consistent with that pre-existing class.

The tree-walk interpreter has NO u64 model: `Value::Int(i64)` is signedness-blind, so every u64 value ≥ 2^63 is handled as its negative i64 two's-complement under `karac run` — mis-PRINTED (`println(f"{hi}")` of 2^63 shows `-9223372036854775808`; `value_type_name(Int)` is hard-coded `"i64"`), mis-COMPARED (`hi > (one << 62)` returns false via signed `eval_binary`), and mis-SORTED (`Column.sorted`/`argsort`, `Tensor.sorted`/`argsort` route through `value_compare`, which orders `Value::Int` signed — 2^63-plus values sort to the FRONT as negatives). Codegen (`karac build`) is CORRECT for all of these (unsigned print, `ugt`/`udiv`/`urem`/`lshr` already lowered per the u64.<op> desugar). Surfaced while implementing S6c u64 Column/Tensor sort under `build`: the codegen half is a one-line unsigned-`UGT` scratch compare (thread an `unsigned` flag through `SortKey::IntValue`/`IndexIntoInt`; the widen for a 64-bit elem is already an identity copy), but shipping it alone would make `build` disagree with `run` for u64 ≥ 2^63, so `sort_key_is_int` keeps the loud u64 rejection until the interpreter catches up. In practice u64 ≥ 2^63 literals are UNREACHABLE (the lexer rejects integer literals > i64::MAX as `Invalid integer literal`, and `hi + hi`-style construction overflow-traps), so the divergence only bites deliberately shift-constructed high-bit values — but it is a genuine silent wrong-result under `run`, independent of sort. FIX (an interpreter epic, NOT a sort slice): give the tree-walker a real unsigned-int model — either a `Value::UInt(u64)` variant or a signedness tag on `Value::Int` — and route `Display`/f-string, `eval_binary` compare/div/rem/shift, `value_compare`, and min/max/sort through it. Blocks the S6c u64 sort follow-on on BOTH surfaces. FIXED 45eb926 (2026-07-07): span-threaded unsigned-64 model — the i64-carrier `Value::Int` stays, but every signedness-sensitive sink reinterprets the bits as `u64` when the static type (via `expr_types`/`args_close_span`) says so (u8..u32 fit i64 non-negatively, so only 64-bit needs it). eval_binary: unsigned div/rem/shr + </<=/>/>= (operand hint from the call site, since a comparison types the expr `bool`) and add/sub/mul trapping at the u64 boundary (matches codegen `uadd.with.overflow`, no more i64::MAX false-trap); print/to_string/f-string render unsigned; Vec/Column/Tensor sort/sorted/argsort/argmin/argmax order by unsigned magnitude (element signedness stashed at the non-aliased close-paren leaf, since the receiver span is clobbered by the Vec[i64]/Option[i64]/Unit result). Two codegen bugs found while verifying run==build parity and fixed in the same commit so the interp fix introduces no silent divergence: (a) operators inside f-string interpolations were never lowered to typed method calls (`InterpolatedStringLit` was a `lower` leaf) so codegen compiled u64 f-string ops signed — lowering now recurses into interpolation parts; (b) `Vec[uN].sort()`'s default-order thunk compared signed, mis-sorting u8>=128 and u64>=2^63 — now unsigned for unsigned widths. Codegen Column[u64]/Tensor[u64] sort still LOUD-rejects (shared scratch-sort kernel, also on the stats path) — tracked follow-on B-2026-07-07-2. Gates: interpreter 1116/0 (+11 new), typechecker 1911/0, codegen 2055/0 (+2 new), memory_sanitizer 534/0, fmt+clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean.

Two PRE-EXISTING residuals of the caller-retains shared-drop model, surfaced while landing B-2026-07-03-28 Phase 2 (both repro on main BEFORE and after that fix). (a) DOUBLE-FREE (exit 133): a struct FIELD typed Vec[struct-with-Option[shared]-or-shared] that is entry-copied (the OUTER struct passed by-value to a copy-supported param) and then WHOLE-dropped (not consumed element-by-element) double-frees the element heap — the Vec[struct] field entry-copy is OUTER-only (elements bit-aliased with the caller) but the struct drop drains elements element-DEEP (this is the 'piece (b)' element-deep entry-copy the original B-28 scope named). MINIMAL: `struct ArgN{name:Option[String],value:Option[Val]} struct AttrN{args:Vec[ArgN]} fn count(a:AttrN)->i64{a.args.len()}` + `for a in items { count(a) }` (Val shared enum). Naive piece (b) via emit_clone_fn is WRONG (emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr routes Option payloads to the type-erased emit_enum_clone_fn("Option") = SHALLOW copy, no rc-inc / no deep buffer copy); a correct element-deep copy must recurse via the entry-copy machinery (deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place per element) — BUT that in turn regresses the for-loop-CONSUME path (the extra per-element rc-incs are STRANDED because for-loop consumption neutralizes the source Vec's element drain), so closing (a) also needs the for-loop-consume-drain semantics fixed. (b) LEAK: a direct-`shared`-field struct passed as an INLINE FRESH-TEMP arg (`f(DirH{value: shared})`, DirH={value:Val}) leaks the box — DirH is not copy-supported (field_copy_supported bails on a direct shared field), so the fresh-temp struct-arg cleanup gate (which requires copy-supported) registers no caller-temp drop; a LOCAL arg (`let d=DirH{..}; f(d)`) is fixed (track_struct_var combined drop). NON-BLOCKING for the self-host port: its Vec[struct] fields are consumed via for-loop (not whole-dropped), and its shared-owning structs use Option[shared], not direct-shared. Both are leak/double-free residuals of the same incomplete ownership model. See [[B-2026-07-03-28]], [[caller-retains-model-spike-phase0]]. UPDATE 2026-07-04: (b) FIXED (f22b58c4) — the fresh-temp struct-arg cleanup gate (call_dispatch.rs) now registers the combined drop (track_struct_var = pure rc-dec, no buffer copy) for a shared-owning struct even when NOT copy-supported; a direct-shared-field struct is caller-retains (never callee-owned), so the inline fresh-temp is the box's SOLE owner. Regression asan_b04_9b_direct_shared_freshtemp_struct_arg_no_leak (macOS ASAN 522/0 + Linux LSan 522/0 + codegen 2043/0, fmt+clippy clean). (a) REMAINS OPEN — CONFIRMED empirically as this entry predicted: an element-DEEP entry-copy of the Vec[struct] field (deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place per element, gated symmetric with vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr) DOES close the exit-133 double-free (repro 133->0, full macOS ASAN 521/0), but REGRESSES the for-loop-CONSUME path under LSan: the existing asan_attr_node_list_drop_consume_and_plain leaks 954 B/24 (and a whole-drop+consume repro 726 B/18). consume(a)'s param becomes an INDEPENDENT copy while the for-loop-consumed source's element drain stays suppressed (the per-shape for-loop-consume suppressor treats the arg as consumed and is NOT migrated to consume_class::binding_only_borrowed), stranding the source elements. This exactly reproduces the B-2026-07-03-28 ATTEMPT regression (240/6 -> 714/18); closing (a) needs the caller-retains model COMPLETION (move-aware entry-copy / consume-site rc-balance for copy-supported shared-owning structs), NOT a contained increment. (a) patch reverted, (b) landed standalone. OPEN (a). FIXED 2026-07-04 (273c9397) — the OPEN-(a) diagnosis above was WRONG: the regression was NOT the for-loop-consume source-drain suppressor / a missing binding_only_borrowed migration, and needed NO caller-retains model completion. Empirical isolation (whole-drop `a.args.len()` = LSan-clean vs destructure `let AttrN{args}=a` = leak) pinned it to a copy/drop DEPTH asymmetry in TWO coupled halves that land together: (1) param_own deep_copy_vec_aggregate_elements_in_place element-deep-copies each Vec[struct/enum/Option] element of an entry-copied field via the entry-copy machinery (deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place / enum / Option — NOT emit_clone_fn, shallow for Option); (2) track_owned_destructure_field_cleanup drains a destructured Vec[<aggregate>] leaf via vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr (track_vec_of_aggs_var) instead of the outer-only track_vec_var, matching the whole-struct drop. On baseline the elements were bit-shared and freed via the source teardown, masking the shallow leaf drain; the deep copy makes them independent so the shallow leaf stranded them (the 954B/24 consume-path leak). Balanced only together. Gates: macOS ASAN full 525/0, Linux LSan FULL SUITE 525/0 (the twice-regressed asan_attr_node_list_drop_consume_and_plain now passes on the authoritative gate), fmt+clippy clean. Closed the three follow-ups noted when the rolling-DP length-pin bounds-check elision first landed (B-2026-07-04-6), generalising which counted-fill shapes establish a `bound == v.len()` pin. FIX 81746fff: (1) FOR-RANGE fills — `for i in 0..BOUND { v.push(x) }` (exclusive, start 0 or omitted) now pins, activated at the tail of compile_for_range_with_step keyed on the range end's span (the range guarantees BOUND iterations from 0, so no counter proof needed). (2) SEED PRELUDES — a `v.push(..)` before the counted fill is allowed; it only lengthens v, so `bound <= v.len()` still holds (v1 bailed on any pre-fill mention of v). (3) ARITHMETIC BOUNDS — BOUND may be any pure-arithmetic expression over idents + int literals (`cols + 1`, `m * 2`, …), not just a bare identifier; bounds normalise to a span-free `BoundTerm` and the fill's bound + a later guard's bound match STRUCTURALLY across surface-Binary vs trait-lowered-Call forms, with every ident of BOUND required unwritten after the fill. The active-pin store changed from `HashMap<String,String>` (bound var → vec) to `Vec<(BoundTerm, String)>` and resolve_len_origin gained a normalised structural match. Every relaxation stays FAIL-CLOSED (a missed pin only keeps a check). Verified: kata #62 still 105ms (no regression, C parity); for-range / non-bare / prelude positives give correct output (run==build); adversarial shapes (for 1..n, cols+1 with cols reassigned after fill) still PANIC — no over-elision. Tests: 22 analysis unit tests (for-range/prelude/non-bare fire + negatives + BoundTerm normalisation) + 3 new E2E (2 positive, 1 must-panic); codegen E2E 2043 + ASAN 519 green.

`infer_binary`'s numeric arithmetic arm required an EXACT type match only for int-int operand pairs (`both_ints`); ANY pair with a float operand fell through to the loose `types_compatible` check, and `types_compatible(Int, Float)` is `true` (it must stay permissive for assignment/other contexts). So a cross-DOMAIN mix — `let z = y * x` with `y: i64`, `x: f64` — PASSED `karac check`, ERRORED under `karac run` (the interpreter has no implicit int→float promotion: `operator 'Mul' is not defined for Int and Float`), and SILENTLY MISCOMPILED under `karac build` (wrong-domain / garbage result — e.g. a fold product `c.fold(1, |a,x| a*x)` on a `Column[f64]` printed the i64 bit-pattern of the f64 accumulator). A three-surface divergence on the most basic operation, silent under build. ROOT: Kāra has no implicit int→float promotion in arithmetic, but the float branch never enforced the domain split — it delegated to a helper that is deliberately permissive about numeric mixing for OTHER contexts. FIX: the arm now guards the split itself — exactly one integer operand (the other a float) is a hard `TypeMismatch` pointing at an explicit `as` cast; `build` gates on the type error so all three surfaces reject consistently. Scope: ONLY cross-domain int/float is newly rejected — same-type float arithmetic, float+unsuffixed-literal promotion (`e + 1`), and the existing mixed-int-width/-signedness rejections are unchanged. Surfaced while probing the S6c `product`-on-`Reduce` follow-on. Regressions: test_mixed_int_float_arithmetic_rejected (5 pairs × ops × orders), test_int_float_arithmetic_explicit_cast_accepted, test_same_domain_float_arithmetic_still_accepted. NO blast radius: typechecker 1902/0, codegen E2E 2043/0, interpreter 1108/0.

A float + unsuffixed-integer-LITERAL arithmetic expression (`let z = a + 1` where `a: f64`) diverges: `karac check` PASSES and `karac build` is CORRECT (both apply Q4 literal promotion — the typechecker re-records the literal's span as `f64`, so `1` becomes `1.0`), but `karac run` ERRORS at runtime (`operator 'Add' is not defined for operands of type 'Float' and 'Int'`). ROOT: the tree-walk interpreter's `eval_binary` does NOT consult the typechecker's promoted literal type (`expr_types`) — it evaluates the bare literal as `Value::Int` and rejects the Int⊕Float pair, unaware the typechecker already unified it to f64. Pre-existing and independent of B-2026-07-04-11 (that fix targets int/float VARIABLE mixes, which are now rejected on all three surfaces; this is the LITERAL-promotion path, which SHOULD succeed and does on check+build but not run). FIX: interpreter arithmetic must honor the recorded promoted type for an unsuffixed numeric literal operand (coerce `Value::Int` → `Value::Float` when the binop's other operand is a float and the literal's recorded `expr_type` is a float), mirroring the codegen literal-promotion lowering. Reachability is high — `f64 + 1` is a natural pattern — but it fails LOUD under run (a runtime error, not silent garbage). FIXED (b8e3d3ab): a shared `promote_int_literal_for_float_peer` helper promotes a direct unsuffixed integer-literal operand to `Value::Float` when its peer evaluates to a float — gated on the AST shape exactly like the typechecker's Q4 rule (so a genuine int/float VARIABLE mix, a hard type error since B-2026-07-04-11, still surfaces under run rather than being silently coerced). Applied at all three interpreter scalar-arithmetic sites: `dispatch_lowered_op` (the `<type>.add(a, 1)` operator-lowering path that normal `a + 1` desugars to), `CompoundAssign` (`a += 1`), and the `ExprKind::Binary` arm (un-lowered contexts). run == build == default auto-par verified; regressions test_float_int_literal_promotion / _compound_assign / test_int_arithmetic_literal_unaffected. Interpreter 1111/0, codegen E2E 2043/0 (isolated; a concurrent-load run flaked 7 SOA-pop tests that pass alone).

title: SHADOW SOUNDNESS HOLE in the rolling-DP length-pin bounds-check elision (B-2026-07-04-6/10), found while auditing the nested-block follow-up. The after-fill invariance scans (vec_readonly_after / var_unwritten_after) recurse into nested blocks through a GENERIC walker that only inspects statement VALUES — it is blind to `let` patterns and assignment TARGETS buried in an inner block. So a NESTED shadow of the pinned Vec or of a bound identifier went undetected and the name-keyed pin wrongly applied. Two confirmed exploits on the prior main (6ca6fe44's parent): (a) `let mut dp=..; while j<n{dp.push} ; while once{ let mut dp=Vec.new(); while d<n{ acc+=dp[d] } }` — the inner EMPTY `dp` shadow got the pin → `dp[d]` OOB read → CRASH (exit 137); `karac run` correctly errors. (b) same but shadowing the BOUND var `{ let n=20; while c<n{ acc+=dp[c] } }` with dp filled to 3 → `dp[c]` read past len with the check elided → SILENT WRONG ANSWER (printed 15, no crash) — the worst class. A nested REASSIGNMENT `n=20` (not a rebind) of a `let mut` bound var was the same hole. FIX 6ca6fe44: `region_bindings`, an EXHAUSTIVE (no-wildcard) fail-closed collector of every name bound-by-pattern (`rebound`, counted) or assigned (`assigned`, target root) anywhere in v's after-fill scope INCLUDING nested blocks; the pin is refused if v is rebound there, or any bound identifier is rebound or reassigned there. Both exploits now panic cleanly, matching the interpreter. Regression: 3 unit (no_fire_nested_shadow_of_vec / _of_bound_var / _reassign_of_bound_var) + 2 E2E must-panic (nested_shadow_vec / nested_shadow_bound). Codegen E2E 2046 + ASAN 521 green.

title: Closed the last length-pin follow-up: NESTED-BLOCK fills. Recognition was function-top-level only, so a DP buffer built inside an outer loop (`while k { let mut dp=..; fill; use }`, the per-iteration-rebuild shape) or an `if`/`match` arm never pinned and kept its bounds checks. FIX 6ca6fe44: `for_each_block` (exhaustive, no-wildcard) drives the per-block fill recognition over the function body AND every nested block; each block is analysed on its own statement list with the invariance region scoped to the rest of THAT block. Guarded by an EXACTLY-ONCE rule — the Vec name must be bound exactly once in the whole function — so a pin (kept active to end of function) can never match a same-named Vec in a sibling/outer scope (the lingering-pin hazard: an inner fill's pin leaking onto a shorter outer `dp` after the inner block; verified via a two-sibling-`dp` adversarial that now correctly panics). Depends on B-2026-07-04-13's `region_bindings` for shadow-soundness. Verified: per-iteration-rebuild nested fill correct (run==build, 84); kata #62 still 105ms/correct. Regression: 3 unit (fires_on_per_iteration_rebuild / _fill_inside_if_block / no_fire_two_vecs_same_name_siblings) + 1 E2E positive (nested_block_fill). RESIDUAL: none known for the counted-fill-then-index class.
