title: S6c-12 slice 4 edge: a GENERIC container impl's trait DEFAULT method fails to resolve at the call site on the SECOND element monomorphization. `trait R[T: Sub] { fn lo(ref self)->T; fn hi(ref self)->T; fn span(ref self)->T { self.hi() - self.lo() } }` + `impl[T: Ord+Sub] R[T] for Column[T] { fn lo=self.min(); fn hi=self.max() }` (span inherited as a default), called as `ci.span()` on `Column[i64]` AND `cf.span()` on `Column[f64]`: the FIRST call type-checks, the SECOND errors `no method 'span' on type 'Column', did you mean 'mean'?` (order-independent — whichever call is second fails). CONTAINER-SPECIFIC and DEFAULT-METHOD-specific: (a) a REQUIRED method on the same generic container impl resolves for BOTH monos (base slice-4 case works — `doubled_sum` over Column[i64]+[f64] = OK); (b) the SAME generic-impl-plus-default shape over a USER STRUCT (`impl[T] R[T] for Pair[T]`) resolves for both monos; (c) a single element mono of the container default resolves fine (slice 3 concrete-target defaults also fine). So the fault is in the builtin-container method-resolution path's handling of a SPLICED default method across two receiver-element instantiations (likely the spliced Function AST is consumed/specialized in place on the first mono's container resolution, so the second element no longer matches). check/build-vs-run DIVERGENCE: `karac run` executes it correctly (interpreter has no such per-mono container-resolution state) — a false REJECTION under check/build, not a miscompile. Base generic-container-impl feature (required methods, multi-mono; single-mono defaults) is DONE and landed S6c-12 slices 1-3; this is the residual edge. Repro: scratchpad s4_twomono.kara. FIXED c495dda3 (Slice 4b): the ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS WRONG — this was a MISDIAGNOSIS, correct-by-design, NOT a container/2nd-mono/default-method bug. Real cause: the repro's bound is `T: Ord + Sub` and `f64` deliberately does NOT implement `Ord` (IEEE-754 NaN breaks total order; only the `F32`/`F64` WRAPPER types do — env_build.rs 'Floats deliberately excluded', design.md total-order-float-types). So `Column[f64]` CORRECTLY fails the `Ord` bound while `Column[i64]` passes — it's f64-specific, NOT order-dependent (verified: i64+i64 both pass, single f64 fails, swap order => f64 fails wherever it sits). `run` 'works' only because `karac run` executes past typecheck errors. The i64-vs-f64 asymmetry was mis-read as required-vs-default because the base slice-4 test used `T: Add` (which f64 DOES satisfy); with `T: Ord` the required methods lo/hi ALSO fail for f64. Real DIAGNOSTIC defect (now fixed): the bound-filtered impl surfaced 'no method span, did you mean mean' (naming the wrong problem). Fix: (1) render_unsatisfied_bound_message (exprs.rs) appends an `F32`/`F64`-wrapper hint when a float primitive fails Ord/Eq/Hash; (2) the not-found arm (expr_method_call.rs) detects a bound-filtered impl via new Env::first_unsatisfied_bound and surfaces the failing bound. Purely diagnostic (resolution decision unchanged). Correct usage = drop the spurious `Ord` bound (span needs only `Sub`; lo/hi call builtin min/max) => checks clean AND runs `8 3` for i64+f64. Tests test_float_ord_bound_hint_points_to_wrapper / test_generic_container_impl_float_ord_bound_actionable_message / test_generic_container_impl_no_ord_bound_ok.

S6c-12 slice 4: a GENERIC TENSOR impl's `T + T` operator lowers as an INTEGER add for a non-i64 element mono under `karac build`. `trait Doubler[T: Add] { fn doubled_sum(ref self)->T; } impl[T: Add] Doubler[T] for Tensor[T, [3]] { fn doubled_sum(ref self)->T { self.sum() + self.sum() } }` then `tf.doubled_sum()` on a `Tensor[f64, [3]]`: builds, then PANICS `integer overflow` at the `+` (the f64 sum bits are added as i64). The i64 mono is correct (12), and `karac run` is correct for BOTH monos (interp fine). CONTAINER-ASYMMETRIC: the exact same shape over a GENERIC COLUMN impl (`impl[T: Add] Doubler[T] for Column[T]`) compiles correctly for i64 AND f64 (12, 14) — so the Column mono threads the element type into the operator/`self.sum()` return but the Tensor mono does not (self's Tensor element defaults to i64, or the Tensor[i64]/Tensor[f64] monos collide on one mangled body — the generic-impl-method path via `make_generic_impl_method_function` may skip the `append_handle_mangle` / element-binding that S6a applies to bound-generic free-fn Column params). Here the overflow CHECK catches it (loud crash), but a bit pattern that forms a non-overflowing i64 add would be a SILENT wrong-answer miscompile → severity medium. Base generic-container-impl feature otherwise works: generic Column impl (i64+f64) and generic Tensor impl (i64) verified run==build (test_e2e_user_generic_trait_impl_over_container). Sibling typecheck edge B-2026-07-04-15. Repro: scratchpad s4_ten_f64.kara. FIXED 735c5717: root cause was NOT a mangle-collision but the generic-user-impl-method DISPATCH (compile_method_call, method_call.rs) binding the impl's leading type param T from the receiver. TWO coupled sub-bugs: (1) a Tensor[T,[3]] receiver's recorded instantiation carries a SHAPE arg ([3]) beside the element, and counting it tripped the explicit-binding `<= n_params` gate → T left UNBOUND, defaulting to i64 → f64 T+T lowered as checked integer add → overflow (Column, single-arg, unaffected — the asymmetry). (2) Even bound, T was sourced from that span instantiation whose element is the constructor LITERAL default (f64 for a narrow-f32 tensor from [1.0,…]) → f32 buffer read with f64 stride → SILENT garbage on BOTH Column and Tensor. Fix sources T from the container's REGISTERED (annotation-derived) element (column_var_infos/tensor_var_infos) via container_receiver_elem_arg + excludes Shape from the fresh-temp fallback gate. Verified run==autopar==build across f64/f32/i32/u32/u8 on both containers. Test test_e2e_user_generic_trait_impl_over_tensor_operator_widths.

PRE-EXISTING (repros on main today for a plain `struct { s: String }`, INDEPENDENT of B-2026-07-04-7): iterating an owned `Vec[<heap struct>]` by value and MOVING the loop element to a NEW owner inside the body double-frees at teardown (exit 133/134; runs correct then aborts). Minimal: `struct A { s: String } ... for a in items { let x = a; }` and the field-move form `for a in items { let w = A { s: a.s }; }` BOTH abort; the String-struct, nested-struct, and (post-B-04-7) Option[heap-enum] variants all reproduce. CONTRAST — CLEAN: a for-loop DESTRUCTURE (`for a in items { let A { s } = a; }`), a pass-by-value call (`for a in items { f(a); }` — f entry-copies), and an OWNED-LOCAL move (`let a = A{..}; let x = a;`) are all fine. So the locus is the WHOLE-struct (or field-into-new-aggregate) MOVE of a for-loop ELEMENT. ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, from probing): the for-loop element binding `a` is a bit-copy ALIAS of the container element, but `mark_for_loop_borrow_if_heap` only marks Vec/String/Option/Result element types as for_loop_borrow_vars (so their consume sites defensively copy via maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg) — a STRUCT/enum element type is NOT marked, and maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg only deep-copies Vec/String slots, so a whole-struct move `let x = a` neither defensively copies nor suppresses the container's per-element drain. Both `x`'s scope drop and `items`'s FreeVecBuffer element-drain then free the same buffer. Pre-B-04-7 the Option[heap-enum] struct had no element drop so it LEAKED here instead of crashing; B-04-7 (correctly) makes it droppable, so it now joins the pre-existing double-free class. Likely fix: mark heap-owning struct/enum for-loop elements as borrow AND give struct/enum a defensive DEEP copy at whole-move consume sites (the struct analog of maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg), OR suppress the container's per-element drain for moved-out elements. Broad for-loop-ownership blast radius — own slice. NON-BLOCKING for typical code (destructure + pass-by-value are the common shapes and are clean). See [[caller-retains-model-spike-phase0]], [[struct-drop-depth-invariant-and-option-blocker]].

Residual of B-2026-07-04-4: a heap `enumerate` whose `(i64, <heap>)` tuple is whole-COPIED downstream (`let X = <tuple>`) still gates to the loud dispatch-fail (NEVER a miscompile). The copy-free simulation in `try_compile_iter_adaptor_collect_to_vec` admits a heap enumerate only when the SINGLE owning tuple binding is threaded by identity to every consumption site; it REJECTS two exotic shapes that reintroduce a whole-tuple bit-copy: (a) a LATER param stage whose closure param name DIFFERS from the tuple's binding (the first downstream param), e.g. `enumerate().filter(|p| p.0>0).inspect(|q| …)` — the `inspect`'s `let q = <tuple>` copies the still-whole tuple; and (b) a NON-terminal `map` that returns the whole tuple (`enumerate().map(|p| p).filter(…)`, identity or re-tuple body) — its `let __icm = <tuple>` materialization copies it. Both are pathological (real code reuses the tuple param name or reduces the tuple before re-binding) and loud-fail cleanly. A robust fix would make `let X = <heap-aggregate-identifier>` a MOVE (suppress the source) in the ordinary codegen ownership path, or alpha-rename the closure param to the tuple binding in the desugar body — both broader than the contained B-2026-07-04-4 fix. karac run executes all of these correctly; codegen loud-fails (no miscompile). See B-2026-07-04-4, B-2026-07-04-2.
resolution: FIXED f1a5d49 (2026-07-07). The two rejected shapes — (a) a later param stage whose name differs from the tuple binding (`enumerate().filter(|p|..).inspect(|q|..)`), and (b) a non-terminal `map` returning the whole tuple (`enumerate().map(|p| p).filter(..)`, or a re-tuple `|p| (p.0,p.1)`) — are now SOUND, and the copy-free gate (plus its `copy_free` simulation of the desugar's name threading) is removed. The desugar always threads the enumerate tuple as a bare identifier (or a re-tuple of its fields), so each downstream `let q = <id>` is an ordinary Vec/String/tuple MOVE that suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg / compile_tuple retire at the source — no alias, no double-free. So the 'robust fix' the entry anticipated (make `let X = <heap-aggregate-identifier>` a MOVE) was ALREADY in place via the ordinary move-suppression; only the over-conservative synthetic gate remained. Verified run==build + LSan-clean across differing-param, non-terminal-map-identity, re-tuple-map, and multi-stage-differing-param shapes. Tests: e2e_iter_adaptor_enumerate_heap_tuple_downstream_copy_codegen (codegen), asan_b05_1_nonterminal_map_tuple / _diff_param_name / _retuple_map / _multistage_diff_params (memory_sanitizer).

title: Residual of B-2026-07-04-17 (struct case fixed 278e1a91): a BARE `Vec[<user enum>]` element MOVED whole to a new owner (`for a in items { let x = a }` over `Vec[E]` where `E` has a heap payload) still double-frees at teardown (ASAN: `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: double-free`; silent corruption without ASAN). The B-04-17 fix wires the for-loop-element defensive deep-copy ONLY at the STRUCT let-binding / struct-literal consume sites (`for_loop_owned_agg_vars` + `deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place` / `deep_copy_one_aggregate_field`); a bare enum element `let x = a` routes through the ENUM let-binding tracking, which has no deep-copy hook, so `x`'s enum-payload drop and the container's per-element drain free the same buffer. A struct FIELD that is an enum / `Option[enum]` IS covered (the struct arm recurses). Fix: mark bare non-shared user-enum for-loop elements too and deep-copy the enum payload in place at the enum let-binding site (`deep_copy_enum_heap_payload_in_place`, already `pub(super)`-adjacent), mirroring the struct arm. Repro: `enum E { A(String), B(i64) } ... for a in vec_of_E { let x = a; match x { E.A(s)=>.. } }`. FIXED 81ad98c (2026-07-07) — mirrors the struct arm exactly. `mark_for_loop_borrow_if_heap` now marks a bare non-shared user-enum element with a heap-bearing variant into `for_loop_owned_agg_vars`, and the enum let-binding site deep-copies the live-variant payload in place via `deep_copy_enum_heap_payload_in_place` (made pub(super)). That copier duplicates EXACTLY the `VecOrString` + `NestedStruct` payloads `emit_enum_drop_switch` frees (copy-depth == drop-depth: `EnumDropKind` has no other heap kind), so every non-shared heap-bearing enum is safe to mark — no separate copy-support gate needed. `Option`/`Result` stay on the `for_loop_borrow_vars` path. Verified build==run oracle + Linux ASAN/LSan for a Vec[enum] with a heap-payload variant and a scalar variant (both the copied and no-op paths). Gates: memory_sanitizer 534/0, codegen E2E 2054/0, non-codegen green, fmt+clippy --all --all-targets --features llvm clean. Test asan_forloop_bare_enum_element_whole_move_no_double_free.

Bound-generic trait method dispatch over a USER-TYPE implementor fails under `karac build` (works under `karac run`). `trait Doubler[T] { fn dbl(ref self) -> T; } struct Wrap { v: i64 } impl Doubler[i64] for Wrap { fn dbl(ref self) -> i64 { self.v + self.v } } fn apply[C: Doubler[i64]](c: ref C) -> i64 { c.dbl() }` called as `apply(w)` on a `Wrap` -> `karac run` prints 42, `karac build` errors `codegen: no handler for method 'dbl' on variable 'c' (method dispatch fell through)`. GENERAL, not stdlib-specific: reproduces identically with the stdlib surface traits `Reduce`/`ElementwiseOrd` when the bound-generic receiver monomorphizes to a user struct (`fn total[C: Reduce[i64]](c: ref C){c.sum()}` over a user `Pair` impl; `fn lo[C: ElementwiseOrd[i64]](c: ref C){c.argmin()}` over a user `Trio` impl). The CONTAINER implementors (Column/Tensor) work on all three surfaces because the concrete-receiver builtin intercept fires inside the mono body (the receiver stays a handle `ptr`); a user-struct implementor has no such intercept, so codegen's `compile_method_call` on the monomorphized `c: ref Wrap` receiver never finds `Wrap.dbl` and falls through. ROOT: the codegen bound-generic mono path resolves builtin/container method dispatch but does not lower a plain user-impl trait method call when the type-param receiver monomorphizes to a user nominal type -- it needs to resolve `<mono-target>.<method>` via the impl table the way concrete `w.dbl()` does. Run/build divergence (loud codegen error, NOT a silent miscompile). Pre-existing since the S6a bound-generic surface landed; latent because every Reduce/ElementwiseOrd/ElementwiseMap bound-generic TEST used a Column/Tensor receiver, never a user-struct implementor. Surfaced probing S6c ElementwiseOrd user impls (the ElementwiseOrd container + user-impl-over-container paths all work on 3 surfaces = full Reduce parity; only this general user-type-under-build path lags, matching Reduce's own pre-existing behavior). Repro: scratchpad plain_bound.kara / reduce_usertype.kara / eo_usertype.kara. FIXED (4f3e5747, S6c-14): the mono param-type-name registration (compile_mono_function, mono.rs) only matched a bare `TypeKind::Path` param, so a `ref C`/`mut ref C` receiver never recorded var_type_names[c]=<concrete> -> inferred_receiver_type(c) returned None inside the mono and the <Type>.<m> user-impl dispatch was skipped. Fix peels a leading ref/mut ref before the name registration (mirrors the enum_inst_var_types peel just below it). Receiver ABI already correct for a non-generic ref-struct param, so recording the name suffices. Verified run==autopar==build for ref/owned/mut-ref over a plain user trait + Reduce/ElementwiseOrd over user structs; codegen 2062 green. Tests bound_generic_dispatch_over_user_type (interp) / test_e2e_bound_generic_dispatch_over_user_type (codegen).

FIX: at every resolver error site that computes a UNIQUE candidate (E0100 UndefinedName module-binding rename + general single-fuzzy-match, E0104 UndefinedType single fuzzy, E0107 UndefinedLabel single nearby label), populate `.replacement` with the TextEdit spanning the misspelled token. Single highest-leverage B->A conversion in the compiler (whole E01xx did-you-mean family), adds no new analysis — the candidate is already computed. Surfaced by the 2026-07-06 diagnostic-fix-invariant audit (resolver family: 0 of 32 variants carry a fix today). See docs/diagnostic-fix-audit.md. FIXED (830831f): the E01xx did-you-mean family (E0100 UndefinedName, E0104 UndefinedType, unknown-module/unknown-item import suggestions) was already machine-applicable as of 76be2de. This commit closed the two named stragglers: (a) E_MODULE_BINDING_NAMING now carries a `.replacement` — a `name_span` field was added to ModuleBinding (the identifier alone, captured at parse) so the SCREAMING_SNAKE rename anchors to exactly the name, and `karac fix` applies `let myConfig` -> `let MY_CONFIG`; (b) E0107 UndefinedLabel now fuzzy-matches in-scope loop labels and emits a `did you mean` suggestion (prose). The label MACHINE replacement is deferred to B-2026-07-07-3: Break/Continue carry no label-token span in the AST, so there is nothing to anchor an edit to yet.

Complete design (all verified working when applied): (1) TYPECHECKER items.rs check_impl_block self_type guard (~1896) -- add `Vec`/`VecDeque` beside Column/Tensor to the type_is_fully_concrete branch so `self` in `impl Trait for Vec[i64]` is `Vec[i64]` not `Vec[]` (else `for x in self` types the element abstract `T` -> 'cannot mix i64 and T'); typechecker suite green (1921). (2) INTERPRETER value_type_name (interpreter.rs ~1687) add `Value::Array(_) => "Vec"` so the builtin-Vec fall-through reaches try_eval_impl_method keyed `Vec.method`; run == correct for direct `v.sum()` AND bound-generic `f[C: Reduce[i64]](c: ref C){c.sum()+c.prod()}` over a Vec. (3) CODEGEN helpers.rs make_impl_method_function (~495) thread Vec/VecDeque target args onto the synthesized `self` param so the body registers vec_elem_types[self]. (4) CODEGEN collections.rs compile_index (~1402) key the Vec index branch on container_recv (accepts SelfValue) not just Identifier so `self[i]` in the body resolves (Slice-5 self-index twin). (5) CODEGEN method_call.rs Vec dispatch (~2540): try compile_vec_method, and on its no-arm Err WHEN a user `Vec.<method>` fn exists, fall through to the generic user-impl dispatch (inferred_receiver_type -> Vec.method, branch ~2917). With all 5, DIRECT calls (v.sum()/v.prod() loop bodies) build+run correct on all 3 surfaces, and a SINGLE bound-generic loop-bodied method builds+runs. REMAINING BLOCKER: when TWO different loop-bodied user Vec methods are each reached via BOUND-GENERIC (mono) dispatch (fa[C](c){c.sum()} + fb[C](c){c.prod()}, or one mono both[C](c){c.sum()+c.prod()}) the built binary SIGTRAPs at runtime (exit 133) though the LLVM module VERIFIES (build succeeds) and `karac run` computes correct answers. Repro matrix: direct sum+prod (both loops)=OK; one bound-generic loop method + one bound-generic non-loop method (c.sum()loop + c.max()self[0])=OK; TWO bound-generic loop methods=SIGTRAP. vec_elem_types IS already in mono.rs SavedVarSideTables save/restore, and compile_vec_method's no-arm path emits no IR (both ruled out). B-2026-07-02-39 family (mono symbol / per-mono impl-method-instantiation collision) for the Vec.method impl fns; needs IR-level diff of the two monos to root-cause. Vec code NOT integrated (would ship a build-time SIGTRAP); design + repro recorded here for a follow-on to resume from the crash.
resolution: FIXED 6321ee8. The reported 'mono symbol collision / two-loop-method SIGTRAP' was a MISDIAGNOSIS. Real root cause: `for x in self` inside a user `impl Trait for Vec[i64]` body. `self` is a `ref Vec` receiver — an `ExprKind::SelfValue`, not an `Identifier` — so the for-loop iterable dispatch (control_flow_for.rs) fell through to the `_ =>` value path (`try_compile_for_vec_value`), which materialize-iterates-DROPS the source. Dropping the BORROWED receiver double-frees the caller-owned Vec buffer and its per-element heap: one loop method -> `free(): double free`; two -> heap corruption SIGTRAP (exit 133). A named `ref Vec` param never hit this (routes to the non-dropping `compile_for_vec_var`). The vec_elem_types mono save/restore and compile_vec_method no-arm path (earlier suspects) were red herrings. FIX: a `SelfValue` arm in the for-loop dispatch routes a container `self` (String/Vec/Slice/Map/Set, registered under name 'self') to the SAME borrow-path iterators as a named Identifier. The five documented plumbing edits were also applied as designed (typechecker items.rs self-type guard adds Vec/VecDeque beside Column/Tensor; interpreter value_type_name Value::Array(_)=>"Vec"; codegen helpers.rs threads Vec/VecDeque self-args; collections.rs compile_index keys the Vec branch on container_recv/SelfValue; method_call.rs Vec dispatch falls through to the generic user-impl dispatch on the builtin no-arm Err when a `Vec.<method>` user fn exists). NOTE: the ledger's claimed 'builtin-reduction body' shape (`self.sum()`/`self.prod()`) is NOT supported — even a plain `v.sum()` method form loud-fails in codegen ('Vec/String method sum not yet supported'; only the free-fn `Stats.sum(v)` form lowers), so the realistic blanket-Vec impl body is a hand-written loop, which now works on all three surfaces (run == direct build == bound-generic mono build), i64 and heap `Vec[String]` elements, LSan-clean. Tests: e2e_blanket_vec_impl_loop_body_mono_dispatch + e2e_blanket_vec_string_impl_loop_body (tests/codegen.rs), asan_b06_5_blanket_vec_string_impl_loop_no_leak (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs).

fix: fddfb9a
title: Borrow-returning fn (`fn f(u: ref String) -> ref String { u }`, and the `ref Vec` analog) writes out of bounds and segfaults under -O2/LLJIT. The returned ref binding is lowered through the owned-value move-out path (the Vec/String arm of `zero_source_move_cap`, src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs), which GEPs field 2 (`cap`, offset 16) off `slot.ptr` and stores 8 bytes to null the moved-from source's cap. But a `ref Vec`/`ref String` param's slot is an 8-byte POINTER into the caller's frame, not a 24-byte {ptr,i64,i64} struct held inline, so the store lands 16 bytes past the alloca and corrupts the stack. Invisible under -O0 (frame slack absorbs the write); the optimizer weaponizes the UB into a crash under -O2, and LLJIT JIT-compiles at ~O2, so the program segfaults there -- surfacing as EMPTY stdout on the JIT execution lane while the AOT test oracle (which did not trigger the crash at its opt level) stayed green. Exactly the run/build divergence class the LLJIT-productionization spike targets, exposed by running the codegen E2E suite under KARAC_TEST_JIT=1 on Linux (5 `test_e2e_borrow_return_*` cases). Confirmed opt-dependent: the SAME emitted IR runs clean at `llc -O0` and segfaults at `llc -O2`. FIX (fddfb9a): mirror the struct arm's inline-ownership guard -- only zero `cap` when the slot holds the Vec/String struct INLINE (`slot.ty == vec_struct_type()`); a `ref` slot (pointer type) takes no ownership and is skipped (a borrow has nothing to move-null). No AOT regression -- codegen E2E 2084/2084 on both the AOT and JIT lanes.

Always-JIT execution lane produced EMPTY output for every non-trivial program on Linux/ELF. ORC's process-symbol-search generator (LLVMOrcCreateDynamicLibrarySearchGeneratorForProcess) resolves the statically-linked `karac_*` runtime FFI via dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT), which on ELF only sees symbols in the executable's DYNAMIC symbol table (.dynsym). Rust links executables without exporting their symbols, so all ~500 karac_runtime_* symbols lived only in .symtab (measured 0/507 in .dynsym) and the JIT failed to materialize `main` (`Symbols not found: [karac_runtime_scheduler_start_dispatcher, karac_runtime_park_slot_new, ...]`), producing empty stdout + a materialize error. Every codegen E2E execution test failed under KARAC_TEST_JIT=1 on Linux: 1416 failed / 649 passed (the 649 passing were IR-assertion tests that never execute). macOS masked it entirely -- Mach-O's dlsym resolves main-image symbols without an export flag, so all prior JIT work (done on macOS arm64) looked green; the spike's own 'green' claims were platform-blind. FIX (199098e): new build.rs emits `-Wl,--export-dynamic-symbol=karac_*` for the JIT-hosting binaries + integration-test binaries on ELF targets (scoped glob keeps .dynsym lean vs a blanket --export-dynamic; no-op on Mach-O/Windows). The in-process test binary (tests/lljit_prototype.rs) additionally force-links the runtime + defines KARAC_SPAWN_SITES stand-ins so its own .dynsym carries the symbols. Also flush libc/Rust stdio in the runner one-shot exit path (the repl/test-batch paths already did; returning ExitCode from main does not reliably run libc's at-exit flush on glibc). Result: codegen E2E via JIT on Linux 1416 failed -> 0 failed (2084/2084); lljit_prototype 15/15, lljit_e2e 16/16.

REPL cross-type rebind crashes the JIT runner on Linux (1 test: repl_jit_cross_type_rebind_uses_new_value). After `let x = 5` (i64) then `let x: String = "hello"; println(x)` in a later cell, the fresh runner subprocess dies with a signal (exit code None) instead of printing `hello`. The equivalent PLAIN program `fn main() { let x = 5; let x: String = "hello"; println(x); }` runs correctly under the interpreter, AOT (`karac build` prints `hello`, exit 0), AND a plain in-process JIT compile (pinned by tests/lljit_e2e.rs::jit_e2e_cross_type_shadow_rebind_prints_new_value), so this is specific to the REPL cell codegen path (compile_to_ir_for_repl_cell + persistent-let replay of the shadowed i64 `x` alongside the new String `x` in one synthesized body) executed under the ~O2 LLJIT on Linux. Likely another optimizer-exposed UB in the same class as B-2026-07-07-4 (a stale i64 slot / scope-exit cleanup applied to the String rebind), or a REPL snapshot-replay codegen gap. Only surfaced once the JIT lane started running on Linux (B-2026-07-07-5); macOS repl_jit was green (platform-blind). NARROW: cross-type same-name rebind across REPL cells; the codegen E2E proof gate (2084/2084) and the `karac test` JIT batch (491/491) are unaffected. Repro: `cargo test --features lljit_prototype --test repl_jit repl_jit_cross_type_rebind_uses_new_value`. Belongs to Slice 5 (repl/test JIT-default) Linux hardening. Next step: emit the failing cell's IR and bisect llc -O0 vs -O2 to localise (the technique that cracked B-2026-07-07-4). FIXED (8ab9e79): root cause is `try_emit_snapshot_capture` (src/codegen/stmts.rs) — it suppressed the source slot's `cap` (zeroing field 2 of a {ptr,i64,i64}) whenever the snapshot `kind` was String/Vec, but `snapshot_capture` is keyed by NAME, so the cross-type rebind fired the branch for the replayed i64 `let x = 5` binding too, GEP-ing offset 16 off an 8-byte `alloca i64` and corrupting the frame (PC=0 under the tighter LLJIT frame). Same class as B-2026-07-07-4, different site. Fix: guard the suppress by the slot's actual LLVM type (`slot.ty == vec_struct_type()`) — the i64 binding has no cap to suppress and is skipped. REPL-only path (snapshot_capture empty off the REPL), no AOT/build/run impact; codegen E2E stays 2084/2084 both lanes; repl_jit 22/23 -> 23/23. All Linux JIT suites now green.

def4648
title: Typechecker accepted a return-position `impl Trait` with MULTIPLE distinct concrete witnesses — a run-vs-build divergence. `fn pick(b: bool) -> impl Rate { if b { Fast {} } else { Slow {} } }` typechecked with 0 errors (each branch independently satisfies `Rate`), but design.md § `impl Trait` (Existential Types) requires "one concrete return per monomorphization": a return-position existential has a single witness type. The interpreter (`karac run`) ran it via dynamic dispatch and printed the right answer; `karac build`/JIT REJECTED it (`with_provider` form: "cannot infer concrete provider type"; direct method-call form: "no handler for method 'factor' on variable 'r'"). Surfaced while building the L632 (runtime-typed provider) workload for the LLJIT epic — L632 is one SYMPTOM of this broader gap (a runtime-typed provider IS a multi-witness `impl Trait`). `dyn Trait` (real dynamic dispatch) is P1-deferred (design.md:735), so the v1-correct fix is Option B: reject at typecheck AND make the error run-fatal (`E0271` / `TypeErrorKind::is_run_fatal`, mirroring `AtomicMissingOrdering`), so `karac run`'s lenient path rejects it too instead of downgrading to a warning and dynamic-dispatching. check/run/build now ALL reject at the same phase — the divergence is fully collapsed, not merely narrowed pending Slice 6. FIX (def4648): the typechecker pins a single witness per return-position existential — `note_return_impl_trait_witness` (hooked in `check_assignable`) records each concrete witness flowing into the current function's return existential (matched by `SpanKey` origin; skips other-existential / non-concrete / Never / Error found types so generics + diverging branches don't false-positive), and `check_impl_trait_single_witness` (end of `check_function`) emits `E_IMPL_TRAIT_MULTIPLE_WITNESSES` naming the distinct witnesses when 2+ are seen. Covers `if`/`match` tail branches and explicit `return`s (both funnel through the return-position assignability check); state saved/restored so nested items don't leak. Single-witness `impl Trait` (incl. the same type on every branch) is unaffected. Tests: `impl_trait_return_multiple_witnesses_rejected`, `_via_explicit_returns_rejected`, `_single_witness_across_branches_ok` (tests/typechecker.rs). Gates: typechecker 1924/1924, full non-llvm suite green, codegen E2E 2084/2084 (AOT), fmt + clippy clean. Subsumes the L632 follow-on (the divergent provider case is now a typecheck rejection).

fix: 59ddabb
title: Ownership-checker FALSE POSITIVE: a closure that captures a Copy scalar (e.g. `i64`) and is returned is rejected as an escaping `ref` capture, though the program is sound. Repro: `fn make(k: i64) -> Fn(i64) -> i64 { return |x| x + k; }` — `karac check` emits `error[ownership]: closure with `ref` capture of `k` escapes its scope by being returned — the borrow of `k` would outlive its source` (RefCaptureEscapesScope), yet `karac run` executes it correctly (`make(1)(10)` = 11, `make(2)(10)` = 12) because `k` is a trivially-copyable `i64`: the closure captures it BY VALUE (a copy lives in the closure env), so there is no borrow to dangle. ROOT CAUSE: the escape check in `src/ownership/closure_escape.rs` (the `for (cap_name, mode)` loop, ~L89–102 of `check_closure_ref_capture_escapes`) fires for ANY capture whose inferred mode is `Ref`/`MutRef` and whose source binding is not ITSELF a borrow (`Type::Ref`/`Type::MutRef`). A read-only capture of an owned `i64` defaults to `Ref` mode, and the check has no exemption for Copy/scalar capture sources — for which a by-ref default is semantically a by-value copy, incapable of outliving its source. FIX SKETCH: skip the escape error (or re-infer the capture as `Own`/copy) when the captured binding's type is a Copy scalar (i64/f64/bool/char/small enums with no heap payload); only heap-owning / borrow-backed captures can actually dangle. IMPACT: this is the `[[ownership-checker-open-false-positives]]` class the ownership-model-mechanization spike scopes out — it gates HEAP-ENV CLOSURES (`fn make(k) -> Fn(...)` stored in a `Vec[Fn]`) out of the Slice-1 drop-soundness fuzzer's valid-program generator, so those shapes are not exercised by the oracle↔codegen differential. Closing this FP re-admits heap-env closures to the generator (spike § Slice 1 “Deliberately excluded”) and lets the differential cover them. NOTE: `karac build`/`run` TOLERATE ownership errors by design (only `karac check` gates), so this FP blocks `check`-gated workflows, not execution. Distinct from the FIXED closure CODEGEN bugs B-2026-06-22-2/-4 (those were miscompiles; this is a static-checker over-rejection).

fix: ac06b64b
title: PERF codegen-gap (no correctness impact): karac fails to strength-reduce the loop-invariant-base linear expression in kata #63's obstacle predicate, so the C/Rust parity kata #62 won (bce_length_pin, B-2026-07-04-6) does NOT fully carry to the obstacle variant. Measured on the Apple M5 Pro reference machine (arm64, clang 21 / rustc 1.95), K=1_000_000 rolling obstacle-DP: karac retires 5.75B instructions vs rustc -O 4.24B and clang -O3 4.21B — 1.36x MORE instructions (wall 190.4ms vs 161.0/161.3ms = 1.18x; the wall gap is smaller than the instruction gap because karac's IPC is actually HIGHER, 6.27 vs 5.75 — the extra ops are cheap well-predicted branches, so instruction count is the honest signal here, not wall-time). EQUAL-SAFETY CONTROL rules out the overflow-safety artifact: rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on adds only 32M instructions (<1%), because LLVM strength-reduces the predicate FIRST and then proves the reduced induction variable cannot overflow and drops the checks. karac pays for the overflow checks precisely BECAUSE it failed to strength-reduce first. ROOT CAUSE (from side-by-side disassembly of both _main inner loops): karac emits ~17 instructions/cell vs rust ~12/cell. The predicate is (i*7 + c*3 + k) % 13 == 0. rust/LLVM maintains the dividend i*7+c*3+k as a SINGLE running register incremented by +3 each cell (add x15,x15,#3) — zero adds to reconstruct it — then does the %13 divisibility check (umulh/lsr/madd) directly on it. karac instead REBUILDS the dividend from three components every cell with overflow checks: `adds x13,x10,x12; b.vs` (i*7 + c*3) then `adds x14,x13,x19; b.vs` (+ k) — 4 instructions/cell that rust reduced to nothing, and amplified because each re-add drags an overflow-check branch. Two secondary misses in the same loop: (2) no paired-load fusion — dp[c-1] and dp[c] are adjacent, rust fuses them into one `ldp x1,x2,[x17,#-0x8]` while karac emits two separate `ldr`s plus an extra address add; (3) an overflow check on dp[c]+=dp[c-1] that LLVM proves away for rust (counts are bounded by the path-count ceiling) but karac keeps (`adds...b.vc`). The %13 magic-multiply itself is well lowered in both. FIX HYPOTHESIS: karac's IR for the loop-variant linear index/predicate expression is not in the canonical phi-based induction-variable form LLVM's IndVarSimplify + LSR can recognize, so the expression is never strength-reduced and the overflow checks are never proven away. Direction: lower loop-variant linear integer subexpressions as phi-carried induction variables (and/or emit nsw adds / order the checked-arith lowering after LLVM canonicalization) so LSR can fold the re-adds and the no-overflow proof can drop the checks — the same class of frontend-IR-shape fix as bce_length_pin was for bounds checks. NEXT STEP: dump karac's -emit-llvm for unique_paths_ii.kara, diff the inner-loop IR against rustc's, confirm the missing induction-variable canonicalization, and check whether emitting the predicate dividend as an incremented phi lets LLVM reduce+prove it. NOTE: this replaced the kata's earlier cloud-container snapshot (x86-64) where karac read as 0.95x rust — that parity was an x86/container artifact and does not hold on the M5 corpus machine; the kata README's Benchmarks tables + parity prose still quote the stale container numbers and need an M5 refresh (separate follow-on). Evidence + full instruction/cycle table live in the kata README bench section. Repro: cd kara-katas/leetcode/1-100/63-unique-paths-ii/bench && ./bench.sh (then /usr/bin/time -l on target/unique_paths_ii_kara vs _c / the rust bins). FIXED (ac06b64b): the dominant cause — the strength-reduction miss (sub-issue 1) — is resolved by broadening karac's monotone-counter `llvm.assume(x >= init)` emission from index-only counters to ALL non-poisoned monotone counters (src/codegen/control_flow_bce.rs: drop the `index_used` gate + dead `collect_index_idents`). The obstacle predicate's `i`/`k` counters were used only in arithmetic, not as array indices, so they never got the non-negativity fact; without it LLVM couldn't prove `i*7+c*3+k` in-range and kept 2 `sadd.with.overflow` per cell, which blocked reassociation (hoisting invariant `i*7+k`) and forced signed `srem`. With the assume, the inner loop now matches rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on EXACTLY: one plain `add nuw nsw` + `urem`; overflow checks 5->3 (remaining 3 = `dp[c]+=dp[c-1]` + hash sink, which rust keeps too — equal-safety parity). Measured M5 seq: instructions 5.75B->5.19B, wall 190.4->178.8ms (1.18x->1.11x vs rust), sigma 10.9->1.1ms (the eliminated branches were the variance source). CORRECTION to the original diagnosis: sub-issue (3) `dp[c]+=dp[c-1]` overflow check was NOT a gap — rust-ofl keeps it too; it only vanishes under rust's wrapping release build. Sub-issue (2) paired-load fusion is a minor LLVM-backend residual. The remaining 1.11x wall gap is a SEPARATE Vec-fill/alloc idiom gap (kata's `Vec.new()`+push-loop with capacity-doubling reallocs vs rust's `vec![0;n]` single alloc_zeroed) — opened as [[B-2026-07-08-7]]. General fix: helps every loop whose monotone counter feeds arithmetic, not just kata #63. Gates: codegen E2E 2086/2086, par_codegen 153/153, fmt+clippy clean; kata sink 583461340 identical under run/build/KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0.
investigation: 2026-07-08 reproduction attempt (cloud x86-64 container, LLVM 18): NOT REPRODUCED on x86-64 or any arm64 cost-model LLVM 18 can target (cortex-a710/x2, apple-m1/m2/m3 — the closest proxy to M5, which postdates LLVM 18). Method: dumped karac's pre-opt LLVM IR for two faithful reconstructions of the hot loop — (1) the synthetic obstacle predicate (i*7+c*3+k)%13==0 + rolling 1-D DP dp[c]+=dp[c-1], and (2) a flattened 2-D obstacle grid grid[i*n+c] — and ran karac's exact pipeline (opt -O2 -> llc, same LLVM 18 karac links). Findings, consistent across ALL modeled arm64 cores incl. apple-m3: the linear dividend/flat-index is STRENGTH-REDUCED to a single running induction-variable register (sub/add of the constant stride per cell, used directly in the %13 madd — NO rebuild-from-3-components), the loop-invariant part (i*7+k / i*n) is HOISTED to the outer-loop preheader, and the overflow-check branches on the linear expression are PROVEN AWAY (all nsw, no trap edges). Measured ~9-12 instr/cell, at parity with rust — the 17-instr/cell defect described above did not appear. So the ledger's root cause (checked arithmetic defeating LSR/SCEV) is already handled: LLVM's O2 pipeline recovers the IV form from karac's current checked-arith IR; the fix hypothesis is effectively already realized. The only surviving overflow check is on dp[c]+dp[c-1] (memory-loaded values, genuinely unprovable without value-range info — rust with overflow-checks=on keeps it too; ledger point 3's 'rust proves it away' only holds for grid dimensions small enough that LLVM can bound the sum, which it cannot do in general). RESIDUAL: the gap is either (a) a stale measurement predating a prior IV/nsw codegen improvement, or (b) apple-M5-microarchitecture-specific LSR cost-model behavior that LLVM 18 cannot model. LEFT OPEN pending a re-run of kara-katas/leetcode/1-100/63-unique-paths-ii/bench/bench.sh with the CURRENT karac on the M5 corpus machine; if instr/cell is now ~12, close as already-resolved. No speculative codegen change pushed — the current x86/modeled-arm64 output is already optimal and a pre-reduction change risks regressing it.

fix: cfbf0e7
title: [FIXED] Raw-pointer instance methods (`.offset` / `.read` / `.write`) are spec'd (design.md § raw pointers, L3319/L3337) but unimplemented in codegen: `p.offset(i)` fails with 'no handler for method offset on variable p', and `.write` on a non-identifier receiver (a chained `p.offset(i).write(v)`) fails with 'no handler for method write on non-identifier receiver'. Blocks the sound *manual* FFI ownership-handoff round-trip (allocate a raw buffer in Kāra, fill it via pointer writes, hand the pointer to C, free via a Kāra export) — the alternative to the auto-boxing/auto-destructor sugar for additive-interop Slice 4. Also `p[i] = x` index-store on a raw pointer is rejected ('Index store on non-array type'). Fix: add dispatcher arms in `compile_method_call` for the inherent pointer methods on `*const T`/`*mut T` (offset/read/write/read_unaligned/write_volatile), including chained (non-identifier) receivers. Found while building the producer-mode FFI handoff; `forget` (the handoff primitive) shipped, but the round-trip needs these.

fix: FIXED (LLJIT Slice 6c prereq). ROOT CAUSE: `compile_for` (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs) peeled `.iter()`/`.into_iter()`/`.chars()`/`.bytes()`/`.step_by()` off the for-loop iterable but had NO arm for `.enumerate()`, so `for (i,v) in xs.iter().enumerate()` landed on the dispatcher's silent `_ =>` skip-body arm — the loop body was never emitted, so EVERY outer-variable mutation inside an enumerate loop was lost under codegen (not Map-specific: a plain `sum = sum + v` accumulator also stayed 0). NARROWED via: plain `.iter()` loop persists (len=3), enumerate loop does not (len=0); a plain-i64 `sum`/`count` accumulator in an enumerate loop reads 0 vs the interpreter's 60/5. FIX: added an `.enumerate()` arm to `compile_for` that recognises a 2-tuple pattern over an indexable receiver (`for_receiver_is_indexable`: Vec/Slice/array var), stashes the index sub-pattern in a new `Codegen.enumerate_index_pattern` field, and recurses on the inner `.iter()` receiver with the ELEMENT sub-pattern. The underlying `compile_for_{vec,slice,array}_var` loops already carry the storage index as their induction variable `cur` — which IS the enumerate index — so each now calls `bind_enumerate_index(cur)` right after binding the element, which `take()`s the stashed pattern (so nested loops don't inherit it) and binds it. Codegen-only: the tree-walk interpreter was already correct and is untouched. VERIFIED: examples/leetcode/two_sum.kara now prints `Found: nums[0]+nums[1]=9` under interp, AOT, and JIT (was `No solution` under AOT/JIT); full codegen suite 2086/2086, memory_sanitizer 557/0, new regression test `e2e_enumerate_loop_body_and_outer_mutations_execute` in tests/codegen.rs. COVERAGE: `.iter().enumerate()` over a Vec/Slice/array VARIABLE and over a struct FIELD (`obj.field.iter().enumerate()`, via the field-iter synth path) are both fixed. Still falling through to the prior skip (unchanged, rarer, follow-on): enumerate over array-LITERALS, index receivers, and Map/Set/String receivers.
title: SILENT WRONG OUTPUT (exit 0): under codegen (both `karac build` AOT and the Slice-6b `KARAC_RUN_JIT=1` JIT path), a `Map` insertion performed inside a `match m.get(k) { ... None => { m.insert(...) } }` arm WITHIN A LOOP is lost across iterations — a later iteration's `m.get()` misses the key that was inserted, so the canonical get-then-insert-in-loop Map idiom silently produces wrong results. `examples/leetcode/two_sum.kara` is the flagship case: the tree-walk INTERPRETER prints the correct `Found: nums[0]+nums[1]=9` (2+7=9), but the compiled binary AND the JIT print `No solution found` for every case, at exit 0. This is a genuine interpreter-vs-codegen divergence — surfaced by LLJIT Slice 6b routing `karac run` onto the same codegen as `karac build` (lenient interpreter-run had hidden it; the epic exists to expose exactly this class). AOT and JIT agree, so the defect is codegen-side, NOT JIT-specific. MINIMAL REPRO (mapiter.kara): `let mut seen: Map[i64,i64] = Map.new(); for (i, num) in [2,7,11,15].iter().enumerate() { let complement = 9 - num; match seen.get(complement) { Some(j) => println(f"pair {j},{i}"), None => { let _ = seen.insert(num, i); } } } println("done");` — interp prints `pair 0,1` then `done`; AOT prints only `done`. NARROWING (each tested interp==AOT except the last): (a) `m.insert(k,v)` then `m.get(k)` with NO loop and NO match -> WORKS (got 42); (b) insert in a PLAIN loop `for k in 0..3 { m.insert(k, k*10) }` then get OUTSIDE -> WORKS (got 10); (c) insert inside a `match m.get(5) { None => { m.insert(5,99) } }` arm with NO loop, then get again -> WORKS (post 99); (d) insert inside a `match m.get(k)` None-arm INSIDE a loop, get in the next iteration -> FAILS (miss). So the trigger is specifically loop + match-on-get + insert-in-arm together — likely the `match seen.get(complement)` scrutinee holds a borrow/temporary of the map (or a snapshot of its buffer pointer) across the arm, and the `seen.insert` in the None arm mutates through a path codegen doesn't reflect back into the loop-carried map slot (stale header/length, or the get's temporary aliases a pre-insert buffer that a realloc-on-insert leaves dangling). SEVERITY high: exit 0 with wrong output is the worst failure class and this is a textbook idiom. NEXT STEP: dump codegen IR for mapiter.kara, inspect how `match m.get(k)` lowers the scrutinee temporary vs the loop-carried map slot, and whether `insert`'s potential realloc updates the slot the next iteration's `get` reads. Repro files were in scratch during the Slice-6b verification; reconstruct from the snippet above.

fix: 776169c (non-generic) + generic/mono leg (this commit)
title: FIXED (both legs). A function that returns an owned, heap-owning STRUCT param leaked the arg buffer under `karac build`. NON-GENERIC leg (776169c): the caller's return-passthrough guard (`call_arg_flows_into_return`, B-2026-07-01-7) skipped the arg-temp drop when the callee CAN return the param, on the premise the callee FORWARDS the buffer — but a copy-supported heap struct param is ENTRY-COPIED at the callee (`make_aggregate_param_callee_owned` -> `deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place`), so the callee returns an INDEPENDENT copy and the original moved-in buffer (caller already suppressed its cleanup as a move) is orphaned. Fix: `arg_is_entry_copied_heap_struct` (call_dispatch.rs) mirrors the callee's entry-copy predicate; on the passthrough path the caller still registers the struct drop for an entry-copied arg (forwarded params — bare String/Vec, Map/shared/non-copyable Option, user-Drop via a Call arg — unaffected, preserving the B-2026-07-01-7 double-drop guard). GENERIC/MONO leg (this commit): the monomorphized call path had NO ownership handling — `compile_mono_function` (mono.rs) registered no owned-aggregate param drop (unlike `compile_function`) so a non-returned owned heap-struct param was never freed, and `compile_generic_call` did no caller-side arg-temp registration (unlike `compile_call`), so std.cmp `min`/`max`/`clamp[T: Ord]` over a heap Ord type leaked every arg buffer. Fix brings the mono path to ownership parity: (A) `compile_mono_function`'s param prologue calls `make_aggregate_param_callee_owned` for bare (non-ref) struct/enum params at the CONCRETE monomorph type (from `var_type_names`) — the returned param is move-suppressed by the existing `suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return`; (B) `compile_generic_call` registers the caller's arg-temp drop (`track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg`) gated by `!call_arg_flows_into_return || arg_is_entry_copied_heap_struct`, the same rule as `compile_call`. A+B are paired (the callee returns an independent copy, so the caller's original is orphaned without B). Ground-truthed balanced via a malloc interposer: generic `min(Name,Name)` = 4 mallocs / 4 frees; `gid`/`gpick` balanced. Validation: memory_sanitizer 559 (incl. the three new regression tests: asan_return_owned_heap_struct_param_no_leak, asan_generic_fn_returns_owned_heap_struct_param_no_leak, asan_std_cmp_min_max_clamp_heap_ord_no_leak) + codegen 2088 + par_codegen + lljit_e2e + all non-llvm phase suites green; NO double-free regressions. The par cooperative-cancel tests (test_e2e_par_branch_(err)defer_fires_on_cooperative_cancel) are pre-existing timing-flaky under parallel load — they flake on BASE too (3/4) and the affected program's binary is byte-identical with/without this change, so unrelated. SECONDARY (still open, separate): the ownership checker treats a generic trait-method value arg as a MOVE not a borrow — a user-written generic `min` (`match a.cmp(b) {...}`) is rejected at `karac check`; the baked stdlib min/max/clamp compile only because baked stdlib bypasses ownershipcheck. That is a checker-precision gap, not a codegen leak, and does not affect the shipped stdlib functions.

fix: this commit (characterization — no code change; Linux glibc shows karac already wins, macOS-only platform-allocator artifact, allocator surgery unwarranted)
title: PERF codegen-gap (no correctness impact): karac's `Vec.new()` + push-loop fill does not lower to a single sized zeroed allocation the way rust's `vec![0; n]` does — surfaced as the residual gap after B-2026-07-08-3 fixed kata #63's obstacle-predicate strength-reduction. On M5 seq, kata #63 is 1.11x wall / 1.23x instructions (5.19B vs rust 4.24B) behind AFTER the predicate loop reached exact rust parity, and the remaining delta localizes to the per-call dp-buffer construction. The kata builds dp via `let mut dp = Vec.new(); while j < cols { dp.push(0); j+=1 }`; at -O2 this lowers to an empty alloc (cap 4) plus a fill loop that, per element, tests `needs_grow` (j==cap) and on hit doubles capacity via `umax(2j,4)` and reallocs — so for the swept n in [2,33] each of the 1,000,000 calls does ~log2(n) reallocs (cap 4->8->16->32) + n grow-checks + n stores. Rust's `vec![0; cols]` is one `__rust_alloc_zeroed` (calloc) + zero fill, no per-element grow check, no reallocs. Same allocation-traffic class as the known OPEN Vec/String alloc gap (#405, ~2.7x rust). FIX DIRECTIONS (not yet chosen): (a) recognize the `Vec.new()` + counted `push(const)` loop idiom and rewrite to `with_capacity(n)` + memset (frontend peephole); (b) teach `push` codegen / the growth policy to presize when the loop trip count is a known SCEV; or (c) provide/lower a `Vec.filled(n, x)` builtin the kata + mirrors can call, matching rust's `vec![x; n]`. NOTE the kata<->mirror idiom asymmetry: the kara source uses a push-loop while the rust/c/go mirrors use sized fills, so this also affects benchmark apples-to-apples — worth a mirror/idiom review when fixing. Cross-ref [[B-2026-07-08-3]] (the now-fixed predicate half). Repro: cd kara-katas/leetcode/1-100/63-unique-paths-ii/bench && ./bench.sh; compare instructions-retired of target/unique_paths_ii_kara vs the rust bin (the predicate loop is now identical, so the delta is the fill). REOPENED 2026-07-08 (revert 3a4e6135): the 546a8c2 fix was REVERTED — bisect-confirmed it REGRESSED its own target kata #63 by +8.4% instructions (5.19B->5.62B, deterministic; neutral on #64). The fill peephole rewrote #63's `Vec.new()+push(0)` dp buffer to `Vec.filled`, and that construction change broke the obstacle-predicate BCE/strength-reduction that B-2026-07-08-3 (ac06b64b) installed. CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (the original reallocs premise was wrong): (1) reallocs are NOT the gap — `with_capacity` presizing gives zero improvement; (2) kāra's `Vec.new()+push-loop` codegen is EXCELLENT — 3.7x FASTER than rust's own manual push-loop (52 vs 194 ms on a 2M-iter fill+sum), so kāra's Vec is not deficient; (3) `Vec.filled` and the push-loop have NEAR-EQUAL instruction counts (~1.3B), and LLVM's LoopIdiomRecognize already converts kāra's fill store-loop to memset at -O2 (verified in IR — an explicit memset emit is redundant, no-op); (4) the ONLY reason rust wins #63 is its mirror uses `vec![0;n]` (`__rust_alloc_zeroed`/calloc) while the kata uses a push-loop — a benchmark idiom asymmetry, not a kāra codegen deficiency; (5) the true residual (kāra 53 ms / 1.32B vs rust 44 ms / 1.30B on the fill+sum micro, NEAR-EQUAL instructions but ~1.2x wall) is ALLOCATOR/MEMORY-bound (IPC) — rust's alloc_zeroed + allocator throughput vs kāra's malloc/free churn on 2M tiny per-call buffers — i.e. the [[#405]] Vec/String alloc class, NOT fill codegen. NET: the peephole addressed the wrong root cause AND regressed the target kata, so it is reverted; `Vec.filled` (the method) and the B-2026-07-08-10 stride test are retained. PROPER FIX (if pursued): profile the small-per-call-buffer alloc/free path (bump/arena allocator or per-call buffer reuse); LOW priority — it is a ~1.2x memory-bound gap on a micro-pattern, and kāra's Vec codegen itself is already strong. Any future fill peephole MUST A/B instructions on #63 (not just fill-only microbenchmarks) to avoid re-breaking the scan BCE. SLICE 2026-07-09 (safe half of fix-direction (c), NO auto-peephole): added a `calloc`-backed zeroed-alloc runtime entry point `karac_alloc_zeroed_or_panic(count, size)` (runtime/src/alloc.rs) + the `__karac_alloc_zeroed_or_panic64` wasm i64-dims shim (wasm_alloc.rs), and taught `build_vec_filled` (src/codegen/collections.rs) to lower an explicit `Vec.filled(n, 0)` — any statically all-zero-bits fill of a trivially-copyable element — to it, SKIPPING the malloc + runtime fill loop entirely. This matches rust's `vec![0; n]` (`__rust_alloc_zeroed`/calloc, OS-lazily-zeroed pages), closing the specific rust advantage the corrected diagnosis pinned in points (4)/(5) for the zeroed-fill idiom. Gated STRICTLY on a compile-time zero (int/bool/float all-zero-bits), so it never rewrites anyone's `Vec.new()+push` construction (unlike the reverted 546a8c2 auto-peephole) and therefore cannot re-break #63's obstacle-predicate BCE. IMPORTANT — this does NOT close the kata-#63 residual: #63 must keep its push-loop dp buffer (for the BCE), so its remaining gap is still the allocator-bound tiny-per-call-buffer churn (the LOW-priority [[#405]] Vec/String arena/reuse work), untouched here. Verified: runtime unit tests (calloc non-null + fully zeroed + degenerate 0-dims), IR (zero -> `karac_alloc_zeroed_or_panic`, no `filled.body`; non-zero -> keeps the fill loop, regression guard), E2E all-zeros readback, ASAN calloc buffer freed once (no leak/UAF), both wasm clippy arms green. Status stays OPEN pending the #405 allocator work. RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-08 (current main, fresh archives): #63 push-loop = 5.19B instructions (1.22x vs rust-ofl 4.26B; 1.11x wall) — the ac06b64b baseline HOLDS, NO regression. Independently re-confirmed on current karac that the `Vec.filled(cols,0)` construction REGRESSES #63 to 5.60B (breaks the obstacle-predicate BCE), so the push-loop stays the optimal shape and there is NO codegen win left to grab; the 1.22x residual is genuinely allocator/memory-bound (~1M tiny per-call dp buffers) = the broad #405 class. TAKE (recommendation): not worth #63-scoped allocator surgery; the fix belongs to a dedicated, corpus-validated #405 allocation-throughput slice — prefer a runtime small-object size-class free-list (Linux-LSan-gated) over escape-analysis->alloca. Two MEASUREMENT/ENV gotchas surfaced and fixed while taking this: (a) `karac build -o PATH` IGNORES -o and emits ./<stem> to CWD, so measuring a pre-existing target/ binary silently reads a STALE artifact (a Vec.filled-era 5.60B build here) and fabricates a phantom regression — a 5-build git-bisect chased it before catch; always rebuild to a clean dir and verify the sink. (b) installed archives at ~/.local/lib + ~/.cargo/lib were STALE (missing karac_alloc_zeroed_or_panic from 6d068281), so EVERY Vec.filled(n,0) program failed to link with the installed toolchain — rebuilt lean+full and refreshed both install dirs + target/release; verified a Vec.filled program links via default resolution again.
resolution: FIXED for concrete 64-bit-element (i64/u64/usize) Vecs (546a8c2): a new pre-size rewrite `fill_to_filled` (src/presize.rs) collapses `Vec.new()` + an EXACT counted `push(<integer literal>)` fill (both `for I in 0..BOUND` and `while IV<BOUND` with IV proven 0/step+1) to a single `Vec.filled(BOUND, LIT)` — fix direction (c), driven from the frontend peephole of direction (a). At -O2 this lowers to `alloc + memset` (the `vec![0;n]` shape): NO per-element grow check (the residual the `with_capacity` pre-size left — its self-referential capacity phi defeats SCEV), NO reallocs, and because `Vec.filled` sets len==BOUND directly, LLVM then proves idx<len and elides the downstream DP-loop bounds checks itself (subsuming the bce length-pin for this shape). Verified on x86-64 + LLVM-18-modeled arm64 (apple-m3): rolling-DP `dp[c]=dp[c]+dp[c-1]` inner loop drops from 6 pre-opt bounds checks + grow check to ZERO. Correctness checked interp==compiled across for/while/counter-used-after(fixup)/small-bound shapes. SCOPE: the rewrite fires only when the element type resolves to a concrete 64-bit int — narrow elements (Vec[i32] etc.) are EXCLUDED because `Vec.filled` itself mis-sizes narrow buffers (the compiled i64 literal vs i32 element stride) — that latent codegen bug is filed as B-2026-07-08-10; and UN-ANNOTATED bindings (element still a type variable at the `Vec.new()` initializer) fall back to the correct `with_capacity` path. So an un-annotated kata `dp` needs a `: Vec[i64]` annotation (or the B-2026-07-08-10 fix) to reach the memset lowering. M5 re-run of the kata bench recommended to confirm the wall/instruction delta closes for the annotated form. RESOLVED 2026-07-10 (Linux x86-64 / glibc measurement — the AUTHORITATIVE CI-gate platform): the gap DOES NOT EXIST on Linux; it was an Apple-M5/macOS-allocator artifact, not a karac codegen or allocator deficiency, so NO fix is warranted. Deterministic callgrind Ir + min-of-9 wall on this box (kata #63, the exact bench source, 1M-iter sweep): karac 5.186B Ir / 584 ms; rust -O 5.549B Ir / 745 ms; rust -O3 -Ctarget-cpu=native 5.261B Ir / 656 ms. karac wins on BOTH instructions and wall at EVERY rust opt level (the ledger's prior '1.22x behind, 5.19B vs rust 4.24B' was M5/arm64/macOS — the 4.24B is unreachable on glibc). callgrind function breakdown shows WHY the sign flips: karac's allocator cost is malloc 45M + _int_free 54M ~= 99M Ir (1.9%), served from glibc's per-thread TCACHE fast path; rust's vec![0;n] -> calloc bypasses tcache into _int_malloc 110M + calloc 68M + _int_free / _int_free_merge_chunk / _int_free_maybe_consolidate ~140M ~= 320M Ir (5.8%). So on glibc the allocator is karac's ADVANTAGE, the inverse of macOS libmalloc (nano + lazy-zeroed pages) where calloc is cheap. A matched-idiom Vec fill+sum micro (BOTH sides Vec::new()+push-loop, 2M iters) is even starker: karac 63 ms vs rust 259 ms = 4.1x FASTER on Linux, confirming the entry's own note that karac's push-loop Vec codegen is excellent (not the deficient side). DECISION: do NOT build the proposed thread-local small-object free-list. It would give ZERO Linux benefit (karac malloc is already 0.87% via tcache), risk REGRESSING that tcache fast path, and at best help a macOS micro-pattern that (a) is a ~1.1x platform-allocator gap on ONE idiom, (b) is already matched by the landed Vec.filled(n,0)->calloc lowering wherever a static zero fill applies, and (c) cannot be validated on the Linux memory-sanitizer/bench CI gate. Severity downgraded high->low and status closed as a platform-allocator characterization: there is no actionable codegen/allocator work on the authoritative gate. Reproduce: kara-katas/leetcode/1-100/63-unique-paths-ii/bench, build the .kara and .rs, `valgrind --tool=callgrind` for Ir + min-of-9 `time` for wall on any glibc host.

title: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE + kata fixed. Original report ('escaped f-string braces {{}} render wrong') was WRONG about the mechanism: Kāra's f-string brace escape is BACKSLASH — `\{` / `\}` — NOT the Python/Rust `{{` / `}}`. `\{\}` renders literal `{}` correctly in BOTH interp and codegen (verified). A bare `{` always opens an interpolation, so `f"a{{}}b"` parses as `a` + interpolate(`{}`) + `b`, where `{}` is an empty BLOCK expression of type unit — the kata author used the wrong (Python-convention) escape. examples/leetcode/valid_parentheses.kara used `{{}}`/`{{[]}}` expecting literal braces; FIXED to `\{\}`/`\{[]\}` (now interp == AOT == the Expected-output comment). RESIDUAL REAL BUG (low severity, degenerate — reachable only by deliberately interpolating a unit value, e.g. `f"{ {} }"` or `f"{()}"`): displaying UNIT diverges between backends — the interpreter renders `()`, codegen renders `0`. Neither is clearly 'right' (displaying unit is nonsensical). RECOMMENDED FIX: make a unit-typed f-string interpolation a TYPE ERROR (unit is not Display) in the typechecker — closes the divergence at the source for both backends and rejects the meaningless case; alternatively make codegen render unit as `()` to match interp. Not an LLJIT regression; predates the epic. Downgraded to low severity now that the only real-world occurrence (the kata) is fixed.
resolution: 2026-07-08 FIXED (the residual unit-Display divergence). `type_supports_display` (src/typechecker/derives.rs) listed `Type::Unit => true`, so a unit-typed f-string interpolation slipped past the interpolation Display check (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) and then rendered DIFFERENTLY per backend — interpreter `()`, codegen `0`. Changed to `Type::Unit => false`: unit is not Display (Rust has no `Display for ()` either), so the existing check now rejects it at typecheck with `type '()' does not implement Display; cannot interpolate in f-string` for BOTH the explicit `f"{()}"` and the degenerate `f"a{{}}b"` (where `{}` parses as an empty unit block). This closes the run-vs-build divergence at the source and turns the meaningless case into a clear error across every Display context (f-string / println / to_string). The kata (valid_parentheses) was already corrected to the backslash escape `\{`/`\}` earlier. Regression test: tests/typechecker.rs::test_unit_is_not_display_in_fstring. Full suite green after the change (nothing legitimately displayed unit): typechecker 1926, lib 863, interpreter 469, codegen 2097, clippy both cfgs + fmt clean.

title: CODEGEN GAP (blocks Slice 6c): built-in `Option[T]` / `Result[T,E]` values have NO Display support under codegen — neither in an f-string (`f"{opt}"`) NOR via `println(opt)` — while the interpreter renders them correctly (`Some(7)` / `None` / `Ok(..)` / `Err(..)`). `karac build`/JIT abort with `error: codegen failed: Display of a struct ... is supported when the argument is a variable or field access ... bind ... to a `let` first (user-struct Display, subtask-5 follow-on)`. IMPORTANT — that error message is MISLEADING for this case: binding to a `let` does NOT help. Verified: `let x = get(1); f"{x}"` (Option via variable) fails identically to `f"{get(1)}"` (Option via call result); `println(x)` fails too. The message is accurate only for USER structs/enums (which do render via var/field), not for the built-in Option/Result enums, which no Display arm handles — so an Option value (lowered to a tagged struct) falls through `fstr_render_part` (src/codegen/runtime.rs ~6417) and the `println` struct-arg path (~method_call.rs) to the generic struct-value error. ROOT CAUSE: `src/codegen/synth_display.rs` synthesizes Display fns for structs / Vec / Map / Set (`emit_display_fn_for_type`, `emit_vec_display_body`, `emit_map_display_fn`, `emit_set_display_fn`) but has NO Option/Result arm, and `expr_user_enum_name{,_any}` only recognize USER enums, so the built-in Option/Result enums route nowhere. FIX (a bounded codegen slice, ~150-250 lines + tests): add `emit_option_display` / `emit_result_display` (or a general built-in-enum Display) that loads the discriminant/tag, branches None -> literal "None" and Some -> "Some(" + <recurse: the payload's own per-type Display fn> + ")" (and Ok/Err similarly), reusing the existing per-type Display-fn cache for the payload; then route Option/Result exprs to it from BOTH `fstr_render_part` and the `println` struct-arg path BEFORE they hit the generic struct-value error. TEST MATRIX: Option[i64], Option[String], Option[user-struct], Some/None, Result[T,E] Ok/Err, and a nested Option[Option[i64]] / Vec[Option[i64]]. Also fix the misleading error message. This is one of the ~16 codegen gaps the Slice-6c blast-radius sweep surfaced (blocks lru_cache and any program that prints an Option/Result); closing it is prerequisite work for the 6c JIT-default flip. Not an LLJIT regression — a pre-existing codegen-vs-interpreter gap the epic's run->codegen routing exposed.
investigation: 2026-07-08 deep dive (traced the full Display path): the general enum-Display synthesizer `emit_enum_display_fn` (src/codegen/synth_display.rs) ALREADY handles Unit/Tuple/Struct variants and recurses into each payload field via `emit_enum_field_display` -> the field type's own Display fn — so Some(T)/None and Ok(T)/Err(E) are structurally covered. The blocker is TYPE PLUMBING, not the render logic: `expr_user_enum_name_any` explicitly excludes Option/Result (`tn != "Option" && tn != "Result"`) because they are GENERIC built-ins — the variant def is `Some(T)`, so `emit_enum_field_display` would call `llvm_type_for_type_expr(T)` on the unsubstituted generic `T`, not the concrete payload type. To render `Option[i64]` vs `Option[String]` the Display fn must know the CONCRETE payload TypeExpr, and codegen has no ready accessor: it consumes purpose-built side-tables derived from `TypeCheckResult.expr_types` in the LOWERING pass (e.g. `var_elem_type_exprs` for Vec element types), and there is NO Option/Result-payload-TypeExpr table. That is why even the VARIABLE case (`let x = get(1); f"{x}"`) fails, not just call results. CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION PATH (a real cross-cutting slice, ~2-3 files): (1) in the lowering pass, populate a new side-table from expr_types mapping Option/Result exprs (by var name AND by span) to concrete payload/ok/err TypeExprs; (2) add `emit_option_display_te(payload_te)` / `emit_result_display_te(ok_te, err_te)` modeled on `emit_vec_display_fn_te` (concrete-type-keyed cache; load tag word 0; None -> "None", Some -> "Some(" + payload Display + ")"; Ok/Err similarly); (3) route Option/Result exprs to them from `fstr_render_part` (runtime.rs ~6360-6428) and the `println` struct-arg path BEFORE the generic struct-value error, spilling non-place values to an alloca (as `render_user_enum_display` already does). Reuse `Self::option_payload_te` (param_own.rs:1257) to split `Option[T]`. The render machinery is done; the work is the payload-TypeExpr plumbing through lowering. Also fix the misleading 'bind to a let first' error message — the let does not help for Option/Result.
resolution: 2026-07-08 FIXED for the variable/place case (inline-primitive payloads). Implemented the payload-TypeExpr plumbing the investigation called for: (1) typechecker `record_pattern_binding_surface_types` (src/typechecker/patterns.rs) now records Option/Result let-binding surface types into pattern_binding_inner_types, mirroring Map/Set; (2) codegen let-path (src/codegen/stmts.rs) routes those through `register_var_from_type_expr`, which (src/codegen/types_lowering.rs) populates two new side-tables `var_option_payload_te` / `var_result_payload_te` (src/codegen.rs) via `Self::option_payload_te` / new `Self::result_payload_tes` (src/codegen/param_own.rs); (3) new `emit_option_display_te` / `emit_result_display_te` (src/codegen/synth_display.rs) load the tag word, branch None->"None"/Some->"Some("+payload+")" (Ok/Err likewise), reusing `emit_enum_field_display` for the payload; (4) both `try_compile_collection_display` (f-string path) and `compile_print` (println path, src/codegen/control_flow.rs) dispatch to them. Payloads are guarded by `is_inline_displayable_payload` (primitives + String/str/char/bool only) to avoid invalid IR on compound (boxed/wide-struct) payloads, which the 4-i64 aggregate reload cannot reconstruct — those still fall through to the (now-accurate) struct-Display error. Regression test: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_option_result_display_matches_interpreter (Option[i64]/Option[String]/Result[i64,String] via both f-string and println, interp==AOT). FOLLOW-ON (still open, tracked here): (a) the CALL-RESULT case `f"{cache.get(1)}"` / `println(cache.get(1))` is NOT yet supported — needs a span-keyed (not just var-name-keyed) payload-TypeExpr lookup so a bare call expr can find its concrete payload type; lru_cache still can't print an inline `cache.get(N)` (and has a separate pre-existing all-None logic bug). (b) compound (non-inline) payloads: Option[user-struct-with-Display] etc. still error. The 'bind to a let first' hint is now ACCURATE for Option/Result primitive payloads (binding does help). | 2026-07-08 FOLLOW-UP: the CALL-RESULT case is now ALSO fixed (`f"{get(1)}"` / `println(get(1))` with no intervening `let`). Added a span-addressed payload table `Program.display_option_result_types` (forwarded from `TypeCheckResult.expr_types` in the lowering pass, filtered to `Type::Named{name:"Option"|"Result"}`) → codegen side-table `display_option_result_types` → new `try_compile_option_result_display(expr)` (src/codegen/synth_display.rs) which splits the payload (same `is_inline_displayable_payload` guard), spills the non-place call value to an alloca (mirrors `render_user_enum_display`), and renders via `emit_option_display_te`/`emit_result_display_te`. Dispatched from both `fstr_render_part` (src/codegen/runtime.rs) and `compile_print` (src/codegen/control_flow.rs) after the variable-case arms. Also swapped into the stdlib-body span-table swap. Regression test: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_option_result_call_result_display_matches_interpreter. STILL OPEN follow-on: compound (non-inline) payloads (Option[user-struct-with-Display] etc.). NOTE: `examples/leetcode/lru_cache.kara` still does not build — but NOT for a Display reason anymore: it hit a SEPARATE pre-existing codegen bug (a struct with a `Map` field constructed inside an associated `new()` emits invalid IR) filed as B-2026-07-08-12, plus a pre-existing interpreter all-None logic bug. The Display gap this entry tracks is closed.

title: SILENT WRONG OUTPUT (exit 0): `Vec.filled(n, val)` (and the `Vec[val; n]` repeat literal, which shares `build_vec_filled`) mis-sizes the buffer for a NARROW (sub-64-bit) element type. `build_vec_filled` (src/codegen/collections.rs) sizes the allocation and the fill stride from `val.get_type()` — the COMPILED value type — not the destination element type. A bare integer literal compiles to i64, so `let v: Vec[i32] = Vec.filled(5, 7)` allocates + fills at 8-byte (i64) stride while every `v[i]` read GEPs at 4-byte (i32) stride: the buffer is 2x too large AND the slots are misaligned. MINIMAL REPRO: `fn main() { let v: Vec[i32] = Vec.filled(5, 7); print(v[1] as i64); print(v[2] as i64); print(v[3] as i64); }` -> the tree-walk INTERPRETER prints `777` (correct), the COMPILED binary prints `070` (v[1]=high half of slot0's i64 7 = 0, v[2]=low half of slot1 = 7, v[3]=high half of slot1 = 0), exit 0. Value 7 in v[0]/v[4] happens to read 7 by low-byte alignment, masking the bug on those indices. SEVERITY high (exit-0 wrong output). AFFECTS all sub-64-bit element types (i8/i16/i32, u8/u16/u32, bool, char) filled with an unsuffixed integer literal; i64/u64/usize/f64 elements are correct (stride matches). The push-loop path coerces the pushed value to the element width (see the 'narrow the value to element width' store in vec_method.rs) — `Vec.filled` does not. FIX: size the alloc and coerce/store `val` using the destination element type (available as `pending_let_elem_type` for a let-binding, or the `elem_te` TypeExpr already threaded for the heap-clone path), mirroring the push-store narrowing; fall back to `val.get_type()` only when no destination type is known. NOTE this is exactly why the B-2026-07-08-7 `fill_to_filled` pre-size rewrite EXCLUDES narrow-element Vecs (fires only for concrete 64-bit elements) — fixing this would let that rewrite (and hand-written `Vec.filled`/`Vec[v;n]`) be correct for all element widths. Cross-ref [[B-2026-07-08-7]].
resolution: FIXED (fa51734): `build_vec_filled` (src/codegen/collections.rs, shared by `Vec.filled` and the `Vec[v;n]` repeat literal) now derives the destination element LLVM type from the threaded `elem_te` TypeExpr (via `llvm_type_for_type_expr`) and uses it for the alloc size and every GEP stride, and coerces the scalar fill value to that width with `coerce_scalar_to_type` (truncate i64->i32 etc.), mirroring the `push` store's narrowing. Falls back to the compiled value type only when no destination type is known (e.g. a `Vec.filled(..)` not in a typed binding). No-op for aggregate/pointer (heap) elements and matching widths, so `Vec[String]`/`Vec[i64]` are unchanged. Verified interp==compiled for i32/u8/i16/bool/i64, the `Vec[v;n]` literal, and heap `Vec[String]` (memory_sanitizer green, no leak/UAF). Regression test `tests/codegen.rs::vec_filled_narrow_element_stride` reads the stride-sensitive middle slots. RESIDUAL: a narrow-element `Vec.filled(..)` with NO destination type in scope (not a typed let/field/arg — the `elem_te`-None case) still falls back to the value width; not observed in practice and left as-is.

title: Ownership-checker FALSE POSITIVE: a method call on a GENERIC-type receiver dispatched through a single trait bound (`a.cmp(b)` where `a: T`, `T: Ord`, and `cmp(ref self, other: ref Self)`) treated the `ref Self` PARAMETER `b` as a MOVE instead of a borrow, so reusing `b` after the call false-rejected with `value 'b' moved here, used again here` at `karac check`. A concrete-receiver call (`Name.cmp(b)`) borrowed correctly. This is the secondary finding split out of B-2026-07-08-6: a user-written generic `fn min[T: Ord](a, b) -> T { match a.cmp(b) { Greater => b, _ => a } }` was rejected at check (the baked stdlib min/max/clamp compiled only because baked stdlib bypasses ownershipcheck). ROOT CAUSE: the two ownership move-analyses both resolve a method call's param/self modes via `method_callee_types[span] -> method_param_modes[key]`, but the typechecker records NO `method_callee_types` entry for a type-param receiver (it feeds codegen/effect dispatch, which must key on a CONCRETE type) — it records only `method_typeparam_receiver[span] = "T"`. So the mode lookup missed and the arg defaulted to consume (`method_arg_is_borrow_position` returns false on a missing key). `method_param_modes` ALREADY contains trait-method keys (`"Ord.cmp" -> [Ref]`, collected from `Item::TraitDef`), so the modes were present but unreachable. FIX: (typechecker) `dispatch_typeparam_receiver_method`'s single-candidate arm records the resolved `"Trait.method"` key in a new dedicated `TypeCheckResult.method_typeparam_trait_key: HashMap<SpanKey,String>` (NOT `method_callee_types`, to avoid misrouting codegen's `get_function(key)` / the effect seeds). (ownership) both move-analyses — the legacy `states` machine (`ownership/borrow.rs`) and the predicate pipeline / use-classifier (`use_classifier.rs`) — gain a `resolved_method_mode_key` helper that prefers `method_callee_types` and falls back to `method_typeparam_trait_key`; `method_arg_is_borrow_position`, `method_consumes_receiver`, and `method_self_borrow_kind` all route through it. This also fixes a latent UNDER-consume: a generic trait method with an OWNED `self` now correctly consumes its receiver (was defaulting to read). More correct, not less: `ref`/`mut ref` params/self resolve to borrow, `own` to consume — matching the concrete-receiver behavior exactly. Regression: tests/ownership.rs::generic_trait_method_ref_self_arg_is_borrow_not_move + generic_ord_min_body_passes_ownership. Validation: ownership 347, typechecker 1132, interpreter 345, resolver 323, effectchecker 1925, lib 855, codegen 2090, memory_sanitizer 560 — all green, no regressions. NOTE: the shipped baked stdlib min/max/clamp are unaffected (they bypass ownershipcheck); this fix makes an EQUIVALENT user-written generic pass check, closing the run-vs-check divergence for that shape.
