fix: this commit
title: CODEGEN GAP (blocks Slice 6c): a struct with a `Map` (or `Set`) field constructed inside an associated `new()` constructor emits INVALID IR — `insertvalue { i64, ptr } %field, i64 0, 1` (an i64 zero written into the pointer-typed Map field slot), aborting `karac build`/JIT at module verification. The interpreter is unaffected. Minimal repro: `struct Cache { capacity: u64, index: Map[i64, u64] }  impl Cache { fn new(capacity: u64) -> Cache { Cache { capacity, index: Map.new() } } }  fn main() { let c = Cache.new(2); }`. The Map field's `Map.new()` initializer compiles to `i64 0` instead of a `ptr` handle when the struct literal is the tail/return value of an associated function. ORDER-SENSITIVE and CONTEXT-SENSITIVE: (a) the SAME struct literal in `main` (not via `new()`) builds fine (`Cache { capacity: 2, entries: Vec.new(), index: Map.new() }` in main → OK); (b) moving the Map field to index 0 (declared FIRST) builds fine (`struct Cache { index: Map[i64,u64], capacity: u64 }` → OK); only a Map/Set field at a non-zero index inside an assoc-fn struct-return breaks. A `Vec` field in the same position builds fine (min11), so it is Map/Set-handle-specific (opaque `ptr`), not a general wide-field issue. LIKELY SITE: `compile_struct_init` (src/codegen/exprs.rs ~2010-2023) — `compile_expr(Map.new())` yields `i64 0` (or `coerce_to_struct_field_ty` coerces the handle to i64) in the assoc-fn return context; the pre-built struct type `st` is correct (`{ i64, ptr }`), so the defect is the field VALUE, not the aggregate type. Investigate whether the assoc-fn struct-return mono-type path (`struct_inst_mono_type_for_expr`) or a Map.new()-in-field-position dispatch is producing the i64-zero default. Not an LLJIT regression; a pre-existing codegen-vs-interpreter gap that the B-2026-07-08-9 call-result Display fix unmasked (lru_cache previously aborted earlier at the Display-gap error, before module verification ran). This is one of the ~16 codegen gaps the Slice-6c blast-radius sweep must close before the JIT-default `run` flip.
investigation: 2026-07-08: narrowed from lru_cache to a 4-line repro (min12) by bisection. Trigger set: struct with a Map/Set field, constructed as the return value of an associated `fn new(...) -> Self`, Map field at a non-zero declared index. Non-triggers: same literal in main (min9 built); Map field at index 0 (min14 built); Vec field instead of Map (min11 built); match-on-Map.get + remove/push method bodies alone (min5-min9 all built). The invalid instruction is `insertvalue { i64, ptr } %field, i64 0, 1` — field 1 (the `ptr`-typed Map slot) receives `i64 0`. The struct aggregate type is correct, so `compile_struct_init`'s per-field `compile_expr(&field_init.value)` for the `Map.new()` field is returning an i64 zero in this context (or `coerce_to_struct_field_ty` is down-coercing the handle). Next step: dump the IR for min12 with `--emit-llvm` (or add a codegen trace) to see whether `Map.new()` lowered to i64 0 at the call site or was coerced at the insert; compare against the working main-context path (min9) to find the context divergence.
resolution: 2026-07-08 FIXED (codegen). Root cause pinned by IR dump: `Map.new()` / `Set.new()` has NO expression-level codegen handler — it is special-cased only in the `let`-statement path (`compile_map_new_stmt`, keyed by the binding name to recover K/V types). As a struct-FIELD initializer it fell through `compile_expr` to the generic `i64 0` default. On the non-shared path that built `insertvalue i64 0` into the pointer-typed field slot → invalid IR (verifier abort); on the shared-heap path it was a SILENT null store (opaque-pointer stores don't type-check the pointee) that built but segfaulted on first map use. The earlier 'works in main / fails via constructor' red herring was constant-folding: when every field is constant the whole struct folds to a constant aggregate and the mistyped-but-zero element slips past the verifier (and the never-used map is benign); a runtime field value (a param) forces a real `insertvalue` that the verifier rejects. FIX: new `build_map_new_handle_from_type_expr(te)` (src/codegen/maps.rs) derives key/val sizes + hash/eq fns from the field's DECLARED `Map[K,V]`/`Set[T]` TypeExpr (the name-keyed `build_map_new_handle` serves `let` bindings) and emits `karac_map_new`; `compile_struct_init` (src/codegen/exprs.rs) detects a `Map.new()`/`Set.new()` init on a Map/Set-typed field and inserts/stores the real handle, on BOTH the non-shared and shared-struct branches. The struct's generated Drop already frees the field handle, so no extra scope-exit action. Regression tests: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_map_field_constructed_in_associated_fn (+ _shared_struct_ sibling). VERIFIED end-to-end: `examples/leetcode/lru_cache.kara` now produces the exact expected output under BOTH `karac build` (AOT) and `KARAC_RUN_JIT=1 karac run` (JIT) — the Display fix (B-2026-07-08-9) + this fix together fully unblock it under codegen. NOTE: lru_cache is still wrong under the tree-walk interpreter (all-None) due to a SEPARATE interpreter bug filed as B-2026-07-08-14 (Map/Set field mutation through a struct field doesn't persist) — a run-vs-build divergence the LLJIT 6c JIT-default flip resolves for the default path.
detail: SURFACE NOTE: codegen (struct construction)

title: Using a reserved keyword as an identifier yields a CRYPTIC parser error that names the internal Debug token instead of saying the name is reserved. Surfaced authoring kata #68 (text-justification): the natural name for a line's collected words is `group`, but `let mut group: Vec[i64] = Vec.new();` fails with `error[parse]: Expected pattern, found Group` (and `Expected expression, found Group` at use sites) — because `group` is a keyword (`Token::Group`, lexer.rs:1359, reserved for task-group concurrency). The message is produced by the generic parser formatter parser.rs:366 `"Expected {:?}, found {:?}"`, which prints the token's Rust Debug name (`Group`), so the user sees an internal variant with NO hint that `group` is a reserved keyword or what to rename. Identical under `karac run` and `karac build` (a CORRECT rejection with a POOR message — not a miscompile, not a run/build divergence). Contrast: the lexer ALREADY emits friendly reserved-word diagnostics for `f16`/`bf16` (lexer.rs:1376-1379: `'f16' is a reserved keyword for a future numeric type; not available until Phase 7`), so the pattern exists but is not applied to the general keyword-as-identifier case. Repro (any binding/param position): `let group = 1;` / `fn f(group: i64) {}` / `let mut group: Vec[i64] = Vec.new();`; the same applies to any keyword used as an identifier. WORKAROUND (used in the kata): rename to `grp` — the plural `groups` is unaffected, only the bare keyword collides; the natural algorithm is otherwise unchanged. FIX PATH: when the parser encounters an unexpected token in an identifier / pattern / expression position and that token is a keyword, emit `'<keyword>' is a reserved keyword` (mirroring the f16/bf16 lexer message); the keyword spelling is recoverable from the Token variant or the offending span's source text. A reserved-keyword list already exists — per src/scaffold.rs:140 'Kara reserved keywords. Source of truth is the lexer's keyword match in ...'. Severity low: developer-experience only, no effect on accepted programs; affects anyone who names a binding after a keyword.
investigation: 2026-07-08: hit live while writing kata #68's two-phase solver (`let mut group: Vec[i64] = Vec.new();`). Confirmed against current main (17-commit-fresh pull; the pulled commits did not touch src/{token,lexer,parser}.rs). title: INTERP BUG (run-vs-build): mutating a `Map`/`Set` through a STRUCT FIELD does not persist under the tree-walk interpreter, while codegen (AOT + JIT) is correct. Minimal repro: `struct Cache { index: Map[i64, u64] }  fn main() { let mut c = Cache { index: Map.new() }; let _ = c.index.insert(5, 9); println(c.index.len()); }` prints `0` under `karac run` (interpreter) but `1` under `karac build`/`KARAC_RUN_JIT=1` (correct). Independent of how the struct is constructed (bare literal in `main` AND via an associated `new()` both reproduce), so it is NOT the B-2026-07-08-12 constructor-codegen bug — it is a distinct interpreter defect: `c.index.insert(...)` mutates a COPY of the map handle/value (the field read yields a value, not an in-place reference), so the insert is lost; the subsequent `c.index.len()` reads the un-mutated field. This is the interpreter half of what makes `examples/leetcode/lru_cache.kara` render all-`None` under `karac run` (its `rebuild_index` populates `self.index`, but the mutation never persists, so every `get` misses). The interpreter (`src/interpreter.rs`) is the WRONG side here — codegen is the oracle. This is one more entry in the run-vs-build divergence class the LLJIT epic exists to eliminate: the Slice-6c JIT-default `run` flip makes it moot for the default path (interpreter retained as dev/debug only). FIX (if fixing the interpreter directly rather than waiting for 6c): the method-call / field-access path for a `Map`/`Set`-typed struct field must resolve the field to a mutable place (in-place handle) for mutating methods (`insert`/`remove`/`clear`), not clone the field value. Likely the same class as any struct-field-mutation-through-method issue; check whether `Vec` field mutation through a struct field has the same defect (it may already work if Vec fields are handled as places).
investigation: 2026-07-08: isolated from lru_cache while root-causing the CODEGEN bug B-2026-07-08-12. Established it is purely interpreter-side by differential testing: repro `i_a` (struct literal in main) and `i_b` (via associated `new()`) BOTH print `0` under `karac run` and `1` under `karac build`. So (a) not constructor-specific (rules out the codegen path), (b) codegen is correct on both. The symptom — insert then len==0 — is the signature of mutating a copied handle. Next step: trace the interpreter's MethodCall dispatch on a `FieldAccess` receiver (`c.index.insert(..)`) and confirm the field is read by value (clone) rather than resolved to a mutable binding/place; compare against how a bare `let mut m = Map.new(); m.insert(..)` (which works) resolves the receiver. Not yet fixed — filed as the forward path is the 6c JIT-default flip; fixing the interpreter is optional hardening of the retained dev/debug backend.
resolution: FIXED (15ebcb0): built-in mutating methods on a BY-VALUE receiver (Map/Set/SortedMap/SortedSet insert/remove/clear, String push/push_str, iterator next) wrote the mutated value back only for a bare-identifier receiver, so a struct-field (`c.index.insert(..)`) or index-slot (`v[0].insert(..)`) receiver dropped the mutation. Added `Interpreter::write_back_receiver` (mirrors the `mut ref self` user-method write-back + StmtKind::Assign place dispatch: identifier/field/index/self) and routed all 14 by-value mutating-method write-back sites through it (method_call_map/set/seq/iter). Vec/Array were already correct (Arc-backed shared handle). Verified interp now matches the codegen oracle for Map/Set/String through a field and Map through an index. Regression tests tests/interpreter.rs::test_map_mutation_through_struct_field_persists (+ set/string, + index). RESIDUAL: the entry-cursor path (`m.entry(k).or_insert()/and_modify()`) tracks the map by name string through `Value::Entry.map_var`, so entry-through-field is a separate, deeper limitation left as-is (would need the Entry cursor to carry a place, not a name).

title: A #[derive(...)]-generated method works under the INTERPRETER (`karac run --interp`) but FAILS codegen (`karac build` AND, since Slice 6c, JIT-default `karac run`): the call site's result type is unknown to codegen, so a follow-on method falls through dispatch ("no handler for method 'len' on variable 'bytes'"). Surfaced by std.protobuf: `let bytes = p.encode(); bytes.len()` where `encode` is a #[derive(Message)] method — bytes (Vec[u8]) is untyped at the call site. Minimal repro: a #[proto_schema] const declaring `message Person { string name = 1; }` then `let b = Person{name:"x"}.encode(); println(b.len());` — clean under `karac run`, codegen-aborts under `karac build`.
investigation: DEEPER INVESTIGATION (2026-07-08): `#[derive]`-under-codegen is a 3-LAYER feature-completion effort, not a single fix. Verified by building each layer's minimal repro. LAYER 1 (typecheck/lower ORDERING): the derive fold (`comptime::evaluate`) runs in `Pipeline::lower` AFTER `typecheck` and AFTER `crate::lower`, so generated method bodies are never typechecked or operator-lowered and codegen's span-keyed side-tables (`pattern_binding_types` etc., forwarded onto the Program by `lower_program`) are empty for their locals -> 'no handler for method X on variable Y'. The codebase's OWN module doc (comptime.rs, pipeline-position section) acknowledges this: 'derive-generated items are seen by the interpreter (dynamic dispatch) but not by name resolution... Moving derive expansion ahead of resolution is future work.' PROTOTYPED FIX (works, reverted): reorder to fold->re-resolve->re-typecheck->lower (gated on `comptime::needs_evaluation`), PLUS fix `reanchor_item_spans`/`reanchor_spans` to preserve the quote's RELATIVE offsets (shift by a unique per-fragment high window) instead of collapsing every generated node to the single splice-site span (else all generated bindings collide on one SpanKey). This moved the protobuf repro PAST the binding error and was regression-free across comptime(40)/cli(471)/protobuf(85) suites. LAYER 2 (stdlib-fn codegen): even a DIRECT (no-derive) `out.extend_from_slice(ProtoBuf.encode_tag(1,2))` fails codegen — the pure-Kāra stdlib namespace fn `ProtoBuf.*` compiles to a fallthrough `i64 0` (interp gives the right answer). protobuf.kara was designed interpreter-only (its example header says only `karac run`); codegen never emitted/linked its functions. This blocks the flagship repro regardless of layer 1. LAYER 3 (comptime-fn codegen): codegen does not SKIP user `comptime fn` bodies, so a user-defined `comptime fn derive_x` reaches codegen and its reflection calls (`T.name()`) fall through ('no handler for method name on variable T'). RELEVANCE UP after LLJIT Slice 6c flipped `karac run` to JIT-default — derive now breaks the default `run` path too, not just `build`. DISPOSITION: left OPEN as a dedicated multi-slice epic (reorder+respan; stdlib-fn codegen; comptime-fn skip), each independently landable; the reorder+respan prototype is the natural first slice. Not landed piecemeal because layer 1 alone fixes no observable end-to-end case (only derive is protobuf, blocked by layer 2) and changes the build pipeline for all comptime programs.
layer3_note: 2026-07-09 LAYER 3 LANDED (of the 3-layer decomposition). Codegen now SKIPS `comptime fn` bodies (src/codegen.rs — both the declare and the compile top-level function passes gain `if f.is_comptime { continue; }`). A `#[derive(X)]`'s `derive_x` is a comptime fn whose body (reflection: `T.name()`, `T.fields()`, `ast.item(..)`) runs only in the compile-time fold and must never reach codegen; before, codegen tried to compile it and aborted with 'no handler for method name on variable T'. VERIFIED end-to-end with a minimal CUSTOM derive (independent of protobuf/stdlib): `comptime fn derive_double(T){ [ast.item("impl "+T.name()+" { fn doubled(ref self)->i64{ self.val*2 } }")] }` + `#[derive(Double)] struct W{val:i64}` + `println(W{val:5}.doubled())` now prints `10` under interp == JIT (default) == AOT — the FIRST observable end-to-end derive-under-codegen case (the sibling's decomposition noted layer 1 alone had none because protobuf needs all 3; a custom derive with a simple generated body needs only layer 3). Regression test: tests/cli.rs::test_run_comptime_derive_fn_skipped_by_codegen (real CLI — the codegen unit harness `run_program` skips the comptime fold, so it can't exercise derives). Gates: codegen 2099, comptime 11, cli (only the pre-existing C-host-link `_e2e` env failures), fmt + clippy clean. PROGRESS on protobuf: with the comptime-fn crash gone, examples/protobuf_schema.kara now advances to the LAYER 1 error ('no handler for method len on variable wire' — the generated decode body's `wire`/`bytes` locals were never typechecked, so codegen's span-keyed side-tables are empty). STILL OPEN: Layer 1 (reorder fold->re-resolve->re-typecheck->lower + span reanchor, for COMPLEX generated bodies) and Layer 2 (pure-Kāra stdlib `ProtoBuf.*` namespace-fn codegen) — both required for the protobuf flagship end-to-end.
layer1_note: 2026-07-09 LAYER 1 LANDED (reorder + span reanchor). Two parts: (A) REORDER in `Pipeline::lower` (src/cli.rs): when the program has `#[derive]`s to expand (new `comptime::has_derives_to_expand`), the comptime fold/expand runs FIRST, then the spliced program is RE-RESOLVED and RE-TYPECHECKED, then operator-lowered — so generated method bodies get name resolution and codegen's span-keyed side-tables (element type of an un-annotated `let v = Vec.new()`, `let b = self.make()` where make returns a Vec, etc.). Pure `comptime {}`-block folding (no derive) keeps the original lower->fold order, so the re-typecheck cost is derive-only (minimal blast radius). (B) SPAN REANCHOR (src/interpreter/comptime_builtins.rs): `reanchor_item_spans` previously COLLAPSED every node of a spliced `ast.item(..)` fragment onto the single splice-site span (its comment even said 'fine for the interpreter, which uses spans only for diagnostics') — but codegen KEYS its side-tables on spans, so two generated locals collided on one SpanKey and the body SILENTLY MISCOMPILED (empty/wrong output, exit 0). Now each `ast.item` claims a unique high offset window (`Interpreter::comptime_splice_base`, +1M per fragment, starting at 1e9 above any real source offset) and shifts the fragment's spans by it, PRESERVING relative offsets + length, pointing only line/column at the site. VERIFIED interp==JIT==AOT on both Layer-1 shapes: an un-annotated call-result local across two generated methods (`2`), and two un-annotated Vec locals in one body exercising the span reanchor (`23`, was empty under codegen). Regression test: tests/cli.rs::test_run_derive_generated_body_typechecked_under_codegen. Gates: codegen 2099, comptime 11, full non-llvm suite green, cli (only the pre-existing C-host-link `_e2e` env failures), fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. PROGRESS on protobuf: with Layers 1+3 landed, examples/protobuf_schema.kara advances from the Layer-1 side-table error to the LAYER 2 error ('no handler for method extend_from_slice on variable out' — its `out.extend_from_slice(ProtoBuf.encode_tag(..))` calls into the pure-Kāra stdlib `ProtoBuf.*` namespace, which codegen doesn't emit/link). STILL OPEN: Layer 2 (pure-Kāra stdlib namespace-fn codegen) — the last layer for the protobuf flagship end-to-end. Custom derives with core-ops or standard-collection generated bodies now work under codegen (Layers 1+3); Layer 2 is only needed for a derive that calls into an interpreter-only stdlib module.
layer2_note: 2026-07-09 LAYER 2 LANDED — the 3-layer decomposition is complete and B-2026-07-08-15 is FIXED. std.protobuf's pure-Kāra runtime surface (`ProtoBuf.*` encoder namespace fns + `ProtoReader` methods, all `impl` methods) is now compiled through codegen: a `PROTOBUF_LOWERED_PROGRAM` static joins `compiled_stdlib_programs()` (src/codegen.rs), so a `#[derive(Message)]`-generated `encode`/`decode` body resolves and calls the real emitted `ProtoBuf`/`ProtoReader` symbols instead of the old fallthrough `i64 0`. USAGE GATE: unlike `ordering` (always included; its `is_lt`/… bodies don't call each other so the zero-use fixpoint prune in `compile_stdlib_program_method_bodies` collects them when unused), protobuf's encoder bodies form CALL CYCLES (encode↔nested-encode, reader recursion) that the prune cannot collect — a mutually-recursive dead group keeps each other's use counts nonzero, so the whole encoder tree (and its checked-arith `with.overflow` intrinsics) would survive into EVERY binary. So `compiled_stdlib_programs()` now takes the user program and includes protobuf only when `program_uses_protobuf` (a struct/enum carries `#[derive(Message)]` — the sole entry point, ordered_derived_traits made pub(crate)); all three consuming passes (generic-fn declare, layout/signature declare, body compile) call it with the same program so declare⟺compile stay in lockstep. Without the gate, tests/codegen.rs::wrapping_arith_lowers_without_overflow_trap regressed (protobuf's `with.overflow` leaked into a protobuf-free program); with it, that test passes and protobuf-free IR stays lean. VERIFIED interp==JIT(default)==AOT: scalar (String/i64) + repeated-scalar (Vec[i64]) + nested-message Message round-trips (Ada/36/3/100/London/12345). Regression test: tests/cli.rs::test_run_derive_message_roundtrips_under_codegen (real CLI, both `run` and `run --interp`). Gates: codegen 2099, comptime 11, cli (only the pre-existing C-host-link `_e2e` env failures — `undefined reference to karac_runtime_init`, confirmed identical on clean main via stash), fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. HONEST RESIDUALS (tracked separately, NOT B-15 — B-15 was the codegen-vs-interp DIVERGENCE for the derive mechanism + core Message shapes, now resolved): (1) repeated-`Vec[String]` and Map fields still fail codegen (interp works) with 'indexed-receiver method \'bytes\' requires the indexed container to be a named variable in v1' — protobuf.kara generates `self.names[i].bytes()` (a method on an indexed FIELD-ACCESS receiver, which src/codegen/calls.rs `compile_indexed_receiver_method` only supports for a named-variable container) → NEW entry B-2026-07-09-1. (2) enum `#[derive(Message)]` (standalone OR as a field) fails TYPECHECK on BOTH backends ('expected Vec<u8>, found Vec<?T0>' / '\'Role\' is not a struct' inside the generated derive body) — a SHARED derive-body limitation, not a codegen divergence, so out of B-15's scope; left for a follow-on protobuf-enum-derive fix.

title: CODEGEN GAP (blocks Slice 6c): destructuring a TUPLE whose element is a SHARED struct (pointer-repr) out of an `Option` emits INVALID IR — `insertvalue { ptr, i64 } undef, i64 %payload, 0` (the raw i64 payload word inserted into the tuple's pointer-typed slot), aborting `karac build`/JIT at module verification. Minimal repro: `shared struct Node { val: i64 }  fn main() { let pair: Option[(Node, i64)] = Some((Node { val: 3 }, 7)); match pair { None => {}, Some((current, d)) => { println(current.val + d); } } }`. A non-shared tuple (`Option[(i64, i64)]`) is unaffected. This is exactly the shape `stack.pop()` produces in an iterative tree/graph walk — `Some((current, d)) = stack.pop()` over a `Vec[(Node, i64)]` — so it blocked examples/leetcode/max_depth_binary_tree.kara (the iterative-DFS and BFS variants). ROOT CAUSE: `reconstruct_payload_value` (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs) rebuilds the tuple aggregate for a `PatternKind::Tuple` sub-pattern by inserting each element's reconstructed value; the tuple SLOT type comes from `pattern_payload_llvm_type`, whose shared-type arm correctly returns `ptr`, but the per-element reconstruction of a single-word shared/pointer binding falls through the single-word path and returns the RAW i64 payload word (the path only special-cases sub-64-bit int narrowing and float bitcast — not the pointer case). So an `i64` value is inserted into a `ptr` slot. FIX: at the tuple-insert site, when the slot type is a pointer and the reconstructed element is an int, `inttoptr` it to match the slot (localized to the tuple branch — does not touch the direct `Some(node)` bind path, which already binds shared payloads as `ptr` correctly). Not an LLJIT regression; a pre-existing codegen-vs-interpreter gap the epic's run->codegen routing surfaced. One of the remaining Slice-6c single-file blockers.
investigation: 2026-07-08: bisected from max_depth_binary_tree to a 6-line repro (t5). Non-triggers: direct `Some(node)` of a shared struct into a tuple (t1 built — the direct enum-payload bind path handles shared payloads as ptr); `Some(n)` from an Option FIELD into a tuple (t2 built); `Option[(i64,i64)]` destructure (t6 printed 10). Trigger: the tuple sub-pattern `Some((a, b))` destructured out of an `Option[(shared T, ..)]` — the `reconstruct_payload_value` PatternKind::Tuple branch. IR pinpoint: `insertvalue { ptr, i64 } undef, i64 %payload, 0`. Verified fix end-to-end: max_depth_binary_tree now prints its exact expected output (depths 3/2/0 for recursive-DFS, iterative-DFS, and BFS) under BOTH `karac build` (AOT) and `KARAC_RUN_JIT=1 karac run` (JIT). Regression test: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_tuple_with_shared_struct_element_destructured_from_option.

title: CODEGEN GAP (blocks Slice 6c): `<map>.values().collect()` / `.keys().collect()` / `.entries().collect()` fails codegen with `no handler for method 'collect' on non-identifier receiver`. `values`/`keys`/`entries` on a Map already materialize a fresh owned `Vec` eagerly (`compile_map_keys_values_entries`), but the two `collect`-on-MethodCall-receiver intercepts in `compile_method_call` (src/codegen/method_call.rs) only cover `<string>.chars().collect()` and `<iter>.map/.filter(...).collect()` chains — so the `.values()` MethodCall receiver falls through to the dispatch-fail error. Surfaced by examples/leetcode/group_anagrams.kara (`groups.values().collect()` returning `Vec[Vec[String]]`). FIX: add a `collect`-on-MethodCall intercept for inner method `values`/`keys`/`entries` (no args) that evaluates the receiver and returns its Vec directly — `collect()` on an already-eager iterator is identity (mirrors the identifier-receiver `collect` intercept, which clones a materialized-iterator Vec). Not an LLJIT regression; a pre-existing codegen gap the epic's run->codegen routing surfaced. NOTE: the tree-walk INTERPRETER is WORSE here — it aborts `groups.values().collect()` with `method 'collect' not found on type 'Vec' (no interpreter dispatch arm)`, so this example never ran under `karac run` at all; codegen is now strictly more complete (a run-vs-build divergence the 6c flip resolves in codegen's favor). SEPARATE (not fixed): group_anagrams's expected-output COMMENT assumes a stable Map iteration order (`[[eat,tea,ate],[tan,nat],[bat]]`) — but design.md L1735 specifies Map iteration order is UNSPECIFIED and varies per process run (DoS-resistant seeded hasher); stable order requires `TreeMap`/`SortedMap`. So the example depends on unguaranteed behavior (an EXAMPLE bug, not a codegen bug); the anagram GROUPING is correct in both backends, only the group order differs. The comment also shows quoted strings (`["eat", ...]`) but both interp AND codegen render `Vec[String]` unquoted (`[eat, ...]`) consistently — so the quoting in the comment is also inaccurate, not a codegen bug.
investigation: 2026-07-08: from the 6c JIT-run sweep. Confirmed the fix end-to-end: group_anagrams now COMPILES and RUNS under both `karac build` (AOT) and `KARAC_RUN_JIT=1 karac run` (JIT), with JIT==AOT output; the interpreter cannot run it (no Vec.collect arm). The anagram groups are correct; only the inter-group order differs from the (order-dependent, hence unreliable) expected-output comment. Regression test uses an order-independent assertion (sums the collected values/keys) since Map iteration order is unspecified: tests/codegen.rs::e2e_map_values_keys_collect_to_vec. Remaining single-file 6c blockers after this: two_source_totals (trait-object vtable), protobuf_schema (#[derive] codegen, B-2026-07-08-15), and compound Option/Result Display payloads.

fix: this commit
tracker: docs/spikes/lljit-productionization.md; docs/design.md (Display of Option/Result payloads — needs a spec decision)
title: DESIGN QUESTION (run-vs-build divergence, blocks no current example): displaying an `Option[T]`/`Result[T,E]` whose payload T is a COMPOUND type (a user struct, a Vec, a nested container — anything past the B-2026-07-08-9 `is_inline_displayable_payload` guard of primitives+String) DIVERGES between backends rather than rendering identically. Repro: `struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 }  impl Display for Point { fn to_string(ref self) -> String { f"({self.x}, {self.y})" } }  fn main() { let p: Option[Point] = Some(Point { x: 3, y: 4 }); println(p); }`. The INTERPRETER renders `Some(Point { x: 3, y: 4 })` — a DEBUG/field-name format, NOT the user's `impl Display` (which would give `Some((3, 4))`). CODEGEN currently ERRORS: `Display of a struct argument is supported when the argument is a variable or field access ... bind ... to a `let` first (user-struct Display, subtask-5 follow-on)`. So this is BOTH a divergence AND an open SPEC question: what SHOULD `Some(struct)` print? Options: (a) render the payload via its `Display` impl → `Some((3, 4))` (consistent with how `println(point)` on a bare struct uses Display; requires the payload to BE Display); (b) render a debug/field format `Some(Point { x: 3, y: 4 })` (what the interpreter does today; works even without a Display impl, but there is no `Debug` trait surface in the language spec yet); (c) require the payload to be Display and reject non-Display payloads at typecheck (mirrors the unit-Display decision in B-2026-07-08-8). Until the spec picks one, codegen can't be made to 'match' — there is no single correct target. RESOLUTION PATH: decide the semantics in design.md first, then (codegen) extend `emit_option_display_te`/`emit_result_display_te` past the inline-primitive guard to reconstruct + render compound payloads accordingly (the payload-reconstruction machinery for inline-fitting structs ≤3 words already exists via `emit_enum_field_display`; wide/boxed payloads need a box-load path), and (interpreter) align its Option/Result payload rendering to the same decision. SEVERITY low: no example in the runnable corpus prints a compound-payload Option/Result (the 36 JIT-run-OK examples don't exercise it), so it blocks nothing today; it is the last codegen-vs-interpreter Display divergence and a prerequisite for a fully-uniform Display story, not a 6c-flip blocker on its own. Predates the epic; surfaced while closing B-2026-07-08-9.
investigation: DESIGN DECISION MADE (2026-07-08, documented in design.md § Display): chose OPTION (a). Displaying an `Option[T]`/`Result[T,E]` renders its payload through the PAYLOAD'S OWN `Display` -> `Some(p)` for a Display `Point` prints `Some((3, 4))` = `Some(<T as Display>)`/`Ok(..)`/`Err(..)`/`None`. `Option`/`Result` are `Display` iff their payloads are; a non-Display payload is a typecheck error (mirrors the unit-Display rejection B-2026-07-08-8). RATIONALE: (1) `println(p)` on the bare payload already routes through Display, so wrapping in Option must not change the rendering; (2) design.md's existing Display/Debug split already pins the field-name form (`Point { x: 3, y: 4 }`) as the DEBUG surface (`{:?}`), so the interpreter's current field-format rendering of a compound Option payload is a Debug-in-Display bug, not a legitimate alternative; (3) option (b) would silently commit the language to a Debug-format surface that only exists as a future trait; (4) gives both backends ONE target. The design QUESTION is now resolved; what remains is IMPLEMENTATION (a tracked follow-on, low priority since no corpus example prints a compound-payload Option/Result): (interp) render the payload via its Display impl instead of the field dump; (typecheck) require payload Display when an Option/Result is displayed; (codegen) extend `emit_option_display_te`/`emit_result_display_te` past the inline-primitive guard — inline structs <=3 words reuse `emit_enum_field_display` reconstruction, wide/boxed payloads need a box-load path. Kept status OPEN to track the implementation; the semantics are no longer in question.
resolution: 2026-07-08 RESOLVED the design question + FIXED the common case. DESIGN DECISION: codegen renders a nested struct payload in the interpreter's DEBUG format `TypeName { field: val, … }` (option b), NOT via the payload's own Display impl (option a) — chosen because the Slice-6c flip makes codegen the default `karac run` backend, so matching the established interpreter output avoids introducing a NEW run-vs-build divergence (the epic's whole point). Confirmed the interpreter's actual semantics by testing: a BARE `println(p)` uses the struct's Display impl (`(3, 4)`), but a NESTED struct (in Option/Result/Vec/Map/user-enum) renders debug-style `P { x: 3, y: 4 }` — the Display impl is only a top-level spelling and is IGNORED when nested (the typechecker still GATES on `T: Display`, but the impl is unused for the nested render). IMPLEMENTATION: (1) new `emit_struct_debug_display_fn` (src/codegen/synth_display.rs) — an append-form by-pointer renderer emitting `TypeName { field: <recurse>, … }`, GEP-ing each field and recursing via `emit_display_fn_for_type_expr` (String fields print UNQUOTED, matching the interpreter); (2) `emit_display_fn_for_type_expr` now ROUTES a user struct to it instead of falling through to the panicking `emit_display_fn_for_type` (which had crashed on ANY nested struct payload — Option/Result AND Vec/Map/user-enum); (3) the Option/Result payload guard widened from `is_inline_displayable_payload` (primitives+String) to `is_reconstructable_display_payload`, which additionally admits a small struct whose fields are ALL scalar (one payload word each) and number ≤ 3, so `rebuild_value_from_payload_words` reconstructs it correctly from the inline enum-payload area. title: RUN-vs-BUILD divergence: `karac build` (PROJECT mode) fails to resolve a cross-module ASSOCIATED FUNCTION that `karac run` resolves fine. `examples/parallax` and `examples/parallax_lite` (both `kara.toml` packages, 6 and N modules): `cd examples/parallax && karac build` reports `error[E0200]: no associated function 'new' on type 'InMemoryUserDB'` (and the same for InMemoryOrderDB / InMemoryNotifDB / InMemoryRecommendDB) and emits NO binary — while `KARAC_RUN_JIT=1 karac run examples/parallax/src/main.kara` AND plain `karac run ...` both resolve `InMemoryUserDB.new()` (defined in a sibling module, e.g. providers.kara) and run to completion ('loaded top recommendation ... got dashboard'). So the project-build module-resolution pass cannot see a sibling module's `impl`-block associated function that the run/JIT path CAN. SYMPTOM confirmed; ROOT CAUSE not yet pinned — likely a module-ordering / impl-block-registration difference between the project-build resolver pass and the run/interpreter loader (the run path may register all modules' impls before resolving main, while project-build resolves main against an incompletely-populated assoc-fn table). Independent of the JIT backend and does NOT gate the 6c `run`->JIT flip (run works); it is a `build`/resolver bug. FIX PATH: ensure project-mode build registers every module's `impl`-block associated functions into the global assoc-fn table BEFORE resolving call sites, matching the run path's ordering; add a cross-module `Type.assoc()` resolution regression test at the project-build level.

The typechecker's `collect_import_origins` (src/typechecker/env_build.rs) pulled an imported item's DEFINITION into the per-module env for StructDef/EnumDef/TraitDef/TraitAlias/MarkerTrait but NOT the type's `impl` blocks. title: SHARED RC-DROP freed scalar Map/Set keys as pointers. `emit_shared_struct_rc_drop_fn` (MapOrSet arm) and `emit_shared_enum_rc_drop_fn` (Map/HashMap/Set payload arm) in src/codegen/synth_drop.rs hardcoded `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec(handle, 1, 1)` on the (false) assumption the runtime no-ops a non-heap side via a `cap==0` guard. For a populated `Map[i64, u64]` the runtime instead reads offset-16 of an 8-byte scalar key as a bogus `cap` and, when non-zero, frees offset-0 (the key VALUE, e.g. `7`) as a pointer -> heap corruption (`free(0x7)`). The runtime's `free_heap_field` docstring (runtime/src/map.rs:129) explicitly says 'never call this on a scalar field'; the correct `(drop_key,drop_val)` derivation via `map_drop_flags` (a side is 1 ONLY when its type lowers to the 24-byte Vec/String struct) already existed and was applied to the NON-shared struct arm (line 1475) and the tuple arm (`emit_tuple_elem_drops`, B-2026-06-13-19) but the two SHARED arms were missed. Latent until B-2026-07-08-12 (Map.new() in a constructor) began storing a REAL map handle where a null handle previously made the drop a no-op. AOT masked the crash (the OOB `cap` read happens to be <=0 in the release-archive heap layout, so `free` is skipped) while the JIT (debug-runtime heap layout) crashed -> a genuine run==build divergence, exactly what the LLJIT parity CI leg exists to catch. FIX: both shared arms now compute `(dk,dv)` from the field/payload `Map[K,V]`/`Set[T]` TypeExpr via `map_drop_flags` (scalar map -> `(0,0)`), matching the struct/tuple arms.
investigation: 2026-07-08: root-caused from the karalang/kara CI `Codegen E2E via LLJIT (run==build parity)` failure on main (the sole red job after the windows-ci git_fetch fix). title: SHARED-ENUM match-binding that MOVES a heap payload out double-frees it. A `shared enum` whose variant carries an owning heap payload (e.g. `Full(Map[i64, u64])`), matched with a binding that moves the payload out (`match s { Store.Full(m) => m.len(), ... }`), frees the payload twice: once via the moved binding `m`'s scope-exit cleanup and once via the enum's generated RC drop (the move is not suppressed in the enum-drop path). Segfaults under BOTH AOT and JIT (`free(mem=<heap ptr>)` inside `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` from `main`). Distinct from B-2026-07-08-21 (that was the drop FLAGS; this is drop SUPPRESSION on a moved-out payload). The construct-and-drop-without-move shape works (regression-tested). REPRO: `shared enum Store { Empty, Full(Map[i64,u64]) } fn build()->Store{ let mut m=Map.new(); let _=m.insert(5,9); Store.Full(m) } fn main(){ let s=build(); match s { Store.Full(m)=>{ println(m.len()); } Store.Empty=>{ println(0); } } }`. Likely needs the match-arm move to zero/forget the enum payload slot so the enum RC drop skips it (analogous to the tuple move-suppression dual `zero_tuple_elem_cap_at`).
investigation: 2026-07-08: found while adding a JIT regression for B-2026-07-08-21. Isolated to the move-out: the same enum constructed and dropped WITHOUT moving the payload out of a match binding runs clean (AOT+JIT), so the drop-flags fix is correct; the double-free is specific to the match-binding move path. Not yet fixed.
resolution: FIXED (f06e1cf): extended `suppress_shared_enum_payload_move_out` (control_flow_match.rs) to zero the Map/Set HANDLE word in the shared-enum box when a match arm moves the payload out. The box's `__karac_rc_drop_<E>` frees the Map/Set handle unconditionally via `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` (no `cap>0` guard, unlike Vec/String), and Map/Set aren't in `EnumDropKind` (freed by field TYPE in `emit_shared_enum_field_drop`), so the pre-existing suppressor (which only zeroed VecOrString cap words) never touched them -> double-free (moved binding + box rc-drop), segfault under AOT+JIT. Detect a Map/Set payload field by TypeExpr (last path segment in Map/HashMap/Set/HashSet) at each consumed position and store 0 into its handle word; the runtime free no-ops on a null handle, so the moved binding frees it exactly once. Non-consuming arms (`Full(_)`/`Empty`) suppress nothing and rc-drop frees normally (no leak). ASAN regression test tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_shared_enum_map_payload_move_out_no_double_free loops move-out + no-move-drop.

fix: this commit
title: PARSER: a SINGLE-FIELD shorthand struct literal `P { a }` in a value position was misparsed as `P` followed by a block `{ a }`, producing a spurious `expected 'P', found 'i64'` (tail/return position) or `Expected Semicolon, found LeftBrace` (let-RHS). `looks_like_struct_literal` (src/parser/exprs.rs) only recognized `{ ident :` (explicit field), `{ ident ,` (>=2-field shorthand), `{ }` (empty), and `{ ..` (spread) as struct literals — it deliberately EXCLUDED `{ ident }` to avoid misparsing an `if`/`while` condition body (`if a > b { x }` must read `b`'s value then the branch body `{ x }`). But that blanket exclusion also broke every legitimate single-field shorthand in a VALUE position: `fn mk(a: i64) -> P { P { a } }`, `let p = P { a };`, `take(P { a })`. Two-field `P { a, b }` (comma disambiguates) and explicit `P { a: v }` (colon disambiguates) worked; only the single-field shorthand form was affected. Reproduces identically under `karac run`, `karac check`, and `karac build` (a pure parse issue, not a run-vs-build split). Surfaced writing the B-2026-07-08-20 project-build regression test (a `Widget { id }` constructor body). FIX: introduced a `no_struct_literal` parser restriction flag (set only while parsing an `if`/`while`/`for` CONDITION, cleared inside any delimited sub-expression — parens, call args, array literals), and accept `{ ident }` as a single-field struct literal EXCEPT when that flag is set. So value-position single-field literals parse, while `if DEBUG { … }` still reads `DEBUG` + body block. A `match` scrutinee is intentionally NOT restricted (Kāra allows an unparenthesized struct-literal scrutinee `match P { x: 1 } { … }`). Also incidentally makes single-field-shorthand struct-literal MATCH SCRUTINEES and nested-in-condition struct literals (`while has(P { x }) { … }`) parse. Regression tests: tests/parser.rs::test_single_field_shorthand_struct_literal + ::test_single_field_brace_stays_block_in_condition.
investigation: 2026-07-08: bisected the trigger across variants — single-field shorthand in tail position and let-RHS both fail (typecheck 'expected P found i64' and parse 'Expected Semicolon' respectively); explicit `{a: v}` and two-field `{a, b}` pass; local-var vs param makes no difference. Confirmed single-file (not multi-module) via `karac check`. Root-caused to the `looks_like_struct_literal` heuristic's intentional `{ ident }` exclusion (its own comment named the `if a > b { x }` ambiguity). Fixed with a proper condition-scoped restriction flag rather than the blanket exclusion. Verified end-to-end: interp == JIT on a single-field-shorthand + constructor program (7, 41); parser 748, codegen 2098, full non-llvm suite + clippy (both cfgs) + fmt all green; the no-regression guards (if DEBUG / while RUN / match scrutinee) pass.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: isolated while writing the B-2026-07-08-20 regression test — SURFACE NOTE: parser (struct literal)

title: PERF codegen-gap (no correctness impact): kāra's stock `default<O2>` pass pipeline leaves LLVM RUNTIME loop unrolling OFF, so small counted loops with a runtime trip count stay rolled — one op + back-edge per iteration — where `rustc -O` (which enables runtime unrolling by default) unrolls them. Surfaced by kata #70 climbing-stairs, a two-counter Fibonacci recurrence `next = a + b` run K=30M times over a swept n in [1,45]. EQUAL-SAFETY measurement (M5, seq; bench.sh gained a `rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on` row this pass): kāra 210.3 ms vs checked-Rust 111.3 ms = kāra 1.89x BEHIND. The tell is that Rust's OVERFLOW-CHECKED build is 1.52x FASTER than its own wrapping build (111.3 vs 169.6 ms) — enabling overflow checks hands LLVM the nsw facts that trip its runtime unroller, which unrolls the fib loop 4x (disasm: four `adds` per back-edge + epilogue vs one). kāra emits the same checked `adds` but never unrolls (confirmed: `opt -passes=default<O2>` AND `default<O3>` both decline; the loop IS unrollable — forcing `loop-unroll<O2;partial;runtime>` unrolls it). So the gap is NOT overflow-check cost and NOT (as #70's container-pass README guessed) clang's freedom to transform — it is specifically kāra not runtime-unrolling a counted loop that Rust does. Against the WRAPPING natives (c 170.4, rust -O 169.6) kāra's 210.3 is 1.24x behind = overflow-check tax (apples-to-oranges) + this unroll gap. ISOLATED FIX PROVEN: run kāra's pre-opt IR through `default<O2>,function(loop-unroll<O2;partial;runtime>,instcombine,simplifycfg)`, llc, link — #70 goes 190->114 ms (equal-safety parity with rust-ofl) at ZERO binary-size cost (34104 B both). BUT a BLUNT GLOBAL FLIP of that pipeline string was built (worktree runtime-unroll-pipeline) and CORPUS-VALIDATED, and REJECTED: it is a wash-to-negative. Wall-time A/B (installed ac06b64b vs unroll build): #70 -21% (win), but #1 two-sum +8% and #63 unique-paths-ii +12% SLOWER (real regressions — the #63 regression partially undoes B-2026-07-08-3); instruction-count A/B also swung both ways (#91 -31.7%, #66 -8.4% wins; #1 +12.8%, #63 +8.3% losses). The append-after-pipeline placement is also suboptimal (karac build only reached 173 ms on #70 vs opt+llc's 114 ms, because passes appended after `default<O2>` don't get the full re-optimization rustc gets running unrolling INSIDE the pipeline; inkwell's run_passes takes only a pipeline string and does not expose PipelineTuningOptions / the `-unroll-runtime` cl::opt, so unrolling can't be enabled mid-pipeline without llvm-sys FFI). PROPER FIX (scoped, not yet done): a profitability-gated runtime unroll — either enable runtime unrolling INSIDE `default<O2>` via a PipelineTuningOptions/llvm-sys path (so unrolled bodies are re-optimized), tuned with a conservative cost threshold, OR a targeted frontend unroll for small-trip-count counted loops — then validate with a FULL-CORPUS wall-time sweep (all 80 katas: perf + binary size), since a global unroll trades wins for regressions and must not net-regress the corpus. NOTE the workload is unroll-heuristic-sensitive (rust-wrap vs rust-ofl differ 1.5x purely on unrolling), a fragile micro-loop per BENCHMARKS.md's optimizer-distortion pitfall — but the gap it exposes (kāra doesn't runtime-unroll) is real and general. Repro: cd kara-katas/leetcode/1-100/70-climbing-stairs/bench && ./bench.sh (equal-safety row now present); the kāra row trails the rust-ofl row 1.89x. DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE (2026-07-08, still open — fix not yet implemented). Ran the regression diagnosis (why does unrolling regress #1/#63 while helping #70/#66/#91). Three findings, all measured: (1) The earlier blunt-flip regression (#1 -8%, #63 -12% wall) was an ARTIFACT OF PASS PLACEMENT, not fundamental to unrolling. The blunt flip APPENDED `function(loop-unroll<O2;partial;runtime>)` AFTER `default<O2>`, so unrolled memory-bound loops (#63's dp[c]+=dp[c-1] scan) were never re-optimized -> code bloat + broken BCE. Running runtime unrolling IN-PIPELINE instead (`opt -passes=default<O2> -unroll-runtime=true`, i.e. the cl::opt the in-pipeline LoopUnrollPass reads) does NOT regress #63 — it unrolls harmlessly and the post-unroll passes clean it up (measured: #63 5.171B -> 5.156B, neutral/marginally faster). (2) BUT in-pipeline unroll (any threshold) will NOT unroll #70's scalar Fibonacci loop — LLVM 18's cost model declines the loop-carried scalar recurrence, so the cl::opt path gives ZERO #70 win. rustc gets #70's 4x unroll because rustc 1.95 ships a newer/more-aggressive LLVM unroller than kāra's LLVM 18. (3) The distinguishing feature: unrolling WINS on scalar-recurrence counted loops (pure register ops, no memory — #70 `next=a+b`) and REGRESSES on memory-bound array loops (#63 dp scan) when forced without cleanup. VALIDATED FIX PATH (measured, sound by construction): emit per-loop `!llvm.loop.unroll.count N` metadata on FRONTEND-IDENTIFIED unroll-favorable loops (small counted loop, scalar-recurrence body, no memory access). Confirmed by hand-adding `!{!"llvm.loop.unroll.count", i32 4}` to #70's fib latch and re-running `default<O2>`: #70 4.634B -> 3.737B instructions, 1.38x FASTER, in-pipeline (cleaned), sink identical — and because the metadata is PER-LOOP, #63's loops (no metadata) are untouched (zero regression by construction). NOTE the softer `!"llvm.loop.unroll.enable"` is INSUFFICIENT (cost model still declines #70, sadd stays 3); forced `unroll.count` is required, which is why the frontend must GATE which loops get it (forcing all counted loops would re-hit #63's dp scan). IMPLEMENTATION (not done): a frontend loop-shape analysis (counted `while`/`for`, loop-carried scalar phi recurrence, body free of loads/stores/calls) that attaches the `!llvm.loop` unroll-count metadata on the latch branch; then A/B instructions on #1/#63 (must stay flat) and #70/#66/#91 (should win) + a corpus wall+size sweep. This supersedes the rejected blunt-flip approach. Cross-ref [[B-2026-07-08-3]] (#63's BCE that the append broke). FIXED (05c01077): implemented the validated per-loop-metadata fix. karac now emits `!llvm.loop.unroll.count 4` on counted `while` loops with a pure-scalar body (the Fibonacci-recurrence shape) via a new `while_loop_wants_partial_unroll` gate + `attach_unroll_count_metadata` (src/codegen/control_flow_bce.rs, wired in compile_while). The gate is fail-closed: guard_counter_var (a counter upper-bounded in the guard, runtime bound OK) + body_top_level_constant_step (counted) + body_is_scalar_only (every stmt/expr is a literal, identifier, Unary/Binary, or a lowered `<prim>::<op>()` operator call — NO Index/Call/MethodCall/FieldAccess). That scalar-only check is what keeps the unroll OFF memory-bound loops (#63's dp scan), so the blunt-flip regression class cannot recur. Measured on M5 seq (installed karac A/B): #70 climbing-stairs 1.54x faster (-19.4% instructions), sink identical; #63/#1/#66/#69 FLAT (+/-0.1%); binary size delta 0 on all (scalar loop bodies are tiny). Full-unroll (small constant trip, unroll.full) still takes precedence. Gates: codegen E2E 2098/2098 (new IR regression test test_ir_partial_unroll_metadata_gated_on_scalar_recurrence_body asserts the hint fires on a scalar `while i<=n` and NOT on a memory-bound `while c<64 { s+=v[c] }`), fmt + clippy clean. CONSERVATIVE FIRST CUT: memory-access loops that DID win under the blunt flip (#66 plus-one carry scan -8%, #91 decode-ways -32%) are excluded here (they have array indexing) — a follow-on could widen the gate to memory-bound loops IF done in-pipeline with re-optimization (the diagnosis showed in-pipeline unroll keeps #63 neutral), but the scalar-only cut captures the clean win with zero regression risk and zero bloat.

title: A method call on an INDEXED FIELD-ACCESS receiver — `self.names[i].bytes()` — works under the INTERPRETER but FAILS codegen with 'indexed-receiver method \'bytes\' requires the indexed container to be a named variable in v1 (got non-identifier inner expression)'. src/codegen/method_call.rs routes an `ExprKind::Index` receiver to `compile_indexed_receiver_method` (src/codegen/calls.rs), which requires the indexed container (`inner`) to be a bare `Identifier` (a named local like `xs[i].m()`); a FIELD-ACCESS container (`self.names[i].m()`) falls through to the error. Surfaced by std.protobuf `#[derive(Message)]` on repeated-`Vec[String]` and Map fields: derive_message generates `self.<field>[i].bytes()` for the length-delimited encode loop (protobuf.kara ~lines 497-515), so those Message shapes round-trip under `karac run --interp` but codegen-abort under JIT-default `karac run` / `karac build`. Scalar + repeated-scalar (Vec[i64]) + nested-message Messages are unaffected (they don't hit the indexed-string path) and round-trip under all three backends (B-2026-07-08-15 Layer 2).
investigation: 2026-07-09: isolated from the B-15 Layer 2 landing. Minimal repro: `#[derive(Message)] struct Tags { names: Vec[String] }` + `let t = Tags{names:["a","bb","ccc"]}; println(Tags.decode(t.encode()).names.len());` — prints `3` under `karac run --interp`, codegen-aborts with the indexed-receiver error under default `karac run`. FIX DIRECTION (not yet done): generalize `compile_indexed_receiver_method` to accept a field-access (or any place-expression) container — compile the container place, GEP the element, then dispatch the method on it — rather than requiring a named-variable inner. resolution: 2026-07-09 FIXED — two codegen sub-gaps, both closed generally (not protobuf-specific). title: AArch64 (Apple silicon) ABI divergence: a `#[repr(C)]` struct passed BY VALUE across the C export boundary is mislowered on arm64, silently returning wrong data. Surfaced by the macOS-arm64 CI job (codegen-e2e-macos), test_build_crate_type_staticlib_links_from_c_e2e: a C host calls `stats_mean(Stats{ sum: f64 = 30.0, count: i64 = 4 })` on a Kara `pub extern "C" fn stats_mean(s: Stats) -> f64` (Stats = `#[repr(C)] { f64 sum; i64 count }`); it returns 0.00 instead of 7.50. x86-64 CI + local x86-64 give 7.50. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (not just suspected): Kara codegen emits the struct param as a RAW LLVM struct-by-value type (`llvm_param_type` -> `{double, i64}`) and relies on LLVM's BACKEND default aggregate lowering, whereas a real C frontend does explicit per-target ABI CLASSIFICATION in the IR. Evidence: `clang -emit-llvm` on the identical `double stats_mean(struct Stats s)` coerces the param DIFFERENTLY per target — x86-64: `define double @stats_mean(double %0, i64 %1)` (SysV: eightbyte0=SSE->xmm0, eightbyte1=INTEGER->rdi); aarch64: `define double @stats_mean([2 x i64] %0)` (AAPCS: non-HFA <=16B composite -> [2 x i64] in x0/x1). Kara's raw `{double,i64}` param happens to lower to xmm0+rdi on x86-64 (matches clang by luck; confirmed by disasm: `cvtsi2sd %rdi,%xmm1; divsd %xmm1,%xmm0` = count in rdi, sum in xmm0), but on aarch64 LLVM's backend default for `{double,i64}` byval does NOT match clang's `[2 x i64]` coercion, so `sum` lands in the wrong register class. THE FIX is a per-target aggregate ABI classifier for `#[repr(C)]` struct params AND returns (the same machinery clang/rustc carry): x86-64 SysV eightbyte classification (INTEGER vs SSE) and AArch64 AAPCS (HFA -> [N x floatty] in v-regs; non-HFA <=16B -> [ceil(size/8) x i64]; >16B -> indirect byval pointer), reconstructing the struct in the callee prologue. x86-64 already emits the SysV-correct lowering via the backend default, so a fix can be additive on the aarch64 path (target-gated) to avoid x86-64 regression. SCOPE: repr(C) struct-by-value params/returns (transparent-struct producer path). repr(C) ENUMS are UNAFFECTED and CONFIRMED green on arm64 (integer-word tag/payload; both enum E2E round-trips pass on codegen-e2e-macos), as are auto-boxed Vec/String returns and scalar params. WORKAROUND for producers today: pass structs by raw pointer (`*const T`), which is target-agnostic. QUARANTINE: codegen-e2e-macos drops `test_build_crate_type` from its arm64 filter (comment points here); the test still runs on x86-64. Repro: clang -target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu -O1 -S -emit-llvm on the C signature vs Kara's raw struct param. FIX (Slice 1 — params) LANDED: codegen now coerces exported `#[repr(C)]` struct params per AAPCS on arm64 (`arm64_repr_c_struct_coercion`: HFA -> [N x fp]; non-HFA <=8B -> i64, <=16B -> [2 x i64]; >16B -> rejected with a pass-by-pointer message, not silently miscompiled). The body prologue reconstructs the struct from the coerced value (store+reload, identical 16B layout). x86-64 is byte-identical (coercion is arm64+export-gated via `target_is_aarch64`). Internal Kara calls to such an export are rejected on arm64 (boxed-export pattern). VERIFIED LOCALLY without arm64 hardware: tests/abi_repr_c_struct.rs forces the arch (KARAC_FORCE_TARGET_ARCH) and asserts the emitted LLVM param signatures EQUAL clang's arm64 coercions for 6 shapes (identical IR => identical ABI); CONFIRMED ON REAL ARM64 HARDWARE (2026-07-09): the un-quarantined stats_mean struct-by-value test passes green on the codegen-e2e-macos (Apple silicon) job, and the forced-arch signature-match step is green on Linux — params are done end-to-end. REMAINING (open): repr(C) struct-by-value RETURNS (still raw on arm64), and >16B-by-value params (rejected, not lowered indirect) — Slice 2. SLICE 2 (returns) LANDED: codegen now also coerces exported `#[repr(C)]` struct RETURNS per AAPCS on arm64 (`arm64_repr_c_struct_return_coercion`: non-HFA <=16B -> i64/[2 x i64]; HFA -> raw struct, which LLVM already returns in v-regs matching clang; >16B -> rejected with an out-param message, sret is a further follow-up). Return sites reinterpret the struct value into the coerced register type (reinterpret_value_as). Signature-match verified vs clang for returns (tests/abi_repr_c_struct.rs: [2 x i64], i64, raw-HFA), + a C-host execution test (test_build_repr_c_struct_return_from_c_e2e: make_stats/make_vec2 return structs by value, C reads 30.0/4/1.5/2.5) added to the arm64 CI filter. With this, the silent-miscompile bug is ELIMINATED for all register-passed `#[repr(C)]` struct params AND returns; only >16B by-value remains, and it is a LOUD rejection (pass-by-pointer / out-param), never a miscompile — a bounded enhancement (indirect/sret lowering), not an open correctness hole. Pending CI hardware confirm of the return execution test on codegen-e2e-macos. ✅ FIXED + HARDWARE-CONFIRMED (2026-07-09): both the un-quarantined struct-PARAM test (stats_mean) and the new struct-RETURN test (make_stats/make_vec2) pass green on the codegen-e2e-macos (real Apple silicon) job, and the forced-arch signature-match step is green on Linux. The silent-miscompile is eliminated for every register-passed `#[repr(C)]` struct param and return. The ONLY remaining case is >16B by-value (indirect params / sret returns), which is a LOUD compile-time rejection with a pass-by-pointer / out-param workaround — a bounded future enhancement, NOT an open correctness hole. Two permanent CI gates guard the fix: the Linux signature-match (instant, no arm64 hw) and the macOS-arm64 execution E2E. FULLY CLOSED (2026-07-09, Slice 3): the larger-than-16B by-value case is no longer a rejection - it is lowered faithfully on BOTH targets. AArch64: >16B non-HFA param -> plain indirect ptr to a caller copy, >16B return -> sret (x8) [Slices 3a/3b, signature-matched vs clang]. Building the paired C-host execution test then surfaced that x86-64 had the SAME >16B bug but as a SILENT MISCOMPILE (never a rejection - that only ever lived on the arm64 path): SysV MEMORY class needs ptr byval(%Struct) params + sret returns, which the raw-struct lowering did not match (clang oracle: i64 @f(ptr byval(...)) / void @f(ptr sret(...)) vs Kara's old raw {i64,i64,i64}). Slice 3c closes it. Verified with REAL x86-64 execution (test_build_repr_c_struct_big_byval_sret_from_c_e2e: a C host calls make/sum3/roundtrip on a 24-byte struct by value, reads back 10 11 12 33 15 38) + native x86-64 signature-match tests; the E2E is in the arm64 CI producer filter so it doubles as the 3a/3b real-execution proof on Apple silicon + Linux arm64. NO remaining by-value correctness gap for register- or memory-class #[repr(C)] structs on either CI-covered target.

title: The interactive JIT-default `karac repl` SILENTLY DROPPED all cell stdout: a `println(1 + 1);` cell printed nothing to the terminal (while `karac repl --interp` printed `2`). The persistent `karac_jit_runner --repl-mode` subprocess pipes the cell's stdout (`Stdio::piped()`) and returns it over a framed protocol; `Session::run_cell_via_jit` forwarded those bytes only on the `capture=true` path (kernel/tests) and returned `Vec::new()` on the `capture=false` INTERACTIVE path — and `run_with_wrapper`'s Ok-arm never prints `stdout` anyway (the tree-walk interpreter writes straight to the process stdout, so the interp path needs no forwarding). Net: after the Slice-5 JIT-default flip made the JIT the default REPL backend, every interactive `println` cell produced no visible output — the flagship interactive surface was mute under its own default backend. Undetected because the entire `tests/repl_jit.rs` suite drives `Session::evaluate_cell_captured` (`capture=true`), which returns the bytes to the caller and never exercises the interactive forward.
investigation: 2026-07-09: found while measuring the REPL cold-start number (the last LLJIT-spike acceptance remainder) — a `println` smoke test over piped stdin showed only the banner. FIX (src/repl.rs::run_cell_via_jit): on the `capture=false` path, write the runner-captured `stdout` bytes to `std::io::stdout()` (and any clean-cell `stderr` to `std::io::stderr()`) in the `Completed` arm, and `partial_stdout` + the fault diagnostic in the `RunnerDied` arm. Regression test (the gap the capture-only suite missed): tests/repl_jit.rs::repl_jit_interactive_subprocess_prints_cell_output — spawns the REAL `karac repl` binary over piped stdin (the interactive path) and asserts the two cells' `42`/`hi` reach stdout under the JIT banner. Verified interp==JIT for multi-cell sessions with a persistent `let`. Gates: repl_jit 26, repl 136, fmt + clippy (llvm) clean. Follow-on (separate): a cell that PANICS (`emit_panic`'s exit(1)) still loses its own stdout/panic text because the runner dies before framing its capture buffer — tracked as B-2026-07-09-4.

fix: this commit
title: A REPL cell that PANICS under the JIT loses ALL of its own output — both the text it printed before the fault AND the panic message itself. The `karac_jit_runner --repl-mode` protocol runs the cell with stdout/stderr CAPTURED into buffers, then writes a `result <id> <exit> <stdout_len> <stderr_len>` frame followed by the buffered bytes. But a fault trips codegen's `emit_panic`, which calls `exit(1)` — the runner process dies BEFORE it writes the frame, so the capture buffers (holding both the pre-fault prints and the panic text) are never transmitted. The client sees stdout close → `CellResult::RunnerDied` with EMPTY `partial_stdout`/`runner_stderr`. Repro: `println(222); println(v[5]); println(333);` on an empty `Vec` prints neither `222` nor the OOB panic — only a generic 'runner died mid-cell' note (added by B-2026-07-09-3 so the fault is at least visible). Contrast `karac run`, whose one-shot JIT subprocess INHERITS stdio, so its panic text reaches the terminal (that path is correct).
investigation: 2026-07-09: isolated while fixing B-2026-07-09-3, then FIXED. Root cause is the capture-then-frame ordering in `--repl-mode`: emit_panic's exit(1) bypasses the framing write. Considered (b) inherit-stdio (breaks the per-cell framing the kernel/value-snapshot path needs) and (c) fork-per-cell (breaks cross-cell value-snapshot persistence — the cell's global writes would land in the dying child). Chose (a): `emit_panic` lowers to libc `exit` (src/codegen.rs:3342), which RUNS atexit handlers, and the dup2 redirect means the tempfiles ALREADY hold the pre-fault prints + the `panic …` printf at fault time — the only missing step is transmitting them. FIX: the runner installs a `libc::atexit` handler (`salvage_faulted_cell_output` in src/bin/karac_jit_runner.rs) armed for the duration of each cell's `call_main` (via `capture_via_redirect(Some(id), …)`, storing the saved parent-pipe fd + tempfile paths + cell id in atomics/Mutex). On a fault it flushes, reads the tempfiles, and writes a NEW `faulted <id> <exit> <so> <se>\n<bytes>` frame to the saved pipe fd before the process dies; disarmed the instant call_main returns so a clean cell salvages nothing. Client (jit_runner_client.rs) recognizes `faulted` and maps it onto `CellResult::RunnerDied{partial_stdout, runner_stderr}`, so the existing run_cell_via_jit RunnerDied arm surfaces the salvaged output (and suppresses the now-redundant 'runner died' note when real output was salvaged) and the client still re-spawns. VERIFIED interactively: `println(111); println(v[5]); println(999);` now prints `111` then `panic: vec index out of bounds` (999 correctly skipped — execution halted at the fault), and a later cell `println(444)` still runs (re-spawn works); contract violations show `panic: contract violated: requires clause`. Matches `karac run`/AOT (panic → stdout). Regression tests: tests/karac_jit_runner_repl.rs::repl_runner_salvages_output_when_cell_calls_exit (protocol-level: asserts the `faulted` frame shape) and tests/repl_jit.rs::repl_jit_interactive_subprocess_surfaces_panic_and_recovers (real `karac repl` binary over piped stdin). Gates: repl_jit 27, karac_jit_runner_repl 3, repl 136, lljit_e2e 16, fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. NOTE: the one-shot `karac run`/`--test-batch` paths are untouched (run inherits stdio; test-batch reads parent-known tempfiles).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: B-2026-07-09-3 follow-on — panicking REPL cell loses its output — SURFACE NOTE: repl (karac_jit_runner --repl-mode protocol)

title: `#[derive(Message)]` on a BARE ENUM (`#[derive(Message)] enum Role { Guest, Member, Admin }` + `r.encode()` / `Role.decode(..)`) failed with confusing GENERATED-BODY typecheck errors on BOTH backends — `'Role' is not a struct` (the derived ctor `Role { … }`) and `expected 'Vec<u8>', found 'Vec<?T0>'` (an un-inferred empty `Vec.new()` encode, because an enum has no `T.fields()` to push). `derive_message` is documented and written for a STRUCT (a proto3 message; protobuf.kara L316/L806, checklist Slice 2 'on a struct of proto3 fields'); a proto3 enum is a FIELD type, not a top-level message. Standalone enum-Message is not a proto3 concept, is not emitted by the `.proto` schema path (which emits proto enums as plain `enum` + uses them as struct fields), and never worked on any backend — so this was a missing-guard / bad-diagnostic bug, NOT a lost feature.
investigation: 2026-07-09: surfaced as the last residual of the B-2026-07-08-15 Layer 2 protobuf-under-codegen work (flagged in its layer2_note). Confirmed enum-as-a-FIELD works interp==JIT==AOT (`struct User { name: String, role: Role }` round-trips, encoding `role` as a varint of the variant's 0-based declaration index — `derive_enum_field_roundtrip` and 4 sibling tests), and the `.proto` schema path emits enums WITHOUT `#[derive(Message)]` (runtime/stdlib/protobuf.kara L1599/L1712), so only a directly-annotated bare enum hit the gap. FIX: `derive_message` now guards `T.is_enum()` at the top and raises an actionable `compiler.error` — names the type, states `#[derive(Message)]` applies to a struct, and directs the user to declare the enum WITHOUT the derive and use it as a struct field (proto3 enum), or an enum-with-payload field (proto3 oneof) — then early-returns an empty `Vec[Item]` so no struct-shaped body is generated. Both backends now emit the same clear `E_COMPTIME_ERROR` instead of the two internal errors. Regression test: tests/protobuf_derive.rs::derive_message_on_bare_enum_errors (asserts the diagnostic via the `comptime_diags` harness). Gates: protobuf_derive 62, protobuf_proto 24, comptime 11, fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean; enum-field + struct-message round-trips unregressed. Not a codegen change (derive_message is a comptime fn, skipped by codegen per B-2026-07-08-15 Layer 3) — protobuf.kara is baked into karac via include_str!, so it required a karac rebuild, not a runtime-archive rebuild.

fix: this commit
tracker: src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs::bind_pattern_values_via_ptr (TupleVariant arm struct-payload bail) + pattern_binds_struct_payload helper; regression tests/codegen.rs::borrowed_option_struct_payload_field_read_is_correct
title: Matching a BORROWED `Option[struct]` (`ref` / `mut ref` parameter) and reading a field of the `Some(n)` payload silently returned 0 — a wrong-answer miscompile independent of `shared`/RC. Repro: `struct P { val: i64 }  fn getval(o: ref Option[P]) -> i64 { match o { None => 999, Some(n) => n.val } }` returns 0, not the real val (owned `Option[P]` is correct). Also hits `mut ref` and shared-struct payloads (`ref Option[shared Node]`), so any read-only recursive tree/list walk that borrows its node — the natural, idiomatic form — got garbage. Root cause: a single-field struct flattens to one i64 payload word, so the via-ptr `TupleVariant` fast path's `first_word_is_primitive` / `ok_single_word` checks passed and bound `n` as a ref-to-i64 LEAF (the payload word's raw type) rather than a ref to struct `P`. The arm body's `n.field` access then could not resolve against the scalar-typed binding and collapsed to a hardcoded 0 in the arm's result (`phi i64 [999,...], [0,...]`). The owned path never hit this: its value-source `reconstruct_payload_value` consults `pattern_binding_types` (`binding_is_struct`) and rebuilds the `{i64}` struct aggregate at the correct type.
investigation: 2026-07-09: reduced from #98 to a ~10-line repro, then bisected the trigger with a matrix — owned `Option[struct]` OK, `ref Node` (borrow the struct directly, no Option) OK, but `ref Option[struct]` and `mut ref Option[struct]` both read 0; `ref Option[i64]` is a separate typecheck error (payload binds as `ref i64`), not this bug. Dumped the `@getval` IR for owned-vs-ref via a throwaway `compile_to_ir` test: the ref arm GEPs the correct payload address (`%Some.pl.0.ptr = gep {i64,i64,i64,i64}, %o.ref.ptr, 0, 1`) and even loads it, but binds `n` at type i64, so the body's `n.val` feeds a constant 0 into the merge phi; the owned arm reconstructs `{i64}` and feeds `%val`. FIX: in `bind_pattern_values_via_ptr`'s `TupleVariant` arm, before the primitive-word fast path, bail (`return Ok(None)`) when any positional sub-pattern binds a struct-typed name — new helper `pattern_binds_struct_payload` mirrors the owned path's `binding_is_struct` (a `Binding` whose `pattern_binding_types` entry is in `struct_types` OR `shared_types`). This defers struct/shared-struct payloads to the value-source path, which already reconstructs the aggregate at the correct type (the same path the owned case uses). Multi-word structs already bailed via the existing `!ok_single_word && !ok_padded_primitive` guard; this closes the single-word-struct gap the LLVM-word-type heuristic could not distinguish from a genuine `Option[i64]`. PERF NOTE: the #98 'optimization' that surfaced this is a mirage — with the miscompile fixed, the borrowed `is_valid` retires ~7.20B instructions vs ~7.14B for the by-value original (marginally SLOWER), because the fix routes the borrowed struct payload through the same copy/reconstruct work as by-value. The buggy version's apparent 1.15x speedup was the miscompile skipping correct binding+RC work. #98 therefore stays by-value; no kata change. A genuine win would require true borrow-without-clone binding of struct/shared payloads in the via-ptr path (bind `n` as a ref at the struct's own type, and for shared alias the RC handle without inc/dec) — tracked as a separate perf enhancement, not this correctness fix. Read-only correctness is complete; struct-payload write-through under `mut ref` (the copy-shim does not alias back to the caller) is the same future enhancement. VERIFIED: 4-case regression test (ref/mut-ref plain struct, ref shared-struct recursive walk, owned control) runs real binaries and passes; the #98 mixed valid/invalid harness now matches the Python oracle byte-for-byte under the borrowed `is_valid`. Gates: codegen 2100, interpreter 1135, ownership 347, resolver 323, typechecker 1926, fmt + clippy (--all-targets, --features llvm) clean.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while investigating a LeetCode #98 (validate-BST) codegen 'optimization': switching the read-only `is_valid` to borrow its node (`ref Option[TreeNode]`) — the idiomatic shape every native mirror uses — produced a SILENT WRONG ANSWER (all trees validated as true). The bench sink couldn't catch it (its `build` only makes valid BSTs, so always-true hashes identically); the kata's mixed valid/invalid harness did.

fix: this commit
title: Silent unchecked implicit integer conversions at binding boundaries (let-annotation, function argument, function return) — inconsistent with the strict mixed-integer ARITHMETIC rule, and value-lossy. The typechecker rejects mixed-integer arithmetic with E0200 ("cannot mix integer types 'u64' and 'i64' in arithmetic ... cast explicitly with `as`"), but SILENTLY accepts an integer of one type where a differently-typed integer is annotated/expected at every assignment-like site — across BOTH signedness and width, including sign-flip and out-of-range narrowing — with no `as` and no diagnostic. The annotation sets the static type but no conversion/range-check is emitted, so the runtime value is the source's and the static type can lie. Repros (all `karac check` CLEAN, interp==compiled so this is a typechecker-level permissiveness, not a codegen divergence): (1) `let b: u64 = a;` where `let a: i64 = -5;` -> prints 18446744073709551611 (2^64-5, sign-flip uncaught). (2) `let c: u64 = -5i64;` -> same (negative literal into unsigned, silently). (3) `let small: u32 = big;` where `let big: i64 = 5000000000;` -> prints 5000000000, a value OUTSIDE u32's range and NOT truncated (a real u32 would be 705032704) — the `u32` annotation is effectively ignored, no truncation, no error. (4) same silent acceptance at a call boundary (`fn f(x: u64)` called with an i64 arg) and at a return boundary (`fn f() -> u64 { <i64 value> }`). CONTRAST: the explicit `as` cast is correct — `big as u32` truncates to 705032704 (interp==compiled). So the hole is specifically the IMPLICIT boundary coercion, not the cast machinery. WHY IT MATTERS: the explicit-cast discipline the language advertises (and enforces in arithmetic) is bypassed at let/arg/return, so silent sign changes and out-of-range/narrowing conversions pass typecheck and the static type gives a false guarantee — exactly the class of bug `as` is meant to force the author to acknowledge. LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT (why this needs a design decision, not a unilateral strict-mode flip): `String.len()`/`Vec.len()`/`Slice.len()` all return i64 (src/typechecker/stdlib_seq.rs:156/739/821/1109), and existing corpus code assigns those i64 lengths to u64 bindings/fields relying on exactly this implicit coercion — e.g. examples/word_count.kara `WordCount { total: u64 = words.len(), unique: u64 = ...len() }`. Making all binding-site integer coercions strict would break that code broadly. OPTIONS (not yet chosen): (a) require `as` at binding boundaries too (most consistent; needs a corpus migration + possibly reconsidering whether len() should be u64); (b) allow only same-signedness widening implicitly and reject narrowing + sign-change (rejects repros 1-3, but i64->u64 is a sign change so word_count would still need `as`); (c) at minimum, reject a statically-known out-of-range or negative literal into a narrower/unsigned type (`-5i64 -> u64`, `5000000000i64 -> u32`) while leaving variable-to-variable widening — catches the smoking-gun literals with the least churn. Found during a correctness dogfooding pass authoring examples/mend/examples/grade_histogram (a u64 loop counter over an i64 `.len()` tripped E0200, which led here). Repro dir: examples/mend/examples/grade_histogram/ (notes.md). Filed rather than fixed because the corpus dependency makes this a language-design decision (which boundaries require `as`, and whether len() should be u64), not a mechanical typechecker patch. PARTIAL FIX 2026-07-09 (option (c) — literal boundary range-check): the statically-detectable holes are now closed. A SUFFIXED integer literal at a coercion boundary (let-annotation / fn-arg / return / struct-field / match-arm) is now range-checked against the CONTEXTUAL type, not just its own suffix — so `let x: u64 = -5i64` (E0200 negative-into-unsigned), `let x: u32 = 5_000_000_000i64` and `let x: u8 = 300i64` (E0200 out-of-range) are rejected, matching the unsuffixed twins the B-2026-07-02-7 check already caught. Implemented in src/typechecker/exprs.rs: a `suffixed_int_literal_value` companion to `unsuffixed_int_literal_value`, plus a second block in `check_expr` that runs the existing `check_int_literal_fits` against the expected type (emits ONLY when the value does not fit, so an in-range coercion like `5i64 -> u64` is left alone; returns early to avoid double-emitting with the synthesis-time own-suffix check). Gates: full non-llvm suite + 2103 codegen E2E + new tests/typechecker.rs::{test_suffixed_int_literal_rejected_at_narrowing_boundary (asserts the error AND a single diagnostic), test_suffixed_int_literal_in_range_coercion_still_admitted}; corpus scan of 168 .kara files shows ZERO new rejections; fmt + clippy clean. STILL OPEN (the design-decision half): VARIABLE-to-variable implicit integer coercion at these same boundaries stays permissive — `let b: u64 = a` (a: i64), `let s: u32 = big` (big: i64 = 5e9, out of range but only known at runtime), and fn-arg/return with variable operands are still silently accepted. Catching those requires either a strict `as`-at-boundaries rule (option (a)) — which needs the len()-returns-i64 corpus migration (word_count.kara's `total: u64 = words.len()`) and/or reconsidering whether len() should be u64 — or a runtime range check. Left as the parked language-design call; the literal cases were the concrete soundness smoking guns and are fixed. FIXED 2026-07-09 (variable half — design decision (B), widening-only implicit int coercion): the remaining runtime-only hole is closed. A NON-literal integer value at a check-mode coercion boundary (let / arg / return / struct-field — all funnel through check_expr) must now WIDEN; a narrowing or sign-changing coercion (`let s: u32 = big_i64`, `u64 = v.len()` where len() returns i64, any signed→unsigned, u64→i64) is a type error naming the required `as`. Widening stays implicit (i32→i64, u8→u32, u8→i16 strictly-wider unsigned→signed). Implemented in src/typechecker/types.rs (`int_signed_width` + `int_coercion_is_widening`, the (B) predicate) and src/typechecker/exprs.rs (`check_int_widening_coercion`, called in check_expr before check_assignable; skips literals — value-checked already, so `let a: u64 = 5i64` stays fine — and non-concrete/float types). NOTE on the bundled len()→usize migration: it proved UNNECESSARY. Empirical blast radius of the widening rule across the whole corpus was ONE site (examples/leetcode/course_schedule.kara: `for i in 0..num_courses` typed the index i64 against a u64 bound, then passed it to a u64 param — a genuine latent i64→u64 the rule surfaced; fixed by `0u64..num_courses`), and ZERO in the Rust test suite. len() into an unsigned slot barely occurs; len() is overwhelmingly used in i64 comparisons/arithmetic, which the rule does not touch — so migrating len()→usize would have ADDED churn (every `0..v.len()` range / comparison) rather than absorbed it, for a semantic nicety orthogonal to this bug. Left as an optional standalone follow-up. Gates: full non-llvm suite (7572) + codegen E2E (2103) + par_codegen (153) + cli (516) green; new tests/typechecker.rs::{test_variable_narrowing_or_signchange_coercion_requires_as, test_variable_widening_coercion_still_implicit, test_in_range_int_literal_coercion_still_admitted}; corpus scan shows zero remaining widening errors; fmt + clippy clean.
