title: Windows x64 `#[repr(C)]` struct-by-value ABI is unhandled — the raw-struct lowering does not match the Microsoft x64 calling convention, a latent silent-miscompile for any `pub extern "C" fn` taking/returning a `#[repr(C)]` struct by value on a Windows target. Discovered while implementing B-2026-07-09-2 Slice 3c (SysV x86-64 >16B byval/sret). The Microsoft x64 convention differs from SysV: an aggregate whose size is not 1/2/4/8 bytes (i.e. 3/5/6/7 or >8 bytes) is passed/returned BY REFERENCE (a pointer to a caller-allocated copy), NOT in registers and NOT SysV-`byval`-on-stack; only power-of-2 sizes up to 8 bytes go in a single register. So neither the raw-struct lowering NOR the SysV byval/sret path (B-2026-07-09-2 Slice 3c) is correct on Windows. To avoid applying an unverified SysV convention there, `native_target_is_x86_64()` excludes the `*-windows-*` triple, so Windows keeps its (also-unverified) raw-struct lowering rather than a wrong SysV one — no regression vs the prior state, but the gap is now explicit. FIX LANDED (2026-07-09): a Windows-x64 aggregate ABI classifier is now in codegen. Params: 1/2/4/8-byte structs → `Coerced(iN)` (single integer register); every other size → `Indirect` as a plain `ptr` (NO `byval` attribute — the Microsoft convention is caller-owned copy passed by address, which a plain `ptr` captures; SysV's `byval` exists to model callee-side copy semantics Windows doesn't need). Returns: same 1/2/4/8-byte rule → `Coerced(iN)` in RAX; everything else → `Sret`. Wired into `functions.rs` alongside the existing AArch64 (AAPCS) and x86-64 SysV branches through the new `target_is_windows_x86_64` gate (SysV `target_is_x86_64` stays deliberately Windows-excluded, so the SysV `byval` application never fires on Windows). Internal Kara calls to a Windows-classified export are rejected with the broadened boxed-export message. VERIFIED LOCALLY without a Windows LLVM 18 install: signature-match tests in `tests/abi_repr_c_struct.rs` under `KARAC_FORCE_TARGET_ARCH=windows_x86_64` cover the six key shapes (single i32/i64 register coercion, {i32,i32} 8B → i64, 16B and >16B indirect ptr, all-float NON-HFA fallback, small/big returns, and the combined sret+indirect-ptr param case) — identical IR lowers identically through LLVM, so signature match = ABI match; the same test file uses this trick for arm64 successfully (B-2026-07-09-2). NATIVE WINDOWS CI LEG (Stage 4) DEFERRED (2026-07-10): the `codegen-e2e-windows` job attempted in PR #1 ran three times and hit a hard upstream ecosystem gap on the third — `llvm-sys 181` requires `llvm-config.exe` at `<PREFIX>/bin/`, and the official LLVM Windows NSIS installer (and every downstream: Chocolatey `llvm`, `KyleMayes/install-llvm-action`, direct download) OMITS it. In-tree probe confirmed: extracted LLVM 18.1.8 Windows tree contains `clang-*.exe`, `lld*.exe`, headers, and libs, but no `llvm-config*`. Alternatives (shim script, MSYS2 MinGW LLVM, from-source LLVM) each add long-term cost that outweighs a nice-to-have execution proof, so the leg is dropped from the CI matrix and the roadmap Tier 5 entry is updated to name the deferral. Reinstate once LLVM ships `llvm-config.exe` on Windows, an accepted community redistribution includes it, or someone signs up to maintain a shim. LOW-ish priority note stays true: Windows producer output (.lib/.dll) was previously unverified end-to-end, so no user relied on Windows struct-by-value exports before this fix.
resolution: Classifier + signature-match tests landed in 4c90993d and remain the correctness gate. The Linux `codegen-e2e` job runs `cargo test --features llvm --test abi_repr_c_struct` under `KARAC_FORCE_TARGET_ARCH=windows_x86_64` on every push and PR to main; identical IR lowers identically through LLVM so a signature match is an ABI match (same forced-arch trick that carries arm64 correctness from Linux). Verified green across three PR runs (29066039424, 29066527100, 29067120775 — all failed only at the deferred native Windows execution leg, never at the signature-match step). Native Windows hardware confirmation is deferred pending the upstream LLVM Windows `llvm-config.exe` gap being closed; the Windows classifier is complete + validated on every merge without it.

Three-part wiring: (1) `type_satisfies_bound` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) gained a `Default` arm delegating to `type_supports_default`, so the `T: Default` bound discharges for `#[derive(Default)]`/primitive concrete args instead of falling through to the empty impl-table and rejecting every arg; (2) `compile_assoc_call` (src/codegen/assoc_call.rs) resolves `type_name` through `type_subst_names` at entry so `T.default()` keys on the concrete `S.default` (derived inherent fn) inside the mono, plus a `primitive_default_value` helper emits the correctly-typed zero for i64/f64/bool/char/String (the old i64-0 fallthrough zeroed only 8 of String's 24 bytes — a double-free); (3) the interpreter's `fn_param_mut_ref_flags` + a `primitive_default_value` intercept (src/interpreter.rs, eval_call.rs) close the interpreter legs for baked-stdlib `mut ref` write-back forwarding and primitive `T.default()`. Also fixed a latent ASAN-harness gap: `run_under_asan` skipped `desugar_program`, so any derive-dependent program miscompiled under it (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs). std.mem `take` now ships as a real generic source body. title: Generic `T.default()` under a `T: Default` bound does NOT monomorphize in codegen (it runs correctly in the interpreter). `Default` is a DERIVE-ONLY builtin — `#[derive(Default)]` synthesizes a concrete INHERENT `impl Type { fn default() -> Type }` (src/desugar.rs synthesize_default_impls), there is NO `trait Default { fn default() }` declaration. Concrete `S.default()` compiles + runs correctly; but a generic body `fn make_default[T: Default]() -> T { T.default() }` monomorphized to `S` emits a PLACEHOLDER `i64 0` for the `T.default()` call instead of a call to `S.default()`, so `karac build` fails module verification: 'Function return type does not match operand type of return inst: ret i64 0 { i64 }'. `karac run` (interpreter) executes the same program correctly (prints the default). So the generic typeparam-assoc-fn dispatch (`T.method()` where `T: SomeBound`) does not resolve `default` to the concrete synthesized inherent assoc fn in the mono — likely the same family as the ownership generic-trait-method gap (B-2026-07-08-11) but for CODEGEN assoc-fn dispatch, and complicated by `Default` having no real trait method to route through (find_trait_method('Default','default') returns None; the interpreter is lenient and resolves it at runtime via the concrete instantiation). BLOCKS std.mem `take` (roadmap Phase 8): `take[T: Default](dest: mut ref T) -> T { replace(dest, T.default()) }` as a source wrapper compiles+runs in the interpreter but fails `karac build`, so `take` is deferred (swap/replace shipped as intrinsics). FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) route a generic `T.default()` in a mono to the concrete `<ConcreteT>.default()` synthesized inherent fn (needs the typeparam-assoc-fn codegen dispatch to consult the derive-synthesized impls at the resolved type); or (b) introduce a real baked `trait Default { fn default() -> Self }` and have the derive emit `impl Default for T` so normal trait-method mono dispatch applies (larger, but removes the derive-only special-case) — this also unblocks `take` as a plain source body. Repro: `#[derive(Default)] struct S { x: i64 } fn md[T: Default]() -> T { T.default() } fn main() { let s: S = md(); println(f"{s.x}"); }` — `karac run` prints 0, `karac build` fails verification.

Niche-optimized `Option[shared T]` value stored into a CONVENTIONAL 4-word field slot crashed codegen — and the crash was INVISIBLE because all three selfhost PARSER oracles were vacuously skipping on it. A niche-ABI `Option[shared T]` value is a bare pointer (null=None); a niche-returning fn like the self-hosted parser's `parse_else() -> Option[Expr]` yields one, and `let else_branch = parse_else(); IfExpr { else_branch, .. }` stores it into `IfExpr.else_branch`, a CONVENTIONAL `{tag,w0,0,0}` slot (IfExpr is a non-`shared` node struct, so its `Option[shared]` field is not niche-laid-out). `emit_rc_inc_for_captured_option` (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs) assumed a struct value and panicked at `val.into_struct_value()`; with that guarded, the raw pointer was `insertvalue`'d into a 4xi64 aggregate -> LLVM 'Invalid InsertValueInst'. Pre-existing since before the 2026-07-09 pull window (bisect: every tested commit back to 5a5cbca is bad; the regressing commit predates it). MASKING BUG (test integrity): tests/selfhost_parser{,_types,_items}.rs classified only `error[`/`codegen failed`/`parse error`/`Module verification failed` as a compile error; a Rust PANIC matched none, so `!bin.exists()` fell through to the 'no llvm / missing runtime archive' SKIP and the oracle reported a vacuous 'ok'. Result: the ENTIRE parser port (slices 1-3c) was differentially UNVERIFIED for weeks while CI stayed green. FIX (706a71e): (1) `emit_rc_inc_for_captured_option` handles the niche pointer/int representation (null-guarded rc-inc) as well as the conventional struct; (2) new `widen_niche_option_ptr_to_field` normalizes a niche pointer to `{tag, w0, 0, 0}` at both struct-field-init sites (shared-struct GEP-store branch + non-shared insertvalue branch), a no-op when the value is already conventional; (3) all four selfhost oracles now treat a compiler panic (`panicked at`) or signal-kill (`status.code().is_none()`) as a HARD FAILURE, never a skip. Gates: codegen 2106/0, memory_sanitizer 562/0, clippy + fmt clean; the 7 existing `option_shared_niche` tests stay green.
resolution: Fixed the niche->conventional boundary conversion at struct-field-init + hardened the oracle skip-classification. NOTE: with the build panic gone the parser now COMPILES but crashes at runtime on basic inputs (B-2026-07-09-12) — the three parser oracles are #[ignore]'d pending that fix, so full differential re-verification is still owed.

title: Self-hosted parser BUILDS (after B-2026-07-09-11) but SEGFAULTS / heap-corrupts at RUNTIME on control-flow expressions. NARROWED 2026-07-09 (valgrind): the crash class is a for-loop over an owned `Vec[shared T]` (or a plain `Vec[struct/enum-with-shared-field]`) that CONSUMES each element by matching the shared enum and MOVING a heap child OUT of a NestedStruct payload. Minimal repro (double-free, valgrind-clean once fixed): `struct Id { name: String, span: i64 } shared enum Expr { Ident(Id) } fn render_expr(e: Expr) -> String { match e { Ident(n) => { let Id { name, span } = n; name } } } fn go(v: Vec[Expr]) -> String { let mut o = "".to_string(); for e in v { o.push_str(render_expr(e)); } o }` — returning the extracted `name` double-frees it against the shared box's `__karac_rc_drop_Expr` recursion into the `Id` NestedStruct payload. `Vec[String]` and `Vec[struct{String}]` for-loops are CLEAN; the bug is specific to a shared-handle element / shared NestedStruct payload whose extracted heap CHILD is moved out. ROOT: `suppress_shared_enum_payload_move_out` (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs) zeros a moved-out `VecOrString` / `Map`/`Set` payload field IN THE BOX so the rc-drop skips it, but DELIBERATELY excludes `NestedStruct` — correct for the common case (a NestedStruct binding is a shallow VIEW; the box retains ownership and frees it, the binding does not) but WRONG when the binding's heap child is further moved out (then both the returned child and the box free it). TRAP (verified 2026-07-09): naively extending the suppressor to also zero NestedStruct fields fixes this repro but REGRESSES 17 memory_sanitizer tests (asan_match_byvalue_shared_enum_bind_without_consume, asan_struct_wrapped_*, asan_vec_of_shared_enum_*, …) into LEAKS — the shallow-view cases where the box legitimately owns the children. The correct fix needs an OWN-vs-SHARE distinction (does the arm move a heap child OUT of the nested-struct binding?), i.e. deep move-analysis, OR a deep-clone of the nested-struct payload at the shared-enum match bind (perf cost). ADDITIONALLY: the real parser's `{ a; }` render shows a DISTINCT corruption (the ExprStmt's `expr` reads back as `(error @1:1)` — a use-after-free during render, not just a drop-time double-free) that the minimal repro does NOT reproduce (needs the full 19-variant 152-byte Expr layout and/or the parse-side ownership), so there is >=1 further nested-drop bug beyond the one above. NEXT: decide the own-vs-share fix design; reproduce the render-corruption variant; then un-ignore selfhost_parser/_types/_items (keyed to this id).
resolution: OPEN. Investigated deeply 2026-07-09: precise minimal repro + root cause (shared-enum NestedStruct payload move-out double-free) identified; a naive suppressor extension regressed 17 asan tests and was reverted. Needs a careful own-vs-share design (move-analysis or deep-clone-on-bind), plus a second nested-drop bug (render use-after-free) still to reproduce. The 3 parser oracles stay #[ignore]'d. DEEPER ANALYSIS 2026-07-10 (fix design settled, NOT yet implemented): the double-free needs a heap child to be MOVED OUT of the shared-enum NestedStruct payload binding (repro F returns the extracted String); the single-value case is clean, Vec-sourced (for-loop OR v[i] index) is not, and `Vec[String]`/direct-`VecOrString`-payload for-loops are clean (only NestedStruct payloads whose extracted CHILD escapes). The shared-enum NestedStruct binding is a VIEW BY DESIGN: `pattern_binding.rs` ~L402 skips `track_struct_var` when `pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_shared_enum` (B-2026-06-14-31) because the binding aliases the RC box's inline buffer and the box's rc-drop is the sole owner — this is SOUND FOR rc>1 (you cannot move out of a shared box). Therefore my reverted 'suppress the box + let the binding own' idea is UNSOUND for genuinely shared (rc>1) boxes (it would strand the other references) and ALSO leaked (17 asan regressions) because the binding registered no drop. The SOUND fix is DEEP-CLONE-ON-BIND: when a shared-enum match arm binds a NestedStruct payload, deep-clone the struct into the binding (via the existing `emit_struct_clone_fn`) and register its `track_struct_var` drop, leaving the box UNTOUCHED (box frees its own original; binding frees its clone). Sound for any rc. TRADEOFFS to weigh before implementing: (a) a deep clone per shared-enum NestedStruct match — the parser matches AST nodes constantly, and cloning a node whose payload holds a `Vec`/recursive child is potentially expensive and exercises the clone path on complex nested structures; (b) it changes deliberate load-bearing design (B-2026-06-14-31) with existing regression tests. A more surgical alternative is CLONE-ON-EXTRACT-FROM-VIEW (clone only the specific heap field when it is destructured out of a shared-view struct binding) — cheaper but needs the destructure site to know the binding is a shared-enum-payload view (no per-binding flag exists today; only the per-match `pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_shared_enum`). RECOMMENDATION: implement deep-clone-on-bind gated hard on the full memory_sanitizer suite; fall back to clone-on-extract if the clone cost/regressions bite. BLOCKER on the deep-clone-on-bind approach found 2026-07-10: the clone infrastructure (emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr / emit_struct_clone_fn, src/codegen/clone_drop.rs) does NOT rc-inc a SHARED field — clone_drop.rs:~102 falls through to emit_primitive_clone_fn (a bare `*dst=*src` pointer copy) for shared/RC types. So deep-clone-on-bind is correct only for shared-field-FREE payload structs (repro F's `Id { name: String, span }` works), but would DOUBLE-FREE for the parser's real AST node structs (Block { stmts: Vec[Stmt], tail: Option[Expr] }, ExprStmt { expr: Expr }, …) which carry shared `Expr` fields the clone would alias without an rc bump. CONCLUSION: B-2026-07-09-12 is a multi-PART compiler feature, not a single patch — it needs EITHER (a) escape analysis (clone a heap leaf only when it escapes the arm), OR (b) a corrected deep-clone that rc-incs shared struct fields PLUS deep-clone-on-bind + drop registration; AND separately the distinct render use-after-free (the `{ a; }` `(error @1:1)` corruption, not reproduced by the minimal repro). All in load-bearing drop code that regressed 17 asan tests on the first touch. RECOMMENDATION: schedule as a focused, multi-commit task with fresh context; do not rush. The 3 parser oracles stay #[ignore]'d against this id; selfhost_lexer stays green; main is known-good. PARTIAL FIX 2026-07-10 (copy-supported payload sub-class — deep-clone-on-bind): the minimal double-free repro (repro F: a `Vec[shared enum]` for-loop whose arm destructures a NestedStruct payload and MOVES a heap child out — `let Id { name, span } = n; name`) is FIXED for payloads whose heap is fully outer-buffer duplicable. Mechanism: at the shared-enum match bind (src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs, the `!pattern_binding_is_borrow` struct arm) the reconstructed payload VIEW is upgraded to an OWNED deep clone IN PLACE via `emit_struct_clone_fn` + `track_struct_var`, leaving the RC box's original untouched (box frees original, binding frees clone — sound for any refcount). fix: this commit. ROOT CAUSE was NOT struct-key-specific (the original entry misattributed it): the trigger is a `let` binding between a borrow-returning collection accessor and the consuming match — `let g = coll.get(k); match g { Some(v) => <move/drop v> }`. `Map.get` returns `Option[V]` whose payload ALIASES the bucket's stored value (and Vec/Slice/Array `.get`/`.first`/`.last` return `Option[ref T]` aliasing element storage); the codegen borrow-alias protection (`scrutinee_is_borrow_call` + `clone_escaping_borrow_payload_binding`) only recognized a DIRECT `match coll.get(k)` method-call scrutinee. Through the intermediate `let g`, the scrutinee is an IDENTIFIER, so the protection was skipped: an arm that moved/dropped the payload freed the aliased buffer a second time against the collection's own value/element drop (`karac_map_free_with_drop_vec`). The struct-key repro in the original entry just happened to trip glibc's tcache double-free detector (ASan/valgrind confirmed the free came from `main`'s payload drop, not the hash path — which is correct); the identical i64-key `let`-form double-freed too, and Vec.get `let`-form was the same class. FIX: a new `borrow_accessor_let_payload: HashMap<var, Option-te>` records a `let` binding whose RHS is a borrow-returning stdlib-collection accessor (Map/SortedMap `.get`; Vec/Slice/Array/VecDeque `.get`/`.first`/`.last`) at the let-site (src/codegen/stmts.rs). `scrutinee_is_borrowed_binding` re-admits such an identifier scrutinee into the borrow protection, and `borrow_get_payload_clone_te` recovers the payload type for it — so the Map payload clones on escape exactly as in the direct form and the ref-typed Vec payload self-gates to alias-only. Cleared per-function alongside `for_loop_borrow_vars`. Tests: codegen test_ir_map_get_letbound_moveout_emits_payload_clone; memory_sanitizer asan_letbound_map_get_moveout_no_double_free (bare-String value + struct KEY + if-let sibling, looped). Full suites green (codegen 2112, memory_sanitizer 569, interpreter 1138, par_codegen 154); read-only map.get stays zero-cost (no clone). RESIDUAL (known limitation): the fix covers the common `let g = coll.get(k); match g`/`if let` idiom, but the alias model is still fragile through OTHER indirections — passing `g` to a function, returning it, or chained rebinds (`let h = g; match h`) — because the borrow property is only propagated one hop. These are rarer (the ergonomic path is to match at the call site or `.clone()`). The principled long-term fix is to RETYPE `Map.get -> Option[ref V]` (like `Vec.get`) so the typechecker REJECTS escapes and forces an explicit `.clone()` to own — aligning the type with the codegen reality (the payload IS a borrow) and retiring the whole clone-on-escape patch family. That is an API/semantics decision (touches typechecker + interpreter + all Map.get usage), deferred to a design discussion rather than a bug-fix slice.
title: [root cause corrected — see fix] A struct-KEYED `Map[S, String]` (S a `#[derive(Hash, Eq, PartialEq)]` struct) double-frees a String VALUE under codegen (`karac build`/JIT) on the get-after-multi-insert path; the interpreter runs the same program correctly. Minimal repro: `#[derive(Hash, Eq, PartialEq)] struct Point { x: i64, y: i64 } fn main() { let mut m: Map[Point, String] = Map.new(); m.insert(Point{x:1,y:2}, "a".to_string()); m.insert(Point{x:3,y:4}, "b".to_string()); match m.get(Point{x:1,y:2}) { Some(v) => println(v), None => println("miss") } }` -> `karac run --interp` prints `a`; JIT/AOT aborts `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`. ISOLATION: the double-free needs ALL of (struct key) + (heap/String VALUE) + (>=2 inserts) + (a get). Narrowing that flips it back to clean: `Map[Point, i64]` (POD value, 2 inserts+get) is clean; `Map[Name{first:String}, i64]` (String-in-KEY, POD value) is clean; `Map[i64, String]` and `Map[String, String]` (non-struct key, String value, 2 inserts+get) are clean; struct-key + String value with ONLY 1 insert (no get) is clean; struct-key + String value with 2 inserts and NO get is clean. So the trigger is specifically a struct-key map's `get(...) -> Option[V]` when V is heap-owning and the table has >1 entry. LIKELY CAUSE: the struct-key `get` lowering returns the stored String VALUE by shallow copy (aliasing the bucket's {ptr,len,cap}) rather than an owned deep-copy / borrow, so the match-bound `v` and the map's own scope-exit drop free the same buffer twice -- the same ownership family as B-2026-06-20-8's `get_or` owned-copy fix, but on the `get`+struct-key path (the >1-entry / get combination suggests the struct-key hash bucket walk selects a value pointer the caller then adopts). The struct-KEY hash path ITSELF is correct (POD and String-field keys both hit the right bucket), so this is a VALUE-ownership bug surfaced by the struct-key get codepath, not a derive(Hash) miscompile. Found while surveying the roadmap `std.hash` item; NOTE for that survey: `#[derive(Hash)]` codegen for Map/Set keys already works (contra the roadmap's 'codegen path (interpreter form already shipped)' phrasing) -- the open `std.hash` work is the user-facing `Hash` trait + `Hasher` interface surface, not the Map-key byte-hash which ships.

EXACT TRIGGER (bisected by add-back): ALL THREE needed — (1) the outer struct is LET-BOUND before use (`let block = Block{..}; Expr.Blk(block)` crashes; the INLINE `Expr.Blk(Block{..})` WORKS); (2) the struct has an `Option[SHARED]` field (`tail: Option[Expr]`) — `Option[i64]` in the same slot WORKS, and dropping the tail field entirely WORKS; (3) plus the `Vec[Stmt]` field that reads back corrupt. A probe of `block.stmts[0]` placed RIGHT AFTER `let block = ..` and BEFORE the `Expr.Blk` pack already misbehaves (stack-overflow/garbage), so the corruption is in CONSTRUCTING/STORING the let-bound local `Block` (compile_struct_init writing the struct literal into the block alloca), NOT in the shared-enum pack (`coerce_to_payload_words`) or the reconstruct/render. HYPOTHESIS: a struct-field-layout / offset mismatch when a struct carries a NICHE-optimized `Option[shared]` field (1 pointer word, null=None) — the alloca-store field-init path (GEP by field, compile_struct_init) computes a different width/offset for the `Option[shared]` field than the struct's LLVM type / the SSA insertvalue path uses (which is why the INLINE literal, built via insertvalue, is fine but the let-bound alloca store corrupts the neighboring `Vec` field). Repro saved at examples-scratch B-2026-07-10-1-min.kara. NEXT: inspect compile_struct_init's field offset/width handling for a niche `Option[shared]` field vs the registered struct LLVM layout; the codegen (call_dispatch.rs::coerce_to_payload_words / control_flow_match.rs::reconstruct_payload_value) are likely NOT the culprit — struct construction/layout is. LOCALIZATION SHARPENED 2026-07-10 (corrects the earlier 'compile_struct_init' guess): let-binding the struct ALONE is CLEAN — `let block = Block{stmts,tail:None,span}; <read block.stmts[0]>` with NO shared-enum pack round-trips correctly (interp==compiled). The corruption is specifically the PACK of a LET-BOUND (alloca-LOADED) struct into the shared-enum payload: `Expr.Blk(block)` CRASHES but `Expr.Blk(Block{..})` (INLINE SSA literal, same fields) WORKS. So the culprit is `coerce_to_payload_words` (call_dispatch.rs:4324) / the oversize-BOX decision (`out.len() > num_words`) / `reconstruct_payload_value` coherence — the #44/#49 lineage — behaving DIFFERENTLY for a struct VALUE loaded from an alloca (let-bound) vs a fresh insertvalue aggregate (inline), when the struct carries a NICHE `Option[shared]` field. Hypothesis: the loaded-from-alloca Block's `Option[Expr]` field arrives with a different LLVM width/representation (niche 1-word ptr vs conventional 4-word Option) than the inline-built one, so `llvm_type_word_count` yields a different field word count, flipping the inline-vs-BOX decision between the pack of the two forms while the unpack (`reconstruct_payload_value`) assumes one — the classic pack/unpack box-decision mismatch (#44) but triggered by the alloca-load representation of a niche Option field, not the field count. This is a codegen PACKING bug (not struct-init, not memory-safety/drop). Next: dump + diff the IR of `Expr.Blk(block)` vs `Expr.Blk(Block{..})` for the same fields, focus on the `tail` field's extracted width and the `out.len()` vs `num_words` box branch; make the box decision + reconstruct consult the SAME niche-aware width for a loaded value. CORRECTION 2026-07-10 (refutes the niche-mismatch hypothesis): the non-shared struct's `Option[shared]` field IS a CONVENTIONAL 4-word slot — compile_struct_init WIDENS a niche ptr into it (exprs.rs:2101, `widen_niche_option_ptr_to_field`, B-2026-07-09-11), consistently for BOTH the inline and let-bound forms. So the built Block VALUE is identical either way; the struct layout is NOT the bug. The true minimal condition is that BOTH the let-binding AND the pack are required: V4 (let-bind + `Expr.Blk(block)`) CRASHES, but V5 (let-bind + read, NO pack) WORKS and V4_inline (`Expr.Blk(Block{..})`, no let) WORKS. So the defect is the INTERACTION of the let-bound local's cleanup TRACKING + MOVE-SUPPRESSION with the enum pack: when `block` (a tracked local carrying a `Vec[Stmt]` cleanup AND an `Option[shared]` cleanup) is MOVED into `Expr.Blk(block)`, the move-suppression (`suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg` / the Option[shared] move handling) and the `coerce_to_payload_words` read of the just-suppressed local interact and corrupt the `Vec[Stmt]` field's words — plausibly the suppression zeroing a word at an offset miscomputed because of the 4-word Option field between the Vec (field 0) and span (field 2), or the box/inline num_words decision differing once the source is a tracked+moved alloca. NEXT (clear path): dump the IR for V4 vs V4_inline (via a throwaway `compile_to_ir` unit test, as prior #44/#49 fixes did) and diff the `Expr.Blk` lowering — specifically the move-suppression stores into `block`'s alloca and the coerce word extraction — to find the miscomputed word offset. The bug is in the enum-pack + move-suppression of a let-bound struct with a `Vec` field and a 4-word `Option[shared]` field. FIXED 2026-07-10 (root cause + one-spot fix): the corruption is NOT struct-init and NOT the pack box-decision (both inline and let-bound BOX the 8-word Block identically). The IR diff of let-bound vs inline `Expr.Blk` showed the let-bound form emits an EXTRA `__karac_vec_elem_full_drop_Block(%block)` — the moved-out let-bound local's scope-exit COMBINED drop. That drop calls `__karac_drop_struct_Block` (frees the Vec buffer, `cap>0`-guarded) AND runs a SEPARATE, LEN-driven per-element rc-dec walk over `Vec[Stmt]` (rc-dec each `Stmt::Exp(ExprStmt)`'s shared `Expr` — the B-2026-06-14-28 combined-drop for a Vec whose element transitively owns a shared handle). The whole-struct move-suppression `zero_struct_move_caps` (call_dispatch.rs:3558) zeroed only the Vec `CAP` (field 2), which neutralizes the buffer free but NOT the LEN-driven element rc-dec walk — so moving `block` into `Expr.Blk(block)` (whose boxed payload co-owns the same Stmt elements / Expr handles) still rc-dec'd those handles → premature free → the stmt-expr read back as a garbage `Error` node (and heap corruption). FIX: `zero_struct_move_caps` now ALSO zeroes the Vec `LEN` (field 1) for a `Vec`/`VecDeque`/`String` field, so the len-driven walk skips too and the moved-out source's drop is fully neutralized (harmless when the element owns no shared handle — no such walk exists). Explains every observed condition: needs the let-binding (→ a tracked local with a scope-exit drop), the Vec field (→ the len-driven element walk), AND the `Option[shared]` / shared-bearing element (→ the walk does rc-decs); the INLINE form has no local, hence no drop, hence worked. Gates: memory_sanitizer 580 (+1 regression asan_letbound_struct_vec_shared_elem_moved_into_enum_ctor_no_uaf), codegen 2120, fmt + clippy clean; the self-hosted parser now renders `{ a; }` / `{ a; b }` / `{ a; b; }` statement exprs CORRECTLY (interp==compiled). The parser oracle still CRASHES on the fuller corpus — that residual is the SEPARATE B-2026-07-09-12 render UAF (`malloc unaligned tcache`, the entry-copy fresh-vs-retained issue), not this wrong-value bug.

fix: this commit. A generic (monomorphized) fn whose IMPLICIT TAIL expression is a bare `f"…"` double-freed the returned String under codegen (`karac run`/`build`); the interpreter was correct. `compile_mono_function` (src/codegen/mono.rs) lacked the InterpolatedStringLit-tail cap-suppression block that `compile_function` (src/codegen/functions.rs) has: when a function's final expression is a bare f-string, the loaded {data,len,cap} is the return value, but the f-string accumulator's queued `FreeVecBuffer` frees `data` between the return-value load and `ret` (a use-after-free the caller then double-frees against its own binding). `suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return` only covers Identifier-tail moves, and the f-string acc is staged in `last_fstr_acc` only during `compile_expr`, so the mono needed the same post-compile `zero_vec_alloca_cap(last_fstr_acc.take())` guard. ISOLATION: only the generic + implicit-tail + f-string combination breaks — non-generic tail f-string, generic `let s = f".."; s`, generic `return f".."`, generic tail `.to_string()`/Vec-literal all already worked (they route through suppression or a non-tail path); even a no-interpolation tail f-string in a generic fn double-freed (so it is NOT Display- or param-interpolation-specific — it is the mono tail-f-string ownership transfer). Surfaced while verifying the Display trait surface (which is otherwise complete: user `impl Display`, `#[derive(Display)]`, the non-Display f-string typecheck rejection, and generic `T: Display` dispatch all work in both backends) via `fn describe[T: Display](x: T) -> String { f"item is {x}" }`. FIX: add the guarded `last_fstr_acc.take()` → `zero_vec_alloca_cap` block to `compile_mono_function` right after `suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return`, mirroring `compile_function`. Valgrind-confirmed the pre-fix free came from the caller's read-after-free of the returned buffer; ASAN-clean post-fix. Tests: codegen e2e_generic_tail_fstring_return_codegen; memory_sanitizer asan_generic_tail_fstring_no_double_free (Display struct + primitive + String + no-interp tail, looped). Full suites green (codegen 2122, memory_sanitizer 581, interpreter 1139).
title: Generic (monomorphized) fn with an IMPLICIT TAIL bare `f"…"` double-frees the returned String under codegen (interpreter correct). `compile_mono_function` lacked the InterpolatedStringLit-tail cap-suppression that `compile_function` has. NOT Display-specific — surfaced via generic `T: Display` f-string dispatch.

fix: this commit
tracker: src/codegen/calls.rs (try_compile_option_result_method extract path) — no move-suppression of a let-bound Option/Result receiver whose payload is extracted
title: `Option`/`Result` `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_err` / `expect_err` on a LET-BOUND receiver with a HEAP payload double-frees. `let r: Result[String, i64] = ...; r.unwrap()` (or `let r: Result[i64, String]; r.unwrap_err()`) extracts the payload by reconstituting the {ptr,len,cap} words — a SHALLOW alias of the let-bound receiver's inline payload buffer — and returns it; the extracted String/Vec is then freed by its consumer AND by the let-bound receiver `r`'s scope-exit drop → `free(): double free`. A FRESH-TEMP receiver (`f().unwrap()`, `m.get(k).unwrap()`) is CLEAN (the temp has no separate scope-exit drop to double it), and a non-heap payload (i64) is clean (nothing to free), which is why the common cases work and this stayed latent. The extract path (`try_compile_option_result_method`, calls.rs) neither deep-copies the extracted heap payload NOR suppresses the let-bound receiver's drop (cap-zero). FIX: on a heap-payload extract from a LET-BOUND (identifier) Option/Result receiver, either deep-copy the payload buffer (mirror `clone_owned_vec_index_element`) OR cap-zero the receiver's payload words so its drop no-ops (the receiver is consumed by unwrap). Pre-existing (predates unwrap_err); surfaced by the B-2026-07-09-10 unwrap_err work.
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-10 (this commit): the extract-or-panic path (`try_compile_option_result_method`, src/codegen/calls.rs) now calls `suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move(object)` after building the extracted value — zeroing a tracked inline/boxed `Option`/`Result` IDENTIFIER receiver's slot so its scope-exit drop no-ops (the receiver is CONSUMED by unwrap/expect/unwrap_err/expect_err and the returned value now solely owns the aliased buffer). No-op for a fresh-temp receiver (not an identifier — already single-owned) and for a non-heap payload (not in the tracked sets), so the already-working cases are untouched. Covers all four extract methods incl. the new unwrap_err/expect_err (B-2026-07-09-10). Gates: memory_sanitizer 582 (+1 regression asan_letbound_result_option_heap_unwrap_no_double_free — let-bound `Result[String,_]`.unwrap(), `Result[_,String]`.unwrap_err(), `Option[String]`.expect(), looped x20 under LSan), codegen 2123, fmt + clippy clean; `let r = f(); r.unwrap()` on heap payloads is now double-free-free.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while fixing B-2026-07-09-10 (unwrap_err/expect_err)

title: Returning a heap FIELD through a BORROWED receiver (`fn name(ref self) -> String { self.n }`, or a `ref` param) double-frees under codegen; the interpreter is correct. The borrow does not own the field, so codegen returned an ALIAS of the receiver's {ptr,len,cap} buffer, which the caller's drop of the receiver then freed a second time (and any reuse of the receiver dangled). `karac check` accepts the program (copy-out semantics; the interpreter clones). Fires non-generically; unmasked while making generic associated-type field-returns usable.
fix: this commit. `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` (src/codegen/runtime.rs) — the return-value hook run on the tail/return expr in `compile_function` — gained a `FieldAccess` arm: when the receiver is a borrow (`SelfValue`/identifier in `self.ref_params`) and the accessed field is a non-shared heap-owning type (`te_owns_heap_below_buffer` && not `shared_heap_type_for_type_expr`), the loaded field value is deep-CLONED via `emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr(field_te)` (alloca src+dst, call, load) so the returned value owns an independent buffer. The receiver's struct name comes from `inferred_receiver_type(object)` (which resolves `self` too), the field TypeExpr from `struct_field_names` + `struct_field_type_exprs`. Gated on `ref_params` membership so an OWNED receiver's field move-out (handled by zeroing the source cap in `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg_ex`, which requires the receiver to be dropped by this frame) is untouched — the two cases are mutually exclusive. Shared (RC) fields are left to the refcount machinery. ISOLATION: the receiver is used AFTER the call in the tests (`x.name()` then `x.n`), proving a move would be wrong and a clone is required; covers `ref self` / `mut ref self`, String and Vec[i64] fields. Tests: codegen e2e_ref_self_heap_field_return_codegen; memory_sanitizer asan_ref_self_field_return_no_double_free (looped, leak+double-free clean under LSan/ASan). Suites green: codegen 2127, memory_sanitizer 584, interpreter 1141.

title: The `?` operator does not support MULTI-WORD error types in codegen — a `Result[T, E]` where E is (or contains) a String / Vec / multi-field struct. `karac run --interp` handles it; `karac build`/JIT fails LLVM module verification. The common case is the CROSS-error `?` `From` chain into an error struct carrying a String message: `struct AppError { msg: String }` + `impl From[String] for AppError` + `fn run() -> Result[i64, AppError] { let v = may_fail()?; … }` where `may_fail() -> Result[i64, String]`. Same-error `?` and single-word cross-error `?` (e.g. `i64 -> struct{i64}`) both work; only multi-word E is the gap.
fix: this commit. The `?` error path now round-trips MULTI-WORD error payloads. `rebuild_value_from_payload_words` (src/codegen/calls.rs) generic-struct arm advances a word cursor field-by-field, giving each field its own window of words (1 scalar / 2 Slice / 3 String-Vec, recursively for nested structs) via the new `payload_words_for_type` helper — so `AppError { msg: String }` claims all three words for its String field instead of insertvalue'ing a lone i64 into a 3-word slot. `compile_question` (src/codegen/exprs.rs) now (a) extracts ALL inner-error words gated on the INNER value's LLVM width, (b) reconstructs the `From` source arg at the param's true type via `rebuild_value_from_payload_words` (a String param gets its full {ptr,len,cap}), (c) packs the converted target error back into the OUTER Err slot via `coerce_to_payload_words` across all outer payload words, and (d) the `main() -> Result[(), E]` exit path uses the converted value / reconstructs E from all words. Verified value-correct AND valgrind-clean across: same-error String, cross-error String->struct{String}, i64->struct{i64}, same-error Vec[i64], cross-error String->struct{i64,String} (4-word), and `main() -> Result[(),String]` exit. Full --features llvm suite green (codegen 2127, memory_sanitizer 584, par_codegen 155, cli 516).
detail: The `?` error path represents the Err payload as uniform i64 words (tag + w0/w1/w2), and multiple sites assume <= 1 word per struct field: (1) `rebuild_value_from_payload_words` (src/codegen/calls.rs:1503) — the generic-struct arm (line ~1577) inserts exactly ONE word per field, so `AppError { msg: String }` gets `insertvalue {{ptr,i64,i64}} undef, i64 %w0, 0` (an i64 into a 3-word String field) -> verify failure; it must consume as many words as each field needs (recurse into multi-word fields, tracking a word offset). (2) The `?` cross-error `From`-conversion arg marshaling in `compile_question` (src/codegen/exprs.rs ~1487) reconstructs only single-field structs from `w0` and truncates every other shape to `w0`, so `Target.from(e: String)` is called as `Target.from(i64)`. (A local fix using `rebuild_value_from_payload_words(from_param_ty, w0,w1,w2)` fixes THIS site but exposes the next.) (3) The Err-RETURN packing (src/codegen/exprs.rs ~1533/1571) `coerce_to_i64(propagated_payload)` collapses the multi-word target error to one word and inserts a single `propagated_word` into the Result Err slot; it must decompose via `coerce_to_payload_words(propagated_payload, payload_word_count)` and insert every word. (4) The main-result-exit path (~1544) and the enum-layout payload sizing for a multi-word-E Result must agree on the word count. FIX SHAPE: make the four sites use `coerce_to_payload_words` / a word-offset-aware `rebuild_value_from_payload_words` coherently so an N-word error round-trips pack->unpack. Substantial, memory-safety-critical (error-payload representation) — deferred for review rather than landed piecemeal. In-code comments already flag it ('a multi-word E sees only w0 here — the same documented limitation'). WORKAROUND: use a single-word error type (a bare String is NOT single-word; an i64 code or an enum whose payload fits one word is), or run under `--interp`.

title: Memory leak: `match … { Err(e) => println(e.heapfield) }` where `e` is a struct bound out of an enum/Result payload and the heap field is passed DIRECTLY as a call argument (not via an f-string) leaks the field's heap buffer. Narrow: a plain local struct `println(w.msg)` is clean, and the f-string form `println(f"{e.msg}")` is clean — only the enum-payload-bound-struct + direct-field-arg combination leaks.
fix: this commit
detail: Repro (valgrind: `3 bytes definitely lost`): `struct AppError { msg: String } fn run(x: i64) -> Result[i64, AppError] { if x > 0i64 { Result.Ok(x+1i64) } else { Result.Err(AppError { msg: "neg".to_string() }) } } fn main() { match run(-1i64) { Ok(v) => println(f"{v}"), Err(e) => println(e.msg) } }`. The struct `e` is materialized from the Result Err payload in the match arm; `println(e.msg)` moves the `msg` String field out as a direct call argument. The move-out consumes the field but the residual struct/field buffer is never dropped on this path. CONTRAST (all clean): plain local `let w = AppError{..}; println(w.msg)` (lk1); f-string `println(f"{e.msg}")` (q1f); multi-field struct via f-string `println(f"{e.code}:{e.msg}")` (q6). So the gap is the intersection: enum/Result-payload-bound struct binding + heap field passed as a DIRECT call arg. Leak only (no double-free / UAF) — LSan/valgrind class, not ASan-UAF. Discovered while validating the B-2026-07-09-20 `?` multi-word fix; independent of `?` (repros with direct `Result.Err(...)` construction, no `?`). FIX SHAPE: the match-arm struct-payload cleanup must drop heap fields not consumed by the arm body, and/or the direct-field-arg move-out from a match-bound struct must schedule a drop of the containing struct's residual. Compare the (clean) f-string path to see how it wires the field read+drop.
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-10. Root cause (asan + IR dump): a `match` scrutinee of an Option/Result whose INLINE struct payload (word count <= the seed enum inline area, 3 for Option / 5 for Result) is bound WHOLE as `e` never freed the struct payload's own heap fields. The dedicated inline Option/Result cleanup (FreeInline{Option,Result}Payload) frees only a bare {ptr,len,cap} payload (a direct String/Vec), NOT a struct payload's inner fields; and suppress_inline_{option,result}_payload_cleanup zeros the source cap because a `Some(e)`/`Err(e)` binding counts as consuming (pattern_consumes_field) -- so on BOTH the fresh-temp scrutinee (no source cleanup at all) and the named-binding scrutinee (source suppressed) the struct's String was owned by NOBODY and leaked. The ledger's original framing (only the direct-field-arg println(e.msg) shape leaks, f-string clean) was WRONG: the f-string form println(f"{e.msg}") leaks the SAME 3 bytes (it frees its own COPY, not e's original buffer) -- the leak is the struct payload binding itself, independent of how the body reads the field. FIX (src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs): the pattern-binding user-struct arm now also track_struct_var's a copy-supported INLINE Option/Result struct payload (new is_inline_optres_struct_payload gate), so its scope-exit StructDrop frees the fields; the same whole-value / field move-out suppression set (zero_struct_move_caps / zero_struct_field_move_cap) that makes the non-Option/Result arm sound covers `Err(e) => take(e)` / `Err(e) => e` without double-free. Gated to inline payloads via a new pattern_binding_scrutinee_optres_area (3/5) threaded from compile_match, so a heap-BOXED wide payload (owned by the box drop) is left untouched. Regression: asan_result_struct_payload_direct_field_arg (memory_sanitizer; 585 green incl. new test, + codegen 2127 / par_codegen 155 / clippy / fmt). if-let/while-let use a separate binding path (they do not set the flag) -- unaffected, not re-checked here.

fix: this commit
title: `Vector[T, N]` (a fixed-size SIMD value) was not classified Copy, so a bare rebind `let e1 = ux;` where `ux: Vector[f64, 2]` was treated as a MOVE and every later use of `ux` fired a spurious use-after-move. Using a vector in an arithmetic expression (`ux * v`, `ux - uy`) was fine (a read, not a consume) — only a bare identifier-RHS rebind moved it, so aliasing a SIMD lane-bundle for readability was wrongly rejected.
detail: Repro (ownership check fails; `ownership_ok` expects clean): `fn mix() -> Vector[f64, 2] { let ux = Vector[f64, 2].splat(2.0); let uy = Vector[f64, 2].splat(3.0); let e1 = ux; let e4 = uy; ux + uy + e1 + e4 }` — errors `value 'ux' moved here, used again`. Root cause: `is_copy_type` (src/ownership.rs) enumerated Int/UInt/Float/Bool/Char/Unit + Tuple/Array(of Copy)/Slice(imm)/Pointer/Shared|Rc|Arc/Ref/Function/Named(derive Copy) but had NO `Type::Vector` arm, so a SIMD vector fell through to `_ => false` (non-Copy). A `Vector[T, N]` is a fixed-size, register-resident POD bundle of N primitive lanes — semantically Copy exactly like the fixed `Array` arm directly above it (and its lane type is always a Copy scalar). Fathom's Mandelbrot SIMD kernel never hit this because it only ever reuses vectors via binops / reassignment (`zr * zr`, `zr = ...`), never a bare `let x = zr;`; Slipstream's collide kernel aliases `ux`/`uy` (the lattice e1..e8 directions), the first bare Copy-rebind of a SIMD value.
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-11. Added `Type::Vector { element, .. } => is_copy_type(element, tc)` to `is_copy_type` in src/ownership.rs, mirroring the `Array` arm (element-wise Copy). SIMD lane types are always primitive scalars so this is always Copy, but keying it on the element keeps the rule principled. Unblocks the Slipstream `Vector[f64, 2]` collide kernel (native oracle checksums byte-identical to the scalar kernel: 1582897806 / 793640938 / 680974524). Regression: tests/ownership.rs::test_vector_is_copy (348 ownership tests green; fmt + clippy --all-targets clean).

title: Self-hosted ITEM/TYPE parser crashes at runtime (heap corruption) — DISTINCT from the B-2026-07-09-12 auto-par bug. After B-2026-07-09-12 fixed the auto-parallelization of `mut ref self` calls (which unblocked the EXPRESSION parser oracle, now un-ignored + passing), the sibling `selfhost_parser_items` / `selfhost_parser_types` oracles STILL crash on ~28/102 item inputs (any `enum` with fields, `fn` with params, `trait`, `impl`, generic item, doc-comment/attr item) — e.g. `pub fn id(x: i64) -> i64 { x }`, `enum Shape { Circle(i64), Rect(i64, i64) }`, `impl Calc { fn add(ref self, a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 { a + b } }`. Crucially it is NOT auto-par: it fails IDENTICALLY with `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0`. gdb shows the crash in `__GI___libc_free` (heap corruption / double-free) reached from `render_item` via inlined drop helpers (`render_item -> ?? -> free`), i.e. a DROP-TIME double-free while rendering/dropping an item AST node. This is a residual of the original nested-drop / shared-enum-payload move-out double-free family (B-2026-07-09-12's ORIGINAL description) on the WIDER item AST — `FnDefNode` (Vec[FnParamNode], Option[TypeExpr] return, Block body), `EnumDefNode` (Vec[VariantNode] each with Vec of field types), `StructDefNode` (Vec[StructFieldNode]), `TraitDefNode`, `ImplBlockNode` — whose Vec-of-nested-struct-with-shared-child drops are not fully covered by the 6 intra-function clone-on-extract increments that fixed the expression-node cases. REPRO (argv-driven, build once): copy selfhost/src, main reads `Env.args()` and calls `render_item(parse_item_str(argv[1]))`, then sweep the item corpus; ~28 crash. NEXT: asan-trace `render_item` on `pub fn id(x: i64) -> i64 { x }` (drop of a FnDefNode) to pin which Vec[nested-struct]/shared field double-frees; extend the clone-on-extract / drop-synthesis coverage to it. Also recall the sibling drop-synthesis inconsistency observed while investigating B-2026-07-09-12: `__karac_drop_struct_<S>` for a struct with an `Option[shared]` field drops only the FIRST heap field (misses the Option[shared] tail) while `__karac_vec_elem_full_drop_<S>` double-drops the Vec elements — reconcile those two Block/item drop fns as part of this. PINNED 2026-07-10 (asan + gdb, argv-driven item oracle): the crash is `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `__GI___libc_free(mem=<garbage, e.g. 0x555555665>)` inside `__karac_vec_elem_full_drop_FnDefNode`, reached via the RENDER path `render_item -> render_type -> <inlined drop>`. The faulting instruction is a `cap>0`-guarded String/Vec buffer free (`cmpq $0, 0x10(%rdi); free(*(%rdi))`) whose data pointer is a garbage sub-binary-base value (a SCALAR field misread as a `{ptr,len,cap}` header, or a stale slot after a render-consume). The doc-comment / attribute crashers turned out to be a DISTINCT root cause from the render-consume nested-drop family above — NOT a drop-synthesis gap at all, but a MISCOMPILE of `match`-then-reassign on a loop-carried Option/enum local. Discriminators: needs the loop (straight-line clean), needs the payload BINDING `Some(prev)` (wildcard `Some(_)` / `is_some()` clean), needs the reassign after the match (no-reassign clean). ROOT CAUSE (from real IR with ownership loaded, then objdump): the ownership RC-fallback predicate boxes `buf` (auto-RC), so its slot is a `{refcount, value}` box POINTER; reads deref correctly but the whole-value assignment `buf = Some(..)` stores the 4-word Option struct straight into the 8-byte pointer slot (`store {i64,i64,i64,i64} into ptr %buf`), smashing it + 24 bytes of stack — the reload then treats the tag (0x1) as a pointer (`mov 0x9,%rbx` / `decq 0x1` / `free(0x1)` in the optimized asm). WHY the predicate fires: formal `rc_candidates` needs dominance-incomparable (C=match-in-loop-body, U=return-in-exit); the loop back-edge gives the exit an entry-predecessor so the in-loop reassign block does not *dominate* the exit, and the pure-dominance `reassign_kills` is (per its own doc) vacuous for the RC shape — misses the reassign every real C->U path threads. The TREE-WALK INTERPRETER handled the same code (implicit widen), so it was a run==build DIVERGENCE (interp passed, codegen failed). Repro: `fn main(){ let b="A".bytes(); let c=b[0i64]; let mut v:Vec[i64]=Vec.new(); let mut i=0i64; while i<128i64 {v.push(i); i=i+1i64;} println(f"{v[c]}"); }` — interp printed 65, `karac build` failed verification. Binary 33.4 KiB (C parity), runtime RSS 1.4 MiB (C parity), compile 89 ms (~rustc) — the whole gap is the runtime hot loop. HOT LOOP (bench/minimum_window_substring.kara fn min_window): `while r < n { let cr = s[r]; have[cr]+=1; ...; while formed==required { let cl = s[l]; have[cl]-=1; ...; l = l + 1 } r = r + 1 }` with n = s.len() and s an unmutated `ref Vec[i64]`. Ran `opt -passes='default<O2>'` on the raw codegen IR of the minimal two-pointer repro with `scan` marked `noinline` (so its `ref Vec` param stays opaque — the un-annotated repro const-folds away because main passes a literal vector, a probe trap worth noting). Result, stable across one AND two O2 runs (so NOT phase-ordering): s[r] has ZERO surviving checks — its upper bound is compile-time elided via the `r<n` guard and its neg-check folds via the existing `r>=0` monotone assume under a SINGLE O2 (the post-inline `getelementptr i64, ptr %v.data, i64 %r.032` in while.body has no guard). Exactly ONE check survives: the `vidx.oob` on `s[l]` (`%l.126`) in the inner shrink loop — the soundly-required one (l<n unprovable). So the 'monotone-assume needs the midpoint extra-pass' hypothesis is FALSE: the monotone assumes already fold everything foldable under one O2. CONCLUSION: every lead is now exhausted — s[l] BCE (unsound, Rust checks it too), count-table Vec-vs-array (optimizer-erased, 0.03%), and s[r] phase-ordering (already folds) are all ruled out. There is NO localized, sound codegen fix for this kata; the residual ~1.12x (kara 12.46B vs rust_ovf 11.14B instrs) is DIFFUSE codegen quality (overflow-check placement / instruction selection on the arithmetic-heavy inner loop), not one eliminable check. Kept OPEN as an honest small perf gap but NOT PURSUING further — no action item remains. If ever revisited, the only remaining angle is whole-inner-loop instruction-sequence diffing (kara vs rustc) for the arithmetic, which is a general codegen-quality effort, not a #76-specific bug. GENERALIZED 2026-07-10 (the gap is instruction DENSITY, visible only when throughput-bound — confirmed on #77/#78). Instruction-count comparison across the compute-bound backtracking siblings shows the SAME density gap as #76, just latency-hidden. Kata #78 subsets (warm, /usr/bin/time -l): kara 3.110B instructions vs C 2.392B (1.30x) vs rust_ovf 2.908B (1.07x) vs rust 2.573B — yet CYCLES are all within ~1% (kara 2.508B, C 2.514B, rust_ovf 2.539B, rust 2.532B), so wall-time is a dead heat (kara 2nd of five, AT the C floor, ahead of both Rust builds). #77 combinations is the same shape (5-way dead heat). The discriminator is IPC / whether the loop is throughput- or latency-bound: on #76 (a tight scan, kara IPC 8.00, throughput-bound) the extra instructions have nowhere to hide and show as the 1.24x wall-time loss; on #77/#78 (recursion, kara IPC ~1.2, latency/stall-bound on call-return + path push/pop memory traffic — even C is IPC 0.95) the extra instructions execute in the stall shadow for free, so equal cycles -> parity. So the accurate characterization is NOT '#76-specific gap' but 'kara's codegen emits ~1.1-1.3x the instruction count of C/rustc generally (bounds checks, overflow checks, less-tight instruction selection; e.g. #78's kara `while p<plen { path[p] }` indexed fold vs Rust's iterator), and it costs wall-time ONLY on throughput-bound loops'. The lever, if ever pursued, is general codegen density (broad overflow-check elision on provably-safe ops + tighter selection), which would lift the throughput-bound cases (#76) and is invisible on latency-bound ones (#77/#78) — a general codegen-maturity effort, not a per-kata fix. No new action; this sharpens the scope. Sinks all correct, so it is density not miscompilation (kara does MORE work, not less). TWO FLAVORS 2026-07-10 (#81 adds an IPC/scheduling flavor, distinct from density). Kata #81 (search-rotated-sorted-array-II, a cache-hot duplicate-aware binary search) puts kāra LAST of five on the M5 (c 137.8 < go 148.0 < rust 167.3 < rust_ovf 203.4 < kara 219.9 ms; 1.60x C, 1.08x equal-safety rust_ovf). But unlike #76/#79 this gap is NOT instruction density: kāra retires 3.554G instructions to rust_ovf's 3.540G (identical, 1.004x), yet burns 1.10x the cycles at a LOWER IPC (kara 3.55 vs rust_ovf 3.89). So the same emitted work schedules ~10% worse on the M5 pipeline — an instruction-SELECTION/SCHEDULING quality gap, not a count gap. (Ruled out the tempting 'nums[mid] bounds check survives because the guard is `lo <= hi` not the strict `lo < hi` the midpoint BCE needs' hypothesis: if kāra kept an extra check rust_ovf elides, kāra's instruction count would exceed rust_ovf's — it does not. Confirming via the instruction count BEFORE claiming, per this entry's own #76 reversal.) Also note overflow checks genuinely cost on #81 (rust_ovf 203.4 vs rust 167.3 = 1.22x; midpoint arithmetic + rolling hash on the hot path), unlike the free-overflow katas. So B-2026-07-10-5 now covers TWO diffuse codegen-quality sub-flavors, both throughput-visible / latency-hidden: (a) instruction DENSITY — kāra emits ~1.1-1.75x C/rustc's instruction count (#76/#79/#80); (b) instruction SCHEDULING — kāra emits the SAME count but ~10% lower IPC (#81). Neither has a single lever; the general remedy is codegen maturity (tighter selection + scheduling + broad overflow-check elision on provably-safe ops). No per-kata fix. #87 CORROBORATION 2026-07-11 (density flavor (a) on RECURSION, throughput-exposed; plus a kata-code caveat that refines the Vec-vs-array finding). Kata #87 scramble-string, the O(n^4) top-down MEMOISED recursion, on the production-representative x86-64 Linux container: at EQUAL SAFETY kara 826.6 ms vs rust_ovf 643.8 vs c 679.5 (kara 1.28x rust_ovf / 1.22x C). Static disasm of the hot `scramble`: kara 14 `jo` (overflow) + 10 `jae` (bounds) = 24 safety branches vs rust_ovf 10 + 5 = 15 (LLVM elides ~half rustc's bounds + ~4 overflow checks that kara's survive); computing memo[key] from (i1*n+i2)*(n+1)+len emits 4 `jo` + 1 `jae` for one indexed read. REFINES this entry two ways: (1) the '#77/#78 recursion is latency-bound so density is hidden -> parity' claim is NOT universal — #87's memoised recursion is throughput-exposed enough (tight per-call char-count loop + memo-index arithmetic between calls) that the SAME density gap costs ~1.14x wall, i.e. recursion CAN lose, IPC-dependent. (2) The '#76 Vec-vs-array count table was optimizer-erased (0.03%)' conclusion does NOT generalize: #87's char-count table written as `Vec.new()`+push is allocated PER-CALL INSIDE the recursion (not loop-invariant like #76's), so it is NOT erased — rewriting it as `Array[i64,26]` (matching C/Rust stack arrays) dropped instrs 32.9M->28.7M and seq wall ~9% (810->736 ms), sink preserved. LESSON for the density measurements: a fixed-size scratch buffer must be a stack `Array`, not a `Vec`, or the per-call heap alloc inflates the gap and is mistaken for codegen density. Kata #87 fixed to Array[i64,26] accordingly. Still no new action item — confirms the general codegen-density scope; no per-kata fix. INDEPENDENT REPRO 2026-07-12 (x86-64 Linux container, clang/opt/callgrind 18.1.3 -- fresh toolchain, CONFIRMS no-bounded-fix and SHARPENS the overflow-check evidence). Re-audited from scratch on the new environment. (A) Overflow-check parity with EQUAL-SAFETY C: built a representative two-pointer + flat-index kara repro (`while r<n { acc+=s[r]; while acc>k {acc-=s[l]; l+=1} best+=(r*n+l)*(n+1)+r; r+=1 }`) and the byte-equivalent C at `clang -O2 -ftrapv`; identical sink. Static disasm: kara's inlined loop emits EXACTLY the same 6 `jo` overflow branches as clang -ftrapv (the only extra is the one soundly-required `s[l]` bounds check; C is unchecked). On a constant-bounded loop (`while i<1000 { sum += i*2; sum += i+1; i+=1 }`) kara and clang BOTH SCEV-elide every induction-variable overflow check (`i*2`, `i+1`, `i=i+1` -> plain lea/add, no jo) and BOTH keep jo only on the unbounded `sum` accumulator. So kara's overflow-check ELISION already matches clang -ftrapv -- the 'broad overflow-check elision on provably-safe ops' lever this entry kept naming is ALREADY DONE by LLVM for kara; not a deficiency. CAVEAT refining the #87 evidence: raw cross-compiler `jo`-COUNTS are confounded by UNROLL FACTOR (kara unrolled the constant-bound loop x4, clang x2 -> 7 vs 6 jo for identical per-iteration checks), so the #87 'kara 14 jo vs rust_ovf 10' static count OVERSTATES any elision gap; the dynamic callgrind Ir is the trustworthy signal. (B) Dynamic Ir reproduces the band: amplified loop-dominated repro (2.5M inner iters, 99.25% Ir in the inlined scan): kara 46.6M vs C -ftrapv 41.5M (1.12x, EXACTLY this entry's equal-safety band) vs C -O2-unsafe 29.0M (1.61x). The 5.1M / 1.12x over equal-safety C is ~2 instr/iter = the required `s[l]` bounds check + diffuse selection, NOT any eliminable overflow check. NET: every sound lever independently re-confirmed done-or-unsound on fresh tooling; investigation stays CLOSED-no-fix, severity low. The only remaining axis is general instruction-selection maturity (unroll/scheduling), not a localized kara bug. DENSITY EFFORT 2026-07-12 (x86 container, callgrind Ir; owner-directed general density pass — CORRECTS this entry's framing). Added a KARAC_NO_AUTOPAR escape hatch (cli.rs, 1f39fea) so sequential lowering can be measured in isolation, then measured the representative two-pointer scan and the count-table (have[cr]/need[cr]) pattern SEQUENTIALLY vs equal-safety rustc. FINDINGS: (1) auto-par overhead is NEGLIGIBLE here — seq 46.56M vs auto-par 46.61M Ir (~0.1%); the reduce-worker the scan lowers into is a single sequential partition, so the earlier 1.12x callgrind number was NOT auto-par overhead. (2) At EQUAL SAFETY on x86, kara BEATS rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on on instruction count: two-pointer scan kara 46.56M vs rust_ovf 51.65M (kara 0.90x, 10% FEWER); count-table kara 36.12M vs rust_ovf 37.02M (kara 0.976x). vs UNSAFE C -O2 -ftrapv (no bounds checks) kara is 1.089x, the entire delta being the memory-safety bounds check on the unprovable-relational s[l] (l<=r not syntactically provable — same check rust_ovf keeps). (3) ASM CONFIRMATION of kara's sequential scan loop: s[r] loaded ONCE and reused for both acc+= and best+= (CSE'd like C's r10), indexed addressing (rax,rdi,8), loop-counter inc with NO overflow check (elided like clang), s[r] upper-bound check elided via the r<n guard; the only structural extra vs C is the required s[l] bounds check. Also confirmed opt -O2 fully CSEs a doubly-emitted s[r] read (one bounds check/load/panic-site survive). CONCLUSION: kara x86 sequential codegen DENSITY is not behind — it is 2-10% AHEAD of equal-safety rustc on these loops; every named sound lever (overflow-check elision, counter-overflow elision, index-load CSE, single-load reuse, indexed addressing, provable-bounds elision) is already done. The original 'kara 1.12x behind rust_ovf' gap is therefore aarch64/M5-specific instruction SELECTION/SCHEDULING (consistent with this entry's own #81 'same instruction count, ~10% lower IPC' note), NOT x86 instruction density, and the residual vs C is memory safety (unsound to remove). No x86 density fix exists to make; the honest remaining axis is aarch64 scheduling/selection maturity, out of reach in this x86 container. FIXED 2026-07-15 (2fa6513) — ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND CORRECTED, and it was NONE of the axes this entry investigated: not BCE (the s[l] check is soundly required and rust_ovf keeps it too), not phase ordering, not Vec-vs-array, not scheduling — karac simply NEVER COMMUNICATED THE VEC-LENGTH BOUND to LLVM. rustc folds len-derived overflow checks because slice lengths are capped by the Layout <= isize::MAX allocator contract; karac's len loads carried no such fact, so at EQUAL safety the emitted loop kept (a) a per-iteration overflow-FLAG re-check (cbnz) on the hoisted n+1 and (b) a full checked add PLUS a duplicate increment for l+1 under the dominating l <u len bounds check — exactly +1 instr/outer-iter and +2 instrs/inner-iter, the documented 1.12x instructions-retired deficit vs rust_ovf. FIX (three legs): (1) runtime/src/alloc.rs gains KARAC_MAX_ALLOC_BYTES = 2^61-1 — a ceiling in karac_alloc_fallible/karac_realloc_or_panic/karac_alloc_zeroed_or_panic that is unreachable on real hardware (VA <= 2^57) and exists purely to make len <= cap <= cap*elem_size < 2^61 a PROVABLE invariant of every live Vec/String; (2) codegen annotates Vec len loads with !range [0, 2^61) at .len(), both emit_split_bounds_check len loads, and the for-in bound (annotate_len_load_range; zero-sized elements — legal via struct E {} — are structurally detected and skipped; slice sites skipped: Array-backed slices are not allocator-bounded); (3) checked_alloc_bytes (umul.with.overflow -> panic 'capacity overflow') at every user-controlled count*elem_size site (with_capacity/try_with_capacity/Vec.filled/ String.repeat) — which ALSO closes a latent MEMORY-SAFETY hole this investigation exposed: Vec.with_capacity((1<<61)+1) of an 8-byte element previously WRAPPED the byte multiply to an 8-byte allocation while recording cap = 2^61+1, a heap overflow on the first pushes; it now panics up front with a source location. EVIDENCE (cross-ISA static diff, in-container LLVM 18 opt/llc — the 'only remaining angle' this entry named, done statically on x86 by retargeting karac's IR to arm64-apple-macosx -mcpu=apple-m1): #76 minimal two-pointer repro outer/inner loop 23/10 instructions BEFORE -> 22/8 AFTER = EXACT structural parity with rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on (22/8, same csel bounds-merge, same single unchecked increments); x86-64 whole-function 70 -> 61. Sink preserved (500497157161, AOT = JIT = interp), valgrind clean. Tests: ir_vec_len_load_carries_range_metadata / ir_zero_sized_elem_vec_len_has_no_range_metadata / e2e_with_capacity_count_overflow_panics + 2 runtime alloc units; codegen 2382 / par_codegen 159 / memory_sanitizer 716 green; fmt + clippy (native + both wasm cfgs) clean; all four runtime archives rebuilt. RESIDUALS: (i) M5 wall-time re-bench of kata #76 is owner-side (this container is x86; static instruction parity predicts the 1.12x equal-safety deficit closes; the ~1.24x-vs-C residual is the soundly-required s[l] check C does not pay); (ii) the #81 flavor-(b) same-count/lower-IPC scheduling gap is NOT addressed — remains documented-no-lever; (iii) slice len loads unannotated pending a type-level Array size cap; (iv) interp reports capacity overflow as a raw Rust panic (diagnostics polish).

Turbofish-inferred raw-pointer binding loses its pointee in codegen: `let p = ptr.null[u8](); unsafe { p.read() }` fails with 'no handler for method read on variable p', while the annotated form `let p: *const u8 = ptr.null()` works. Root cause: a turbofish constructor's `*const T` return does not thread T=u8 into the binding's type as a clean `Type::Pointer` reaching the read's receiver `obj_ty`, so the typechecker's `Type::Pointer` method arm never records `pointer_method_receiver_pointees` and codegen's `raw_pointer_pointee_types` has no entry. Pre-existing (reproduces on 5931619, before the E_RAW_POINTER_UNRESOLVED_POINTEE slice). Surfaced because the E_RAW diagnostic recommends `ptr.null[u8]()` as a fix-it — the annotation fix-it is the reliable one until this lands. Typechecks fine (no type error); codegen-only. FIX DIRECTION: register the pointee for an inferred (non-annotated) pointer let-binding from its inferred `Type::Pointer` type, or ensure the turbofish return-type substitution yields a `Type::Pointer` at the binding's use-site occurrences. RESOLVED 2026-07-11 (8c4a32f): ptr.null[u8]() parses as Call{Index{FieldAccess{ptr,null},u8}} (indexing/turbofish ambiguity like size_of[T]()); neither typecheck's explicit-generic-args route nor codegen's pointer-intrinsic route recognized it, so T never bound (*const T -> Type::Error, no pointee, value stored i64). FIX both phases: expr_call.rs routes the Index/2-seg-Path dotted-builtin turbofish through infer_explicit_generic_args_call; call_dispatch.rs mirrors ptr.null() lowering via compile_ptr_module_call. fix: ed07aed
title: An explicit `par { }` block's top-level `let` bindings did not ESCAPE the block: `par { let a = fa(); let b = fb(); } /* use a, b */` failed with `error[resolve]: undefined name 'a'` after the block. The join barrier is meant to make each branch's result live in the ENCLOSING scope (the shape examples/db_pipeline::execute_pair and design.md's structured-concurrency model rely on); the previous design only exposed branch bindings to an optional tail expression INSIDE the block (`par { …; (a, b) }`). ROOT CAUSE: every phase gave the par block a private scope for its branch bindings that was popped at block end — resolver `resolve_par_block` (re-)defined the join bindings into an intermediate block scope, typechecker routed `ExprKind::Par` through `infer_block` (pushes/pops a scope), interpreter `eval_par_block` pushed/popped a merge scope, and codegen `compile_par_block` only materialized return slots for names read by `block.final_expr` (so a binding consumed AFTER the block, invisible to the tail-expr read set, got no slot). FIX (B-2026-07-11-3): the join barrier now hoists each branch's top-level `let` into the ENCLOSING scope across all four phases — resolver defines join bindings into the enclosing scope (no private block scope), typechecker checks branch stmts in the enclosing local_scope, interpreter merges branch vars into the current scope, and codegen gives EVERY top-level branch binding a return slot bound into the surrounding scope. Mirrors the auto-parallelizer, whose grouped `let`s are ordinary enclosing-scope locals already (that's why auto-par never had this bug and why the hard parts — slot liveness / drop across the join barrier — were already solved). Sibling isolation (B-2026-07-02-5) is preserved: each branch RHS still resolves in its own child scope and a sibling read still gets the cross-branch diagnostic (message updated to note bindings are usable after the block, not only in a tail expr). Both the escape form and the tail form work. Verified: resolver/typechecker/interpreter/ownership/effectchecker/concurrency suites, par_codegen (E2E escape test), codegen 2131, and an ASAN test asserting escaped heap (String) owners drop exactly once (no leak / double-free). Found by the docs/book audit; unblocks examples/db_pipeline.

fix: 8be6c95
title: `spawn(|| work())` — a closure-literal thunk with NO LHS annotation — failed type inference with `cannot infer type parameter 'T'; add a type annotation`. design.md:707 specifies `spawn[T](f: OnceFn() -> T) -> TaskHandle[T]`, so `T` must be inferable from the closure's return type. ROOT CAUSE: in `check_call_args_with_substitution_full` (the generic free-function call inference), pass 1 SKIPS closure args (`arg_tys.push(None)`) because closures are checked in pass 2 with param-type pushdown — but pass 2 checked each closure against the resolved slot and never unified the closure's INFERRED type back into the instantiated slot. So a type param appearing ONLY inside a closure param's type (`spawn[T](OnceFn() -> T)`, where `T` is fixed solely by the thunk's return, with no other argument to bind it) stayed an unsolved metavar — the return `TaskHandle[T]` came back with `T` unbound and the `let` binding tripped the unsolved-type-param diagnostic. The named-fn form `spawn(make_int)` worked (a fn ref is a NON-closure arg, inferred + unified in pass 1) and any LHS-annotated form worked (the annotation pins `T` from the LHS), which is why every existing spawn test passed and the closure-thunk gap slipped. FIX (B-2026-07-11-4): pass 2's closure branch now unifies the closure's inferred type into the un-resolved slot via `unify_types` (whose `Fn`→`OnceFn` cross arm descends into the return type), binding `T` from the closure body; a no-op when `T` was already solved from another argument. Both the free `spawn(|| …)` and method `tg.spawn(|| …)` forms now infer without an annotation; `spawn(work())` (a non-thunk VALUE) stays rejected because `spawn` wants a thunk. Verified: typechecker suite + two new closure-thunk inference tests (i64 and String returns), spawn_e2e, codegen 2131. Found by the docs/book audit; makes docs/book/src/ch14-concurrency.md compiler-accurate.

fix: this commit
title: Matching a `ref`-scrutinee enum and using a non-i64-word payload (String / bool / narrow int / float) miscompiles: the via-ptr fast path binds the leaf directly at the i64 payload WORD, so `*binding` / a method call deref-loads the wrong shape. A String payload → codegen PANIC `into_struct_value` "Found IntValue … expected the StructValue variant" (`%s.deref = load i64`) at the `.push_str(s)` dispatch; a bool payload → module-verify `Branch condition is not 'i1' type! br i64 %b.deref`.
detail: Minimal repro (panics on `karac build` AND `karac run` JIT): `enum E { S(String), N(i64) } fn render(e: ref E, out: mut ref String) { match e { S(s) => { out.push_str(s); } N(n) => { out.push_str("num"); } } }`. Root cause: `bind_pattern_values_via_ptr`'s `TupleVariant` arm (`src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs`) took a `ok_padded_primitive` fast path (meant for `Option[i64]`'s over-wide 3-word slot) whenever the FIRST payload LLVM word was primitive — but every heap aggregate flattens to `{ptr:i64,…}` so its first word IS i64, and narrow scalars sit in an i64 slot too. It then `emit_ref_leaf_binding_at_ptr(s, field_ptr, field_ty=i64)` bound the leaf as a `ref i64`. The value-source (copy-shim) path already reconstructs payloads at their true type (narrowing bool→i1, rebuilding String/Vec), so the fix is to DEFER to it.
source: dogfood:examples/json.kara (recursive JSON enum, `match v { Num(n) => out.push_str(n), Bool(b) => if *b … }`)
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-11. In the via-ptr `TupleVariant` arm, added `declared_mismatches_word`: look up the leaf binding's recorded surface type (`pattern_binding_types`) → `llvm_type_for_name`, and if it isn't the i64 payload word, `return Ok(None)` to defer to the value-source path. Covers String/Vec (struct ≠ i64), bool (i1), narrow ints (i8/i16/i32), char (i32), f64 — while `Option[i64]` (name "i64" == i64 word) keeps the fast path. Type-info-absent bindings keep the legacy heuristic (no regression). Generalizes the B-2026-07-09-6 struct-payload guard to every non-word payload. Regression tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_ref_enum_string_and_bool_payload; 2130 codegen + 587 asan green.

fix: this commit
title: A `Vec[struct]` bound as an enum payload loses its element TypeExpr, so `for e in entries { e.field }` binds the element without a struct type and the field read returns garbage (`i64 0`) → codegen PANIC at the `push_str(e.field)` dispatch. A `Vec[i64]` enum payload iterates fine (primitive elements need no field GEP), and a plain `let es: Vec[Ent]` local field-access works — only the intersection (Vec-of-struct AS an enum payload) breaks.
detail: Minimal repro: `enum J { N, Obj(Vec[Ent]) } struct Ent { key: String } fn ser(v: ref J, out: mut ref String) { match v { N => {out.push_str("n");} Obj(entries) => { for e in entries { out.push_str(e.key); } } } }`. Root cause: the value-source enum-payload binding (`src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs`, the `"Vec"|"VecDeque"` arm) registered `vec_elem_types[name]` (the LLVM element type — enough for a for-loop over a `Vec[i64]` payload) but NOT `var_elem_type_exprs[name]` (the element TypeExpr that struct-field GEP resolves through). A plain local gets both via `register_var_from_type_expr`; the payload path got only the former, so a struct element had no TypeExpr and `e.field` fell through to an i64 read.
source: dogfood:examples/json.kara (`Obj(entries: Vec[Entry]) => for e in entries { escape_into(e.key, out); ser_into(e.val, out) }`)
resolution: FIXED 2026-07-11. The `"Vec"|"VecDeque"` payload-binding arm now also `self.var_elem_type_exprs.insert(name, inner_te.clone())` alongside `vec_elem_types`, so the for-loop element carries the struct TypeExpr and `e.field` GEPs correctly — identical to a plain `let es: Vec[Ent]`. Regression tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_ref_enum_vec_struct_payload_field_access; 2130 codegen + 587 asan green.

fix: this commit
title: `?` on a `Result[<concrete user enum>, E]` truncates the multi-word Ok payload to its first word: `let v = pv()?` where `pv() -> Result[Json, String]` and `Json` is a wide (>1-word) enum yields `v` typed as a bare `i64` (the tag/first word), not the full enum aggregate. A later use (`Entry { val: v }`, method call) then mis-types it → module-verify `Invalid InsertValueInst operands! insertvalue { …, {i64,i64,i64,i64} } …, i64 %v, 1` (an i64 inserted where the 4-word enum struct is expected). Explicit `match pv() { Ok(x) => x, Err(e) => return … }` works — ONLY the `?` sugar truncates.
detail: Minimal repro (`karac build` / JIT fail; interpreter fine): `enum Json { Null, Str(String), Obj(Vec[Entry]) } struct Entry { key: String, val: Json } fn pv() -> Result[Json, String] { Result.Ok(Json.Null) } fn po() -> Result[Json, String] { let mut es: Vec[Entry] = Vec.new(); let v = pv()?; es.push(Entry { key: "k", val: v }); Result.Ok(Json.Obj(es)) }`. ROOT CAUSE (precise): `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` (`src/codegen/exprs.rs`) rebuilds a multi-word Ok payload only when its type is found in `string_typed_exprs` (String) or `enum_inst_type_exprs` (generic `Named`); otherwise it `return Ok(w0)` — truncating to one word. `enum_inst_type_exprs` is populated in `src/lowering.rs:~498` with a `Type::Named { args } if !args.is_empty()` filter, which EXCLUDES a concrete (arg-less) user enum like `Json`. So `?` on `Result[Json, …]` can't find `Json`'s type and truncates. String/Vec[T]/generic payloads work because they land in one of the two tables. FIX DIRECTION: give `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` the concrete-enum Ok payload type — either a dedicated `?`-Ok-payload TypeExpr table (populated from `tc.expr_types` at the `?` span, which already holds the unwrapped type per the fn's own comment), or broaden the `enum_inst_type_exprs` filter to include arg-less enums (verify the other consumer — the Some-payload heap-vs-word decision — is unaffected). The failure-path (`Err`) already reconstructs wide payloads via `rebuild_value_from_payload_words`; the Ok-path needs the same type resolution for concrete enums.
