COST TO WEIGH, and the reason this is not obviously a win: the user body has to be emitted TWICE (once in the ASCII inner loop, once on the multibyte path), which roughly doubles the IR for every `.chars()` loop in the program. Most `.chars()` loops are not hot, so this wants either a size gate or evidence that the code-size cost is acceptable across the corpus — measure `tests/` binary sizes and compile time, not just the kata.
resolution: FIXED with the dual-region shape this entry proposed. `compile_for_string_chars_bailout_inner` (src/codegen/control_flow_for.rs) replaces the single loop with a NESTED pair: an inner ASCII scan whose only backedge advances the offset by exactly 1, wrapped in an outer loop that the multibyte path re-enters after decoding one scalar. The user body is emitted once per region, each with its own LoopFrame, so `continue` reaches the latch that advances by the right width and `break` reaches the shared exit. Correctness is a RUNTIME check (`byte < 0x80`), so unlike B-2026-07-27-7 this needs no compile-time proof and covers every string. THE WIN IS BIGGER THAN THIS ENTRY PREDICTED, AND IT COMES IN TWO HALVES. Measured by intervention on a 400k-call `replace_char(word: ref String, ..)` probe (callgrind Ir, x86, deterministic; all variants print 4000000): the general loop is 243,541,256; a stride-1 byte walk WITHOUT a dominating ASCII check is 195,581,283 (-19.7%); the same walk WITH the check is 181,501,256 (-25.5%). The second half was not in this entry's analysis and is the more interesting one: inside the fast region `fast.peek` dominates the body with `byte < 0x80`, so the bound `char` carries that range and `out.push(ch)` folds its branchless UTF-8 width computation (cmp/sbb/cmp/cmovb/cmp/cmovb, ~10 instructions) to a constant 1. The shipped lowering lands at 189,901,256 (-22.0%), i.e. 86% of the hand-written ceiling; the emitted fast loop is `movzbl (%rdx,%rdi,1)` / `js slow` / `lea 0x1(%r13),%rbx` with the width chain and the codepoint stack-store both gone. WHOLE-KATA: #127 1,962,274,718 -> 1,782,103,822 Ir (-9.2%, answer unchanged at 755481159), which moves it from 1.235x to 1.122x the equal-hash Rust lane; #126 2,268,624,095 -> 2,100,359,999 (-7.4%, answer unchanged). Both well above this entry's 3.7% estimate, which was an arm64 wall-clock figure for `replace_char` alone and did not account for the push-folding half. THE CODE-SIZE COST THIS ENTRY FLAGGED AS DECISIVE TURNS OUT TO BE SMALL, and the reason is the gate rather than luck. Across the 31 buildable .kara programs in examples/ + kara-katas that contain a `.chars()` loop: total text +0.4171% (10,801,400 -> 10,846,456 bytes), only 10 of 31 changed size at all, worst case +2.319% (count-and-say, +8 KiB on 353 KiB). Compile time is the realer cost: +11.5% on kata #127 and +6.7% on examples/json.kara (min of 9 runs each, debug-build compiler), scaling with the number of QUALIFYING chars loops rather than with program size. WHAT KEEPS DUPLICATION SAFE is src/codegen/chars_bailout.rs, a fail-closed allowlist over an EXHAUSTIVE match with no wildcard arm, so a new AST variant breaks the build instead of silently joining the fast path (the `ascii_const_chars` discipline). Rule 1 — NO NESTED LOOPS — does most of the work and was the key design realization: auto-par / `par` reduction lowering only ever attaches to a loop, so barring nested loops keeps `record_spawn_site` (which mints a fresh par_id and a KARAC_SPAWN_SITES row per CALL, the one genuinely identity-keyed side effect in reach) out of duplicated code entirely; it also makes duplication non-recursive, since nested duplicable chars loops would otherwise cost 2^depth copies. It costs nothing real, because a chars loop containing a loop is not the hot inner loop. Rule 2 excludes closures (a module-level fn per occurrence), comptime, par/seq/lock/providers, unsafe/try, and defer/errdefer. Rule 3 is a 96-node budget; charging per node also bounds the walker's own recursion depth, so it cannot overflow the stack. `KARAC_CHARS_ASCII_BAILOUT=0` forces the single-copy lowering back, matching KARAC_RC_ELIDE_REF_PARAMS=0. VERIFIED against the silent-miscompile risk, which is the whole reason this was split out as its own bounded task rather than done at the tail of the previous session. A 19-shape gauntlet (empty; single 1/2/3/4-byte scalars; pure ASCII; pure multibyte; leading/trailing/adjacent/alternating mixes; a 39-char mixed run) crossed with 11 body shapes (codepoint sum, count, push round-trip, continue from BOTH regions, break from the fast region, break from the slow region, return, labeled continue on the loop itself, labeled continue/break to an OUTER loop from both copies, an index-sensitive replace, and a `match ch` body) ran identically across all EIGHT of {old lowering, new lowering} x {interp, JIT, AOT-O2, AOT-O0} — byte-identical output, with the old lowering as the reference so the new shape is pinned to pre-existing semantics rather than to itself. valgrind memcheck clean (0 errors) on the gauntlet at both opt levels and on the probe. Suites green: codegen 2594, interpreter 1313, typechecker 2091, par_codegen 200, memory_sanitizer 855, cli 537, selfhost_codegen (the self-host oracle — the selfhost lexer/parser/typechecker are themselves full of chars loops), lib 1105, plus ownership/resolver/parser/lexer/effectchecker/module_graph/concurrency/ comptime/wasm_codegen/lljit_e2e/drop_differential/json/closures/lowering/ book_snippets/walker/monomorphization and the four selfhost check suites. Both clippy gates and fmt clean. NOTE ON A FULL `cargo test --features llvm`: it cannot link in this container — ~40 debug test binaries at ~200 MB each exceeds the session disk allowance, surfacing as `linking with cc failed` on whichever targets happen to be last. That is an environment limit, not a code failure; every target above was run individually and passed.

title: A plain (non-`shared`) struct that reaches ITSELF through a `Vec` field OVERFLOWS THE COMPILER'S STACK during codegen — every adjacency-list graph (`struct GraphNode { mut edges: Vec[GraphNode] }`) aborts karac, on a program that passes `karac check` clean.
fix: cb38efe
detail:
REPRO: `karac run examples/tangle/src/cross_graph.kara` (a checked-in example; `karac check` on it reports `All checks passed`) aborts with `has overflowed its stack`. Still overflows at a 64 MB stack, so the recursion is UNBOUNDED, not merely deep. Minimal shape: `struct Node { val: i64, mut kids: Vec[Node] }` plus a by-value `fn total(n: Node)`.

ROOT CAUSE: the copy-support ANALYSIS and the copy EMITTER walked to different depths.

`aggregate_param_copy_supported_struct` (src/codegen/param_own.rs) already carries a `stack: &mut Vec<String>` of in-progress struct names precisely to break cyclic types. But `field_copy_supported`'s path arm returned `true` for `"String" | "str" | "Vec" | "VecDeque"` WITHOUT inspecting the Vec's element type, so the walk terminated at the `Vec` and the guard never got a second look at the enclosing struct. Analysis therefore answered `copyable`, and the by-value param was made callee-owned.

The EMITTER does not stop at the Vec. Since B-2026-07-04-9(a), `deep_copy_one_aggregate_field` descends into a `Vec[struct]`'s elements via `deep_copy_vec_aggregate_elements_in_place`, whose loop body INLINES a per-element `deep_copy_struct_heap_fields_in_place`. For a self-referential type that is struct -> Vec-element -> struct with no base case. gdb shows the exact 3-frame cycle (param_own.rs:563 -> :884 -> :1126 -> :563).

WHY NO FINITE EMISSION EXISTS: the per-element copy is UNROLLED at emission time, so terminating would require the emitted nesting depth to equal the runtime data depth, which is unknown at compile time. Emitting a real recursive LLVM function per type would fix it generally; short of that the analysis must DECLINE the type.

FIX: consult `stack` in the `Vec`/`VecDeque` arm — if the element type is a non-shared user struct already on the stack, report not-copyable. The param then falls back to caller-retains, the same conservative treatment every other non-copyable field shape already gets (no entry copy, no callee drop, so no double-free). Narrowed to exactly the emitter's descent condition (`ElemCopy::Struct`), so nothing else changes.

VERIFICATION: an IR-equivalence oracle over all 221 in-repo `.kara` files (`compile_to_ir` on each, before vs after) shows EXACTLY ONE file's output changed - cross_graph.kara, from stack-overflow to real IR. The other 205 emit byte-identical IR. Regression test `test_e2e_self_referential_struct_through_vec_does_not_overflow_codegen` in tests/codegen.rs; it also pins that the declined copy still yields a correct program (JIT and interpreter both print `total: 3`).

NOTE: fixing the crash does NOT make cross_graph.kara correct - see B-2026-07-28-4.

title: THREE of the five `examples/tangle` programs - the flagship ownership-soundness dogfood corpus - do not match the expected output their own README documents, and nothing in CI runs them.
fix: edde4a7
resolution: CLOSED 2026-07-28. All five `examples/tangle` programs now match the output their README documents, on BOTH backends, and the README oracle (tests/tangle_corpus.rs) gates every one of them with no `KnownBroken` entries left. Four distinct defects, each filed and fixed separately: cross_graph's double free (edde4a7 — a self-referential struct param whose declined entry-copy fell back to caller-retains, restored to a true move); undo_redo's dropped write (B-2026-07-28-6); doubly_linked's interpreter hang (B-2026-07-28-7, a general match-arm miscompile with nothing to do with this corpus); doubly_linked's uninitialized read (B-2026-07-28-8); and undo_redo's heap corruption (B-2026-07-28-9). Every program is valgrind-clean except parent_tree, which retains 256 bytes in 6 blocks — the reference cycle its own source comment documents as the honest cost of strong back-pointers under RC, not a defect. VERIFICATION CAVEAT: all of this was measured on x86-64 Linux (valgrind memcheck + the x86 memory_sanitizer/LSan suite); per CLAUDE.md the arm64 leak leg is a separate gate and has not been run here.
detail:
examples/tangle/README.md documents exact expected output per program, so the corpus already HAS an oracle - it just is not wired to anything. Measured 2026-07-28 with both backends (after the B-2026-07-28-3 crash fix):

  parent_tree    codegen OK   interp OK
  interp         codegen OK   interp OK
  cross_graph    codegen WRONG (prints NOTHING, exit 1, empty stdout AND stderr)   interp OK (`diamond reachable-sum (d counted twice): 14`)
  doubly_linked  codegen WRONG (forward/backward correct, then prints `3636832955035936679` where the README says `3` - an uninitialized read)   interp HANGS (killed at timeout)
  undo_redo      codegen WRONG (`30 / 30 / 30 / 30` where the README says `30 / 20 / 10 / 20`) AND THEN CORRUPTS THE HEAP (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`)   interp OK

So: 3/5 wrong under codegen, 1/5 wrong under the interpreter, and undo_redo is a memory-safety bug, not merely a wrong answer. The undo_redo heap corruption and the doubly_linked garbage read are each likely separate root causes; filed together because they were found by one oracle run and share the corpus.

These are the shapes the corpus exists to prove sound (cross-edge graph, doubly-linked list with `mut prev`/`mut next`, undo/redo writing through a shared cell handle). The README asserts of interp.kara only that it is "Verified through BOTH the interpreter and codegen" - the other four make no codegen claim, which is consistent with codegen never having been checked here.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: nothing runs these. Grep across .github/workflows, tests/, and scripts/ finds no reference to examples/tangle except one comment in tests/ownership.rs. The package also has no `src/main.kara` or `src/lib.kara`, so `karac build` in the package dir errors with "no entry file" - the five programs are only reachable via `karac run <file>`.

SUGGESTED FIX ORDER: (1) wire the README's documented outputs into a test that runs all five on BOTH backends - the oracle already exists in prose; (2) then chase undo_redo's heap corruption first (memory safety), doubly_linked's uninitialized read second, cross_graph's empty output third. UPDATE 2026-07-28 (85fc58c): undo_redo's WRONG ANSWER is fixed — it now prints the README's `30 / 20 / 10 / 20`. Root cause was B-2026-07-28-6 (a store through a `shared struct` field fell through to codegen's no-op tail and was silently dropped). Its HEAP CORRUPTION at exit SURVIVES that fix, which settles this entry's open question: the two are separate defects, not one. Remaining under this entry: undo_redo's `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`; cross_graph, which under codegen STACK-OVERFLOWS (re-measured after cb38efe — this entry originally recorded empty output + exit 1); and doubly_linked, which prints an uninitialized value under codegen AND hangs under the INTERPRETER (still the corpus's only interpreter-side failure). parent_tree and interp remain correct on both backends. The suggested first step — wire the README's documented outputs into a test — is still undone and still the right next move, since 2 of 5 programs are now correct on both backends and could regress unnoticed. UPDATE 2026-07-28 (edde4a7): CROSS_GRAPH FIXED, and the oracle this entry asked for FIRST is now wired (tests/tangle_corpus.rs — all five programs, BOTH backends, still-broken entries pinned as `Expect::KnownBroken` so fixing one turns the test RED and forces promotion rather than landing silently). cross_graph prints its documented `diamond reachable-sum (d counted twice): 14`, valgrind-clean at 0 bytes in use at exit. ROOT CAUSE, and it was NOT the cross-edge or the RC fallback: it reduces to ten lines with neither. `struct N { val: i64, mut edges: Vec[N] }` + `impl N { fn add(mut ref self, t: N) { self.edges.push(t); } }` + `b.add(d); a.add(b);` double-frees. B-2026-07-28-3 correctly made the copy-support analysis DECLINE for a self-referential struct (the per-element copy is unrolled at emission and has no finite form), but the decline falls back to CALLER-RETAINS, which hands the callee an ALIAS. That is safe only while the callee reads it; `self.edges.push(t)` — the entire point of an adjacency list — stores the alias into an owning container, so the container and the caller's binding both free it. The decline therefore swapped a compile-time stack overflow for a runtime double-free. Fixed by restoring language-level semantics for exactly the shape that cannot be copied: a bare `T` param is owned, so the argument is MOVED and the caller drops its cleanup. Note for anyone touching this: the by-value arg loop exists in FOUR places and cross_graph needs the impl-method one specifically — hooking only `call_dispatch` looks correct and changes nothing. DOUBLY_LINKED ROOT-CAUSED (not yet fixed), and it is an INTERPRETER bug, not codegen — codegen handles a single middle removal correctly (`1 3 4` / `4 3 1`). The interpreter hangs before ANY output, so it is not the removals: bisected to TWO `push_back`s followed by the forward walk. A bounded walk shows `node1.next` pointing at node1 ITSELF. Minimal repro, and the back edge is the trigger — with only `a.next = Some(b)` BOTH backends are correct; adding `b.prev = Some(a)` makes the interpreter self-cycle: `shared struct Node { mut val: i64, mut prev: Option[Node], mut next: Option[Node] }` / `fn link(a: Node, b: Node) { a.next = Some(b); b.prev = Some(a); }` / a `Holder` whose `push` does `match self.tail { Some(old) => { link(old, node); … } }`. Calling `link` on two PLAIN LOCALS is correct on both backends, so the trigger is specifically an `Option[shared]` field of a `mut ref self` bound by `match` and passed as an owned argument alongside a fresh node — the two arguments end up aliasing inside the callee. The codegen leg (an uninitialized value printed after the three splices) is still unattributed. STILL OPEN under this entry: doubly_linked (both legs) and undo_redo's heap corruption at exit (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`), which survived the B-2026-07-28-6 wrong-answer fix and is a separate defect. parent_tree, cross_graph, undo_redo (output) and interp are now correct on both backends and gated. PROGRESS 2026-07-28 (7e1729f): the `doubly_linked` INTERPRETER leg is FIXED and promoted to `Expect::Matches` in tests/tangle_corpus.rs. Root cause turned out not to be an ownership defect at all and not to be specific to this corpus — it is B-2026-07-28-7, a general match-arm miscompile that had nothing to do with shared structs. Narrowing it collapsed a 40-line linked-list program to four lines of plain `Option[i64]`. The interpreter is now the AUTHORITATIVE ORACLE for the remaining codegen leg: it prints exactly the README's `1 2 3 4` / `4 3 2 1` / `3` / `3`. STILL OPEN under this entry: (a) `doubly_linked` under CODEGEN prints the two walks correctly and then an UNINITIALIZED value where `3` belongs — the last surviving node is read after the three splices dropped its last counted reference, so the RC accounting across the neighbour relink (`p.next = n.next` / `nx.prev = n.prev`, each a store of an `Option[shared]` field read out of a third node) is off by a retain. (b) `undo_redo` prints correct output on both backends but still corrupts the heap at exit (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`); confirmed separate from B-2026-07-28-6, which fixed only its wrong answer. PROGRESS 2026-07-28 (fa8ae31): `doubly_linked` is now FULLY FIXED — both legs match the README and both are `Expect::Matches` in tests/tangle_corpus.rs. The codegen leg was B-2026-07-28-8, a plain-struct `Option[shared]` field store that dropped the old value before retaining the new one; valgrind goes from 22 invalid reads and 29 frees against 27 allocs, to 27/27 with zero errors and zero bytes at exit. 4 of the 5 corpus programs now pass on both backends. REMAINING under this entry, and it is now the ONLY thing left here: `undo_redo` still reports 2 invalid reads (4 errors, 2 contexts) under valgrind. Its `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected` ABORT is gone as a side effect of B-2026-07-28-8 — consistent with the tcache damage having been that fix's double free — but a use-after-free READ survives, so this is a distinct defect and not merely a residue. Output is correct on both backends and 9 allocs / 9 frees balance, so only a sanitizer sees it; a plain run and the corpus oracle both pass. SEPARATE OBSERVATION, NOT PART OF THIS ENTRY: `parent_tree` leaks 256 bytes in 6 blocks at exit (13 allocs, 7 frees) with no valgrind errors and correct output. It cannot be B-2026-07-28-8 fallout — parent_tree has no plain struct with an `Option[shared]` field, so it never reaches the changed path; its only field store is `child.parent = Some(parent)` on a `shared struct`, which routes through the already-correct shared destination. Needs its own investigation (cycle-vs-defect). CLOSED 2026-07-28 (e2dfc58): the last leg was undo_redo's heap corruption, which turned out to be B-2026-07-28-9 — a moved-out struct's `shared` handle field was never nulled, so the source's drop rc-dec'd a second time for one owned reference. undo_redo now runs valgrind-clean at 9 allocs / 9 frees, 0 bytes at exit, 0 errors. WHAT THIS ENTRY ACTUALLY BOUGHT, since it is worth recording: the entry began as 'three of five corpus programs are silently wrong and nothing tests them'. Wiring the README as an oracle turned each wrong answer into a separate, narrowable bug, and two of the five root causes were NOT ownership defects at all — one was a general match-arm miscompile in the interpreter that broke every linked-structure walk in the language, and it was only reachable because the corpus happened to contain the shape. The dogfood corpus found a compiler bug far outside its own subject area, which is the argument for keeping such corpora gated rather than merely present.

LEDGER CORRECTION (2026-07-29): the `fix` field read `e2dfc58`, which is not a commit on main — a pre-rebase SHA recorded before the branch was replayed onto main, a hazard of this repo's concurrent-session workflow. The actual fix is edde4a7, whose commit message names this bug. Corrected so the pointer resolves.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara): `Option[<shared enum>]` has no kind of its own — `kind_of_ty` special-cases only `Option[String]` and collapses every other `Option[T]` to `Option[i64]`, so an `Option[Expr]` field stores the RC handle as a raw i64 payload, is judged POD, and is never released. Emits invalid IR today; would be a silent leak once that IR is fixed. Blocks ast.kara together with B-2026-07-27-6.
fix: 4afbc56
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while completing B-2026-07-27-6's Vec slice (Slice 67), by feeding ast.kara to the port and isolating what it stopped on. MECHANISM: `kind_of_ty` maps `Option[T]` by inspecting the generic — `gk == 2` (String) yields the synthetic kind 1001, and EVERY other T falls through to 1000 (`Option[i64]`). So `Option[Expr]`, where Expr is a `shared enum`, is typed as `Option[i64]`: the payload slot holds the handle as an integer, `en_has_heap(0)` is false so the field reads as POD, and no release is ever emitted for it. TODAY IT FAILS LOUDLY, WHICH IS LUCK RATHER THAN DESIGN: constructing such a field emits `insertvalue { i64, { i64, i64 } } %t5, { i64, i64 } 0, 1`, which LLVM rejects with 'integer constant must have integer type'. Anyone who fixes only that malformed constant converts a hard failure into a SILENT SUBTREE LEAK — so the two must be fixed together, and the kind is the real fix. SCOPE: give `Option[<shared>]` its own kind whose payload slot is a `ptr`; construction of `Some(h)` retains, `None` stores null; the match/projection path loads the handle; and the enum counts as heap-owning so `sh_struct_release_text` / `emit_free_struct_val` emit a tag-conditional `@sh_release_<ei>`. `Option[String]` (kind 1001) is the sibling case: it is a heap-bearing BY-VALUE enum, correctly REFUSED by `sh_struct_ok` today, and needs the tag-conditional free that the text-returning release path cannot currently emit. ast.kara needs both — 36 Option-typed fields, e.g. `BreakExpr.value: Option[Expr]` and `LoopExpr.label: Option[String]`. PROGRESS 2026-07-28 (c150b49): REPRESENTATION SETTLED, construct/layout/release DONE, match still missing and now REFUSED LOUDLY. THE SCOPE ABOVE WAS WRONG ON THE EXPENSIVE POINT, and correcting it is most of the value here: this does NOT need a kind of its own. A new kind band would have meant auditing the 167 sites that key off the 1000..2000 range. `Option[<shared enum>]` is the NICHE representation — a nullable handle, bit-identical to the bare handle with null standing for `None` — so it simply REUSES the inner enum's kind. `kind_of_ty` is a five-line change. Everything downstream was then already correct, and each was CHECKED rather than assumed: `ty_text` renders `ptr`; `en_stride` sizes it 8; it classifies as heap-owning so a release is emitted; `@sh_release_<ei>` already opens with `%isnull = icmp eq ptr %p, null`, so a `None` releases nothing with no special case; and bare `None` already emits `zeroinitializer`, which is null at pointer type. It is also exactly what the seed emits. The malformed `insertvalue` is gone and the field now lowers as `{ i64, ptr }`. WHAT REMAINS is ONE thing: `match` over such a value. It needs a null test rather than a tag load, for two independent reasons — the tag lives behind the handle, so reading it through a `None` dereferences null; and `None` is not a variant of the inner enum, so it falls through to `bind_whole` and becomes a CATCH-ALL that silently wins every arm. The second is why this could not simply be left: it would convert today's loud LLVM-parse failure into a silent wrong answer. `emit_match` therefore REFUSES loudly on it, naming this bug. SUGGESTED SHAPE FOR THE REMAINING SLICE, which avoids a parallel lowering entirely: synthesize the tag instead of loading it — `%t = zext i1 (icmp ne ptr %s, null) to i64` — then map `None` to tag 0 and `Some` to tag 1, and bind `Some`'s payload to the scrutinee pointer itself at kind `1000+ei` instead of GEP'ing into the node. That reuses the whole existing arm machinery (guards, typed result slot, binding slots) and should be well under 100 lines. Detection is by arm name: a `None`/`Some` pattern whose `en_variant_tag(ei, name)` is < 0 — which is exactly the condition the refusal already computes. VERIFIED so far: the 183-program corpus still matches the seed, plus a new entry pinning construct-and-drop; that program is valgrind-clean at 0 bytes at exit and survives 25 consecutive runs. FIXED 2026-07-28 (4afbc56) — match leg complete. TWO FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING. First, the tag must be emitted LAZILY, decided by the first arm that names a variant, not up front. Deciding up front requires pre-scanning the arms, and `arms.clone()` on a `Vec[MatchArm]` CORRUPTS THE HEAP in the seed-compiled emitter — the elements carry `shared enum` handles that the clone does not retain. That is split out as B-2026-07-28-11 with a ten-line repro; it is the CLONE-path twin of B-2026-07-28-9's move path. Laziness also fixes a second hazard independently: an all-catch-all match tests no tag, and eagerly loading one dereferences a handle that is null for a `None`. Second, the ownership checker treats a shared-enum handle moved into a struct field as a real move and rejects a later use of the source, so `Some(h)` always CONSUMES `h`. That is why passing the handle through with no retain is correct rather than merely lucky — and why the corpus needed the `ref`-walked chain, whose handles stay live, to test the retain accounting at all.
resolution: Fixed across two commits. (1) `kind_of_ty` maps `Option[<shared enum>]` to the INNER enum's kind, because the niche makes them one representation — a nullable handle, null being `None`. No new kind band was needed, which is what kept the change small: 167 sites key off the 1000..2000 range and a band of its own would have meant auditing all of them. `ty_text`, `en_stride`, the heap-owning classification and `@sh_release_<ei>`'s null guard were already correct for it. (2) 4afbc56: `emit_match` lowers a match over one as a NULL TEST — the discriminant is synthesized as `zext i1 (icmp ne ptr %s, null)` so the existing arm machinery (guards, typed result slot, binding slots, or-patterns) runs unchanged over it, `Some`'s payload binds the scrutinee handle itself, and `Some(x)` construction passes the handle through instead of wrapping it in the `Option[i64]` layout. `opt_mode` is decided from the first arm that names a variant and the tag is emitted lazily at that point. VERIFIED: 186-program differential corpus matches the seed, including three new entries — construct-and-drop, an owned recursive walk, and a three-deep chain walked twice through `ref` (the load-bearing one: every handle in the first two is a move, so their refcounts could balance without any retain being correct). Each is valgrind-clean at 0 bytes in use at exit and survives 25 consecutive runs.

title: Assigning through a `shared struct` field of a plain struct (`h.cell.value = v`) writes into the FIELD SLOT instead of through the RC handle, so the mutation is invisible to every other holder of that cell. Binding the field out first (`let a = h.cell; a.value = v;`) is correct, which localizes it to the nested field-path ASSIGN lowering. This is the root cause of undo_redo's wrong answer in B-2026-07-28-4.
fix: 85fc58c
detail: SOURCE NOTE: narrowed from B-2026-07-28-4's `examples/tangle/src/undo_redo.kara`, which prints `30 / 30 / 30 / 30` under codegen where the README documents `30 / 20 / 10 / 20`. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DIAGNOSIS, and it rules out the obvious hypothesis. A deep copy of the handle would break reads and writes alike; here only WRITES break. In the 6-line repro, writing through `h.cell` does not reach `c` (codegen prints 10, interp 99), but writing through `c` IS visible via `h.cell` (both print 7). So the field holds the CORRECT pointer and the read path dereferences it properly — it is the assign path that does not, storing into the Holder's own field slot rather than through the handle. CONFIRMED BY DISCRIMINATOR: `let a = h.cell; a.value = 99;` — the same write with the field bound out to a local first — is CORRECT on both backends (99). Binding forces a load of the handle; the direct nested path `h.cell.value = 99` does not emit that load. That narrows the fix to the nested field-path assign lowering: when an intermediate segment's declared type is a `shared struct`, the path must LOAD the handle at that segment and continue projecting from the loaded pointer, instead of GEP-ing onward as if the field were inline. SEVERITY: the optimizer proves the write cannot alias and constant-folds the later read — the disassembly of the repro bakes in `mov $0xa,%ecx` (the pre-write value 10) — so this is a silent wrong answer, not a crash. It hits exactly the pattern `shared struct` exists for: a handle stored in a record and mutated through that record (Rust's `Rc<RefCell<T>>` in a struct field). SCOPE NOTE: B-2026-07-28-4 also reports undo_redo CORRUPTING THE HEAP (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`) at exit. That is NOT established to be the same defect — writing to the wrong slot would scribble over `Holder`'s own field, which could plausibly explain it, but that is a hypothesis, not a measurement. Re-check the corruption after this fix rather than assuming it goes away. The other two tangle failures are separate: `cross_graph` under codegen STACK-OVERFLOWS (measured 2026-07-28 after cb38efe; B-2026-07-28-4 recorded it as empty output + exit 1, so re-measure), and `doubly_linked` prints an uninitialized value under codegen AND hangs under the INTERPRETER, the only interpreter-side failure in the corpus.
resolution: FIXED. The mechanism was a GUARD, not the GEP, and that is the part worth remembering: `compile_field_store`'s nested branch resolved the parent's layout via `struct_types`, where a `shared struct` is NEVER registered (it lives in `shared_types`). A shared parent therefore failed the `if let` and fell straight through to the function's no-op tail — the emitted IR loaded the handle and then simply did not write. Confirmed by dumping the IR: `%nested.store.chain.p = getelementptr { ptr }, ptr %h, i32 0, i32 0` followed by `%nested.store.shared.h = load ptr, ...` and then NOTHING before the next statement. This is the same 'fell through to the no-op tail and was silently dropped' defect the two branches immediately above it were each written to fix, for the one receiver shape neither covered. TWO HALVES, because fixing the guard alone is not enough: (1) `nested_store_place_ptr` now dereferences a shared-typed field to the heap node, done INSIDE the place walk rather than at the call site, so `a.b.c.value` works when the shared hop is at any depth (a call-site-only fix passes the depth-2 test and silently fails depth 3 — that case is in the test); (2) the caller resolves its layout from `shared_types` first and routes through `shared_gep_layout`, so the refcount-header shift — one word headed, TWO for a weak-targeted type, zero headerless — stays expressed in exactly one place instead of being re-derived here. DIAGNOSTIC NOTE for the next person in this area: the ASYMMETRY is what identifies this class. Reads through the field were always correct, so any test that only reads passes either way; the regression test asserts both directions deliberately. VERIFIED: 4 new assertions (write-through-holder, index-rooted parent `v[0].cell.value`, depth-3 `o.inner.cell.value`, and a plain non-shared nested struct as the fallback control), codegen 2596, memory_sanitizer 855, interpreter 1313, typechecker 2091, par_codegen 200, cli 537, shared_ownership_matrix, drop_differential, selfhost_codegen all green; both clippy gates and fmt clean. `examples/tangle/src/undo_redo.kara` now prints the `30 / 20 / 10 / 20` its README documents. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated because this entry raised it as a hypothesis and the measurement now settles it: undo_redo STILL corrupts the heap at exit (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`). The wrong-answer half and the memory-safety half are SEPARATE defects — writing to the wrong slot was the plausible common cause and it turns out not to be. B-2026-07-28-4 keeps the corruption, plus cross_graph's codegen stack overflow and doubly_linked's interpreter hang / uninitialized read.

title: INTERPRETER: an assignment to the scrutinee inside a match arm is SILENTLY REVERTED — `match cur { Some(n) => { cur = n.next } }` leaves `cur` at its pre-match value, so every linked-structure walk and most state machines loop forever. Regression from B-2026-07-23-12's payload write-through, which stored the reconstructed pre-body scrutinee back unconditionally.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced as `examples/tangle/src/doubly_linked.kara` hanging under the interpreter (tracked as a leg of B-2026-07-28-4, where it was mis-framed as an ownership/aliasing defect of `Option[shared]` links). Narrowing killed that framing entirely: the shared structs, the `mut ref self` receiver, the two-argument `link` call and the loop are all incidental. The bug reproduces in four lines of plain `Option[i64]` with no loop at all. MECHANISM: B-2026-07-23-12 (low, run-vs-build) taught `eval_match` to write a match payload's in-arm mutation back to the scrutinee place, because the interpreter binds payloads BY VALUE while codegen binds by pointer. It did so UNCONDITIONALLY: after the arm body ran, it rebuilt the ORIGINAL scrutinee value with the current binding values patched in and stored that back to the place. When the body had ALSO assigned to the scrutinee place itself, that store overwrote the assignment with the pre-body value — silently, with no diagnostic. `cur` therefore never advanced, and the canonical walk `loop { match cur { None => break, Some(n) => { ..; cur = n.next } } }` became an infinite loop. Reads of `cur` inside the SAME arm saw the assignment, so the value looked correct right up until the arm exited — which is why the symptom presented as a self-referential node (`node1.next == node1`) rather than as a lost write. WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE FOR FIVE DAYS: codegen is correct here, so only the interpreter leg diverged; the one corpus program that exercises the shape had no oracle wired to any test (the gap B-2026-07-28-4 exists to close), and the interpreter suite's own while-let / match coverage never assigned to a scrutinee inside its own arm. FIX: `Env` gains a small watch stack (`push_watch` / `pop_watch`); `Env::set` flips the flag of every active watch naming the slot it writes, including the redirected SharedCell / MapSlotRef / VecSlotRef forms, since each still replaces what the name denotes. `eval_match` watches the scrutinee's slot across the arm body and skips the write-through when the body replaced it. A STACK rather than a single slot because matches nest — an assignment made inside an inner match must still be seen by the outer one, or the inner match hides the write and the outer write-through reverts it anyway. WHY DYNAMIC RATHER THAN A STATIC AST SCAN: a syntactic 'does this arm assign to the scrutinee' walk would have to enumerate every ExprKind and would silently go wrong the day a variant is added, and it could only over-approximate a CONDITIONAL assignment — skipping the write-through even on the branch that does not fire, which would regress B-2026-07-23-12. The watch observes what actually happened, so both bugs are fixed exactly, and it also catches writes the scan could not see at all: a `mut ref` param CICO write-back, a method-call receiver write-back, or `cur.f = x` on a value-type struct, each of which replaces the slot through `Env::set`. SEMANTICS, and it matches codegen rather than merely avoiding the hang: under codegen the payload binding is a POINTER into the old storage, so replacing the place leaves later mutations of the binding invisible to the place — it does not resurrect the old value. Skipping the write-through is that behaviour. VERIFIED: 5 new interpreter tests (4 of which were confirmed RED with the fix disabled, the 5th is the over-fire guard and is green either way); interpreter 1318 pass; codegen E2E 2597 pass; drop_differential, shared_ownership_matrix, rc_fallback, closures, book_snippets green; tangle_corpus green with `doubly_linked`'s interp leg promoted from `KnownBroken` to `Matches`. The three B-2026-07-23-12 write-through tests still pass, and a new test pins the interaction directly: an arm that mutates a bound `Vec` payload AND assigns some OTHER variable still writes through.
resolution: Fixed in 7e1729f: scoped write-watch on the scrutinee slot (`Env::push_watch`/`pop_watch`, hooked in `Env::set`), consumed by `eval_match` to skip B-2026-07-23-12's payload write-through when the arm body reassigned the place.

title: CODEGEN: storing into a PLAIN (value-type) struct's `Option[shared T]` field drops the old value BEFORE retaining the new one, so an aliasing RHS (`h.head = n.next`) is freed by that very drop — use-after-free on the next read, double free at scope exit. The shared-struct destinations already retained first; the plain-struct fall-through never did.
fix: fa8ae31
detail: SOURCE NOTE: the codegen leg of `examples/tangle/src/doubly_linked.kara` under B-2026-07-28-4 — it printed the two walks correctly and then an uninitialized value where the README documents `3`. Reachable only after B-2026-07-28-7 fixed the interpreter leg, which is what gave this one an oracle to diff against. MECHANISM: `compile_field_store` special-cases every SHARED destination (`node.next = ..`, `v[i].next = ..`) and routes it to `emit_option_shared_field_store`, which loads the old slot, retains the new inner, stores, and only THEN releases the old. A PLAIN struct holding the list head (`struct DList { mut head: Option[Node] }`) has no such case and fell through to the generic path: `drop_old_plain_struct_field` (B-2026-07-15-25) followed by a raw store. That order is correct for a FRESH rhs and wrong for an ALIASING one. In `self.head = n.next` the RHS is a field read that yields the handle un-retained; dropping the old head takes its refcount to zero, which runs its recursive drop, which releases its own `next` — the very node the RHS just loaded — and the store then commits a dangling pointer. IR confirms it exactly: `%next.niche.ptr = load ptr, ptr %sh_next` with no `rc_inc` between it and `call void @karac_drop_Option_Node(ptr %old_head_ptr34)`. SYMPTOMS AND WHY THEY LOOKED UNRELATED: an ordinary run printed garbage (a stale slot), while the SAME binary under valgrind printed the correct `3` — freed memory keeps its contents, so the debugger disagreed with the program. Under the JIT the same shape aborted with `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`, which is the double free at scope exit rather than the read. FIX: `try_plain_struct_option_shared_field_store` routes both plain-struct branches — the owned local and the `mut ref` struct param — through `emit_option_shared_field_store`, returning before `drop_old_plain_struct_field`, whose job the retain-aware store subsumes. Retain-then-release is also what makes `h.head = h.head` safe. Only the non-niche variant is reachable: niche-opt is recorded on `shared_types` (`niche_field_inner_heap_type` looks the OUTER type up there) and a plain struct is never in that map, so its `Option[shared]` field always uses the full four-word `Option` layout. VERIFIED: doubly_linked matches its README on both backends and is valgrind-clean at 27 allocs / 27 frees, 0 bytes at exit (was 22 invalid reads, 29 frees against 27 allocs); codegen E2E 2598, memory_sanitizer 856, par_codegen 200, interpreter 1318, selfhost_codegen, tangle_corpus, drop_differential, shared_ownership_matrix, rc_fallback all green. NOTE the LSan caveat in CLAUDE.md: this was verified on Linux valgrind + the x86 memory_sanitizer suite; the arm64 leg has not been run here.
resolution: Fixed in fa8ae31: `try_plain_struct_option_shared_field_store` in src/codegen/expr_ops.rs routes a plain struct's `Option[shared]` field store through `emit_option_shared_field_store` (retain new / store / release old), hooked into both the owned-local and `mut ref`-param branches of `compile_field_store` ahead of `drop_old_plain_struct_field`.

title: CODEGEN: a whole-struct MOVE does not null a `shared struct` / `shared enum` HANDLE field, so the moved-out source's drop rc-dec's a second time for one owned reference — the second dec reads the refcount word of a block the first already freed. Alloc/free counts still balance, so only a sanitizer sees it.
fix: fab2ba3
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the last open leg of B-2026-07-28-4 — `examples/tangle/src/undo_redo.kara` printed correct output on both backends but reported 2 invalid reads under valgrind, and before B-2026-07-28-8 aborted outright with `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`. MECHANISM: `zero_struct_move_caps_mono` neutralizes every heap-bearing field of a moved-out struct so the source's drop is a no-op — `cap`/`len` for Vec/String (B-2026-07-10-1), the tag for Option (B-2026-07-03-28), the payload area for Result (B-2026-07-21-15), the handle for Map/Set (B-2026-07-15-23). A SHARED HANDLE field had no arm: a shared enum does have an `enum_layouts` entry but the loop skips it for `is_shared`, and a shared struct is explicitly excluded from the nested-struct recursion (`struct_types.contains_key(fname) && !shared_types.contains_key(fname)`), so both fell through to nothing. The source stayed live; its `__karac_vec_elem_full_drop_<S>` rc-dec'd the handle, and the destination's drop rc-dec'd it again. WHY IT HID: the two decs are for ONE owned reference, so the first takes the count to zero and frees; the second then reads the refcount word of freed memory. That read is the defect. It rarely yields 1, so the second `free` does not fire and ALLOC/FREE COUNTS BALANCE — the program prints the right answer, leaks nothing, and looks healthy to everything except a sanitizer. Under the JIT the same corruption surfaced as an unrelated-looking `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`. FIX: one arm nulling the source handle, placed before the enum/struct arms it would otherwise fall past. The synthesized drop already null-guards the field (`nstr.sh.isnull`), so this is a pure codegen null-store exactly parallel to the Map/Set arm — no runtime change. VERIFIED: undo_redo valgrind-clean at 9 allocs / 9 frees, 0 bytes at exit, 0 errors; 3 new ASAN cases, with BOTH arms confirmed load-bearing by disabling the fix and re-measuring (each probe reports an invalid read without it); memory_sanitizer 859, codegen E2E 2598, par_codegen 200, interpreter 1318, selfhost_codegen, tangle_corpus, drop_differential, shared_ownership_matrix, rc_fallback all green. CAVEAT: x86-64 Linux only — the arm64 LSan leg (CLAUDE.md) has not been run here.

LEDGER CORRECTION (2026-07-29): the `fix` field read `e2dfc58`, which is not a commit on main — a pre-rebase SHA recorded before the branch was replayed onto main, a hazard of this repo's concurrent-session workflow. The actual fix is fab2ba3, whose commit message names this bug. Corrected so the pointer resolves.
resolution: Fixed in e2dfc58: `zero_struct_move_caps_mono` (src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs) gains a `shared_types.contains_key(fname)` arm that null-stores the handle, ordered before the `enum_layouts` / `struct_types` arms that previously swallowed both the shared-enum and shared-struct cases.

title: INTERP: `Column.from_arrow_ipc` (and the Column constructors generally) ignore the binding's declared element type, so `let c: Column[i64] = Column.from_arrow_ipc(<Utf8 stream>)` yields a Column holding Strings under `karac run`, while `karac build` traps. Run-vs-build divergence on a genuinely ill-typed program.
fix: b72fab5
detail: Surfaced while landing the Arrow IPC READ direction under AOT (`karac_arrow_column_from_ipc`). Codegen knows the declared `T` (it sizes the data buffer from it), so the runtime is told the target `(elem_size, kind)` and REJECTS a stream whose element type does not convert — String and bool convert only to themselves, since rendering a number as text or a string as 0 would turn a type error into corrupt data. The interpreter has no such check: `eval_column_new` (src/interpreter/method_call_column.rs) builds `Value::Column` straight from whatever `column_from_ipc` decoded, with no access to the `let` annotation. Repro: `let s: Column[String] = Column.from_vec(["a", "b"]); let bad: Column[i64] = Column.from_arrow_ipc(s.to_arrow_ipc()); println(bad.len());` — `karac run --interp` prints 2, `karac build` panics with the actionable from_arrow_ipc message. NOTE the looseness is NOT specific to Arrow: `Column.from_vec` has the same shape (it clones the source array without consulting the annotation), so a fix wants an expected-element-type channel into `eval_column_new` rather than a one-off guard in the arrow arm. The COMPILED behaviour is the correct one — `Column[i64]` must hold i64 — so this is an interpreter-side under-check, not a codegen over-reach. Only reachable on a program that is already ill-typed at the value level; a well-typed round-trip agrees on both backends (asserted by `test_e2e_from_arrow_ipc_round_trips`, 10 cases). TENSOR FACE (same root cause, found landing the tensor leg): `Tensor.from_arrow_ipc` builds from the stream's own dims without consulting the annotation, so `let bad: Tensor[i64, [3, 2]] = Tensor.from_arrow_ipc(<a [2,3] stream>)` yields a [2,3] tensor under `karac run` while `karac build` traps on the shape reconciliation. Same fix shape: the interpreter's constructors need an expected-type/shape channel, not per-constructor guards.
resolution: Fixed in b72fab5 with the expected-type CHANNEL this entry asked for, not per-constructor guards: `Interpreter::pending_let_ty` carries the whole `let` annotation into the RHS, saved/restored exactly like the existing `pending_tensor_fill` (the same idea for `Tensor.zeros`'s fill type) so nested `let`s in a block-expr RHS nest correctly. `column_ann_mismatch` mirrors the runtime's `write_slot` rule exactly — a numeric `T` takes any numeric value, `String` and `bool` take only themselves — and `tensor_ann_shape_mismatch` compares the stream's dims against a fully-static annotated shape. BOTH CHECKS DECLINE WHERE THEY CANNOT BE CERTAIN (no annotation, a non-Column/Tensor one, an unrecognized element type, or a shape carrying a `?` / param / splice). Rejecting a program the compiled backend accepts would be a worse divergence than the one being fixed. OVER-FIRE CAUGHT BY THE SUITE, worth recording: the first version checked every slot, including NULLs. The runtime's `write_slot` runs only for `Some(slot)`, so a null in a `Column[i64]` is not a type error — checking them turned four existing round-trip tests red. Nulls are skipped now. VERIFIED on both backends: the ill-typed Column and Tensor programs are each rejected by both (interpreter runtime error, AOT panic — the arrow archive was built to run the compiled leg), and the well-typed round-trips print identically. Four new interpreter tests: one rejection and one acceptance per face, the acceptances covering numeric / String / float element classes so the guard cannot silently start over-firing. interpreter 1322, codegen E2E 2601, memory_sanitizer 860, json, typechecker 2091 green.

title: CODEGEN: `Vec[<struct carrying a shared handle>].clone()` does not retain the cloned elements' handles, so the clone's drop and the original's drop both release — use-after-free on the second, and heap corruption (`malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`) in a larger program. The clone-path twin of B-2026-07-28-9.
fix: a4711ca
detail: SOURCE NOTE: hit while implementing B-2026-07-28-5's match leg. The natural way to decide whether a match is over an `Option[<shared enum>]` is to pre-scan its arms, which needs `arms.clone()` on a `Vec[MatchArm]` — and `MatchArm` carries a `Pattern` handle, an `Option[Expr]` and an `Expr` handle. The seed-compiled emitter then aborted with `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected` on the selfhost corpus. That is what forced the lazy, no-clone design there; the underlying defect is this entry. MECHANISM: a `Vec[T].clone()` where `T` is a plain struct with a `shared struct` / `shared enum` HANDLE field copies the element bytes without an rc-inc on the handle, so the cloned element aliases the same node with no counted reference. Both vectors' element drops then release it: the first takes the count to zero and frees, the second reads the refcount word of freed memory. Exactly the accounting error B-2026-07-28-9 fixed for the MOVE path (`zero_struct_move_caps` had no shared-handle arm); this is the same gap on the CLONE path, where the fix is the mirror image — the move path had to stop releasing, the clone path has to start retaining. WHY IT LOOKS BENIGN: alloc/free counts BALANCE (the garbage the second release reads is rarely 1, so no second `free` fires), the program prints the right answer, and only a sanitizer sees it — until a bigger program corrupts the allocator outright, which is how it surfaced. SCOPE: the element clone needs an rc-inc per shared-handle field, reached through the same per-type walk `zero_struct_move_caps_mono` uses to find them. Check the sibling shapes at the same time: a bare `<plain struct with a shared field>.clone()`, a `Vec[<shared handle>].clone()` (element IS the handle), and a Map/Set value of either.
resolution: Fixed in a4711ca: `emit_owning_clone_fn_for_type_expr` (src/codegen/clone_drop.rs) emits `karac_cloneown_<t>` for a shared handle — copy the pointer and rc-inc it, null-guarded — and the six container-clone bodies (Vec element, Map key and value, tuple element, struct field, enum payload) dispatch through it. THE SCOPING IS THE CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT, and getting it wrong first is worth recording: the initial attempt put the retain in the shared `emit_clone_fn_for_type_expr` dispatcher, which has twenty-odd OTHER callers that are move/transfer contexts rather than duplications and already manage RC themselves. `nodes[0].neighbors.push(nodes[1])` emits its own retain (B-2026-07-21-13), so the dispatcher-level change double-counted there and turned two existing ASAN tests RED under LeakSanitizer — the fix's own over-fire, caught by the suite it was meant to satisfy. The two clone kinds now emit distinct symbols under distinct cache keys so they coexist. VERIFIED: four shapes, each confirmed RED with the fix disabled and clean with it — a Vec of a struct carrying a handle, a Vec whose element IS the handle, a Map value carrying one, and a `shared struct` handle rather than a `shared enum` one. A bare `<plain struct>.clone()` turned out not to be a defect at all: the typechecker has no such method. memory_sanitizer 860, codegen E2E 2600, par_codegen 200, interpreter 1318, selfhost_codegen, tangle_corpus, drop_differential, shared_ownership_matrix, rc_fallback all green. CAVEAT: x86-64 Linux only; the arm64 LSan leg (CLAUDE.md) has not been run here.

title: CODEGEN: `println(<Vec expression>)` renders EMPTY (or a stray tab) when the operand is not an identifier — `println(vec![9i64, 8i64])`, `println(t.shape())`, `println(mk())` all print blank under `karac build` while the interpreter prints `[9, 8]`. Binding to a `let` first prints correctly on both.
detail: Found while eyeballing `karac build` vs `karac run --interp` output for the Arrow IPC tensor round-trip: `println(f"shape={t.shape()}")` rendered `shape=` under build and `shape=[2, 3]` under interp. NOT Arrow-specific and NOT tensor-specific — the minimal repro has no stdlib involvement at all: `fn main() { println(vec![9i64, 8i64]); }` prints a stray tab + space under `karac build`, while `let v: Vec[i64] = vec![9i64, 8i64]; println(v);` prints `[9, 8]` correctly. A free function returning a Vec (`println(mk())`) and a method returning one (`println(t.shape())`) both reproduce it too, so the discriminator is the OPERAND SHAPE — identifier vs. any other expression — not what produced the Vec. Confirmed pre-existing on a clean tree (stash + rebuild) at 4fe0f0b, so it predates the Arrow work. Chained use of the same temporary is fine (`println(c.to_arrow_ipc().len())` prints 456 on both), which points at the Vec-formatting path receiving the aggregate rather than a pointer to it, not at the Vec itself being wrong. Both directions of the Arrow IPC surface agree on VALUES under both backends (`test_e2e_from_arrow_ipc_round_trips` / `test_e2e_to_arrow_ipc_matches_interpreter_bytes`), so this is confined to printing a temporary Vec.
resolution: Added a span-addressed `display_vec_types` side-table (element `TypeExpr` per `Vec[T]`-typed expression), forwarded from `TypeCheckResult.expr_types` through `Program` to codegen — the exact sibling of `display_option_result_types` for Option/Result and `display_tuple_types` for tuples. `try_compile_vec_display` (src/codegen/synth_display.rs) keys off it, so an unbound Vec renders through the SAME `emit_vec_display_fn_te` the identifier path already used; wired into both sinks, `compile_print` and f-string interpolation. A materialized temporary is registered with `track_vec_var` rather than freed inline: routing it through the existing `FreeVecBuffer` drain drops per-element heaps, which an outer-buffer free does not (LSan caught exactly that — 16 bytes in 4 allocations across two two-element `Vec[String]` temporaries). Scope-timed cleanup was checked against the case that could have broken it: the temporary lives in one reused entry alloca, so a 64-iteration loop printing unbound Vecs would leak 63 buffers if the frame drained only at function exit — it drains per iteration, and the ASAN test pins that. Tests: `test_e2e_unbound_vec_prints_like_a_bound_one` (6 element/producer shapes, each asserted in BOTH bound and unbound form so the test cannot pass with both backends wrong the same way) and `asan_unbound_vec_display_no_leak`.

fix: c1eeed5
title: explicit `par {}` over 18 arms that all READ one shared graph crashes nondeterministically (~0.8%): silent exit 133 (SIGTRAP) and 139 (SIGSEGV), empty stderr, correct output whenever it does exit 0 — failure rate scales with worker count (0/200 at 1-2 workers, 2/200 at 18)
detail:
SURFACE NOTE: this is an EXPLICIT `par {}` block, not auto-parallelization; 'autopar' is used here as the parallel-execution surface. The layer is NOT yet isolated — the fault could be in codegen's lowering of concurrent reads of a shared structure or in the runtime's par machinery (`karac_par_run` is the only par symbol in the binary). Whoever picks this up should not assume either.

SHAPE: kara-katas leetcode/101-200/133-clone-graph/bench/clone_bfs_par.kara. A 19-way tuple destructuring `let (s1..s18) = par { let s1 = sum_clones(root, 28); ... }` where every one of the 18 arms reads the SAME `root` node graph (built once, sequentially, before the block). No arm mutates it. The workload clones the graph per call, so the shared read set is the original node/neighbour structure.

SYMPTOM: the process dies with NO output on stderr — no panic message, no contract-fault text, no backtrace. Exit codes observed are 133 (128+5, SIGTRAP) and 139 (128+11, SIGSEGV). The SIGSEGV is the important half: this is not a trap firing on a detected condition, it is memory unsafety. Whenever the process DOES exit 0 the sink is correct (0 wrong answers in 500 runs), so it is a crash-or-correct failure, never silent corruption.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS KATA: the failure is silent and intermittent at a rate low enough (~1%) to pass a casual run and low enough that a benchmark harness doing one run per kata would mostly not see it. It was found because a bench script happened to invoke the binary ~60 times.
repro:
Requires the kara-katas sibling repo.
  cd kara-katas/leetcode/101-200/133-clone-graph/bench
  karac build clone_bfs_par.kara && mv clone_bfs_par target/clone_bfs_par_kara
  fail=0; for i in $(seq 1 500); do ./target/clone_bfs_par_kara >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail=$((fail+1)); done; echo $fail/500
Expected: 0/500 and sink 500 every run. Actual on karac f80bb80b605f (7db7009e), M5 Pro 6P+12E, macOS 25.5.0: 4/500 non-zero exits (three 133, one 139), 0 wrong outputs.
A single run is NOT a repro — at ~0.8% you need a few hundred trials to see it reliably.
investigation:
WORKER-COUNT DIFFERENTIAL (200 trials each, same binary):
  KARAC_PAR_WORKERS=1   0/200
  KARAC_PAR_WORKERS=2   0/200
  KARAC_PAR_WORKERS=18  2/200  (1.0%)
So the fault requires real concurrency and its rate rises with the number of workers — consistent with a data race on the shared `root` graph being read by all 18 arms at once, and inconsistent with a plain scheduler/dispatch bug (which would not care that the arms share a read set).

NOT ESTABLISHED AS A REGRESSION. This kata's par lane benched clean on 2026-06-15, but at a ~1% rate a single clean bench run is entirely consistent with 'already broken, got lucky' — it is roughly a coin-flip whether 60 runs show it. No bisect has been done and no claim is made about when it started.

The kata's SEQ lane (clone_bfs.kara) is unaffected and has never failed.
resolution: WITHDRAWN as a live defect 2026-07-28 — STALE-BINARY ARTIFACT, the same class as B-2026-07-21-19. The reported program DOES NOT COMPILE on current main. `karac build clone_bfs_par.kara` refuses it with `error[ownership]: shared struct 'Node' cannot be accessed from multiple concurrent tasks (binding 'root' reachable from two par-block branches)`, and that gate PREDATES the report: `src/ownership/concurrent_shared.rs` already carried the message on 2026-07-13, two weeks earlier. `bench/bench.sh` rebuilds only when the source or the INSTALLED `karac` is newer than the cached `target/clone_bfs_par_kara`, so a binary built before the gate survives any number of dev rebuilds — which is how a program the compiler rejects kept producing a runnable binary. THE CRASH ITSELF WAS REAL AND IS EXACTLY WHAT THE GATE PREVENTS, so the evidence corroborates rather than contradicts: `emit_rc_inc` is a plain load/add/store, and the atomic path (`emit_arc_inc`) fires only for a `par struct` / `par enum` or an Arc-promoted binding. Eighteen threads traversing one plain `shared struct` race on its refcount, and a lost increment frees the graph while other tasks still hold it. That accounts for every reported symptom — real concurrency required, rate scaling with worker count, a READ-ONLY share sufficing, and crash-or-correct rather than silent corruption. The entry's instinct not to assume a layer was right; the layer is the front end, and it was already doing its job. WHAT LANDED (c1eeed5): the gate was pinned by NOTHING, so a regression would silently make the crashing shape compilable again. Three tests now cover it — `par {}` branches (ownership), `TaskGroup.spawn` captures (the TYPECHECKER, as `E_NOT_CROSS_TASK` — a different phase, so gating one surface would have left the identical race reachable through the other), and an accept-case so the gate cannot start over-firing. FOR THE KATA, and this is a real ergonomic finding rather than a workaround: the diagnostic's advice (`replace 'Node' with the 'par' form`) does not directly apply. A `par struct`'s `mut` field must be `Atomic[T]` or `Mutex[T]`, and this graph is CYCLIC — neighbours are wired after construction — so `mut neighbors: Vec[Node]` cannot simply become immutable. Making the par lane legal means `Mutex[Vec[Node]]` (changing the cost model the benchmark measures) or rebuilding the graph per worker, which is what the rayon lane already does for the same reason (`Rc` is not `Send`). ALSO WORTH FIXING SEPARATELY: `bench.sh`'s cache key should include the compiler actually used, or the bench should run `karac check` before trusting a cached binary. Two ledger entries have now been spent on binaries the compiler would refuse.

fix: 46acf5b
title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara): `Option[<plain struct>]` has no representation — `kind_of_ty` collapses it to `Option$i`, whose payload slot is an i64, so constructing `Some(<struct>)` emits `insertvalue { i64, i64 } %t6, i64 %t5, 1` with `%t5` a struct. Fails at LLVM parse. The third member of the `Option[T]` family after B-2026-07-28-5 (shared enum) and the `Option[String]` leg of B-2026-07-27-6.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: B-2026-07-27-6 recorded this as its own LAST REMAINING SHAPE and characterized it as 'an AGGREGATE-slot enum (en_extra >= 0) which sh_byval_enum_ok still refuses'. Both halves are wrong, which is why it is being restated here rather than inherited. `kind_of_ty` maps `Option[T]` by inspecting the generic: String yields 1001, a `shared enum` yields the inner enum's kind (B-2026-07-28-5's niche), and EVERYTHING ELSE falls through to 1000 = `Option$i`. `Option$i` has variants None/Some(i64), no aggregate slot, and `en_has_heap` false — so a plain-struct payload is neither slotted nor refused, it is simply typed as an integer.

FAILURE MODE, and it is the good one: LOUD. Constructing the `Some` emits an `insertvalue` of a struct value into an i64 field and `llvm-as` rejects it outright. A `None`-only program emits VALID IR and runs correctly, because nothing is ever stored in the slot — so the shape is latent until the first `Some`.

SCOPE OF THE FIX: unlike `Option[<shared enum>]` there is NO niche to reuse — a plain struct has no null representation — so this needs a real synthetic enum per distinct `Option[<struct>]`, registered like `Option$i` / `Option$s` but carrying that struct in an aggregate slot. The slot machinery is no longer the obstacle (dd14643 made aggregate slots unbounded); the work is REGISTRATION. `kind_of_ty` is `ref self` and cannot register on demand, so a pre-pass must walk every type annotation in the program (struct fields, fn params and returns, `let` annotations) collecting `Option[<struct>]` instantiations before any kind is resolved — the same problem Pass A0 solved for names.

ast.kara has 7 such fields, all `Option[GenericParamsNode]`.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-07-28 (46acf5b). `collect_sigs` registers a synthetic `Option$<Struct>` enum per DECLARED struct, with the struct in an AGGREGATE slot. There is no niche to reuse here — a plain struct has no null representation, which is what separates this from `Option[<shared enum>]` (B-2026-07-28-5) — so it needs a real enum, and that only became expressible when dd14643 removed the two-aggregate-slot cap.

WHY EVERY STRUCT, not only the instantiations in use: finding those means pre-scanning every type annotation in the program INCLUDING inside fn bodies (`let x: Option[G]`), and a missed instantiation would be an emit-time refusal. One two-variant entry per struct is cheap, it turns the lookup into a name search instead of a discovery pass, and it costs nothing in the emitted IR because an enum nothing references is never rendered.

Both sides pick the same enum from the same fact — `kind_of_ty` from the annotation's generic, the `Some(x)` arm from the payload's KIND — which is how the existing Option$i / Option$s split already worked, so no new agreement mechanism was needed. `None` needed nothing: `zeroinitializer` is tag 0 in this layout as in the others.

RESULT BEYOND THE SHAPE: `ast_render` and `resolver` moved from invalid IR to IR `llvm-as` accepts. Seven of the nine self-host modules now emit valid IR (span, token, ast, lexer, typechecker, ast_render, resolver); `parser` and `codegen` remain, on unrelated gaps — parser on `'%t4440' i64 but expected '{ ptr, i64 }'`, codegen on `'%t3395' i1 but expected 'i64'`.

VERIFIED: the 191-program corpus matches the seed. The new entry covers a POD payload and a String-bearing one, both arms of each, construction inline and through a fn return, a struct FIELD of that type read and consumed, and the same inside a shared node; it is valgrind-clean at 0 errors and 0 bytes lost and survives 25 consecutive runs, and fails at LLVM parse on the parent commit.

COVERAGE GAP, and it is a SEED bug not a port one: no arm reads an `Option[<HEAP struct>]` out of a struct field and passes it to an owning parameter, because that DOUBLE-FREES IN THE SEED — found while writing this very test, filed as B-2026-07-28-16. A differential oracle cannot compare against a crashing reference, so that shape is deferred here until the seed is fixed.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara): no IMPORT resolution — a type named by an `import` hits `kind_of_ty`'s i64 fallback SILENTLY, so an imported struct lowers to a bare integer and the emitter produces well-formed IR for a program the seed REFUSES. This, not any payload shape, is what gates module-level self-hosting.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found by feeding each self-host module to the port after dd14643 lifted the aggregate-slot cap (B-2026-07-27-6). All six modules now EMIT — none reaches a refusal — but five produce IR `llvm-as` rejects, and narrowing the smallest of those (ast_render) landed here rather than on a payload bug.

MECHANISM: `emit_program` walks the items of ONE parsed module. `Import` items are ignored, so nothing an import names is ever registered in `st_names` / `en_names`, and `kind_of_ty` returns 0 — i64 — for a name it cannot find. Pass A0 (Slice 65) made that fallback unreachable by a FORWARD reference within a module; an IMPORTED name still reaches it, and silently.

WHY IT IS HIGH RATHER THAN A MISSING FEATURE: the outcome is not a refusal but a wrong lowering that type-checks at the IR level. In the emitted ast.kara, `@u_clone_span` has signature `(i64) -> i64` although `Span` is a four-field struct — an identity function over a truncated value, well-formed IR, no diagnostic. Where the mistyped value is then used structurally the IR happens to fail to parse (that is the only reason four of the five modules are caught at all); where it is merely passed through, it compiles and is simply wrong.

TWO-PART FIX, and the first part is small and independently worth doing: (a) REFUSE an unresolvable type name instead of calling it i64. `kind_of_ty` must first admit the scalar names it legitimately does not register (`i64`/`i32`/`u8`/… all currently reach the same `0` by design) and refuse only what is left, so this is not a one-line change and carries real regression risk against the 190-program corpus — but it converts this whole class from silent to loud. (b) Resolve imports: collect the imported modules' items into the same tables before Pass A0, which is the actual feature.

UNTIL (a) LANDS, treat single-module emitter output as UNTRUSTWORTHY for any module with imports — `llvm-as` accepting it is not evidence of correctness.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-07-28 (04964fa), in two halves that turned out to be very unevenly sized.

THE MISCOMPILE: `kind_of_ty` now lists the primitive type names explicitly (`primitive_kind_of_name`) and REFUSES anything that is neither a primitive nor a declared struct/enum, printing the name it could not resolve. The name is printed rather than interpolated into the panic because the seed only propagates a STRING-LITERAL panic message, and a refusal that cannot say WHICH name it failed on is barely better than the silent i64 it replaces. `f32` is deliberately absent from the primitive list: only `f64` has a kind, so an `f32` annotation would have become an integer — the same class of silent wrong lowering.

THE OTHER HALF NEEDS NO EMITTER CHANGE AT ALL, which is the finding worth keeping and is why the entry over-estimated the work. The entry called import resolution 'the actual feature'. It is not: the emitter consumes a flat `Vec[Item]`, so CONCATENATING a module with its transitive imports gives one program in which every name is declared — `import` lines are inert and duplicates are harmless. `scripts/selfhost-emit-module.sh` derives the closure from the `import` lines and emits; with it `@u_clone_span` gains its true `{i64,i64,i64,i64}` signature and four modules (ast, token, lexer, typechecker) move from invalid IR to IR `llvm-as` accepts. What remains unimplemented is per-module emission with imported functions `declare`d rather than defined, which nothing currently needs.

VERIFIED: the 190-program differential corpus is green with the refusal in place — no legitimate name in it trips the primitive list, which was the whole regression risk of tightening a fallback that scalars also reach. The minimal repro (a module the seed refuses with "'P' is not a struct") now refuses by name instead of emitting `define i64 @u_getx(i64)`.

NOTE for anyone reading the module table in the commit: span and token declare no functions, so their 'IR VALID' is module scaffold only. The load-bearing ones are lexer (43 fns -> 43 defines) and typechecker (41 -> 47, the extra being shared-enum release helpers).

title: SEED CODEGEN: an owned struct's `Option`/`Result` field passed BY VALUE to a parameter that owns it was not treated as a move — the callee freed the payload and the struct's scope-exit drop freed it again. Hits `Option[String]` and `Option[Vec]` as well as the `Option[<struct>]` this was filed on. Interpreter correct; JIT and AOT both abort.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while writing the corpus entry for B-2026-07-28-14 (the self-hosted emitter's `Option[<plain struct>]` support). The test program was written against the SEED as the oracle and the seed crashed on it — so this is a seed defect surfaced by port work, not a port defect.

NARROWED, and each negative below is a measured run rather than an assumption:
  * The payload must OWN HEAP. The identical program with a POD payload struct (`Option[G]`, G = { n: i64 }) runs correctly on all three backends.
  * The Option must be read out of a STRUCT FIELD. The same `Option[H]` held in a plain local and passed to the same function is fine.
  * The consumer must take it BY VALUE. Matching the field inline, without a call, is fine.
  * No `shared` type is involved — the first repro had one, and removing it did not change the outcome.

BACKENDS DISAGREE, which is the usual signature of an ownership-convention bug rather than a layout one: the interpreter prints the right answer; `karac run` (LLJIT) and `karac build` both abort with `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` (exit 134), and valgrind on the AOT binary reports `Invalid free() / delete / delete[] / realloc()`, 1 error from 1 context.

RELATIONSHIP TO B-2026-07-21-16 ('owned-struct Option field consume/move sites double-free'), which is the same sentence at a different layout: that fix evidently covers the Option layouts whose payload sits in the two-word tagged form, and not the AGGREGATE-slot form an `Option[<struct>]` uses. Worth checking whether the fix generalizes rather than adding a second special case.

IMPACT beyond the port: `Option[<struct>]` fields are ordinary user code, so this is reachable from any program, not only from self-host work.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-07-28 (6dc5854). The call site already had the right idea — B-2026-07-10-4 wired `suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move` there for exactly this move — but that helper matches an `Identifier` and returns immediately for anything else, so a `FieldAccess` argument was never treated as a move. `let o = nd.opt; consume(o)` was fine while `consume(nd.opt)` aborted, and B-2026-07-21-16's source-zeroing (built for the pattern, `let` and assign move sites) simply never reached the call-argument site. The fix adds that fourth leg.

THE ENTRY UNDERSTATED THE SCOPE, and correcting that matters more than the fix: it described an `Option[<struct that owns heap>]`, because that is where it surfaced (writing B-2026-07-28-14's corpus program against the seed as oracle). Measured afterwards, `Option[String]` and `Option[Vec[i64]]` fields abort identically. This was ordinary user code, not a corner of self-host work, and the severity was right for the wrong reason.

TWO CLASSES, NOT ONE — the first attempt conflated them and that is the reusable finding. Widening the shared `place_optres_field_move_info` in place fixed the call site and turned two previously-clean programs into LEAKS. The PATTERN leg only zeroes the source when the arm's BINDING takes over the payload's free, which holds for an inline `{ptr,len,cap}` payload and not for a struct/enum one: `match nd.hp { Some(x) => println(x.label) }` stranded 4 bytes under valgrind. A WHOLE-value move has no such question — the callee receives tag and payload together — so it got its own entry point, `place_optres_field_whole_move_info`, whose payload class mirrors `emit_struct_drop_synthesis`'s OptionInline classifier exactly. That mirroring is the invariant worth stating: the source zero must fire precisely when the struct drop would free the field, or it is a double-free (too narrow) or a leak (too wide).

STILL OPEN, split out as B-2026-07-28-17: the same call when the struct is a payload bound out of a `shared enum`. `field_chain_place_ptr` correctly bails on that root — zeroing a field inside an RC node would corrupt every other holder — so the fix there is a defensive COPY at the call site, a different mechanism. Confirmed narrow by control: the identical program over a NON-shared enum is clean.

VERIFIED: 2603 codegen E2E, 861 memory_sanitizer (gcc ASAN+LSan), the 191-program selfhost corpus and the non-llvm suite all green; clippy + fmt clean. Both new tests were checked to BITE (reverting just the two source files makes the ASAN test report `double-free`), and both cover the LEAK direction as well — an unconsumed field must stay owned and readable. The E2E test uses single-use holders because the ownership checker correctly rejects reading a field after it was moved; that is the language being sound, not a test limitation.

fix: 09ffe5a
title: SEED CODEGEN: passing an `Option[<heap>]` field of a struct bound out of a `shared enum` payload to an owning parameter double-frees — `match a { V(nd) => consume(nd.hp) }`. The owned-root form of this was fixed as B-2026-07-28-16; this root is an RC node, which needs a defensive COPY rather than a source zero.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the residue of B-2026-07-28-16, which fixed the same call for an owned struct local (and for a non-shared enum payload binding). Split out because the FIX is a different mechanism, not because it is a different symptom.

WHY THE -16 FIX DOES NOT EXTEND: that fix neutralizes the SOURCE — it zeroes the Option tag in the owning struct so the struct's drop skips the payload the callee now owns. Here the owning struct lives inside an RC node that other handles may still read, so writing to it is not allowed; `field_chain_place_ptr` already bails on a borrowed root for exactly this reason, which is why the -16 suppressor is a no-op on this shape (it does not misbehave — it simply does not fire). The correct fix is a defensive COPY of the payload at the call site, so the callee frees its own copy and the node keeps its original — the territory the B-2026-07-21-16 design assigned to 'the -9/-14 ref-param clone legs'.

CONFIRMED NARROW by control: the identical program with a NON-shared enum is clean on all three backends, so this is specific to a `shared` root and not to match-bound payloads in general.
resolution:
FIXED 2026-07-29 (09ffe5a). `clone_shared_view_optres_field_arg` gives the callee a defensive COPY of the Option value when the argument is an `Option`/`Result` field read out of a struct in `shared_enum_payload_view_vars`; the node keeps its original. It defers to `emit_option_value_clone_fn`, which self-gates on the payload actually owning heap, so a POD payload keeps the shallow copy and costs nothing. This is the same trade the `let`-site clone-on-extract (B-2026-07-09-12) already makes for a Vec field of such a view.

TWO WRONG TURNS, recorded because both were plausible and neither is the right place. (1) `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` looked like the natural hook — it already deep-clones a heap field read through a borrowed receiver — but instrumenting it showed its FieldAccess arm is never reached for a user-fn argument at all; it runs on the return path and on a few container sinks. (2) Widening its receiver gate to `borrowed_agg_payload_struct_vars` changes nothing, because that set is only populated on the `pattern_binding_is_borrow` path and a match over a shared-enum LOCAL is not classified as a borrow scrutinee. The working hook is the user-call argument loop itself, between `compile_expr` and the `compiled_args.push`.

THE REGRESSION TEST IS STRAIGHT-LINE ON PURPOSE, and this is the part worth carrying forward. Two properties of this shape let a routine test pass vacuously, and both were established by running the candidate against the PRE-FIX compiler rather than assumed:
  * The payload must ESCAPE the callee — the arm has to return `x.label`. A consumer that merely reads it (`x.label.len() + x.k`) binds a borrow, frees nothing, and the program is clean with or without the fix. A first draft did exactly that and passed both ways.
  * Wrapping the body in a `while` loop SUPPRESSES it. That is the accumulate-so-any-imbalance-shows idiom the sibling B-2026-07-28-16 test uses and it is the wrong instinct here: the looped form passed pre-fix, the straight-line form aborts. So the test asserts stdout and repeats the shape with distinct bindings instead of iterating.

VERIFIED: 2603 codegen E2E, 862 memory_sanitizer (gcc ASAN+LSan), 200 par_codegen, the 191-program selfhost corpus and the non-llvm suite all green; clippy + fmt clean. The new test was checked to bite (ASAN reports `attempting double-free` without the fix). The entry's own 12-line repro now matches the interpreter line-for-line and is valgrind-clean, as are all ten shapes in the -16/-17 scratch battery.

title: SELFHOST EMITTER (codegen.kara): `==` with a BOOL operand emits an i64 compare against an i1 value — `icmp eq i64 %t, false` — which LLVM rejects. `not b` is unaffected. This is the only thing between the port and emitting codegen.kara itself.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found by feeding each self-host module to the port with its import closure after B-2026-07-28-14/-15 moved seven of nine modules to valid IR. `codegen.kara` was one of the two remaining; this is its first error.

MECHANISM: the equality lowering picks the i64 lane for its `icmp` regardless of the operand's kind, so a bool operand — which `ty_text` renders `i1` — is compared at the wrong width. The literal is emitted as `false`/`true`, so the mismatch is between an i1 register and an i64 comparison, not between two registers.

NARROWED, each measured rather than assumed:
  * `b == false` — INVALID. `b == true` — INVALID. So it is not about which literal.
  * A bool LOCAL and a bool PARAM both fail, so it is not about where the operand comes from.
  * `not b` is VALID. The unary path already lowers at i1, so only the binary `==` arm is wrong.

FAILS LOUDLY (LLVM rejects the module at parse), so nothing silently miscompiles today.

IN SITU: `Emitter.collect_sigs`, from `while vj < cnt and eshared == false` — the emitted IR is
  %t3395 = load i1, ptr %v19, align 8
  %t3396 = icmp eq i64 %t3395, false

MODULE FRONTIER at the time of filing (`scripts/selfhost-emit-module.sh --all`, which supplies each module's transitive import closure):
  span        IR VALID   (0 fns — scaffold only)
  token       IR VALID   (0 fns — scaffold only)
  ast         IR VALID   (3 fns -> 6 defines)
  lexer       IR VALID   (43 fns -> 43 defines)
  typechecker IR VALID   (41 fns -> 47 defines)
  ast_render  IR VALID   (21501 lines)
  resolver    IR VALID   (20823 lines)
