fix: 895d4da
title: CONTRADICTORY RULES: E_ENUM_NESTED_ENUM_PAYLOAD said to mark a nested inner enum `shared`, while E_NOT_CROSS_TASK said a `shared enum` cannot cross a task boundary and to use `par` — but the nesting check counted a `par enum` as a VALUE enum, so it rejected `par` too. A type needing both properties could not be written.
detail:
REPRO — the shape `examples/db_pipeline` actually needs:

  par enum Value { Int(i64), Null }                       // for the cross-task rule
  enum Query { Delete { table: String, value: Value } }    // nested one level
  // ... Value also reachable from the provider crossing `with_provider`

Marking `Value` `shared` satisfies the nesting rule and trips E_NOT_CROSS_TASK.
Marking it `par` satisfies the cross-task rule and trips
E_ENUM_NESTED_ENUM_PAYLOAD. There was no third spelling: the two diagnostics'
remedies were mutually exclusive.

ROOT CAUSE: `derives.rs` built its value-enum set with `!e.is_shared` and
skipped outer enums with `if e.is_shared`, in both places ignoring `is_par`.
So a `par enum` was treated as a by-value enum.

WHY THAT IS WRONG: design.md § Type Kinds makes `shared` and `par` the two
reference-semantics tiers — single-task RC and cross-task respectively. Both are
a single pointer word, which is the entire basis of the nesting rule's
exemption (the code's own comment: "`SharedFoo` is a single pointer word and is
allowed"). The size argument applies identically to `par`.

FIX (2026-07-31): both sites treat `par` like `shared`, and the diagnostic now
offers `par` alongside `shared`, flagged for when the value must cross a task
boundary. `value_enum_payload_still_trips_the_nesting_rule` pins that a plain
VALUE enum is still rejected, so this adds a tier rather than dropping a rule.

IMPACT: examples/db_pipeline type-checks with 0 errors, down from 18 at the
start of the sweep, and left KNOWN_BROKEN_PACKAGES.

title: INTERPRETER LOSES PROVIDER MUTATIONS: a `mut ref self` provider method called inside `with_provider` has no visible effect — two `bump()` calls read back 0, not 2. Codegen gets it right (prints 2), so this is a silent WRONG ANSWER that diverges from the backend it is meant to preview.
detail:
MINIMAL REPRO (24 lines):

  trait Counter { fn bump(mut ref self); fn get(ref self) -> i64; }
  effect resource Ctr: Counter;
  struct InMem { n: i64 }
  impl Counter for InMem {
      fn bump(mut ref self) { self.n = self.n + 1; }
      fn get(ref self) -> i64 { self.n }
  }
  fn do_bump() with writes(Ctr) { Ctr.bump(); }
  fn read() -> i64 with reads(Ctr) { Ctr.get() }
  fn main() {
      let c = InMem { n: 0 };
      with_provider[Ctr](c, || { do_bump(); do_bump(); println(f"{read()}"); });
  }

  karac run --interp  ->  0     WRONG
  karac run (JIT)     ->  2     correct

No error, no warning — the interpreter simply computes the wrong answer. That
makes it worse than a compile failure: `karac run` is the ergonomic default and
is meant to preview what a built binary does.

CONTRADICTS THE DOCUMENTED CONTRACT: `ownership.rs`'s
`collect_callee_param_modes` records `with_provider(value, body)`'s value slot
as non-consuming "per the documented mutation-visible-after-pop semantics", and
`examples/db_pipeline/src/db.kara` carries a comment describing the same
expectation. Mutations are supposed to be visible.

SOURCE NOTE: found the moment examples/db_pipeline first type-checked
(B-2026-07-31-3). Its seed INSERTs run, then every SELECT prints "(no rows)" —
the provider's `tables` map is unchanged. That package cannot run correctly on
either backend today: the interpreter loses the writes, and codegen rejects the
structural `==` on its reference-typed `Value` enum (a gap that diagnostic
documents, and which a `shared enum` hits equally, so it is not a consequence
of choosing `par`).

── FIXED 2026-07-31 (interpreter) ──

ROOT CAUSE. `dispatch_resource_method_with_values` (resource_method.rs) resolves
the active provider as `(*provider_arc).clone()` — a by-value copy of the frame's
`Arc<Value>` — binds it as the implicit `self`, runs the method body, then pops
the scope and DISCARDS the (possibly mutated) `self`. So a `mut ref self` method
like `bump()` mutates only the arm-local copy; the provider frame is never
updated, and the next call re-clones the unchanged original. Two `bump()`s read
back 0.

FIX. After the body, gate on the receiver mode exactly as the normal-method CICO
write-back in `method_call.rs` does — `method_self_param(type_name, method) ==
Some(SelfParam::MutRef)` — read the `self` binding back BEFORE `pop_scope`, then
write it into the provider frame via a new `update_provider(resource, value)`
(top-down search for the frame binding the resource, replace its `Arc`). A `ref
self` reader / owned-self method never rebinds, so read-only calls are untouched.
This is the mutation-visible-after-pop contract the entry cites, and it matches
what codegen already does (the repro prints 2 on both backends now).

VERIFIED: the 13-line repro now prints 2 on interp == JIT; a heap-field provider
(`Vec[String].push` via `mut ref self`, three puts then count) prints 3 on both;
a `ref self`-only reader is unchanged (5+5=10). Interpreter twin tests added
(`test_with_provider_mut_ref_self_mutation_visible_across_calls`,
`_mutates_heap_field`, `_ref_self_does_not_rebind_provider`), the first checked
NON-VACUOUS (fails with the write-back disabled). Suites: interpreter 1338,
effectchecker 409.

SEPARATE GAP FOUND, filed as B-2026-07-31-9: the `providers { R => v } in { }`
BLOCK form (as opposed to `with_provider[R](v, ||{})`) emits NOTHING under
codegen/JIT — even a read-only `Ctr.get()` — while the interpreter runs it
correctly. That is a codegen no-output gap, orthogonal to this interpreter
mutation-loss fix, and not addressed here.

fix: ccf4053a
title: SILENT WRONG OUTPUT + OUT-OF-BOUNDS READ (run-vs-build): a `ref Slice[T]` / `ref Vec[T]` PARAM forwarded to a BY-VALUE `Slice[T]` parameter is read as if its alloca held the header. `fn blen(v: Slice[i64]) -> i64 { v.len() }` with `fn via(v: ref Slice[i64]) -> i64 { blen(v) }` over `let a: Array[i64,4] = [100,7,3,4]` returns 4 under `--interp` and, per lane: a STACK ADDRESS under the JIT (`karac run`, exit 0, no diagnostic) and the constant 1073741824 under `karac build` (default auto-par and KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 alike). The indexing direction is worse: `v[1]` returns 4 — the slice's own len field — because the data pointer becomes the HEADER, so the callee reads OUT OF BOUNDS and the JIT does not trap; the AOT bounds check does, panicking `vec index out of bounds` on a valid index. A `Slice[String]` element printed garbage bytes from a bogus pointer. `karac check` passes on every one of these. THE SOURCE IS IRRELEVANT — an owned `Array[i64,N]` local and a `Vec[i64]` local reproduce identically, and so does a `ref Vec[T]` forwarding param — which is what separates this from the Array-header family (B-2026-06-19-1 / B-2026-07-30-3 / B-2026-07-30-6): the defect is in how the FORWARDING BINDING is read, not in what it points at. NOT the `ref`-arg path either: bare->bare and ref->ref both were and stay correct, so it takes a `ref` param feeding a BY-VALUE `Slice` param. ROOT CAUSE: `coerce_to_slice`'s Identifier fast-path (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs) read the payload straight out of `variables[name].ptr` in two arms — the `slice_elem_types` arm (`build_load(slice_ty, slot.ptr)`) and the `vec_elem_types` arm (`build_struct_gep(vec_ty, slot.ptr, 0/1)`). That is the header only for an OWNED local; for a `ref` param the alloca holds a POINTER to the caller's header, so the load produced `{header_ptr, whatever sits next on the stack}` — which is exactly why `.len()` read as an address under the JIT (ASLR, different every run) and as a constant under AOT (a fixed adjacent stack word), and why `v[i]` indexed off the header. The sibling arms already handled the fork: the ArrayType arm below reads `ref_params`, and `get_data_ptr` is the canonical `owned alloca | ref-param deref | module global` accessor that the `ref`-arg fast path in call_dispatch.rs uses. FIX: both arms go through `get_data_ptr(var_name).unwrap_or(slot.ptr)`. One line of behaviour, and it also corrects an RC-promoted binding in the same position (its alloca holds the box pointer, not the header). FIXED ccf4053a. VERIFIED, all four surfaces byte-identical on 8 probe programs (`--interp` / `run` / `build` / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 `build`), each measured A/B against a baseline compiler built in the SAME worktree against the SAME runtime archive. Suite: codegen E2E 2639/0, plus the full `cargo test --features llvm` sweep green; clippy `--all --all-targets --features llvm` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. `selfhost_codegen_matches_seed_run` is RED both with and without this change (pre-existing, B-2026-07-16-16).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found writing kata #237 (237-delete-node-in-a-linked-list, Delete Node in a Linked List), not by probing. The kata's `fn report(vals: ref Slice[i64], node: i64)` — `ref` because `report` is called twice on one array, which is the mode B-2026-07-01-10 settled as correct — forwards to `fn build(vals: Slice[i64]) -> Vec[Node]`, and the built pool came back empty, so the first delete panicked `vec index out of bounds`. That is the ordinary spelling of a two-function kata, which is why this was reachable without any generic, any Array-header shape, or any unusual argument form. HARNESS NOTE, since it cost a false reading mid-investigation: the first probe sweep in a FRESH WORKTREE reported the build lane as correct when in fact `karac build` had failed to link at all (no runtime archives in a new worktree) and the harness was reading the PREVIOUS lane's stdout file. Fresh output files per lane and the program's own exit status — never a pipeline's — is the only safe shape; this is the same class of harness fault recorded in B-2026-07-29-37's retraction. INVESTIGATION NOT DONE: no ASan/valgrind run on the out-of-bounds JIT read (it reads within the caller's frame, so it is unlikely to trip a page guard). Not bisected — the two arms have read `slot.ptr` since they were written, so there is no regression point to find. UNKNOWN whether the same fast-path is reached with a `mut ref` container param forwarding to a `mut Slice[T]` param, or through a struct-field place (`self.items`) rather than an Identifier; both were left unprobed. The mono path (`compile_generic_call`) reaches `coerce_to_slice` through the same helper and is therefore covered by construction, but a generic callee taking a BY-VALUE `Slice[T]` fed from a `ref` param was not separately measured.

title: A value enum's own `impl Drop` body fired at SCOPE EXIT under codegen but at the binding's NLL live-range end under the interpreter — `mid|DS` vs `DS|mid` for `{ let b = Bare.Full(7); println("mid"); }`.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: surfaced by the B-2026-07-30-11 enum-leg shape sweep, not reported
independently. Measured on the UNMODIFIED compiler before that fix, so it is a
pre-existing defect and not a regression the enum leg introduced.

design.md § Drop ordering puts a destructor at its binding's live-range end, which is
what the interpreter implements and what B-2026-07-21-1 already aligned codegen to for
value STRUCTS. Enums were left behind: `fire_due_user_drops`'s filter admitted a
`UserDrop` only when its `type_name` was in `struct_types`, and an enum name never is.
So the enum's `karac_drop_<E>` wrapper stayed in the frame and drained at scope exit.

Observable exactly when the body has side effects, which for an `impl Drop` is the normal
case — a print, a close, a release. Any program whose enum RAII interleaves with other
output printed in a different order depending on which backend ran it.

FIX: one clause in the same filter — admit a `type_name` that names a non-shared entry in
`enum_layouts`. Safe because `karac_drop_<E>` is BODY-ONLY for an enum: the wrapper
emitter's field-bodies step and its struct-memory step both decline for an enum name, and
payload memory is the separate scope-exit `EnumDrop` action. So firing it early frees
nothing early. Shared enums are excluded for the same reason shared structs are — their
drop is refcount-driven.

Landed together with the B-2026-07-30-11 enum leg because the same shape sweep found both
and the interleave between them (own body first, then payload bodies — the order
`run_user_drop_body` + `drop_user_drop_fields_of_binding` produce) is only pinnable with
both in place. Twinned E2E tests in tests/codegen.rs and tests/interpreter.rs assert the
identical string.

fix: d5f45d6
title: A `Result[T, E]` whose payload is HEAP-BOXED got the INLINE payload cleanup registered ON TOP of the correct box drop, so the inline overlay read the box POINTER as the first word of the payload struct — running a user Drop body on garbage and freeing whatever those words held.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while scoping the Option/Result half of B-2026-07-30-11, by
running a heap-payload `Result[Res, i64]` under valgrind and diffing `karac run`
against `karac build`. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING on the commit before that entry's
enum leg — not a regression from it.

REPRODUCTION.

    struct Res { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }
    impl Drop for Res { fn drop(mut ref self) { println("D " + self.name + " " + self.buf.len().to_string()); } }
    fn mkres() -> Res { ... }          // returns a Res with a real heap String and Vec
    fn main() {
        let d: Result[Res, i64] = Result.Ok(mkres());
        println("d");
    }

    karac run --interp  ->  d
    karac build         ->  d
                            D  0        <-- a Drop body on an EMPTY Res

MECHANISM. `Res` has two heap fields, so `coerce_to_payload_words` spills the
payload behind a `malloc`'d box and stores the box POINTER in word 0. Two cleanups
end up registered on the one binding:

  * `BoxedEnumDrop` — correct: loads the box pointer, runs
    `__karac_drop_struct_Res` on the box contents, `free`s the box.
  * `FreeInlineResultPayload` with `ok_payload_struct_drop = karac_drop_Res` —
    WRONG for a boxed payload: it calls `karac_drop_Res(payload_ptr)` where
    `payload_ptr` is `&slot.word1`, i.e. it reads `{box_ptr, 0, 0}` as
    `Res { name: String, buf: Vec }`. `name` comes out as a String with len 0
    (hence the empty body print) and `buf` as a zero Vec.

The observable symptom is a run/build divergence, but the real defect is that
`karac_drop_Res` is body AND memory: it also runs the free paths over those
misread words. It stayed benign only because the trailing words happened to be
zero, so every `cap > 0` guard skipped. A payload whose overlay window lands on
non-zero words is a free of an address the program never allocated.

FIX. `track_inline_result_payload_var` returns early when the binding is already
in `boxed_enum_payload_vars`. The box registration runs first at the same
let-site, so membership is visible; the box drop is the one that walks the
payload correctly.

NOT FIXED HERE, and worth stating: the box drop is MEMORY-ONLY
(`__karac_drop_struct_Res`), so the payload's user `Drop` BODY still never runs
for a boxed Option/Result payload. That is the still-open Option/Result half of
B-2026-07-30-11, and this fix changes it from "a body runs on garbage" to "no
body runs" — the same silence every other Option/Result payload already had.

VERIFIED: interp/AOT parity on the reproduction and on annotated / unannotated /
call-returned Option and Result variants; valgrind clean. E2E test checked
NON-VACUOUS (fails with the guard removed). Suites: codegen 2644,
memory_sanitizer 871, par_codegen 202, cli 545, drop_differential 13,
selfhost_codegen 1.

fix: d5f45d6
title: An UNANNOTATED `let` of an `Option`/`Result` whose payload is heap-BOXED registered no cleanup at all and leaked the whole box, payload heap included — `let b = Option.Some(mk());` leaked where `let b: Option[Res] = Option.Some(mk());` did not.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found in the same valgrind sweep as B-2026-07-31-6, one binding
form over. Also confirmed PRE-EXISTING before the B-2026-07-30-11 enum leg.

    let a: Option[Res] = Option.Some(mkres());   // 0 leak records
    let b = Option.Some(mkres());                // 320 bytes definitely lost

MECHANISM. The boxed-payload registration resolved the binding's type from, in
order, the LET ANNOTATION and then `untyped_let_boxed_enum_te`. The latter reads
`fn_return_type_exprs` keyed on a bare-`Identifier` callee (`let o = make_opt()`)
and returns `None` for anything else. `Option.Some(mkres())`'s callee is the PATH
`Option.Some`, so neither source produced a type, `boxed_enum_payload_variants`
was never consulted, and the emitted IR contained no drop for the binding at all
— not a shallow free, none.

Everything reachable from the box leaks: the box itself, the payload struct's
String buffer, its Vec buffer, recursively.

WHY IT HID. The annotated form always worked, and the annotated form is the
natural way to write both a test and an example — which is exactly the shape the
suite had. The unannotated form is the one people actually write.

FIX. Insert the typechecker's recorded instantiation between the two existing
sources: annotation, then `enum_inst_type_exprs` keyed on the value's span, then
the call-return fallback. That map is not new machinery — the sibling
inline-payload registration two blocks below in the same function already reads
it for the same purpose.

RISK NOTE, since this WIDENS drop registration to shapes that previously
registered nothing: the failure direction of getting it wrong is a double-free,
not a leak. Checked accordingly — the ASAN test keeps both the annotated and the
unannotated bindings live so a fix that over-swings shows up as an ASAN error
rather than silently, and it was verified NON-VACUOUS (fails with the
`enum_inst_type_exprs` source removed). Full suites green after: codegen 2644,
memory_sanitizer 871, par_codegen 202, cli 545, drop_differential 13,
selfhost_codegen 1.

LSan CAN witness this one directly, unlike the bodies-only legs of
B-2026-07-30-11 — it is a genuine leak of a malloc'd box, so the Linux
memory-sanitizer CI job is a real gate for it.

fix: db59de2
tracker: src/codegen/reduce.rs (clamp_iter_total_nonneg + the scalar and Collect iter_total sites); src/codegen/disjoint_par.rs
title: An INVERTED loop range (`for y in 5..3`) makes auto-par's `iter_total` negative, and the descriptor field is `u64` — so a loop that runs ZERO iterations sequentially fans out over ~2^64, hanging a scalar reduction and writing out of range on the indexed-write shape.
resolution: Fixed with the indexed-write fan-out lowering slice. One shared clamp helper, applied at all three stamping sites.

tracker: src/codegen (providers-block lowering); interp path src/interpreter/eval_call.rs eval_providers_block
title: The `providers { R => v } in { body }` BLOCK form emits NOTHING under codegen/JIT — even a read-only `R.get()` — while the interpreter runs it correctly. A silent no-output run-vs-build divergence for the block sugar; the `with_provider[R](v, ||{})` call form works on both backends.
resolution:
FIXED. `compile_expr` had no `ExprKind::Providers` arm, so the block fell through to the catch-all `_ => Ok(const 0)` (exprs.rs) and its BODY WAS NEVER EMITTED — the compiled program printed nothing and exited 0. The entry's guess was right: codegen simply did not lower the form.

LOWERING. `compile_providers_block` (codegen/provider.rs) mirrors the interpreter's `eval_providers_block` phase for phase: resolve every binding, push one frame each outer-to-inner, compile the body, pop in reverse. The frame-alloca / push / pop steps were factored out of `compile_with_provider` and are now shared by both surfaces, so they cannot drift apart.

NOT lowered as nested `with_provider` calls — the obvious shortcut, and wrong on ORDERING. The interpreter evaluates ALL provider expressions before pushing ANY frame, so in `providers { A => InMem { n: 7 }, B => InMem { n: ra() } }` the call `ra()` reads the OUTER `A`. Nesting would evaluate `B`'s value with the new `A` already installed, trading the fixed divergence for a subtler one. Pinned by `e2e_providers_block_multi_binding_nesting_and_order`.

SECOND DEFECT, not visible from the entry. A TRAIT-LESS `effect resource R;` overridden only through the block form got no `(U, R)` vtable and no method order, failing with "no method order for resource" even after the body started compiling. Both are minted by the eager `emit_ambient_provider_vtables` pre-pass, which walked `with_provider` CALLS only. It now visits `Providers` nodes through the same `record_ambient_override_site` helper the call arm uses; sharing it is load-bearing, because the two surfaces disagreeing about method ORDER would be a silent wrong-method call rather than an error.

EARLY RETURN IS NOW REFUSED, LOUDLY — and this is the one behaviour REGRESSION, so it is stated plainly. A body ending in a terminator (`return`, or `break`/`continue` out of an enclosing loop) would have the pops appended after that terminator, i.e. invalid IR. The block form now returns an actionable diagnostic naming the cause. Previously that same program COMPILED and printed a wrong answer (the whole block was constant 0), so a refusal is strictly better — but a program that used to build now does not. The hole is NOT new and NOT specific to the block form: `with_provider`'s closure body fails today with the same "Terminator found in the middle of a basic block" verifier error. Filed as B-2026-07-31-11.

VERIFIED on all three backends (`--interp`, JIT, AOT) for: single and multiple bindings, nesting with shadowing and restore, cross-binding evaluation order, body-local heap bindings (the cleanup frame drains before the pops), block-as-value, mutation through a `mut ref self` provider method, a block inside a method, a block inside a loop (entry-block frame alloca reused per iteration, as `with_provider` already does), and identifier / struct-literal / constructor-call providers.

GATES: `test_providers_block_run_build_parity` (tests/cli.rs) compares the two BACKENDS rather than an expected string, because the failure mode was one backend emitting nothing — an interpreter-only test cannot see that. Verified to fail without the fix (left "42\n", right ""). Plus `e2e_providers_block_runs_body`, `e2e_providers_block_multi_binding_nesting_and_order` and `e2e_providers_block_trait_less_ambient_resource` (tests/codegen.rs).

WHY THE SUITE WAS GREEN THROUGHOUT: every pre-existing provider test uses the desugared `with_provider[R](v, ||{})` call form, which was always correct on all three backends. The sugar had no codegen test at all, so the form users reach for first was unguarded.

fix: f068f0e (indexed-write path) + 269d9ce (reduction path)
title: `body_is_memory_bound` classifies a 7-tap vector CONVOLUTION as memory-bound — it keys on "has an index read and no substantial CALL" and cannot see that the body's work is a runtime-bounded nested LOOP. Narrowly worked around for the indexed-write fan-out (measured 21% of wall time on Prism's Lanczos); the REDUCTION path still carries it.
detail:
FOUND by converting `apps/prism/prism.kara` to the natural loop form (the acceptance sub-slice of the auto-par indexed-write entry). The horizontal pass fans out; the vertical pass is PROVEN disjoint and then declined by the cost model with `cost_gate: declined_memory_bound`.

THE BODY IN QUESTION (prism.kara, vertical pass) is not memory-streaming:

    let mut acca = Vector[f64, 2].splat(0.0);
    let mut accb = Vector[f64, 2].splat(0.0);
    let mut sy = lo;
    while sy <= hi {                       // lanczos-3: up to ~7 taps
        let w = Vector[f64, 2].splat(ywgts[base + (sy - lo)]);
        let p = (sy * dw + dx) * 4;
        acca = acca + Vector[f64, 2](tmp[p], tmp[p + 1]) * w;
        accb = accb + Vector[f64, 2](tmp[p + 2], tmp[p + 3]) * w;
        sy = sy + 1;
    }

That is a per-output-pixel convolution with vector FMA, i.e. compute.

MEASURED (1600x1200 -> 800x600 lanczos resize, 4 cores, 9 runs, median):

  sequential (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0)                       72.1 ms   1.00x
  shipped (h-pass fans out, v-pass declined)          43.8 ms   1.65x
  both passes fanned out (gate bypassed)              34.5 ms   2.09x

So the gate costs 21% of the remaining wall time on the flagship kernel and holds the speedup at 1.65x where 2.09x is available. User-CPU barely moved (0.061 -> 0.066 s), so the parallel work is NOT being wasted — this is not the kata-153 pathology the gate was built for.

WHY IT MISFIRES. `body_is_memory_bound` is `memory_count > 0 && !substantial_call`: at least one Index/FieldAccess and no substantial function/method call. It was calibrated on kata-153's `let x = nums[i]; if x < m { m = x; }`, where that predicate is exactly right. It has no notion of a body whose work is a runtime-bounded NESTED LOOP rather than a call — which is precisely the convolution shape, and precisely the shape `VARIABLE_K_PER_ITER_FLOOR_UNITS` already recognises elsewhere in the same file (`RUNTIME_NESTED_LOOP_MULTIPLIER`, 64, documented as "the per-iteration work must be at least one nested loop's worth").

CANDIDATE FIX (deliberately NOT applied here). Treat a body containing a runtime-bounded nested loop as not-memory-bound. It is narrow, it reuses a distinction the cost model already draws, and it leaves kata-153 classified correctly (that body has no nested loop). NOT applied in the conversion slice because `body_is_memory_bound` is SHARED with the reduction lowering and was calibrated against reduction benchmarks that are not available in this environment; changing a calibrated model deserves its own slice with its own validation rather than a drive-by during an acceptance test. The measurement above is recorded so that slice starts from data instead of a hunch.

IMPACT IF UNFIXED: every separable-convolution kernel (the second pass of any separable resample, gaussian blur, sobel, unsharp) leaves roughly a quarter of its available parallelism on the table, silently — the query reports `declined_memory_bound`, so it is at least discoverable.

PARTIAL FIX LANDED (indexed-write path only). `par_cost::fanout_verdict_indexed_writes` skips the memory-bound gate when the body already scores at least `VARIABLE_K_PER_ITER_FLOOR_UNITS` — the constant the cost model ALREADY uses to mean "at least one nested loop's worth of work" — so no second threshold was invented. Applied there and not to reductions because that calibration was set against reduction benchmarks unavailable in this environment.

WHY IT COULD NOT WAIT. Prism's Lanczos previously hand-rolled a band fan-out over BOTH passes. Converting to the natural loop form with the gate in place fanned out only the horizontal pass, making the conversion a ~27% REGRESSION against the code it replaced — not something to ship to a live public app as the acceptance test of a feature. With the narrow fix the converted kernel is 37.4 ms median vs the hand-rolled 48.8 ms (1600x1200 -> 800x600, 4 cores, 11 runs, byte-identical output): 23% FASTER than the hand-written concurrency it deletes.

STILL OPEN: the reduction path. A reduction whose body is a nested-loop convolution is still classified memory-bound and still declines. Closing it needs the reduction benchmarks re-run.

REDUCTION LEG CLOSED. The carve-out now runs for BOTH fan-out shapes: `fanout_verdict` skips the memory-bound gate whenever the per-iteration estimate already clears `VARIABLE_K_PER_ITER_FLOOR_UNITS`, and `fanout_verdict_indexed_writes` is gone (one function, both callers).

WHAT THE RE-BENCH ACTUALLY FOUND, which is not what this entry predicted. The claim above — 'a reduction whose body is a nested-loop convolution is still classified memory-bound and still declines' — is only half true, and the reason matters. `MemoryBoundDetector::visit_expr` has NO `While` / `For` / `Loop` arm; those fall through its `_ => {}`. So a body whose loads all sit inside a nested loop has `memory_count == 0` and was never classified memory-bound in the first place. The gate fires on such a body only when it ALSO reads memory at the TOP level — which is exactly Prism's vertical pass (the `out[...] = ...` writes are top-level; the tap loop's reads are not).

MEASURED, 4-core Linux container, medians, all outputs byte-identical to their `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` twins:

  (d) conv2 — 7-tap convolution reduction, one top-level index read
      (the reduction twin of Prism's vertical pass).  THE FIX.
        sequential                       172.2 ms
        fanned out                       107.5 ms   1.60x
      Three interleaved runs put the ratio at 1.45-1.60x.

  (a) scan — kata-153's `let x = nums[i]; if x < m { m = x; }`.  CONTROL.
      Body scores 14 against the floor of 64, so it stays
      `declined_memory_bound`, wall unchanged (39.9 vs 41.7 ms, neither
      build links par_reduce). The calibration is intact. NOTE the
      original wording here said a FLAT body scores far below the floor —
      see the correction at the end of this entry; that generalization is
      false.

  (c) grid — 2000x2000 strided sum, 32 MiB working set.  RISK CASE.
        sequential 73.2 ms / fanned out 34.6 ms — 2.12x.
      At 4000x4000 (128 MiB): 156.2 vs 104.1 ms — 1.50x.
      This is the shape the gate is nominally FOR, it escapes today via the nest-blindness above, and fanning it out is a large WIN on this machine. Making the detector nest-aware was implemented behind a temporary lever, measured, and REJECTED for exactly that reason: it would reclassify (c) and (d) as memory-bound and give back both wins.

CAVEAT ON THE CALIBRATION. The original gate was calibrated on an M5 Pro (~30 GB/s, where one core evidently could saturate memory). These numbers are a 4-core Linux VM where it clearly cannot — more cores extract more bandwidth. That is why the gate was NARROWED rather than removed: the carve-out ('a body with a runtime-bounded nested loop does >= 64x a flat body's work per iteration, so dispatch amortizes') holds on both machines, whereas deleting the gate would rest on one machine's bandwidth curve.

NOTED IN PASSING, not acted on: with the memory-bound gate disabled entirely, kata-153's shape STILL declines — via `declined_variable_k_param_bound` (B-2026-07-23-25's gate), which subsumes it. So the memory-bound gate may no longer be load-bearing for the shape it was built for. Not pursued here; removing a calibrated gate deserves a cross-machine measurement this environment cannot provide.

CORRECTION (2026-07-31, found while converting Prism's `grayscale` at a reader's prompt). This entry justified the carve-out with "a flat body scores far below the floor, so it cannot reach kata-153's shape". The second clause is true; the FIRST IS FALSE and the justification does not hold. The gate is skipped on a COST THRESHOLD, not on the presence of a nested loop, so any body scoring >= 64 escapes it — including a flat one that is merely long.

Measured with a new `KARAC_COST_DEBUG=1` lever: kata-153's two-statement body scores 14, but a flat Rec.601 grayscale body (four index reads, ~12 statements, NO nested loop) scores 161 and escapes. Converting Prism's `gray` from its strided `while i < n { ... i = i + 4 }` to `for p in 0..w*h` therefore makes it fan out — `proven` / `fanout`, and the binary links par_reduce.

Whether that is a misfire: measured NO. 12 MP, 4 cores, 9 interleaved reps, setup subtracted — 29.3 ms/rep sequential vs 22.1 ms/rep fanned out, 1.32x. Lower than the convolution shapes (1.5-2.2x), which is what you would expect from a genuinely bandwidth-heavy kernel, but still a win. So the wider reach is earning its keep on this machine.

Two consequences. (1) The real boundary is "more than roughly ten statements of scalar work", of which a nested loop is one instance — any future narrowing should start from that, not from the nested-loop story. (2) This reach PREDATES this slice: it arrived with the indexed-write carve-out in f068f0e, whose `substantial` test was already `per_iter_cost >= floor`. What this slice changed was the reduction path and the (wrong) description, not this behaviour.

fix: 9cfd715
title: An early `return` out of a provider body — `with_provider`'s closure OR the `providers { } in { }` block — cannot be compiled: the `karac_provider_pop` is emitted after the body, so a terminator inside the body makes it unreachable. `with_provider` fails with a raw LLVM "Terminator found in the middle of a basic block"; the block form refuses with a diagnostic. Both mean the shape is uncompilable, while `--interp` runs it.
resolution:
FIXED as prescribed: the pop is a scope-cleanup action, drained on every exit path. New `CleanupAction::ProviderPop` (codegen/state.rs) + its two drain arms (codegen/runtime.rs: `record_drop_obs` -> None, `emit_cleanup_action` -> emit the `karac_provider_pop()` call). All three emission sites (trait-ful `compile_with_provider`, the ambient form, `compile_providers_block`) route the body through one helper, `compile_provider_body_with_pop_frame(n_pops, body)`: push a dedicated cleanup frame holding one ProviderPop per pushed provider frame, compile the body (its own frames nest INSIDE), then — fall-through: `drain_top_frame_with_emit()` lands the pops exactly where the old inline emission put them; terminated body: just discard the frame, because the exit site's `emit_scope_cleanup` walk already drained it innermost-first, so body-local drops fired BEFORE the pop (the interpreter's order) and before the terminator. The block form's refusal arm is deleted; `emit_provider_pop` lost its last caller and is removed. An enclosing-loop `break` works for free: `compile_break` drains from the loop's cleanup depth, which sits below the pop frame — and a loop INSIDE the body leaves the pop frame untouched.

VERIFIED: the ledger repro prints 8/8 for BOTH forms on all three backends (--interp, JIT, AOT). Probe matrix beyond it: nested with_provider whose inner call early-returns, then the OUTER resource read again (107 — the dangling-frame scenario the 'do not skip the pop' warning describes); `?` error-path propagation out of the body; a heap-owning body local (f-string) freed on the return edge; multi-binding block popping BOTH frames on the return edge with a healthy push/dispatch after; break out of an enclosing for-loop from both forms with re-push on the next iteration (acc 0+1+2=3).

GATES: seven codegen E2Es (tests/codegen.rs, `early_return`/`loop_break_pops` groups), `test_provider_early_return_run_build_parity` (tests/cli.rs — the B-2026-07-31-9 parity gate extended to early-return bodies for BOTH forms per the validation bar; a `codegen failed` stderr FAILS it rather than soft-skipping, since a codegen refusal was this bug's exact failure mode), and `asan_provider_early_return_frees_body_local` (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs — ASAN/LSan on the return-edge free, 200 iterations x both forms x both paths). Non-vacuity: with the provider.rs rewiring reverted, `e2e_with_provider_early_return_body` fails with the original verifier error.

THREE RESIDUAL GAPS FILED, all exposed by the validation probes, none regressed by this fix: B-2026-07-31-15 (interp returns UNIT from an i64 fn when the body breaks an enclosing loop — codegen now runs that shape type-soundly), B-2026-07-31-16 (form A `return` in NON-tail position: typechecker+interp treat it as closure-scoped — `let x = with_provider(..., || return 8); x + 1` is 9 under --interp — while codegen lowers `return` as a fn-level ret and still fails verification; tail position, where the two semantics coincide, is what this fix covers), B-2026-07-31-17 (the generic sibling: `let x = { return 5; }; tail` verifier-fails with no providers involved).

fix: 66ec99f
tracker: src/codegen/json.rs (lift walker allocations), src/codegen/declarations.rs (Json seed drop kinds), match payload binding registration
title: `Json.parse` of a STRING / ARRAY / OBJECT leaks the lifted Kāra-side tree's heap payloads under codegen — one tree per parse, even when the payload is never used. Scalars are clean; the interpreter is clean. A service parsing request bodies accumulates this per request.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: observed under valgrind while landing B-2026-07-30-15 (Json.Int).
Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: the reproduction leaks identically on the commit before
that fix with a pure-float payload, so it is not the Int variant's.

SHAPE MATRIX, measured (AOT binaries, valgrind --leak-check=full, one
`definitely lost` record per parse of a heap shape):

    Json.parse("42")        -> stringify   clean
    Json.parse("\"hello\"") -> stringify   LEAKS
    Json.parse("[1,2]")     -> stringify   LEAKS
    Json.parse("{\"a\":1}")  -> stringify   LEAKS
    Json.parse("[1,2]")     -> UNUSED      LEAKS  (binding never touched)
    construct-side (Json.Int / Json.Number / Json.Object literal + stringify):
                                           clean

So the leak is the PARSE side only: the FFI tree itself is freed
(karac_runtime_json_free_value runs), but the Kāra-side copies the lift walker
mallocs — the String byte buffer, the Vec[Json] element buffer, the
Vec[(String, Json)] pair buffer, recursively — are never released once the
`Result.Ok(j)` payload binding dies.

TWO COOPERATING GAPS, read off the code:

  (1) REGISTRATION: a match-BOUND payload (`Result.Ok(j) => ...`) gets no
      EnumDrop registration — `track_enum_var` fires at let-sites; the pattern
      binding path does not register the Json binding, so nothing frees even
      the outer buffer. This is why the UNUSED-binding case leaks too.

  (2) DEPTH: even with a registration, the seeded drop for Array/Object is
      `EnumDropKind::VecOrString` — the OUTER buffer only. Nested element
      Strings / child arrays need a recursive Kāra-side walker (the seed
      comment in declarations.rs already anticipates this: 'Array/Object need
      recursive child cleanup ... when the higher-level Vec[Json] /
      Vec[(String, Json)] drop landing arrives'). A one-level fix converts the
      leak from 'whole tree' to 'everything below the first level'.

MAGNITUDE: one lifted tree per parse call — bounded per call, unbounded over a
service's lifetime. The HTTP server path parses request bodies per request, so
this is the accumulating-leak class, not a one-shot.

INTERPRETER: clean (values are Rust-managed). This is codegen-only.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not prescriptive): a `__karac_json_free_kara_tree` synthesized
walker — the memory-side sibling of the existing `__karac_json_kara_to_ffi` tag
switch — registered for the parse result's payload binding at the match/if-let
bind site, plus cap-zero disarm when the payload is moved out. The recursion
problem is the same one `emit_enum_drop_switch`'s NestedStruct arm already
solves for one level; Json needs it self-recursive.

── FIXED 2026-07-31, both cooperating gaps, in the order filed ──

GAP 1 (REGISTRATION): `bind_pattern_values` gained the ENUM sibling of the
B-2026-07-10-3 inline-optres STRUCT arm — an `Option`/`Result` scrutinee whose
INLINE payload is a value enum bound whole (`Ok(j)` with `j: Json`) now gets
`track_enum_var(tn, alloca)`. Same gates as the struct precedent: owned bind
only (`!pattern_binding_is_borrow` block), non-shared enum, and the layout's
word count within `pattern_binding_scrutinee_optres_area` so a heap-BOXED wide
payload — owned by the box drop — stays untouched. `track_enum_var` puts the
binding on exactly the channel a `let`-bound enum uses, so the whole existing
move-out suppression set (destructure cap-zeroing, tail-return, the
callee-copy convention) composes with no new disarm surface.

GAP 2 (DEPTH): `emit_enum_drop_switch` special-cases `Json` to a new dedicated
recursive walker (`emit_json_recursive_drop_fn`, src/codegen/json.rs), emitted
under the standard `__karac_drop_Json` name so every caller that resolves
through the switch — the `EnumDrop` drain, the inline-Result payload cleanup,
struct enum-field drops — picks it up. The walker is the memory-side sibling
of `__karac_json_kara_to_ffi`: same 32-byte `Vec[Json]` and 56-byte
`(String, Json)` strides, direct self-call recursion (the thing the generic
per-variant synthesis structurally cannot express), every free `cap > 0`-
guarded so the move-out cap-zeroing disarms it exactly as it disarmed the
generic one — a wiped node walks nothing.

VERIFIED: the full 11-probe leak matrix is now 0 records (scalar / string /
array / object / unused-binding / the multi-shape composite / all four
construct controls); a 50-iteration deep-nesting + destructure-move-out stress
is valgrind-clean with zero invalid accesses and three-backend parity (5500 ==
5500 == 5500). New `asan_json_parse_tree_freed_once` is the permanent gate —
LSan witnesses this leak DIRECTLY (real malloc'd buffers), and the test was
checked NON-VACUOUS (fails with both halves disabled); it also guards the
unsafe direction (a double-free of a moved-out payload trips ASAN). Suites:
codegen 2648, memory_sanitizer 873, interpreter 1338, typechecker 2118, json 8,
cli 546, par_codegen 211, http_server 27.

RESIDUAL, stated: a destructured-OUT payload's own nested heap
(`Json.Array(xs) => …` — `xs` gets buffer-only `track_vec_var`, so its
ELEMENTS' nested trees are not walked) still leaks one level down. That is the
long-standing bound-Vec depth limitation shared with every enum, not Json-
specific, and it is a leak, not a double-free — the safe side.

fix: 269d9ce
title: `codegen/reduce.rs` open-coded its own copy of the fan-out gate sequence instead of calling `par_cost::fanout_verdict` — the exact drift `par_cost` was extracted to prevent. The copies diverged silently: changing the shared function moved `karac query concurrency`'s verdict while the emitted binary kept the old behaviour.
detail:
FOUND while closing B-2026-07-31-10's reduction leg. `par_cost.rs` exists because the query side physically could not reach codegen's gates (B-2026-07-29-29 / -33), and its module doc is explicit: "A second copy of a *calibrated* cost model drifts from the first, and a drifted copy makes the query confidently wrong, which is worse than the disclaimer it replaces. One definition, two callers."

The extraction gave the QUERY a `fanout_verdict` function. Codegen kept its own inline copy of the same three gates (memory-bound -> const-K threshold -> variable-K param floor), because it needed `per_iter_cost` to stay in scope for the descriptor's runtime-gate field. Two implementations, agreeing only by being identical.

HOW IT SURFACED: narrowing the memory-bound gate in `par_cost::fanout_verdict` flipped `karac query concurrency` to `cost_gate: "fanout"` for the target shape while `nm` on the built binary still showed zero `karac_par_reduce` references. A query claiming a loop fanned out when the binary runs it sequentially is worse than no query.

FIX: added `par_cost::fanout_verdict_with_cost`, which returns `(FanoutVerdict, u64)` — the second element is the per-iteration estimate codegen needed, so keeping it in scope no longer requires a private copy of the gates. `codegen/reduce.rs` and `codegen/disjoint_par.rs` both call it; the open-coded block (~4.5 KB of gate logic + rationale) is deleted, and the rationale now lives on the `FanoutVerdict` variants and the constants they threshold against. `disjoint_par.rs` also stopped walking the body a second time for its own estimate.

TEST: `tests/cli.rs::test_query_concurrency_nested_loop_body_escapes_memory_bound_gate` pins the query's verdict on the same source `tests/par_codegen.rs::test_ir_memory_bound_gate_nested_loop_body_fans_out` pins the IR for — both directions of one shape, so a future divergence moves one of them.

fix: 7375ecf
title: `karac query concurrency` reports `fanned_out: true` / `cost_gate: "fanout"` for a reduction with a FLOAT accumulator, which codegen always refuses to fan out (float reassociation needs an `#[fp_reassoc]` opt-in that does not exist in v1). The query is confidently wrong about the binary.
detail:
FOUND while re-benching the reduction cost gate. A 7-tap convolution reduction accumulating into `f64` queries as `fanned_out: true, cost_gate: "fanout"`; the identical program with an `i64` accumulator links `karac_par_reduce` and the f64 one does not (`nm -C` count 1 vs 0).

The rejection is deliberate and correct — `codegen/reduce.rs` requires the accumulator's lowered type to be an integer of width 8/16/32/64, and its comment says so: "float reductions specifically need an `#[fp_reassoc]` opt-in (see `ReductionOp` doc comment) and aren't in v1." The defect is that the gate is invisible to the query, whose own doc states `fanned_out` is a COMPILE-TIME fact about the emitted binary.

DISTINCT FROM B-2026-07-31-13, which was two copies of the COST gates drifting. This one is a codegen gate the query has no copy of at all, because it is a TYPE gate: `effect_graph`/`concurrency` see the AST, not lowered LLVM types.

FIX SHAPE (not attempted here). `concurrency_analyze_typed` already accepts an optional `TypeCheckResult`, so the accumulator's source type is reachable without new plumbing. Record it on `LoopReduction`, add a `FanoutVerdict::DeclinedNonIntegerAccumulator` variant with its own tag + reason, and check it first in `fanout_verdict_with_cost` — which also makes codegen's own type check redundant, collapsing another divergence. Wants a test pair mirroring B-2026-07-31-13's (IR + query on one source).

WHY NOT NOW: it changes the recognizer's data shape and adds a public enum variant, which is a different slice from re-calibrating a cost gate. Filed instead of folded in.
resolution: Implemented per the filed fix shape. `FanoutVerdict` gains `DeclinedNonIntegerAccumulator` (tag `declined_non_integer_accumulator`), checked FIRST in `fanout_verdict_with_cost` via a new `accumulator_fans_out: bool` parameter — a TYPE gate ahead of every cost gate. The two sides feed it from their own representations: codegen/reduce.rs classifies the accumulator's LOWERED type (IntType of width 8/16/32/64 — the authoritative check; the IntType itself is still extracted for identity/combine synthesis, but the pass/fail DECISION now routes through the shared verdict and the old pre-verdict `return Ok(None)` is gone), while the query side records the accumulator's SOURCE type on `LoopReduction` (`accumulator_type: Option<String>`, resolved in `ConcurrencyChecker::accumulator_source_type` from `expr_types` at an identifier use of the accumulator inside the loop body — `pattern_binding_types` only records Named types, so primitives need the expr-level lookup) and classifies it with the new `par_cost::accumulator_type_fans_out` (integer names fan out; None — untyped analysis or unresolvable — is treated as eligible, preserving pre-gate behavior rather than inventing a decline codegen might not apply). Collect reductions record no type and indexed-write loops pass `true`: their Vec/no accumulator never consults the scalar gate. Verified on the filed convolution shape: the f64 program queries `fanned_out:false` / `declined_non_integer_accumulator` for BOTH loops and its binary has 0 `karac_par_reduce` symbols; the i64 twin still queries outer-fanout/inner-memory-bound (the B-2026-07-31-13 expectations, unchanged) with 1 symbol; both print 42000. Non-vacuity by stash-revert (the query test FAILS pre-fix). Suites: lib 1024, concurrency 134, par_codegen 215, cli 550, codegen 2676 green; fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. New coverage: the test pair the filing asked for — par_codegen `test_ir_float_accumulator_reduction_never_fans_out` (+ an E2E value check) and cli `test_query_concurrency_float_accumulator_reduction_declines`, both on the float twin of MEMORY_BOUND_NESTED_LOOP_SRC.

tracker: src/interpreter/eval_call.rs (invoke_zero_arg_closure / eval_with_provider); typecheck gate for break/continue crossing a with_provider closure
title: `break` out of an enclosing loop from inside a `with_provider` closure body makes the interpreter return UNIT from an i64 function — the Break control flow escapes the loop machinery entirely — while codegen (post B-2026-07-31-11) runs the shape type-soundly with transparent-break semantics. The typechecker accepts the program, so one backend yields a wrong-TYPED value.
resolution: Root cause was one layer down from the filing: not the with_provider machinery but the interpreter's STATEMENT layer. A control-flow signal escaping an expression (the closure's `break` mapped through invoke_zero_arg_closure -> set_cf, or a `break` escaping a plain block expression -- no providers needed) reaches the enclosing statement as pending_cf plus a poison Unit value. `Let` and `Expr` statements propagate the pending signal before using the value, but THREE arms in eval_stmt.rs used the poison first: `Assign` stored it into the target (the filed symptom -- an i64 accumulator became Unit, so the fn returned `()` from an i64 signature), `CompoundAssign` fed it into eval_binary (Unit+Int internal error) and then stored, and `LetElse` fell into the else block spuriously on the pattern miss. Fix: the same propagate-before-use guard the `Let`/`Expr` arms already had (`if let Some(cf) = pending_cf.take() { return Err(cf) }`) added to all three arms -- after the Assign RHS eval, after each CompoundAssign operand eval, and after the LetElse scrutinee eval. Semantics decision recorded: option (b) -- unlabeled break/continue through the with_provider closure body are loop-TRANSPARENT (matches the typechecker's acceptance and codegen's lowering; the closure is an immediately-invoked body). A LABELED break through the closure boundary is rejected by the resolver ('undefined loop label') -- the de-facto rule is transparency for unlabeled signals only, and `return` stays closure-scoped (B-2026-07-31-16). Verified: the -11 ledger repro shape now prints 3 under interp == JIT (pre-fix `()` vs 3); a 4-shape probe (continue 8, inner-loop break 14, compound-assign 103, let-else 3) agrees across backends; the provider-free block-expr shape prints 3 on both; `v[9] += 1` OOB produces the clean runtime error instead of feeding poison to eval_binary. Non-vacuity by stash-revert: pre-fix interp printed `()`, `()`, and died on Unit+Int for the probes. Suites: interpreter 1343, cli 548, lib 1024, codegen provider subset 34, json/comptime*/protobuf*/example_packages/slice_aliasing all green; fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. Tests: 5 interpreter regressions (assign, continue, compound-assign, let-else, provider-free block-expr) + the stale codegen-side comment updated.

fix: 7cd69b0
tracker: src/codegen/provider.rs (compile_with_provider_body); return lowering in stmts/exprs for closure-scoped retargeting
title: `return` inside a `with_provider` CLOSURE body is closure-scoped per the typechecker and interpreter (`let x = with_provider[R](v, || { return 8; }); x + 1` typechecks and yields 9 under --interp), but codegen lowers it as a FN-level ret — so the non-tail shape still fails module verification. B-2026-07-31-11 fixed tail position, where the two semantics coincide observably.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: exposed by the B-2026-07-31-11 validation probes; pre-existing (the shape never compiled), unchanged by that fix.

REPRO:
  fn f() -> i64 with reads(Ctr) {
      let x = with_provider[Ctr](InMem { n: 8 }, || { return read(); });
      x + 1
  }
  --interp -> 9 (x = 8: the closure's return is CLOSURE-scoped; invoke_zero_arg_closure catches
               ControlFlow::Return and makes it the with_provider value)
  build    -> error: Module verification failed: "Terminator found in the middle of a basic block"
               (the inlined body's `return` emits scope cleanup + a fn-level `ret`; the let-site then
               stores the result after the terminator)

THE TYPECHECKER IS THE AUTHORITY and it says closure-scoped: the closure's return type is inferred from its `return` statements, the with_provider expression types as that R, and `x + 1` is accepted with x: i64. Contrast the BLOCK form, where `providers { } in { return E; }` types as `!` (fn-level return) and the non-tail misuse is rejected at typecheck — form B has no such gap; only the closure form does.

FIX SHAPE: lower `return` inside a with_provider closure body as a branch-to-merge with value, i.e. return-retargeting: a provider-body return-target stack entry (merge BB, result slot, cleanup depth recorded BEFORE the ProviderPop frame is pushed), and a Return compilation arm that — when the stack is non-empty — drains frames above the recorded depth (which includes the ProviderPop frame, so the pop fires), stores the value, and branches to the merge BB instead of emitting a fn-level ret. That is `compile_break`'s cleanup_depth pattern applied to return. CAUTION: the stack must be saved/cleared when codegen descends into a body compiled as a DIFFERENT LLVM function (real closures, par-branch workers, coroutines) or the retarget would branch across functions. Note `?` inside the body does NOT need this today only by accident: its Err early-return happens to feed an outer `?` in every probed shape, making fn-level and closure-scoped propagation observationally equal there — a non-tail `?` use diverges the same way plain `return` does.

Until fixed the failure stays LOUD (verifier error with the --interp hint), and tail-position early returns — the common shape — work (B-2026-07-31-11). Workaround: restructure to fall through or bind the value without an inner return.
resolution: Implemented closure-scoped return RETARGETING in codegen, per the filed fix shape. Authority settled first: design.md § with_provider signature types the body as a genuine closure (`f: Fn() -> T with R, E`) and the call returns `T`, so `return E` inside it returns from the CLOSURE — the interpreter already evaluated it that way; codegen's fn-level lowering was the outlier. Class upgraded codegen-gap -> miscompile: after the B-2026-07-31-17 terminator guard landed (e92c16b), the non-tail shape stopped verifier-failing and silently returned from the wrong scope (`let x = wp(..., || { return read(); }); x + 1` printed 8 under JIT/AOT vs interp's 9). Mechanism: a fn-tagged `ReturnRetarget` stack (state.rs) is live while a with_provider closure body inline-lowers (both trait-ful and ambient paths route through `compile_wp_closure_body_retargeted`; the `providers {} in {}` BLOCK form deliberately keeps fn-level lowering — its body is a block, not a closure). The `ExprKind::Return` arm, when the top entry's fn matches current_fn, compiles the value with the fn-level early-return path's move-out suppressions, does an emit-only `emit_scope_cleanup_from(depth)` drain (body locals innermost-first, then the ProviderPop frame at the recorded depth — the interpreter's order), and branches to a lazily-minted merge block with the value in an entry-block slot; `join_retargeted_returns` stores the fall-through tail into the same slot and positions at the merge. A body with no `return` never mints the block — zero IR overhead. Cross-function safety by fn-tagging (a `return` inside a real closure / par branch / mono body compiled while an entry is live runs with a different current_fn and takes the ordinary fn-level path) — no save/clear needed at the 7 mem::take sites. The fn-level machinery (ensures/invariants, ref-return, sret/arm64 coercion, coroutine completion) is skipped on retargeted returns: a closure return is not a function exit. Verified interp == JIT == AOT: the repro (9), conditional return + fall-through join (101/4), nested wp with inner-only return (1021), heap String moved through the closure return (got-v-42), valueless `return;` gating a side effect, body-local heap drop on both edges (501/5), and provider-stack health after a retargeted return (56). fix: e92c16b
tracker: src/codegen/stmts.rs (let-init of a terminated value expr; statement sequencing after a terminator)
title: A let-bound value expression that TERMINATES (`let x = { return 5; }; tail`) fails module verification under codegen — the let-site emits its store after the terminator — while --interp runs it (prints 5; the return is fn-scoped, matching the typechecker's `!` typing). No providers involved; the generic sibling of B-2026-07-31-16's shape.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while triaging B-2026-07-31-11's non-tail probes — the minimal no-provider control reproduces the same verifier error, proving the let-site half is generic.

REPRO:
  fn t() -> i64 {
      let x = { return 5; };
      7
  }
  --interp -> t() = 5 (the block's return exits the fn; the let never completes — fn-scoped, consistent
               with the typechecker typing the block `!`; the typechecker accepts the unused binding)
  build    -> error: Module verification failed: "Terminator found in the middle of a basic block"

MECHANISM: `compile_block_with_frame` correctly skips its drain when the body terminated, but the LET-SITE then unconditionally stores the (meaningless) result value into x's alloca and continues compiling subsequent statements into the already-terminated basic block.

FIX SHAPE: after compiling a let-init (or any statement-position expression), if the current insert block has a terminator, position the builder at a fresh unreachable continuation block before emitting the store / subsequent statements (the standard dead-block continuation LLVM frontends use), letting the verifier-clean dead code fold away. Alternatively suppress the store and skip remaining statements in the block; the dead-block route is simpler and composes with arbitrary consumers. LOW severity: the failure is loud with the --interp hint, the shape is rare (a binding whose initializer unconditionally returns), and no wrong answer is produced.
resolution: Fixed with terminator guards in codegen's statement lowering rather than a dead-block continuation: when a `let` init / assignment RHS TERMINATES the current block (a `!`-typed block expression `{ return 5; }`, an if/match whose every arm returns, a block that breaks the enclosing loop), there is nothing to bind and no live insertion point, so the arm now returns early instead of emitting the store/binop after the terminator. compile_block's existing per-statement terminator check then stops the enclosing block, exactly as it does for a bare `return;` statement -- no dead block needed, and dead-code emission stays zero. Guards added at four sites in src/codegen/stmts.rs: the generic Let path (after the shadow-dance state restore, before any further IR emission), the generic Assign path, and both reachable CompoundAssign paths (identifier target before the binop; field/index target before the place store). The guard is strictly fail-to-working: it fires only where verification previously FAILED, so no compiled-and-verified program changes behavior. Scope was wider than filed: the same crash hit `let x = if c { return 1; } else { return 2; };`, match-all-arms-return inits, `let x = { break; };` in a loop, and the Assign/CompoundAssign twins (`x = { return 5; };`, `x += { return 6; };`) -- pre-fix all six shapes verifier-failed (entry/ifmerge/cleanup.skip/match.merge/then labels), confirmed by stash-revert. Verified interp == JIT == AOT on an 8-shape probe (5, 1, 2, 5, 7, 10, 20, 3) plus the assign twins (5, 6); a live heap local at the terminating init is drained by the return edge (probe value 7; ASAN/LSan gate asan_terminated_let_init_frees_live_heap_local, 200 iterations, pre-fix non-compiling so non-vacuous). Suites: codegen 2662, par_codegen 213, memory_sanitizer 875, cli 548, lljit 16 green; fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. New coverage: 7 codegen E2Es + 1 ASAN case. Residual: a terminating RHS reaching the exotic entry-slot deref compound-assign paths (`*m.entry(k).or_insert(0) += { return 5; }`) is not guarded -- same crash class, vanishingly rare shape; extend the guard there if ever hit.

fix: 64c4df5
tracker: src/typechecker.rs (return-type check inside with_provider closure bodies)
title: The typechecker types a `return E` inside a `with_provider(p, || { ... })` closure body against the ENCLOSING FUNCTION's return type, not the closure's. design.md § with_provider signature types the body as `f: Fn() -> T with R, E` (a genuine closure), so returns are closure-scoped — the interpreter and (since B-2026-07-31-16) codegen both evaluate them that way. Spec-valid divergent shapes are rejected: `fn f() -> i64 { let s = with_provider[R](p, || { return f"x"; }); s.len() }` errors 'expected i64, found String' at the return, and a bare `return;` in a unit closure inside a non-unit fn errors 'expected return value of type i64'.
detail: Only type-CONVERGENT shapes (closure return type == enclosing fn return type) currently typecheck, which masks the closure-scoped semantics for every other case. The check should infer/verify the closure's own return type from its return statements plus its tail, per the design.md signature. SOURCE NOTE: found while fixing B-2026-07-31-16 — the String-returning and unit-returning probe arms were rejected and had to be rewritten convergent to exercise the codegen retargeting.
resolution: Scope was broader than filed: EVERY closure literal — not just with_provider bodies — typed its `return E` against the enclosing FN's return type (the closure arm in typechecker/exprs.rs never overrode the return context). Fixed with a collector, mirroring the existing `break_value_types` pattern: a new `closure_return_types: Vec<Vec<Type>>` stack pushes a frame around each closure body's inference; the `ExprKind::Return` arm, when a frame is active, INFERS the value and records its type in the innermost frame (bare `return;` records Unit) instead of checking against `current_return_type`; after body inference the closure arm unifies the collected types with the body's tail type — a `!` tail contributes nothing, conflicting concrete types are a hard error at the closure ('closure returns conflicting types: T vs U', ReturnTypeMismatch) — and the unified type becomes the closure's return type (feeding closure_type_with_capture_inference). `?` deliberately stays on the fn-level path — its closure-scoped typing is B-2026-07-31-19's scope. Verified: the divergent shapes now check and run — plain closure returning String in an i64 fn (6), wp closure returning String in an i64 fn (interp 4), bare `return;` in a unit wp closure gating a println (7 / seen-5 7) — and the conflict negative hard-errors. Non-vacuity by stash-revert (pre-fix: 'expected i64, found String' at the return; the new positive tests FAIL). Suites: typechecker 2122, interpreter 1345, effectchecker 409, ownership 381, codegen 2669, cli 549, par_codegen 213, memory_sanitizer 876 green; fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. Tests: 4 typechecker (3 positive via typecheck_ok, 1 conflict negative) + 2 interpreter. Residual filed as B-2026-07-31-20: codegen never registers heap-type metadata for a with_provider-result binding, so `s.len()` on a String wp result loud-bails under build/JIT ('no handler for method len') — PRE-EXISTING (the tail-String shape with no `return` anywhere bails identically on pre--18 main) and now more visible since -18 admits more such programs.

title: `?` inside a `with_provider` CLOSURE body lowers as a FN-LEVEL early return of the Err, but per design.md (body is `Fn() -> T`) and the interpreter it is closure-scoped: the Err becomes the with_provider call's VALUE. Observable silent miscompile when the wp result is handled locally instead of propagated: `fn probe(n) -> Result[i64,String] { let r = wp(p(n), || { let v = might_fail(read())?; Ok(v*10) }); match r { Ok(v) => Ok(v), Err(_) => Ok(-1) } }` — interp prints -1 on the failing input (match handles the Err), JIT/AOT return Err from the whole fn (unwrap_or prints -99). Repro: scratchpad b16_question.kara, verified 2026-07-31.
detail: Fix shape: extend the B-2026-07-31-16 ReturnRetarget to `compile_question`'s fail path — when a retarget is active (fn-tagged, same check as the Return arm), build the Err value in the CLOSURE's Result shape (not `fn_val.get_type().get_return_type()`, which is the enclosing fn's), do the bounded emit-only drain from the retarget depth (error-path variant so body-scoped errdefers fire), store to the retarget slot and branch to the merge. The blocker is knowing the closure's Result LLVM shape at the `?` site — the retarget entry could carry it, seeded from the typechecker's type for the wp call expression once B-2026-07-31-18 makes that type trustworthy for divergent shapes. Until then every `?`-in-wp-body program where the Err does NOT immediately feed an outer `?` of the same type misbehaves silently. The -11-era probes agreed by coincidence (the Err fed an outer `?` in a same-typed fn).
resolution: Implemented closure-scoped `?` end to end, building on the -16/-18/-20 machinery. TYPECHECK (the prerequisite the filing flagged): the ClosureReturnFrame collector (B-2026-07-31-18) now also collects `?` demands — resolve_question, when a closure frame is active, records the operand's Err type (Result form) or Option-ness on the innermost frame and returns the payload type, skipping the fn-return checks; after body inference, solve_closure_question_demands unifies the demands and pins the closure's Result[T, E] (substituting an unbound Err slot left by a bare `Ok(v)` tail — exactly the shape that used to fall to the Error-typed fallback), with hard errors for conflicting Err types, mixed Result/Option `?`, or a non-Result return with demands. Cross-error `From` conversions are NOT applied at closure `?` sites (exact match required; conversions + closure-body errdefer semantics deferred together as the closure-scoped error-path design). With the closure Result now concrete, the B-2026-07-31-20 wp-typing commits, and the recording moved to cover EVERY concretely-typed wp call (not just let RHS). CODEGEN: compile_question's fail path, when a wp ReturnRetarget is active, does the bounded emit-only drain from the retarget depth (body locals then ProviderPop; UserErrDefer skipped, see above), builds the Err in the CLOSURE's Result shape — derived from the retarget's result_type_expr, the wp call's typechecked TypeExpr threaded via the new call_span parameter — copies the payload words (multi-word String Errs round-trip), and routes to the retarget merge via the shared store_wp_retarget_value_and_branch (factored out of the `return` path). Verified interp == JIT == AOT: the filed repro prints 30/-1 on both (JIT was -99); Err String payload survives (err-big-9); the established `wp(...)?` continuation is unchanged (21/-1); a heap body-local live at the `?` drains on the fail edge (8/-1); the full 8-shape provider probe matrix and all -16/-17/-18 probes still match. ASAN/LSan: asan_wp_closure_question_fail_edge_frees_body_local (200 iterations, 2600). Suites: typechecker 2122, interpreter 1345, effectchecker 409, ownership 381, codegen 2676, cli 549, par_codegen 213, memory_sanitizer 877, lljit 16 green; fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. New coverage: 4 codegen E2Es + 1 ASAN case.

fix: a710d6c
title: codegen never registers heap-type metadata (string_vars / vec_elem_types / var_type_names) for a `let` binding whose RHS is a with_provider call, so method dispatch on the result loud-bails under build/JIT while check+interp run fine: `let s = with_provider[Ctr](p, || { f"v-{read()}" }); s.len()` dies with 'codegen: no handler for method len on variable s'. PRE-EXISTING and independent of the closure-return work — the closure's TAIL being a String (no `return` anywhere) reproduces on pre-B-2026-07-31-18 main ('All checks passed' + the same codegen bail).
detail: Scalar wp results work (no metadata needed); f-string interpolation of a String wp result works (display path). Only method dispatch on a heap-typed wp result is affected. Fix shape: the Let arm's binding registration needs the wp call's result type — codegen's established channel for this is a lowering-pass hint table derived from TypeCheckResult.expr_types (the typechecker records the wp call span's type, which since B-2026-07-31-18 is the closure's unified return type); alternatively compile_with_provider could report the body's Kara-level type back to the Let arm. Register string_vars/vec_elem_types/var_type_names accordingly, then the existing dispatch arms fire. SOURCE NOTE: surfaced by the B-2026-07-31-18 divergent-shape probes; minimized to the tail-only shape to prove pre-existence.
resolution: Root cause was one layer deeper than filed: the with_provider CALL ITSELF was never typed — `with_provider` is a recognized form with no ordinary env signature, so generic dispatch silently typed every wp call as `Type::Error` (tolerated downstream), and there was no real type for codegen to register. Fixed in three layers: (1) typecheck (expr_call.rs) — the existing wp-shape intercept now infers the closure argument and, when its return type is FULLY CONCRETE (no inference vars / unbound params / Error, checked recursively through the substitution map by `wp_ret_is_fully_concrete`), commits it as the call's type per design.md (`f: Fn() -> T` -> the call returns T); a non-concrete return (`Ok(v)` tail leaving `Result[i64, ?E]`) falls through to the old tolerant Error path so established `wp(...)?` propagation shapes keep working. (2) recording (items.rs Let arm) — a wp-call Let RHS with a concrete type records span -> TypeExpr into the new `wp_result_types` table (TypeCheckResult -> lowering.rs forward -> Program -> codegen field, the established hint channel). (3) codegen (stmts.rs Let arm) — an unannotated wp-call RHS reads the entry as an IMPLICIT TYPE ANNOTATION, making the binding behave exactly like `let s: T = wp(...)`, which already compiled correctly; all existing registration/dispatch machinery then fires. Verified: the tail-String repro prints 4 under JIT (was the loud bail), the closure-return String sibling and a Vec shape (len + indexing, 209) work, and the full earlier probe matrix (prov_probe 8 values incl. `wp(...)?` propagation, b16 retargeting shapes, b15 break shapes) is unchanged. Suites: typechecker 2122, interpreter 1345, effectchecker 409, ownership 381, codegen 2669, cli 549, par_codegen 213, memory_sanitizer 876, lljit 16 green; fmt + clippy (both cfgs) clean. New coverage: 3 codegen E2Es (tail-String, return-String, Vec). Residual: the non-concrete fallback keeps `?`-continuation shapes on the old Error-typed path — real bidirectional wp inference (and the `?` closure-scoping itself) remains B-2026-07-31-19.

title: Map/Set capacity grows linearly with TOTAL removals, not live size -- a sliding-window map leaks memory without bound (297 MB where Rust holds 2.4 MB)
detail:
`Map[K,V]` (and `Set[T]`, which lowers to a Map with val_size=0) never compacts in
place. `remove` tombstones a bucket (runtime/src/map.rs:250 -- len -= 1, tombstones += 1)
and the growth trigger counts tombstones (`(len + tombstones + 1) * 4 > capacity * 3`,
line 203), but the only response is `resize`, which ALWAYS doubles (line 260:
`let new_cap = self.capacity * 2`). `try_resize` doubles too (line 379). There is no
same-capacity rehash. So for any map whose inserted and removed keys DIFFER, capacity
ratchets upward once per ~0.75 * capacity removals and never comes back down --
asymptotically O(total removals), independent of how few keys are live.

MEASURED (scratchpad churn2.kara: insert key t, remove key t-1024, live size pinned at
1024 forever; peak RSS via /usr/bin/time -v):

  total ops    kara RSS     rust RSS (HashMap, identical program)
   1,000,000     20.6 MB      2.4 MB
   4,000,000     75.8 MB      2.4 MB
  16,000,000    297.1 MB      2.4 MB

Kara is exactly linear in the op count (4x ops -> 4x RSS); Rust is FLAT. At 16M ops that
is 124x Rust for a map holding 1024 entries. hashbrown handles this by rehashing in place
at the SAME capacity when tombstones dominate but the live count is low; kara has no such
path, so the table can only ever get wider.

THE TOMBSTONE-REUSE ESCAPE HATCH IS WHY THIS HAS GONE UNNOTICED. `find_insert_slot`
reuses the first tombstone in the probe chain and `insert` decrements `tombstones` when it
fills one (line 212). So if a removed key is later RE-INSERTED, it lands on its own
tombstone and nothing accumulates. That makes the bug invisible to any workload with a
bounded key range:

  * A first probe that removed key K then re-inserted K measured 2.4 MB -- FLAT, and it
    initially looked like a refutation. It was a bad probe.
  * kata #146 lru-cache churns ~12M removals but draws keys from a 4096-wide range, so
    keys repeat constantly and its measured peak RSS is 1.4 MB. It does NOT reproduce.

The bug needs distinct keys, which is the common case for a sliding window, a
time-series/session cache, a dedup set over a stream, or a BFS frontier keyed on a
monotone id -- i.e. exactly the long-running-service shapes where unbounded growth is
worst. A server holding a Map keyed on request id or timestamp grows until it is OOM-killed.

SEVERITY high because it is unbounded memory growth in a long-lived process, it is silent
(no diagnostic, correct results throughout), and the workaround -- periodically rebuild the
map into a fresh one -- requires the author to know about it.

SUGGESTED FIX: in `resize`, choose the new capacity from the LIVE count rather than
unconditionally doubling -- if `len * 4 <= capacity * 3` the live set already fits, so
rehash into a fresh table of the SAME capacity (dropping tombstones) instead of a wider
one. `rehash_from` already does exactly the right thing for either target and its safety
contract ("capacity strictly greater than the live count") still holds. That is a
same-capacity branch on one line of `resize`, not a redesign.

SOURCE NOTE: found while auditing the #146 C mirror for cross-language parity (kata task
58). The mirror uses a direct-index table, so it never modelled the runtime's growth; the
question of what the runtime ACTUALLY does led to the probes above. Related: B-2026-07-30-5
(VecDeque pop_front O(n)) is a separate structure with a separate cause.
resolution:
FIXED with the entry's own suggested shape, plus one hazard it did not name. `next_capacity()` (map.rs) picks the width when the load-factor trigger fires: SAME capacity when the live count is at or below ~3/8 of it, else double; `resize` and `try_resize` both consult it, and `rehash_from` drops every tombstone either way. The hazard: gating same-width on merely 'the live set fits under 3/4' leaves the compacted table right at the trigger, so the NEXT insert re-fires it — an O(len) rehash per insert at the boundary. The 3/8 headroom bound (half the trigger) guarantees each compaction buys ~3/8*capacity further operations, the same amortization doubling provides.

MEASURED, same sliding-window shape as the entry (window 1024, distinct keys, AOT against the rebuilt archives, peak RSS via getrusage — this container has no GNU time): 4M ops = 10.1 MB, 16M ops = 10.2 MB. FLAT (pre-fix: 75.8 MB / 297.1 MB — linear). The ~10 MB is the binary+runtime baseline, not the map.

GATE: `churn_with_distinct_keys_keeps_capacity_bounded` (runtime/src/map.rs tests) — 200k-op distinct-key churn, asserts len == window, capacity <= 8192, and a post-churn lookup. Non-vacuous: with unconditional doubling restored it fails at capacity 131072. Interp/JIT parity on a 50k churn (the interpreter's assoc-Vec Map has no tombstones and needed no change). Suites: runtime lib 360, codegen 2678, memory_sanitizer 878, cli, interpreter map slice; fmt + clippy (plain, llvm, wasm32-wasip1, wasm32-wasip1-threads) clean; lean/full/wasm/wasm-threads archives rebuilt (no new symbols — link-compatible, behaviorally fresh).

fix: ef85e85
tracker: src/codegen/runtime.rs (disarm_container_bodies_move_sources, disarm_container_bodies_for_arg), src/codegen/stmts.rs (Let/Assign hooks, tuple_var_elem_tes), src/interpreter/eval_stmt.rs (record_container_bodies_move_sources, rearm_container_bodies_for_name)
title: A whole-value MOVE of a binding carrying a container-bodies walk (enum payload / Vec element / tuple element) left the source's __karac_dropelems_* action armed: the payload's user Drop body fired TWICE, and under codegen the second fire read the cap-zeroed moved-from slot and printed a silently WRONG value (self.id == 0).
detail:
Found while scoping the B-2026-07-30-11 Option/Result leg: before adding a new container emission arm, the whole-value-move disarm surface of the three LANDED legs (enum b55743b-era, Vec b55743b, tuple 9edc231) was probed shape-by-shape. Every landed leg had the hole; the per-leg verifications covered pattern-destructure move-outs (match/if-let) and never the whole-binding moves.

MEASURED MATRIX on unmodified main, enum Slot.Held(Res{id}) with body println(90+self.id):
  let a2 = a;      interp 91 91 (double)      JIT 91 90 (second fire on ZEROED payload)
  let t2 = t;      interp 91 91 (tuple)       JIT 91    (dest cannot re-register)
  let v2 = v;      interp 92 92 (Vec)         JIT 92 92 (both walk the shared buffer)
  let c = make();  interp 93 93 (return-move) JIT 93
  f = g;           interp 97 97 (reassign)    JIT 97 97
  Box2 { s: d }    interp 94                  JIT silent (blanket name-keyed suppress)
  v.push(e)        interp 95                  JIT 90    (zeroed fire at NLL end)
  (h, 10) literal  interp 98                  JIT 90
  consume(b)       balanced on both (the one shape that already worked)
The '90' rows are the load-bearing ones: a resource's drop body running over a cap-zeroed payload is the silent wrong-value profile the B-2026-07-30-11 layer-3 note warned about — no crash, no sanitizer hit, wrong output. Direct struct rebinds were already balanced (B-2026-07-29-38's suppress_let_rebind_user_drop / suppress_user_drop_for_var), which is the proof the DISCIPLINE existed and the container actions were simply never wired into it.

FIX — one shared rule, applied uniformly on both backends: on a whole-value move, disarm the SOURCE's container-bodies action; the destination registers per its own let-site rule.
  CODEGEN: disarm_container_bodies_move_sources(rhs) — prefix-keyed retraction (suppress_container_elem_bodies_for_var) for a bare Identifier/SelfValue RHS, struct-literal field identifiers, and tuple-literal element identifiers — called from the Let and Assign arms; disarm_container_bodies_for_arg at the consuming-method arg sites beside each existing cap-zero (Vec push/push_back/try_push*/push_front/try_push_front/insert, Map/Set insert) — literally the 'action-removal beside each existing cap-zeroing call' the -30-11 entry prescribed. Plus tuple_var_elem_tes: element TypeExprs recorded at the tuple let-site so a bare rebind's DESTINATION can re-register its bodies walk (tuple_binding_elem_tes gains an Identifier arm) — without it codegen goes silent where the interpreter fires.
  INTERP: moved_out_container_bodies_bindings, a name set consulted by run_array_element_user_drops and run_enum_payload_user_drops AT FIRE TIME — a set rather than an action retraction because the source's Drop action may live in an OUTER block's cleanup vec (a move inside an if body), which a current-frame retain() cannot reach. Recorded at the Let/Assign arms, the return statement hook, the block-tail hook, and the same consuming-method arg sites; a struct whose FIELDS carry the drop routes to the existing moved_out_drop_field_bindings instead. Fresh let/assign of the same name REMOVES it from all three moved-out sets (rearm_container_bodies_for_name) — without the re-arm, a stale record from a previous same-named binding silences the new one, a bug the existing two sets share and now also avoid at these sites.
