Set/SortedMap shape (probe b198_d): the interpreter fires the source's value/element bodies at the source's death (`drop 3 s3` before the holder is even used) while AOT no-ops (the move nulls the source slot, so the registered walker's null check declines) -- a run-vs-build divergence. Vec shape (probe b198_b, `let v: Vec[Holder]` with `Holder { xs: Vec[Res] }` built from a local `xs`): BOTH backends fire the source `xs` walk at its death AND the owner-death walk -- the element's body prints twice, parity-equal but a semantic double (one value, two body fires). Root: the struct-literal-sources suppression at the Let registration (suppress_user_drop_for_var / interp moved_out_container_bodies_bindings) covers struct-typed sources but not container-typed sources moved into literal fields. Both symptoms verified PRE-EXISTING on main before the B-2026-08-02-18 fix (which only added the owner-death fires). Probes: b198_b, b198_d. FIXNOTE (2026-08-02): both legs fixed in 61e68c5. The two symptoms had ONE shape in common -- the source-disarm that the let-RHS position performs was missing at two other positions -- and the fix at each is the symmetric widening. LEG 1 (Set/SortedMap, interp-only divergence): the interpreter's `record_container_move_source_name` matched EnumVariant/Array/Tuple/Map but not Set/SortedMap/SortedSet, so `let h = SetHold { s: s };` left the source's element/value bodies walk armed and it fired early at `s`'s death; codegen never had the bug (the move nulls the source slot, so its registered walker's null check no-ops). LEG 2 (Vec, BOTH backends, parity-equal double): the consuming-ARG disarm handled only bare identifiers, so a container moved into a struct literal that is a CALL ARGUMENT -- `v.push(Holder { xs: xs })` -- kept the source armed and the element body printed TWICE (once at the source's NLL end, once at the container's death). The let-RHS control `let h = Holder { xs: xs };` was always correct, which is what localized it. codegen's `disarm_container_bodies_for_arg` gains the StructLiteral / Tuple arms its let-RHS sibling `disarm_container_bodies_move_sources` already had; the interpreter gains `record_container_move_sources_in_aggregate_arg`, called alongside the existing `record_ctor_arg_moves` at the Vec push / push_back / push_front and Map/Set insert sites. Aggregate shapes ONLY on both backends -- a bare-identifier arg keeps its existing whole-value channel untouched, so no identifier-arg behavior changes. Pins (ALL STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin container_into_literal_field_arg_single_fire (carries the always-correct let-RHS control in the same program) and interp set_and_sortedmap_into_literal_field_source_walk_suppressed. Probes b198_b / b198_d / b200_a all vg=0 parity=OK.

title: struct-field Set[DropStruct] leaks element heap; struct-field SortedMap[K, DropStruct] leaks the WHOLE handle tree at owner death
detail: Probe b198_d, verified pre-existing on main (pre-B-2026-08-02-18 build leaks identically): `struct SetHold { s: Set[Res] }` leaks the element's String buffer (2 bytes, valgrind 'definitely lost'), and `struct SmHold { m: SortedMap[i64, Res] }` leaks the ENTIRE map handle allocation tree (732 = 72 direct + 660 indirect bytes from karac_map_new) at owner scope exit -- the field's handle free appears not to be registered at all for the Drop-valued sorted shape. Binding-death siblings are clean (B-2026-08-01-18 fixed Set/SortedSet element buffers for BINDINGS; B-2026-07-16-1 covers Map fields with heap values) -- this is the struct-FIELD position for Drop-STRUCT-valued tables. Needs narrowing: which MapOrSet-arm derivation declines (element/val drop fn for a user-Drop struct value?) and whether plain Map[i64, Res] fields share it (probe b195_b/b198_f say no -- unsorted Map fields free correctly, so the Set element half and the SortedMap registration are the suspects). SOURCE NOTE: found sweeping table-field shapes after landing the -18 bodies walks. FIXNOTE (2026-08-02): fixed in 7cf6db5. Two stacked gaps in the struct-drop MapOrSet field machinery (synth_drop.rs), narrowed via IR (the SmHold drop fn did not exist at all; SetHold's called karac_map_free_with_drop_vec(handle, 0, 0)). (1) The FieldDrop name classifier matched Map/HashMap/Set/HashSet but NOT SortedMap/SortedSet, so a Sorted field classified None and its whole handle tree leaked -- the Sorted heads are now in the MapOrSet arm (the downstream helpers map_kv_type_exprs / set_inner_type_expr already handled them). (2) The field arm never derived a per-KEY drop fn, so Set elements' / Map keys' owned heap below the one-level overlay leaked; it now mirrors the B-2026-08-01-18 binding-death channel: map_val_drop_fn_for_type_expr(&k_te/elem_te) + emit_map_key_drop_fn_walk(handle, key_fn) before the handle free (null-guarded, so a moved-out field's nulled slot no-ops), with the key flag forced 0 when the walk owns the release. Flag derivation also resolves the field TE through the mono subst now (a generic parent's Map[i64, T] at T=String gets the value flag from the mono type). Pin: asan_struct_field_set_and_sortedmap_freed (STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix -- LSan caught both leaks) + e2e/interp bodies-order twins. Probe b199_a (field-insert shape) vg=0 parity=OK; b198_d memory now clean, its remaining divergence is exactly B-2026-08-02-20 (open).
fix: 7cf6db5

title: Vec[(T, ...)] with a heap/Drop-bearing TUPLE element: no element memory drop and no element bodies walk — heap leaks and the Drop body never fires (both backends)
detail: `let mut t: Vec[(Res, i64)] = Vec.new(); t.push((Res { id: 9, name: f"in{9}" }, 8));` with `Res { name: String }` and `Res: impl Drop` -- at `t`'s death NOTHING happens: no Drop body on either backend, and valgrind reports the name buffer 'definitely lost'. The container's per-element machinery does not descend into a TUPLE element on either axis -- not the memory drop (`emit_vec_elem_*` / the type-driven element free) and not the bodies walk (`emit_vec_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn`, whose targets are named struct / enum elements only; the tuple walker `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn` exists but nothing dispatches it per Vec element). The DIRECT control `Vec[Res]` is clean on both axes (probe b201_g: vg=0, body fires at the container's death), so this is specific to the tuple element type. SECONDARY SYMPTOM, same root: when the tuple is built from a NAMED source (`let r = Res { ... }; t.push((r, 8));`, probe b201_d) the container never takes drop responsibility, so the source binding's own-body action stays armed and fires at `r`'s NLL end instead -- under AOT over a slot whose String field has already moved into the tuple, printing `drop 4 ` with an EMPTY name while the interpreter prints the correct `drop 4 tt4` (a run-vs-build divergence), and the buffer still leaks. Probes: b201_f (inline element, no move -- the minimal repro), b201_d (named source), b201_g (clean control). CORRECTION (2026-08-02, same day as filing): this row's ORIGINAL title and detail attributed the bug to the B-2026-08-02-20 leg-2 aggregate-literal arg disarm picking the container-element channel where an own-Drop source needs the whole-value channel, and proposed a channel-selection fix. That diagnosis was WRONG and is retracted: probe b201_f shows the leak and the silence with an INLINE tuple element and no move at all, so the move-source disarm is not involved. Suppressing the source (the retracted fix) would have traded a mis-timed fire for total silence while leaving the leak -- worse, not better. Recorded rather than quietly edited because the ledger's value depends on a wrong root cause never outliving the probe that refutes it. FIX SHAPE (now): give the Vec element machinery a tuple arm on both axes -- dispatch the existing `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn` per element for the bodies walk, and the existing `emit_tuple_elem_drops` / `synthesize_tuple_drop_fn_te` for the element memory free -- then the named-source symptom resolves on its own, because the container becomes the owner the existing disarm already hands off to. FIXNOTE (2026-08-02): fixed in 98b3898, matching the CORRECTED diagnosis above (both axes of the Vec element machinery, not the move-source disarm). MEMORY: `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr` gains a tuple arm routing to the same TypeExpr-driven `synthesize_tuple_drop_fn_te` the struct-field NestedTuple arm uses -- gated on a leaf actually owning heap, so an all-scalar tuple element keeps its heapless fast path. BODIES: `emit_nested_vec_elem_bodies_fn` gains a tuple arm dispatching the existing per-tuple walker `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn` over the vec's elements; the loop is factored out as `emit_vec_elem_walker_loop` and shared with the Vec-of-Vec arm, since the element STRIDE TYPE was the only thing that differed. INTERP: the Vec element-bodies loop (`run_array_element_user_drops`) gains the matching Tuple arm, forward element order. DOWNSTREAM, as the corrected row predicted: with the container now the owner, the consuming-arg disarm can safely do its job, so its aggregate arms were promoted to the STRONG `suppress_user_drop_for_var` (already what the let-RHS `struct_lit_sources` path uses) and the named-source symptom -- AOT's early `drop 4 ` with an empty name plus the leaked buffer -- resolved without a separate mechanism; the interp twin adds the own-Drop source to `moved_out_user_drop_bindings`. Pins (ALL STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin vec_of_tuple_element_drop_bodies (inline AND named-source shapes in one program) and asan_vec_of_tuple_element_heap_freed. Probes b201_f/b201_d now vg=0 parity=OK with exactly one fire each; the Vec[Res] control b201_g is byte-identical. Suite 12838/0.

title: aggregate-literal source disarm has depth-1 / same-frame reach: a NESTED literal or a CALLEE-built literal fires the moved source's element bodies twice on both backends
detail: Two positions the B-2026-08-02-20 leg-2 disarm does not reach, each firing one logical value's Drop body TWICE (once at the moved source's death, once at the owner's) identically on both backends -- so parity diffing is blind to them and only a fire-COUNT oracle catches it. Memory is clean (vg=0) in both. (1) NESTED literal: `v.push(Outer { inner: Inner { xs: xs }, tag: 5 })` -- the walk inspects only the outer literal's immediate fields, and `inner` is a StructLiteral rather than an Identifier, so `xs` is never disarmed (probe b201_a). Depth-1 by construction in both backends' walkers (disarm_container_bodies_for_arg / record_container_move_sources_in_aggregate_arg and their let-RHS siblings). (2) CALLEE-BUILT literal: `fn mk(v: Vec[Res]) -> Holder { Holder { xs: v, tag: 9 } }` called as `let h = mk(xs);` -- the owned param `v` moves into the returned literal, but the param's element walk fires at the callee's exit as well as `h`'s at the caller (probe b201_b). The disarm machinery is per-frame and the tail-return path records the RETURNED expression's sources, not an owned param consumed by a literal inside it. SOURCE NOTE: both found immediately after B-2026-08-02-20 by counting body fires instead of diffing backends -- the same oracle that exposed -20's own leg 2. PROGRESS (2026-08-02): LEG 1 (nested literal) fixed in 249ac62; the row stays OPEN for LEG 2 (callee-built returned literal). Leg 1: both backends' disarm walks inspected the OUTER literal's immediate field values and matched only `Identifier`, so a field whose value is itself a literal terminated the search before reaching any source named inside it. Each side now collects sources through a recursive `collect_aggregate_literal_sources` (one per backend, deliberately mirrored -- they must enumerate the SAME sources or the disarm diverges), shared by the let-RHS and consuming-arg walks alike; recursion is bounded by the expression's finite structure and non-literal field values (calls, field accesses, indexes) are skipped since they are not move sources of a named binding, so nothing beyond the nesting gap is newly suppressed. Pins (both STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin nested_literal_move_source_disarm; probe b201_a now fires exactly once at the container's death. Suite 12841/0. LEG 2 REMAINS: `fn mk(v: Vec[Res]) -> Holder { Holder { xs: v, tag: 9 } }` called as `let h = mk(xs);` still fires twice (probe b201_b) -- the owned param `v` moves into a literal that crosses the frame boundary, and the disarm machinery is per-frame: the tail-return path records the RETURNED EXPRESSION's sources, not an owned param consumed by a literal inside it. That needs a callee-side rule (an owned param consumed by the returned value hands its walk to the caller's binding), which is a distinct mechanism from the same-frame recursion landed here.
fix: LEG 2 FIXED (b208): the callee-built returned literal turned out to be TWO separate defects, neither of them the per-frame tail-return rule the leg-2 note predicted. Probing the shape (b205/b206/b209, 20 programs) relocated the duplicate fire: it is the CALLER, not the callee. Under the caller-drops-the-owned-arg convention the caller fires the arg binding's body at the call -- correct when the value dies inside the callee (`fn consume(v) -> i64 { v.len() }` fires exactly once, and still does), a DUPLICATE when the callee hands that value back out. Two gaps made that happen. (a) `call_arg_flows_into_return` was consulted only by the memory and Option/Result channels; the `UserDrop` bodies channel never consulted it, so even the minimal `fn passthru(v: Vec[Res]) -> Vec[Res] { v }` over `let ys = passthru(xs);` double-fired -- the bare-identifier passthrough that `fn_returns_param` ALREADY recognized. The arg loop now retracts the arg binding's walk when the position flows into the return. (b) `fn_returns_param` recognized only a BARE-identifier return site, so `Holder { xs: v, tag: 9 }` was not a return site at all and (a) never engaged for the shape this row was filed for. Its `expr_is_ident` now also descends StructLiteral/Tuple return expressions -- the param crosses the frame boundary inside the aggregate exactly as it does bare. Because that predicate is the SHARED ast helper both backends gate on, one edit fixed codegen and interp together. The retraction is deliberately the CONTAINER-ONLY disarm, not the strong whole-value form: `karac_drop_<T>` is body + fields + MEMORY under one name, and an own-`Drop` struct param is entry-copied by the callee, so the strong form orphaned the caller's copy (measured: `fn mk(r: Res) -> Bx { Bx { r: r } }` went vg-clean -> 3-byte definite leak). `arg_is_entry_copied_heap_struct` cannot gate it -- that helper matches only literal and call args, and the shape here is a bare identifier. A `suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return` aggregate-literal arm was added too and does carry its own weight: it is what fixes a LOCAL source moved into a returned literal (probe b205_c), which was AOT-only-wrong. Interp twin: `record_passthrough_arg_moves`, routed through `record_container_move_source_name` so it records container/field walks and leaves an own-`Drop` binding armed, matching codegen leg-for-leg. RESIDUALS, both duplicate-body only and both vg-clean: (i) an own-`Drop` struct param returned inside a literal still fires twice (b205_b) -- the callee entry-copies it, so two real values exist and the two bodies match the two frees; (ii) a TRANSITIVE passthrough `fn outer(v) -> Holder { mk(v) }` (b206_i) fires twice, because recognizing it needs a program-level fixpoint over callees rather than the single-Function walk `fn_returns_param` performs. Pins (all STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin passthrough_arg_and_returned_literal_single_fire (bare passthrough + returned literal + a non-returning `consume` control that must keep its single fire), and asan passthrough_arg_returned_no_double_free for the leak side of the container-only choice.

title: interpreter misses a Map VALUE struct's Vec-field element bodies at owner death; AOT fires them
detail: `let mut m: Map[i64, Holder] = Map.new(); m.insert(1, Holder { xs: xs, tag: 7 });` with `Holder { xs: Vec[Res] }` and `Res: impl Drop` -- at `m`'s death AOT correctly prints the element body (`drop 3 mm3`, after the `m.len()` line) and the interpreter prints NOTHING. Memory is clean on both (vg=0); this is a missing interpreter walk, so it is a run-vs-build divergence in the SILENT direction on the interp side. The interpreter's Map-value walk (`run_map_val_user_drops` / the B-2026-08-02-18 field twin `run_field_map_val_user_drops`) dispatches a value struct's OWN body and recurses via `drop_user_drop_fields_of_value`, but the value here carries its Drop only through a Vec FIELD's elements -- the value-shape gate reaching that path declines for a struct with no own `impl Drop`. Codegen's side goes through the map val-drop fn, which already walks one container level. Probe b201_e. Adjacent to B-2026-08-01-23 (recursive element-bodies walkers) but at the Map-VALUE-struct-field position rather than a directly Vec-valued V. FIXNOTE (2026-08-02): fixed in 0a422d8. The defect was in the type-level GATE, not the walk: `type_name_runs_user_drop` (pattern_match.rs) recursed into a struct's fields by HEAD NAME only, so a `Vec[Res]` field read as head "Vec" -- no struct def, no Drop -- and `Holder { xs: Vec[Res] }` classified drop-free. `record_map_val_bodies_te`'s `qualifies` check consults that gate, so `map_val_bodies_tes` was never populated for the binding and `run_map_val_user_drops` returned early before reaching the walk that would have fired (the walk itself, and `value_runs_user_drop`'s field recursion, were already correct after B-2026-08-02-18). The field recursion now routes through a new `field_te_runs_user_drop` that sees ONE container level -- Vec/VecDeque elements, Map/SortedMap values, Set/SortedSet elements, and tuple elements -- which is the interp twin of codegen's `type_runs_user_drop` widening (B-2026-08-01-22 leg b, extended by B-2026-08-02-18). Both backends' type-level gates now classify identically, which is the property that keeps this class from re-diverging rather than just patching the one shape. Pin: interp map_value_struct_vec_field_element_bodies (STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix). Probe b201_c -- the last parity divergence left from the b201 fire-count round -- is now OK on both of its legs. Suite 12839/0.

title: MATCH-ARM LEG ONLY (displacement leg fixed in 21a1fb6): consuming an Option[Drop] payload via a match/if-let arm binding on a NAMED binding with a boxed payload runs no user `impl Drop` body under `karac build` while the interpreter runs it — a run-vs-build divergence on the shipping path. Blocker identified: the body's only fire path for a boxed payload is the box drop, which the arm's memory suppressors disarm, so the fix must key on that disarm rather than on arm consumption
detail: Found by drop_fuzz's drop-log oracle on the first run after B-2026-07-30-11 was closed (8de98fe). That closure fixed the struct-field-reassign shape on BOTH backends and the Option/match-arm shapes on the INTERPRETER only; codegen was left behind, which turns what used to be a shared gap into a run/build split. REPROS (all with `struct Tracked { tag: i64, name: String }` + `impl Drop for Tracked { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"D{self.tag}"); } }`, and `new_tracked` printing `N<tag>` before constructing):  (1) `let mut o: Option[Tracked] = Some(new_tracked(1,..)); o = None;` — interp `N1 D1`, build `N1` (no D1).  (2) `o = Some(new_tracked(2,..))` instead — interp `N1 N2 D1 D2`, build `N1 N2 D2` (the displaced tag-1 body never runs).  (3) `match o { Some(x) => { tracked_len(x); }, None => {} }` — interp `N1 42 D1`, build `N1 42`.  NOT A LEAK, and that is the point: a 50-iteration loop of shape (1) under ASan+LSan exits 0 with no report while printing 50 `N1` and zero `D1`. The heap is freed correctly; only the user-visible destructor side effect is lost, so no sanitizer can see this class and neither the memory_sanitizer suite nor the pre-widening drop_fuzz corpus would ever flag it. Severity high rather than medium (cf. B-2026-08-02-24, the mirrored interp-misses case) because here it is `karac build` — the shipping path — that silently skips the destructor while `karac run` is correct, so a program tested under the interpreter changes behaviour when shipped.  STILL CORRECT after 8de98fe, for contrast: `c.field = new_tracked(..)` on a struct field, and `for e in Vec[Tracked]`, both agree on both backends.  MEASUREMENT: 13 of 30 generated programs fire `seq:drop-never-ran` and `autopar:drop-never-ran`, 0 fire `interp:drop-never-ran` (was ~62% on all three surfaces before 8de98fe). drop_fuzz's KNOWN_OPEN pin is repointed from B-2026-07-30-11 to this entry.  CROSS-REF (added 2026-08-03 by the b211 sweep, NOT a claim on this row -- it stays yours): two more consuming-pattern positions show the same run-vs-build profile as repro (3) and are probably the same root cause, so whoever fixes this should check them in the same pass. (a) `if let Option.Some(r) = o { .. }` -- interp fires the body, AOT silent (probe iflet_bind). (b) `let H { r, t } = h;` destructuring a struct whose field is Drop-bearing -- interp prints `drop 1 x1`, AOT prints `drop 1 ` with an EMPTY NAME, i.e. the body DOES fire under AOT but reads a moved-from/stale slot, which is a wrong-value print rather than silence (probe struct_destr). (c) `let (a, b) = t;` destructuring a tuple with a Drop element -- interp fires, AOT silent (probe tuple_destr). All three are vg-clean. Separately filed and NOT part of this row: B-2026-08-03-1 (Option/Result payload silent in every NESTED position, both backends) and B-2026-08-03-2 (clear/truncate skip element bodies, both backends) -- those are parity-EQUAL and so a different class from this row's run-vs-build split. PARTIAL FIX: the DISPLACEMENT leg (`o = None`, `o = Some(fresh)`) is fixed — the Assign arm's value-enum leg excluded Option/Result by name, so an Option/Result sibling was added that calls `__karac_dropelems_opt_*` (bodies only, frees nothing by construction) on the old slot before the store, gated on `has_armed_container_elem_bodies` and on the RHS not mentioning the LHS (a roundtrip's bodies come from the NLL channel). Instantiation comes from `optres_var_payload_tes`. Regression: codegen.rs::e2e_option_displacement_runs_displaced_payload_user_drop. Suites green: codegen 2754, memory_sanitizer 908, interpreter 1418, par_codegen 224. Fuzzer rate 30/30 programs: 13 -> 11 firing per surface. RESIDUAL (match-arm leg, still open): `match o { Some(x) => .. }` on a NAMED Option binding with a payload wider than the inline area still runs no body under AOT. The inline arm in pattern_binding.rs declines on word count and the boxed arm on `pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_fresh_owning_temp`. Simply dropping that temp test DOUBLE-FREES (asan_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fire_once, whose `match c { Some(r) => { n = n + 1 } }` arm binds without consuming): only a CONSUMING arm retracts the source walk via `suppress_optres_payload_bodies_for_match`, so the registration must be conditioned on that retraction, and the consuming/non-consuming split (`pattern_consumes_field`) is not visible at pattern-binding time. Attempted and reverted; the gate now carries this reasoning as a comment. MATCH-ARM LEG, further diagnosis (2026-08-03, not landed): the residual is NOT simply a missing registration. For a BOXED Option payload the body already has a fire path — `emit_option_drop_fn` calls the payload's drop fn, which for a Drop-declaring type is the wrapper (body + memory) — and that is why `asan_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fire_once` double-freed the moment the fresh-temp gate was dropped: its `match c { Some(r) => { n = n + 1 } }` leaves the box alive to scope exit, so the box drop runs `Full.drop` (`self.buf.clear()`) and a binding-side walker makes it twice. In the silent shape (`match o { Some(x) => x.tag }`) the arm's memory suppressors (tag-zero / cap-zero) disarm the source's box drop so it cannot double-free the moved payload — and with it the only fire path disappears. So the two cases differ by whether the box drop was suppressed, not by whether the arm consumes: a correct fix has to register the binding-side bodies walk exactly when the source's box drop was disarmed, which is a different signal from `pattern_consumes_field` and from `pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_fresh_owning_temp`. Threading it is the remaining work.  CROSS-REF ADDENDUM (added 2026-08-03 by the b215 sweep, again NOT a claim -- the row stays yours): a DISCRIMINATOR for repro (3). The `Result` sibling of that exact shape is CORRECT on both backends -- `let o: Result[Res, i64] = Result.Ok(Res { .. }); match o { Result.Ok(r) => { println(r.id) } .. }` prints the body at the arm's end under AOT and under `karac run` alike (probe b215/n2), while the Option spelling prints nothing under AOT (probe b215/n1). Both are vg=0, so this is body-registration, not memory. Whatever registers the consuming arm binding's own body fires for a Result payload and not for an Option one; that asymmetry looks like the shortest path to the root cause and it needs no tuple, no boxing question, and no fuzzer to reproduce.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 542d7d7) -- the match-arm leg, and with it the whole row. FIRST, A CORRECTION to this row's own 2026-08-03 cross-ref addendum, which read the `Result` spelling of repro (3) as CORRECT and the `Option` spelling as broken and called that asymmetry the shortest path. It is not an Option-vs-Result asymmetry at all -- it is WIDTH. The inline payload area is 3 words for `Option` and 5 for `Result`, so `Res { id: i64, name: String }` (4 words) is BOXED in an Option and INLINE in a Result; the two probes differed by which side of the boxing threshold they landed on, not by which enum they used. Measured all four corners: Option/3-word payload FIRES, Option/4-word SILENT, Result/4-word FIRES, Result/7-word SILENT. Same trap as the analogue probe that mis-cleared B-2026-08-03-3 leg B -- an Option/Result pair is only a controlled comparison when the payload sits on the same side of both thresholds.  ROOT CAUSE, as this row's own further-diagnosis predicted: for a boxed payload the source binding's `__karac_dropelems_opt_*` walk is the body's ONLY fire path (the box drop calls the payload's MEMORY-only drop since B-2026-08-03-10), and a consuming arm retracts that walk via `suppress_optres_payload_bodies_for_match` -- a Binding sub-pattern counts as consuming by definition. The inline bind-site arm had already declined on word count and the boxed one on `pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_fresh_owning_temp`, so the body ran nowhere.  THE FIX is a RE-HOMING, not a new registration, and that distinction is the whole content of it. `scrutinee_armed_payload_bodies_action` samples the source's armed `(slot, walker)` ABOVE the arm loop -- before any suppressor runs, so every arm reads the same pre-retraction state -- and the bind site re-registers that SAME walker against that SAME SOURCE SLOT under the arm binding's NAME. Renaming is what moves the fire from the source's death to the binding's, which is where the interpreter puts it.  WHY NOT THE BINDING'S OWN COPY: the first attempt registered `__karac_dropbodies_only_<T>` over the arm binding's reconstructed payload alloca, and that DOUBLE-FREED every consuming shape whose Drop body MUTATES a heap field. A boxed payload's memory stays owned by the box; the binding holds a copy of `{ptr,len,cap}`. `self.buf.clear()` run against the copy frees the buffer and zeroes the COPY's cap while the box keeps the stale pointer, and the scope-exit box drop frees it again (measured: 600 invalid frees over 200 iterations, probes b225/cl2, as_a/b/c). Running the source's walk instead puts the mutation in the box -- the storage the later free reads -- and all of it goes vg=0. The read-only Drop bodies the E2E pins use cannot see this class at all, which is why the ASan pin's payload deliberately mutates.  A SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT fell out of the same reasoning and is filed as B-2026-08-04-1: the FRESH-TEMP route still registers the bodies-only walker over the binding's copy, so `match opt(i) { Some(r) => .. }` with a mutating body double-frees. Pre-existing (stash-proven identical before this fix), untouched here, and the fix shape is known -- thread the staged temp's slot the way this leg threads the source's.  VERIFIED on 27 probes, every one `SAME` between AOT and `karac run` and vg=0: named match / if-let / let-else / boxed-Result / guard arm / loop / move-out-to-fn-arg, plus the three CONTROLS that must not change -- non-consuming `Some(_)` (source keeps its walk), inline payload (the pre-existing arm), and no-match-at-all. A 21-probe stash diff attributes exactly 7 output changes to this commit, all of them a missing body appearing; nothing else moved. `let … else` needed the re-homing too and is the reason the subject had to be the source slot rather than a bodies-only walker on the copy: its binding lands in the ENCLOSING frame, and only a `__karac_dropelems_` action passes `fire_due_user_drops`' NLL gate, so the body printed after the rest of the function instead of at the binding's death.  KNOWN RESIDUALS, both parity-EQUAL (so not run-vs-build, and out of this row's scope): a struct-PATTERN destructure of a boxed payload (`Some(Res { id, name })`) runs no body on either backend (probe b225/ p10), and an OWNED-PARAM scrutinee runs none either (probe b225/p4) -- the callee is correctly silent under caller-retains, but the caller never fires it. Separately, moving the arm binding OUT (into a struct literal, or as the match's tail value) double-frees under AOT with a READ-ONLY body, on both named and fresh-temp scrutinees, pre-existing and unaffected by this commit -- filed as B-2026-08-04-2.
fix: 542d7d7 (src/codegen.rs, src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs, src/codegen/runtime.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_named_optres_boxed_payload_arm_runs_user_drop_body -- stash-proven RED, missing D1/D2/D3/W4 -- its interpreter ORACLE twin interpreter.rs::test_named_optres_boxed_payload_arm_runs_user_drop_body with a byte-identical expectation, and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box, the guard for the mutating-body double-free the first attempt caused)

title: a TUPLE binding whose element is a container of Drop values (`let t = (xs, 9)`, xs: Vec[Res]) runs no Drop body and leaks the elements under AOT while karac run is correct
detail: `let t = (xs, 9);` with `xs: Vec[Res]` and `Res: impl Drop`: AOT prints NOTHING and leaks 3 bytes per live element; `karac run` fires the body once, correctly. A run-vs-build divergence AND a leak, in the plainest shape in the family -- no function call, no generics, no move-into-a-call. Two independent gaps stacked on one root cause. BODIES: `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn` accepted an element only if it was a `Path` naming a type in `struct_types`, so `Vec[Res]` read as head "Vec", matched nothing, `targets` came back empty and the whole walker declined -- the tuple-element peer of the one-container-level widening struct FIELDS already got in B-2026-08-02-18 / -22. MEMORY: the let-site prefers the LLVM-type aggregate drop whenever `aggregate_has_heap_field` sees a vec-struct field, and that walk frees the element Vec's BUFFER shallowly, leaking each live `Res`'s String; the TypeExpr-driven path that can reach element leaves sat in an `else if` it never reached. UNDER BOTH: `infer_arg_elem_te` builds a head-name-only TypeExpr (`generic_args: None`), so the element type was bare `Vec` at every decision point -- another facet of declared-name erasure, this time at the tuple-literal inference step rather than at a generic struct's field list. CONTROLS that localize it: a tuple with an INLINE direct Drop element (`(Res { .. }, 9)`) was already correct, so tuples were not wholesale broken; a STRUCT with the same `Vec[Res]` field was already correct, so the container widening existed everywhere except tuple elements. Probes b206_l, b207_o, b207_p, b205_f.
fix: Three edits, one per gap. (1) `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn` now selects targets via a new TypeExpr-keyed gate `elem_te_runs_user_drop` (the codegen twin of interp's `field_te_runs_user_drop`, assembled from the same three head extractors that widened `type_runs_user_drop` for struct fields) and dispatches each element through a new `emit_tuple_elem_bodies_at` carrying the same four legs the struct-FIELD walker has -- direct struct, Vec/VecDeque element, Map/Set value, nested tuple -- so a tuple element and a struct field of the same type now run the same bodies. Its memoization key moved from the element HEAD NAME to the full mangled TypeExpr, because `(Vec[Res], i64)` and `(Res, i64)` both keyed `0_Res` and the second shape would have reused the first's walker; a direct struct element still mangles to its bare name, so existing symbol names are unchanged. (2) `emit_tuple_elem_drops`' Vec arm diverts to the recursive `karac_drop_Vec_<E>` (drain live elements, then free the buffer) when the Vec's element owns heap, and the let-site prefers the TypeExpr path over the LLVM-type path when a new `tuple_elem_needs_deep_drop` predicate says an element would otherwise be freed shallowly. String and `Vec[primitive]` keep the shallow path, where the buffer free alone is exact. (3) `tuple_binding_elem_tes` refines each literal element through a new `refined_tuple_literal_elem_te`, which rebuilds `Vec[E]` for a collection BINDING from `var_type_names` + `var_elem_type_exprs` and takes a free-function CALL's declared return type verbatim, falling back to the old head-name inference for anything else -- kept local to the tuple let-site rather than changing `infer_arg_elem_te`, which has many other callers. Pins: e2e + interp twin tuple_binding_container_element_drop (all three element sources: named binding, fresh call, annotated) and asan tuple_binding_container_element_heap_freed. The e2e and asan pins were STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix; the interp twin PASSES pre-fix and is deliberately kept, since the interpreter's value-driven tuple walk never lost the element type and the twin pins the parity the fix restored.

title: an own-Drop source moved into a let-RHS TUPLE keeps its own body armed: fires twice on both backends, and under AOT the first fire reads the moved-from slot
detail: `let r = Res { id: 1, name: f"a{1}" }; let t = (r, 9);` fires `r`'s Drop body TWICE on both backends -- and under AOT the first fire runs over the moved-from slot, printing an EMPTY name (`drop 1 ` instead of `drop 1 a1`), so it is a wrong-value print as well as a duplicate. Memory is balanced (vg=0), which is why it survived leak checking. B-2026-08-02-22 promoted the aggregate arms of the consuming-ARG disarm (`disarm_container_bodies_for_arg`) to the strong `suppress_user_drop_for_var` for exactly this reason at the push/insert position, and the let-RHS sibling `disarm_container_bodies_move_sources` was not promoted with it -- it still used the container-only `suppress_container_elem_bodies_for_var`, which removes element walks but leaves the binding's own `karac_drop_<T>` action armed. The interpreter had the matching hole one level down: `record_container_move_source_name` deliberately skips an own-`Drop` struct ("handled by `suppress_let_rebind_user_drop`'s action retraction"), but that retraction only sees a BARE rebind `let b = a;`, never a source consumed by a literal. The inline control `let u = (Res { .. }, 4);` already fired exactly once, which is what proves the tuple binding owns the body and makes the promotion safe rather than a trade. Probe b207_n. Found by the fire-count oracle while probing B-2026-08-02-23 leg 2.
fix: Codegen: the TUPLE arm of `disarm_container_bodies_move_sources` now uses the strong `suppress_user_drop_for_var`, matching its consuming-arg sibling. Interp: the tuple arm of `record_container_bodies_move_sources` routes through the existing `record_container_move_sources_in_aggregate_arg`, the consuming-arg helper that already put own-`Drop` sources on `moved_out_user_drop_bindings`; the two positions move the value identically, so they now record identically. CORRECTION ON THE RECORD: the first attempt promoted the STRUCT-literal arm alongside the tuple arm, on the reasoning that it would be a no-op because the let-site's `struct_lit_sources` block already retracts the same names. That reasoning covered only the BINDING path. On the WILDCARD path (`let _ = W { r: r0 }`) `struct_lit_sources` never runs, and unlike the tuple position there is no struct-literal discard walker to take over, so the promotion silenced r0's body outright -- caught by `e2e_wildcard_let_discard_place_shapes_single_fire`, the existing pin for exactly that position, which went RED in the full suite. The struct-literal arm therefore stays on the container-only form on BOTH backends, and the asymmetry is deliberate: the tuple arm is safe only because its wildcard position has an owner (`track_discarded_tuple_elem_bodies`) and the struct one does not. GENERALIZABLE: when promoting a disarm to the strong whole-value form, check every POSITION that reaches the same call site -- binding, wildcard discard, arg -- not just the one in the repro; a disarm is only safe where some other channel is provably the new owner. Pins (both STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin tuple_literal_own_drop_source_disarm, each carrying the inline-element control alongside the named-source case so a future change cannot fix the duplicate by silencing both.

title: a call result consumed directly as another call's argument (`use_it(mk(xs))`) leaks the inner temp's heap under AOT and fires its Drop body at a different time than karac run
detail: `fn mk(v: Vec[Res]) -> Holder`, `fn use_it(h: Holder) -> i64`, called as `println(use_it(mk(xs)));`. The intermediate `mk(xs)` result is never bound, so no binding-death channel owns it. AOT LEAKS the element's String (vg=99, 3 bytes definitely lost) and fires the body AFTER the println; `karac run` fires it BEFORE, and does not leak. So: a real leak on one backend plus a run-vs-build TIMING divergence on the shared body. Fire COUNT is now 1 on both (it was 2 on both before B-2026-08-02-23 leg 2 landed, which is what uncovered the residual underneath). The nested-call temp position is the one slot in this family with no owner at all -- neither the caller's binding channel (there is no binding) nor the callee's frame (which correctly hands the value out). Probe b206_h. NOT a regression from leg 2: the same vg=99 was present before that fix, which only removed the duplicate fire layered on top of it.
fix: LEAK LEG FIXED (b210). The SHAPE-2 fn-call arm of `track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg` registered the field-BODIES walk and then RETURNED, omitting the memory drop that its struct-LITERAL sibling registers for the identical value -- the two arms differ only in how the temp was produced (a call vs an inline literal), which is not a reason to own it differently. That is why the body printed normally while nothing freed the buffer: a leak that produces CORRECT OUTPUT, so neither parity diffing nor the fire-count oracle could see it; only valgrind did. The arm now mirrors the sibling exactly: the same `needs_memory_drop` gate (LLVM-visible heap field, or a copy-supported struct with a drop-heap field TypeExpr), `track_struct_var` pushed FIRST and the bodies walk second, since the frame drains LIFO and the body must run before the fields it reads are freed. Sound for the same reason the sibling is: the callee entry-copies a copy-supported struct -- `arg_is_entry_copied_heap_struct` already resolves exactly this Call shape through `fn_return_type_names` -- so the caller temp is an INDEPENDENT buffer and freeing it cannot touch the callee's copy. Fixing the order also settled the timing divergence for the bound-result shape (`let n = use_it(mk(xs));`), which now matches `karac run` on both the body position and the value. RESIDUAL (timing only, no leak, tracked here): when the consuming call is NESTED INSIDE another call -- `println(use_it(mk(xs)))` -- AOT fires the temp's body at STATEMENT end (after the enclosing println emits) while the interpreter fires it when the inner call completes (before). Both are self-consistent notions of the temp's death and both are leak-free; reconciling them means changing one backend's temp-drop timing convention wholesale, which is a much larger change than this leak fix and is deliberately not attempted here. Statement-end is codegen's established convention for temps (B-2026-08-01-5). Pins: e2e + interp twin nested_call_temp_owned_arg_drop (bound result, bare-statement discard, and an inner call taking no argument -- the three shapes where both backends agree) and asan nested_call_temp_owned_arg_freed for the leak itself. The e2e and asan pins were STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix; the interp twin passes pre-fix and is kept to pin the order codegen now has to reproduce.

title: an Option/Result payload never runs its user Drop body in ANY nested position — struct field, Vec element, Map value, tuple element — on BOTH backends; only a direct binding works
detail: `Option[Res]` / `Result[Res, E]` where `Res: impl Drop` runs the payload's Drop body ONLY when bound directly (`let o: Option[Res] = Some(...)` fires correctly). In every NESTED position the body is silent on BOTH backends: struct field `H { o: Option[Res] }` (probe o1), struct field `Result[Res, i64]` (o2), Vec element `Vec[Option[Res]]` (o3), Map value `Map[i64, Option[Res]]` (o4), tuple element `(Option[Res], i64)` (o5). Memory is clean in all five (vg=0), so no sanitizer sees it, and both backends agree, so parity diffing sees nothing either -- the parity-equal class only a fire-COUNT oracle catches. ROOT CAUSE (predicted, to be confirmed at fix time): the one-container-level widening that Vec/VecDeque, Map/SortedMap, Set/SortedSet and tuple elements received in B-2026-08-01-22 leg b, B-2026-08-02-18 and B-2026-08-02-26 was never extended to Option/Result. The three codegen gates (`type_runs_user_drop`'s field walk, `elem_te_runs_user_drop`, and the per-position dispatch in `emit_user_drop_field_bodies_fn` / `emit_tuple_elem_bodies_at` / `emit_nested_vec_elem_bodies_fn` / `emit_map_val_user_drop_bodies_fn`) each enumerate a fixed head-name set that omits Option and Result, and the interpreter's `field_te_runs_user_drop` mirrors the same set. A payload-bodies walker ALREADY EXISTS for the direct-binding position (B-2026-07-30-11's Option/Result leg, `track_discarded_optres_payload_bodies` and siblings), so this is expected to be a wiring gap rather than missing machinery. SEVERITY high: `Option[T]` is the idiomatic way to hold an optional resource, so a Drop-bearing type in an Option field -- a connection handle, a file, a lock guard -- silently never releases, and the shape is common rather than exotic. SOURCE NOTE: found by a 30-shape valgrind + parity + fire-count sweep (probe b211) run after B-2026-08-02-28 closed; 7 of 30 shapes were anomalous. NOT the same as B-2026-08-02-25, which is a run-vs-build split on Option DISPLACEMENT and match-arm consumption -- this one is both-backends-silent and is about nesting position, not consumption.
fix: Root cause confirmed as predicted -- a wiring gap, not missing machinery: the tag-guarded payload walker `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn` already existed for the direct-binding position and simply was not reachable from any nested one. Option/Result needed adding at THREE layers, and finding all three is the substance of the fix: (1) the REACHABILITY gates -- a new `optres_payload_heads` extractor (the Option/Result sibling of `vec_field_elem_head` / `map_or_set_field_val_head` / `tuple_field_elem_heads`, and the first to return MULTIPLE heads, since either of Result's arms can be live and carry a Drop) wired into `type_runs_user_drop`'s field walk and into `elem_te_runs_user_drop`; (2) the field-INDEX selector `user_drop_field_indices_mono`, whose omission meant widening the gate alone still left the field out of the walk set; (3) the per-position DISPATCHERS -- an Option/Result arm in `emit_user_drop_field_bodies_fn`, in `emit_tuple_elem_bodies_at`, in `emit_nested_vec_elem_bodies_fn` (striding by the Option LLVM type via the shared `emit_vec_elem_walker_loop`), and in `emit_map_val_user_drop_bodies_fn`. A fourth gap was DECLARED-NAME ERASURE again: `Option.Some(x)` in a tuple literal is a ctor Call naming no function, so `refined_tuple_literal_elem_te` fell through to head-name inference and the element read as bare `Option`; it now rebuilds `Option[P]` from the ctor's own argument. INTERPRETER (needed independently, and mid-fix AOT briefly fired while interp did not -- a divergence that would have been worse than the original both-silent bug): the `field_te_runs_user_drop` gate learned to check a RANGE of generic args rather than one index; `field_value_carries_user_drop` gained an Option/Result payload arm; and FOUR separate walks needed the arm because this side splits them differently than codegen does -- struct field, Vec element, the field-level map walk AND the binding-level map walk, plus the binding-level map REGISTRATION gate (`record_map_val_bodies_te`), which is the gate-before-walk shape B-2026-08-02-24 already taught: the walk was correct and simply never armed. All routed through `run_discarded_value_user_drops`, the value-driven recursion this side already used for these built-ins. UNMASKED, NOT INTRODUCED -- filed as B-2026-08-03-3: two positions (a `Result[Res, i64]` struct field, and a tuple-held `Option[Res]`) go vg-clean -> vg=99 with this fix. Verified latent rather than regressed with `valgrind --trace-malloc=yes` on the stashed build: the pre-fix binaries allocated the payload buffer ZERO times, LLVM having elided a heap value nothing ever read. Making the body read `self.name` is what brings the allocation to life and exposes a free that was always missing. Same discriminator, same conclusion as B-2026-08-02-19. The full suite is green (6867/0) with those leaks present, so nothing existing depended on the silence. Pins (all three STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin optres_payload_bodies_in_nested_positions, covering all four nested positions plus a `None` control that must stay silent; asan optres_payload_nested_positions_clean, deliberately scoped to the three positions whose memory was already correct, so it guards the new walks without baking in the B-2026-08-03-3 leaks.

title: a container element destroyed WITHOUT being bound never runs its Drop body — clear, truncate, discarded remove/swap_remove/pop, and whole-container reassign; two of those also LEAK, and two more disagree between backends
detail: SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-03 (the original filing understated this badly: it named only clear/truncate, claimed 'both backends agree' throughout, and missed the leaks entirely). A follow-up sweep over the whole removal surface shows one invariant behind all of it -- an element destroyed with NO BINDING to receive it never runs its Drop body -- and three distinct defect classes within that. Probes b211/k*, b211/m*, one `Res { id, name: String }` element unless noted.  CLASS 1, body silent, memory clean, both backends: `v.clear()` with 2 elements -> 0 fires (k1); `m.clear()` -> 0 (k2); `v.truncate(1)` from 2 -> the REMOVED element is silent while the survivor's body still fires at scope exit, so the count looks plausible and is wrong (k3/m6); `v = w` whole-container reassign -> the DISPLACED old element is silent, only the new one fires at scope exit (m7).  CLASS 2, body silent AND LEAKS, both backends: a DISCARDED `v.remove(0);` (m1, vg=99) and `v.swap_remove(0);` (m3, vg=99). Binding the result fixes both -- `let r = v.remove(0);` fires once and is vg-clean (m2) -- which localizes it to the discard position rather than the removal itself.  CLASS 3, RUN-VS-BUILD DIVERGENCE: a discarded `v.pop();` (m4) and `m.remove(5);` (m5) fire correctly under AOT and are SILENT under the interpreter. This class was entirely absent from the original filing, which asserted the opposite ('both backends agree'); it is the shipping-path-correct direction, unlike B-2026-08-02-25.  CONTRAST that still holds: `let p = v.pop();` and `let g = m.remove(k);` -- any BOUND removal -- are correct on both backends, so the single-element machinery has the right ownership wiring and it is specifically the unbound/bulk positions that lack it. SEVERITY raised low->high: `clear()` on a Vec of connection handles silently skips every close, class 2 is a real leak on the shipping path, and class 3 is a run/build split. SOURCE NOTE: class 1 found by the b211 fire-count sweep; classes 2 and 3 only surfaced when the removal surface was enumerated systematically against BOUND controls -- the bound/unbound contrast is what made the single root cause visible. `Set.clear()` does not exist yet (typecheck: no method 'clear' on type 'Set'), so that arm is untested rather than passing.
fix: CLASS 3 FIXED (b213), row stays OPEN for classes 1 and 2. The interpreter's bare-statement discard arm (`StmtKind::Expr`'s MethodCall branch) only ever admitted USER methods, while the `let _ = v.pop();` form went through `discard_rhs_produces_owned_value`, whose method list already covers the builtin container removals -- so the two DISCARD STATEMENT SHAPES disagreed with each other, and against codegen, which fires for both. The bare arm now runs the same walker on the same method list. DELIBERATELY GATED to an Option/Result-shaped result, which is exactly codegen's current reach: its discard registrar is the optres payload walker and the only receiver it resolves a type for is Map-shaped, so `v.pop()` and `m.remove(k)` are covered there while `v.remove(i)` and `v.swap_remove(i)` (bare `T`) are not. The first attempt used the unrestricted list and FLIPPED those two from both-silent to interpreter-fires/AOT-silent -- strictly worse, since AOT also leaks them. Caught by re-running the probe matrix before committing; the gate is what keeps this a pure divergence-removal. GENERALIZABLE: when closing a run-vs-build split by moving one backend, check every shape the change admits, not just the reported one -- a fix that widens a gate can convert a shared gap into a divergence, which is the worse failure mode. STILL OPEN: class 1 (clear / truncate / whole-container reassign -- body silent, memory clean, both backends) and class 2 (discarded `v.remove(i)` / `v.swap_remove(i)` -- body silent AND leaking, both backends). Class 2 needs codegen's discard registrar to resolve a Vec receiver's element type and to own the removed element's memory, which is the substantive remaining work. Pin: interp `bare_statement_container_removal_discard_fires` (STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix), carrying the bound-removal control alongside the two fixed shapes. CLEAR FIXED (b213b), covering the `clear()` half of class 1 on both backends. Both arms turned out to do all the MEMORY work and none of the body work, which is exactly why the shapes were vg-clean and silent: codegen's `Vec.clear` went straight to `emit_vec_drop_fn` (drain + free) and its `Map.clear` to the shared rc-dec walks plus the per-value drop fn, while the interpreter's arms called Rust's `Vec::clear` / replaced the table with an empty one -- operations that reclaim storage and know nothing about Kara destructors. Each now runs the SAME element/value bodies walker the binding-death path uses, BEFORE the memory work on the codegen side (the walker frees nothing, so it cannot disturb the drop, and running it first is what lets a body read the fields it prints) and after the container is emptied on the interpreter side (so no read guard is live while a body runs, in case a body touches the container). Pins (both STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin container_clear_runs_element_drop_bodies, carrying a two-element Vec (order matters), a Map, and a clear-then-reuse control that checks the buffer is still usable and the replacement element still fires at scope exit. CLASS 1 REMAINDER, still open: `truncate(n)` (the REMOVED tail is silent while the survivors still fire, so a naive whole-container walker would be wrong here -- truncate needs a RANGED walk over [n, len), which is why it was not folded into this change) and whole-container reassign `v = w` (the displaced old container's elements). Class 2 (discarded Vec remove/swap_remove: silent AND leaking) is untouched and remains the substantive work. CLASS 2 FIXED (b214). A discarded `v.remove(i);` / `v.swap_remove(i);` hands the element back BY VALUE with nothing to receive it, and the discard battery could not tell what it was holding: its method arm resolves a return type through `fn_return_type_names`, keyed `Type.method`, and BUILTINS have no entry there (they are not declared impl methods). So the registration was skipped entirely -- no body, no free. The arm now falls back to the receiver's recorded element TypeExpr (`var_elem_type_exprs`), the same side-table the container's own drop machinery keys on, for a Vec/VecDeque receiver and the two by-value removals. `pop` is deliberately NOT in that fallback: it returns `Option[T]`, which the optres arm of the same battery already owns. Once codegen could own the element, the interpreter's bare-statement gate was widened to match (and `swap_remove` added to both its method lists, having been absent from each). SEQUENCING WAS THE POINT: codegen first, interpreter second. The class-3 pass had already shown that widening the interpreter alone converts a shared gap into a divergence -- worse, here, because AOT was also leaking -- so the interpreter arm stayed narrow until the backend that ships could own the value. Verified by re-running the full removal matrix after EACH half, not just at the end. Pins (all three STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin discarded_vec_removal_fires_and_frees, carrying the always-correct BOUND control and a two-element `survivor` case that checks only the REMOVED element fires early while the one left behind still fires at scope exit; asan discarded_vec_removal_no_leak for the leak half. CLASS 1 REMAINDER, the only part of this row still open: `truncate(n)` (needs a RANGED walk over [n, len) -- its survivors correctly fire already, so the whole-container walker used for `clear` would double-fire them) and whole-container reassign `v = w` (the displaced old container's elements). CLASS 1 COMPLETED (b215) — the row is now CLOSED, all three classes fixed. The two remaining positions had the same memory-yes/bodies-no split as `clear`, but needed different walks, and getting that distinction right is the substance: `truncate(n)` required a RANGED walk. Its existing loop already stepped [n, len) freeing each removed element, and it ran no body -- so the removed tail lost its destructors while the SURVIVORS still fired at binding death, a fire count that looks plausible and is wrong. The whole-container walker used for `clear` is NOT usable here: it would re-fire the survivors. The per-slot bodies dispatcher now runs inside that same [n, len) loop, ahead of each free. Whole-container reassign `v = w` DOES displace every old element, so there the whole-container walker is correct; it now runs before the reassign path's per-element release and buffer free. The interpreter needed the mirror-image edits: a tail snapshot in `truncate`, and a `Value::Array` arm in the displaced-value match, which previously handled only Struct and EnumVariant. REFACTOR: `emit_tuple_elem_bodies_at` was renamed `emit_slot_drop_bodies_at` and made pub(super). It was written for tuple elements and named for them, but its contract -- run the bodies reachable from ONE SLOT of a given type -- was never tuple-specific, and truncate needed exactly that per-slot dispatch. Pins (both STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin truncate_and_reassign_run_displaced_drop_bodies, whose truncate case is what pins the RANGE -- the removed tail fires at the truncate, the survivor fires at binding death, neither twice -- plus a truncate(0) case and the reassign case.

title: a tuple-held Option[Struct] / Result[Struct, E] payload is never freed in ANY position, and a `let x = t.N` move-out fires the source element's Drop body twice -- tuple legs FIXED, the Result STRUCT FIELD leg still open
detail:
TWO ORIGINAL LEGS, filed together because -1 unmasked both at once. (A) TUPLE-HELD Option/Result -- FIXED (c775e70). (B) `Result[Res, i64]` STRUCT FIELD (`struct H { r: Result[Res, i64] }`, probe b211/o2) -- STILL OPEN. Both were vg-clean before B-2026-08-03-1 only because nothing ever READ the payload, so LLVM elided the allocation entirely -- `valgrind --trace-malloc=yes` on the pre-fix binaries counts ZERO allocations of the buffer and one after. Arming the payload's Drop body (which reads `self.name`) makes the allocation live and the missing free observable. Same discriminator and conclusion as B-2026-08-02-19. LEG A ROOT CAUSE: `emit_tuple_elem_drops` had a hard `"Option" | "Result" => {}` no-op, and every admit gate above it routes through `type_expr_has_drop_heap`, which hardcodes those two heads as heapless (load-bearing, must not change). So a tuple whose only heap hung off an Option/Result payload looked heapless at every gate and got NO drop at all -- in a binding, a by-value param, a returned tuple, a `Vec[(Option[Res], i64)]` element, and a nested tuple. The direct `Vec[Option[Res]]` control was clean throughout, which is exactly what kept the tuple hole invisible. LEG A FIX: `tuple_elem_optres_drop_ok` restates the element shapes `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr` admits as a pure `&self` gate (Option[shared] excluded -- rc machinery owns it, matching the cap-zero dual's existing arm); `emit_tuple_elem_drops` routes an admitted element to the tag-guarded `karac_drop_Option_

` / `karac_drop_Result__`; `zero_tuple_elem_cap_at` gains the matching move-out neutralizer (Option -> tag to None, Result -> payload area zeroed) and the two must stay in lockstep or a moved tuple double-frees; `synthesize_tuple_drop_fn_te` and `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr`'s tuple arm OR the new admit into their heapless bail. THIRD BUG FOUND WHILE FIXING (also fixed here, no separate row): `let x = t.N` moves ONE tuple element out. Cap-zeroing already neutralized the source's MEMORY drop but its `__karac_dropelems_tuple_*` walk stayed fully armed and fired that element's body a SECOND time over the zeroed slot -- `drop 1 ` with an empty name under AOT, a full duplicate under the interpreter. Present with NO Option involved (`let t = (Res{..}, Res{..}); let x = t.0;`), so it predates -1 entirely; the struct-FIELD sibling `let x = s.r` was correct all along. Fixed by re-emitting the walker with only that index masked (`disarm_tuple_elem_bodies_at` + `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn_skipping`), so sibling elements still fire; the interpreter twin is a per-`(binding, index)` record consulted by the tuple walk. LESSON, third instance this week: closing a leak by ARMING a new free turns every position that already consumes that value into a double-free candidate. Enumerate the consumers before landing -- here `let x = t.N` (the cap-zero dual) and `match t.N { Ok(v) => .. }` (a new `suppress_tuple_elem_optres_payload_cleanup`, the tuple-element sibling of the `inline_{option,result}_payload_vars` match suppressors) each needed their own neutralizer, and the second was found only by the full ASAN suite going RED. LEG B (still open) ROOT CAUSE, read at fix time for -1: the `OptionInline` field classifier admits an Option field whose payload is a struct/enum via `option_payload_struct_or_enum_drop_ok`, but the sibling Result arm requires `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` -- DIRECT String/Vec halves only -- so a struct Ok-payload falls through and no field drop is registered. The asymmetry looks deliberate: the Option admit is paired with `param_own`'s `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`, and Result has only `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` (halves, no struct payload). Freeing a Result struct payload in the field drop WITHOUT first giving the entry copy its struct-payload counterpart risks double-freeing a callee-shared buffer, so it needs the copy side and the drop side landed together, with the caller-retains vs entry-copy reasoning re-derived for Result. LEG B ATTEMPT 1 (2026-08-03, NOT LANDED -- reverted). The row's stated precondition turned out to be NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the main result to carry forward. Built exactly what the row prescribed: `result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok` (at least one side owns heap; every heap-owning side is a non-shared struct/enum, kept DISJOINT from `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` so each class keeps one copy helper), the entry-copy twin `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` (tag dispatch, then the boxed-or-inline payload copy factored out of the Option helper), wired into BOTH `field_copy_supported`'s Result arm and the `OptionInline` drop classifier. Result: the LOCAL-BINDING leak closes (probe b215/t7 vg=99 -> 0, both backends agreeing) but the BY-VALUE PARAM case DOUBLE-FREES (`fn take(h: H) -> i64 { h.t }`, probe b215/r2: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`) and the by-value-param-plus-consuming-match case SIGSEGVs (probe b215/r7). Diagnostic state at revert: the copy dispatch IS reached and its gate IS true (confirmed by instrumenting the dispatch), so the copy is emitted -- the fault is NOT a missing copy. The remaining suspects are (i) the boxed-vs-inline width decision disagreeing between the pack site (`coerce_to_payload_words`), the copy, and `emit_result_drop_fn`, and (ii) the second-order effect of the admit: making the Result field copyable flips the WHOLE struct `H` from caller-retains to callee-owned, which changes ownership for every field and every call site at once -- so the next attempt should isolate which of those two it is before rebuilding the mechanism. MEASURED BASELINE for the whole Result-struct-field family (current main, all `struct H { r: Result[Res, i64], t: i64 }` unless noted): local binding LEAKS (t7); by-value param LEAKS (r2); returned from a fn LEAKS (r3); `let x = h.r` move-out LEAKS **and DOUBLE-FIRES the body on BOTH backends** (r4 -- the Result-field sibling of the tuple-element move-out double-fire fixed in c775e70, and the one shape here that is a wrong-OUTPUT bug rather than a pure leak); `Result[Res, Bad]` with struct on BOTH sides runs NO body at all on either backend and is vg=0 (r5); `Result[Res, String]` mixed likewise (r6); by-value param + consuming `match h.r` prints `drop 7 ggggggg1` then a garbage `drop 7 drop 7 ` under AOT while `karac run` prints one correct fire -- a run-vs-build divergence on top of the leak (r7). Probes are in the b215 scratch set. COUPLING NOTE (2026-08-03, after B-2026-08-03-8 closed): that row's warning is now discharged in one direction. `let x = h.r` on a Result struct field no longer double-fires the body -- it fires once, on both backends -- so the shape is a PURE leak again, exactly like the other three in this row's baseline. The move-out neutralizers (tag/payload zero + the masked bodies walk) are in place, which means arming this row's field free will NOT reintroduce the SEGV that -8's Option leg had: the disarm the crash needed already exists for Result too. LEG B, SUSPECT (i) RULED OUT (2026-08-03, probes b215/p1-p3, no code change needed). The Option analogue of the failing shape is CLEAN: `struct Hopt { o: Option[Res], t: i64 }` -- `Res` being 4 words, so the payload is heap-BOXED exactly like the Result case -- through the identical by-value param `fn take(h: Hopt) -> i64 { h.t }` prints one body and reads vg=0 on both backends, as does the returned-from-a-fn variant. So a boxed payload DOES survive the callee-owned entry copy today, and neither `boxed-vs-inline width disagreement` nor `the callee-owned flip is inherently unsound` explains leg B's double-free. The next attempt should assume a SLIP in the new Result copy helper (most likely the tag dispatch or the payload GEP) and diff it against `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`, which is known-good on this exact shape. Caveat carried from the same probe run: the INLINE-payload Option field is NOT clean -- it triple-fires its body under AOT -- filed separately as B-2026-08-03-10, so 'the Option pairing is sound' holds for the boxed path only. LEG B FIXED (2026-08-03, ATTEMPT 2). The row's stated precondition was right and attempt 1's mechanism was right; what killed attempt 1 was a single constant. The `Result` payload AREA is FIVE words (`declarations.rs`'s `result_payload_words = 5`, the width `coerce_to_payload_words` packs at and `emit_result_drop_fn` boxes beyond) while the `Option` area is THREE. Attempt 1 factored its payload copy out of `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place` and carried that helper's `payload_words > 3` boxing test with it, so the canonical 4-word `Res { id: i64, name: String }` -- which a `Result` stores INLINE and an `Option` stores BOXED -- was copied as if boxed: word 1, actually `id`, was read as a box pointer. That is suspect (i) after all. The probe that 'ruled it out' compared against the Option analogue, which boxes the SAME struct because of the SAME area difference, so it confirmed only that a boxed payload survives -- it never exercised the inline path the Result case actually takes. LESSON: when porting a helper between the Option and Result families, the boxing threshold is NOT shared; an analogue probe that silently crosses the boxed/inline boundary proves nothing about the shape under test. THE FIX IS FOUR PIECES, and three of them are the arming-exposes-consumers pattern this row already records. (1) ADMIT + COPY: `result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok` (control_flow_match.rs) -- structurally DISJOINT from `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` (that one needs a direct String/Vec heap half and rejects a struct/enum one; this one is the mirror image), so each class keeps exactly one copy helper -- plus `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` (param_own.rs), a per-half tag-dispatched copy boxing at `> 5` in lockstep with `emit_result_drop_fn`, wired into `field_copy_supported`'s Result arm (via `result_payload_struct_enum_copyable`), `deep_copy_one_aggregate_field`'s Result arm, and the `OptionInline` drop classifier. That alone fixed the local binding, the by-value param and the returned-from-a-fn shapes. (2) MOVE-OUT: `let x = h.r` then leaked -- the source is correctly zeroed but `place_optres_field_move_info_ex`'s Result arm still admitted only the direct-vecstr class, so the leaf registered nothing. Widened it (and the two `stmts.rs` destructure sites), which is the same pairing rule the Option arm's comment already states: the source zero must fire precisely when the struct drop would free the field. (3) CONSUMING MATCH: `match h.r { Ok(x) => .. }` printed a spurious `drop 0 ` after the binding's correct fire, because `zero_result_payload_area` is NOT the dual of `zero_option_field_tag_at` -- it zeroes the payload WORDS and leaves the TAG selecting the live arm. Every memory consumer tolerates that (their frees are cap-guarded), but `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn`'s tag SWITCH does not: it still picked the Ok case and ran the payload's body over the zeroed slot. New `invalidate_result_tag_at` stores -1 so the switch takes its default, exactly like `None`. (4) OWNED-PARAM MATCH: `match h.r` inside `fn take(h: H)` fired the callee's body ON TOP OF the caller's, because `scrutinee_is_owned_param_binding` -- the B-2026-08-01-13 gate that routes a payload bound out of a by-value param's entry copy to a memory-only registration -- matched only a BARE Identifier. A `p.field` scrutinee binds out of the same entry copy, so it carries the same caller-retains body ownership; the test now walks FieldAccess / TupleIndex chains to their root. This one hid behind the area difference too: the Option twin never reached the registration at all (4 words > the 3-word area means BOXED, which fails the inline-payload gate), so the family looked correct until the Result class -- where the same payload is inline -- got a body to fire. RESIDUAL, split out as its own row: a MIXED `Result[, String]` FIELD is admitted by NEITHER gate -- the vecstr gate rejects the struct half, the new gate rejects the String half -- so its STRUCT half registers no field free and leaks (probes b215/u1, u2: 5 bytes definitely lost on the Ok side; the String half IS freed by the existing overlay route, so the gap is the struct payload alone). Both the field drop (`emit_result_drop_fn`) and the binding cleanup (`track_inline_result_payload_var` via `result_inline_payload_struct_drops`) already dispatch PER HALF across the two representations, so only the admit gate and the entry copy are missing. Filed separately rather than widened in here, to keep this row's two-disjoint-classes invariant -- the thing that makes copy-depth == free-depth checkable by inspection -- intact while it is verified. MEASURED AFTER (all `SAME` on AOT vs `karac run --interp`, all vg=0, was the baseline table above): t7 local binding, r2 by-value param, r3 returned-from-fn, r4 `let x = h.r` move-out, r5 struct-on-both-sides, r6 mixed halves, r7 param + consuming match, plus s10 the `Result[String,i64]` control, s11/s13/s15/s16 the four Option twins, s12/s14/s17 the marker variants that localize which side fires.
fix: Leg A + the move-out double-fire: c775e70 (src/codegen/synth_drop.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/runtime.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs, src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs, src/codegen.rs, src/codegen/functions.rs, src/interpreter.rs, src/interpreter/eval_stmt.rs; pins test_e2e_tuple_held_optres_payload_freed_and_dropped, test_e2e_tuple_elem_move_out_single_body_fire, test_tuple_held_optres_payload_bodies_fire, test_tuple_elem_move_out_single_body_fire, asan_tuple_held_optres_payload_freed). Leg B: 8cfe5be (src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/param_own.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs, src/codegen/synth_drop.rs; pins test_e2e_result_struct_payload_field_freed_and_single_body (stash-proven RED -- pre-fix the local-match position prints a spurious `drop 5 drop 5` and the param-match position fires twice), asan_result_struct_payload_field_freed (stash-proven RED with a heap-use-after-free), and the interpreter ORACLE twin test_result_struct_payload_field_freed_and_single_body, which is GREEN under the stash by construction -- the interpreter was correct on all seven positions throughout, which is what makes it the oracle).
