tracker: the stdlib Map API surface (src/interpreter + codegen Map lowering, wherever `get`/`insert` are defined) — needs an in-place map-value mutation path: a `get_mut`-shaped borrow, an entry API, or a `Map.append`-style helper for the container-valued case
title: the canonical `Map[K, Vec[V]]` grouping idiom taught by the corpus is QUADRATIC, but the language already has the O(k) answer -- `Map.entry(k).or_insert(..)` ships on both backends and measures flat. The gap is signposting: nothing leads an author from `get`/`insert` to `entry`, so a lint with a machine-applicable fix is the durable close (headline claim 'no in-place map-value mutation' DISPROVED, see detail)
detail:
SHAPE. Kara has no in-place mutation of a map VALUE. The corpus idiom for
`Map[K, Vec[V]]` (documented in `kara-katas leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams/
map_of_lists.kara` and reused by the new #244 kata) is therefore:

    match index.get(w) {
        Some(existing) => {
            let mut hits: Vec[i64] = existing.clone();   // <-- FULL COPY
            hits.push(i);
            let _ = index.insert(w, hits);
        }
        None => { ... }
    }

`get` yields a BORROW of the map's list and the map still owns it until the
reinsert lands, so the clone is not optional — it is what the language forces.
The consequence is that appending the k-th occurrence of a key copies k-1
elements, so building the index for a key seen k times costs O(k^2) element
copies. Every mirror language does this in O(k): Python
`setdefault(w, []).append(i)`, C++ `m[w].push_back(i)`, Rust
`m.entry(w).or_default().push(i)`, Go `m[w] = append(m[w], i)`.

MEASURED. Single-key list of n entries (`"the"` repeated), the degenerate case
of the same idiom, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` AOT build vs CPython 3, same machine:

    n         kara       cpython
    32000     0.10 s     0.004 s
    64000     0.52 s     0.011 s
    96000     5.60 s     0.009 s
    128000   13.37 s     0.013 s

4x the input costs kara 134x the time while CPython stays flat. At n=128000
kara is ~1000x slower than CPython doing identical work. This is not a
micro-difference that a constant factor explains — it is a complexity-class
difference in a bread-and-butter idiom (grouping, adjacency lists, inverted
indexes, bucketing all have this shape).

NOT THE BUFFER CACHE. `KARAC_BUF_CACHE=0` reproduces the same curve
(64k 0.49 s, 96k 5.77 s, 128k 13.26 s), so B-2026-07-30-4's allocator path is
not involved.

ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. The step between n=64000 and n=96000 is
10.6x for 1.5x the input — steeper than the quadratic the construction
explains. It is not the buffer cache (above). A plausible reading is the
clone's working set (source + destination, 2 x 768 KB at n=96000) outgrowing
L2 so every copy streams from DRAM, but that was NOT confirmed and is recorded
here as an open observation, not a finding. The quadratic itself is certain
and is what this entry is about.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. Any one of:

  * a `get_mut`-shaped borrow returning a mutable handle to the value in place;
  * an entry API (`map.entry(k).or_default()`) — the Rust spelling, and the one
    that composes best with the existing borrow rules;
  * a narrow `Map.append(k, v)` helper for the container-valued case, which
    covers the grouping idiom specifically without opening general in-place
    value mutation.

SOURCE NOTE. Found writing the #244 kata (map of position lists + two-pointer
merge). The kata KEEPS the natural quadratic phrasing — it is the honest way to
write this in Kara today, and per the kata rules the gap is filed rather than
routed around. The kata's scaled bench uses a count-then-fill construction
instead, which is linear and natural in all five languages, so the benchmark
compares one algorithm rather than smuggling this gap into a cross-language
number; that choice is documented in the kata README next to this id.

WORKAROUND EXISTS IN-LANGUAGE, and it is measured — recorded here so the
severity is judged on complete information. Routing the lists through an index
indirection (`Map[String, i64]` word -> slot, plus a side `Vec[Vec[i64]]`) makes
the append `lists[s].push(i)`, which mutates IN PLACE and is O(1). Same sweep,
same machine, same `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` build:

    n         direct (Map[K, Vec[V]])   pool (index indirection)
    32000     0.10 s                    0.00 s
    64000     0.49 s                    0.00 s
    96000     5.98 s                    0.00 s
    128000   14.21 s                    0.00 s

So this is a performance TRAP rather than a wall. Severity stays high anyway,
on two grounds: the trap is SILENT (nothing in `karac check` or any diagnostic
tells the author their grouping build just became quadratic — it compiles clean
and runs correctly, only slowly), and the direct phrasing is the one every
mirror language's idiom translates to, so it is what a newcomer writes first.
The indirection is a known corpus workaround (#49 `count_signature.kara`,
#244 `shortest_distance_pool.kara`), not something the language guides anyone
toward.

── HEADLINE CLAIM DISPROVED (2026-08-04). REFRAMED, SEVERITY high -> medium. ──

This entry asserts "Kara has no in-place mutation of a map VALUE". THAT IS
FALSE. The language has exactly that, it has shipped on BOTH backends, and it
is O(k):

    index.entry(w).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(i);

`Map.entry(k) -> Entry[K, V]` and `Entry.or_insert(default) -> mut ref V`
(plus `or_insert_with(|| ..)` and `and_modify(|v| ..)`, both verified) are
implemented in `src/typechecker/stdlib_map.rs::infer_entry_method` and lower on
interp, `karac run` and AOT. `or_insert`'s doc comment even cites kata 3629's
`bucket.entry(p).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(j)` as the shape it was pushed-down
for -- so the API predates this entry.

MEASURED, same machine, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` AOT, single-key list (this entry's
own degenerate shape), clone idiom vs entry API:

    n         clone       entry      cpython (this entry's column)
    32000     0.10 s      0.006 s    0.004 s
    64000     0.52 s      0.007 s    0.011 s
    96000     6.22 s      0.008 s    0.009 s
    128000   13.38 s      0.010 s    0.013 s

The clone column reproduces this entry's numbers. The entry column is FLAT --
4x the input for 1.7x the time -- and lands in CPython's range. The quadratic
is real; it is a property of the IDIOM, not of the language.

The interpreter has the same asymptotics (entry ~linear 0.26/0.44/0.69 s at
n=4000/8000/16000; clone quadratic 1.40/5.92/21.28 s over the same range), so
this is not a codegen-only path either.

NOT A TOY-ONLY RESULT. The real group-anagrams shape -- `Map[String,
Vec[String]]`, COMPUTED String key, string values -- runs correctly on interp
and AOT through `groups.entry(k).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(w)`.

WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS, and it is a real one, just much smaller than
filed. Nothing leads an author from `get`/`insert` to `entry`, and the CORPUS
teaches the clone: `kara-katas leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams/
map_of_lists.kara` documents clone-reinsert as THE `Map[K, Vec[V]]` pattern,
and #244 inherited it. So the measured 1000x is the cost of a kata following
documented guidance that happens to be the slow path.

Remaining work, none of which is "implement in-place map mutation":
  * CORPUS -- retarget `map_of_lists.kara` and #244 onto the entry API (the
    kara-katas repo, not this one).
  * DIAGNOSTICS -- the compiler can recognize the clone-reinsert shape
    (`match m.get(k) { Some(x) => { let mut y = x.clone(); y.push(..);
    m.insert(k, y); } None => .. }`) and emit a machine-applicable fix to
    `m.entry(k).or_insert(..)`. That is the durable fix: it turns a
    discoverability gap into a `karac fix` the Mend loop applies, and it is
    what would have kept the corpus off the slow path in the first place.

SEVERITY high -> medium. The "high" rested on a complexity-class hole in a
bread-and-butter idiom. There is no hole -- there is a signposting gap with a
shipped O(k) answer one method call away.

PROCESS NOTE, the third of this shape in this ledger (cf. B-2026-08-01-33's
own "par struct shares lock-free" retraction, and the HTTP/2 sibling-stream
claim). All three were written from a failed or assumed path without testing
the sanctioned alternative, and all three were caught by one probe. Filing a
MISSING FEATURE deserves a stronger check than filing a bug: grep the method
table for the capability before concluding it is absent. `require_known_method`
lists every Map method in one place -- "entry" is in it.

── CLOSED d166203 — `map_value_clone_reinsert` lint ──

The reframe above named a lint as the durable close: recognize the
clone-reinsert shape and offer `entry().or_insert()` as a machine-applicable
fix, so the discoverability gap becomes something `karac fix` applies rather
than something every author has to independently not-fall-into. Done.

`src/map_entry_lint.rs`, registered in `src/lints.rs` (default Warn).
Suppressible with `-A map_value_clone_reinsert` and via the manifest's
`[lints]` table; per-ITEM `#[allow(map_value_clone_reinsert)]` is NOT honoured,
because this module emits outside `TypeChecker::type_lint_warning`, which is
what consults item attributes. `must_use_lint` has the identical limitation
(it passes the same `false` triple for source-level flags) — wiring attribute
scope is a shared follow-up for both, and is deliberately not faked here.
VERIFIED both ways: default fires, `-A` suppresses. Emitted into `typed.warnings`
rather than through a bespoke lint channel, which means it rides plumbing that
already existed: `--output=json` renders it with `lint_name` and `fix_it`, and
`karac fix` applies the edit.

VALIDATED AGAINST THE REAL ARTIFACT, not just a synthetic probe. Run against
the pre-fix `kara-katas` #244 `shortest_distance_ii.kara` — the file that
carried this entry's measured 1736x slowdown — the lint fires at the right line
and emits exactly the rewrite that was made by hand:

    index.entry(w).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(i);

End to end on a probe: `karac fix` collapsed the 12-line match to that line,
output unchanged (interp / JIT / AOT all 4), and the lint does not re-fire on
its own output.

THE SHAPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, because this lint REWRITES WORKING CODE — a
false positive silently changes behaviour, which is a worse failure than the
quadratic it fixes. It requires: scrutinee `M.get(K)` typed `Option[<container>]`;
exactly two arms; each arm exactly three statements (`let mut v = ..` /
`v.<m>(args)` / `let _ = M.insert(K, v)`); the Some arm's init is `b.clone()`;
and M, K, method and args spelled identically across both arms. Every negative
test is a rewrite that would be WRONG, not merely noisy:

  * scalar-valued map        -> O(1) already, nothing to fix
  * an arm with a 4th stmt   -> the rewrite has nowhere to put it. This is #49's
                                `map_of_lists.kara` (`order.push(key)` records
                                first-seen order); firing there would silently
                                drop it. Verified silent against the real file.
  * bound `insert` result    -> the DISPLACED value is in use; `or_insert` never
                                displaces, so the rewrite loses it
  * different keys per arm   -> not one logical append
  * no clone                 -> nothing quadratic present
  * already-fixed form       -> fixpoint, so `karac fix` cannot oscillate

TWO THINGS FOUND ALONG THE WAY, both worth keeping:

  1. `expr_types` AT A RECEIVER SPAN IS THE ENCLOSING CALL'S TYPE. Typing `m` in
     `m.get(k)` returns `Option[V]`, not `Map[K, V]` — a chained access shares
     its start offset with the enclosing call, the same span-overwrite hazard
     `ownership.rs` documents for projections. The lint reads the value type off
     the SCRUTINEE's `Option[V]` payload instead, whose span is unambiguous.
     Anyone reaching for a receiver's type by span needs to know this.
  2. `cmd_fix` READ ONLY `typed.errors` FIX-ITS, never `typed.warnings`. Until
     this lint there was no warning-with-a-fix producer, so nothing surfaced it
     — but the JSON already advertised `fix_it` on warnings, so any future
     warning-borne fix would have been advertised and then not applied. Now
     read. A warning's fix is optional-but-safe by construction, which is
     exactly what `fix` is for.

KNOWN LIMITATION, pre-existing and NOT introduced here: typecheck warnings do
not render in `karac check`'s TEXT output at all — verified by checking that an
existing warning (unreachable match arm) is equally invisible there, while both
appear under `--output=json`. So a human running bare `karac check` will not see
this lint; the Mend loop (`--output=json`) and `karac fix` both do, which is the
channel that motivated it. Worth filing separately for the whole warning class;
deliberately not widened here, since adding a text renderer would change output
for every existing typecheck warning at once.

title: an Option field whose payload is INLINE (a struct narrow enough to fit the 3-word payload area) fires its Drop body THREE times under AOT when the owning struct is passed by value — the BOXED-payload sibling is correct
detail: `struct Small { id: i64 }` + `impl Drop`, `struct Hsm { o: Option[Small], t: i64 }`, `fn take(h: Hsm) -> i64 { h.t }`, `println(take(h))`. `karac run` prints `drop 3` ONCE; `karac build` prints it THREE times, and one of them lands before the `4` rather than after (probe b215/p2). Pre-existing -- verified by rebuilding src/ at 9a5ce03. vg=0 throughout: `Small` owns no heap, so this is a pure body-COUNT bug with no memory consequence, which is also why no sanitizer can see it. THE DISCRIMINATOR, and the reason this is worth its own row: the same shape with a WIDER payload is CORRECT. `struct Res { id: i64, name: String }` is 4 words, so `Option[Res]` heap-BOXES its payload, and `struct Hopt { o: Option[Res], t: i64 }` through the identical by-value param prints exactly once on both backends, vg=0 (probe b215/p1); so does the returned-from-a-fn variant (p3). So the entry-copy / field-drop / bodies-walk pairing for an Option struct field is sound on the BOXED path and triple-fires on the INLINE one -- the split is `llvm_type_word_count(payload) > 3` in `emit_option_drop_fn` and `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`, which is the first place to look. Three fires suggests three separate owners each running the body over the same inline words: plausibly the caller's binding, the callee's entry copy, and one of the field-bodies walks firing on a slot the inline path did not neutralize (the boxed path's neutralizer is a pointer store, the inline path's would have to be a tag or cap write). FOUND WHILE probing B-2026-08-03-3 leg B: p1/p2 were built to discriminate that row's two suspects, and p1's cleanliness is what rules out `a boxed payload cannot survive a by-value param` as the explanation for leg B's double-free -- so leg B's failure is most likely a slip in the new Result copy helper rather than a structural impossibility. That conclusion is recorded on -3 as well.  ROOT CAUSE + FIX (2026-08-03, 257d666). `emit_drop_fn_for_type_expr` (src/codegen/clone_drop.rs) carries a guard, documented since B-2026-07-30-11, that routes a Drop-bearing bare user STRUCT to the MEMORY-ONLY synthesis so the memory channel never re-runs a body the NLL `UserDrop` channel already owns. The guard's own FALLBACK -- taken when `emit_struct_drop_synthesis` returns None because the struct has no heap to free -- called `emit_primitive_drop_fn(&type_name)`, and that emitter OPENS with the same `module.get_function("karac_drop_<T>")` lookup the guard exists to bypass. That name IS the user-drop WRAPPER, so the memory channel was handed the wrapper and fired the body a second (and, once the field's own registration also routed through it, a third) time. Only shapes that REACH the memory channel for such a struct were affected, which is exactly why every neighbour read correct in the narrowing matrix: a BOXED payload (`Option[Big]`, q5), the `Result` sibling whose narrower admit registers no memory drop on this route (q6), a DIRECT `Option[Small]` binding (q4) and a direct `Small` field (q7). Minimal repro q2 needs no function call at all: `struct Small { id: i64 }` + `impl Drop`, `struct Hsm { o: Option[Small], t: i64 }`, `let h = Hsm { .. }; println(h.t);`. FIX: name the fallback `<T>$mem` -- a `$` cannot appear in a user type name, so the lookup can never alias the wrapper again. LESSON: a guard that exists to bypass a name lookup must not delegate to a helper that re-performs the same lookup; the bypass has to hold for the helper's whole call tree, not just the guard's own body.
fix: 257d666 (src/codegen/clone_drop.rs; pin test_e2e_inline_option_payload_field_body_fires_once, stash-proven RED -- pre-fix AOT prints `drop 1` twice and `drop 2` three times where the interpreter prints each once)

title: a struct field holding a MIXED `Result[<Drop struct>, String]` -- one half a direct String/Vec, the other a struct/enum -- is admitted by NEITHER Result field-drop gate, so the STRUCT half's heap is never freed
detail: SURFACED while closing B-2026-08-03-3 leg B (8cfe5be), which armed the field free for a Result whose heap-owning halves are ALL non-shared structs/enums. That gate (`result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok`) and the older `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` were deliberately made structurally DISJOINT so each class binds to exactly one entry-copy helper and copy-depth == free-depth stays checkable by inspection. The consequence is a hole between them: a field typed `Result[Res, String]` (Res a Drop struct owning a String) has one heap half of each kind, so the vecstr gate rejects it for the struct half and the new gate rejects it for the String half. No field free is registered and the struct payload's buffer is orphaned.  MEASURED (probes b215/u1 and b215/u2, `struct Hm { r: Result[Res, String], t: i64 }`): 5 bytes definitely lost under valgrind on the Ok side, AOT and `karac run --interp` agreeing on output throughout, so parity is blind to it and only the leak oracle sees it. u2 reads BOTH halves (`match h.r { Ok(x) => x.id, Err(e) => e.len() }` through a `ref` param) to rule out the elided-dead-allocation artifact that made this family look clean before B-2026-08-03-1; the Err String is correctly freed by the existing overlay route, so the gap is the struct payload alone.  WHY IT SHOULD BE SMALL. Both FREE sides already dispatch per half across the two representations: `emit_result_drop_fn` branches independently on Ok and Err, and `track_inline_result_payload_var` pairs `result_inline_payload_elems` (overlay) with `result_inline_payload_struct_drops` (full struct drop) per side. Only the ADMIT GATE and the ENTRY COPY are single-class. Suggested shape: require at least one struct/enum heap half (which preserves disjointness from the vecstr gate) while also ACCEPTING a direct String/Vec heap half, and extend `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` to emit the `{ptr,len,cap}` overlay copy for such a half instead of skipping it -- the same dance `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` already performs, worth factoring into a shared per-half emitter so the two cannot drift. Keep the `> 5` boxing threshold; the Option family's `> 3` is what broke leg B's first attempt.  FIXED (2026-08-03, 0567cea) exactly along the shape this row predicted, in three small pieces. (1) `result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok` now REQUIRES at least one struct/enum heap half and ACCEPTS a direct String/Vec half alongside it (new `result_half_is_direct_vecstr`, which carries over the vecstr gate's shared-element exclusion -- the defensive copy emits no per-element rc-inc). Disjointness from `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` is preserved, and now rests on the struct/enum REQUIREMENT rather than on a prohibition: this gate demands one, that gate rejects any. (2) The `{ptr,len,cap}` overlay dance was extracted out of `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` into `emit_result_half_overlay_copy` (caller owns the tag test and the blocks; builder must be positioned in the taken arm), so the two entry-copy helpers that need it cannot drift. (3) `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` classifies each half up-front -- heapless skips, struct/enum takes the boxed-or-inline dance at the Result area's `> 5`, direct String/Vec routes to the extracted overlay copy -- and `result_payload_struct_enum_copyable` admits the direct half (its own gate already vetted it). No change was needed on either FREE side: `emit_result_drop_fn` and `track_inline_result_payload_var` already dispatched per half, which is what made this a three-piece fix rather than a redesign.  VERIFIED across six positions on both backends, all `SAME` and vg=0 (probes b215/u1, u2, u3): Ok-struct binding, Err-String binding, by-value param, `let x = h.r` move-out, and the SWAPPED arrangement `Result[Vec[String], Res]` on each side -- the half-order control, since the admit is per half and not per position. u2 additionally reads BOTH halves so the elided-dead-allocation artifact cannot mask the result.  ORACLE NOTE, worth keeping: this row is one the parity oracle cannot see at all. The interpreter matched AOT line-for-line before the fix and the Drop body count was already right; only LSan saw the orphaned buffer (stash-proven RED at 123 bytes in 6 allocations). The codegen E2E pin `test_e2e_mixed_halves_result_struct_field_freed` is therefore a COMPANION guard, green before and after -- its job is the other direction, pinning that arming this class did not turn any of the six consuming positions into a double-free or double-fire, which is the failure mode B-2026-08-03-3 hit three times.
fix: 0567cea (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/param_own.rs; pins asan_mixed_halves_result_struct_field_freed -- the leak oracle, stash-proven RED with 123 bytes leaked in 6 allocations under LSan -- and the companion E2E test_e2e_mixed_halves_result_struct_field_freed, which is green under the stash by construction and guards the six consuming positions against the double-free/double-fire that arming a free invites)

title: `coroutine_preserves_active_span_across_suspend` (tests/coro_e2e.rs) is INTERMITTENT -- the post-resume log line came back unstamped (`[info] after-resume`, span_id=0) on one full-suite run and has not reproduced in 19 attempts since
detail:
SURFACE NOTE: filed as `codegen` because the assertion guards the coroutine state-machine transform's active-span save/restore (`emit_coro_park_suspend`'s frame snapshot + the resume-edge restore); if the nondeterminism is in the harness rather than the transform, the surface should be corrected when it is diagnosed. `source` carries the real provenance.  OBSERVED ONCE, 2026-08-03, during a full `cargo test --features llvm` run (33 passed / 1 failed in coro_e2e; every other target green). The assertion wants `[info] after-resume span_id=7`; the run produced `["BOUND_PORT=37223", "[info] after-resume", "2"]` -- the line is there, the program exits successfully and prints `2`, only the span stamp is missing, which per the test's own comment is exactly the shape of a Phase-2 regression (span_id=0 renders no suffix).  NOT REPRODUCED SINCE: 4 standalone runs, 15 consecutive runs while a full suite was saturating the machine, and a second complete `cargo test --features llvm` (12,900 passed / 0 failed). So it is rare and load-correlated at most.  WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY. This is a required CI gate as of B-2026-07-31-44 (coro_e2e was one of the 17 dark targets added to `codegen-e2e`), so a rare miss turns into a red build nobody can reproduce -- and the failure is indistinguishable from a real span-preservation regression, which is the expensive kind of ambiguity.  DISCRIMINATOR TO TRY. `service_one_connection` retries the connect for up to 3s specifically to absorb the race between `bind`'s BOUND_PORT print and the coroutine's fd registration -- so whether `accept()` actually PARKS is timing-dependent. Both paths should yield span 7 (no park: the body runs on the calling thread inside `with_span`; park: the save/restore reinstalls it), so a run that prints 0 means one of those two is not airtight. Start by making the park deterministic (a probe binary that logs whether it suspended) rather than by chasing the assertion.

FIXED 2026-08-04. NOT a harness flake -- a real data race in the coroutine
transform, and the entry's `codegen` surface guess was right.

MECHANISM. `emit_coro_park_suspend` (src/codegen/coro.rs) emitted the pre-suspend
active-span snapshot AFTER `karac_runtime_event_loop_register_fd_cancel`. That call is the
publication point: it inserts the frame-resident parked record into the (sharded) event loop
and wakes its poller, and the `llvm.coro.save` immediately above it exists precisely so a
resume is legal from there on -- the code's own comment says the dispatcher "can claim and
resume ... this frame before the worker thread running the ramp reaches the `coro.suspend`
below". So the ordering was:

    coro.save                     <- resume becomes legal here
    register_fd_cancel(...)       <- frame published to the reactor
    store parked.token
    %snap = call karac_tracing_get_active_span()   <- RACING a resumer
    store active_span_slot, %snap                  <- RACING a resumer
    coro.suspend

and the resume edge LOADS `active_span_slot` to reinstall the span. When the dispatcher won
the race it read the slot before the ramp wrote it, got the fresh frame's zero, and called
`set_active_span(0)` -- so the post-resume log line rendered with no span suffix. That is a
data race on the slot, not merely a lost value.

Everything the entry recorded follows: rare (the resumer has to win a two-instruction
window), load-correlated (the comment above notes the fd "is often immediately ready" under
load), and specifically `span_id=0` rather than a wrong span (zeroed frame memory).

THE ENTRY'S SUGGESTED DISCRIMINATOR WAS BASED ON A FALSE PREMISE, recorded here so nobody
retries it. It said "whether `accept()` actually PARKS is timing-dependent" and advised
starting there. It is not: `emit_state_machine_invocation_for_park_on_fd` (src/codegen/tcp.rs)
routes unconditionally to `emit_coro_park_suspend` inside a coroutine -- there is no
try-syscall-first fast path, the register+suspend always happens, and the actual `accept`
syscall is emitted on the resume edge. Both of the entry's two hypothesised paths were really
one path.

REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY, which is what turned this from a suspicion into a fix. A
temporary `karac_debug_park_race_delay()` extern (env-gated busy-spin, added to the runtime
and called from codegen between `register_fd` and the snapshot, then removed) widens the
window:

  delay off, pre-fix    13 runs, 0 failures     (10 baseline + 3 control)
  delay 2 ms, pre-fix    5 runs, 4 failures
  delay 2 ms, post-fix   8 runs, 0 failures
  delay 20 ms, post-fix  6 runs, 0 failures

and the forced failure is identical in shape to the one this entry recorded:
["BOUND_PORT=43695", "[info] after-resume", "2"] versus the filed
["BOUND_PORT=37223", "[info] after-resume", "2"].

FIX: hoist the snapshot above `coro.save`, so every frame write the ramping thread performs
completes before the frame is reachable by anyone else. Value-preserving -- the read is of
the ramping thread's own TLS and nothing between the old and new positions touches it.

THE SIBLING STORE IS BENIGN, checked rather than assumed, because it looks like the same bug
and the next reader will ask. `store parked.token` is also below the publication and cannot
be hoisted (the token does not exist until `register_fd` returns it). The difference is what
consumes it: the post-suspend edges load that field only to pass to `deregister_fd`, and the
dispatcher claims every registration through a one-shot `take_registration` BEFORE it fires
-- so in exactly the racing case the deregister is already a no-op whatever the field holds.
The active-span slot had no such property; its value was used.

REGRESSION GUARD is an IR ORDERING pin,
`coroutine_active_span_snapshot_precedes_frame_publication` (tests/coro_e2e.rs), asserting
the snapshot call precedes `register_fd_cancel` in the ramp. It has to be structural: the
behavioural sibling passed 10/10 here and 19/19 when this entry was filed WITH the bug
present, so it cannot hold this line. Verified to bite -- reverting the hoist fails it
(snapshot@3188 vs publish@2755). The pin anchors on publication rather than `coro.save`
because CoroSplit consumes the save intrinsic; publication is the property that actually
matters and it survives the split.

TEST-INFRA NOTE: this makes the E2E sibling's required-CI status (B-2026-07-31-44) safe
again; the ambiguity the entry called "the expensive kind" is resolved in favour of a real
defect.
tracker: src/codegen/coro.rs (emit_coro_park_suspend: active-span snapshot hoisted above coro.save/register_fd)

title: FRESH-TEMP twin of B-2026-08-02-25's match-arm leg: a heap-BOXED Option/Result payload bound out of a `match mk() { Some(r) => .. }` arm runs its Drop BODY against the binding's reconstructed COPY, not the box, so a body that MUTATES a heap field (`self.buf.clear()`) frees the buffer while the box keeps the stale pointer and the scope-exit box drop frees it again
detail: REPRO (probe b225/as_e, 20 iterations, exit 134 under glibc and 20 invalid frees under valgrind): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` with `impl Drop for Full { fn drop(mut ref self) { if self.buf[0] < 0 { println(self.buf[0]); } self.buf.clear(); } }`, `fn opt(i: i64) -> Option[Full] { return Option.Some(mk(i)); }`, and `match opt(i) { Option.Some(r) => { n = n + r.buf.len(); } ... }`. `Full` is 6 words, so it is BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area. The interpreter is correct; AOT double-frees.  MECHANISM, and it is exactly the one B-2026-08-02-25's fix had to avoid on the NAMED route. `bind_pattern_values` reconstructs a boxed payload into a struct-VALUE alloca -- a copy of the box's `{ptr,len,cap}` -- and the fresh-temp arm of `is_boxed_optres_drop_payload` registers `__karac_dropbodies_only_<T>` over THAT alloca. The box, not the binding, still owns the payload's memory. A read-only Drop body is harmless there, but a mutating one writes to the wrong storage: `clear()` frees `buf.data` and zeroes the COPY's cap, the box's words are untouched, and `karac_drop_Option_Full` -> the payload's memory drop frees the same pointer a second time.  NOT A REGRESSION -- stash-proven identical before and after the B-2026-08-02-25 fix (which touched only the named-source route). It went unnoticed because no test paired a fresh-temp match arm with a MUTATING Drop body: `asan_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fire_once` has the mutating body but its fresh-temp cases hold the Option without matching on it, and every E2E pin in this family uses a read-only `println` body, which cannot witness the class.  FIX SHAPE IS KNOWN, by symmetry with the closed leg: run the walk against the BOX. The named route does this by re-registering the source's own `__karac_dropelems_opt_*` action (slot + walker sampled by `scrutinee_armed_payload_bodies_action`) under the binding's name. A fresh temp has no named source to sample, but `compile_match` does stage the scrutinee -- thread that staged slot to the bind site the way `freshtemp_enum` / `freshtemp_inline_res` are already threaded, then instantiate `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn` from the scrutinee's Option/Result te and register THAT over the staged slot under the binding's name. The `__karac_dropelems_` prefix also satisfies `fire_due_user_drops`' NLL gate, so the timing comes along for free.  ORACLE NOTE: parity diffing DOES see this one (AOT aborts, `karac run` prints the answer), and so does valgrind/LSan. What no oracle in the suite saw is the input -- a fresh-temp arm over a mutating body. Worth a drop_fuzz corpus entry: mutating Drop bodies are under-represented against every payload-position axis, not just this one.  FIXED (2026-08-04, c89192f) exactly along the fix shape this row predicted. `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` now RETURNS the `__freshtemp_boxed_scrut` alloca it stages; `freshtemp_payload_bodies_action` resolves the scrutinee's Option/Result instantiation (the span table first, then the fn-return / pop-family derivation `track_discarded_optres_payload_bodies` already used), instantiates `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn`, and hands the `(slot, walker)` pair to the SAME re-homing branch B-2026-08-02-25 added for the named route. So the bind site now has ONE code path fed by one field, and the two routes cannot drift: whichever supplies the pair, the walk runs against a slot holding the box pointer rather than against the arm binding's reconstructed copy.  FALLBACK IS THE OLD BEHAVIOR, deliberately: any missing ingredient -- no staged slot (non-boxed, non-fresh, or a borrow scrutinee), no resolvable instantiation, or a payload that runs no user Drop -- leaves the previous bodies-only-over-the-copy registration in place, so nothing outside the boxed fresh-temp shape can move.  VERIFIED by pre/post stash attribution over two probe sets. Of 7 fresh-temp probes (b226/f1-f7) exactly 5 change, every one from a double-free ABORT to correct output: bare match, if-let, let-else, boxed `Result` past its wider 5-word area, and `while let Some(r) = v.pop()` (the one shape whose type comes from the pop-family derivation rather than the fn-return table). The other two are CONTROLS and are byte-identical -- a borrow scrutinee (`m.get(k)`, whose payload aliases the map's storage) and a non-consuming `Some(_)` arm. Of the 35 probes from the named-route slice exactly ONE changes -- `as_e`, which is this bug. All 6 fixed probes are vg=0.  A THIRD DEFECT fell out of the control: the `Some(_)` probe leaks 32 bytes, stash-proven identical before and after, filed as B-2026-08-04-3 (a wildcard payload leaves `inner_struct_name` empty so the box drop is box-only). It is kept OUT of this row's ASan pin so LSan cannot misattribute it there.  ORACLE NOTE, and the reason this outlived the leg that shares its root cause: the read-only `println` Drop bodies every E2E pin in this family uses cannot witness the class at all -- they touch no heap, so copy-vs-box is unobservable. Both new pins mutate on purpose. That is also the generalizable gap: mutating Drop bodies are under-represented in the corpus against every payload-position axis, which is worth a drop_fuzz entry independent of this row.
fix: c89192f (src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_freshtemp_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_freshtemp_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box, both stash-proven RED -- the E2E aborts before flushing any output (`left: ""`) and the ASan pin reports a double-free at exit 23)

title: A heap-BOXED Option payload bound by a consuming match arm and then MOVED -- into a struct literal, or out as the match's tail value -- double-frees under `karac build` while the interpreter is correct; read-only Drop body, both named and fresh-temp scrutinees
detail: REPROS, all with `struct Res { id: i64, name: String }` (4 words, so BOXED at Option's 3-word area) and a READ-ONLY `impl Drop for Res { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"drop {self.id} {self.name}") } }` -- the body touches no heap, so this is NOT the mutating-body class of B-2026-08-04-1.  (1) probe b225/p5, move into a struct literal: `let o: Option[Res] = Option.Some(Res { .. }); match o { Option.Some(r) => { let w = W { r: r }; println(w.r.id); } ... }` -- interp `got 5 / drop 5 eeeee5 / end`, AOT `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`, exit 134.  (2) probe b225/p6, the binding escapes as the match's VALUE: `let r2 = match o { Option.Some(r) => r, Option.None => Res { .. } }; println(r2.id);` -- same split, same abort.  (3) probe b225/p5t, the FRESH-TEMP spelling of (1) (`match mko() { .. }`) -- same abort, so the defect is not specific to a named source.  CONTROLS that pin the boundary: with an INLINE payload (`struct Res { name: String }`, 3 words) shape (1) is fully correct on both backends (probe p5i), so BOXING is the discriminator. Shape (2) with an inline payload is a DIFFERENT and milder defect (probe p6i): AOT prints a spurious leading `drop ` with an EMPTY NAME before the real body -- a stale-slot read rather than a double-free -- which looks like the same move-out bookkeeping gap seen from the inline side and is probably worth fixing in the same pass.  PRE-EXISTING, and measured as such: identical output before and after the B-2026-08-02-25 match-arm fix (542d7d7) on all four probes. That fix only re-homes the payload's Drop BODY (a walk that frees nothing by construction) and changes no memory action, which is why it neither caused nor cured this.  STARTING POINT: the arm's memory suppressors decide who owns a boxed payload's interior after the bind. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` handles a struct SUB-PATTERN (`Some(Res { name })`) by cap-zeroing the consumed fields INSIDE the box, but there is no equivalent for a WHOLE-payload binding that then moves: the destination (the struct literal's field, the match result) takes ownership of the payload's heap children and frees them, while the box drop still frees the same buffers. Compare against the INLINE path, which gets this right -- it suppresses via the source's cap/tag zeroing and the binding's own `track_struct_var`.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 8f8696d).  FIRST, A CORRECTION to this row's own framing. It described the class as firing with a READ-ONLY Drop body and recorded that the same shapes were clean without an `impl Drop` -- treating the Drop impl as the discriminator. It is not one. Those clean readings were a DEAD-ALLOCATION artifact: with nothing reading the moved payload's heap field the buffer is elided and every case looks fine. Add one `println(w.r.name)` and the no-Drop program aborts identically (probe b227/h3). The Drop impl was only ever keeping the buffer live. Same trap as this family's other two rows, from the opposite direction -- there a read-only body hid the bug, here a dead buffer did.  MEASURED SURFACE, with the payload's field forced live (probes b227/k1-k7): FOUR move destinations abort and two positions are correct. Broken: a struct-literal field, the match's own tail value, a plain `let` rebind, and a container push -- named and fresh-temp scrutinees alike. Correct: a by-value fn ARG, and no move at all.  ROOT CAUSE: the arm binding is an unboxed COPY of the box's `{ptr,len,cap}` words and registers no memory drop of its own, by design -- the `BoxedEnumDrop`'s `inner_drop_fn` owns the interior, which is what keeps `if let Some(r) = v.pop()` from double-freeing. Once the binding moves, the destination registers its own drop over those same buffers and both free them. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` already solves the STRUCT-SUB-PATTERN case (`Some(H { v, .. })`) by cap-zeroing the named fields inside the box; there was no equivalent for a whole-payload binding.  THE FIX records the binding in `boxed_optres_payload_view_vars` (name -> scrutinee slot, snapshotted with the per-arm var environment) and, at each move site, clears the source `BoxedEnumDrop`'s `inner_drop_fn`, leaving a BOX-ONLY free. Sites: struct-literal fields, the let RHS, the match tail, and the container-consuming-arg hook.  WHY RETRACT THE WALK RATHER THAN CAP-ZERO THE BOX, which was tried first and is the more obvious move given the struct-sub-pattern precedent: the box's words are ALSO what the re-homed payload-BODIES walk reads -- B-2026-08-02-25 / B-2026-08-04-1 point it at the source slot precisely so a mutating Drop body lands on the storage the later free sees. `zero_struct_move_caps` clears `len` alongside `cap` for this shape, so the body then printed an EMPTY string (probe b227/m1: `in-callee [eeeeeeee5] len=9` but `drop 5 [] len=0`). That converts a double-free into a silent wrong-value -- strictly worse. Clearing the action's fn pointer touches no data, so the body still reads the live payload. The two landed rows and this one are only mutually consistent under the walk-retraction form.  THE BY-VALUE ARG IS NOT A MOVE, and this cost a cut. The first version dispatched the neutralizer from `suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move` to inherit its 13-site roster; that roster includes call args, where the callee takes an entry COPY under caller-retains. Neutralizing there LEAKED the box's copy (9 bytes, probes g5d/m1). Both new pins carry that control explicitly.  VERIFIED: 17 b227 probes all parity-equal and vg=0. Across the 43 probes from the two preceding rows, exactly THREE change -- p5, p6, p5t -- which are this row's own repros, every other one byte-identical.  RESIDUAL, unchanged and still open: the INLINE sibling of the tail-value shape (probe b225/p6i) prints a spurious leading body with an EMPTY name -- a stale-slot read rather than a double-free. Same move-out bookkeeping seen from the inline side; not touched here.
fix: 8f8696d (src/codegen.rs, src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/exprs.rs, src/codegen/functions.rs, src/codegen/mono.rs, src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs, src/codegen/runtime.rs, src/codegen/shadow.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_boxed_optres_payload_view_move_transfers_box_interior (stash-proven RED -- aborts before flushing any output) and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_view_move_has_one_owner, both carrying the by-value-arg and no-move controls that the first cut got wrong)

title: A FRESH-TEMP boxed Option/Result scrutinee matched by a WILDCARD payload arm (`match mk() { Some(_) => .. }`) gets a box-ONLY free, so the payload struct's inner heap leaks -- the whole-binding sibling (`Some(r)`) is correct because only a Binding sub-pattern populates `inner_struct_name`
detail: REPRO (probe b226/f7, 32 bytes definitely lost under valgrind, parity-EQUAL so no run-vs-build split): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` with any Drop impl, `fn opt(i: i64) -> Option[Full] { return Option.Some(mk(i)); }`, and `match opt(7i64) { Option.Some(_) => { println("arm"); } Option.None => { println("none"); } }`. `Full` is 6 words, so it is BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area. Change the arm to `Option.Some(r)` and the same program is vg=0.  MECHANISM: `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` decides how deep the box drop goes from the PAYLOAD SUB-PATTERN. Its `inner_struct_name` match arm is `PatternKind::Binding(_) if !scrutinee_is_borrow => .. pattern_binding_types.get(pkey) ..`, with `_ => None` for everything else. A WILDCARD payload therefore yields `None` and `track_boxed_enum_var` registers a box-ONLY free: the box allocation is reclaimed, the payload struct's `Vec`/`String` fields inside it are not.  The `_ => None` arm is CORRECT for a struct-DESTRUCTURE payload (`Some(H { v, .. })`), whose leaf bindings each own and free their own field -- walking the interior there would double-free, and the existing comment says so. The gap is that a WILDCARD binds nothing at all, so nobody owns the interior and the `_ => None` arm treats it like the destructure case. The fix has to distinguish binds-nothing from binds-the-parts, which the current match on `payload.kind` collapses.  SCOPE: also check `Some(_)` inside a tuple/struct sub-pattern that leaves SOME fields unbound, and the `Result` Err-side twin. The NAMED-source sibling of this shape is a different code path (`boxed_enum_payload_vars` + `BoxedEnumDrop`) and was not measured here.  PRE-EXISTING and independently attributed: stash-proven identical (vg=99, 32 bytes) before and after B-2026-08-04-1's fix, which changed only the BODY walk's subject and registers nothing at all for a wildcard arm (no payload binding => no registration site reached).  ORACLE NOTE: invisible to parity diffing and to fire counting -- AOT and `karac run` print the same thing and the Drop body correctly does not run -- so only valgrind/LSan sees it. Deliberately kept OUT of `asan_freshtemp_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box` (whose `d` case is this exact shape, minus the leak-triggering heap field) so LSan does not attribute this row's leak to that pin.  FIXED (2026-08-04, bad9a7a). The row's diagnosis was right about the `_ => None` arm and about needing to separate binds-nothing from binds-the-parts, but it missed a SECOND gate that had to move first: a wildcard carries no type, so `pattern_payload_word_count` falls to its 1-word default and the WIDTH check above the derivation rejected the arm before `inner_struct_name` could be reached at all. Splitting the `_ => None` arm alone changed nothing (measured). Both the size and the payload struct NAME now come from the SCRUTINEE's instantiation -- `optres_scrutinee_payload_struct_name_for`, reusing `optres_scrutinee_type_expr`, with the variant selecting which generic arg to read so `Result`'s Ok and Err halves cannot be crossed. The variant extraction was hoisted above the width gate to make that possible.  Borrow scrutinees stay excluded for the reason the `Binding` arm gives: their box interior aliases the container's storage, so zeroing or walking it would strand or double-free the container's buffers.  VERIFIED: probes b228/x1 (`Option`) and b228/x6 (`Result` Err side) go from 32 bytes definitely-lost to vg=0; the three controls -- whole binding (x2), named scrutinee (x5), inline payload (y3) -- are unchanged and clean. Suites: codegen 2775, memory_sanitizer 923, interpreter 1437, drop_differential 13, par_codegen 226 = 5374 passed, 0 failed.  NOT RE-RUN: the full `--features llvm` suite. Two full runs were green earlier in the session (12,912 and 12,914) but neither includes this commit.  WHAT THE SWEEP ALSO FOUND, and why this row's own scope note was well-placed: it asked whoever fixed this to check partial struct sub-patterns. Those probes never ran -- a struct destructure of a boxed payload PANICS the compiler (`ExtractOutOfRange`), filed as B-2026-08-04-5 (HIGH, ICE) and pre-existing. Its fix will make `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` reachable for the first time, which is where the partial-destructure ownership question actually gets answered.
fix: bad9a7a (src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs; pins memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_wildcard_boxed_optres_payload_frees_the_struct_interior, stash-proven RED under LeakSanitizer, covering the `Option` wildcard, the `Result` Err-side wildcard, and a whole-binding control)

title: INTERPRETER: a Drop-body move record is keyed by BINDING NAME and outlives its block, so a later same-named binding that was never moved is treated as moved and its user `impl Drop` body is silently skipped -- rename the second binding and the body fires
detail:
MINIMAL REPRO (probes b227/w1 vs b227/w2, interpreter only; AOT is correct in both, so this is a run-vs-build split on the `karac run` side). `struct Res { id: i64, name: String }` with a printing `impl Drop`, then two sibling blocks in one `main`:  BLOCK 1 -- `let o: Option[Res] = Option.Some(Res { .. }); let mut v: Vec[Res] = Vec.new(); match o { Option.Some(r) => { v.push(r); } .. } println(v[0].name);`  BLOCK 2 -- `let o2: Option[Res] = Option.Some(Res { .. }); match o2 { Option.Some(X) => { println(X.name); } .. }`  With X = `q` the interpreter prints `pay4 | D4 | pay6 | D6 | end` -- correct. With X = `r`, reusing block 1's binding name, it prints `pay4 | D4 | pay6 | end`: D6 is GONE. Nothing else differs.  So the move recorded for block 1's `r` (pushed into the Vec) is still live when block 2's unrelated `r` is bound, and suppresses that binding's body. The name is the whole trigger.  SCOPE, from a prefix bisect over a 7-block program (probes b227/c1..c1234): only the CONTAINER-PUSH move leaves the sticky record. A struct-literal move, a match-tail move, and a `let` rebind in block 1 all leave block 2's body firing. So the suspect is the push/insert consuming-arg move record specifically, not the general move bookkeeping -- start at the interpreter twin of `disarm_container_bodies_for_arg` (`record_container_bodies_move_sources` and its neighbours) and check whether its record is scoped to the enclosing block the way the let-RHS and aggregate-literal ones are.  HOW IT SURFACED, which is worth keeping: it was found while building the B-2026-08-04-2 regression pin. A 7-case E2E program was parity-equal on the five MOVE cases and diverged on the two CONTROLS -- AOT firing, interpreter silent -- while each control in ISOLATION was parity-equal. That shape (a test that passes case-by-case and fails combined) is the signature of exactly this kind of leaked per-name state, and it is a reason to be wary of the convenience of reusing `r` for every case in a multi-case pin. The B-2026-08-04-2 pin was consequently split: five move cases combined, both controls as their own single-case programs.  NOT CAUSED BY the B-2026-08-04-2 fix, which is codegen-only -- the interpreter path is untouched by it, and the AOT side of the same program is correct.

── FIXED 168c887 ──

The entry's suspicion was right and its pointer landed on the exact line. The
interpreter's move-out sets are keyed by BINDING NAME with no scope component,
so every site that rebinds a name has to RE-ARM it —
`rearm_container_bodies_for_name` exists for precisely that. `StmtKind::Let`
called it, `StmtKind::Assign` called it, and a MATCH ARM did not. One call
added at the arm's bind site (`interpreter/pattern_match.rs`, right after
`bind_pattern`) closes it.

REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly as filed. Two programs differing only in the second
arm's binding name:

    second binding `q`   interp: pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end   aot: pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end
    second binding `r`   interp: pay4 D4 pay6 end      aot: pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end
                                          ^^ D6 gone

After the fix both spellings print `pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end` on interp and AOT.

WHY IT WAS ONLY THE CONTAINER-PUSH MOVE, which the entry's prefix bisect had
already narrowed and which this explains: the let-RHS and aggregate-literal
move recorders run at sites that also REBIND, so their records were re-armed
incidentally by the `let` path. The push/insert consuming-arg record is made
inside a match arm, which had no re-arm at all, so its record was the only one
that could outlive its block.

THE TEST PINS BOTH SPELLINGS, not just the broken one
(`tests/interpreter.rs::match_arm_rebinding_a_moved_name_still_runs_its_drop_body`).
Pinning only the reused-name case would pass against a fix that broke the
distinct-name control, and asserting one output would not express the actual
invariant, which is that the two must be EQUAL — a binding's name must not
change observable drop behaviour.

WORTH KEEPING from the entry, because it generalises past this bug: the defect
surfaced as a 7-case E2E that was parity-equal case-by-case and diverged only
when the cases were COMBINED. A test that passes in isolation and fails in
combination is the signature of leaked per-name interpreter state, and it is a
standing argument against reusing one convenient binding name across the cases
of a multi-case pin.

title: ICE: destructuring a heap-BOXED Option/Result payload with a STRUCT sub-pattern (`match o { Some(Full { name, buf }) => .. }`) panics the compiler with `ExtractOutOfRange` -- `build_extract_value` runs against the Option aggregate instead of the deboxed payload
detail: REPRO (probes b228/y1 named scrutinee, b228/y2 fresh temp -- BOTH panic, so it is not a scrutinee-shape gap): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` (6 words, BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area), then `match o { Option.Some(Full { name, buf }) => { println(name); println(buf.len()); } Option.None => {} }`.  `karac build` aborts with `thread panicked at src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ExtractOutOfRange` -- a compiler CRASH on a well-typed program, not a diagnostic. `karac check` is clean, so nothing warns first.  CONTROL (probe b228/y3): the same destructure over an INLINE payload (`struct Narrow { name: String }`, 3 words) compiles and runs clean on both backends. BOXING is the discriminator, as everywhere else in this family.  SITE: the `PatternKind::Struct` arm of `bind_pattern_values`. An earlier branch handles the INLINE payload by extracting the enum aggregate's payload WORDS and reconstructing each field; a boxed payload falls past it to the plain struct-destructure fallback, which does `build_extract_value(sv, idx, "field")` with `sv` still being the `Option` aggregate `{tag, w0, w1, w2}` and `idx` a field index into `Full`. The fallback assumes `scrut` is already the payload struct value. The boxed path never deboxes -- w0 holds the box POINTER, and the fields have to be loaded through it.  NOTE that `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` exists and is written specifically for this shape (it cap-zeroes the consumed fields INSIDE the box so the box drop skips them). That suppressor is therefore unreachable today for a whole-struct destructure of a boxed payload: codegen panics before it can matter. Whoever fixes the debox should check that the suppressor then does the right thing, and that the partial form (`Some(Full { name, buf: _ })`, probe b228/x4, same panic) leaves the UNBOUND field owned by the box.  PRE-EXISTING and independently attributed: the same panic reproduces with `src/` checked out at e51d795, this session's base commit (same site, line 1320 there vs 1401 at 604f765 -- the shift is purely from insertions above it).  HOW IT SURFACED: while probing the wildcard-payload leak (B-2026-08-04-3), whose row asked whoever fixes it to also check partial struct sub-patterns. Those probes never got as far as running.  DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION (2026-08-04, same day, before any fix attempt). This row's SITE paragraph says the boxed path "never deboxes". That is too strong and would send the next attempt down the wrong road. Reading the code, the debox machinery is all present and looks like it should fire for this shape:  (1) `reconstruct_payload_value` has an explicit debox arm gated on `want > field_words.len() && !field_words.is_empty()` -- it inttoptrs word 0, loads `pattern_payload_llvm_type(sub_pat)` through it, and re-splits via `coerce_to_payload_words`.  (2) `pattern_payload_word_count` HAS a `PatternKind::Struct` arm that returns the named struct's full LLVM word count (added for the "Undefined variable" class), so `want` should be 6 for `Full`, not the 1-word default.  (3) `pattern_payload_llvm_type` HAS a matching `PatternKind::Struct` arm, so the load should produce a real `Full` value.  With all three in place `want`(6) > `field_words.len()`(3) ought to hold and the Struct bind arm ought to receive a 2-field `Full` StructValue, on which `build_extract_value(sv, 0|1)` is in range. It panics anyway, so ONE of those three is not doing what its code reads like for this scrutinee -- e.g. `field_words` arriving longer than 3, `want` resolving to something small because the path segment is not found in `struct_types` at that point, or this Struct sub-pattern reaching `bind_pattern_values` by a route that never calls `reconstruct_payload_value` at all.  START BY INSTRUMENTING rather than by adding a debox: print `want`, `field_words.len()` and the incoming `scrut` type at the Struct arm for probe b228/y1. The answer is which of the three is lying, and the fix follows from that. Adding a second debox path without knowing would likely double-load.  ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-08-04, instrumented per the note above; partial fix written, measured, then REVERTED unfinished -- nothing landed). It is a NAME COLLISION, not a debox gap at all. `variant_pattern_enum_name` resolves a bare single-segment path by searching variant names across every known enum INCLUDING THE PRELUDE'S, and the prelude declares `enum ChannelError { Full, .. }`. So the user's `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }`, destructured as `Full { name, buf }`, resolves to `Some("ChannelError")`. Measured directly: `[B5] reconstruct kind=Struct["Full"] want=1 field_words=3 enum_name=Some("ChannelError") in_struct_types=Some(true)`.  BOTH payload-sizing arms then take their enum branch, miss `enum_layouts` for `ChannelError`, and fall to their defaults -- `pattern_payload_word_count` to 1 and `pattern_payload_llvm_type` to i64. With `want`=1 the debox predicate `want > field_words.len()` (1 > 3) is FALSE, so no debox happens; `coerce_to_payload_words` builds a `{ i64 }`, and the Struct bind arm's `build_extract_value(sv, 1)` on a 1-field aggregate is the `ExtractOutOfRange`. Every step of the earlier diagnosis-correction was right that the debox machinery is fine -- it simply never gets asked.  This is the same CLASS as B-2026-08-03-5 (a user type whose name collided with a generic enum's PARAMETER name gained a phantom Drop walker). Renaming the struct to anything the prelude does not use as a variant name makes the program compile, which is the one-line bisect.  PARTIAL FIX, measured but NOT landed: adding a `struct_pattern_path_is_user_struct(path)` predicate (single segment AND present in `struct_types`) and guarding the enum branch of BOTH sizing arms with it moves `want` from 1 to 6 and makes the debox fire (`[B5] want=6 fw=3`). The ICE PERSISTS at the same bind site even so, so there is a SECOND consumer downstream still handing a `{ i64 }` -- or re-deriving the wrong type -- after reconstruction. Next step is to re-print the Struct arm's incoming `scrut.get_type()` with the two sizing arms fixed: if it is still `{ i64 }`, the reconstruction path for a Struct sub-pattern is not rebuilding the aggregate; if it is a proper `Full`, the panic has moved to a different index computation.  The two-arm guard is a prerequisite either way and is the right shape -- it just is not sufficient alone. Whoever picks this up should reapply it first, then instrument the bind site.  ALSO WORTH CHECKING once it compiles: `variant_pattern_enum_name` is consulted from many other sites, so the same prelude-variant collision may mis-route decisions beyond these two. A user `struct Full`, `Empty`, `Closed` (or any other prelude variant name) is the general hazard, and a targeted audit of that fn's callers is probably worth more than this one ICE.  THIRD AND FINAL NARROWING (2026-08-04, measured, still not landed). With the two-arm guard applied so `want`=6 and the debox fires, the Struct bind arm STILL receives `{ i64 }`: `[B5-bind] Full scrut=StructType("{ i64 }")`. So `reconstruct_payload_value` is not packing the deboxed words back into the payload struct's aggregate -- it has an explicit `PatternKind::Tuple` arm that rebuilds a tuple element-by-element, and NO `PatternKind::Struct` counterpart, so a struct sub-pattern falls through to the single-word default no matter how many words the debox produced.  THE FIX IS THEREFORE TWO PARTS, both needed, neither sufficient alone: (1) the `struct_pattern_path_is_user_struct` guard on both sizing arms, so `want` and the LLVM type are right and the debox runs; and (2) a `PatternKind::Struct` arm in `reconstruct_payload_value` that packs `field_words` into the struct's LLVM aggregate field-by-field, mirroring the Tuple arm right above it (walk the struct's field types, slice the words per field width, `insertvalue` each). With both, the bind arm receives a real 2-field `Full` and the extract is in range.  Everything above was measured on probe b229/y1 with temporary instrumentation; nothing was committed. The remaining work is writing part (2), then the usual verification -- and note the INLINE control (b228/y3) already works, so whatever the new arm does must leave the non-boxed path byte-identical.  CORRECTION TO THE PRECEDING PARAGRAPH (same session, on further reading): part (2) is NOT "add a `PatternKind::Struct` arm to `reconstruct_payload_value`". One effectively exists already -- `binding_is_struct` there is explicitly true for a `PatternKind::Struct` whose path names a `struct_types` entry (the slice-3t 1-word-struct case), and with the sizing guard in place `want_words` is 6, so the `(want_words <= 1 || field_words.len() <= 1) && !binding_is_struct` single-word gate is NOT taken and control reaches the multi-word struct-building path below it.  So the remaining defect is INSIDE that multi-word struct-building path: with `want`=6, the debox firing and the single-word gate bypassed, the Struct bind arm still receives `{ i64 }` (measured: `[B5-bind] Full scrut=StructType("{ i64 }")`). Read that path next -- it is the code immediately after the `want_words` gate in `reconstruct_payload_value` -- and find where it derives the aggregate type it builds into. The suspicion is that it re-derives from something that still resolves `Full` through the enum-variant route rather than from `pattern_payload_llvm_type`, in which case the guard needs applying at a third site; but that is UNVERIFIED and should be measured, not assumed.  Part (1) -- the `struct_pattern_path_is_user_struct` guard on both sizing arms -- remains verified and necessary: it demonstrably moves `want` from 1 to 6. Reapply it first.  AUDIT of `variant_pattern_enum_name`'s callers (2026-08-04, read-only; this is the broader item the row asked for).  COLLISION SURFACE. The fn never consults `struct_types` at all. Its order is: qualified `E.V` -> the match scrutinee's enum hint -> ANY enum carrying that variant name, preferring user enums but FALLING BACK TO SEEDED ones. So a bare name that is a user STRUCT resolves to a prelude enum whenever no user enum claims it. The seeded variant names, from the 14 enums registered in `declarations.rs` (`seeded_enum_names`), are: AlreadyExists, Array, Bool, Display, Env, Equal, Full, Greater, IncompleteSequence, Int, InteriorNul, Interrupted, InvalidByte, InvalidUtf8, Less, None, NotFound, NotPresent, NotUnicode, Null, Number, Object, Other, PermissionDenied, Some, String, Timeout, UnexpectedEof. Several are entirely plausible user struct names -- `Display`, `Object`, `Number`, `Int`, `Timeout`, `NotFound`, `Full`, `Other`, `Env`.  17 CALL SITES, classified:  (a) CONFIRMED HARMFUL -- the six inside `pattern_payload_word_count` (3 arms) and `pattern_payload_llvm_type` (3 arms). These recurse over SUB-patterns, so `Some(Display { .. })` reaches them, and a mis-resolve silently yields the 1-word / i64 default. That is this row's ICE.  (b) NARROW BY VARIANT NAME -- `compile_match`'s scrutinee-shape derivations and `set_scrutinee_shape_flags_for_pattern` (5 sites) only act on the answer when it is literally "Option" or "Result", so they can only misfire for a user type named `Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Err`. Implausible but not impossible, and the failure would be a wrong payload-area/boxing classification -- i.e. the same memory-corruption family this session spent the day on, not a crash.  (c) SELF-CORRECTING BY ACCIDENT -- `bind_pattern_values` (1 site) takes the enum branch but then looks up `enum_variant_struct_field_names(enum, variant)`, which returns None for a unit variant, so it falls through to the struct path. Right answer, wrong reason; a seeded enum that ever gains a STRUCT variant of the same name would turn this into a silent mis-bind.  (d) GATED ON A SUBSEQUENT LOOKUP -- the four freshtemp/shared-enum trackers (`materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee`, `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee`, `track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee`, `drop_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee_on_miss`) each require the resolved name to pass a further test (an Option/Result area, a `shared_types` entry, a drop-kind layout) that a mis-resolve fails, so they decline rather than misfire. Declining is a LEAK on the safe side, not a corruption -- but it means a user `struct Full` silently loses its box tracking, which is exactly the shape of B-2026-08-04-3.  RECOMMENDATION, which supersedes this row's two-site guard: put the struct preference INSIDE `variant_pattern_enum_name`, not at the call sites. One site instead of six, and it fixes classes (a) and (d) together. Restrict it to `PatternKind::Struct` (leave TupleVariant and Binding alone -- a bare `Int(v)` tuple-variant pattern must still resolve through the scrutinee hint) and place it AFTER the qualified and scrutinee-hint checks, so `match tok { Int(v) => .. }` with both `enum Token { Int }` and `struct Int` in scope keeps binding to `Token`. A `PatternKind::Struct` whose single-segment path names a `struct_types` entry is unambiguously a struct destructure -- there is no syntax where it means a unit variant.  NOT DONE HERE: the audit is read-only. No code changed.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 9908f6a). The final narrowing above was right that the collision is the whole story, and WRONG about where the third site was: the multi-word struct-building path in `reconstruct_payload_value` is fine. `reconstruct_payload_value` never reached it -- the `enum_layout_type_for_variant_pattern` branch ABOVE the single-word gate returns early, and it resolves through `variant_pattern_enum_and_tag`, a SECOND copy of the same bare-name scan that `variant_pattern_enum_name` has. `ChannelError`'s unit-only layout is literally `{ i64 }`, which is exactly the aggregate the bind arm was measured receiving. Guarding one resolver and instrumenting downstream of the other is why the earlier attempts kept finding the same `{ i64 }` in a new place.  SHIPPED SHAPE, per the audit's recommendation: one predicate, `struct_pattern_names_a_user_struct` -- a `PatternKind::Struct` whose single-segment path names a `struct_types` entry and whose name the match scrutinee's own enum does not claim -- consulted from THREE sites rather than guarding six callers: both resolvers (after their qualified and scrutinee-hint checks) and the arm-CONDITION guard in `compile_match`. That third site was not in the audit and had to be found by probing: it uses `enum_tag_for_variant`, a third bare-name lookup with no struct awareness, so with only the two resolvers guarded a plain `struct Item` scrutinee matched by `Item { a }` (with `enum Holder { Item { .. } }` in scope) stopped ICE-ing and started tag-comparing the struct's first field against `Holder.Item`'s tag, falling through every arm and returning junk -- an ICE traded for a SILENT WRONG ANSWER. Probe b230/y6a; the fix covers it, and b230/y6b (the same bare name over a scrutinee that IS the enum) proves the scrutinee-hint escape keeps the variant reading.  The `PatternKind::Struct` restriction is deliberate and load-bearing: a bare `Int(v)` TupleVariant pattern must still resolve through the scrutinee hint when a `struct Int` is in scope, and no syntax spells a unit variant as `Name { .. }`.  AUDIT CLASSES (a) and (d) are both closed by this -- the six sizing-arm callers and the four freshtemp/shared trackers all go through one of the two resolvers. Class (b) (the five Option/Result-literal comparisons) and class (c) (`bind_pattern_values`' self-correcting lookup) were assessed as safe and are unchanged.  VERIFIED on probes b230/y1..y10 and t1..t3: named scrutinee, fresh temp, `Result`'s Err half, partial destructure (`buf: _` and `..`), if-let, while-let over `Vec.pop`, the INLINE 3-word control, a plain-struct scrutinee, and all three collision tiers -- every one correct, AOT/interp parity-EQUAL, valgrind 0. Targeted suites green.  SUPPRESSOR NOTE, answering this row's own question: with the debox now firing, `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` is reachable for the first time and the leaf bindings own the interior exactly once -- pinned under ASAN/LSan.  RESIDUAL FOUND AND FILED SEPARATELY (B-2026-08-04-6): a FRESH-TEMP scrutinee whose struct destructure leaves the `Vec` field UNBOUND leaks that buffer. Kept OUT of the ASAN pin so LeakSanitizer does not attribute it there.
fix: 9908f6a (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_deboxes and ::e2e_struct_pattern_wins_over_a_same_named_enum_variant, both stash-proven RED with the exact `ExtractOutOfRange` ICE, their interpreter oracles interpreter.rs::test_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_deboxes and ::test_struct_pattern_wins_over_a_same_named_enum_variant, and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_owns_the_interior_once for the ownership side the debox made reachable)

title: A FRESH-TEMP boxed Option/Result scrutinee destructured by a PARTIAL struct sub-pattern (`match mk() { Some(Full { name, buf: _ }) => .. }`) leaks the unbound `Vec` field's buffer -- the box drop stays box-ONLY for any struct destructure, which is right when every field is bound and wrong when some are not
detail: REPRO (probes b230/p1, p2, p3 -- 32 bytes definitely lost under valgrind each, parity-EQUAL so no run-vs-build split): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }`, `fn opt(i: i64) -> Option[Full] { return Option.Some(mk(i)); }`, and `match opt(4i64) { Option.Some(Full { name, buf: _ }) => { println(name); } Option.None => {} }`. `Full` is 6 words, so it is BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area. The `..` spelling (`Full { name, .. }`, p2) and the `Result` Err-side twin (p3) leak identically.  CLEAN CONTROLS, which is what localizes it: the NAMED-scrutinee twin (p6 -- `let o: Option[Full] = ...; match o { ... }`) is vg=0; the FULL destructure from a fresh temp (p5) is vg=0; and the whole-binding form is vg=0. So it is specifically fresh-temp + partial.  MECHANISM: `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` derives `inner_struct_name` from the payload sub-pattern. A `PatternKind::Struct` destructure falls into the `_ => None` arm and the free goes box-ONLY. That arm is CORRECT for a FULL destructure -- each leaf binding owns and frees its field, so walking the interior would double-free -- and it is what B-2026-08-04-3 deliberately left alone when it split the WILDCARD case out. A PARTIAL destructure is the third case neither answer fits: some fields are owned by bindings, the rest by nobody. Fixing it needs a FIELD-SELECTIVE walker (free exactly the unbound fields), not a whole-struct one -- that is why it is not a one-line extension of the wildcard arm.  THE "STRING IS CLEAN" ASYMMETRY IS AN ARTIFACT -- resolved, do not chase it. First pass observed that only an unbound `Vec` field leaks: probe p7 (`Full { name: _, buf }`, with a deliberately long f-string) and p9 (a 3-field `Two` with the middle `String` unbound) were both vg=0, which read like something already owning an unbound String. It does not. Valgrind's ALLOCATION COUNT gives it away: p5 (both fields bound) does 5 allocs, p7 does 3. The String was never allocated -- nothing in the whole program ever reads that field, so LLVM elides the malloc outright, and an allocation that does not happen cannot leak. This is the same dead-allocation false-negative that has misled this bug family twice before.  DECISIVE PROBE b230/p10: same shape, but the String is built by mutation (`String.new()` + two `push_str`, the second from an f-string) so the buffer is genuinely materialized, and the struct is padded to 6 words with scalars so boxing does not depend on the String's width. Result: 4 allocs / 3 frees, 76 bytes DEFINITELY LOST. An unbound `String` field leaks exactly like an unbound `Vec` field.  So the rule is uniform and the fix does not need a per-field-type carve-out: for a fresh-temp scrutinee, EVERY field the struct pattern leaves unbound is unowned. A field-selective walker over the unbound set is the whole fix. Corollary for whoever writes it: any probe here MUST force the allocation (mutate the buffer, or read it) or a broken fix will measure clean.  MECHANISM CONFIRMED, and it explains the named-vs-fresh split exactly: the NAMED path already handles this. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` walks the struct pattern's fields and skips any `field: _` sub-pattern with the comment "the box keeps that field" -- so bound fields get their cap zeroed inside the box and unbound ones stay owned by the box's inner-struct walker. That suppressor bails at its first line for a fresh temp, because it requires `ExprKind::Identifier` for the scrutinee. The fresh-temp side has no equivalent: `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` decides whole-interior vs box-only from the sub-pattern KIND alone and has no third option. Porting the named path's per-field decision to the fresh-temp tracker is the shape to aim for.  PRE-EXISTING in the sense that matters: the shape did not COMPILE before 9908f6a (it ICE'd -- B-2026-08-04-5), so this leak has never shipped in a working program. It is nonetheless a genuine gap in the box-drop ownership model, not a regression from that fix, which changed only name resolution.  ORACLE NOTE: invisible to parity diffing and to fire counting -- AOT and `karac run` print the same thing -- so only valgrind/LSan sees it. Deliberately kept OUT of `memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_owns_the_interior_once` (whose partial case is the clean NAMED-scrutinee twin) so LSan does not attribute this row's leak to that pin.  SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while verifying B-2026-08-04-5's fix, which is what made the shape compilable and therefore measurable at all -- and which is what B-2026-08-04-3's scope note predicted would happen.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 7ecdec0). Shipped as the shape this row's own mechanism note pointed at: the NAMED path's per-field split, ported to the fresh temp rather than reinvented. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure`'s body is now shared; a fresh-temp entry point takes the box slot `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` already stages (the same `__freshtemp_boxed_scrut` alloca B-2026-08-04-3 started returning), and the tracker gained a `PatternKind::Struct` arm that walks the WHOLE interior. The two halves meet in the middle: the suppressor cap-zeroes every BOUND field inside the box before the walk can reach it, so per field the binding frees what it took and the box frees the rest. All-fields-bound degenerates exactly to the old box-only behavior -- every cap zeroed, walk is a no-op -- which is what makes the tracker arm safe to apply unconditionally rather than only to partial patterns.  ONE TIGHTENING BEYOND THE ROW, and it is UNPROVEN: the disarm condition was `Wildcard`-only, so a field the pattern merely TESTS (`Full { name: "x", buf }`) was disarmed with nothing taking ownership -- a leak by the same argument. It now asks whether the sub-pattern binds anything, via a codegen-local `pattern_binds_anything` mirroring the `use_classifier` one. This is a correctness tightening on BOTH paths, but probe b230/p11 (a literal-test on a String field, named scrutinee) is vg=0 at base too, so no program was found where the old condition observably leaked. Recorded as reasoning, not as a measured fix.  VERIFIED: 25 probes (b230/p1..p11, t1..t3, y1..y10) -- all correct, AOT/interp parity-EQUAL, valgrind 0. The four that leaked at base are the load-bearing ones: p1 (`buf: _`), p2 (`..`), p3 (`Result` Err side) at 32 bytes each, and p10 (the non-elidable String half) at 76. Suites: codegen 2777, memory_sanitizer 925, interpreter 1440, drop_differential 13, par_codegen 226 = 5381 passed, 0 failed.  THE PIN CARRIES THIS ROW'S PROBE-HYGIENE WARNING IN ITS FIXTURE, not just its comment: both `String`s are built by MUTATION and every bound field is read, because an unread field's malloc is elided outright (5 allocs vs 3, measured) and an elided allocation cannot leak. A lazier fixture passes against a completely broken fix. Stash-proven RED under LeakSanitizer at 19,200 bytes.
fix: 7ecdec0 (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/control_flow.rs; pins memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_freshtemp_boxed_payload_partial_destructure_owns_every_field, stash-proven RED under LeakSanitizer at 19,200 bytes, covering `field: _`, `..`, the String half, the `Result` Err side, and an all-fields-bound control for the double-free direction)

title: EVERY project-mode `karac build` fails immediately: it opens the PACKAGE NAME as a source path (`error: cannot read 'solo'`), so a manifest-driven build cannot run at all -- 36 tests/cli.rs cases fail on main
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while running the full suite to verify B-2026-08-03-12. Not caused by that
change -- `tests/cli.rs` fails 524 passed / 36 failed identically with and without it (the
change was stashed and the suite re-run to confirm).

REPRODUCTION, by hand, four lines:

    mkdir -p /tmp/p/src
    printf '[package]\nname = "solo"\n' > /tmp/p/kara.toml
    printf 'fn main() {}\n'              > /tmp/p/src/main.kara
    cd /tmp/p && karac build
    error: cannot read 'solo': No such file or directory (os error 2)

That fixture is copied verbatim from
`test_build_offline_no_deps_project_succeeds_without_vendor`, so it is the contract the suite
itself asserts.

BLAST RADIUS IS ALL OF PROJECT MODE, not the offline path the failing test names:

    karac build              -> cannot read 'solo'
    karac build --offline    -> cannot read 'solo'
    karac build --release    -> cannot read 'solo'
    karac check              -> "missing file argument"   (separate: project mode unsupported)

`strace` confirms the literal package name is opened relative to CWD, once:

    openat(AT_FDCWD, "solo", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT

so the manifest IS found and parsed -- `solo` is its `[package] name` -- and the failure is
downstream, where the package name reaches a slot expecting a source path. The message comes
from `read_source` (src/cli.rs:911), which `process::exit(1)`s, so the build dies before any
compilation. Arg parsing is NOT at fault: with no positional the parser correctly produces
`Command::BuildProject` (src/cli/args.rs, `match file { Some(f) => Build, None =>
BuildProject }`). The read site is deeper than `cmd_build_project`'s prologue; that is where
to start.

WHY HIGH: project mode is the manifest-driven build path -- the only way to compile a
multi-file package -- and it is not degraded but completely non-functional, on the default
invocation, with an error that names a package rather than a path so it reads as user error.

NOT BISECTED. Main advanced by roughly sixty commits during this session and rebuilding at
candidate parents was not affordable here; `fac3bf2` ("honor -o/--out for executable builds")
is the nearest suspect by area, but its subject is an OUTPUT path while this is a READ, so

Related: B-2026-08-03-12 (the entry whose verification run surfaced this).

FIXED (2026-08-04, 4c52d82) -- and BISECTED, which this row asked for first. The suspect named above (`fac3bf2`, `-o`/`--out` handling) is NOT it; the row's own instinct that an OUTPUT-path change is the wrong shape for a READ failure was right.
