Four matched karac+archive sides, each built at its own commit, archive configuration held constant (LEAN pinned via `KARAC_RUNTIME` on every side), `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0`, every binary sink-checked at 762965 before timing, `hyperfine --warmup 5 --runs 25 --shell=none` in BOTH orders, plus exact `scripts/pmc.c` counters. The two middle sides did not exist before: `KARAC_MAP_TAG` postdates 58412d9f, so "58412d9f without its tag compare" was previously unmeasurable. It was produced by patching that commit's own `emit_mono_map_get_body` to call `emit_map_is_occupied` -- exactly what the shipped fix does on arm64 -- and, for the fourth side, by ALSO swapping that commit's occupancy test to the flag form described below.

  a42b5338 (= 58412d9f~1)                        768.7 / 767.0 ms
  58412d9f, tag compare removed + FLAG-form test 770.7 / 786.9 ms   <- PARENT LEVEL
  58412d9f, tag compare removed (sign-form test) 894.1 / 908.0 ms   <- 1.16-1.18x
  current main (tag off, sign-form test)         859.0 / 859.3 ms   <- 1.12x

ANSWER 1 -- AT 58412d9f THE NON-TAG REGRESSION IS ENTIRELY THE OCCUPANCY TEST'S LOWERING, and it is fully recoverable there. The commit changed what the control byte holds, which changed how "is this bucket occupied" is written: `status >= 0x80` (a SIGN-BIT test) instead of the parent's `status == 1`. On arm64 those lower differently -- `ldrsb` + `tbz` versus `ldrb` + `cmp` + `b.cc` -- and the three-instruction form with a flag-setting compare is FASTER than the two-instruction test-and-branch. Writing the identical predicate as `status > TOMBSTONE` (exactly equivalent: the only bytes below 0x80 are EMPTY=0 and TOMBSTONE=1) restores the flag form and recovers the parent's time to within noise.

ANSWER 2 -- AND YET THAT FIX IS WORTH NOTHING ON CURRENT MAIN. The same one-line swap, on current main, moves kata:170 from 859.0 to 855.2 ms, i.e. nothing; and on kata:219 it is 1.01-1.03x WORSE. So the mechanism that costs 1.16x at 58412d9f is no longer live: something in the ~800 commits since changed the surrounding code enough that the sign-bit form stopped being penalised. The lowering hazard is therefore LATENT, not current -- worth knowing before anyone "fixes" it, because the obvious fix is measurably useless today.

ANSWER 3 -- WHERE THE LIVE RESIDUAL ACTUALLY IS: the ~800 commits after 58412d9f. Holding the test form constant at the flag form, 58412d9f measures 770 ms and current main measures 855 ms; holding it at the sign form, 58412d9f measures 894-908 ms and current main 859 ms. Either way current main sits ~1.11x above where 58412d9f lands once its own regression is undone. That interval is UNBISECTED and is what this row now needs. NOTE the earlier "+1.4% from 58412d9f to current" figure this row used for its arithmetic was measured with the tag ON, where the tag compare dominated and masked this; it does not survive as an argument once the tag is off.

RULED OUT ALONG THE WAY, both by measurement:
  * THE keys() WALK. This row and its predecessors repeatedly suspected `control_flow_for.rs`'s occupancy test in the `keys()` iteration, since kata:170 runs it ~1.23B times. An ablation that keeps the walk and drops the gets measures a42 471M cycles vs current main 476M -- equal -- while instructions FALL 8.3%. The walk is also only ~12% of the kata's cycles, not the majority this row assumed.
  * THE BUCKET LAYOUT. Diffed rather than assumed: 58412d9f changes no allocation, no stride, no alignment. `status[capacity]` and the kv array are byte-for-byte the same shape as at the parent; only the byte's VALUE and the tests over it change.

A METHOD WARNING WORTH MORE THAN THE ABOVE, because it nearly produced a wrong fix. An ablation of kata:170 that keeps the gets and drops the `keys()` walk -- same map, same key distribution, same 201.6M gets, keys materialised into a `Vec` once outside the timed loop -- reports the flag-form test as a 1.34x WIN. The real kata reports 1.00x for the same change. The probe over-responds by more than twenty times, and it was deliberately built to be faithful. This row already carries one refuted synthetic probe (the high-load-factor one); this is a second, subtler instance, and the rule it argues for is: an ablation may be used to LOCATE a cost, never to SIZE a fix. Every number that decided anything here was taken on the unmodified kata.

WHAT THIS ROW NEEDS TO CLOSE, unchanged in shape but now correctly aimed: bisect kata:170 across 58412d9f..main (~800 commits, arm64, matched karac+archive per step, sink-checked, tag-off held constant on both sides via `KARAC_MAP_TAG=0` so the shipped fix does not confound the comparison). The endpoints are verified: 770 ms and 855 ms with the test form held constant.

 RESIDUAL FULLY ATTRIBUTED — AND IT IS NOT A MAP PROBLEM AT ALL (2026-08-06). Bisected across the 905 commits this row identified, 8 steps, on CYCLES (the endpoints differ 8.3% in cycles and 0.003% in instructions, so the instruction-count method this repo prefers is blind here), with the tag compare patched off and the occupancy test held in the flag form at every step so the range's two opposing effects could not cancel. Every binary sink-checked at 762965.

THE CULPRIT IS 36a7fa5a (2026-07-30, "make println line-atomic by staging payload+newline into one write", B-2026-07-30-9). Parent b84477dd 3.561B cycles / 781 ms; 36a7fa5a 3.958B / 850 ms; 1.09x on wall clock in both orders, and the 777 commits after it all sit on the slow plateau. kata:170 calls `println` ONCE.

The carrier is CODE PLACEMENT, not work: instructions differ by 0.008%, the binaries are EXACTLY the same size (285,592 B both), `main`'s prologue is identical (`sub sp, sp, #0x80`), and the 4 KiB staging alloca lives in the new helper rather than in the caller. What moves is `_main`'s address, 0x7c8 -> 0x860.

FILED AS B-2026-08-07-10, which owns it from here.

SO THIS ROW'S ARITHMETIC IS COMPLETE: the 7-bit tag compare (1.14x, fixed by the arch x key-type gate) times the placement effect (1.09x) is 1.24x, against the 1.29x this row opened with; the remainder is drift across the range. Nothing map-shaped is left unexplained, which is why every map-shaped hypothesis this row chased — the keys() walk, the bucket layout, the load factor, the encoding — measured clean. CLOSING.
fix: c4e6d76e (the tag compare); the placement half is B-2026-08-07-10
tracker: CLOSED 2026-08-06. Two unrelated causes, both now attributed by measurement: the 7-bit tag compare (1.14x) fixed in c4e6d76e by the arch x key-type gate in src/codegen/mono.rs::map_tag_compare, and code placement from 36a7fa5a (1.09x), which is NOT a map issue and is owned by B-2026-08-07-10. Follow-on B-2026-08-06-33 is also CLOSED (2026-08-07): the x86 primitive-key sign was measured on a quiet x86_64 host and the tag PAYS there (kata:170 +12.2% to drop it, distributions disjoint, A/A control 0.2%; kata:128 Set +5.4%; kata:217/219 neutral), so the arch condition is load-bearing on evidence rather than on an unresolved dispute, and the x86 Set probe is no longer unmeasured.

title: Bounds checks survive in a CALLEE that walks a caller-owned buffer at a caller-chosen offset — `fn f(v: ref Vec[u8], base: i64, len: i64) { while lo <= hi { v[base+lo] .. v[base+hi] } }`. The bound holds only ACROSS the call boundary (every caller passes `base = k*len` with `k < n`, and `v.len() == n*len`), and every BCE analysis in bce_length_pin.rs is per-function by construction, so no local fact exists to prove. Carries the whole of kata #246's residual 1.28x vs equal-safety C. Survives INLINING (measured), and LLVM's IRCE does not reach it either (measured, byte-identical assembly). Split off B-2026-08-04-8, whose intra-function shape is fixed.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the residual half of B-2026-08-04-8 (closed e94e6bd9 + 55f3d4a3),
carved out when that entry's named shape — the converging base-offset scan
written INLINE — was finished. Everything below was measured on the x86
container while working that entry; none of it is hypothesised.

THE SHAPE. Kata #246's punch loop, verbatim:

    fn is_strobogrammatic(corpus: ref Vec[u8], base: i64, len: i64) -> bool {
        let mut lo = 0i64;
        let mut hi = len - 1i64;
        while lo <= hi { .. corpus[base + lo] .. corpus[base + hi] .. }
    }

There is no fill loop, no enclosing counter, and no length pin in this function.
`base + lo < corpus.len()` is TRUE at run time only because of a caller
invariant. This is the ordinary 'hand a helper a row of a flat buffer' shape —
matrix row operations, fixed-stride record scans, per-row palindrome and
two-pointer checks — so it is not specific to #246.

WHY THE PARENT'S FIX CANNOT BE EXTENDED TO IT. `compute_converging_skips`,
`compute_descending_skips` and `compute_vec_length_pins` all take `&Block` and
scan `func.body`. Each of the three facts they compose (a length pin on `v`, an
enclosing counter bounding the row index, a linear `base` in that counter) is
established by a STATEMENT in the same function. Here all three arrive as
parameter values. No amount of strengthening the per-function analysis reaches
this; it needs a fact that crosses the call.

TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT CLOSE OFF THE CHEAP ROUTES, both worth recording because
both look like they should work:

(1) INLINING DOES NOT RESCUE IT. B-2026-08-04-8's EVIDENCE 2 already proves this
    though it does not draw the conclusion: `is_strobogrammatic` is FULLY
    INLINED into `main` in both binaries, and adding Kara-equivalent bounds
    checks to the C mirror makes clang -O3 emit a loop instruction-for-
    instruction isomorphic to kara's — 21 instructions, checks intact. That is
    clang with full post-inline visibility declining to eliminate them. So
    'emit it and let LLVM see through the call' is not a plan.

(2) IRCE IS NOT THE ANSWER EITHER. LLVM ships inductive range-check elimination
    and it is NOT in the `default<O2>` pipeline karac runs, which makes enabling
    it look like a one-line win. Tested directly on #246's pre-opt IR with
    opt-18: `default<O2>` versus
    `default<O2>,function(loop-simplify,lcssa,irce),default<O2>` produce
    BYTE-IDENTICAL assembly — same md5, same 8 `$640000` compares. IRCE does not
    match this shape: the index is a SUM `base + j` whose range is fixed JOINTLY
    by two co-moving induction variables, not by one affine IV against a
    loop-invariant bound. Recorded so the pipeline-flag idea is not re-derived
    by the next person who notices IRCE is off.

FIX DIRECTIONS, both real features rather than extensions:

  (A) INTERPROCEDURAL PRECONDITION. Infer `base + len <= v.len()` as a callee
      precondition from the index sites, discharge it at every call site with
      the machinery that already exists per-function (the call sites in #246 DO
      have the pin, the counter and the linear base locally), and skip the check
      only when every reachable call site discharges it. Fails closed on any
      address-taken / externally-callable function. This is the direct fix and
      it is the first interprocedural analysis in the compiler, which is the
      reason it is scoped separately rather than tacked on.

  (B) LOOP VERSIONING. Emit a checked and an unchecked copy of the loop, chosen
      by ONE widened test in the preheader. Note this is the semantics-preserving
      form: naive PREDICATION — hoisting the widened check and deleting the
      per-iteration ones — would move WHERE a panicking program panics (a
      program that reads 3 valid elements and then goes out of range must
      produce those 3 iterations' effects before panicking), so it is not a
      legal rewrite for Kara's checked semantics. Versioning costs code size and
      needs a profitability gate.

SIZING, so this is not mistaken for a small job: (A) touches the analysis
pipeline's shape, not just codegen, and needs a call-graph pass plus a
conservative escape/visibility rule; (B) is contained in codegen but needs the
duplication machinery and a heuristic. Neither is a slice.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. On #246, the full 1.28x — the entire remaining gap to
equal-safety C, since B-2026-08-04-8's EVIDENCE 2 showed karac's codegen is at
clang -O3 parity on this kata once safety is equalized. On a work-identical
minimal probe the missing elision alone measured 1.93x. NOT a correctness issue:
the checks are sound, just not elided. The kata is NOT written around it and
must not be — it stays the natural converging two-pointer.

METHOD NOTE, carried over from the parent because it cost real time: timing this
shape is corpus-size dependent in a way that INVERTS the result. At n=400000
(12.8 MB, memory-bound) the 2-check probe measured FASTER than the 0-check one —
the checks are free when the loop is waiting on DRAM. The 1.93x is a
cache-resident measurement (640 KB), and only that regime is informative here.

RESOLVED by direction (A), the interprocedural precondition — implemented as
`src/codegen/bce_interproc.rs`, a new whole-PROGRAM analysis that runs once in
`compile_program` and is merged into the existing per-function
`converging_skips` map at `compile_function`.

CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S SIZING. The claim above that (A) "is the first
interprocedural analysis in the compiler" is WRONG, and it is what made the
job look larger than it was. `src/call_graph.rs` already exists (backing
`karac query affected-by`), and `effectchecker/inference.rs` already does
SCC-based interprocedural effect inference over a call graph it builds itself.
Neither was reusable here — the affected-by graph is name-keyed and
deliberately over-approximates method calls, and neither carries the argument
EXPRESSIONS a precondition has to substitute — but "the compiler has no
interprocedural machinery" was not the obstacle it was recorded as.

WHAT MADE IT A CONTAINED CHANGE, and the part worth reusing. The new pass
emits the SAME plain-data `ConvergingSkip` record `compute_converging_skips`
already produces, keyed by the same inner-loop condition `SpanKey`. So
`compile_while` cannot tell the two provenances apart and needed no change at
all: the entire codegen-side cost is one `entry().or_insert_with()` merge.
Framing an interprocedural result as "the existing intra-function fact, proven
a different way" is what kept this off the IR surface. Codegen containment
holds — the pass is AST-only plain data, no LLVM type crosses it.

THE TWO HALVES.
  1. INFER (`infer_precondition`): recognise the converging two-pointer in a
     callee whose `base` is a PARAMETER (the one structural difference from
     the intra path, which requires a local `sole_scalar_init`), and record
     `base + hi_init < v.len()` plus `base + lo_init >= 0` over the callee's
     PARAMETER names.
  2. DISCHARGE (`discharge_call_site`): substitute the caller's actual
     argument terms for those names and re-prove with the caller's own facts,
     through the SAME `init_below_bound` / `sum_nonneg_at_min` linear
     cancellation the intra path uses. All-or-nothing: one undischarged site
     disqualifies the callee, because one body is emitted so one fact must
     cover every call.

WHY "EVERY CALL SITE" IS KNOWABLE. Checked in src/cli.rs rather than assumed:
both multi-module paths hand codegen a merged SUPER-PROGRAM carrying every
module's items (`try_build_run_super_program` for an entry file, the stitched
`super_items` for a project build), so the census sees every caller in the
compilation unit. The `pub` gate closes the rest — a `pub` fn can be called
from outside the unit, where no census reaches. If the pipeline ever compiles
modules separately, this pass must be disabled with it (noted in the module
doc).

MEASURED, x86 container, the probe shape from this entry verbatim (20000 rows
x 32 bytes = 640 KB, the cache-resident regime this entry's METHOD NOTE says
is the only informative one), 400 reps:

  callee form, before          123 ms
  callee form, after            93 ms   <- 1.32x
  inline form (intra skip ON)  111 ms
  inline form, KARAC_BCE_CONV_SKIP=0
                               122 ms

The last two rows are the calibration that made the reproduction unambiguous:
the unfixed callee form lands exactly on the skip-DISABLED inline number, which
is what "the checks survive the call boundary" looks like as a measurement
rather than an inference. (The 1.32x here is smaller than this entry's 1.93x
minimal-probe figure because this probe carries more non-loop work; it is the
same elision.)

SOUNDNESS EVIDENCE, beyond the suite. Four hand probes, AOT vs interpreter,
all matching: the discharging shape (84/84); a direct out-of-range call (both
trap); a MIXED program where a good loop caller and a bad direct caller share
one callee (prints 84 then traps on BOTH backends -- the bad site disqualified
the callee, so the good rows kept their checks too); and an off-by-one caller
guard `i <= n` (both trap). Binary-identity discrimination on the same five
programs: the skip fires on exactly the two that should discharge and on none
of the three that should not, and both kill switches reproduce the pre-fix
binary byte-for-byte.

TESTS. 13 unit tests in the module (each gate: pub callee, mut-ref buffer,
duplicated name, fn-as-value, no caller pin, non-arithmetic argument, index
stepped before use, reassigned parameter, call from a closure body, off-by-one
bound, second undischarged site) + 3 IR-level tests + 2 E2E tests in
tests/codegen.rs. NON-VACUITY, stated precisely: only
`test_ir_interproc_row_helper_bce_skip_wiring` is RED before the fix -- it is
the one that asserts the check is GONE. The other four pass on the unfixed
compiler by construction, since they assert the check SURVIVES or that output
is correct; their job is to catch a future regression in the gates or a
miscompile introduced here, not to witness the fix.

NOT DONE, deliberately. Direction (B) (loop versioning) is not implemented and
is not needed for this shape. The pass handles ONE buffer and ONE `base` per
helper; a second of either disqualifies rather than proving the first. Only
free functions are candidates (a method can arrive through dynamic dispatch).
`KARAC_BCE_INTERPROC=0` is the kill switch; `KARAC_BCE_CONV_SKIP=0` also
disables it, since it feeds that mechanism.

fix: ef9c1b1 + aaadaac + 33f1ca0 + 0965dbc + 103c518 + 0830bbc (leak A) + f380a8f (leak B) — row STAYS OPEN for the remaining 10, all leaks + 5d48b3c + b359f437 (tensor fresh-temp owned arg) + 70c15e83 (boxed Option/Result payload box, both sites)
title: ~23 heap-ownership shapes emit a DOUBLE FREE; the `ok_or` String Err payload case is CONFIRMED to abort on a DEFAULT -O2 `karac build` as soon as the payload is read (SIGABRT, glibc `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`) -- it looked -O0-only because the fixture read it through `.len()` alone, which lets LLVM delete the allocation
detail:
CONFIRMED THROUGH THE ORDINARY CLI, not just the ASAN harness. Reduced from
`tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_option_ok_or_string_err_no_leak`, verbatim
fixture body in a file, built with `karac build`:

  fn main() {
      let mut i: i64 = 0;
      let mut errs: i64 = 0;
      while i < 6 {
          let o: Option[i64] = if i % 2 == 0 { Some(i * 10) } else { None };
          let r: Result[i64, String] = o.ok_or(f"absent-{i}-padded-well-past-inline-width");
          match r {
              Ok(v) => println(v),
              Err(e) => { errs = errs + e.len(); },
          }
          i = i + 1;
      }
      println(errs);
  }

  KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=2 (default) -> prints 0 / 20 / 40 / 114, exit 0
  KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0           -> `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`,
                                 SIGABRT, exit 134

So codegen emits TWO frees for the `ok_or` String Err payload. At -O2 the
payload is read only through `.len()`, which makes the buffer a provably
dead allocation LLVM deletes outright -- and a second free of an allocation
that never happened is invisible. The bug is in the emitted ownership, not
in the optimizer; -O2 is masking it, not fixing it.

USER-REACHABLE. `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0` is a documented, supported knob (the
"did the optimizer eat my IR construct?" debugging fallback -- see
`read_opt_level_env`'s table in src/codegen/driver.rs), so a user who drops
to -O0 to debug an unrelated problem gets a hard SIGABRT in code that works
at -O2. The masking is also fragile at -O2: the moment a program does
anything with the payload beyond taking its length -- read a byte, print it,
store it -- the allocation stops being dead and the second free lands.

SCOPE: ~23 of the 932 `memory_sanitizer` fixtures fail under
`KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 cargo test --features llvm --test memory_sanitizer`
(908 passed / 23 failed), every one of them a heap-ownership shape. Only the
`ok_or` case above has been reduced and confirmed outside the harness; the
other 22 are ASAN-confirmed at -O0 but not yet individually triaged, and it
is NOT established that they are all one root cause. The list:

  b27_option_enum_undestructured_drop_no_leak
  b27_option_struct_undestructured_drop_no_leak
  b28_option_shared_and_direct_shared_struct_drop_no_leak
  boxed_option_moved_into_struct_literal_no_uaf
  collect_all_vec_capturing_closures_no_uaf
  collect_all_vec_gather_no_double_free
  fstring_match_arm_value_no_double_free
  generic_enum_heap_payload_bind_return_no_leak_or_double_free
  generic_enum_struct_heap_payload_bind_no_leak_or_double_free
  generic_struct_field_receiver_param_indexed_no_leak
  generic_struct_heap_field_move_out_no_double_free
  map_get_unwrap_struct_heap_value_no_double_free
  match_variant_name_shared_across_enums_string_payload_no_leak
  nested_option_pattern_boxed_payload_lifecycle_clean
  option_ok_or_string_err_no_leak
  optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fire_once
  optres_tuple_payload_is_owned_exactly_once
  shared_payload_view_optres_field_call_arg_copy_no_leak_no_double_free
  surface_binary_string_concat_temp_no_leak_no_double_free
  tensor_lifecycle_clean
  unwrap_or_fresh_string_default_no_leak
  user_method_builtin_name_on_literal_receiver_clean
  vec_get_unwrap_struct_heap_field_no_leak_no_double_free
  vec_get_unwrap_struct_with_heap_field_no_double_free

HOW IT STAYED HIDDEN, which is the B-2026-08-04-17 connection: every one of
these fixtures asserted a clean ASAN run at -O2 over a payload the optimizer
had already deleted. The suite was green because nothing was allocated, not
because nothing was wrong. `asan_option_ok_or_string_err_no_leak` measured
exactly 3 allocations at -O2 (the ASAN runtime's own startup baseline, i.e.
zero program allocations) and 4 at -O0. This is the first CONFIRMED
COMPILER BUG recovered from the vacuous-fixture population, and it argues
the remaining 73 are worth the effort.

NOT DIAGNOSED HERE: which emitter double-frees. `ok_or` packing a String
into a Result Err slot is B-2026-07-15-15's surface, so the built Result and
the source temporary both claiming the buffer is the obvious first place to
look, but that is a hypothesis, not a finding.

UPGRADED, SAME DAY: THE DOUBLE FREE FIRES AT -O2 TOO. The row above framed
-O2 as masking and called the fragility a prediction; it is now measured. Take
the same program and give the Err payload ONE byte-level read so the buffer
stops being dead -- `starts_with` was used because `contains` on a
pattern-bound String does not compile at all (B-2026-08-05-8):

      Err(e) => {
          if e.starts_with("absent") { hits = hits + 1; }
          errs = errs + e.len();
      },

  KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=2 (DEFAULT) -> `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`,
                                 SIGABRT, exit 134
  KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0           -> same abort

versus the `.len()`-only original, which is clean at -O2 and aborts only at
-O0. So this is NOT an -O0-only defect and the severity is not about a
debugging knob: any program that READS the `ok_or` Err payload -- prints it,
matches on its bytes, stores it -- double-frees on a DEFAULT `karac build`.
The `.len()`-only shape is the single narrow case where -O2 happens to delete
the evidence, and that shape is exactly what the fixture used.

This also means the -O0 sweep is a DISCOVERY tool here rather than the
condition of the bug: it surfaced 23 fixtures whose payloads are dead at -O2,
but the underlying emission is wrong at every level. Whether the other 22
behave the same way once their payloads are made live is UNTESTED -- only the
`ok_or` case has been carried through.

TRIAGE OF THE 23, and it CORRECTS THIS ROW'S OWN FRAMING. The row was filed
saying these were bugs 'hiding behind vacuous fixtures' -- i.e. that -O2 missed
them for the same dead-payload reason B-2026-08-04-17 documents. Checked
against the -O2 allocation audit, that is TRUE FOR EXACTLY ONE of them:

  masked at -O2 by a dead payload (3 allocs = zero program allocs):  1
      option_ok_or_string_err_no_leak   <- the one reduced and confirmed
  allocates substantially at -O2 and STILL PASSES there:            10
      optres_tuple_payload_is_owned_exactly_once            1809 allocs
      optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fire_once              803
      unwrap_or_fresh_string_default_no_leak                 503
      map_get_unwrap_struct_heap_value_no_double_free        283
      generic_enum_heap_payload_bind_return_...              204
      vec_get_unwrap_struct_heap_field_...                   123
      generic_struct_field_receiver_param_indexed_no_leak     83
      vec_get_unwrap_struct_with_heap_field_...                8
      generic_enum_struct_heap_payload_bind_...                4
      nested_option_pattern_boxed_payload_lifecycle_clean      4
  no -O2 audit line (different assertion helper):                  12

So the vacuous-fixture story explains ONE of the 23. The other ten are not
vacuous at -O2 by any measure -- one of them does 1809 allocations -- and are
clean there while failing at -O0. That is a DIFFERENT phenomenon and this row
should not be read as claiming otherwise.

FAILURE MODES at -O0, parsed from the run:
  use-after-free  17
  double-free      5
  leak             1  (tensor_lifecycle_clean)

WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Established: the `ok_or` double free is real
at -O2 (see the upgrade above). NOT established: that the other 22 are real
-O2 bugs. The plausible mechanism for the ten that allocate is the same KIND
of masking rather than the same instance -- ASAN sees a UAF only if the
program actually loads from freed memory, and at -O2 LLVM may forward or
delete the offending load, hiding a genuinely wrong emission. But that is a

FAIL-CLOSED ON THE ARMS, and this is where the design decision is. An arm
tail qualifies only if it is a value this frame may own — a non-borrow
Call/MethodCall, an f-string, a String concat, or a string LITERAL (cap 0,

nor double-frees). Anything else declines the WHOLE match, because an arm
yielding a PLACE — a payload binding (`E.A(n) => n`), a field, an element —
hands back storage its container still owns, and freeing the phi would
double-free precisely when that arm is the one taken. One disqualifying arm
is enough: the phi is a single value and the frame cannot know at compile
time which arm produced it.

SITE 1 -- a user enum's `Option`/`Result` payload had NO drop at all.

      box is freed once, by the frame that owns the value. Freeing the INTERIOR
      would double-free the buffer a `W(Some(s))` arm's `s` already owns, so
      the interior stays the pre-existing leak it was.

      from `is_heap_bearing()` to `!= None` so this kind IS zeroed there. It is
      the one site where the source must be disarmed: the destination gets the
      box pointer verbatim. Found the hard way -- `let w2 = w;` aborted with an
      ASAN double-free the moment the drop existed.

      payload struct) instead of routing the word through
      `emit_owning_clone_fn_for_type_expr`, which would read the box POINTER as
      the Option's tag. The interior stays shallow -- the same shared-buffer
      semantics the whole-value bitcopy already gave it -- because deep-cloning
      it would leave the clone's interior owned by nobody.

title: `s.contains(other)` on a String bound out of a `Result[String, E]` Ok arm fails to COMPILE -- "Binary op Eq: right operand has non-comparable type { ptr, i64, i64 }" -- while `karac check` passes and the interpreter runs it correctly; the same call on a TUPLE-element String payload compiles fine
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: hit while writing B-2026-08-05-3's regression fixture. The direct-String-payload CONTROL arm would not build, so it had to be dropped from that fixture; this row carries it instead.

REPRO (whole program):
    fn mks(k: i64) -> String { let mut s: String = String.new(); s.push_str(f"pay-{k}"); return s; }
    fn dig(i: i64) -> String { let mut d: String = String.new(); d.push_str(f"{i}"); return d; }
    fn main() {
        let n: i64 = env.args().len();
        let r: Result[String, i64] = Result.Ok(mks(n));
        match r { Result.Ok(s) => { if s.contains(dig(n)) { println(f"c3:{s.len()}"); } } Result.Err(e) => { println("c3:err"); } }
    }

  karac check        -> All checks passed.
  karac run --interp -> c3:5   (correct)
  karac build        -> error: codegen failed: Binary op Eq: right operand has non-comparable type
                        StructType({ ptr, i64, i64 }) (likely a typechecker gap -- `assert_eq` and
                        `==` should reject mismatched operand types before reaching codegen)

SO IT IS A RUN-VS-BUILD DIVERGENCE, not a diagnostics nit: the program is accepted by every check and runs correctly on one backend, while the other refuses it with a message that blames the typechecker for an `==` THE SOURCE DOES NOT CONTAIN.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT LOCALIZES IT, checked rather than assumed. The identical call on a TUPLE-ELEMENT String payload compiles and runs clean:
    let r: Result[(String, i64), i64] = Result.Ok((mks(n), 5i64));
    match r { Result.Ok(x) => { if x.0.contains(dig(n)) { ... } } ... }   -> builds, 10 allocs / 10 frees, valgrind-clean
So it is specific to a DIRECT `String` payload binding -- not to `contains`, and not to Result as a carrier.

READING OF THE SYMPTOM, explicitly NOT a diagnosis -- no IR was dumped and no codegen path was read. `contains` presumably lowers through a comparison helper, and the error says one operand arrived as a raw `{ptr,i64,i64}` String struct where a scalar was expected. A direct payload binding is reconstructed differently from a tuple element (the single-word vs multi-word split in `reconstruct_payload_value`), so the natural first place to look is whether the direct-String binding reaches the comparison lowering without the shape the tuple path gives it. The tuple spelling being AHEAD here is the REVERSE of the usual tuple/field asymmetry, which is itself a hint about which path is the reference implementation.

NOT the same bug as B-2026-08-05-3 -- that is a leak with correct output, this is a hard compile failure -- but found on the same fixture, hence the followup source.

INDEPENDENT SECOND SIGHTING, same day, reached from B-2026-08-05-7 rather
than from B-2026-08-05-3 -- `contains` was the byte-level read that
B-2026-08-04-17's authoring rule recommends, and it would not compile on the
pattern-bound receiver a heap-payload ownership fixture usually has. Same
error text, same `{ptr,i64,i64}` operand. Adding the coverage matrix, which
widens the shape well past the `Result` Ok arm and narrows the search:

  let-bound String          .contains     -> OK
  for-loop element binding  .contains     -> OK
  struct FIELD access       .contains     -> OK
  Result `Err(e)` arm       .contains     -> FAILS
  Option `Some(e)` arm      .contains     -> FAILS
  user enum arm             .contains     -> FAILS
  `if let Some(e)`          .contains     -> FAILS
  Result `Err(e)` arm       .len()        -> OK
  Result `Err(e)` arm       .starts_with  -> OK

TWO THINGS THAT FOLLOW, one of which corrects a clause above.

(1) It is NOT Result-specific and not Ok-arm-specific: Option, a user enum,
and `if let` all fail the same way. The carrier is irrelevant; what matters is
that the receiver came from a PATTERN BINDING. A `let`, a for-loop element,
and a struct field are all fine.

(2) The row above says it is 'specific to a DIRECT `String` payload binding --
not to `contains`'. The second half of that does not hold: `.len()` and
`.starts_with` on the VERY SAME direct pattern-bound String compile and run
clean. So the defect is the PAIR (pattern-bound receiver x `contains`), not
the binding alone -- which is a tighter target, since whatever `starts_with`
does with that receiver is evidently already correct and `contains` is the
outlier. Consistent with the row's own reading that `contains` lowers through
a comparison helper: it looks like the receiver is not recognised as a String
there and falls through to a COLLECTION membership test that compares elements
with `==`, which is why a whole `{ptr,i64,i64}` arrives where a scalar was
expected. Still a reading, not a diagnosis -- no IR was dumped here either.

SEVERITY NOTE, left for the owner rather than changed unilaterally: this row
is `medium`, but the repo has treated check-passes / build-fails as `high`
elsewhere (B-2026-07-30-7 carries exactly that reasoning). Flagging the
inconsistency, not resolving it. FIXED. ROOT CAUSE, and the row's own matrix is what made it findable: a `String` PAYLOAD BINDING registered `vec_elem_types` but never `string_vars`. Those two sets do different jobs and only one was wired. `vec_elem_types` exists for the SCOPE-EXIT BUFFER FREE (a String payload is tracked as `Vec[u8]`-shaped so `track_vec_var` frees it); `string_vars` is what METHOD DISPATCH consults to pick the String arm for a method name String and Vec SHARE. With the binding in the first set only, it looked like a `Vec[u8]` to dispatch, so `s.contains(other)` fell through to VEC MEMBERSHIP — which compares elements with `==` and therefore handed codegen a whole `{ptr, i64, i64}` String where a scalar was expected. That is the entire explanation for the error text blaming the typechecker for an `==` the source never contained. THE ROW'S MATRIX DID THE HARD PART: recording that `.len()` and `.starts_with` work on the VERY SAME binding is what ruled out pattern binding in general and localized this to shared-name dispatch. Confirmed independently while fixing: rebinding the payload through a `let` (`let mut t = s;`) makes `contains` compile, because the let path is one of the ~10 `string_vars.insert` sites — all of which are in stmts.rs / shadow.rs / method_call.rs, and NONE in pattern_binding.rs or control_flow_match.rs (grep count: 0 in both). FIX: one registration in `bind_pattern_values`, beside the existing `vec_elem_types` line for the same payload. Same intent as the Map/Set arm a few lines below, whose comment already says it registers dispatch side-tables 'so `m.len()` / `s.contains(x)` on a match-arm-bound Map/Set dispatches like a let-bound one' — String was the one payload kind that got the free but not the dispatch. `CString` is deliberately EXCLUDED: its methods route through the `CString.<method>` key, so registering it would aim dispatch at the wrong table. VERIFIED: all five carriers the row listed (Result Ok, Result Err, Option Some, user enum, `if let`) build, and AOT == interpreter on each. Valgrind on the combined program: 22 allocs / 22 frees, 0 errors — the free path is unchanged, which is the thing to check when adding a second registration to a binding that already owns a buffer. A companion test pins `.len()` / `.starts_with` so a bad registration cannot pass by firing the String arm where it should not. GUARD FAMILY, checked not assumed: `push`, `concat`, `sorted`, `sorted_by` share the `string_vars` guard. No second LIVE shape exists today — `push` on a String demands a `Char` (typecheck rejects `u8`) and `concat` is not a String method at all — but the gap was one missing registration for the whole family, so the fix is at the registration rather than in the `contains` arm. SEVERITY QUESTION LEFT OPEN, as the row's author left it: this is `medium` while the repo has treated check-passes/build-fails as `high` elsewhere (B-2026-07-30-7). Not resolved unilaterally here either; now that it is fixed the question is really about how the NEXT such row gets triaged.

title: `unwrap_or` with a FRESH F-STRING default leaks on a DEFAULT -O2 build -- 133 leaked allocations in an existing fixture -- while the byte-identical program with a literal `"...".to_string()` default is clean, because the literal default const-folds away and the f-string one does not
detail:
REPRODUCED AS A TWO-LINE EDIT to an existing, currently-passing fixture,
`tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_unwrap_or_fresh_string_default_no_leak`.
Replace its two `unwrap_or` defaults, changing NOTHING else:

    -  let a = opt(i).unwrap_or("odd-default".to_string());
    +  let a = opt(i).unwrap_or(f"odd-default-{i}");
    -  let b = res(i).unwrap_or("res-default".to_string());
    +  let b = res(i).unwrap_or(f"res-default-{i}");

  before  ->  passes, 503 allocations
  after   ->  `ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks`,
              133 byte(s) leaked in 133 allocation(s)

at the DEFAULT optimization level. Not an -O0 artifact: -O0 reports the same
133. The leak count is EXACTLY the `res(i)` Err-path iteration count
(i % 3 != 0 over 0..199 = 133); the `opt(i)` Option path, which discards a
default on 100 iterations, does not contribute. Enlarging the Err payload
(`Err("e".to_string())` -> `Err(f"eeeeeeeeee-{i}")`) holds the count at 133
and takes the bytes 133 -> 1790, so what leaks scales with the ERROR payload,
one per Err-path iteration.

WHY THE LITERAL SPELLING HIDES IT, which is the B-2026-08-04-17 mechanism
arriving one level up: `"odd-default".to_string()` is literal-derived, so LLVM
constant-folds it and deletes the allocation -- there is then nothing to leak
and the fixture is green. An f-string default is runtime-derived and survives.
The fixture has therefore been GREEN SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN without covering the
case it is named for, and the masking is in the fixture's choice of default
spelling rather than anywhere in the assertion.

NOT ISOLATED -- stated plainly because two attempts failed. Neither standalone
reduction reproduced:
  (a) `Result[i64, String]`, `unwrap_or(0 - 1)`, discarding a String Err
      payload over 30 iterations -> clean.
  (b) `Result[String, String]`, `unwrap_or(f"default-{i}")` plus a
      `starts_with` byte read over 30 iterations -> clean.
So the trigger is NOT simply 'unwrap_or discards a String Err payload' nor
'unwrap_or takes an f-string default'. Something about the full fixture --
the Option and Result receivers sharing a loop, the `as i64` casts, the
iteration count, or the absence of a byte read on `b` (adding one to the
reduction was what made (b) clean) -- is part of the condition. Whoever picks
this up should start from the two-line edit above, which reproduces every
time, and bisect DOWN from it rather than building up from a minimal guess.

RELATION TO B-2026-07-16-22, which this fixture pins: that bug was the
discarded default on the PRESENT path leaking. This leak tracks the ABSENT
path count instead, so it is a different arm and not obviously a regression of
that fix -- but the fixture's literal defaults mean the present-path fix has
also never been exercised against a default the optimizer could not delete.
