fix: c6eaeea
title: a heap-BOXED `Option` payload nested inside a `Result`'s INLINE payload area has no owner on any side -- 32 B per construction at -O0
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found as a control while fixing B-2026-08-06-9 leg A; measured
IDENTICAL before and after that change, so it is a separate shape rather than a
residual of it.

SHAPE, KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, 10 iterations:

    fn cls(r: Result[Option[Option[i64]], i64]) -> i64 {
        match r {
            Result.Ok(Option.Some(Option.Some(x))) => x,
            Result.Ok(_) => -1,
            Result.Err(e) => e,
        }
    }
    fn main() {
        let n = env.args().len() as i64;
        let mut i: i64 = 0; let mut acc: i64 = 0;
        while i < 10 {
            let b: Result[Option[Option[i64]], i64] = Result.Ok(Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i)));
            acc = acc + cls(b) - n;
            i = i + 1;
        }
        println(acc);
    }

    -> definitely lost 320 bytes in 10 objects. Clean at -O2, where the box folds
       away, so this is an -O0-leg shape (B-2026-08-04-17).

WHY NOBODY OWNS IT. The box is TWO levels down. `Result`'s payload area is 5
words and the `Ok` payload `Option[Option[i64]]` is 4, so the Result stores it
INLINE and `boxed_enum_payload_variants` reports no boxed variant for the
binding's own type -- correct, as far as it goes. But that inline value is itself
an `Option` whose 4-word inner outgrew the 3-word Option area, so
`coerce_to_payload_words` boxed it during construction. Nothing registers a drop
for a box that lives inside another enum's inline payload: the let site asks
about the OUTER type only, and B-2026-08-06-9 leg A's callee-side registration
is `Option`-gated and likewise asks about the param's own type.

THE DIRECT `Option[Option[i64]]` SIBLING IS CLEAN as of leg A, which localizes
this to the extra `Result` wrapper rather than to the nesting itself.

WHOEVER TAKES IT should note that a fix has to decide the owner for a box the
binding's declared type does not mention, and the `Result` tag is not known
statically -- the same per-variant problem that keeps leg A's registration
`Option`-only.

── FIXED (2026-08-07) ──

THE LET SITE OWNS IT, and unlike the sibling rows in this family there was no
contest over the owner. Every candidate was measured at -O0 BEFORE the fix and
every one leaked the box identically (320 B / 10): matched in place, bound out
by an arm, moved into a struct literal, pushed into a `Vec`, passed by value to
a callee, handed through a passthrough, returned from one. So the source binding
is not the best owner, it is the ONLY one -- which is why a registration lands
here where B-2026-08-06-9 leg A needed two implement-measure-revert cycles.

THE SHAPE IS THE ONLY ONE OF ITS KIND, and that falls out of the seeded areas
rather than being a scoping choice. An `Option` value is always exactly 4 LLVM
words and a `Result` always 6, so against Option's 3-word area a nested
`Option`/`Result` payload NEVER fits (it is boxed at the outer level, where
`boxed_enum_payload_variants` already owns it) and against Result's 5-word area
an `Option` payload ALWAYS does. `Result[Option[Wide], E]` is therefore the only
way a box comes to rest inside an inline area. Both directions are pinned as
controls: `Result[Option[i64], E]` (inner scalar, no box) and
`Option[Result[i64, i64]]` (boxed at the outer level) were clean before and stay
clean.

WHAT LANDED:
  * `nested_boxed_enum_payload_variants` (types_lowering.rs) -- the descriptor,
    written over both seeded enums rather than hardcoding `Result` so it stays
    correct if an area is ever retuned.
  * `CleanupAction::NestedBoxedEnumDrop` + `track_nested_boxed_enum_var` -- a
    TWO-tag walk: outer tag, then the inner enum's tag read from the first
    payload word, then the box from the word after it. Both guards are
    load-bearing; an `Err(3)` leaves the Ok-side words holding an integer and
    reading one as a pointer frees a scalar.
  * the let-site registration (stmts.rs), disjoint from the existing `boxed`
    registration by construction -- an arm is either boxed at a level or inline
    at it, never both -- so the two cannot both fire for one arm.

THREE THINGS BROKE DURING IMPLEMENTATION, each caught by measurement rather
than by reasoning, and each is now a fixture arm:

  1. PASSTHROUGH DOUBLE FREE. `let back = idr(b);` registered a second owner of
     one pointer and aborted with a glibc double free at -O0 -- i.e. the naive
     version turned this row's LEAK into CORRUPTION. Fixed with
     `call_passthrough_armed_nested_source`, the nested sibling of
     B-2026-08-06-21's rule. Chains resolve at the RECORD site (the -9 lesson),
     so `let r1 = id(b); let r2 = id(r1);` is covered and the lookup stays one
     hop.

  2. ESCAPE BY RETURN -- USE AFTER FREE, and this one is the reason the fix is
     narrower than it first looked. A returned binding's box outlives the frame,
     so freeing it at scope exit hands the caller freed memory: measured as an
     `Invalid read of size 8` AND a wrong answer (-20 for 45). Retracted at BOTH
     return spellings -- the tail walk (`suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return`) does
     not see a `return` nested in an `if`, so the explicit-return arm needs its
     own call. Flow-insensitive like its siblings, so a conditional return
     disarms every path, which can only under-fire back to the leak.

  3. INNER DROP DOUBLE FREE. Registering the boxed payload's own drop as well
     aborted at BOTH opt levels on `Result[Option[Option[String]], i64]`,
     because the arm that binds the String out already owns it. The free is
     BOX-ONLY -- the same conclusion `user_enum_boxed_payload_variants`'s doc
     reached for the same reason, and consistent with what was measured missing:
     32 bytes, the envelope, nothing else. The `inner_drop_fn` parameter and
     field were removed rather than left always-`None`.

THE HAZARD ORDER IS WHAT MADE THIS ROW SAFE TO TAKE. Every failure above is a
case where the naive registration is WORSE than the bug (corruption vs a leak),
and every retraction falls back to the pre-existing leak. So the fix is written
to fail toward leaking, and the residuals below are left leaking rather than
guessed at.

TEST: `asan_box_nested_in_result_inline_payload_area_no_leak` -- ten arms
(matched in place / by-value call / Err-side nesting / bound passthrough /
chained passthrough / discarded passthrough / `Ok(None)` / `Err` / a
`Result[Option[i64], E]` no-box control / a runtime-built heap String).
Stash-proven RED: 8,960 B in 280 blocks (7 boxes x 40 iterations) at
KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, clean at the default -O2 where every box folds away, so the
memory half rides the -O0 leg (B-2026-08-04-17) and the -O2 leg carries the
value plus the allocation floor. Expected value COMPUTED (`7i + 1` per
iteration = 5500) and oracle-checked against --interp, `karac run`, AOT and
`KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` rather than pasted back.

RESIDUALS MEASURED AND FILED SEPARATELY rather than folded in -- B-2026-08-07-2
(the nested box at owner sites with no binding to hang a drop on, plus the
escape and struct-nesting shapes). A pre-existing DOUBLE FREE in the sibling
direct-boxed action, found by the same escape probe, is B-2026-08-07-1.

GATES: memory_sanitizer 964 pass at both opt levels (-O0 leg matches the
quarantine list exactly, 0 known failures), codegen 2833, par_codegen 238,
interpreter 1467, typechecker 2154, ownership 407, cli 574 -- all 0 failures.
All seven self-host oracles pass, including `selfhost_parser_items` (the
sharpest ownership oracle, which killed leg A's caller-side attempt) and the
`selfhost_codegen` fixpoint. clippy `--all --all-targets` with and without
`--features llvm`, and fmt, clean.

fix: ae74c7f
title: a BOXED-payload enum binding that is RETURNED is freed by its own frame -- the caller reads and frees the same box: double free + use-after-free at BOTH opt levels
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found by the escape probe written while fixing B-2026-08-06-32,
which needed to know whether the EXISTING direct-boxed action handles a returned
binding before deciding whether its own nested action had to. It does not. This
is PRE-EXISTING on main, independent of that change, and A/B-confirmed identical
with B-2026-08-06-32's diff stashed.

SHAPE, 10 iterations, reproduces at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 AND at the default -O2:

    struct Wide { a: i64, b: i64, c: i64, d: i64, e: i64 }
    fn mk(k: i64) -> Option[Wide] {
        let b: Option[Wide] = Option.Some(Wide { a: k, b: 1, c: 2, d: 3, e: 4 });
        b
    }
    fn main() {
        let n = env.args().len() as i64;
        let mut i: i64 = 0; let mut acc: i64 = 0;
        while i < 10 {
            let v = match mk(n + i) { Option.Some(w) => w.a, Option.None => -1 };
            acc = acc + v - n; i = i + 1;
        }
        println(acc);
    }

    -> `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`, and under valgrind two
       `Invalid read of size 8` before it. NOT a leak -- memory corruption.

`Wide` is 5 words against Option's 3-word area, so the payload is heap-boxed and
the let site queues a `BoxedEnumDrop`. `b` is then the function's tail: the
caller receives an `Option[Wide]` whose word 0 still points at the box, and
`mk`'s scope-exit drain frees it. The caller then reads `w.a` out of freed
memory and its own drop frees the box a second time.

WHY IT SURVIVED. `suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return` retracts a returned
binding's Vec / String / Map / channel / user-Drop cleanup, and the explicit
`return` arm in `exprs.rs` mirrors that list -- `BoxedEnumDrop` is in NEITHER.
The action post-dates most of that list and was never added to it.

WHOEVER TAKES IT: the retraction shape is already written twice over. The
mechanical part is `suppress_map_cleanup_for_tail_identifier`'s all-frames
`retain` scan, and B-2026-08-06-32 added exactly this retraction for the nested
sibling (`suppress_nested_boxed_drop_for_var`, called from both return
spellings) -- the direct action needs the same treatment at the same two call
sites. Do NOT assume the tail arm alone is enough: a `return b;` nested in an
`if` is not the body's tail and needs the explicit-return call too, which is how
the nested sibling's first attempt shipped a UAF into a probe.

CAUTION, and it is why this is not a two-line change: retracting on a return
must not strand the box when the returned value is NOT the binding. The nested
sibling could be flow-insensitive safely because under-firing there falls back
to a LEAK; here the action already exists and over-retracting turns a working
free into a leak while under-retracting keeps the double free. Both directions
cost, so the control set needs a conditional return, a returned fresh temp, and
a binding returned on one path but consumed on another.

RELATED: `asan_boxed_option_param_payload_move_out` and friends cover the
callee-side move-out mirror, not the caller-side escape, so the existing
fixtures do not reach this.

── FIXED (2026-08-07) ──

DISARMED AT THE RETURN, BY A RUNTIME WORD-0 ZERO rather than by retracting the
queued action -- and that choice is the whole content of the fix. The row's own
caution said both directions cost: over-retract and a working free becomes a
leak, under-retract and the double free stays. A runtime store dissolves the
tension instead of trading one for the other, because it executes only on the
path that actually returns. `suppress_boxed_enum_payload_cleanup_for_owner`
already existed and already did exactly this (zero word 0; the box drop's
existing null-guard then skips), so no new machinery was needed -- only the
calls.

FOUR ESCAPE POSITIONS, not one, and this is what the row underestimated. Each
is a separate walk and none of them sees the others' leaves:

  1. the function-body TAIL              -> `suppress_cleanup_for_tail_return`
  2. an explicit `return b;` in an `if`  -> the `ExprKind::Return` arm
  3. an `if`/`else` BRANCH LEAF          -> `suppress_block_tail_cleanup`
  4. a MATCH-ARM leaf                    -> `compile_match`'s per-arm cluster

The row predicted (1) and (2) from the nested sibling and called the fix
"the same treatment at the same two call sites". That was wrong by half: an
`if hit { b } else { None }` tail and a `match k { 0 => b, _ => None }` tail
both still double-freed after (1) and (2) were done, because the tail walk
inspects the tail EXPRESSION and the leaf is one level down.

(3) and (4) are also where the runtime-store choice pays: both emit into the
BRANCH'S OWN BLOCK, before that frame drains, so a branch that hands the
binding out disarms it while a sibling branch that does not still frees the
box. A compile-time retraction is a single edit to a queue and cannot tell the
two apart. The fixture runs both paths of both shapes (the scrutinee
alternates) so the leak direction is a real assertion, not a dead arm.

VEC / STRING WERE THE ORACLE. Their branchy tails are CLEAN at HEAD, on both
paths -- that is what proved a per-branch mechanism already existed and the box
action simply was not wired into it, rather than the branchy tail being an
unsolved problem. Finding `suppress_block_tail_cleanup` took one probe
(`if k % 2 == 0 { v } else { Vec.new() }` with both paths live) instead of a
search.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN TEXT:

  * The `Result` probe it implies does NOT reproduce. `Result`'s area is 5
    words and the row's `Wide` is exactly 5, so `Result[Wide, i64]` stores its
    payload INLINE and allocates no box -- an early fixture was green for that
    wrong reason. `Result` needs a 6-word payload (`Wide6`) to box at all, and
    then it double-frees exactly like `Option`.
  * "the tail arm alone is not enough" was right, but for a second reason it
    did not name: not only is a nested `return` not the tail, a BRANCH LEAF is
    not the tail either.

WHY THE CALLER DOES NOT ALSO NEED CHANGING, measured rather than assumed: after
the callee disarms, the box still has an owner on the caller side -- a fresh-temp
scrutinee registers one (B-2026-07-18-3) and a named binding registers one at
its let site. So every arm is clean rather than trading the double free for a
leak, which the fixture asserts by running under LSan at both opt levels.

TEST: `asan_returned_boxed_payload_binding_not_freed_by_its_own_frame` -- eleven
arms. Four escape positions (tail / nested return / if-else leaf / match-arm
leaf), plus `Result` with a genuinely boxed 6-word payload and a HEAP-BEARING
interior where the box drop carries an `inner_drop_fn`. The over-suppression
direction gets six of the eleven: a binding never returned, two boxed bindings
with only one returned, both two-path arms with both paths live, a
return-on-one-path/consume-on-the-other, a non-return BLOCK tail whose consumer
owns the box, and a returned fresh temp with no binding to disarm.

Unlike its nested sibling this does NOT ride the -O0 leg: the pre-fix compiler
ABORTS at the default -O2 too, so the ordinary suite run is a real gate.
Stash-proven: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` with four
`Invalid read of size 8` at BOTH opt levels. Expected value COMPUTED
(`11i + 1` per iteration = 8620; the `None` arms return `i` precisely so both
branches contribute equally) and oracle-checked against --interp, `karac run`,
AOT and KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0.

GATES: memory_sanitizer 966 pass at both opt levels (-O0 leg matches the
quarantine list exactly), codegen 2833, par_codegen 239, interpreter 1467,
typechecker 2154, ownership 407, cli 574 -- all 0 failures. All seven self-host
oracles pass. clippy `--all --all-targets` with and without `--features llvm`,
and fmt, clean.

B-2026-08-06-32's shapes re-measured and UNCHANGED: the nested action has its
own armed set (`nested_boxed_payload_vars`), so none of these hooks reach it and
its escape shape stays as B-2026-08-07-2 item 5 describes.

title: the remaining owner sites for a box nested in a `Result`'s INLINE payload area -- ALL SIX RESOLVED. Fixed: no binding (fresh temp), `Vec.push` (the only -O2 leak), escape-by-return, the BOX-INSIDE-A-BOX chain, and finally the STRUCT between the levels (3176865) -- which turned out not to involve `Result` at all: a bare `let w: W` leaks identically, and the blocker was `field_copy_supported` reading a boxed-but-HEAPLESS `Option` field as uncopyable, which switches off the struct drop's whole `OptionInline` pass. Shape 6 was never a member of this family
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the residual set of B-2026-08-06-32, measured as controls while
fixing it and A/B-confirmed IDENTICAL before and after that change. That row
gave the nested box an owner at the LET SITE; these are the positions where
there is no let binding to hang the drop on, or where the box is not where the
descriptor looks. All are leaks, none is a regression, and each is 32 B per
construction at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0.

FIVE SHAPES, each reduced and measured at 10 iterations (320 B / 10 objects):

  1. NO BINDING -- a fresh temp argument. `cls(Result.Ok(Option.Some(
     Option.Some(n + i))))`. There is no slot, so the let-site registration
     cannot apply. The direct-boxed sibling solved its own version of this
     caller-side (B-2026-08-05-7's fresh-temp arm), which is the lead.

  2. NO BINDING -- `Vec.push(Result.Ok(Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i))))`. The
     box pointer is copied into the Vec's buffer and the element drop does not
     know it is there. This is the one shape that leaks at -O2 as well, because
     the Vec keeps the allocation live past the point LLVM could fold it.

  3. A STRUCT BETWEEN THE LEVELS. `struct W { o: Option[Option[i64]] }` used as
     `Result[W, i64]`: W is 4 words, fits Result's 5-word area inline, and the
     box is inside W's field. `nested_boxed_enum_payload_variants` asks whether
     the inline payload IS a seeded enum, not whether it CONTAINS one, so it
     reports nothing. Widening it to walk struct fields is the obvious move and
     is exactly where a second owner becomes possible -- the struct's own
     `__karac_drop_struct_<T>` is the other candidate.

  4. A BOX INSIDE A BOX. `Result[Option[Option[Option[i64]]], i64]`: the outer
     nested box is now freed, but the interior one it points at is not. The free
     is BOX-ONLY by design (running the payload's drop double-freed a
     `Option[Option[String]]` arm -- see the parent row), so the interior needs
     a different mechanism than widening this action.

  5. ESCAPE BY RETURN. `fn mk() -> Result[Option[Wide], E] { let b = ...; b }`.
     The registration is deliberately RETRACTED here, at both return spellings,
     because freeing an escaped box is a use-after-free -- measured as an
     `Invalid read of size 8` and a wrong answer when it was not retracted. So
     this shape stays a leak ON PURPOSE and closing it means giving the box an
     owner in the CALLER, not un-retracting. Its direct-boxed sibling was worse
     (a double free) and is FIXED by B-2026-08-07-1 -- but note its remedy does
     NOT transfer: there the caller already owns the box after the callee
     disarms (a fresh-temp scrutinee or a named binding registers one), so
     disarming is sufficient. Here the caller registers nothing for a NESTED
     box (shape 1 above), so disarming alone would leak, which is exactly what
     the current retraction does. The caller-side owner is still the missing
     piece.

  6. REASSIGNMENT. `let mut b = <nested>; b = <nested>;` leaks the OVERWRITTEN
     value's box; the parent row's fix halved this shape (640 B / 20 -> 320 B /
     10) by freeing the last value at scope exit. The store site would need to
     free the previous occupant, which no cleanup action can do.

PRIORITY NOTE, and it is why this is filed `low` as one row rather than six:
none of these is reachable from a shape the self-host tree or the kata corpus
writes today -- the parent row's own reduction was synthetic, and the whole
family exists because `Result[Option[Wide], E]` is rare in real Kara. They are
recorded so the next person to touch nested-box ownership inherits the measured
map instead of rediscovering it.

CAUTION for all of them: this family's failure mode is a SECOND owner, not a
missing one. Every shape above currently leaks, which is the safe direction; a
fix that registers in two places double-frees, and B-2026-08-06-32's own
implementation hit that three separate times (passthrough, inner drop, escape).
Measure each shape before AND after, at BOTH opt levels, and run
`selfhost_parser_items` -- a hand matrix and both memory_sanitizer legs were
green on an unsound change in this family before.

── THREE OF SIX FIXED (2026-08-07, b55a849) ──

Shapes 1 (fresh temp), 2 (`Vec.push`) and 5 (escape by return) share ONE root
cause and one fix. The row treated them as three problems; they are one.

THE OWNER IS THE CALLEE'S OWNED, NON-ESCAPING PARAM — the same place
B-2026-08-05-7 and B-2026-08-06-9 leg A put it for the directly-boxed sibling,
extended to the nested descriptor (`nested_boxed_enum_payload_variants`). The
lead this row recorded for shape 1 was right, and it turned out to cover shapes
2 and 5 as well:

  * shape 2 reaches it because `cls(v[j])` is a by-value call whose argument is
    a vec_get temp, exactly like a fresh temp. Confirmed by allocation counts
    rather than by reading code: the CLEAN direct sibling `Vec[Option[Option[
    i64]]]` and the LEAKING `Vec[Result[Option[Option[i64]], i64]]` have the
    SAME 17 allocations and differ only in frees (17 vs 7) — so the Vec element
    drop was never what freed the direct one either. Instrumenting the element
    gate showed neither shape gets a per-element drop at all
    (`result_payload_inline_recursive_drop_ok` is false, and the Option arm is
    false too), which refutes this row's own "the element drop does not know it
    is there" reading: there is no element drop to teach.
  * shape 5 was predicted to stay a leak ON PURPOSE, closable only by "giving
    the box an owner in the CALLER". That is precisely what a consumer's param
    is. `cls(mk(n + i))` is now clean at both opt levels with no retraction
    change — the deliberate retraction at the return stays, and the consumer
    picks the box up on the other side.

THE HARD HALF WAS THE SECOND OWNER, exactly as this row's CAUTION says, and it
bit three times. Each was measured as a glibc `double free detected in tcache 2`
at -O0 — strictly worse than the leak it replaced — and each is now an arm of
the fixture:

  * `cls(idr(b))` — the passthrough result IS `b`'s box, and `b` correctly keeps
    its registration (`idr` can return its param, so the callee registers
    nothing). The consumer has to disarm the source it aliases.
  * `cls(idr(idr(b)))` — the outer passthrough's argument is a CALL, so the
    existing one-hop identifier-only resolver stops before reaching `b`.
  * `let c = idr(b); cls(c)` — `c` is an identifier that registers nothing; the
    owner is one `nested_boxed_passthrough_owner_alias` hop away.

So the disarm resolves the owner to a FIXPOINT through both the alias map and
the passthrough argument (`nested_boxed_owner_source_of`), where the let site
needs only one hop. The over-suppression control is `fwd(b)` — a param
forwarded to another by-value param rather than returned: it escapes, so it
registers nothing and the terminal consumer stays sole owner. A rule that
registered per-hop would free once per hop.

STILL OPEN, unchanged and still leaking 32 B per construction at -O0 only:
shape 3 (a STRUCT between the levels) and shape 4 (a BOX INSIDE A BOX). Both
need what this row already says they need — 3 a descriptor that walks struct
fields, with `__karac_drop_struct_<T>` as the rival owner to rule out; 4 a
mechanism other than widening a free that is BOX-ONLY by design.

SHAPE 6 IS NOT A MEMBER OF THIS FAMILY — this row was wrong to list it. Its
DIRECT-boxed sibling leaks identically (`let mut b: Option[Option[i64]] = …;
b = …;` — 320 B / 10 at -O0, clean at -O2), so reassignment fails to free the
overwritten box for boxed enum payloads generally, not for nested ones. Refiled
as B-2026-08-07-4; the parent row's "fix halved this shape" observation belongs
there.

VERIFIED at BOTH opt levels on a 13-program hand matrix (all six shapes, the
three double-free directions, the forwarding and reassignment controls, and the
three direct-boxed siblings), plus `selfhost_parser_types` — the gate this row
names, because a hand matrix and both memory_sanitizer legs were green on an
unsound change in this family before. Fixture
`asan_nested_box_owned_by_callee_when_no_binding_owns_it` is red pre-fix at BOTH
legs (5,120 B / 160 blocks at -O0; 1,280 B / 40 blocks at -O2, which is exactly
32 B × 40 — the `Vec` arm) and green after.

── SHAPE 4 FIXED (2026-08-07, d1aa710); SHAPE 3 ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED ──

SHAPE 4 (box inside a box) was closed by walking the ENVELOPE chain. This row
predicted it would need "a different mechanism than widening this action"
because the free is BOX-ONLY by design. Half right: the free stays box-only,
and walking the chain turned out to be an APPLICATION of that rule rather than
a widening of it. Every level is an envelope minted by
`coerce_to_payload_words`; an envelope is never named by the source program, so
no match arm can bind one out and no other action can own one. The interior --
the `String` an arm binds out, which is what made the payload-drop version
double-free -- is still untouched at every depth, and the chain terminates at
the first payload that FITS its area, because that payload is a value rather
than an envelope. That terminus is the whole safety argument.

The chain also generalises: a QUADRUPLE nest measured 320 B definitely lost
plus 320 B indirectly pre-fix and is now clean, which is the signature of a
chain rather than the single miss this row described.

ORDER was the other half and is the easy way to get this wrong: the pointer to
the next envelope lives INSIDE the current one, so each level must load its
successor BEFORE freeing itself. The emitter descends first and frees on the
join.

SHAPE 3 (a struct between the levels) IS STILL OPEN, and the reason is now
measured rather than predicted. This row named
`__karac_drop_struct_<T>` as the rival owner. It is not; it never runs for
this shape (a bare `let w: W` with an `Option[Option[i64]]` field LEAKS the
box, 320 B / 10 at -O0, so nothing frees it). The real rival is the binding
that MOVES THE FIELD OUT:

    match r { Result.Ok(w) => { let inner = w.o; match inner { … } } }

`inner` is a direct-boxed `Option[Option[i64]]`, so its let site registers a
`BoxedEnumDrop` and owns the box. That shape is CLEAN today. Widening
`nested_boxed_enum_payload_variants` to walk struct fields -- the move this row
calls obvious, and it is -- gives the Result-level action a second claim on the
same pointer, and the shape aborts with a glibc `double free detected in
tcache 2` at -O0. Implemented, measured, reverted.

The gate written to keep the heap-bearing case out (`type_expr_has_drop_heap`
on the struct) did NOT hold either: `Result[W, i64]` with an
`Option[Option[String]]` field went from 10 sanitizer errors to 20 with the
registration in, so the predicate returns false for a struct whose field
carries a String through a boxed enum. Whoever takes shape 3 needs a different
gate and a disarm for the field-move binding; the owner is CONTESTED, which is
what makes it unlike shape 4 and unlike B-2026-08-06-32.

TWO ADJACENT BUGS FOUND while controlling for this and filed separately, both
independent of everything above:

  * B-2026-08-07-7 -- `Result[W, i64]` where `W` has an `Option[Option[String]]`
    field DOUBLE-FREES at BOTH opt levels on main today. Corruption, not a leak,
    and it predates B-2026-08-06-32 (verified by building at e35e36e).
  * B-2026-08-07-6 -- the chain fix's DIRECT sibling. `Option[Option[Option[
    i64]]]` with no `Result` wrapper still leaks its inner envelope, because
    `BoxedEnumDrop` frees one box and has no chain. Same defect, different
    owning action; left alone deliberately since that action is registered from
    many sites and this row's fix did not need to touch it.

── SHAPE 3 FIXED (2026-08-07, 3176865); THE ROW IS CLOSED ──

The last of the six. And the fix is not where this row spent three passes
looking, which is the part worth carrying forward.

THE `Result` WRAPPER WAS NEVER PART OF THE BUG. A bare `let w: W` whose field is
NEVER READ leaks the same 320 B / 10 at -O0. So the shape is not "a struct
between the levels of a nested `Result`" at all -- it is a struct field of type
`Option[P]` with `P` heap-BOXED, and the wrapper this row is named after only
ever supplied the reduction it happened to be found in. Every pass here proposed
widening `nested_boxed_enum_payload_variants`, the RESULT-level descriptor,
because that is what the framing implied; the third pass implemented it and
reverted it for double-freeing.

THE REAL ROOT IS THREE LAYERS UP AND ASKS ONE QUESTION WRONGLY AT EACH. An
`Option` is 4 LLVM words against `Option`'s own 3-word payload area, so
`Option[Option[i64]]` spills behind a pointer with not a byte of heap inside it.
Then:

  * `te_recursive_drop_fully_supported(Option[i64])` is false -- its own comment
    says "boxed non-shared … stay false" -- because it asks whether the PAYLOAD
    owns heap;
  * so `field_copy_supported` reads the field as uncopyable and `W` as
    caller-retains;
  * so `emit_struct_drop_synthesis`'s ENTIRE `OptionInline` pass, which is gated
    on that predicate, never runs for `W`, and the field gets no drop.

This row already recorded the observation that `__karac_drop_struct_W` "never
runs for this shape". That was the clue and it was read as an alibi: it never
runs because it is never SYNTHESIZED.

THE CONTESTED OWNER RESOLVES ITSELF once the fix is at the field. The rival this
row measured is `let inner = w.o`, whose let site registers a `BoxedEnumDrop`
over the same box, and it is why the Result-level registration aborted with a
glibc double free. Classifying the field the way its heap-payload sibling
(`Option[Option[String]]`) is classified also inherits that sibling's move-out
neutralization, because `place_optres_field_move_info_ex` keys on the SAME
classifier and documents the two as a pair. Both moved-out shapes measure clean.

COPY == DROP, ONE PREDICATE. `option_payload_boxed_envelope_only` is consulted
by `field_copy_supported` and by the drop classifier, so the two cannot drift.
It admits only a payload the entry copy actually descends into -- a non-shared
`Path` head that is a user struct or seeded enum, which is
`deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`'s own admission test. A TUPLE
payload is the counterexample that makes the restriction load-bearing:
`Option[(i64, i64, i64, i64)]` is boxed too, but the copy's `TypeKind::Path`
bind fails and it duplicates nothing, so admitting it would leave the callee's
struct and the caller's original one box between them and two frees. Excluded,
and still leaking 320 B / 10 -- recorded here rather than fixed, because pairing
a drop with a copy that does nothing is how this family produces double frees.

NO NEW DROP FN WAS NEEDED, which is the pleasant part and worth noting because
B-2026-08-07-7's third pass built one (`emit_option_box_only_drop_fn`) and
reverted it. `emit_option_drop_fn`'s boxed branch already calls the payload's
drop and then frees the box; for a heapless payload that inner call is the no-op
`emit_drop_fn_for_type_expr` synthesizes. It is the deep drop applied to a
payload with nothing deep in it.

MEASURED at both opt levels, 10 iterations, valgrind -- the row's own
`Result[W, i64]` shape, the bare `let w: W`, the never-read field, both
moved-out rivals, a boxed all-scalar STRUCT payload, `Vec[W]`, a struct nesting
`W`, and the `Option[Option[String]]` heap-interior controls: all clean, none
previously corrupting.

Pinned by `asan_struct_field_boxed_heapless_option_envelope_owned`, red at BOTH
legs pre-fix (5,088 B / 159 at -O0; 1,280 B / 40 at -O2, the latter because its
`Vec[W]` arm keeps the box live past the point LLVM folds it -- the same reason
shape 2 was this family's only -O2 leak).

STILL LEAKING, both recorded elsewhere rather than left implicit: a fresh-temp
`W` passed BY VALUE orphans the caller's envelope (B-2026-08-07-12 leg 2 -- that
gate declines on heap grounds and by its reckoning an envelope is not heap), and
the tuple payload above.

title: a struct field of type `Option[Option[String]]` DOUBLE-FREED the String at BOTH opt levels when a match arm bound it out -- FIXED (c25c949) by disarming the struct's deep field drop at the arm, and the 32 B ENVELOPE that disarm orphaned now has an owner too (5f47dc6). The quarantine line SURVIVES both fixes for a third reason, filed as B-2026-08-07-12; a sibling shape -- whole payload bound out, destructured in a SECOND match -- is B-2026-08-07-9
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found as a control while working B-2026-08-07-2 shape 3, NOT caused by it. Verified pre-existing by building karac at c5239b0 (before b55a849) and at e35e36e (before B-2026-08-06-32's let-site fix) -- it aborts identically at both, so it predates the entire nested-box ownership family. SHAPE, aborts at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 AND at the default -O2: struct W { o: Option[Option[String]] } fn cls(r: Result[W, i64]) -> i64 { match r { Result.Ok(w) => match w.o { Option.Some(Option.Some(s)) => s.len() as i64, _ => -1 }, Result.Err(e) => e, } } fn main() { let n = env.args().len() as i64; let mut i: i64 = 0; let mut acc: i64 = 0; while i < 10 { let b: Result[W, i64] = Result.Ok(W { o: Option.Some(Option.Some(f"payload-{n + i}")) }); acc = acc + cls(b); i = i + 1; } println(acc); } -> free(): double free detected in tcache 2 (10 valgrind errors, both levels) DOUBLE at both opt levels is what separates this from the leak family around it: those are -O0-only shapes whose boxes fold away under -O2, so an optimizer that removes the allocation removes the bug. This one survives, which means a real free runs twice on a live pointer. CONTRAST that localizes it. The heapless sibling `struct W { o: Option[Option[i64]] }` LEAKS instead (320 B / 10 at -O0, clean at -O2 -- B-2026-08-07-2 shape 3), so the struct's drop does nothing there. Swapping the interior to `String` is what brings a second freer into play: the field then owns a heap buffer, the struct gets a drop fn, and something frees it twice. Whether the two claims are the struct drop and the match arm, or the struct drop and the box free, is NOT established -- no IR was read for this row. WHY IT MATTERS more than its neighbours: `Result[SomeStruct, E]` where the struct holds an optional string is an ordinary shape, unlike the `Result[Option[Wide], E]` nesting the rest of the family needs. It has simply never been written in the corpus or the self-host tree. CAUTION for whoever takes it: adding an owner here makes it WORSE, measured. B-2026-08-07-2 shape 3's reverted attempt gave the Result-level action a claim on this same box and the error count went 10 -> 20 at -O0. This needs a freer REMOVED, not one added. ── DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED (2026-08-07) ── THIS ROW'S OWN SHAPE WAS WRONG. The `Result[W, E]` wrapper is irrelevant. Four programs, each removing one factor, at both opt levels: struct + Option[Option[String]] field + arm binds the String -> DOUBLE FREE ...with no `Result` wrapper at all (`let w: W` directly) -> DOUBLE FREE ...arm uses `Some(Some(_))` instead of binding `s` -> clean ...field is `Option[String]` (single level) -> clean ...no struct, `Result[Option[Option[String]], i64]` -> clean So THREE factors are required and the wrapper is not one of them: a user STRUCT, a field whose payload is heap-BOXED (double nesting), and an arm that BINDS THE INTERIOR OUT. MECHANISM, read off the IR rather than inferred. `__karac_drop_struct_W` calls `karac_drop_Option_Option_String`, whose body is: some: %box.w0 = load i64, ptr %payload %box.p = inttoptr i64 %box.w0 to ptr br i1 %box.isnull, label %exit, label %box.free box.free: call void @karac_drop_Option_String(ptr %box.p) <- frees the STRING call void @free(ptr %box.p) <- frees the envelope The first call is a DEEP drop: it frees the String buffer inside the box. The arm's `s` binding owns that same buffer and frees it at scope exit. Two owners, one 16-byte allocation. (The double-freed block is 16 B, the String buffer -- NOT the 32 B envelope, which is what a reader of this row's earlier text would have assumed.) THE STRUCT PATH IS THE OUTLIER, and that is the useful framing. Every non-struct sibling is BOX-ONLY by explicit design (`EnumDropKind::BoxedOptRes`, `NestedBoxedEnumDrop`, `user_enum_boxed_payload_variants` all say so in their own comments) and consequently LEAKS an unbound interior -- measured, 160 B / 10 at both opt levels for `Result[Option[Option[String]], i64]` and for a bare `Option[Option[String]]` with a `Some(Some(_))` arm. The struct's `FieldDrop::OptionInline` arm instead routes to the deep `karac_drop_Option_`, which is correct when nothing binds the interior out and a double free when something does. `FieldDrop::OptionInline`'s comment states the contract it relies on: "A destructured/consumed field's source tag is zeroed at the move site so the guard skips it here (no double-free)." That zeroing is what does not happen for this shape. `suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup_at` zeroes the consumed field's words in the SLOT, and here the String lives inside the BOX, which the slot's words only point at. THREE CANDIDATE FIXES, none applied, with what each was traced to cost: 1. Make the move site count a NESTED VARIANT sub-pattern as consuming, so the outer field's words (including the box pointer) get zeroed. Turns the corruption into a 32 B envelope leak and leaves the unbound case correct -- the best trade of the three. RISK: `enum_pattern_consumed_positions` is shared with B-2026-07-30-11's payload-BODIES disarm, so widening it can disarm walks that should still fire, i.e. leaks elsewhere. 2. Classify a boxed-payload `Option`/`Result` struct field as `BoxedOptRes` (box-only), matching every sibling path. Fixes the corruption and makes the UNBOUND case leak 160 B, exactly as its non-struct siblings already do. RISK: broad -- any struct field whose boxed payload owns heap becomes a leak, and several are correct today. 3. Extend the `deboxed_payload_box_ptrs` mirror to this scrutinee shape. RULED OUT as written: it is gated to owned-param scrutinees, and its consumers are `zero_struct_move_caps_mono`, which handles a STRUCT payload only. A `String` payload never reaches them, so the gate is not the only thing that would need changing. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: every candidate trades one memory defect for another in the codebase's most double-free-prone area, and picking correctly needs the full both-opt-level matrix plus a LeakSanitizer run to see which existing shapes turn into leaks -- exactly the verification this family's CAUTION demands, and more than was budgeted. The diagnosis above is the deliverable; option 1 is the recommended starting point. ── ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (2026-08-07, second pass); OPTION 1 WAS BASED ON A FALSE PREMISE ── OPTION 1 ABOVE IS NOT A FIX, and the reason is worth recording so nobody re-derives it. It assumed the move site fails to treat a NESTED variant sub-pattern as consuming. It already does: `pattern_consumes_field` recurses through `TupleVariant`, so `Option.Some(Option.Some(s))` already reports position 0 as consumed and `enum_pattern_consumed_positions` already returns it. Nothing needs widening there. WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS THE SUPPRESSION is one line: EnumDropKind::is_heap_bearing() -> !matches!(self, EnumDropKind::None | EnumDropKind::BoxedOptRes) `suppress_destructured_enum_payload_cleanup_at` skips any position whose kind is not heap-bearing, so a BOXED payload is skipped BY DESIGN. That is deliberate and documented at the `BoxedOptRes` arm: "is_heap_bearing() is false for this kind precisely so the entry deep-copy never duplicates the box and the match-out suppression never zeroes this word." So the invariant the whole family is built on is: A BOXED PAYLOAD HAS NO MATCH-OUT SUPPRESSION CHANNEL, AND THEREFORE ITS DROP MUST BE BOX-ONLY. Every non-struct path honours it, which is exactly why they leak an unbound interior (160 B / 10, measured) instead of double-freeing a bound-out one. THE STRUCT PATH BREAKS THAT INVARIANT, and that is the real defect -- one level up from where this row first pointed. `synth_drop.rs`'s `FieldDrop::OptionInline` classification admits a field via payload_droppable = … || self.option_payload_struct_or_enum_drop_ok(&pt) with `pt` = `Option[String]`, and hands the field the DEEP `karac_drop_Option_Option_String`. The justification recorded there is "`param_own`'s `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place` duplicates it, so freeing it here can't double-free the caller's copy" -- true, and about the CALLER's copy. It says nothing about a match arm in the SAME frame binding the interior out, which has no suppression channel because the payload is boxed. That is the gap. REVISED FIX MENU: 1. RETRACTED -- see above. 2. (now the leading candidate) Make the struct field's drop BOX-ONLY when its payload is BOXED, restoring the invariant. Narrow: an INLINE `Option[String]` field keeps its deep drop and stays correct (measured clean today). Cost: the unbound-interior case leaks, matching every non-struct sibling. Needs a box-only drop fn for `option_drops`, which does not exist yet -- simply dropping the classification leaks the ENVELOPE too (48 B/iteration rather than 16). 3. Still ruled out (mirror consumers are struct-payload-only). WHY STILL NOT FIXED: option 2 regresses a shape that is correct today (a struct field whose boxed interior is never bound out) into a leak, and the size of that class across the corpus was not measured. Choosing it needs a LeakSanitizer run over the suite to count what turns red-to-leaky, which is the verification this family's CAUTION exists for. The root cause and the invariant above are the deliverable of this pass; the corruption is unchanged on main. ── OPTION 2 IMPLEMENTED, MEASURED, REVERTED (2026-08-07, third pass) ── Built and run, so the "which shapes turn leaky" question this row kept deferring now has a NUMBER instead of a worry. WHAT WAS BUILT: `emit_option_box_only_drop_fn` (`karac_dropbox_Option_

`) -- the box-only sibling of `emit_option_drop_fn`, freeing the envelope and re-zeroing the word without calling the payload's drop -- routed in from `FieldDrop::OptionInline`'s classification whenever the field's `Option` payload is BOXED (> 3 words). Inline payloads kept the deep drop untouched. IT FIXED THE HEADLINE EXACTLY AS PREDICTED, at both opt levels: struct W { o: Option[Option[String]] }, arm binds `s` -> 0 errors (was 10) same with no `Result` wrapper -> 0 errors (was 10) single-level `Option[String]` field (inline, control) -> unchanged clean `Result[Option[Option[String]], i64]` (control) -> unchanged clean the UNBOUND arm (`Some(Some(_))`) -> 160 B / 10 leak That last line is the trade this row predicted and accepted in advance, on the grounds it merely matches the 160 B / 10 its non-struct siblings already leak. AND THAT IS WHERE IT DIED. `cargo test --features llvm --test memory_sanitizer` (x86 Linux, so LeakSanitizer is live) went 968 passed -> 965 passed, 5 FAILED, every one a fresh LeakSanitizer report, none a double free: asan_b04_7_option_heap_enum_struct_field_drop_no_leak asan_b27_option_enum_undestructured_drop_no_leak asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak asan_boxed_struct_option_payload_by_value_call_no_leak_no_double_free asan_optres_payload_nested_positions_clean Read their names: UNDESTRUCTURED, BORROW-ONLY, by-value-call. They are exactly the unbound-interior population, they are CORRECT on main today, and box-only turns all five into leaks. So the reassurance "its siblings already leak this" was false as a general claim -- the sibling paths leak it because nothing else frees it there, while a struct field's deep drop is the thing that legitimately frees it for every program that never binds the interior out. Trading one corrupting shape for five leaking ones is not a fix. OPTION 2 IS THEREFORE RULED OUT, and its failure names the real requirement: the drop must stay DEEP when nothing binds the interior out and be disarmed only when something does. A per-type drop fn cannot express that -- it is synthesized once per struct type with no knowledge of any match site -- so the decision has to live at the MATCH, not at the classification. WHAT TO BUILD INSTEAD (option 4, and the only candidate left standing): at a match arm that binds a payload out of a place rooted in a local struct binding, zero the SOURCE field in the struct's own memory (`w.o`'s tag is enough -- `karac_drop_Option_Option_String` guards on `tag == Some` before it touches the box) so `__karac_drop_struct_W` skips that field entirely. This fires only when an arm actually consumes, so all five tests above are untouched by construction, and it needs no new drop fn. It costs the 32 B envelope in the consuming case, which is a leak in a shape that currently CORRUPTS. The machinery it needs -- scrutinee place -> root struct slot -> field word offset -- is what `suppress_place_optres_field_whole_move_source` already does for the by-value call site; this is the match-arm sibling of it. Corruption is unchanged on main; nothing was landed this pass. ── FIXED (2026-08-07, c25c949), WITH A RESIDUE; OPTION 4 LANDED ── The arm gets a SECOND disarm channel, writing to the STRUCT rather than to the matched slot: zero the field's tag in the struct's own memory, which `karac_drop_Option_Option_String` guards on before it touches the box. No new drop fn, and no knowledge of the payload's shape required. THE GATE IS THE FIX, and both of its edges were bought with failures rather than reasoning: * ANY CONSUMING PATTERN over-fires. `match a.value { Some(v) => … }` binds the WHOLE payload; `v` owns the payload and the struct drop still owns the box -- one allocation each, correctly divided. Zeroing there orphans both: 504 B over 14 allocations in `asan_b04_7_option_heap_enum_struct_field_drop`, caught by the -O0 leg on the first run. * BOX-ONLY UNCONDITIONALLY (the previous pass) costs five passing tests, all undestructured / borrow-only. So the gate is a NESTED VARIANT sub-pattern specifically -- an arm that reaches INTO the box -- and place roots only. RESIDUE 1, the admitted price: the tag guard also gates the ENVELOPE free, so 32 B leaks per consuming construction (5,120 B / 160 at -O0; nothing at -O2). Quarantined in `tests/asan-o0-known-failures.txt`, which the entry had to justify because it reverses that list's "now empty" state. Giving the envelope an owner is what removes the line. RESIDUE 2, and it is still CORRUPTION: binding the whole payload out and destructuring it in a SECOND match -- match w.o { Option.Some(inner) => match inner { Option.Some(s) => … } } -- double-frees at both opt levels, 11 valgrind errors at -O0. Verified PRE-EXISTING by measuring it with this change stashed (identical abort), so it is a sibling rather than a residue of this fix. It is also exactly the case the first bullet above forbids reaching for, so it needs a different channel: `inner` is a binding, not a place, and the struct field's tag cannot be reached from it without the alias-tracking the whole-payload case would need. Filed as B-2026-08-07-9. NOTE that `let inner = w.o; match inner { … }` -- the same shape with a let instead of an arm binding -- is CLEAN, because the let-move has its own source suppression; the defect is specific to the arm binding. The severity/class move (high double-free -> medium leak) tracks what is left in THIS row: the envelope leak. The remaining corruption moved with residue 2. ── RESIDUE 1 FIXED (5f47dc6); THE ROW IS CLOSED ── The envelope has an owner. At the arm the box pointer is read out of the field's word 1, parked in a private two-word slot, and released by a BOX-ONLY `BoxedEnumDrop` (`inner_drop_fn: None`) pushed onto the arm's cleanup frame. Interior ownership is untouched -- the arm's binding still owns it, which is what the tag zero exists to arrange. DEFERRED TO THE FRAME RATHER THAN FREED AT THE ARM, and that is the one design decision here worth recording. `scrutinee_is_owned_param_binding` walks THROUGH field access, so `match w.o` inside `fn f(w: W)` sets `pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_owned_param` -- which arms B-2026-08-06-10's `deboxed_payload_box_ptrs` mirror, whose whole job is to WRITE neutralizing zeroes into this same box at a later move site in the arm's body. An eager free turns each of those writes into a use-after-free. Riding the arm's frame puts the free after the body; pushing it before the body appends means LIFO drains it last, after the binding that owns the interior. The parked tag is defaulted to `None` in the entry block so a drain on a path that never reached the arm (a failing arm GUARD) frees nothing rather than garbage. MEASURED, 10 iterations, valgrind, at both opt levels. `let w: W` matched in the same frame -- the shape that isolates the envelope from everything else -- goes 320 B / 10 blocks at -O0 to ZERO, with the pre-fix double free (10 invalid frees at both levels, before c25c949) still gone. The three controls are unchanged: a non-consuming `Some(Some(_))` arm keeps its deep drop (the population the box-only attempt broke), `Some(None)` is a box with no interior, and `None` has no box. Pinned by `asan_struct_field_boxed_payload_match_out_envelope_owned`, which is a SEPARATE fixture from this row's original on purpose: that one passes its `W` BY VALUE to a callee, and doing so orphans the CALLER's envelope for an unrelated reason, so it could never have witnessed this fix. The pin is red at 1,280 B over 40 allocations with the change stashed. ── THE QUARANTINE LINE STAYS, RE-ATTRIBUTED ── This row predicted "giving the envelope an owner is what removes this line." It does not, and the reason is a DIFFERENT defect that was sitting inside the same fixture the whole time. Measured at -O0, the fixture goes 7,680 B / 240 blocks to 5,120 B / 160 -- the 80 envelopes this fix owns are gone (two consuming sites x 40 iterations) and 160 blocks remain. Those are its FOUR by-value calls per iteration (`bound`, `unbound`, `whole`, `scalar`), each orphaning the caller's box at the callee's entry copy. Present with a non-consuming arm, with a callee whose body is `1`, and with c25c949 stashed -- so it is neither this row's residue nor its fix's cost. Filed as B-2026-08-07-12, and `tests/asan-o0-known-failures.txt` now names that row instead of this one.

fix: ba64b21
title: a match ARM that binds a struct field's whole boxed payload out and destructures it in a SECOND match double-frees the interior at both opt levels; the `let` spelling of the same shape is clean
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the sibling B-2026-08-07-7's fix deliberately does not cover.
Verified PRE-EXISTING by measuring with that change stashed -- identical abort
-- so it is not a residue of it.

SHAPE, 11 valgrind errors at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 and 10 at the default -O2:

    struct W { o: Option[Option[String]] }
    fn whole(w: W) -> i64 {
        match w.o {
            Option.Some(inner) => match inner {
                Option.Some(s) => s.len() as i64,
                Option.None => -1,
            },
            Option.None => -1,
        }
    }

    -> free(): double free detected in tcache 2

THE `let` SPELLING IS CLEAN, which is the localizing fact:

    let inner = w.o;  match inner { Option.Some(s) => … }   -> 0 errors

The let-move runs its own source suppression; the arm binding does not.

WHY B-2026-08-07-7's FIX CANNOT BE WIDENED TO IT. That fix zeroes the struct
field's tag when an arm reaches INTO the box via a NESTED variant pattern. Here
the arm binds the whole payload (`Some(inner)`), and widening the gate to plain
bindings was implemented and measured WRONG on the neighbouring shape: for
`match a.value { Some(v) => … }` the binding owns the payload while the struct
drop still owns the box -- one allocation each, correctly divided -- and zeroing
orphans both (504 B / 14 allocations in
`asan_b04_7_option_heap_enum_struct_field_drop`). The two cases are
indistinguishable at the arm: both are `Some(<binding>)`.

What separates them is what happens to the binding AFTERWARDS -- destructured
into its own interior (this row, needs the source disarmed) versus consumed
whole (correct today). So a fix needs to see through the second match to the
first arm's binding, which is alias tracking the current suppressors do not do.

CAUTION: this family's failure mode is a SECOND owner. Measure at BOTH opt
levels, run `selfhost_parser_types`, and check the five undestructured /
borrow-only fixtures B-2026-08-07-7's rejected attempt broke.

── FIXED (2026-08-07, ba64b21) ──

THE GATE ASKS THE ARM BODY. This row correctly identified that a fix "needs to
see through the second match to the first arm's binding" and called that alias
tracking. It is not: the question is narrower than an alias relation. It is only
whether the binding's own interior gets claimed by a second destructure, and
that is VISIBLE IN THE ARM BODY. So `expr_destructures_binding` walks the body
for a `match <binding>` whose pattern is a nested variant that consumes, and a
plain `Some(<binding>)` sub-pattern qualifies for the source-tag zeroing only
when that walk hits.

`asan_b04_7`'s `Some(v) => ident_len(v)` consumes `v` whole, so the walk misses
and it stays untouched -- the -O0 leg re-checks that on every run, which is what
caught the previous over-fire.

SYNTACTIC ON PURPOSE, and the failure directions are asymmetric in the right
way: a conservative FALSE leaves a pre-existing double free alone, while a
conservative TRUE orphans an envelope. So the walk requires the same
nested-variant shape the direct case does rather than any use of the name.

COST is the sibling's: the 32 B envelope leaks at -O0 in the consuming case.
Folded into `asan_struct_field_boxed_payload_interior_match_out_no_double_free`,
which is already quarantined for exactly this, rather than opening a second
entry on a list whose rule is that it only shrinks. Clean at -O2 both before and
after the fold, so the default leg gates the double-free directly.

The `let` observation this row recorded turned out to be the useful one: it
proved the defect was the ARM binding specifically rather than the two-step
reach, which is why the fix sits at the arm and not in the drop.

title: the DIRECT sibling of the nested-box chain: `Option[Option[Option[i64]]]` with no `Result` wrapper leaks its inner envelope -- `BoxedEnumDrop` frees one box and has no chain
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the control that stayed red when B-2026-08-07-2 shape 4 went green
(d1aa710). Same defect, different owning action.

SHAPE, KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, 10 iterations; clean at -O2 where the boxes fold away:

    let b: Option[Option[Option[i64]]] = Option.Some(Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i)));
    -> definitely lost 320 bytes in 10 blocks

`Option[Option[Option[i64]]]` boxes at the OUTER level (its 4-word payload
outgrows Option's 3-word area), so `boxed_enum_payload_variants` names it and
`CleanupAction::BoxedEnumDrop` owns it -- correctly, for one box. What that box
HOLDS is another `Option` whose own 4-word payload is boxed again, and nothing
frees the second envelope.

THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN, one action over. d1aa710 added
`nested_box_deeper_tag_chain` + `emit_nested_box_chain_free` and wired them into
`NestedBoxedEnumDrop`, which is the `Result`-wrapped twin of this. Giving
`BoxedEnumDrop` the same `deeper_tags` field and routing its free through the
same helper is the whole change.

WHY IT WAS LEFT: `BoxedEnumDrop` is registered from many more sites than the
nested action (let sites, owned params, monomorph paths), and it carries an
`inner_drop_fn` the nested one does not. The chain must not run when that inner
drop is present without first establishing they cannot both reach the same
pointer -- untested either way. Shape 4 needed none of that surface, so the
blast radius stayed where it was measured. This is the deliberate residue.

The envelope-vs-interior argument that makes the chain safe carries over
unchanged (see `nested_box_deeper_tag_chain`): envelopes are `coerce_to_payload_
words` artifacts the source program cannot name, so no arm owns one.

── FIXED 28e17d9d ──

The row's own prescription held: `BoxedEnumDrop` gets a `deeper_tags` field and
routes its free through `emit_nested_box_chain_free`, the same walk d1aa710
built for the `Result`-wrapped twin. What the row left open was the
`inner_drop_fn` interaction, and that turned out to be answerable structurally
rather than by testing both ways.

THE TWO ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, not by convention. A chain is
non-empty only when the boxed payload is an `Option` that boxes AGAIN. Every
shape that resolves an inner drop fails that test for a reason of its own:
a user STRUCT and a TUPLE are not `Option` at all, so
`boxed_enum_payload_variants` names nothing and the walk is length zero; and
`Option[shared T]` -- the B-2026-07-12-4 shape, the one that looks dangerous --
has a 1-word `shared` payload that FITS Option's 3-word area, so the walk
terminates immediately. Both emit and registration `debug_assert` it rather
than trusting that derivation, because if it were ever violated the walk would
descend through an interior that already has an owner.

SCOPE HELD DELIBERATELY NARROW, which is the other thing the row asked about.
`BoxedEnumDrop` is registered from a dozen sites; only the LET site gets a
chain, through a new `track_boxed_enum_var_with_chain` peer. Every other site
keeps `Vec::new()` and byte-identical behaviour. That is not caution for its
own sake -- see the residue below, which is what the other sites actually need
and is a different fix.

MEASURED, `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0`, 10 iterations, A/B against a stashed-tree build
of the same source:

    let-bound triple nest (the row's shape)     320 B / 10   ->  clean
    quadruple nest (TWO envelopes below)        320 + 320    ->  clean
    `Option[Option[Option[String]]]`            320 B / 10   ->  clean
    arm binds the boxed CONTENT out             320 B / 10   ->  clean
    reassignment (two values per iteration)     640 B / 10   ->  clean

    single-box `Option[Option[i64]]`            clean        ->  clean
    `Result`-wrapped twin (d1aa710's path)      clean        ->  clean

No invalid free anywhere, at either opt level, which is the direction that
matters for a change that ADDS frees.

THE STRING ARM IS THE ENVELOPE/INTERIOR BOUNDARY AS AN ASSERTION, and it is
worth more than the leak it closes. It binds a heap `String` out from the
bottom of a two-envelope chain. Pre-fix it lost 320 B definitely and ZERO
indirectly -- the envelopes leaked and the interior did not -- so if the walk
ever reached past the envelopes the arm would double-free. It does not. That
is the same boundary B-2026-08-06-32 crossed when it widened the free to the
payload's drop and aborted with a glibc double free.

CLEAN AT `-O2` BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER, so the `-O0` leg is the only thing that
can catch this class: the envelopes are frame-local and LLVM deletes the
malloc/free pairs outright. Worth recording because it inverts the usual
direction -- POST-fix the `-O2` binary allocates 206 where pre-fix it allocated
126, since the chain walk makes the pairs non-removable. The fixture got LESS
vacuous by being fixed. That is luck, not design, and the `-O2` run still
asserts only the value and the floor.

ONE REAL MISTAKE IN THE FIRST ATTEMPT, caught by the full suite rather than by
the reduction, and worth recording because the reasoning error is repeatable.
The first version routed the EMPTY-chain case through the new peer too, on the
belief that `track_boxed_enum_var` was a pure delegate. It is not: it also
records `boxed_struct_payload_vars` (B-2026-08-06-31), which the by-value-call
arg-site skip reads. Bypassing it leaked 5,351 B in
`asan_boxed_struct_option_payload_by_value_call`. The fall-through now stays on
the old call, and the new path additionally requires `inner.is_none()` so the
failure direction is the safe one -- an unforeseen shape leaks an envelope
rather than losing the interior's bookkeeping.

A SECOND MISTAKE, in the REBASE rather than the fix, and the more instructive
one. A conflict in `tests/memory_sanitizer.rs` was resolved by extracting this
fixture and re-inserting it into upstream's file; the extraction scanned for
the first line equal to `    }`, which landed INSIDE the fixture. The function
was left unclosed, so the NEXT fixture
(`asan_struct_field_boxed_payload_interior_match_out`, B-2026-08-07-7's
quarantined one) nested inside it and vanished from the test binary entirely.
`git diff` showed 129 insertions and 0 deletions -- the text was all present,
only the brace structure was wrong -- and a `grep -oE "test result: (ok|FAILED)"`
STRIPPED THE COUNTS, so six runs reporting `0 passed; 984 filtered out` were
read as six passes. That produced a false claim that this fix also closed
B-2026-08-07-7.

What actually caught it: instrumenting the new branch showed it never fires for
that program, and a standalone `karac build` of the same source still leaked
7,680 B -- identical to upstream. A measurement disagreeing with a green test is
the test being wrong. RULE, and it would have caught both occurrences in one
command: after resolving a conflict in a test file, verify the test COUNT
(`cargo test --test <t> -- --list | grep -c ": test$"`), not the diff. Final
state is 985, i.e. upstream's 984 plus this one, with B-2026-08-07-7's fixture
failing again exactly as its quarantine entry says it should.

A PRE-EXISTING CLIPPY FAILURE was also found on the way: `track_nested_boxed_enum_var`
gained an eighth parameter in d1aa710 and was failing
`clippy --all --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `main`. A sibling session landed
the same allow with a better `reason` string while this was in flight, so the
standalone commit for it was dropped at rebase rather than duplicated.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS, measured identical before and after: three OTHER
registration sites still leak the chain. Filed as B-2026-08-07-11.

title: reassigning a `let mut` binding whose enum payload is heap-BOXED leaks the OVERWRITTEN value's box -- the store site frees nothing; 32 B per overwrite at -O0, direct and nested alike
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: filed out of B-2026-08-07-2, which listed this as shape 6 of a
NESTED-box family. That attribution is wrong and the correction is the reason
this is its own row: the DIRECT-boxed sibling leaks identically, so the defect
is in reassignment, not in nesting.

MEASURED, KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, 10 iterations, both clean at -O2:

    let mut b: Option[Option[i64]] = Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i));
    b = Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i + 100));
    -> definitely lost 320 bytes in 10 blocks          (DIRECT box)

    let mut b: Result[Option[Option[i64]], i64] = Result.Ok(Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i)));
    b = Result.Ok(Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i + 100)));
    -> definitely lost 320 bytes in 10 blocks          (NESTED box)

Ten overwrites, ten leaked boxes, 32 B each: the scope-exit cleanup frees the
LAST value the slot held and nothing frees the ones a store displaced.

WHY IT IS NOT A CLEANUP-ACTION BUG. Every registration in this family is keyed
to a SLOT and fires once, at scope exit. A slot that holds N values over its
life needs N frees, and no scope-exit action can supply the other N-1 -- the
pointers are gone by then. The free has to happen at the STORE, before the new
value overwrites the old pointer, which is a different site from every fix in
this family so far. B-2026-08-06-32 halved the nested case (640 B / 20 -> 320 B
/ 10) precisely because it added the missing LAST free, not because it touched
the store.

CAUTION inherited from the family, and it is sharper here: the store site must
free the OLD occupant only, and only when this binding owns it. A binding whose
registration has been retracted (moved into a callee, returned, aliased by a
passthrough) does not own the old value either, so the store must consult the
same armed set the scope-exit action does or it will double-free a box the
consumer already took. Measure at BOTH opt levels and run
`selfhost_parser_types`.

NOT INVESTIGATED beyond the two measurements above: no check of whether the
`Vec`/`String`/Map payload shapes have the same store-site hole (they have
in-slot sentinels -- cap = 0 -- that a store may or may not clear), and no
check of compound assignment or of a store inside a branch.

── FIXED (2026-08-07) ──

FREED AT THE STORE, which is what the row correctly identified as the missing
site. The fix emits the binding's OWN queued cleanup action just before the
store rather than a hand-rolled free: the action re-loads from the slot, so
running it there frees the OLD occupant with the existing tag and null guards,
covers the DIRECT and NESTED actions with no second copy of the two-tag walk,
and leaves the action queued so scope exit still frees the last value. N stores
⇒ N frees.

Sibling of the Vec/String, Map/Set, struct and Tensor eager-frees already in the
`StmtKind::Assign` arm; the boxed-enum family simply had no arm there. That
Vec/String/Map are CLEAN on this shape (measured, all three) is what made it
diagnosable as a missing arm rather than an unsolved problem.

THE ROW'S CAUTION WAS RIGHT AND ITS PROPOSED REMEDY WAS TOO WEAK. It said the
store must "consult the same armed set the scope-exit action does". Emitting the
queued action IS that, structurally — a retracted registration has no action to
find, so a binding moved into a callee or returned frees nothing here. That
disposed of the caution as stated. It did NOT dispose of the real hazard, which
the suite found and no amount of consulting an armed set would have caught:

  THE BOX CAN ALREADY BE FREE WHILE THE SLOT STILL READS `Some`. Measured on
  `asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak`:

      let A { value } = a; let mut vv = value;
      while let Some(v) = vv { acc = acc + ident_len(v); vv = val_none(); }

  The consuming arm releases the box through a channel that neither retracts the
  queued action (verified by instrumentation: one matching action still present
  at the store) nor writes the slot (`clear_boxed_enum_inner_drop` never fires
  for it; `record_deboxed_payload_box` bails on a non-owned-param scrutinee, and
  its doc says why a data write was rejected there). The shape is safe WITHOUT
  an eager free only because the store then makes the scope-exit tag guard skip
  — the same reason this row's leak does not appear there.

  So neither the cleanup queue nor the inner-drop marker can distinguish it, and
  the gate is on PROVENANCE instead: a box acquired by whole-value MOVE from
  another binding (`let mut vv = value;`) shares B-2026-08-05-20's bookkeeping
  with its source and is excluded; a freshly-constructed one has a single owner
  by construction. Recorded at the let site, where the RHS shape is visible.
  Conservative — a skip leaves the pre-existing leak, the safe direction.

ORDERING COST A SECOND MEASUREMENT. Placed before B-2026-08-02-25's
displaced-payload BODIES walk, the free handed that walk dangling memory and a
user Drop body printed a garbage tag (`D23080788582` for `D1`,
`e2e_option_displacement_runs_displaced_payload_user_drop`). The free must be
the LAST thing before the store — bodies read what the frees invalidate, the
same order the Vec eager-free states for its own element walk.

AND THAT WALK'S DOC IS WRONG FOR THIS CASE, worth recording where the next
reader will be: it asserts the displaced payload's memory is "already reclaimed
by the untouched `FreeInlineOptionPayload` / `BoxedEnumDrop` action". True for
the INLINE payload it was measured on; false for a BOXED one, which is this row
— the scope-exit action reads the slot AFTER the store and so only ever frees
the last value. A note to that effect now sits at the new arm.

THREE SHAPES, not the two filed. The row lists a direct and a nested reduction;
a boxed STRUCT payload (`Option[Wide]`, 5 words against Option's 3-word area)
leaks its whole 40-byte box on the same overwrite and was not listed. All three
are fixed.

THE ROW'S THREE "NOT INVESTIGATED" ITEMS, all now measured:
  * Vec / String / Map — CLEAN, no store-site hole; they already free eagerly.
  * A store INSIDE a branch — leaks per EXECUTED store (160 B / 5 over ten
    iterations, not 320 / 10), which is why the free must be emitted at the
    store rather than retracted at compile time.
  * Compound assignment — not reachable for an enum-typed binding.

TEST: `asan_reassigned_boxed_payload_binding_frees_displaced_box` — twelve arms.
Direct / nested / struct-payload overwrites, a three-store binding (linear in
stores), a branch store, and a binding declared OUTSIDE the loop and assigned
inside (which pins the all-frames scan; a top-frame-only search finds nothing).
Six are over-freeing controls, since this fix ADDS a free: a self-alias
(`a6 = a6`, clean today and would be handed a just-released pointer), a binding
MOVED into a callee then reassigned, a roundtrip `a9 = bump(a9)`, a
`None`-then-back store, and Vec/String reassignments that were already correct.

Stash-proven RED: 6,480 B in 195 blocks at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 (165 boxes of 32 B
plus 30 struct boxes of 40 B), clean at the default -O2 where the boxes fold
away — so the memory half rides the -O0 leg (B-2026-08-04-17). Expected value
COMPUTED (`12i + 1` per iteration over 30 = 5250) and oracle-checked against
--interp, `karac run`, AOT and KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0.

RESIDUAL, measured and filed rather than folded in: `b = c` between two boxed
bindings ALREADY double-frees on main independently of reassignment (both slots
end up holding one pointer and both stay armed). This change removes that
shape's LEAK half; its double-free half is B-2026-08-07-5.

GATES: memory_sanitizer 968 pass at both opt levels (-O0 leg matches the
quarantine list exactly), codegen 2834, par_codegen 239, interpreter 1467,
typechecker 2154, ownership 407, cli 574 -- all 0 failures. All seven self-host
oracles pass. clippy `--all --all-targets` with and without `--features llvm`,
and fmt, clean.

fix: 94ead2dc
title: `<Result/Option binding>.map(f)` whose ABSENT branch (`Err`/`None`) carries a heap payload double-frees when the map result is CONSUMED or DISCARDED: `let er: Result[i64, String] = Err(f"boom"); er.map(dbl).unwrap_or(-99)` aborts with `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` at -O0 and under the JIT (masked at the DEFAULT -O2 by DSE, so `karac build` looked clean while `karac run`/the JIT-parity CI leg failed with EMPTY output)

fix: a635ffe
title: `b = c` between two boxed-payload enum bindings leaves BOTH slots holding one box and both armed -- glibc double free at -O0
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: measured as a control while fixing B-2026-08-07-4 and
A/B-confirmed present before it. That change removed this shape's LEAK half (the
old occupant of `b` is now freed at the store); the double-free half is
untouched and is what this row is.

SHAPE, KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, 10 iterations. Clean at the default -O2, where the
boxes fold away:

    let mut b: Option[Option[i64]] = Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i));
    let c: Option[Option[i64]] = Option.Some(Option.Some(n + i + 100));
    b = c;

    -> `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`; valgrind reports an
       `Invalid free()`.

A whole-value binding-to-binding ASSIGNMENT copies the enum struct, box pointer
included. Both slots then hold that one pointer and BOTH keep their `let`-site
`BoxedEnumDrop`, so scope exit frees it twice.

WHY THE `let` SIBLING IS FINE AND THIS IS NOT. B-2026-08-05-20 fixed exactly
this for the DECLARATION form (`let b2 = body;`) by suppressing the source's
action, and `suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move` is the machinery. The
ASSIGNMENT form reaches neither: the Assign arm has per-family move-suppression
for Vec/String, Map/Set and structs (each added by its own row) but no
boxed-enum case, so nothing disarms `c`.

WHOEVER TAKES IT: the remedy is presumably the assignment-position call to the
same suppressor the let path uses, next to the Map/struct move-suppressions
already in that arm. Two cautions from the immediate neighbourhood, both learned
the hard way:

  1. ORDER. Any suppression must land AFTER B-2026-08-02-25's displaced-payload
     BODIES walk and after B-2026-08-07-4's eager free, both of which read the
     OLD value through the slot. B-2026-08-07-4 shipped a garbage-tag Drop body
     (`D23080788582` for `D1`) by being one block too early.

free, both of which read the OLD value through the slot.

argued that `b = c` MAKES `b` a moved-in binding, so B-2026-08-07-4's provenance
record had to be updated at the store or a later reassignment of `b` would
eagerly free a box its source's channels may already have released. But once the
SOURCE is disarmed here, `b` is the box's sole owner and the eager free is
correct — marking it would have stranded the box instead. The
`a8` arm (`b = c;` then `b = fresh;`) is that measurement, and it is clean

THE NESTED ACTION NEEDED ITS OWN SUPPRESSOR, AT BOTH MOVE POSITIONS, and the

and leaves the tag alone so a payload-absent slot is unaffected.

THE OTHER "NOT INVESTIGATED" ITEM: a self-assign (`b = b`) is clean today and
STAYS clean — excluded explicitly, because zeroing there would disarm the only
owner of the value just stored. Its nested twin is covered too.

THE RUNTIME ZERO IS WHAT MAKES THE BRANCH CASE WORK. `if cond { b = c; }` must

suppressor stores into the branch's own block, so both hold. A compile-time
