SOURCE NOTE: seen while running the full suite to verify B-2026-08-23-13. Not caused by that change -- it alters one diagnostic string and adds a graph build reachable only from the mutual-recursion note emitter, and a note string cannot corrupt a compiled program's heap. Stated as mechanism plus isolation runs, NOT as proof.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL FLAKE. The test is the regression guard added by 114a9d2 for B-2026-08-24-15 -- Vec.insert/remove/swap_remove skipping bounds checks and CORRUPTING THE HEAP, a high-severity soundness fix. A guard that intermittently goes green is the worst possible failure mode for that class: CI can pass while the bug is live. The observed failure is not a timeout or a harness hiccup; it is the ORIGINAL BUG'S SIGNATURE (no panic, allocator abort).

MEASURED: 1 failure in 2 full `--features llvm` runs (the run that failed aborted cargo's remaining ~85 targets, which is how it was noticed); 0 in 1 codegen-only run of 3198 tests; 0 in 3 isolated runs. Both full runs used `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only`, which affects only karac's own debug info, not emitted code.

TWO CANDIDATES, NEITHER DIAGNOSED, and they differ enormously in severity:
  (a) an E2E harness race -- the codegen suite compiles to an output path, and under full-suite parallelism a collision would mean the assertion ran some OTHER binary, which would explain both the missing panic and an unrelated allocator abort. Cosmetic, but it silently weakens every E2E assertion, not just this one.
  (b) a genuinely intermittent failure of the emitted bounds check, i.e. B-2026-08-24-15 is not fully fixed. That would be high severity.
Whoever picks this up should settle (a) vs (b) FIRST -- e.g. by having the harness assert the binary it is about to run is the one it just built, and by looping the full suite. Do not close this by re-running until green; that is the property being reported.

CANDIDATE (a), harness race: ONE MECHANISM RULED OUT, A DIFFERENT ONE FOUND AND CLOSED.

Ruled out: all EIGHT static counters in tests/codegen.rs feed DISTINCT path
templates (karac_e2e_ / _envtrace_ / _mapvd_ / _par_returns_ / _hotswap_ /
_jit_tmpl_ / _ffi_ / _jit_ir_), and every executable path already carried pid +
per-process atomic counter. Two live processes or two threads in one process
therefore cannot collide, so the straightforward "two tests raced on one path"
story does not hold.

Found instead: pid+counter is unique among LIVE processes but NOT over time.
Artifact cleanup runs only on the success path, so a killed run leaks -- 51
stale /tmp/karac_e2e_* files were present during this investigation -- and a
later process reusing that pid restarts its counter at 0, landing on exactly
those leaked paths. Executing one would run an unrelated program, which fits
BOTH reported symptoms (no panic, plus an allocator abort with no connection to
the test). Not proven to be this failure; it is a real hole regardless.

cannot alias, a pre-emptive unlink of both paths so nothing is inherited, and an
assertion after a successful link that the executable actually exists. The
harness can no longer run a binary it did not just build, so a recurrence after
this commit is evidence FOR (b) rather than ambiguous.

This row's core fear -- "a guard that intermittently goes green is the worst
possible failure mode for that class: CI can pass while the bug is live" -- is a
property NO amount of sampling can fix. 30,000 clean compile+runs bounded a rate;
they cannot show the check is present. `codegen_tests::
vec_mutation_bounds_checks_survive_into_emitted_object` now asserts it directly:
for each of insert/remove/swap_remove it compiles a program whose index is
`env.args().len()` (opaque at compile time) and asserts the method's panic
message survives into the EMITTED OBJECT -- past codegen AND the LLVM pipeline,
which an IR-only assertion would not cover.

THREE DESIGN CONSTRAINTS, each found by measurement, each load-bearing:
  - THE INDEX MUST BE OPAQUE. LLVM deleting the check when it can PROVE the index
    in range is CORRECT, so a literal index would assert against legitimate
    optimisation. Measured: with a literal `0` all three messages correctly
    vanish from the binary.
  - ONE PROGRAM PER METHOD. Chained calls let the compiler carry a range fact
    across them: in a combined program `remove`'s check was correctly folded away
    because a preceding successful `insert(i, _)` proves `i <= len`.
  - IT ASSERTS ON THE OBJECT, so it needs no linker and no runtime archive.
    Unlike the E2E guard it has NO soft-skip path and cannot report a vacuous
    green.
It carries its own anti-vacuity assertion (the three messages must be ABSENT from
an object whose program never calls those methods) and was MUTATION-TESTED:
removing the `insert` bounds check from vec_method.rs makes it fail with the
method named; restoring it makes it pass. Runs in 0.05s.

This does not close the row -- it removes the failure mode that made the row
urgent. A future regression that drops a check is now caught deterministically on
every CI run, on every architecture, instead of depending on a rare execution
happening to expose it. The x86_64 sampling leg remains open.

title: An ASSOCIATED fn inside a BOUNDED generic impl saw the impl's OWN bound as unsatisfied on a local receiver

fix:
FIXED by 8e93189. `self` parses as `ExprKind::SelfValue`, NOT `Identifier("self")`, and the generic call path's ref-argument lowering (`compile_generic_call`, src/codegen/mono.rs) produced a pointer from exactly three arms: an `Identifier` through `get_data_ptr`, an index borrow through `ref_arg_index_borrow_ptr`, and `mut_ref_place_arg_ptr` -- which handles only `FieldAccess` / `TupleIndex`, on the explicit stated assumption that "a bare identifier already took the `get_data_ptr` fast path above". `SelfValue` matched NONE of the three, so it fell through to `materialize_rvalue_for_ref_arg` and the callee received a pointer to a COPY of the receiver. Every mutation the sibling made through `mut ref self` landed on that copy and was discarded.

The fix normalises the receiver to the name `self` before the arm chain, so it takes `get_data_ptr`, which loads the stored pointer for a `ref`/`mut ref` param exactly as for any other borrow. Five lines. The same `SelfValue`-is-not-an-`Identifier` normalisation is already spelled out at `control_flow_for.rs`, `calls.rs` and `call_dispatch.rs` -- this is the fourth site to need it, which is the pattern worth noticing more than the individual fix.

MEASURED at -O0, where nothing is inlined, the caller copied the whole `{data,len,cap}` Vec out of `self` into a stack temporary and passed its address:
    mov 0x68(%rsp),%rdx    ; rdx = real self ptr
    mov (%rdx),%rax        ; load self.xs.data
    mov 0x8(%rdx),%rcx     ; load self.xs.len
    mov 0x10(%rdx),%rdx    ; load self.xs.cap
    mov %rax,0x70(%rsp)    ; ...into a LOCAL COPY
    lea 0x70(%rsp),%rsi    ; pass &copy, not %rdi
    call Box.one$i64
At -O2 the same defect reads as a dead store: the optimizer inlined the sibling, saw the length store land somewhere never read back, deleted it, and `probe` returned the length it loaded at ENTRY.

CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S NARROWING, which matters for anyone trimming the regression test. The row reported (a) "one sibling call returning Option[T], NO loop -> correct" and (b) "sibling call + out.push(v), NO loop -> correct", concluding it "takes BOTH the loop and the sibling call". It does not. A SINGLE call already loses the mutation -- `probe()` above returns len 2 instead of 1 after one pop. (a) and (b) looked correct because they checked only the RETURNED VALUE, which is right either way: popping from a copy still returns the correct last element. The receiver's state afterward is the thing that has to be asserted. The loop is not a trigger, it is an amplifier -- it turns a silent wrong answer into a non-terminating one, which is why this surfaced as a hang. Blast radius is correspondingly wider than filed: every `mut ref self` sibling call in a generic impl was affected, loop or not.

fix: FIXED by e01dce4. `break_value_is_fresh_owned_handle` now recurses through `If` / `IfLet` / `Match` / `Block` / `Seq` / `Unsafe` tails. Exactly one tail runs, but the result slot is written once for all of them, so EVERY tail has to manufacture ownership -- an ALL-tails conjunction. An `if` with no `else` declines (it yields unit and can carry nothing) and an empty arm list is guarded explicitly, since `all` over an empty iterator is vacuously true and would claim ownership of a value no arm produces. No emission changed: this is still permission, not mechanism.
title: A BRANCHING `break` carrier that owns heap is still refused: `break if c { Node { v: 4 } } else { Node { v: 5 } }` fails module verification while the interpreter returns 4. Each tail is a fresh temporary, but the `If` itself is not one of the forms `break_value_is_fresh_owned_handle` admits.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: the remainder left by B-2026-08-25-1, which opened the pointer gate to DIRECT rvalue carriers -- a `shared` struct literal and a call / method call -- and deliberately stopped there.

MEASURED on 0892679:
  shared struct Node { v: i64 }
  fn pick() -> Node { let mut i = 0; loop { i = i + 1; if i == 2 { break if i > 1 { Node { v: 4 } } else { Node { v: 5 } } } } }
      interp: 4    AOT/JIT: codegen failed: Module verification failed
A `break match ... { ... }` whose arms construct is the same shape through a different node.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE WITH -1: the predicate there is an ALLOWLIST of forms that manufacture ownership, chosen over a "not obviously borrowed" test because the forms that must keep failing are PLACE reads (`break o.inner`, `break vs[0]`) which hand out a handle the container still owns. Extending it through a branch needs an ALL-tails rule -- every tail fresh, since ONE place-reading tail would be enough to make the store a second owner -- and that is a strictly stronger claim than the direct forms, which the `return` twin's IR settles on its own. `tests/codegen.rs::test_loop_break_borrowed_field_stays_refused` is the guard that a later widening must not break.

WHY IT IS LOW: same three reasons as -1. The workaround is to bind first (`let n = if c { ... } else { ... }; break n`), which is one line; the failure is a loud compile error rather than a wrong answer or a corruption; and the corpus sweep during B-2026-08-24-10 found zero value-carrying breaks anywhere in kara/ or kara-katas/, so nothing in-tree hits it.

LIKELY SHAPE OF THE FIX: recurse `break_value_is_fresh_owned_handle` through `If` / `Match` / `Block` / `Seq` / `Unsafe` tails with an ALL-tails conjunction, mirroring how `init_projects_out_of_container_element` walks the same nodes (note that one uses ANY-tail, because it NARROWS a registration where this WIDENS a permission -- the quantifier flips with the direction of the risk). Verify against `tests/memory_sanitizer.rs`, not output alone, and add a mixed-tail fixture (one tail a literal, one a borrowed field) that must stay refused.
THE QUANTIFIER IS THE WHOLE SUBTLETY, and it is the one thing a later reader is likely to get wrong. The sibling walker over these exact same AST nodes -- `init_projects_out_of_container_element` in `src/codegen/stmts.rs` -- uses ANY-tail. The two are not inconsistent and must not be "aligned": that walker NARROWS a registration, so being wrong leaves the container owning heap it already owned; this one WIDENS a permission, so being wrong is a use-after-free. The quantifier flips with the direction of the risk. Both the rationale and a mixed-tail regression test now guard it.

MEASURED on e01dce4, all three backends agreeing:
  break if i > 1 { Node { v: 4 } } else { Node { v: 5 } }        -> 4
  break match i { 2 => Node { v: 7 }, _ => Node { v: 9 } }       -> 7
  break { let k = i * 3; Node { v: k } }                          -> 6
  break if c { Inner { v: 1 } } else { o.inner }                  -> STILL REFUSED (module verification), interpreter 5
The last line is the point of the ALL rule: one place-reading tail sinks the whole expression, because admitting the branch on the strength of the fresh tail alone would make the slot a second owner on the OTHER path -- a use-after-free reachable only when `c` is false. Pinned by `tests/codegen.rs::test_loop_break_mixed_branch_tails_stay_refused`, alongside the direct-form guard `test_loop_break_borrowed_field_stays_refused` from B-2026-08-25-1.

TWO ASAN FIXTURES cover the admitted shapes bidirectionally (`asan_loop_break_branching_rvalue_single_owner`, `asan_loop_break_match_arm_rvalue_single_owner`): each allocates a scratch handle on EVERY iteration that the breaking path must still drain while carrying an unrelated one out, so too few decs leaks the scratches and too many frees what escaped. The mixed-tail counterpart cannot be exercised under ASAN at all -- it is refused at compile time -- which is why its guard lives in the codegen suite instead.

title: `File.open` takes an owned `String`, so a read-only path predicate cannot borrow one and must clone
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: surfaced writing the TIFF reader for apps/cumulus (kara-katas). The natural shape for `fn is_cstack(path: ref String) -> bool` -- a predicate that opens a file, reads four magic bytes and closes it -- does not compile: `File.open(path)` reports `expected 'String', found 'ref String'` (cumulus.kara:630 at the time). The stdlib signature is `File.open(path: String)`, i.e. it MOVES the path, so any read-only predicate over a path either takes ownership it does not want (and the caller loses the String for its own later use -- the exact ownership warning that led here: `value 'inp' moved here, used again here`) or clones at the call site. Worked around with `is_cstack(inp.clone())`, which is one String clone per program run and costs nothing measurable; the cost is ERGONOMIC, and it is the kind of friction that pushes a writer toward taking ownership everywhere. Rust's `File::open` takes `AsRef<Path>`, which is precisely the affordance missing here. The narrow fix is a `ref String` parameter mode on `File.open` (and the same question applies to `File.create`, and to any stdlib entry point that accepts a path); the broader one is whether Kara wants an `AsRef`-shaped bound at all, which is a design question, not a bug fix. Filed rather than fixed because the workaround is free and the design half is not obviously settled -- see the ownership-tier section of design.md.

fix:
FIXED by cbc545f. ROOT CAUSE: `self` parses as `ExprKind::SelfValue`, NOT `Identifier("self")`, so the `let`-binding site in `src/codegen/stmts.rs` that records a binding's concrete generic instantiation into `enum_inst_var_types` never fired for `let mut h = self`. Its chain was: a concrete generic ANNOTATION, else the span-keyed `enum_inst_type_from_span(value)`, else `field_move_out_struct_inst(value)`. A bare `self` RHS has no annotation, is not a FieldAccess, and the span table is a PRE-monomorphization record -- it can only ever hold the generic form (`Heap[T]`), and for a bare `self` token it holds nothing at all. So `h` got no recorded instantiation.

The consequence is at the sibling CALL site, not at the `let`. `compile_method_call`'s generic-impl arm binds the impl's type params from the RECEIVER's recorded instantiation (the impl's `T` appears only inside the `self` param's `Heap[T]` shape, which `infer_type_args` does not recurse into). With no record for `h`, that binding produced None, so no monomorph was selected and the call was lowered against the UNMANGLED default prototype -- `Heap.pop_one`, built at the all-`i64` base layout.

PROOF, from `objdump` of an -O0 AOT build of the minimal repro: pre-fix the binary contains `Heap.take$struct` and a bare `Heap.pop_one`; post-fix it contains `Heap.take$struct` and `Heap.pop_one$struct`. The working control (the same method called directly from `main`) emitted `Heap.pop_one$struct` all along.

That is also the whole explanation for the two conditions the row narrowed but could not account for. `T = i64` was correct because the default prototype's base layout IS i64 -- a coincidence, not a working path; its symbol table shows the same unmangled `Heap.pop_one`. A heap-carrying `T` reads a 24-byte String control block as a single i64, which is why the Vec length still decremented (giving the right COUNT and a terminating loop) while every element came back empty.

FIX: at the `let` site, resolve a `SelfValue` RHS through the name-keyed `enum_inst_var_types["self"]`, which the monomorph param prologue seeds with the receiver's CONCRETE instantiation. Placed BEFORE the span fallback deliberately: for `self` the name-keyed record is authoritative and the span table structurally cannot carry the concrete args.

REGRESSION TEST: `e2e_generic_impl_rebinding_owned_self_drains_through_sibling_at_heap_t` in tests/codegen.rs. Case (a) is the minimal SINGLE sibling call, (b) the filed drain loop asserting CONTENTS rather than the count, (c) a scalar-`T` control and (d) a non-generic control -- both correct pre-fix, so they pin the diagnosis rather than merely passing. fix: FIXED by 39b159e. `field_copy_supported`'s `Vec`/`VecDeque` arm now asks whether unrolling the emitter's per-element struct copy TERMINATES (`vec_elem_copy_emission_terminates`) rather than whether the element type is already on the walk stack. It declines when the element is an ancestor (B-2026-07-28-3's direct case), can REACH an ancestor (the mutual cycle this row is about), or reaches itself. That makes the analysis walk exactly as deep as the emitter, which is what B-2026-07-28-3's own comment states it intended. An ACYCLIC element type still answers "terminates" and keeps the arm's unconditional `true`, so programs that compile today emit byte-identical IR; only a genuine cycle newly declines, falling back to caller-retains like every other non-copyable field shape. Both cycle shapes are pinned by `tests/codegen.rs::test_e2e_mutual_type_cycle_through_vec_compiles` and `..._direct_type_cycle_...`, so a later edit cannot fix one by regressing the other. TWO LOWERING PATHS, and this is the part that nearly got missed: fixing the
one the repro used made the repro flat, and the bug was still there.
  - `compile_ambient_resource_method` (src/codegen/method_call_ffi.rs) --
    the LOWERCASE `fs.*` / `env.*` ambient-alias path, which compiles its
    args once up front. This is the path the filed repro exercised.
  - `compile_file_constructor` / `compile_file_read_to_string` /

`free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap` is guarded on `cap > 0`, so it no-ops on a
non-heap value and on a borrow view; `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp` gates
it to genuinely fresh temporaries. A plain BINDING argument is never freed
-- that would be a use-after-free, the failure mode this fix could
plausibly have introduced, and it is pinned by a counter-case in the test.

DELIBERATE REMAINDER -- the ambient OVERRIDE paths are untouched.
`compile_ambient_resource_method` returns early for both override branches,
and an override is a user function reached by RUNTIME dispatch: if its
parameter is owned it frees the buffer itself, so freeing at the call site
too would DOUBLE-FREE. Trading a bounded leak for a double free is the
wrong trade. A `with_provider[FileSystem]` override called with a temporary
path therefore still leaks; fixing it needs the free emitted inside the
default arm's basic block, or the override's param modes consulted.
title: A TEMPORARY passed as the path argument to a `#[compiler_builtin]` fs entry point is never freed: ~47 bytes leak per call, under BOTH the owned and `ref String` signatures
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while verifying B-2026-08-24-24 (stdlib paths as `ref String`), and PROVEN PRE-EXISTING by controls in both directions -- NOT caused by that change.

REPRO -- AOT (`karac build`); peak RSS scales linearly with iteration count:
  fn mk() -> String { "<a long path>" }
  fn main() {
      let p = "<the same long path>";
      let mut i: i64 = 0;
      while i < N {
          match fs.read_to_string(mk())      { Ok(s) => {...} Err(e) => {} }
          match fs.read_to_string(p.clone()) { Ok(s) => {...} Err(e) => {} }
          i = i + 1;
      }
  }
  N=20_000  -> peak RSS  4_332 KB
  N=200_000 -> peak RSS 21_248 KB
  => +16_916 KB over 180_000 iterations x 2 temporaries ~= 47 B per temporary.

THREE CONTROLS, all measured -- this is what pins the cause:
  (a) SAME program, PRE-CHANGE compiler (owned `path: String`):
      4_336 KB -> 21_240 KB. IDENTICAL growth. The `ref` signature is
      leak-NEUTRAL and the defect predates B-2026-08-24-24.
  (b) Path as a plain BINDING rather than a temporary
      (`fs.read_to_string(p)`), result still consumed:
      2_560 KB -> 2_528 KB. FLAT. The RETURNED String does not leak.
  (c) A USER-DEFINED `fn takes_ref(s: ref String)` fed the same two
      temporaries: 2_680 KB -> 2_656 KB. FLAT. Ordinary `ref` params
      release their temporaries correctly.
Together: the leak is specific to a TEMPORARY argument crossing a
`#[compiler_builtin]` call, on both the owned and the `ref` signature.

READING (hypothesis, NOT diagnosed): these entry points are
`#[compiler_builtin]` and their runtime counterparts BORROW rather than own
-- `karac_runtime_fs_read_to_string` / `_file_open` / `_fs_write` all take
`(ptr, len)` and copy into a PathBuf/String on the Rust side. Under the
owned signature nothing on either side released the caller's temporary: the
front end treated it as moved into the callee, and the callee never took
ownership. Start at where a temporary argument's release is emitted for a
builtin call versus an ordinary user call -- control (c) shows the ordinary
path already does this correctly, so the fix is likely to make the builtin
path reuse it.

IMPACT: bounded but real. Any loop opening/reading files with a COMPUTED
path -- `fs.read_to_string(dir + "/" + name)`, `File.open(p.clone())` --
leaks a String per iteration. A long-running service walking a directory
tree is the shape that would notice.

NOT COVERED BY THE ASAN SUITE: `tests/memory_sanitizer.rs` has no case
passing a temporary to a builtin fs entry point, which is why a green LSan
run never caught it. A regression test should go there, not just in E2E.

CLOSED 2026-08-25 by e7a99bb.

MEASURED, peak RSS at 20k vs 200k iterations:
  fs.read_to_string temporaries   4_332 -> 21_248 KB  becomes  2_624 -> 2_584 KB
  File.open temporaries           4_360 -> 21_280 KB  becomes  2_488 -> 2_560 KB
Both now flat and level with the control baseline (~2.6 MB).

CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN ARITHMETIC. The filing said "~47 B per
temporary", derived by dividing the measured 96 B/iteration by the two
temporaries per iteration. That was wrong: LSan reports `Direct leak of 58
byte(s) in 2 object(s)` for a fixture containing FOUR temporaries, because

~94 bytes for ONE leaked clone per iteration, not ~47 for each of two. The
RSS numbers were right; the per-object attribution was not.

fix:
FIXED by c91d018. ROOT CAUSE: a copy-depth / drop-depth mismatch, reached through the one path that erases the element's identity. An owned by-value aggregate param is deep-copied at function entry so the callee owns it (`deep_copy_owned_aggregate_field_in_place`, src/codegen/param_own.rs). That copy decides whether to ALSO duplicate each element of a `Vec` field by classifying the element TypeExpr -- `vec_inner_type_expr(fte)` filtered by `elem_te_needs_direct_recursive_drain`. Inside `impl[T] Heap[T]`, a field declared `xs: Vec[T]` yields the BARE PARAM `T`, which is neither String nor Vec nor Map/Set by name, so the filter said "no" and the entry-copy stayed outer-only: a fresh outer buffer, but the element control blocks memcpy'd verbatim, aliasing the caller's element buffers.

The monomorph's struct drop does NOT have that blind spot -- it resolves `T` and is element-deep -- so both the caller's drop and the callee's copy freed the same element buffers. The comment directly above the defective line states the invariant it was violating: "copy-depth must equal drop-depth".

PROOF (ASAN, via `cargo run --features llvm --example asan_build`): `attempting double-free` on an 8-byte region, freed once inline in `main` (the returned Vec's element walk) and once by `main` -> `__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec_i64` -> `karac_drop_Vec_i64`. Element counts chosen so the outer buffer, the element control blocks and each inner buffer have distinct sizes, which is what identifies the region as a single inner element buffer rather than the outer one. Confirmed in the IR: the non-generic twin's entry copy branches to a `dcopy.elem.loop` that clones each element; the generic one has no such loop and goes straight from `memcpy` to building the result.

FIX (src/codegen/param_own.rs): resolve the element through the active monomorph substitution BEFORE classifying it, via `subst_monomorph_type_params`. That helper consults `type_subst_type_exprs` first, so `T` recovers its FULL concrete type (`Vec[i64]`) rather than the head-only `Vec` that `type_subst_names` would give -- which the recursive copy needs in order to size the inner element. Outside a monomorph it is a no-op clone, so every concrete field keeps its existing behaviour.

REGRESSION TEST: `asan_generic_owned_self_field_move_out_does_not_double_free_elements` in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs, so it runs under ASAN and (on Linux) LeakSanitizer. Case (b) uses HEAP-allocated Strings deliberately -- see the correction below. Controls (c) scalar-`T` and (d) non-generic were both correct pre-fix and pin the diagnosis rather than merely passing. Verified RED pre-fix.

VERIFIED: 14 probe programs covering both fixed and control shapes are clean under ASAN post-fix, and the four that exercise the fix are clean under LeakSanitizer too.
title: A generic impl method that transfers heap-owning content OUT of an owned `self` (`fn into_vec(self) -> Vec[T] { self.xs }`, or a drain through `pop`) DOUBLE-FREES every element buffer under JIT and AOT, while the interpreter is correct: the owned-param entry deep-copy classifies the element by the field's DECLARED type, which inside `impl[T] Heap[T]` is the bare param `T`, so it stays outer-only and aliases the caller's element buffers -- while the monomorph's struct drop resolves `T` and walks them. Needs a generic impl + transfer-out + a heap-owning element; `T = i64` and the non-generic twin are correct. TITLE CORRECTED AT CLOSE: as filed this row said the bug required REBINDING the receiver (`let mut h = self`) and that `T = String` was correct. Neither holds -- see the correction in `detail`.

fix:
FIXED by 6789e4a. ROOT CAUSE: `concrete_generic_struct_inst` (src/codegen/mono.rs) records a generic-struct param's CONCRETE instantiation into the name-keyed `enum_inst_var_types`, resolving each bare type param through `mono_state.type_subst_names`. That map is name -> NAME, and the resolved name is wrapped back into a `PathExpr` with `generic_args: None`. A param bound to a type that carries its OWN generic args cannot survive that round-trip: `T = Vec[i64]` came back as the bare head `Vec`, so the recorded instantiation was `Heap[Vec]` instead of `Heap[Vec[i64]]`.

That record is what a receiver binding's scope-exit drop is selected from, so the elementless instantiation picked `__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec`. Its body IS element-deep -- it has the len-driven walk -- but the per-element drop it calls is `karac_drop_Vec`, whose entire body is `ret void`: a `Vec` with no element gives the drop synthesizer nothing to free, so it emits a stub. The CALLER's own drop of the same struct resolved correctly to `__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec_i64` with a real `karac_drop_Vec_i64`, which is why one program emitted both drops and only the monomorph's elements leaked.

The discriminator falls out of the same fact and is what the controls pin: `String` and `i64` are SINGLE NAMES, which a name -> name map represents losslessly, so they were always correct. Only a param bound to a generic-args-bearing type (`Vec[i64]`) reaches the defect.

FIX: prefer the element-aware `mono_state.type_subst_type_exprs` before falling back to the head-only name map -- exactly the precedence `subst_monomorph_type_params` already uses, and the table was already populated at this call site by `resolve_generic_struct_param_substs`. Three lines; the fallback is untouched, so every param bound to a plain name behaves as before.

MEASURED, against main at 682cba8 (which already carries B-2026-08-25-10's fix). No shape regressed; two improved beyond what this row claimed:
  the row's repro   24 bytes / 2 allocations  ->  CLEAN
  temporary receiver 32 / 4                   ->  16 / 2
  rebind, no return  24 / 3                   ->   8 / 1
  read-only method   24 / 3                   ->  24 / 3  (untouched; see REMAINDER / B-2026-08-25-14)

REGRESSION TEST: `asan_mono_receiver_drop_frees_elements_of_a_generic_arg_bearing_param` in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs, so it runs under ASAN and LeakSanitizer. Verified RED pre-fix at 24 bytes in 2 allocations -- exactly the two elements case (a) leaves behind.

VACUITY NOTE, worth reading before editing this fixture: the method must take ONE element and drop the rest. An earlier draft used a full `into_sorted` drain and PASSED pre-fix, because draining every element leaves nothing behind for the stub drop to fail to free. The leak is in the remainder, not in what the method returns.
title: A monomorph's per-element drop for a `Vec[T]` field is emitted as an EMPTY STUB (`karac_drop_Vec`, `ret void`) when the impl's `T` is recorded head-only, so the callee's deep-copied elements are never freed: `Heap[Vec[i64]].take()` leaks 24 bytes in 2 allocations under LeakSanitizer while running correctly. The struct drop mangles `__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec` instead of `...$Vec_i64` -- it walks the elements, but the element drop it calls does nothing.

fix:
FIXED by 443a902. The `FreeInlineResultPayload` cleanup assumes the payload struct "lays out there bit-for-bit" at `&slot.w0` -- true only when the payload is INLINE. A payload wider than `Result`'s 5-word area is heap-BOXED, so w0 holds a POINTER and the drop read that pointer word as the payload's first word, then walked off the end of the 6-word `Result` alloca and freed what followed.

B-2026-08-06-26 had already established this exact class and gated `track_inline_result_payload_var`, stating the rule the fix reuses verbatim: boxed-ness is a property of the payload TYPE, `llvm_type_word_count(T) > area`. The gate simply never reached the OTHER TWO registration sites -- the fresh-temp scrutinee (`control_flow_match.rs`, the `__freshtemp_inline_res` alloca this repro produces) and the discarded-`Result`-temp path (`runtime.rs`). Both now apply it, per half, so a boxed `Ok` beside an inline-heap `Err` keeps the `Err` drop. The overlay-elem, struct-drop and Vec-elem-agg-drop halves are all gated, matching the named-binding site exactly. The third site in `par_blocks.rs` matches over already-registered actions rather than creating one, so it needs no gate.

Suppressing the inline drop is correct rather than a leak because the `BoxedEnumDrop` registered for the same value owns the box and its contents -- which is asserted, not assumed: `tests/memory_sanitizer.rs::test_boxed_wide_result_payload_match_no_leak_no_double_free` runs the boxed shape with real heap in two of three Vecs plus the narrow-Err half, under ASAN+LSan (LSan being the half that would catch a traded-away free; it is live on this Linux container, and the test passes with `KARAC_REQUIRE_RUNTIME_ARCHIVE=1`, which turns a soft skip into a panic). Two E2E tests pin the crash itself and a heap-carrying read-back.

VERIFIED: the original 1..4-Vec x opt/noopt matrix is now 8/8 clean and byte-identical to the interpreter, where it was 4 SEGFAULTs before. SUITES: llvm 15126 passed / 0 failed, default 9898 / 0, clippy clean on both feature legs, fmt clean.
title: `match` on a `Result` whose Ok payload is a struct with THREE OR MORE `Vec` fields SEGFAULTS the compiled binary while the interpreter is correct. 10 lines, no stdlib, no flags; `let r = f()` on the same program is clean, so it is the payload extraction, not the call. This is what blocks registering `std.cli` for AOT.

fix:
FIXED by 0440daa. Closed by adding the discriminator the row asked for, and gating on it in a test rather than at runtime.

THE DISCRIMINATOR. `typecheck_stdlib_module_excluding_self(program, resolve, "cli.kara")` (src/lib.rs) is the verification peer of `typecheck_stdlib_module`, differing only in that `register_baked_stdlib` skips the `STDLIB_PROGRAMS` entry whose key matches the module being compiled (new `TypeChecker::stdlib_self_module`, set by the `excluding_stdlib_self_copy` builder; one `.filter()` in `env_build.rs`). That is the row's SECOND proposed strategy -- typecheck without the injected self-copy -- chosen over error-kind filtering because, as the row's own measurement correction warned, filtering `ConflictingImpl`-on-a-singly-declared-type does not touch an ambiguous-method report at all.

MEASURED, before and after, on all eight lowered modules. Before: protobuf 6 `AmbiguousMethod` (read_varint x4, read_len_delim x2), pool 2 `E_DROP_DUPLICATE_IMPL` (Pool, PooledConnection), cli 2 `AmbiguousMethod` (help_text, version_line) -- 10 errors, 3 modules, 2 kinds, reproducing the row's correction exactly. After: 0 errors in all eight. Both kinds clear BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by classification: with the self-copy gone the module's own declarations own their names, which is precisely the environment a user program compiling that source gets.

THE GATE IS A TEST, NOT A RUNTIME PANIC -- deliberately. `lower_stdlib_source`'s input is `include_str!`, so its typecheck result is a pure function of data fixed when karac itself is compiled; a runtime gate would re-verify a constant on every user build, cost a second full typecheck per lowered module, and -- firing inside a `LazyLock` -- poison it, which is the exact failure the row recorded for the naive attempt. `tests/stdlib_typecheck.rs` catches the same condition at CI time, names the offending file and error, and cannot poison anything. The lowering path is therefore UNCHANGED: `lower_stdlib_source` still calls `typecheck_stdlib_module` and still registers the full prelude, so no program's codegen input moves. Verified across the full `--features llvm` suite.

FIVE TESTS, three of which exist to keep the gate honest -- a check that only ever asserts an empty list is worth nothing if it cannot fail:
  - `every_lowered_stdlib_module_typechecks_clean` -- the gate itself.
  - `gate_rejects_a_borrowed_string_stored_into_an_owned_field` -- non-vacuity in THE SHAPE THAT SHIPPED. Appending `fn f(v: ref String) -> H { return H { value: v }; }` to a lowered module reproduces `expected 'String', found 'ref String'`, the cli.kara error whose codegen consequence was `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`.
  - `gate_rejects_a_return_type_mismatch` -- second shape, so the gate is not keyed to one diagnostic.
  - `errors_are_meaningful_only_with_the_self_copy_excluded` -- pins the difference between the two entry points on cli.kara, so a future "simplification" back to the plain one fails loudly. Its doc comment says that if the double registration is ever fixed at its root, the correct response is to DELETE this test, not to weaken the gate.
  - `lowered_module_list_matches_codegen` -- re-derives the gated set from `src/codegen.rs`'s own text, so a ninth `lower_stdlib_source` call cannot silently escape the gate. That drift is exactly how this hole would reopen.

CONTROL RUN. Re-appending the historical defect to `runtime/stdlib/cli.kara` fails `every_lowered_stdlib_module_typechecks_clean` with `runtime/stdlib/cli.kara does not type-check, but codegen lowers its bodies anyway ... [TypeMismatch] expected 'String', found 'ref String'`. Restored and re-verified clean. The gate also now asserts PARSE cleanliness in release builds, which was previously only a `debug_assert!`.

SURVEY FINDING (bounds the gate, and is why it covers 8 modules rather than all 91). Running the excluding typecheck over the whole of `STDLIB_SOURCES`: 91 modules, 80 clean, 11 dirty -- and not one of the 11 is a lowered module. Every one is a DIFFERENT artifact class from the self-copy: stdlib PRIVILEGE denied to a module compiled standalone, because its items parse with `stdlib_origin = false`. Concretely `E_VARIANCE_USER_DECL_NOT_YET` (option, result, channel -- variance markers are stdlib-only in v1), `F32/F64/F16/Bf16 derives Eq/Hash/Ord but field has non-Eq/Hash/Ord type` (3 each), `ScopeLocalEscape` on task_group's `TaskGroup.new`/`spawn` (4), `DiscriminantError derives Copy but variant field has non-Copy type 'D'`, and `arithmetic operator requires numeric type, found 'T'` in reduce and column. None is a shipping hazard today: those modules are only SIGNATURE-registered, their bodies are never lowered, so there is no discarded-error path for them to corrupt. Extending the gate to all 91 would need a second discriminator for stdlib origin -- out of scope here, and not filed as a row because nothing is currently broken by it. It is recorded so the next person does not read "8 of 91" as an oversight.
title: `lower_stdlib_source` DISCARDS the typecheck errors it computes for every baked stdlib module, so a baked module can ship code `karac check` rejects in user programs -- which is how cli.kara shipped four borrowed-String-into-owned-field stores that DOUBLE-FREED when compiled. The naive fail-closed gate FALSE-POSITIVES on THREE of the eight lowered modules (protobuf 6, pool 2, cli 2) across TWO error kinds; see detail for what a real fix needs.
detail:
`lower_stdlib_source` (src/codegen.rs) computes a typecheck for every baked stdlib module and then USES ONLY ITS TABLES -- `tc` is passed to `lower` and its `.errors` are never inspected. Only PARSE errors are asserted (`debug_assert!` on `parsed.errors`). So a baked module can ship code that `karac check` would reject in a user program, and codegen is left lowering a program the type system never approved.

THIS WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. `runtime/stdlib/cli.kara` carried FOUR instances of storing a BORROWED `String` into an OWNED `String` field -- `val` / `token` bound out of an `Option` by `argv.get(i)` is a `ref String`, and the sites wrote it straight into `ParsedValue.value` / `positional` / `sub_positional`:

    error[typecheck]: expected 'String', found 'ref String'   (x4)

User code cannot compile that -- the same three lines in a user program are a hard type error. The stdlib copy compiled, codegen moved the borrowed buffer into the new owner, and the compiled parser DOUBLE-FREED as soon as a `--name value` pair was actually parsed (`free(): double free detected in tcache 2`). The interpreter, which does not share the move, was correct -- so it presented as an A/B divergence whose compiled half was a heap corruption. Fixed in the same commit as this row by cloning at the four sites; the ROOT enabler -- errors discarded -- is what this row tracks.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT IN THAT COMMIT. Making `lower_stdlib_source` panic on `!tc.errors.is_empty()` was implemented and MEASURED, and it fails on a FALSE POSITIVE: `pool.kara` reports two `E_DROP_DUPLICATE_IMPL` errors (`Pool`, `PooledConnection`), because `typecheck_stdlib_module` deliberately disables the #34 collision-skip so the module does not skip the injected prelude copy of ITSELF -- and the module's own `impl[T] Drop for Pool[T]` then collides with that injected copy. `pool.kara`'s own source contains exactly ONE Drop impl per type, verified by grep. So the naive gate turns every `karac build` into a panic inside a `LazyLock` (poisoning it), which is strictly worse than the hole it closes. Reverted rather than shipped.

WHAT A REAL FIX NEEDS: a check that can tell a genuine module-local type error from the prelude-injection artifact -- either by filtering the error KINDS that the injected-copy overlap can produce (`ConflictingImpl` on a type the module itself declares exactly once), or by typechecking the module WITHOUT the injected self-copy and keeping the collision-skip semantics that user programs get. Until then the class stays open: any baked module can carry a silent type error, and the cli case shows the failure mode is memory corruption in shipped binaries rather than a compile error.

INTERIM MITIGATION (already true, worth stating): `karac check <copy-of-module>.kara` on a baked module's source does surface these -- that is how the four cli.kara errors were found -- so a module can be audited by hand today. `cli.kara` is now `karac check`-clean (0 errors: the 4 type errors cloned, and the 6 `chained_field_receiver` FR4 lint errors removed by the Subcommand flattening in the same commit).

SOURCE NOTE: found while root-causing B-2026-08-25-2's "Args segfault" remainder.

MEASUREMENT CORRECTION (2026-08-25, while scoping this row for parallel work). The detail above names pool.kara as THE false positive. It is not the only one, and E_DROP_DUPLICATE_IMPL is not the only error kind. Surveying all eight modules that flow through `lower_stdlib_source` -- by calling the public `typecheck_stdlib_module` on each module's own source, exactly as the function does -- gives:

    tracing   0     ordering  0     mem  0     regex  0     process  0
    protobuf  6     ambiguous method (read_varint x4, read_len_delim x2) on ProtoReader
    pool      2     E_DROP_DUPLICATE_IMPL (Pool, PooledConnection)
    cli       2     ambiguous method (help_text, version_line) on Parser

So the blocker is THREE modules and TWO distinct error kinds, not one and one. All eight are the same injected-self-copy artifact -- each ambiguous-method report lists two IDENTICAL candidates (`Parser.help_text(Parser) -> String` twice), and grep confirms each of `help_text`, `version_line`, `read_varint` is declared exactly ONCE in its module, the same proof already recorded for pool's single Drop impl per type. A fix designed and tested against pool alone WILL fail on the other two, because filtering `ConflictingImpl`-on-a-singly-declared-type (the first strategy the detail above proposes) does not touch an ambiguous-method report at all. The second proposed strategy -- typecheck without the injected self-copy -- does cover both kinds, which is evidence for preferring it.

BLAST RADIUS CHANGED under 77799b8. `CLI_LOWERED_PROGRAM` did not exist before that commit (verified: `git show 77799b8~1:src/codegen.rs` has zero occurrences, `77799b8` has two), so cli.kara was not lowered at all and its two discarded errors were not being computed. The layout half of B-2026-08-25-2 put cli on the every-program lowering path, so they are now computed-and-discarded on EVERY build. Practical consequence for this row: a naive fail-closed gate now poisons the LazyLock via cli as well as via pool, and any fix must be verified against a plain `karac build` of a program that touches no stdlib module at all.

INDEPENDENT OF the remaining B-2026-08-25-2 work, which is confined to `compiled_stdlib_programs` (~line 693) plus a new usage-detector walker. This row's fix is confined to `lower_stdlib_source` (~line 452). Same file, ~240 lines apart, no shared state, neither needs the other's outcome -- the two can be worked in parallel, with a rebase rather than a conflict at integration.

fix:
FIXED by 6df0bfb. ROOT CAUSE: `make_aggregate_param_callee_owned_inst` (src/codegen/param_own.rs) has two branches that register an owned by-value aggregate param's scope-exit drop. The copy-UNSUPPORTED branch registers it at the param's declared INSTANTIATION (`track_struct_var_inst(type_name, slot, inst)`). The copy-SUPPORTED branch -- which a `Heap[T] { xs: Vec[T] }` takes, since its fields ARE copy-supported -- discarded `inst` and called the name-keyed `track_struct_var(type_name, slot)`, which is literally `track_struct_var_inst(.., None)`.

The resulting `__karac_drop_struct_Heap` resolves the `xs: Vec[T]` field from the erased bare `T`, classifies it as outer-only, and frees only the copied outer buffer. Since B-2026-08-25-10 that entry copy is element-DEEP inside a monomorph, so every element buffer it allocated was left with no owner at all. The doc comment on `track_struct_var_inst` already names this exact failure mode -- "not the name-shared `__karac_drop_struct_S` that resolves the element from bare `T` and leaks every element" -- so the two branches disagreed about a rule one of them had written down.

FIX: pass `inst` on the copy-supported branch too, matching its sibling. One line.

WHY IT SURVIVED TWO PRIOR ROWS ON THE SAME SHAPE: the erased drop is only ever REACHED when nothing moves out of `self`. `let mut h = self` hands ownership to `h`, whose drop is selected from the binding's recorded instantiation (correct since B-2026-08-25-11), and `self`'s own drop is then cap/len-zeroed by the existing move-suppression -- so a method that drains or returns anything never exercises this path. It took the read-only shape (`fn count(self) -> i64 { self.xs.len() }`) to reach it.

MEASURED, against main at 443a902 (which carries -10 and -11):
  read-only owned self, Vec[i64] elems  24 bytes / 3 allocations  ->  CLEAN
  read-only owned self, heap String     15 / 3                    ->  CLEAN
  every other probe                     unchanged (16 of 18 clean)

ELEMENT-TYPE CORRECTION vs B-2026-08-25-11: `T = String` IS affected here, and that row's warning to re-measure rather than assume was correct. -11's erasure lived in the INSTANTIATION RECORD, where `String` is a single name a name-to-name map carries losslessly; this drop was unmangled outright, so any heap-owning element leaks. Measured, not inferred: 15 bytes in 3 allocations for three heap-built Strings.

REGRESSION TEST: `asan_owned_aggregate_param_drop_frees_its_entry_copied_elements` in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs (ASAN + LeakSanitizer). Verified RED pre-fix at 63 bytes in 6 allocations -- (a)'s three Vec buffers (16 + 8 + 24) plus (b)'s three String bodies (5 each), which is the whole leak accounted for exactly rather than approximately.

VACUITY NOTE: the method must transfer NOTHING out. Any method that returns or drains part of the container routes ownership to a binding whose drop is already correct, and the fixture passes pre-fix.
title: An owned `self` aggregate param's OWN scope-exit drop is the UNMANGLED base drop (`__karac_drop_struct_Heap`, outer-only), not the monomorph's, so a generic impl method that takes `self` and transfers NOTHING out leaks every element its entry deep-copy allocated: `fn take(self) -> i64 { self.xs.len() }` on a 3-element `Heap[Vec[i64]]` leaks 24 bytes in 3 allocations while printing the right answer.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: split out of B-2026-08-25-11 rather than found independently, and confirmed DISTINCT by reading the emitted IR rather than assumed. That row fixed the drop selected for a receiver BINDING (`let mut h = self`); this is the drop registered for the owned PARAM itself, a different registration path, and -11's fix measurably does not move it (24 bytes / 3 allocations before and after).

REPRO -- prints `3`, leaks under `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1` (Linux; LSan does not run on macOS, see CLAUDE.md):
  struct Heap[T] { xs: Vec[T] }
  impl[T] Heap[T] {
      fn take(self) -> i64 { self.xs.len() }
  }
  fn main() { let h = Heap { xs: [[1], [2], [3]] }; println(h.take()); }
  => leaks 24 bytes in 3 allocations -- the three element buffers the callee's
     entry deep-copy allocated, one per element.

DIAGNOSIS, from the IR: an owned by-value aggregate param is deep-copied at entry so the callee owns it (param_own.rs #14), and since B-2026-08-25-10 that copy is element-deep inside a monomorph. Its scope-exit drop, however, is emitted as `call void @__karac_drop_struct_Heap(ptr %self)` -- the UNMANGLED base drop, which is outer-only: it frees the copied outer buffer under a `cap > 0` guard and never walks elements. So the copied element buffers have no owner at all.

WHY THE SIBLING SHAPES DO NOT HIT IT: `let mut h = self` moves ownership to `h`, whose drop IS the monomorph's (`__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec_i64`, element-deep since -11), and `self`'s drop is then cap/len-zeroed by the existing move-suppression, so its being outer-only never matters. In the emitted IR the working shape calls BOTH `__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec_i64` (on `h`) and the unmangled base (on `self`); the leaking shape calls only the base. That single difference is the whole bug.

WHERE TO LOOK: the param-drop registration in src/codegen/mono.rs around `make_aggregate_param_callee_owned_inst`, which already receives a `param_inst` (the param's recorded instantiation, now element-correct after -11). The drop it registers should be resolved through that instantiation the same way a `let` binding's is -- `emit_struct_drop_synthesis_mono` with a subst derived from `param_inst`, rather than the name-keyed base drop.

MEASURED SCOPE: 24 bytes / 3 allocations for a 3-element `Vec[Vec[i64]]` -- i.e. proportional to the container, one leaked buffer per element. A single-name element type (`String`, `i64`) is NOT exempt here the way it was in -11: the erasure there was in the instantiation record, whereas this drop is unmangled outright, so any heap-owning element leaks. `T = String` should be re-measured when picking this up rather than assumed correct -- and use HEAP-allocated Strings, since literals live in static rodata with cap 0 and leak nothing (the false-negative that mis-narrowed B-2026-08-25-10).

SEVERITY: medium -- a bounded leak, not corruption, but it needs no unusual shape at all: any read-only method on a generic container that takes `self` by value leaks the whole container's element buffers.

MEASUREMENT HYGIENE: all numbers taken with no `cargo` build in flight; the before/after comparison used two separately built compilers.

REMAINDER, MEASURED AND SPLIT OUT rather than left in this row: two leaks in adjacent shapes survive, both confirmed distinct by their ASAN ALLOCATION STACKS rather than by argument, and both unchanged in size across B-2026-08-25-10, -11 and this fix -- which is the evidence that none of the three touch them.

  B-2026-08-25-16 -- an aggregate TEMPORARY used as an owned-`self` receiver
    (`Heap { ... }.take()`) is never dropped by the caller. Its buffers are
    allocated in `main`, not in the monomorph, so they are the ORIGINAL's, not
    the callee's entry copy. Binding the receiver first is clean. 16 bytes / 2.
  B-2026-08-25-17 -- a DISCARDED method-call result that owns heap is never
    freed (`h.xs.pop();` as a bare expression statement). Allocated inside the
    monomorph and exactly one element wide. 8 bytes / 1.

The three drop-selection rows (-10, -11, -14) were all about WHICH drop a value's owner runs; these two are about a value that never acquires an owner at all. That is the line between the families, and it is why they are separate rows rather than an incomplete fix here.

-16 carries an explicit warning not to fix it naively: its temporary has three element buffers and only TWO leak, so something already frees the third. Registering a drop for all three without first establishing where that free comes from risks converting a leak into a double free -- the exact trade this row's own family made in the other direction.

fix: FIXED by 55f16cb. `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg`'s borrowed-receiver FieldAccess arm (src/codegen/runtime.rs) now admits `borrowed_agg_payload_struct_vars` — the third root class of one shape, alongside `ref_params` (the original) and `for_loop_owned_agg_vars` (added by B-2026-08-01-28 with the same rationale). A one-root widening, not the conditional-exclusion surgery the previous entry proposed; see the CORRECTION below. Regression pins: `e2e_borrow_payload_field_direct_consume_no_double_free` (tests/codegen.rs, all three consume spellings plus a trailing re-read that proves the container survived) and `asan_borrow_payload_field_direct_consume_no_double_free` (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs, 300 iterations under LSan — the leak gate for the widening's mirror-image failure).
title: Returning a heap-bearing FIELD out of a BORROWED match payload (`return pv.value` where `pv` is bound from `.get()` on a `ref self` receiver) MOVES the buffer instead of copying, so the returned String and the still-live owner both free it. 17 lines, no Result/Env/stdlib; interpreter is correct. Found via std.cli's `get_string`, which is the last AOT blocker.
detail:
MEASURED WITH `std.cli` REGISTERED FOR AOT (the registration itself is NOT landed — see below). With B-2026-08-25-12 fixed, the whole `std.cli` builder surface compiles and runs under `karac build`: `Arg.string().required()`, a `fn build() -> Parser` helper, `Parser.new(..).about(..).version(..).flag(..).arg(..).subcommand(..)`, and `match p.parse() { Ok(a) => .. }` all work and match the interpreter. ONE path does not.

THE DEFECT: `args.get_string(name)` DOUBLE-FREES when the argument was actually supplied. ASAN names it exactly — a 2-byte region (the value `"x"` from `--name x`), allocated by `karac_string_clone`, freed twice, BOTH frees in `main`:

    ERROR: AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free on 0x5020000000d0
      #1 in main            <- second free
    freed by thread T0 here:
      #1 in main            <- first free
    previously allocated by thread T0 here:
      #1 in karac_string_clone

`parse()` ALONE IS CLEAN — verified under ASAN with the same `--name x` argv, printing `ok` with no report. Adding the `a.get_string("--name")` call is what turns it into a double free, so the trigger is `get_string`, not the parse loop.

THE SUSPECT LINE, `runtime/stdlib/cli.kara`, `impl Args`:

    fn get_string(ref self, name: String) -> Result[String, CliError] {
        ...  match self.values.get(i) { Some(pv) => { if pv.name == name { return Ok(pv.value); } } ... }

`pv` is a BORROWED payload out of `self.values.get(i)` on a `ref self` receiver, and `pv.value` is a `String` field read out of it and returned as an OWNED `String` in the `Result`. If codegen copies the `{ptr,len,cap}` without cloning, the returned String aliases the Vec element's buffer and both the caller's String and the still-live `Args` free it. Note the typechecker does NOT reject this: a `ref String` bound directly out of an `Option` IS rejected ("expected `String`, found `ref String`" — the four sites fixed in 8a04107), but a `String` FIELD read off a borrowed struct types as owned, so this shape passes `karac check` cleanly. Whether the right fix is a clone in cli.kara or a codegen copy is NOT yet established.

NOT YET REDUCED TO USER CODE, and four attempts are recorded so the next session does not repeat them. All four build and run CLEAN under `karac build`, matching the interpreter:
  - a `String` field off a borrowed match payload pushed into a `Vec[String]`;
  - the same pushed into a STRUCT LITERAL inside a `Vec[Struct]`;
  - the exact `parse`-shaped loop building `Vec[ParsedValue]` inside a wide `Ok(..)` payload;
  - `return Ok(pv.value)` out of a `ref self` method, BOTH standalone and with the receiver itself bound out of a BOXED wide `Result` payload (the closest analogue to the cli call site).
So the reproduction needs more of `cli.kara`'s real context than any of these carry.

RELATION TO B-2026-08-25-12: before that fix this same program SEGFAULTED (the boxed-payload inline-cleanup crash), so this double free was MASKED rather than absent — removing the outer crash exposed an inner one. It is therefore not a regression of that fix, whose own E2E + ASAN/LSan tests and full-suite runs are green; but it also cannot be proven to predate it by direct observation, because the program did not survive long enough to reach `get_string`.

WHY THE REGISTRATION IS STILL HELD: registering `std.cli` today would give a user a CLI parser that silently corrupts the heap the first time an argument is read back — strictly worse than the current loud "no handler for method" compile error, which is the same standard applied at every earlier stage of B-2026-08-25-2. The registration diff is one `LazyLock` + one `compiled_stdlib_programs` entry and is trivially re-applied once this row closes.

--- 2026-08-25 REDUCED TO 17 LINES; the `Result` / `Env` / cli framing was all incidental ---

    struct Pv { name: String, value: String }
    struct Holder { values: Vec[Pv] }

    impl Holder {
        fn get(ref self) -> String {
            match self.values.get(0) {
                Some(pv) => { return pv.value; }
                None => { return "none"; }
            }
        }
    }

    fn main() {
        let heap: String = "x";
        let mut v: Vec[Pv] = Vec.new();
        v.push(Pv { name: "k", value: heap.clone() });
        let h = Holder { values: v };
        println(h.get());
    }

`karac build` -> `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`. `karac run --interp` -> `x`. Writing `return pv.value.clone();` makes the compiled binary correct, which is what identifies the defect: `pv` is a BORROWED view of a `Vec` element (bound out of `Option` by `.get()` on a `ref self` receiver), and returning `pv.value` MOVES the String's `{ptr,len,cap}` out of it instead of copying. The element still holds the same pointer, so the returned String and the still-live `Holder` both free it.

The typechecker does not object: a `String` FIELD read off a borrowed struct types as owned `String` (unlike a bare `ref String` bound directly out of an `Option`, which IS rejected). So the compiler promises a copy at the type level and does not perform one in codegen, while the interpreter does — an A/B run-vs-build divergence whose compiled half is heap corruption.

BISECTED, each variant built and run:
  - `Result` is NOT needed: returning a bare `String` faults identically.
  - `Env.args()` is NOT needed: a local `Vec` faults identically.
  - The match-arm-payload RECEIVER is not needed: a plain local `Holder` faults identically.
  - `.clone()` on the returned field is clean, on every variant.

TWO EARLIER "CLEAN" REDUCTIONS WERE FALSE NEGATIVES, recorded so the trap is not re-entered: both stored the payload as a STRING LITERAL (`value: "x"`), which is static with `cap == 0`, so every free is a no-op and the double free cannot be observed. Any repro for this class MUST put a heap-allocated String in the field (e.g. `heap.clone()`).

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS IS AN OPEN QUESTION, and both options are coherent: either codegen clones when a heap-bearing field is read out of a BORROWED payload and escapes as owned, or the typechecker rejects the move the way it already rejects the bare `ref String` case. The interpreter's behaviour (copy) is the one the type rule implies, so codegen is the side that is wrong today.

--- 2026-08-25 ROOT-CAUSED to a stated assumption with a hole (no fix landed; see the two options) ---

THE SITE IS `borrow_get_payload_clone_te` (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs). It is the deep-clone gate for a payload bound out of a BORROW-ACCESSOR call — `scrutinee_is_borrow_call` classifies `.get()`/`.first()`/`.last()` on a Vec/Slice/Map as exactly that, and `Map.get` is deep-cloned through it (B-2026-07-01-12) precisely because "codegen binds the payload as an ALIAS ... an escaping binding hands that alias to an owner that frees it".

`Vec.get` is deliberately EXCLUDED, and the gate's own doc states the reason:

    "`Vec`/`Slice` `get`/`first`/`last` return `Option[ref T]` and the typechecker
     REJECTS escapes, so their `te` here is a `Ref` (non-`Path` arg) and they
     self-gate to `None`."

THAT ASSUMPTION IS TRUE FOR A SCALAR/STRING PAYLOAD AND FALSE FOR A STRUCT PAYLOAD. Measured both halves:
  - `Option[ref String]` — `match argv.get(0) { Some(val) => { let s: String = val; ... } }` IS rejected: "expected `String`, found `ref String`". The assumption holds.
  - `Option[ref Pv]` where `Pv { name: String, value: String }` — `pv.value` types as an OWNED `String`, because a field read off a borrowed struct is not itself a `ref`. Nothing rejects it, so the alias escapes and the gate that would have cloned it never fires.

So the escape the gate relies on the typechecker to prevent is exactly the escape the typechecker does not prevent, and the two guards leave a hole between them rather than overlapping. The IR confirms the consequence: `Holder.get` loads the element with a single `load { {ptr,i64,i64}, {ptr,i64,i64} }` (a SHALLOW copy of both String headers), boxes that shallow copy as the Option payload, and returns `pv.value`'s `{ptr,len,cap}` verbatim — no `karac_string_clone` anywhere, where the `.clone()` spelling emits one.

The sibling gate `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` (src/codegen/runtime.rs) is the one that DOES handle this family at consume sites, and its membership test is the shape a codegen-side fix would extend: it already covers a borrowed receiver (`ref_params`) and, since B-2026-08-01-28, a for-loop struct ELEMENT binding — added with the rationale that "a for-loop struct ELEMENT binding is a shallow bit-copy of the container's slot, so like a borrowed receiver it does not own its fields". A `.get()` match-payload binding is that same thing and is in neither set.

TWO COHERENT FIXES, deliberately NOT chosen unilaterally because they have different blast radii and the choice is a design call:
  (A) TYPECHECKER — reject a heap-bearing field read off a `ref`-payload binding when it escapes, restoring the invariant the codegen gate already documents as its precondition. Most faithful to the stated design, and it makes the failure a compile error rather than silent corruption; but it can reject existing corpus code that is accidentally fine, so it needs a corpus sweep before landing.
  (B) CODEGEN — extend the clone to the struct-field-escape case (either by admitting struct payloads into `borrow_get_payload_clone_te`, or by adding `.get()`-payload bindings to `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg`'s membership). Narrower, but the mirror-image failure is a LEAK, so it must be landed against the Linux LSan gate, not a local macOS asan run.
Whoever takes it should also re-check the interpreter: it copies here (its output is correct), so whichever way codegen goes, the two backends must end up agreeing by construction.

--- 2026-08-25 THE FIX DIRECTION IS SETTLED: option (A) is REFUTED, and the root cause is sharper than "a missing membership" ---

OPTION (A) — "make the typechecker reject the escape" — IS REFUTED BY EXISTING BEHAVIOUR, not merely less attractive. This compiles, runs, and leaves the receiver usable:

    struct S { n: String }
    impl S { fn name(ref self) -> String { self.n } }
    // s.name() prints "abc"; s.n still prints "abc" afterwards

So the language has ALREADY decided that a heap field read through a borrow and returned as owned is legal, and that codegen's job is to CLONE it — `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg`'s FieldAccess arm exists to do exactly that for a `ref` receiver. Rejecting the escape would break that established, tested shape, and a rule that permits `self.n` from `ref self` but forbids `pv.value` from a `.get()` payload would be arbitrary and unexplainable. The earlier framing of (A) and (B) as equally coherent was WRONG and is retracted.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS AN INCOMPLETE DIVISION OF LABOUR. Four root classes — `owned_struct_params`, `for_loop_owned_agg_vars`, `borrowed_agg_payload_struct_vars` (which a `.get()` borrow-path payload binding DOES join, via `register_borrowed_agg_payload_struct_bindings` gated on `pattern_binding_is_borrow`), and `shared_enum_payload_view_vars` — take their copy from `deep_copy_owned_struct_param_field_move`, which fires at the LET-statement lowering. The arg/return-site helper `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` then UNCONDITIONALLY EXCLUDES those same four roots, with the comment "Roots that ALREADY get an independent buffer from `deep_copy_owned_struct_param_field_move` are excluded, or the two copies stack and the first one leaks."

That split is complete only if every escape of such a field passes through a `let`. It does not. Measured on the 17-line repro:

    return pv.value;              -> DOUBLE FREE   (direct return, no let)
    let s = pv.value; return s;   -> CLEAN         (let-site helper fires)
    out.push(pv.value);           -> DOUBLE FREE   (direct arg, no let)

So a direct return/arg consume site gets the exclusion but never the compensating copy — no copy happens anywhere. The fix is therefore NOT to add a membership (the membership is already there); it is to make the exclusion conditional on the consume site actually being one the let-helper covers, and to perform the copy at the direct return/arg site otherwise. The `let` spelling is a verified user-level workaround in the meantime, though `.clone()` is the clearer one.

BLAST RADIUS BEYOND cli: any `fn get(ref self) -> String` that returns a heap field of a `.get()`-bound payload without an intervening `let`. `runtime/stdlib/cli.kara`'s three sites are fixed in 427f899 by cloning; that makes cli.kara correct, NOT the language — this row remains the general fix.

--- 2026-08-25 FIXED, and the previous entry's account of WHERE the hole was is CORRECTED ---

CORRECTION, retracting a claim in the entry above. It said `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` "UNCONDITIONALLY EXCLUDES those same four roots". That is wrong. The four-root exclusion is real but lives in three UAM sub-helpers in the same file — `uam_defensive_copy_field`, `uam_reclone_source_field`, `uam_defensive_copy_tuple_elem` — every one of them gated on `uam_consume_site_at_root`, i.e. a site the ownership pass flagged as a use-after-move. `return pv.value` is a single consume with no later use, so it is not such a site and never reached those helpers at all. `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg`'s own borrowed-receiver FieldAccess arm has NO exclusion: it carries an INCLUSION list of two roots, and the borrow-payload root was simply not on it. Measured directly, by tracing the arm on the 17-line repro:

    [b15] FieldAccess arm recv=pv field=value
          ref_params=false for_loop=false borrowed_agg=true
          shared_view=false owned_struct=false

So the fix is a one-root widening of an inclusion, exactly precedented by B-2026-08-01-28 (which added `for_loop_owned_agg_vars` to that same list, for the same reason: "a for-loop struct ELEMENT binding is a shallow bit-copy of the container's slot, so like a borrowed receiver it does not own its fields"). A `.get()` match-payload binding is the third instance of that one sentence. The conditional-exclusion surgery the previous entry specified was aimed at a mechanism that is not on this path.

WHY THE TWO COPIERS CANNOT STACK — the leak hazard the previous entry correctly flagged, checked three ways rather than argued:
  - The `let` path never routes through this helper: stmts.rs calls `deep_copy_owned_struct_param_field_move` directly, and no `maybe_defensive_copy_param_arg` call site lives in stmts.rs.
  - The struct-literal field path DOES route here (exprs.rs) — and calls `uam_defensive_copy` immediately after, which excludes this root. That exclusion is what makes the pairing safe.
  - `deep_copy_owned_struct_param_field_move` matches only a FieldAccess RHS, never a literal, so it has no struct-literal twin to double up with (unlike `for_loop_owned_agg_vars`, whose StructLiteral copy was deliberately removed when B-2026-08-01-28 admitted it here).
LeakSanitizer confirms it empirically: the ASAN pin runs 300 iterations and reports no leak. LSan was proved live on the host first (a deliberate 1234-byte `malloc` leak in C is reported), so the clean runs are a real result and not a disabled checker.

THE MEASURED MATRIX, before and after, every shape built and run:

                                  BEFORE                     AFTER
    return pv.value;              double free (SIGABRT 134)  x
    out.push(pv.value);           double free (SIGABRT 134)  x
    return Ok(pv.value);          double free (SIGABRT 134)  380     <- the real cli shape
    return pv.tags;  (Vec field)  SIGSEGV     (rc 139)       860     <- corrupts harder, same cause
    let s = pv.value; return s;   x                          x       <- control: the let-site copier
    return Ok(pv.value.clone());  380                        380     <- control: a MethodCall arg is not a FieldAccess, so the arm declines and there is no double copy
    fn take(h: Holder) -> String  x                          x       <- control: `owned_struct_params` root
    shared-enum payload view      x                          x       <- control: `shared_enum_payload_view_vars` root

Every AFTER cell above is byte-identical across all four surfaces measured
independently: `karac run --interp`, `karac build`, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build`,
and the ASAN+LSan build. The BEFORE column was taken by stashing the one-root
widening and rebuilding, so it is a measurement of this tree rather than a
recollection.

THE OTHER TWO ROOT CLASSES WERE PROBED FOR THE SAME HOLE AND DO NOT HAVE IT (last two rows above), so the widening stays at one root rather than being applied to all four on symmetry grounds.

BLAST-RADIUS SWEEP OVER BOTH CORPORA (312 `.kara` files in kara, plus kara-katas) FOUND TWO MORE LIVE SITES, and they are the argument for having fixed the compiler rather than the stdlib. `runtime/stdlib/cli.kara` has FIVE instances of this shape, not the three that 427f899 hand-cloned: `flags_set.push(fentry.name)` (~line 352) and `sub_flags_set.push(fentry.name)` (~line 302) are on the FLAG path, which the earlier ASAN run did not exercise because it passed `--name x` and a subcommand, never a bare flag. Hand-cloning found 3 of 5. The compiler fix covers all five without anyone having to enumerate them. The three explicit `.clone()`s are now redundant but harmless (verified above: a `.clone()` receiver is a MethodCall, so the arm declines — no double copy, no leak); removing them belongs with the registration slice on B-2026-08-25-2, where cli can finally be AOT-tested end to end rather than by mirror program. The only kata hits are `wd.size` and `nb.val`, both scalar `i64` fields — no heap, no defect.

fix:
FIXED by a9856f1. ROOT CAUSE: the materialized receiver temporary is drop-tracked by BARE NAME. `Heap { .. }.take()` stores the receiver into a `__urecv_tmp` slot (src/codegen/method_call.rs) and calls `track_struct_var(&type_name, slot)`, which is `track_struct_var_inst(.., None)`. The resulting name-shared `__karac_drop_struct_Heap` resolves the `xs: Vec[T]` field from the erased bare `T`, classifies it outer-only, and frees the outer buffer while never walking the elements -- so every element buffer leaked, one per element.

The instantiation was ALREADY IN HAND: the same block seeds `enum_inst_var_types[synth]` a few lines above, precisely so the CALLEE is selected at the right monomorph (B-2026-08-06-12). Only the temp's own drop was still name-keyed, which is why one program emitted the correct `__karac_drop_struct_Heap$Vec_i64` for its named bindings and the erased drop for its temporaries.

FIX: pass that recorded instantiation to `track_struct_var_inst`. Same one-line shape as B-2026-08-25-14, one site over -- there the callee's owned param, here the caller's receiver temp.

MEASURED, against main at bf1f793:
  temporary receiver, nested-Vec elements (8/16/24)  48 bytes / 3  ->  CLEAN
  temporary receiver, heap String elements           10 / 2        ->  CLEAN
  bound-receiver control                             clean         ->  clean
  every other probe                                  unchanged (19 of 20 clean)
The one remaining failure is B-2026-08-25-17 (a discarded call result), untouched by this and a different family.

REGRESSION TEST: `asan_receiver_temporary_drop_frees_its_elements` in tests/memory_sanitizer.rs (ASAN + LeakSanitizer). Verified RED pre-fix at 58 bytes in 5 allocations. Case (a) uses three DIFFERENT element sizes deliberately -- see the correction below for why that is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. (c) is the bound-receiver control that localises the fault to the temporary path.
title: An aggregate TEMPORARY used as the receiver of an owned-`self` method is dropped with the UNMANGLED outer-only drop (`__karac_drop_struct_Heap`), so its heap-owning element buffers leak -- one per element: `Heap { xs: [[1], [2, 2], [3, 3, 3]] }.take()` leaks 48 bytes in 3 allocations under LeakSanitizer while printing the right answer. Binding the same value first (`let h = Heap { ... }; h.take()`) is clean, because the `let` site records the instantiation the temporary path discarded. TITLE CORRECTED AT CLOSE: as filed this row said the temporary was "never dropped by the caller" and that only two of three buffers leaked -- both wrong, see the correction in `detail`.

fix:
FIXED by c8753cd.

THE ROW'S FIRST INSTRUCTION WAS TO ESTABLISH SCOPE BEFORE FIXING, on the
theory that `pop()` was a convenient producer and the class was wider.
MEASURING MADE IT NARROWER. A 10-case producer matrix at top level --
`v.pop()`, `v.remove(i)`, `v.swap_remove(i)`, `Map.remove`, and
functions/methods returning `String` / `Vec` / an owning struct, each
discarded -- is entirely CLEAN under LSan, as are a NON-generic impl
method, a generic FREE FUNCTION, a plain local rebind, and a scalar `T`.

TRIGGER: a generic IMPL METHOD whose receiver was rebound from `self`
(`let mut h = self`) -- the B-2026-08-25-7 shape, whose fix (cbc545f) is in
and closed the sibling-DISPATCH half only. So this is not "discarded values
leak"; it is one more consumer of a pre-monomorphization table read from
inside a monomorph.

ROOT CAUSE: `enum_inst_type_exprs` is span-keyed and PRE-mono, so in the
monomorph it holds the generic `Option[T]`. `option_inline_payload_elem`
cannot read a payload element off that, every tracker in
`track_discarded_temp_cleanup` declined, and the temp fell through to
`materialize_owned_temp`, which does not free it in this shape. Rewriting
the bare param names through the active monomorph substitution
(`subst_monomorph_type_params`) makes `T` concrete.

THE GATE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DEFENSIVE, and this is the part worth
reading before touching this code. The fix is a SEPARATE last-resort
tracker gated to an impl-method monomorph (`enum_inst_var_types` carries a
"self" entry only there). TWO earlier attempts failed: substituting inside
the existing inline-Option tracker, and then running that substitution as a
last resort. BOTH turned a CLEAN generic free-function case into a 16-byte
leak, because `track_discarded_temp_cleanup`'s chain is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE
-- claiming a temp there displaces the handler that was already freeing it.
A handler that claims MORE is not strictly better.
title: A DISCARDED method-call result that owns heap is never freed: `h.xs.pop();` as a bare expression statement leaks the popped element's buffer (8 bytes in 1 allocation for a `Vec[Vec[i64]]` element) under LeakSanitizer. Binding the result (`let _v = h.xs.pop();`) or matching on it is clean, so it is the discarding that leaks, not the pop.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: measured while closing B-2026-08-25-14 and confirmed distinct from it -- its 8 bytes / 1 allocation is unchanged by that fix and by B-2026-08-25-10 / -11. Those rows concern which drop a value's OWNER runs; this is a value that is produced, owns heap, and is then thrown away without ever acquiring an owner.

REPRO -- prints `2`, leaks under `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1` (Linux; LSan does not run on macOS):
  struct Heap[T] { xs: Vec[T] }
  impl[T] Heap[T] {
      fn take(self) -> i64 { let mut h = self; h.xs.pop(); h.xs.len() }
  }
  fn main() { let h = Heap { xs: [[1], [2], [3]] }; println(h.take()); }

The ASAN allocation stack puts the leaked buffer inside the monomorph
(`Heap.take$struct$T_ct_Vec_i64`), and its size is exactly one element -- i.e.
the element `pop()` transferred out and the discarding statement dropped on the
floor.

SCOPE IS PROBABLY WIDER THAN THIS REPRO, and should be established before fixing: `pop()` is just a convenient producer. Any expression statement whose value owns heap and is discarded is a candidate -- `v.remove(i);`, a method returning `String`/`Vec`, a call returning an owning struct. Worth enumerating the producers and testing them as a matrix rather than fixing the `pop` case alone; a targeted fix at `pop` would leave the class open and the next producer would file the same bug again.

Note the interpreter is correct here (it drops the discarded temporary), so this is a codegen-only divergence, which also means the run-vs-build parity gate would catch it only if a fixture ever printed something that depended on it -- it does not, which is why this needed LSan to surface.

SEVERITY: medium -- bounded, non-corrupting, but "call a mutating method for its side effect and ignore the returned element" is an ordinary idiom, and the leak is proportional to how often the statement runs (a loop discarding a popped String leaks per iteration).

MEASUREMENT HYGIENE: numbers taken with no `cargo` build in flight, via the repo's `asan_build` example.
