NARROWED 2026-08-28 on 17148fb, four controls. The trigger is an owned PARAM
scrutinee whose payload is bound out and RETURNED -- not the `match`, and not
the caller binding the result.

    A. baseline (this row)                                interp 1 | compiled 2
       fn take(o: Option[R]) -> R { match o { Some(r) => { r } .. } }
    B. same, `if let` instead of `match`                  interp 1 | compiled 2
       fn take(o: Option[R]) -> R { if let Some(r) = o { return r } R { id: 0 } }
    C. same, result DISCARDED at the call site            interp 1 | compiled 2
       take(o);
    D. scrutinee is a callee LOCAL, not a param           ALL THREE 1
       fn take() -> R { let o: Option[R] = Some(R { id: 1 }); match o { .. } }

D is the one that localizes it: move the `Option` from a parameter to a local
inside the same callee and every backend agrees on one body. B and C rule out
the `match` spelling and the caller's binding respectively. The braces make no
difference either (the bare-arm spelling doubles identically), which is what
separates this row from B-2026-08-28-66.

THE ENTRY-COPY MODEL IS VISIBLE ONE STEP AWAY, and it complicates "which side
is right":

    E. fn take(r: R) -> R { r }                           ALL THREE 2
       let r = R { id: 1 }; let k = take(r);

E constructs ONE `R` and hands it straight through, and every backend runs its
body TWICE. The backends AGREE, so no A/B gate reports it -- but design.md
§ Part 8 says "a value is dropped exactly once, at the live-range end of its
final owner", so two is wrong there as well. That makes compiled's TWO in
shapes A-C consistent with E rather than arbitrary: the caller's entry copy of
the param dies and so does the returned value.

So this row and E are plausibly one defect in the entry-copy/caller-retains
model, seen from two sides -- and the interpreter's ONE in A-C is right for
the wrong reason, since it does not extend to E. A fix that only moves
compiled into line on A-C without settling E would leave the model
inconsistent with itself in the same way B-2026-08-28-53 turned out to be.

NOT ATTEMPTED, deliberately. This is the caller-retains model that
B-2026-08-28-22 and its follow-up B-2026-08-28-70 are actively about, and
another session held those rows while this was measured; a unilateral change
to when a by-value param's entry copy runs its body would collide with that
work. The four controls above are recorded so whoever takes the family can use
them, and E should be filed or folded in as part of that, not separately
patched here.

Confirms the original filing's instrumentation result: no pattern-binding
registration fires for any of A-D.

CORRECTION (2026-08-29, at close). The row's "WHERE THE SECOND BODY COMES
FROM" hypothesis named the wrong frame. It read: "the callee also RETURNS
that payload, so the caller ends up firing both for the entry copy it
retained and for the returned value bound to `k`" -- which is right about the
double ownership but wrong about who emits the second call, and the row
proposed looking at the callee's escape predicates for it.

The callee emits NOTHING. Its IR at -O0 is the match and two `println`s, with
no drop call anywhere:

    define internal { i64 } @take({ i64, i64, i64, i64 } %0) { ... }
      -- no karac_drop_*, no __karac_dropelems_*

BOTH bodies are in the CALLER, three instructions apart. That is why the row's
own instrumentation of every `track_user_drop_var*` site in
`pattern_binding.rs` correctly found none firing: it was looking in the callee.
Marker-instrumented output places the spurious fire between the callee's last
statement and the caller's next one, which reads as "inside the callee" and is
what sent the first reduction to the wrong side of the call boundary.

The row was also right that this is not the arm-registration channel and not
braces-dependent, and both of those held up.
fix:
FIXED by 5746b82, in codegen, by widening the caller-side retraction B-2026-08-09-15
already runs for a user value enum to cover `Option` and `Result`, which it
excluded BY NAME.

The row's hypothesis was right about the mechanism (caller-retains) and wrong
about where the second body came from: it guessed the CALLEE fires it. The
callee emits no drop at all. Dumping `take`'s IR shows an empty function body
apart from the match; both bodies are in the CALLER:

    %call = call { i64 } @take({ i64, i64, i64, i64 } %o2)
    store { i64 } %call, ptr %k
    call void @__karac_dropelems_opt_R(ptr %o)     <- caller-retains, at `o`'s
                                                      live-range end
    ...
    call void @karac_drop_R(ptr %k)                <- `k`'s own wrapper

`o`'s payload-bodies walk fires at the arg's NLL end (right when the value
would have died inside the callee) and `k`'s wrapper fires at scope exit. One
value, two owners, two bodies.

THE CONTROL THAT NAMED THE FIX. The same program spelled with a user value
enum is CORRECT on every backend:

    enum Box2 { Full(R), Empty }
    fn take(o: Box2) -> R { match o { Box2.Full(r) => { r } Box2.Empty => .. } }
      interp / jit / aot -> `dR1`                    all agree

    fn take(o: Option[R]) -> R { match o { Some(r) => { r } None => .. } }
      interp -> `dR1`   jit / aot -> `dR1 dR1`       compiled doubles

B-2026-08-09-15 built exactly this retraction for the enum spelling —
`fn_returns_param_payload` asks the callee whether a `match` arm hands back
something bound OUT of the arg, which `fn_returns_param` cannot see because
the param itself reaches no return site. Its gate then read

    en != "Option" && en != "Result" && enum_layouts.get(en)..!is_shared

with the comment "`Option`/`Result` have their own". They do not, and that
exclusion was the entire defect. Nothing in the retraction is enum-specific:
it acts through `suppress_container_elem_bodies_for_var`, which retains on
`UserDrop { kind: ContainerElemBodies }` keyed by BINDING NAME and never looks
at which walker the binding carries — `__karac_dropelems_enum_<E>` for a user
enum, `__karac_dropelems_opt_*` / `_res_*` for the two built-ins, all the same
channel. The fix flips the two `!=` clauses to `==` disjuncts (call_dispatch.rs).

MEASURED, with a temporary env hatch so one binary answers both directions
(`KARAC_B72_OFF=1` restores the old gate):

    shape                                     interp        PRE          POST
    Option, `Some(r) => { return r; }`        drop 7 e7     DOUBLED      correct
    Option, `Some(r) => { r }` (block tail)   dR1           DOUBLED      correct
    Result, `Ok(r) => { return r; }`          drop 7 e7     DOUBLED      correct
    Option, scalar payload, return-alias      dR7           DOUBLED      correct
    Result, heap payload, return-alias        drop 7 e7     DOUBLED      correct
    GUARD RAIL: payload read, not returned    drop 7        correct      correct
    GUARD RAIL: param never matched           in/drop 7     correct      correct

Note the PRE output of the first row: `drop 7 ` with an EMPTY name. The
spurious fire reads the moved-from slot, so it was already printing a
half-dead value, not merely printing twice.

THE INHERITED TRADE, measured rather than assumed. The predicate is
conservative-TRUE on a mixed-path callee (returns the payload on some paths,
not others), so the caller suppresses on EVERY path and the non-returning
path loses the body. Measured on
`Some(r) => { if keep { return r; } else { return Res { id: 9, .. }; } }`:

    PRE  (Option)  `drop 7 ` / kept 7 / `drop 7 e7` / `drop 8 e8` / .. / `drop 9 n9`
    POST (Option)  kept 7 / `drop 7 e7` / dropped-path 9 / `drop 9 n9`
    interp         kept 7 / `drop 7 e7` / dropped-path 9 / `drop 9 n9`
    value-enum leg kept 7 / `drop 7 e7` / dropped-path 9 / `drop 9 n9`  (PRE == POST)

POST matches the interpreter AND the already-shipped enum leg EXACTLY. So the
lost `drop 8 e8` is not new behaviour this commit invents: it is the trade
B-2026-08-09-15 already made for enums, and taking it here moves codegen ONTO
the interpreter's answer instead of away from it. The pre-fix output was worse
in both directions at once -- a spurious doubled body on the returning path
AND an extra body on the non-returning one. (That both backends now decline
`drop 8 e8` is a separate, SHARED missed body of B-2026-08-28-22's class,
symmetric across backends and so invisible to an A/B gate; it is not touched
here in either direction.)

`Result` is covered by the same widening and pinned separately, because the
`Ok`/`Err` walker is a different symbol reached by the same name test — a
future narrowing could drop the `Result` half while keeping `Option`.

WHY NO ASAN/LSAN FIXTURE. Memory is balanced on both sides of this fix: the
`__karac_dropelems_*` walkers free nothing by construction (that is the
property B-2026-08-02-25's doc rests on), so the defect is invisible to the
memory corpus and to the run-vs-build parity oracle's memory half. An output
pin is the only signal, which is why B-2026-08-09-15's own tests are output
pins too.

TWO RESIDUALS SPLIT OUT, both measured IDENTICAL with the retraction on and
off, so neither is caused or fixed by this commit: B-2026-08-29-7 (an
`Option` arm that rebinds its heap payload to a local and RETURNS it is a
DOUBLE FREE, pre-existing, and the `Result` and value-enum twins are clean)
and B-2026-08-29-8 (a payload rebound to a local and yielded as the arm's
BLOCK TAIL doubles its body on both compiled backends, value enums included,
so it is outside this family entirely).

INTERPRETER SIDE UNPINNED, following the sibling row: B-2026-08-09-15's tests
live in `tests/codegen.rs` and pin the compiled backend only, and these do the
same. The interpreter is correct here before and after.

Verified: codegen 3394 / 0, interpreter 1809 / 0, memory_sanitizer 1299 / 0,
drop_differential 19 / 0; both clippy legs and fmt clean. The two new pins are
RED-verified against the pre-fix compiler (the escape pin fails, the guard
rail passes both ways, which is what a guard rail should do).

title: REGRESSION from 77729f2 (NOT f862656, as first filed): A CONSUMING ARM THAT HANDS ITS BOUND BOXED ENUM PAYLOAD OUT AS THE MATCH'S VALUE DOUBLE-FREES THE PAYLOAD ON BOTH COMPILED BACKENDS -- `let k = match o { Some(g) => { g } .. }` for an own-`Drop` `enum G { A(String), B }` aborts with `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` under plain `karac run`, no sanitizer; the box gained its interior walk without the move-out retraction that keeps a payload the arm hands on from being freed twice
detail:
REGRESSION from f862656 ("fix(drop): run a consuming arm's bound enum payload's
Drop body", B-2026-08-28-63). Both shapes below PASS on f862656^ and FAIL at
f862656 and at HEAD (9b221e7), measured by checking out that parent's `src/`
alone and rebuilding.

SHAPE 1 -- DOUBLE FREE, aborts with no sanitizer involved:

    enum G { A(String), B }
    impl Drop for G { fn drop(mut ref self) { println("drop G") } }
    fn main() { let o: Option[G] = Some(G.A(f"z{9}"));
                let k = match o { Some(g) => { g } None => { G.B } };
                println("kept"); }

      interp                  -> `drop G` / `kept`                    CORRECT
      karac run (JIT, -O2)    -> free(): double free detected in tcache 2
      karac run (JIT, -O0)    -> free(): double free detected in tcache 2
      karac build (AOT, -O0)  -> free(): double free detected in tcache 2
      karac build (AOT, -O2)  -> `drop G` / `kept`                    (see below)

THE AOT -O2 PASS IS AN ARTIFACT, not a limit on the blast radius. That body
prints a LITERAL, so nothing reads the `String` and LLVM deletes the allocation
outright. Give the body a payload read and every compiled path aborts at every
optimization level:

    impl Drop for G { fn drop(mut ref self) {
        match self { G.A(s) => { println(f"drop G{s}") } G.B => { println("drop GB") } } } }

      interp                  -> `drop Gz9` / `kept`                  CORRECT
      AOT -O2 and -O0         -> free(): double free detected in tcache 2

So this is a shipped-binary abort on both compiled backends, not an -O0
curiosity -- `karac run`, the default executor, aborts on the ORIGINAL spelling.

SHAPE 2 -- LEAK, same commit, different direction. `via_whilelet` in the
`asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak` fixture
(`while let Some(v) = vv` over an `Option[Val]` for an own-heap enum `Val`)
leaks 456 bytes in 12 objects at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 -- 192 B / 6 direct (the
boxed `Val`s) plus 264 B / 6 indirect (their `String`s), one per loop
iteration. Clean on f862656^. FIXING SHAPE 1 DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY CLEAR THIS;
re-run that fixture at -O0 before assuming it did.

CI IS RED ON MAIN. `scripts/asan-o0-leg.sh` (the ci.yml asan-o0 job) runs the
memory_sanitizer suite at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 and gates it against
`tests/asan-o0-known-failures.txt`, which is currently EMPTY -- so any -O0
failure fails the job. Measured at 9b221e7: `1290 passed; 2 failed`, and the two
are exactly the fixtures named above
(`asan_consuming_arm_enum_payload_bodies_are_memory_balanced` /
`[escaping-tail]`, which f862656 itself introduced, and
`asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak`).

WHY IT LANDED GREEN. The `escaping-tail` fixture's own comment anticipates this
cell -- "the consumption gate must keep the arm from registering, or the body
and the free both run twice" -- and the fixture does catch it. It only runs at
-O0, and the default `cargo test --features llvm` leg compiles at -O2 where the
literal-printing body lets LLVM delete the allocation. The -O0 leg is a separate
CI job that was not run before the merge.

DISTINCT FROM B-2026-08-28-69 / -72, which are about body COUNTS with balanced
memory ("MEMORY IS BALANCED", "the memory is reclaimed either way") and are
triggered by an owned-PARAM scrutinee; -72's control D -- the same shape with a
callee-LOCAL scrutinee -- is correct for a struct payload. This row is the ENUM
spelling of that control, and it is a heap double free rather than a doubled
body.

SOURCE NOTE: found by sweeping the memory_sanitizer suite at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0
under LSAN_OPTIONS=use_stacks=0; shape 1 turned out to be visible at the DEFAULT
LSan configuration too, and then without any sanitizer at all.

CORRECTED 2026-08-29. The filing named f862656 and that is wrong; the cause is
77729f2. The error was in the METHOD, not the measurement: it checked out
`f862656^ -- src/`, saw a clean tree, and concluded f862656 — but checking out
one commit's PARENT reverts everything after that commit too, so a clean parent
only bounds the defect to `f862656..HEAD`. Walking the range settles it:

    f862656   drop G | kept          CORRECT
    93dbc48   drop G | kept          CORRECT
    77729f2   free(): double free detected in tcache 2
    HEAD      free(): double free detected in tcache 2

That shortcut is a bisect step only when the commit under test is HEAD.
Anywhere else it names the oldest suspect in the range every time.

SHAPE 2 IS SPLIT OUT to B-2026-08-28-75 rather than carried here. The 456 B
`while let` leak in `asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak` is also
77729f2's, and also real, but it is a different mechanism — the box ENVELOPE
going unowned when the scrutinee variable is reassigned mid-loop — and it is
measurably unmoved by the fix that closes this row.
fix:
Fixed in 1caf601 (landed by a concurrent session while this row was being
worked; the same one-gate widening, reached independently). The box-view
registration the neutralizer reads now admits a boxed user ENUM payload, which
is the half B-2026-08-28-64 left out.

ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED, and the correction is the first thing worth recording
because the row was filed with the wrong commit. It blamed f862656
(B-2026-08-28-63). The actual cause is 77729f2 (B-2026-08-28-64), two commits
later. The filing measured "clean at f862656^" and concluded f862656 -- but
`git checkout f862656^ -- src/` reverts EVERYTHING after that commit, not just
that commit, so a clean parent only bounds the defect to `f862656..HEAD`. A
proper walk settles it:

    f862656   drop G | kept          CORRECT
    93dbc48   drop G | kept          CORRECT
    77729f2   free(): double free detected in tcache 2
    HEAD      free(): double free detected in tcache 2

The lesson generalizes past this row: checking out one commit's PARENT is a
bisect step only when that commit is HEAD. Anywhere else it is a revert of the
tail, and it will name the oldest suspect in the range every time.

THE MECHANISM. 77729f2 widened two struct-keyed gates so a boxed user ENUM
payload gets an interior walk: `boxed_enum_payload_variants` (types_lowering.rs)
now NAMES an enum payload, and `track_boxed_enum_var` resolves
`emit_enum_drop_switch` for it, so the source's `BoxedEnumDrop` walks the
payload before freeing the box. That is right for a payload nothing takes --
the leak that row fixed.

There is a third struct-keyed gate on the same axis, and it says the opposite
thing: `boxed_optres_payload_view_vars` in `pattern_binding.rs` records a
binding as a VIEW of the box, and `suppress_boxed_payload_view_move` reads it to
clear the box's `inner_drop_fn` at a move. It stayed struct-only. So the enum
half gained the WALK without the RETRACTION, and a payload the arm hands on had
two owners: the destination and the source's box. `let k = match o { Some(g) =>
{ g } .. }` over `Option[G]` for `enum G { A(String), B }` aborts with
`free(): double free detected in tcache 2`.

The fix reuses `tn_is_boxable_payload` / `tn_wider_than_area` -- the two locals
the bodies gate a few lines up already computes -- rather than writing "boxed
user aggregate" a third time. Keeping the walk and its retraction on ONE
predicate is the point: they went out of step because they were spelled twice.

NOT AN -O0 CURIOSITY, which is how the corpus made it look. The fixture that
caught it prints a LITERAL from its `Drop` body, so nothing reads the payload
buffer and LLVM deletes the allocation at -O2 -- the AOT -O2 build passed while
`karac run` aborted on the same program. Give the body a payload read and every
compiled surface aborts at every optimization level:

    impl Drop for G { fn drop(mut ref self) {
        match self { G.A(s) => { println(f"drop G{s}") } G.B => { println("drop GB") } } } }

      interp                      drop Gz9 | kept        CORRECT
      JIT -O0 / -O2               abort
      AOT -O0 / -O2               abort

Both new fixtures use a reading body for exactly that reason, so they gate on
the default leg rather than only at -O0.

Nine shapes now agree across interp / JIT / AOT / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, pinned in
two suites and RED-verified against the unfixed tree at the DEFAULT opt level:
`codegen::e2e_consuming_arm_handing_a_boxed_enum_payload_out_runs_one_body` and
`memory_sanitizer::asan_consuming_arm_handing_a_boxed_enum_payload_out_frees_it_once`.
Three of the rows are boundaries rather than confirmations -- `read-only-arm`
(the source keeps everything), `discarded` (no destination, so the box must stay
armed; neutralizing there trades the double free for a leak, which is what
`branch_value_is_owned` prevents), and `struct-control` (the axis, correct
before and after).

THE ROW'S SECOND SHAPE IS SPLIT OUT, not fixed here. The 456 B `while let` leak
in `asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak` is also 77729f2's, and also
real, but it is a different mechanism in a different place: a consuming
`while let` takes the payload out of the box and nothing frees the ENVELOPE on
the path where the scrutinee variable is then reassigned. Measured unchanged by
this fix. Filed as B-2026-08-28-75 with its three controls, and quarantined in
`tests/asan-o0-known-failures.txt` under that id so the -O0 CI leg gates again.

title: THREE REAL LEAKS THE DEFAULT LSan CONFIGURATION HIDES: a `shared` ENUM broken out of a `loop` (32 B x 3 fixtures, `pick`) and a tensor ref-return (72 B), reported only under `LSAN_OPTIONS=use_stacks=0` -- the fixtures assert cleanliness by name and pass today; the rest of the suite is clean, with -O2 showing ZERO real leaks across 1289 fixtures
detail:
Found by sweeping the whole memory_sanitizer suite with
`LSAN_OPTIONS=use_stacks=0`, which stops LeakSanitizer scanning thread stacks
for pointers. At process exit a stack slot is NOT an owner -- the program has
ended and nothing will free through it -- so a block reported only under
`use_stacks=0` is a real leak that the default configuration conservatively
calls reachable. This is the same measurement asymmetry B-2026-08-28-49 closed
on.

Measured at 9b221e7, x86_64 Linux, both archives current. Sweep totals:

  -O2 baseline (default LSan)   1289 passed / 0 failed
  -O2 use_stacks=0              1229 passed / 60 failed -- TWO allocation-site
                                signatures, both benign runtime init:
                                  288 objs / 13,824 B  std::sync::once::call_once_force
                                    4 objs /    224 B  karac_runtime_scheduler_start_dispatcher
                                With `leak:std::sync::once` suppressed: 1 failure,
                                the dispatcher `Arc` (runtime/src/event_loop.rs:5446)
                                held by LIVE worker-thread stacks -- exactly what
                                use_stacks=0 stops scanning, so it is a false
                                positive of the sweep, not a leak.
                                >> ZERO real leaks in compiled Kara code at -O2.

  -O0 baseline (default LSan)   1290 passed / 2 failed  (see the -O0 CI row)
  -O0 use_stacks=0              1228 passed / 64 failed -- the same two benign
                                runtime signatures (260 + 4 objects) PLUS the
                                three below.

THE THREE REAL ONES, all confirmed PRE-EXISTING (they reproduce with f862656^'s
`src/`, so they are not part of that commit's regression):

  1. `pick` -- 32 B in 1 object, in each of three fixtures:
       asan_loop_break_match_arm_rvalue_single_owner   [loop-break-match-arm-rvalue]
       asan_loop_break_shared_enum_rvalue_single_owner [loop-break-shared-enum-rvalue]
       asan_loop_break_shared_enum_single_owner        [loop-break-shared-enum]
     All three break a `shared` ENUM value out of a `loop` and return it:
       `fn pick() -> Tree { loop { .. if i == 2 { break t } } }`
     The escaping RC object is read in `main` and never released. The shared
     STRUCT sibling (asan_loop_break_shared_struct_rvalue_single_owner) is
     CLEAN, which localizes it to the shared-enum break transfer rather than to
     `break <value>` generally -- and B-2026-08-25-1's fix note for that family
     says the transfer emits NO ownership action deliberately, so the question
     is who releases it at the far end.

  2. `main` -- 72 B in 1 object, in asan_tensor_ref_return_borrow_clean
     [tensor_ref_return_borrow].

These are worth a row rather than a footnote because the fixtures assert
CLEANLINESS by name (`_single_owner`, `_clean`) and pass today, so nothing
flags them.

THE SWEEP CONFIGURATION IS NOT A CI PROPOSAL AS IT STANDS. `use_stacks=0` costs
60+ false failures from runtime lazy-init and live worker stacks, and the
`leak:std::sync::once` suppression removes only the first class. Making it a
gate needs a second suppression for the dispatcher `Arc` (or a runtime shutdown
that joins the pool), which is its own piece of work; the value here is the
periodic manual sweep and the three findings above.
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-29 (leak 1, the `pick` / shared-enum one). The row frames it
as "a `shared` ENUM broken out of a `loop`", and that is not the trigger.
Neither the loop, nor `break <value>`, nor the return is required. Measured
under plain VALGRIND, which reports it directly and needs no `use_stacks=0`
(useful on its own: this class does not need the sweep configuration to
reproduce).

    shared enum Tree { Leaf(i64), Node(i64, i64) }
    fn mk() -> Tree { Tree.Node(1, 2) }

      match mk() { … }                        LEAK 32 B      <- the real shape
      match Tree.Node(1, 2) { … }             LEAK 32 B
      let t = mk(); match t { … }             clean
      let t = Tree.Node(1, 2); match t { … }  clean
      let t = Tree.Node(1, 2); println("made") clean

The whole trigger is a `match` over a FRESH SHARED-ENUM TEMPORARY. Every
affected fixture reaches it through `match pick() { … }`; the loop and the
`break` are incidental to how `pick` happens to be written. Two of the row's
own controls now read differently: the shared-STRUCT sibling is clean not
because `break` differs for structs, but because that fixture BINDS the result
(`let t = pick();`), and binding is the clean form for enums too.

MECHANISM. `materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee`
(`src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs`) is what gives a fresh-temp enum scrutinee
an owner, and a shared enum leaves it with none: the value is an RC POINTER, so
it never passes the `BasicValueEnum::StructValue` gate, and the `layout.is_shared`
bail below that is about the struct-valued case. The temp has no binding, so no
scope-exit `RcDec` is ever queued and the producer's `+1` is never released.

THE ONE-LINE-LOOKING FIX IS NOT ENOUGH, built and measured. Adding a branch
that recognizes the shape and calls `track_rc_var` on a materialized slot
does register the action — instrumented: the gate is reached
(`fresh=true val_ptr=true enum=Some("Tree")`), both lookups succeed
(`layout_shared=Some(true) in_shared_types=true`), and `track_rc_var` pushes
onto a live frame (`frames=1`) — and the program is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards:
still 9 allocs / 8 frees, still 32 B lost. The dec emits nothing effective.

The likely reason, and where the next attempt should look: `track_rc_var`'s own
doc says it must lazily synthesize the recursive drop fn or "`emit_rc_dec`'s
reverse-lookup would never find a registered drop fn and the recursive chain
leaks". It does that through `struct_name_for_heap_type` and
`emit_shared_struct_rc_drop_fn` — both struct-oriented. So the missing piece is
plausibly the shared-ENUM RC drop synthesis behind the dec, not the dec's
registration. That is a layer below this row as filed, and it is why this was
left open rather than patched.

Leak 2 (the tensor ref-return, 72 B) was not investigated here.
fix:
FIXED by 0ba1f22 — leak 1, the `pick` / shared-enum 32 B, all three fixtures. Leak 2 (the tensor, 72 B) is REAL, re-scoped, and split
to its own row; see the SPLIT note at the end.

ROOT CAUSE. The 2026-08-29 re-scope had the trigger right — a `match` over a
FRESH SHARED-ENUM TEMPORARY — and the mechanism half right. It is exactly the
missing registration; it is NOT the drop-synthesis layer the row guessed at.

`materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee` is the fresh-temp owner-minting path for
VALUE enums, and a shared enum fails it twice over, as the row says. But the
`Option[shared T]` tracker sitting beside it at all four scrutinee sites
(`track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee`) shows the intended shape for an
RC-valued scrutinee, and there was simply no BARE `shared enum` sibling. Added
one: `track_freshtemp_shared_enum_scrutinee`, wired at the same four sites
(match, `if let`, `while let`, `let…else`), gated the same way — fresh, non-
borrow, RC `PointerValue`, `enum_layouts[..].is_shared` — registering one
`RcDec` through `track_rc_var`.

WHY THE ROW'S RECORDED DEAD END WAS A DEAD END, corrected. The row concluded
that registering the dec "emits nothing effective" and pointed at
`struct_name_for_heap_type` / `emit_shared_struct_rc_drop_fn` being
"struct-oriented", calling the shared-ENUM RC drop synthesis the likely missing
piece. That is not so, and it is checkable in one hop:
`emit_shared_struct_rc_drop_fn` opens with `if info.is_enum { return
self.emit_shared_enum_rc_drop_fn(struct_name); }` — it has routed shared enums
to the tag-switched enum walk since B-2026-06-13-11. Nothing below the dec was
missing. This row does not reproduce the "byte-identical afterwards"
measurement and cannot say what that attempt actually registered; what it can
say is that the registration alone, placed at these four sites, is sufficient
and that the layer beneath it was already correct.

THE BOUND SPELLING IS THE ORACLE, and it is what makes this safe rather than
merely plausible. `let t = mk(); match t { … }` was ALREADY CLEAN on every
payload shape measured, so the fix's whole claim is that the unnamed temp now
frees identically. Measured under valgrind at -O0, pre-fix vs post-fix, with
the bound twin beside each (allocs/frees):

  payload of the shared enum        fresh temp        bound twin (oracle)
  scalar `Node(i64, i64)`           9/8  -> 9/9       9/9   (unchanged)
  `String`, arm BINDS it            10/9 -> 10/10     10/10 (unchanged)
  `String`, arm LEAVES it unbound   10/8 -> 10/10     10/10 (unchanged)
  `Vec[i64]`, arm binds it          10/9 -> 10/10     10/10 (unchanged)
  shared CHILD struct               10/8 -> 10/10     10/10 (unchanged)
  recursive `Bin(E, E)`             11/8 -> 11/11     11/11 (unchanged)

Every fresh-temp row now equals its oracle exactly, and no oracle row moved.
valgrind ERROR SUMMARY is 0 on all of them, so the added dec introduced no
double free. All four constructs leak pre-fix and are clean post-fix
(`match` / `if let` / `let…else` / `while let`, and a wildcard arm that binds
nothing). Output is byte-identical across interpreter, JIT, AOT and
`KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` on all 19 probes, before and after.

THE MOVE-OUT HALF NEEDED NO NEW WORK, which is the other reason the fix is one
registration. An arm that MOVES a heap payload out would double-free against
the box's drop walk, except that `suppress_shared_enum_payload_move_out`
already fires per-arm for ANY pointer-valued scrutinee — it is keyed on
`scrut.is_pointer_value()`, not on the fresh-temp tracker — and zeroes the
consumed field's words in the box so the walk skips what the binding now owns.
The `String`-bound row above (10/10, 0 errors) is that path exercised.

THE ROW'S "-O2 SHOWS ZERO REAL LEAKS ACROSS 1289 FIXTURES" NEEDS A CAVEAT, and
it is the reason this leak survived a full sweep. At -O2 LLVM promotes a
never-freed, non-escaping box out of existence: measured pre-fix, EVERY flat
shape above drops to 8 allocations and reports no leak at all (9->8, 10->8,
11->8), including the ones carrying a live heap `String` or `Vec`. So the -O2
sweep's clean result was, for this class, a statement about what the optimizer
elides rather than about ownership. It is not universally elided: a RECURSIVE
shared enum built by a recursive fn leaks 32 B directly + 192 B indirectly at
-O2 (15 allocs / 8 frees), because LLVM cannot promote the tree away. The
suite simply had no fixture of that shape.

That measurement is what the regression tests are built on.
`asan_freshtemp_shared_enum_scrutinee_releases_its_box` (7 rows) and
`asan_freshtemp_shared_enum_payload_moveout_is_balanced` (2 rows) both use the
recursive shape deliberately, since `memory_sanitizer` compiles at -O2
(`read_opt_level_env` defaults to `2`) and any flatter fixture would pass
whether or not the bug is present. Verified non-vacuous: both FAIL on the
pre-fix tree with real LeakSanitizer reports (224 B in 7 allocations, 116 B in
3 allocations) and pass after. The rows include the bound oracle, a place
scrutinee reached through a second binding (the tracker must keep declining, or
the box is released early and the later read is a use-after-free), and a
`while let` with a `break` — the one construct whose registration lands in the
per-iteration body frame rather than the enclosing one.

SPLIT: leak 2 (the tensor, 72 B) is real and is now its own row. It is NOT a
"tensor ref-return" — that framing is wrong the same way leak 1's `loop`/`break`
framing was. Minimized: ANY struct with a `Tensor` field leaks it, with no ref
return, no method, and no read of the field anywhere in the program. The new
row carries the minimal repro, the measured reason a one-line fix would double
free, and the -O0/-O2 note.

title: REASSIGNING AN `Option`/`Result` BINDING WHOSE BOXED PAYLOAD ARRIVED BY A WHOLE-VALUE MOVE FROM ANOTHER BINDING ORPHANS THE PAYLOAD BOX ON EVERY STORE -- `let mut vv = value; vv = anything;` leaks 76 B for a boxed enum payload and 100 B for a boxed struct one, with NO `while let`, NO consumption of the payload and NO loop required (filed as all three); the displaced-box eager free excluded moved-in boxes on PROVENANCE, and the `if let` arm-tail box-view retraction that would have made freeing them safe was never written
detail:
SPLIT OUT OF B-2026-08-28-73, which reported two shapes from one commit. The
DOUBLE FREE half is fixed; this is the LEAK half, and it is a different
mechanism in a different file, so it does not follow from that fix (verified:
identical 456 B / 12 objects before and after it).

REGRESSION from 77729f2 (B-2026-08-28-64). Clean at 93dbc48, its parent;
leaking at 77729f2 and at HEAD. `asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak`
fails at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, which is CI's asan-o0 job.

MINIMAL SHAPE -- 76 bytes per call, 32 B direct (the payload BOX) plus 44 B
indirect (its `String`):

    enum Val { Nothing, Ident(String) }
    fn ident_len(v: Val) -> i64 { match v { Val.Ident(s) => s.len(), Val.Nothing => 0 } }
    fn val_none() -> Option[Val] { Option.None }

    let mut vv: Option[Val] = Some(Val.Ident("....40 chars...."));
    let mut acc = 0;
    while let Some(v) = vv { acc = acc + ident_len(v); vv = val_none(); }

THREE CONTROLS, each CLEAN, and together they say it needs BOTH halves:

  A. the same reassignment with NO while-let        clean
       let mut vv: Option[Val] = Some(..); vv = val_none();
     so the assignment's displacement drop works on its own.
  B. the same while-let with NO reassignment        clean
       while let Some(v) = vv { acc = acc + ident_len(v); break }
     so the consuming bind works on its own.
  C. A's struct-payload twin (`Option[S]`, S boxed) clean

WHAT CHANGED, read out of the emitted IR for the `via_whilelet` shape at
93dbc48 vs HEAD (one function, two dumps):

  93dbc48   `value` is zero-initialized in `entry` and KEEPS its words across
            `let mut vv = value` -- an alias -- and an UNGUARDED
            `karac_drop_Option_Val(%value)` at scope exit frees box + interior
            through it.
  HEAD      the move-out zeroing moved to right after `store %value8, ptr %vv`,
            and the exit action is a TAG-GUARDED `BoxedEnumDrop` on `value`.
            The tag is now zero, so it skips; `vv`'s own `BoxedEnumDrop` also

(`inner_drop_fn: None`) against it -- but it is wired for a struct-FIELD
scrutinee (`match w.o`), not for a local `Option` variable rebound in a loop.

fix:
FIXED by d5c4606, in TWO halves, and neither is shippable alone -- that pairing is the whole content of this row. HALF 1, `src/codegen/stmts.rs`: DELETE the `boxed_moved_in_vars` exclusion from the displaced-box eager free (B-2026-08-07-4's arm). Half 2, `src/codegen/control_flow.rs`: give `compile_if_let` the arm-tail box-view neutralizer its `match` twin has had since B-2026-08-04-2. The provenance set and its recording site are gone; nothing else read them. THE FILING WAS MUCH NARROWER THAN THE DEFECT, and correcting that is the first thing worth recording. The row reported a consuming `while let` over an `Option[enum]` whose scrutinee is reassigned in the loop. Three of those four words are incidental: while let NOT required -- the `match` spelling leaks identically, and so does a program with no construct at all. consuming NOT required -- `Some(_v)` with the binding unused leaks the same 76 bytes. enum payload NOT required -- a boxed STRUCT payload leaks its 100. in a loop NOT required -- one store leaks one box. What is actually required is the pair MOVED-IN BOX + ANY LATER STORE: let value: Option[Val] = Some(Val.Ident("...40 chars...")); let mut vv = value; // the alias -- this is the trigger vv = val_none(); // any store at all The row's own stated "MINIMAL SHAPE" dropped the alias, and it DOES NOT REPRODUCE -- it is clean at every optimization level, before and after this fix. That is worth flagging as a filing hazard rather than a footnote: the shape was reduced from a fixture that had the alias buried in a struct destructure (`let A { value } = a; let mut vv = value;`), the destructure was correctly identified as incidental, and the ALIAS went out with it because both lines vanished together. THE MECHANISM. B-2026-08-07-4 added the eager free that reclaims a boxed payload displaced by a store, and excluded boxes acquired by whole-value move from another binding -- recorded at the let site as `boxed_moved_in_vars` whenever the RHS was an identifier. That gate keyed on PROVENANCE, not on ownership, and the population it excluded is enormous: every `let mut vv = value;` followed by any store to `vv`. Its stated hazard was real, and it is why the obvious one-line deletion is wrong on its own. From the field's own doc: the box can be released through a channel that leaves the SLOT reading `Some` with a stale pointer, so a store-site free that trusts the slot double-frees. Measured here, freshly: with half 1 alone, `let k = if let Some(g) = vv { g } else { Val.Nothing }; vv = none(); ident_len(k)` is a HEAP-USE-AFTER-FREE -- the box's interior walk frees the `String` that `k` now owns and `ident_len` then reads it. Turning a 76-byte leak into a use-after-free is a strictly worse trade. But that hazard is the symptom of a MISSING RETRACTION, not a reason to skip the free. `compile_match` neutralizes the source box's interior walk when an arm hands the bound payload out as the match's value (B-2026-08-04-2, widened to block tails by B-2026-08-28-66). `compile_if_let` never grew the same call. The asymmetry stayed invisible for the same reason the leak did: the eager free declined for exactly this population, so the un-retracted walk was never reached and the shape presented as a 32-byte envelope leak rather than as anything about `if let`. With both halves the walk is retracted wherever the payload escapes, so the store-site free reclaims the ENVELOPE only, and the two sides balance. Verified in all three directions -- free without retraction is a UAF, retraction without free is the leak, neither is the original leak, both is clean. THE `branch_value_is_owned` GUARD ON THE NEW CALL IS LOAD-BEARING, not defensive, and is measured rather than copied: replacing it with `true` leaks 68 bytes in 1 object on `if let Some(g) = vv { g };` in statement position. Neutralizing assumes a destination that registers a drop of its own, and a discarded if-let has none -- exactly what the match site's comment predicts for its own spelling. NOT A REGRESSION FROM 77729f2, which is what the row says. That commit is what made the b31 fixture start FAILING -- true, and re-verified: clean at 93dbc48, leaking at 77729f2 -- but only because the source binding's words had until then survived as an ALIAS that an unguarded `karac_drop_Option_

` freed through. A correct move-out zeroing removed the alias and stopped masking a hole that B-2026-08-07-4 had opened three weeks earlier. The distinction matters for anyone reading 77729f2 as suspect: it made a latent gap visible, which is the opposite of introducing one. COVERAGE. `memory_sanitizer::asan_reassigning_a_moved_in_boxed_payload_frees_ the_envelope`, 18 rows across interp/JIT/AOT: eight shapes that leaked, four hand-out hazard rows (`match-hands-out`, `iflet-hands-out`, `iflet-hands-out-braced`, `two-aliases-one-stored`), and six boundaries that were clean before and must stay so -- `discarded-iflet`, `alias-never-stored`, `direct-init-control`, `self-assign`, `roundtrip`, plus the axis row. RED-verified against the unfixed tree at BOTH optimization levels. THE FIXTURE READS ITS PAYLOAD WITH `contains`, NOT `len`, AND THAT IS THE REUSABLE LESSON. The first draft read it with `s.len()` and was GREEN at -O2 against the unfixed compiler -- the -73 vacuous-pass trap in a subtler dress. `len` reads the `{ptr,len,cap}` HEADER, not the bytes; an f-string's length is known at its construction site, so LLVM propagates it and deletes the `malloc` outright. Reading a payload is not enough to keep it alive; the read has to touch the BUFFER. With that one substitution the fixture went from -O0-only to RED at both levels on the unfixed tree (-O0: 77 B / 2 objects on `whilelet-reassign`; -O2: 293 B / 6 on `loop-reassign`). The payload is also runtime-derived through `env.args().len()` for the same reason. No codegen output-parity fixture accompanies this one, deliberately. All three backends print identically before and after on every shape here -- it is a pure memory bug -- so a parity fixture would be green both ways and would pin nothing. `tests/asan-o0-known-failures.txt` is EMPTY again: the quarantine entry this row's own filing added for `asan_b31_option_agg_payload_borrow_only_no_leak` is gone, and `scripts/asan-o0-leg.sh` reports 1297 passed / 0 failed against a list of zero. TWO RESIDUALS ARE SPLIT OUT rather than buried here. Both are PRE-EXISTING -- measured identical at 93dbc48 and at HEAD, and unchanged by this fix -- so neither is a regression and neither belongs in this row's scope: B-2026-08-29-1 (a bare `String`/`Vec` payload inside `Option`/`Result` never has its buffer freed on ANY reassignment, alias or not) and B-2026-08-29-2 (the nested-box `Result[Option[Wide], i64]` family loses its inner `String`).

title: A BARE `String` / `Vec` PAYLOAD INSIDE AN `Option` OR `Result` NEVER HAS ITS BUFFER FREED WHEN THE BINDING IS REASSIGNED -- `let mut vv: Option[String] = Some(s); vv = None;` leaks the whole buffer (38 B measured), and so does `Option[Vec[i64]]` (80 B) and `Result[String, i64]` (38 B); the displaced payload's user `Drop` BODY fires correctly on all three backends, so this is the memory half alone, and the STRUCT payload twin (`Option[D]` for `struct D { s: String }`) is CLEAN
detail:
SPLIT OUT OF B-2026-08-28-75 as a residual, NOT part of that row's defect. It
is PRE-EXISTING and orthogonal: measured byte-identical at 93dbc48 and at
d5c4606 (the commit that closed -75), so neither 77729f2 nor -75's fix moved
it in either direction.

MEASURED (KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, ASAN + LSan, payloads runtime-derived through
`env.args().len()` so nothing folds, reads via `contains` so the BUFFER is
live rather than just the header):

    Option[String]      reassigned to None      38 B / 1 object    LEAKS
    Option[Vec[i64]]    reassigned to None      80 B / 1 object    LEAKS
    Result[String,i64]  reassigned to Err       38 B / 1 object    LEAKS
    Option[String]      reassigned to Some(x)   38 B / 1 object    LEAKS
    Option[D], D{s:String}                      clean              CONTROL
    plain `String` var  reassigned              clean              CONTROL

The two controls are what make this a narrow, findable hole rather than a
general one. A plain `String` binding DOES get a displacement free
(`lhs_is_tracked_vec` in the `StmtKind::Assign` arm of `stmts.rs`), and an
`Option` whose payload is a heap-bearing STRUCT is fine too. It is
specifically the BARE `String`/`Vec` payload inside `Option`/`Result` that
has no arm.

MINIMAL SHAPE -- no alias, no match, no loop:

    let mut vv: Option[String] = Some(f"payload-{env.args().len()}-aaaa....");
    vv = Option.None;

THE BODIES ARE FINE; ONLY THE MEMORY LEAKS. Verified separately with a user
`impl Drop` on the payload: interp, JIT and AOT all print the displaced
value's body exactly once, in the right place, before the store. So the
fault is entirely on the memory side and a fix must not touch the bodies
channel.

WHERE IT IS. The eager-free ladder in the `StmtKind::Assign` arm
(`src/codegen/stmts.rs`) has arms for Vec/String vars, Map/Set vars, struct
vars, Tensor vars, user value-enum vars, and (B-2026-08-07-4) BOXED
`Option`/`Result` payloads. The INLINE `Option`/`Result` payload has only a
BODIES walk, B-2026-08-02-25's `__karac_dropelems_opt_*`, whose doc states
the reason it is bodies-only:

    "the displaced payload's memory is already reclaimed by the untouched
     FreeInlineOptionPayload / BoxedEnumDrop action -- the pre-fix shape
     leaked nothing under LSan -- so a memory call here would double-free."

That claim is false for this population, and the same doc's own later
paragraph already records the boxed half of the correction ("True for the
INLINE payload it was measured on; NOT true for a boxed one"). The
measurements above say the inline half is wrong too: the scope-exit
`FreeInlineOptionPayload` reads the slot AFTER the store, so it only ever
frees the LAST value.

THE HAZARD THE DOC NAMES IS REAL AND MUST BE RESPECTED. A memory call added
naively here would double-free wherever an arm has already taken the
payload out -- the same shape B-2026-08-28-75's `if let` half was about.
Any fix wants the armed test the neighbouring value-enum arm uses
(`has_armed_container_elem_bodies`) plus the self-alias and
RHS-mentions-LHS guards its siblings carry, and a boundary row for a
DISCARDED destination.

FIXED by 98bddee. `emit_inline_optres_payload_overwrite_free`
(`src/codegen/runtime.rs`), called from the `StmtKind::Assign` arm immediately
after B-2026-08-02-25's displaced-payload BODIES walk.

THE FIX IS THE INLINE HALF OF A CORRECTION ALREADY HALF-MADE. B-2026-08-02-25
added the bodies walk at this exact site and wrote down why it stopped there:

    BODIES ONLY, and deliberately so: the displaced payload's memory is
    already reclaimed by the untouched `FreeInlineOptionPayload` /
    `BoxedEnumDrop` action -- the pre-fix shape leaked nothing under LSan,
    it only lost the body -- so a memory call here would double-free.

B-2026-08-07-4 found that false for a BOXED payload and added the boxed eager
free, appending to that same comment: "True for the INLINE payload it was
measured on; NOT true for a boxed one." This row is that sentence's other half
-- it is not true for the inline payload either, and for exactly the reason the
boxed row gives: the scope-exit action re-reads the slot AFTER the store, so it
frees only the LAST value.

WHY THE ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT SAID "leaked nothing". Not investigated to a
conclusion, and worth saying so rather than guessing. What IS established is
that the claim does not hold for any of the six inline shapes measured here,
at either optimization level, on a tree with that row's own fix in it.

THE IMPLEMENTATION RE-EMITS THE BINDING'S OWN QUEUED ACTION rather than
hand-rolling a free -- the same technique, and the same three reasons, as its
boxed sibling `emit_boxed_enum_overwrite_free`: the tag guard comes along (a
`None` slot frees nothing, a `Result` frees only the live side), the `Option`
and `Result` variants share one walk, and THE QUEUE IS THE ARMED SET. That last
one is what makes the hazard structural rather than predicated: an arm that
took the payload out has already zeroed the source's tag, and a binding whose
registration was retracted has no action to find at all.

That mattered here. Four shapes hand the payload to a destination that then
owns it -- a `match` tail, an `if let` tail, a consuming `while let`, and the
`Result` spelling -- and all four were CLEAN before this change. A naive free
would have double-freed every one of them. They are pinned as hazard rows in
the fixture and are clean before and after.

THE CALL SITE IS OUTSIDE THE BODIES ARM'S `optres_var_payload_tes` LOOKUP, and
that placement is load-bearing rather than incidental. That map is the BODIES
channel's registration -- it records a payload type whose user `Drop` needs
walking -- and a bare `String`/`Vec` payload has no user `Drop` at all. Nesting
the memory call inside that lookup would have skipped every shape this row is
about, which is the shape of mistake that produced the row in the first place.

    Result[String,i64]  -> Ok(x)      38 B / 1     now clean

    plain `String` binding            clean before AND after   AXIS

MEASURED (KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, ASAN + LSan; runtime-derived payload, read via
`contains` so the buffer is live):

    struct Wide { a: String, b: i64, c: i64, d: i64, e: i64 }

    let value: Result[Option[Wide], i64] = Ok(Some(Wide { a: <44 B>, .. }));
    let mut vv = value;            // moved in
    <read the payload through a borrow-only arm>
    vv = Ok(Option.None);          // 38 B / 1 object LEAKED

    ... and the same without the alias:

    let mut vv: Result[Option[Wide], i64] = Ok(Some(Wide { .. }));
    vv = Ok(Option.None);          // 38 B / 1 object LEAKED, identically

BOTH SPELLINGS LEAK THE SAME AMOUNT, which is what separates this from
B-2026-08-28-75. That row was about the MOVED-IN population specifically
(direct-init was already correct there); here the provenance makes no
difference, so the missing work is not the eager free's gate.

WHAT LEAKS IS THE INTERIOR, NOT THE ENVELOPE. 38 bytes is the `Wide.a`
`String` alone -- the box itself is reclaimed. So the displaced-box free
(`emit_boxed_enum_overwrite_free`) fires and does its job for the
`NestedBoxedEnumDrop` action, and the box's own interior walk is either
absent or not reaching one level further down. The `nested_boxed_payload_vars`
population is deliberately kept out of the move-suppression rules
(payload_vars.rs documents why: no destination takes a NESTED box over), so
whatever owns the inner `String` has to be found on the drop side rather
than the move side.

NOT ATTEMPTED. B-2026-08-28-75 established, with measurements, that adding a
free on this axis without its matching retraction turns a leak into a
heap-use-after-free; the nested population has its own separate
non-suppression rule, so the same care is owed here and it is a different
day's work.

SOURCE NOTE: found while narrowing B-2026-08-28-75 -- probe `h6` in that
investigation's hazard matrix, the one row that stayed RED both before and
after the fix.

RE-SCOPED AND RE-MEASURED 2026-08-29, and the filing's framing was wrong in the
same way B-2026-08-28-75's was: reassignment is INCIDENTAL. The trigger is the
TYPE, not the statement. `let vv: Result[Option[Wide], i64] = Ok(Some(Wide{..}));`
followed by nothing at all leaks the same 38 bytes as the version that stores to
it. The filing also called the moved-in/direct-init agreement "what separates
this from -75" — true, and the reason is simply that neither has anything to do
with a store.

FULL TABLE, measured at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 under ASAN+LSan against c1f8847,
payload runtime-derived through `env.args().len()` and read via `contains` so
the buffer stays live. 18 leaking shapes, 5 clean:

  OUTER `Option`
    Option[Option[String]]              38 B / 1     build + drop, nothing else
    Option[Option[Vec[i64]]]            80 B / 1
    Option[Option[Narrow{a:String}]]    38 B / 1
    Option[Option[Wide]]                38 B / 1
    Option[Result[Wide, i64]]           94 B / 2     (a Wide box AND its String)
  OUTER `Result`
    Result[Option[String], i64]         38 B / 1
    Result[Option[Option[String]], i64] 38 B / 1     (no arm binding the leaf)
    Result[Option[Wide], i64]           38 B / 1     the row's own shape
      ... same 38 B via: moved-in alias; direct init; store to Ok(None);
          store to Err; self-assign; returned from a fn; discarded temp;
          and 190 B / 5 over a 4-iteration loop
    Result[Option[Wide], i64] with an arm binding the `Wide` out   38 B / 1

  CLEAN (the axes, and they are what make this narrow)
    Option[Wide]                        flat, one level  -- always correct
    Result[Wide, i64]                   flat, one level  -- always correct
    Result[Option[Option[String]], i64] WITH an arm binding the String out
    Result[Option[Wide], i64] whose arm hands the payload out, then a store
    (a `shared` payload rides RC and was never in scope)

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING. Read out of the IR for `Option[Option[String]]` beside
the flat `Option[String]`, one function each. The flat case emits the payload's
`{ptr,len,cap}` free at scope exit (`optpl.some` -> `optpl.free` ->
`karac_free_buf`). The nested case emits `free(box)` and NOTHING ELSE: no
interior walk exists for the box at all.

Two distinct registrations are involved and both decline for the same reason:

  * `BoxedEnumDrop` (outer `Option`): `track_boxed_enum_var` resolves
    `inner_drop_fn` from a user struct/enum NAME
    (`emit_struct_drop_synthesis(n).or_else(|| emit_enum_drop_switch(n))`).
    A boxed `Option[..]`/`Result[..]` contents is neither, so the name is
    `None` and the box gets no interior drop. Where the contents' own payload
    boxes again, `track_boxed_enum_var_with_chain` takes over and
    `emit_nested_box_chain_free` walks ENVELOPES only -- by construction it
    frees boxes and never touches the leaf.
  * `NestedBoxedEnumDrop` (outer `Result`, where the inline payload area is 5
    words so an `Option[Wide]` fits inside it and only the `Wide` boxes):
    box-only by design, with one narrow exception (`inner_payload_free`,
    B-2026-08-12-18) admitting an `Option` contents whose payload is a direct
    `{ptr,len,cap}`. INSTRUMENTED: for `Result[Option[Wide], i64]` the let-site
    passes `box_contents: None` for this ("DIRECT") half, so even a widened
    resolver sees nothing to resolve. Only the struct-FIELD half carries a
    contents type.

A FIX WAS BUILT AND IS MEASURED WRONG. Recorded in full because the failure is
the specification.

The change: read `inner_drop_fn` as the drop for the value at the BOTTOM of the
envelope chain rather than for the box at hand (with no chain the two coincide,
so every single-box registration stays byte-identical), resolve it from the
contents' TypeExpr via `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr` instead of from a type
name, add a `nested_box_leaf_contents` walk to name that bottom, and hand it to
`emit_nested_box_chain_free` to apply just before the innermost `free`.

It fixed six shapes -- every outer-`Option` row above -- and left the outer-
`Result` rows untouched (the `box_contents: None` finding). Then the full -O0
suite found what the probes could not:

    asan_direct_boxed_enum_chain_frees_every_envelope        DOUBLE FREE
    asan_struct_field_boxed_heapless_option_envelope_owned   DOUBLE FREE

The first is decisive. Its `let c: Option[Option[Option[String]]]` is matched
with `Some(Some(Some(s)))`, and that arm's binding ALREADY owns and frees the
String -- so an unconditional leaf drop frees it twice. This is the same
counter-example the let-site's own comment records ("implemented and measured
WRONG ... aborts with a glibc double free at BOTH opt levels"), which had been
read as applying only to the `Result` half; it applies to both.

WHAT A CORRECT FIX NEEDS, which is now specified rather than guessed:

  1. The interior drop must be RETRACTED when an arm consumes the leaf --
     the `suppress_boxed_payload_view_move` mechanism (walk the queued actions,
     set the drop field to `None`) is the right instrument and is one screenful.
  2. It must distinguish binding the LEAF from binding an INTERMEDIATE
     ENVELOPE, and that is the hard part. A coarse "the pattern binds any name"
     rule was tried on paper and un-fixes half the table: `match vv { Some(o) =>
     match o { Some(w) => .. } }` binds `o`, an envelope, and that binding does
     NOT take over the leaf -- verified, since those rows leak today.
  3. `box_contents` must be plumbed through the `NestedBoxedEnumDrop` DIRECT
     half before any of it can reach the outer-`Result` rows.
  4. Ownership genuinely varies by arm shape, so the classifier has to be
     measured against at least these three: an arm binding the leaf String out
     (arm owns it -- clean today), an arm binding a leaf STRUCT out and passing
     it to an owned param (nobody owns it -- leaks today, 38 B), and no arm at
     all (nobody owns it -- leaks today).

NOT LANDED, and nothing source-side was committed. A partial fix here converts
leaks into double frees, which is strictly worse, and the two fixtures above are
the proof rather than a worry. No regression fixture accompanies this row: the
shapes fail at -O0 AND some at -O2, so a red fixture would break the default leg
as well as the quarantined one.

SEVERITY RAISED low -> medium. The filing scoped this to one exotic type under
reassignment; it is every doubly-nested `Option`/`Result` over a heap payload,
leaking on construction alone, including `Option[Option[String]]`.

NARROWED 2026-08-29 to the outer-`Option` half, which is what the fix closes.
The outer-`Result` spelling is the same defect reached through
`NestedBoxedEnumDrop` rather than `BoxedEnumDrop`, and its direct registration
passes `box_contents: None`, so it needs work this fix does not do; it is split
to B-2026-08-29-18 with the measurements above rather than left buried here.
fix:
FIXED by c876e64, in two halves that are useless apart -- register the
missing drop, and retract it wherever an arm already owns what it would free.

HALF 1, THE MISSING DROP. `inner_drop_fn` on a `BoxedEnumDrop` is now read as
the drop for the value at the BOTTOM of the envelope chain rather than for the
box at hand. With no chain the bottom IS that box, so every pre-existing
single-box registration is byte-identical; with a chain,
`emit_nested_box_chain_free` applies it just before the innermost `free`. The
two used to be mutually exclusive by `debug_assert`, and that exclusion was half
the bug: the chain walks ENVELOPES by construction, so nothing ever freed the
leaf's own heap. The let site resolves it from the contents' TYPE EXPR
(`vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr`) instead of from a user type NAME, which is
what the name-keyed resolution could never answer for a boxed
`Option[..]`/`Result[..]`.

HALF 2, THE RETRACTION, and it is the half that makes half 1 shippable. An arm
written `Some(Some(s))` binds the leaf out and already owns and frees it, so the
box's drop has to stand down. `retract_boxed_leaf_drop_for_consuming_pattern`
walks the queued actions and clears the field, the same instrument
`suppress_boxed_payload_view_move` uses. Without it this change is not a fix but
a DOUBLE FREE: half 1 alone makes
`asan_direct_boxed_enum_chain_frees_every_envelope` and
`asan_struct_field_boxed_heapless_option_envelope_owned` abort under ASAN. That
is the counter-example the let site's own comment records ("implemented and
measured WRONG ... aborts with a glibc double free at BOTH opt levels"), which
had been read as applying only to the `Result` half; it applies to both.

DEPTH IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY, and both halves of the rule are measurements
rather than reasoning.

  * A coarse "the pattern binds any name" rule is wrong in the expensive
    direction. `match vv { Some(o) => ... }` binds an intermediate ENVELOPE, and
    that binding does NOT take the leaf over -- so retracting there puts the
    whole family straight back to leaking. `boxed_leaf_owning_depth` records how
    deep an owner would have to bind (1 for the contents, plus one per envelope,
    plus one more because the drop frees the leaf's payload), and only a binding
    at exactly that depth retracts. A wildcard at that depth names no owner at
    all, so `Some(Some(_))` keeps the box armed.

  * A STRUCT or ENUM leaf takes NO retraction, which is the second half and was
    forced by a failing row rather than foreseen. There the drop is the leaf
    type's field synthesis, so a pattern binding at leaf depth binds the struct
    HEADER, and an arm that does so does NOT take the fields' heap over --
    verified, because `match vv { Some(Some(w)) => wl(w), _ => 0 }` over
    `Option[Option[Wide]]` leaks on an unmodified tree, so nobody owns it and
    retracting would only preserve that leak. `boxed_leaf_owning_depth` returns
    `None` for those leaves. Retracting solely where the leaf is an
    `Option`/`Result` -- whose drop frees the payload the pattern literally
    names -- is what lets `leaf-bound-string` and `leaf-bound-wide` both be
    clean at once.

MEASURED at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, ASAN + LSan, payload runtime-derived through
`env.args().len()`:

    Option[Option[String]]              38 B / 1   -> clean   build + drop only
    Option[Option[Vec[i64]]]            80 B / 1   -> clean
    Option[Option[Wide]]                38 B / 1   -> clean
    Option[Option[Narrow{a:String}]]    38 B / 1   -> clean
    Option[Result[Wide, i64]]           94 B / 2   -> clean   (box AND String)
    ... via an ENVELOPE bind, `Some(o) => match o {..}`
                                        38 B / 1   -> clean
    ... via a leaf WILDCARD, `Some(Some(_))`
                                        38 B / 1   -> clean

    HAZARDS -- clean BEFORE and after, red only if the retraction stops firing
    `Some(Some(s))` / the triple / the `if let` / the struct leaf   all clean

    AXES -- one level, and a POD leaf: correct before and after

COVERAGE. `memory_sanitizer::asan_nested_option_envelope_frees_its_leaf_payload`,
13 rows. `-O0` ONLY, and the fixture says so: every leaking row builds a nested
envelope and drops it, and at `-O2` the whole local non-escaping structure is
scalarized and the box `malloc` removed, so there is no allocation left to leak
-- verified GREEN at `-O2` against the unfixed compiler. Unlike the two
preceding rows' fixtures no read placement recovers that, because the reading
rows are exactly the hazard rows, which are clean either way.
`asan_direct_boxed_enum_chain_frees_every_envelope` states the same limitation
for the same family, and `scripts/asan-o0-leg.sh` is the gate for both. Which
rows carry which signal was measured PER ROW against the unfixed tree rather
than assumed -- `envelope-bind` and `leaf-wildcard` turned out to be red unfixed
and are therefore fixed rows as well as depth-rule pins.

THE OUTER-`Result` SPELLING IS NOT FIXED and is split to B-2026-08-29-18. Its
`NestedBoxedEnumDrop` DIRECT registration passes `box_contents: None` at the let
site -- instrumented -- so there is nothing for this resolver to see, and it
needs the contents plumbed plus its own ownership story before the same
treatment applies. Measured unchanged by this fix.

FILING NOTE: the row was filed as a reassignment bug and re-scoped twice. It has
nothing to do with reassignment -- the trigger is the TYPE, and construction
alone is enough.

title: A GENERIC method that UNCONDITIONALLY returns its owned param still runs the param's `Drop` body TWICE on all three compiled backends against once in the interpreter -- the monomorph path does not reach the method-argument stand-down that B-2026-08-28-70 added
detail:
The residue of B-2026-08-28-70, which fixed the non-generic half of both
directions and the generic DYING half, but not this one.

MEASURED, body counts interp / jit / build / build with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, on
277621a (the -70 fix commit):

    struct R { id: i64, tag: String }
    impl Drop for R { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"drop {self.id}"); } }
    struct G1 { n: i64 }
    impl G1 { fn gm_ret[T](ref self, r: R, t: T) -> R { r } }

      let h = G1 { n: 1 };
      let b = h.gm_ret(R { id: 32, tag: "h" }, 5);   println(f"{b.id}")

        interp:            32 / drop 32              1 body   CORRECT
        jit / build / np:  drop 32 / 32 / drop 32    2 bodies

The NON-generic twin of the same program is correct at one body on all four
surfaces since -70 (`fn id(ref self, r: R) -> R { r }`), and so is the
free-function oracle `fn id2(r: R) -> R { r }`, which is what fixes one as the
right answer.

The generic DYING direction was fixed by the same commit and is the control that
localizes this: `fn gm_dies[T](ref self, r: R, t: T) -> i64 { 3 }` went from zero
bodies in the interpreter to one on all four surfaces. So the generic method
path is not wholly untouched -- only the caller's STAND-DOWN half misses.

WHY. -70 put the stand-down in `codegen/method_call.rs`'s argument loop, gated
on resolving the callee through `find_function_ast`. A generic method is
compiled through the monomorph path (`codegen/mono.rs` has its own argument
loop, which consults `call_arg_flows_into_return` under a mono key), so the
site -70 fixed is not the site this call goes through. The predicate
`fn_always_returns_param` that -70 added is generic-agnostic and would answer
correctly here; it is simply not asked. Note -70 DOES admit generics on its
stand-down leg deliberately -- that leg needs no callee cooperation -- so this
is a reachability gap, not a policy decision.

NOT the same as B-2026-08-28-71, which is about the CALLEE-side flip
(`compile_mono_function`'s param slot holding something the bodies-only walker
misreads, printing a corrupted name). This row is caller-side only and needs no
callee registration: the result binding is already the owner, the caller merely
has to stop firing. The two share the monomorph path and nothing else.

NOT a memory defect: bodies only, valgrind clean at `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0` on the
non-generic twin of this shape, consistent with the rest of this family.

WHAT CLOSING IT NEEDS: ask the same two predicates at the monomorph argument
loop that `method_call.rs` now asks, with that loop's own param-index
convention established by instrumentation first -- the conventions differ per
site in this area (a lowered `Type.method` carries `self` at param 0, the raw
AST method does not), and -70 had to verify both by instrumentation because two
comments in one file disagreed about which applied.

SOURCE NOTE: found while probing the generic shapes of B-2026-08-28-70 before
assuming the non-generic result generalized. Measured on 277621a; no code change
was made for this row.
fix:
FIXED by 7f5d6f9, by asking the monomorph argument loop the same stand-down
question the non-generic method-argument site asks.

The row's diagnosis was right and its "WHAT CLOSING IT NEEDS" was followed
literally, including the warning to establish the loop's param-index convention
by instrumentation first. That warning earned its place: the index at this site
is RECEIVER-INCLUSIVE (a two-parameter method iterates i = 0, 1, 2, the receiver
occupying 0) while `find_function_ast` hands back the raw AST method whose
`params` exclude the receiver -- the OPPOSITE of the sibling loop in
`method_call.rs`, where `i` already counts from the first real argument.
Instrumentation also settled that a generic method reaches this loop under a
plain `Type.method` key rather than a mono-suffixed one, so
`find_function_ast` resolves it directly.

Only the ALWAYS-returns leg is admitted for a generic callee, exactly as the row
anticipated: `fn_always_returns_param` needs no callee cooperation, while the
conditional leg would hand ownership to a callee-side flip
`compile_mono_function` declines for generics (B-2026-08-28-71), leaving nobody
owning the body.

VERIFIED for leaks, not only body counts. A caller stand-down is a LEAK rather
than a wrong line of output if the callee genuinely entry-copies and two buffers
exist, and no body-count fixture would see it; valgrind at
`KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0` is balanced on the fixed shape and on the surrounding
method matrix.

A GENERIC CONDITIONAL case was drafted for the fixtures and REMOVED, which is
the one thing this row did not settle. Measured on the fix commit, all four
surfaces:

    generic method, param DIES      interp 0 / compiled 1
    generic method, param ESCAPES   interp 1 / compiled 2
    generic FREE FN, param dies     0 / 0   (the documented -22 trade)
    generic FREE FN, param escapes  1 / 1   correct

So that shape is divergent in BOTH directions and cannot be settled without the
flip B-2026-08-28-71 covers. Pinning it in a fixture would pin one backend's
defect as expected output, so it is filed on its own row with these four
measurements instead. Note this also refutes a line in B-2026-08-28-70's
reasoning -- that a generic conditional param is "the one shape this frame must
NOT claim" because codegen's caller keeps firing. Codegen's caller does fire,
and the interpreter claiming nothing is exactly what makes the dying direction
diverge; the two do not cancel.

FIXTURES in both suites, RED-verified against the pre-fix compiler (`drop 32` /
`32` / `drop 32` against `32` / `drop 32`), carrying the generic DYING
direction plus the non-generic method twin and the free-function twin as
controls -- the two oracles that make one body the right answer.

Gates: codegen 3399, memory_sanitizer 1305, interpreter 1815, non-llvm suite all
green; fmt clean; clippy clean on both feature legs.

title: A METHOD that hands an inline `Option`/`Result` argument back DOUBLE-FREES the payload on all three compiled backends (glibc abort, valgrind `Invalid free()`, 10 allocs against 11 frees) while the interpreter and the free-function twin are clean -- `call_passthrough_armed_source` matches `ExprKind::Call` only, so no ownership alias is recorded and the result binding registers a second owner of the source's buffer. NOTE: this row was FILED asserting an off-by-one on the argument index; that root cause was measured and REFUTED -- see the fix prose
detail:
A run-vs-build DOUBLE FREE, not merely a body-count divergence. The interpreter
is correct; every compiled backend aborts.

MEASURED, on 277621a and identically on its parent (pre-existing, NOT introduced
by B-2026-08-28-70 -- verified by re-measuring with that commit's `src` stashed):

    struct Bx { n: i64 }
    impl Bx { fn take(ref self, o: Option[String]) -> Option[String] { o } }

      let b = Bx { n: 1 };
      let s = f"heap-payload-{b.n}";
      let src = Option.Some(s);
      let out = b.take(src);
      match out { Option.Some(v) => { println(f"got {v}"); } Option.None => { println("none"); } }

        interp:            `got heap-payload-1`                     CORRECT
        jit / build / np:  `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`

    valgrind, KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0:
        Invalid free() / delete / delete[] / realloc()
        ERROR SUMMARY: 1 errors from 1 contexts

The f-string payload matters: a string LITERAL is rodata with `cap == 0` and is
never freed, so it cannot witness this. Note also that `karac build` at the
default -O2 must be run for the abort to be reliable -- and that a `karac`
binary built WITHOUT `--features llvm` silently falls back to type-check and
prints "All checks passed", which is how this nearly went unnoticed.

ROOT CAUSE, read directly rather than inferred. In `codegen/method_call.rs`'s
argument loop, `pidx = i + 1` is the RECEIVER-INCLUSIVE index and is correct for
`ref_flags` and for `callee_optres_param_entry_copied`, which subtracts one for
an impl method. The inline Option/Result move-suppression gate alongside them
does NOT subtract:

    let arg_flows_into_return = self.program_snapshot.as_deref()
        .and_then(|p| super::declarations::find_function_ast(p, &qualified))
        .is_some_and(|f| crate::ast::fn_returns_param(f, pidx));

`find_function_ast` returns the RAW AST method, whose `params` EXCLUDE the
receiver -- confirmed by instrumentation during B-2026-08-28-70 (`B2.pick` ->
`self_param=true params=["r", "k"]`). So for the first real argument (`i = 0`,
`pidx = 1`) the predicate answers about the SECOND parameter, or about nothing at
all when the method has only one -- `params.get(1)` is `None`, so
`fn_returns_param` returns false. `arg_flows_into_return` is then wrongly false,
`suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move` runs, the caller's source slot is
zeroed as a MOVE -- and the comment on that very gate says why that is wrong
here: it is "gated OUT of a return-passthrough (`fn take(mut ref self, o) ->
Option { o }` -- the callee hands `o` back and the caller's RESULT binding owns
it, so the source must stay live)". The gate is present and correct in
intent; it just never fires, because the index it asks on is off by one.

The sibling comment two dozen lines above already flags the discrepancy without
resolving it -- it notes that this call "is the odd one out on this key" -- so
the two indexing conventions in this loop were known to disagree and the
disagreement was documented rather than settled.

WHAT CLOSING IT NEEDS: pass the receiver-EXCLUDING index (`i`) to
`fn_returns_param` here, matching what `find_function_ast` hands back and what
the neighbouring `call_arg_moves_into_outliving_place` call already uses; or
route it through a helper that subtracts like
`callee_optres_param_entry_copied` does. Both are one line. What the fix needs
beyond that is a RED-verified ASAN fixture and a sweep of the OTHER shapes this
channel covers (`Result`, boxed enum payloads, `mut ref self` receivers, a
method with two or more args where the off-by-one silently reads a real
neighbouring param rather than falling off the end -- that case may answer TRUE
wrongly and suppress a move that should happen, which is the leak direction of
the same bug and has not been probed).

SOURCE NOTE: predicted by reading the argument loop while fixing
B-2026-08-28-70, then reproduced. The row is filed rather than folded into that
fix because it is a distinct channel (inline Option/Result payload memory, not
the user-`Drop` body) with a distinct failure mode and deserves its own
fixtures.
fix:
FIXED by 8d8d1b4, by recording the PASSTHROUGH ALIAS for a method call.

THIS ROW'S STATED ROOT CAUSE WAS WRONG, and correcting it is the first thing to
record. The row asserted an off-by-one: that the method argument loop asks
`fn_returns_param` with a receiver-INCLUSIVE `pidx` against an AST whose params
exclude the receiver, disabling the return-passthrough carve-out on the inline
Option/Result move suppression. The REPRODUCTION was real and is unchanged; the
MECHANISM was inferred from reading and then written up as though measured.

It is refuted directly. Fixing the index -- confirmed reaching the site and
flipping the predicate from false to true by instrumentation -- changed NOTHING:
every shape still aborted. Instrumenting the whole gate shows why:

    [dbg94] gate Bx.take i=0 flows=true entry_copied=true suppress=false

`entry_copied` is TRUE, so `!arg_flows_into_return && entry_copied.is_none()` is
false whatever the first term says. The suppression never fires for this shape,
with or without the index fix, so it cannot be the cause. The clinching control:
the failing program and a CLEAN one (same call, result never consumed) produce
BYTE-IDENTICAL gate state, which localizes the defect away from the argument
side entirely. The index change was reverted; it is a real latent inconsistency
with no observed symptom, noted below rather than filed.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE, and it is the same structural pattern as B-2026-08-28-70: a
mechanism built for free functions that method calls never reach.
`call_passthrough_armed_source` (control_flow_match.rs) tests `ExprKind::Call`
alone. A method call therefore records no `passthrough_owner_alias`, so the
result binding registers its OWN inline-payload owner while the source stays
armed, and both free the same buffer once the result is consumed.

MEASURED, on the parent of this fix:

    impl Bx { fn take(ref self, o: Option[String]) -> Option[String] { o } }
      let src = Option.Some(f"heap-{b.n}");
      let out = b.take(src);
      match out { Option.Some(v) => { println(f"got {v}"); } ... }

        interp:            `got heap-1`   10 allocs, 10 frees, clean
        jit / build / np:  `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`
                           valgrind `Invalid free()`, 10 allocs, 11 frees

    free-function twin:    clean on all four, 10 allocs, 10 frees

The EQUAL ALLOCATION COUNT is the load-bearing measurement. It rules out the
entry-copy story the gate's own comments would suggest: nothing makes a second
buffer, so the two bindings genuinely alias and exactly one may own it. Reached
only after correcting the oracle -- an earlier comparison used `f"heap-1"`, a
literal with no interpolation, which is rodata with `cap == 0` and is never
freed, so it silently tested nothing and made the free function look
distinguishable for the wrong reason.

Shapes confirmed fixed, all four surfaces byte-identical and valgrind-balanced:
one argument handed back; two arguments with the FIRST returned; two with the
SECOND returned (together these pin that the alias follows the argument the
callee actually returns rather than a fixed position); `mut ref self`;
`Result[String, i64]`; and a no-passthrough control whose freshly produced
payload must NOT be aliased.

THE FIX IS TWO EDITS, and the second is the one that mattered. Widening the
matcher alone changed nothing, because the `let`-site that records the alias
(stmts.rs) is itself gated on the RHS being an `ExprKind::Call`, with the
`.map` passthrough shapes admitted one at a time. The method shape is admitted
the same way. That the first edit was a measurable no-op is what located the
second.

SCOPE, and this is a real remainder: the `let`-bound spelling only. The
INLINE-SCRUTINEE form `match b.take(s) { .. }` also double-frees -- but so does
its FREE-FUNCTION twin `match takef(s) { .. }`, identically, at baseline and
after this fix. That is a different and wider defect, not a method-path gap, and
is filed as B-2026-08-29-6 rather than folded in here. It was found only because
the ASAN fixture was first written in the inline form, after every shape had
already passed individually in the `let`-bound one.

NOTED, NOT FILED: the `fn_returns_param(f, pidx)` index in the method argument
loop is genuinely inconsistent with its neighbours -- `find_function_ast`
returns params excluding the receiver, the sibling
`callee_optres_param_entry_copied` subtracts one for an impl method, and this
call does not. It is masked today by `entry_copied` on every shape probed, so it
has no observable symptom and no test could pin it; changing it would be an
unverifiable behaviour change. Recorded here so the next reader of that loop
does not have to re-derive it.

FIXTURES in all three suites, RED-verified against the pre-fix compiler: the
ASAN twin aborts, the codegen cases return empty output where the process died,
and the interpreter cases are CONTROLS -- that backend was already correct, so
they pin that codegen moved onto its answer rather than both moving. Each
carries a no-passthrough control, so a fix that aliased unconditionally would
strand the fresh payload with no owner at all.

Gates: codegen 3393, memory_sanitizer 1300, interpreter 1811, non-llvm suite all
green; fmt clean; clippy clean on both feature legs. Re-verified after rebasing
onto 98bddee, which touches the same inline Option/Result payload area.

title: A DISCARDED BRANCH CONSTRUCT STRANDS WHATEVER ITS TAKEN ARM HANDS OUT -- `if let Some(s) = vv { s };` in statement position leaks the whole 38 B buffer with NO reassignment anywhere in the program, and so do `match`, a struct payload, and (the half the row was filed too narrow to name) a plain `if seed() > 0 { a } else { b };` over two ordinary locals with no pattern and no payload in sight; binding the payload and USING it is clean, so it is the hand-out-into-nothing that leaks
detail:
SPLIT OUT OF B-2026-08-29-1, where it turned up as a control row that failed
for an unrelated reason. It has nothing to do with reassignment: the store the
control carried is not needed, and removing it changes nothing.

PRE-EXISTING AND INDEPENDENT. Measured byte-identical at 93dbc48, at d5c4606
(B-2026-08-28-75's fix) and at c1f8847, and unchanged by B-2026-08-29-1's fix.

MEASURED (KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, ASAN + LSan; runtime-derived payload via
`env.args().len()` so nothing folds):

    let vv: Option[String] = Some(<38 B>);
    if let Some(s) = vv { s };                    38 B / 1 object   LEAKS

    match vv { Some(s) => s, None => "zz".to_string() };
