title: A METHOD whose owned param is conditionally returned via a `match` ARM loses the param's `Drop` body in the INTERPRETER on the DYING path -- interp `got 9`/`drop z` vs all three compiled backends `drop h`/`got 9`/`drop z`; identical for the generic and non-generic spelling, and the free-function twin is correct everywhere
detail:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING B-2026-08-29-16, as one cell of the 16-cell spelling matrix
run to bound what that fix actually reached. -16 fixed the if/else BLOCK-TAIL
spelling of "conditionally returns its owned param"; this is the `match` spelling
of the same shape, on the DYING path, and it is still divergent.

    struct R { id: i64, tag: String }
    impl Drop for R { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"drop {self.tag}"); } }
    struct G { n: i64 }
    impl G {
        fn nmat(ref self, r: R, k: i64) -> R
            { match k { 1 => { r } _ => { R { id: 9, tag: f"z" } } } }
        fn gmat[T](ref self, r: R, k: i64, t: T) -> R
            { match k { 1 => { r } _ => { R { id: 9, tag: f"z" } } } }
    }
    fn main() {
        let g = G { n: 1 };
        let h: R = g.nmat(R { id: 7, tag: f"h" }, 0);   // DYING path
        println(f"got {h.id}");
    }

MEASURED at 59df774, all five surfaces (interp / LLJIT / AOT / AOT with
KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 / AOT at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0):

      interp   -> `got 9` / `drop z`                ZERO bodies for R{7}
      jit      -> `drop h` / `got 9` / `drop z`     ONE     CORRECT
      build    -> same as jit
      nopar    -> same as jit
      O0       -> same as jit

Exactly one `R{7}` is constructed and it reaches nobody, so one body is due and
the compiled backends have it. The interpreter loses it.

BOTH the generic and the NON-generic method spelling behave this way, identically
-- so this is not a generics gap and B-2026-08-28-71 is not the missing piece. The
ESCAPING direction of the same two methods is correct on every surface (`got 8` /
`drop i`), so this is the dying direction only.

THE FREE-FUNCTION TWIN IS CORRECT on all five surfaces, generic and non-generic
alike (`drop p` / `got 9` / `drop z`), which is what makes one body the established
answer here rather than a preference, and points at the interpreter's METHOD path
specifically -- the same asymmetry B-2026-08-28-70 addressed for the if/else
spelling.

LIKELY SHAPE OF THE FIX: `method_param_drop_names` hands a conditionally-returned
param to the per-path flag rather than claiming it, and the flag is not being armed
or cleared for a `match`-arm exit on the method path, so nobody ends up owning the
body. The free-function path claims it and is right, which is the useful contrast.

NOT a memory defect: bodies only. Valgrind at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 over the matrix is
balanced with zero errors.

SOURCE NOTE: cells 3 and 7 of the matrix recorded in B-2026-08-29-16's close.

CLOSED INVALID 2026-08-29, the same day it was filed, by the session that filed
it. THE PREMISE IS MISATTRIBUTED. The behaviour is real but it is not about the
`match` spelling: the repro program above gives `nmat` and `gmat` the SAME
parameter name `r`, and the interpreter's `moved_out_user_drop_bindings` is keyed
by bare name with no frame qualifier, so the mark left by an earlier ESCAPING call
silenced the later DYING one. That is B-2026-08-29-11, which is open and carries
the measurements.

Re-measured with distinct parameter names, at the commit this row was filed
against: the `match` spelling is CORRECT on all five surfaces in both directions,
for the generic and non-generic method alike. An isolated dying call was correct
even with the names reused -- it takes a preceding escaping call to show anything,
which is precisely the -11 signature and not a property of `match`.

Filed off a 16-cell probe matrix in which every callee reused one parameter name.
Varying the names is what refuted it. No fix is needed for this row; the residual
it pointed at is tracked by B-2026-08-29-11.

title: A VALUE-POSITION BLOCK OR BRANCH WHOSE TAIL MINTS A FRESH OWNED TEMP LEAKS IT WHEN THE CONSUMER IS A METHOD RECEIVER OR A CALL ARGUMENT -- `if c { mk(n) } else { mk(n+1) }.contains("x")` strands 36 B, and so do the `match` spelling, a BARE BLOCK `{ mk(n) }.contains("x")` with no branch in it at all, and `use_it(if c { mk(n) } else { mk(n+1) })`; the same call unwrapped is clean, so it is the block/arm hand-out into a non-registering consumer that leaks
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while narrowing B-2026-08-29-5, and deliberately left out
of its fix. That row is about a branch whose value is DISCARDED; here the
value IS consumed -- by a method receiver, or by a call argument -- so every
mechanism that row added is correctly inert on this one. Measured
byte-identical before and after a86e5d1, on all four spellings.

MEASURED (KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, valgrind, runtime-derived payload via
`env.args().len()` so nothing folds; `mk(n) -> String` returns a 36 B buffer):

    let b = if n > 0 { mk(n) } else { mk(n+1) }.contains("payload");
                                                  36 B / 1 object   LEAKS
    let b = match n { 1 => mk(n), _ => mk(n+1) }.contains("payload");
                                                  36 B / 1 object   LEAKS
    let b = { mk(n) }.contains("payload");        36 B / 1 object   LEAKS
    println(f"{use_it(if n > 0 { mk(n) } else { mk(n+1) })}");
                                                  36 B / 1 object   LEAKS

    CONTROL -- the same call with no wrapper:      clean
    let b = mk(n).contains("payload");

THE BRANCH IS NOT THE VARIABLE. The third row has no branch in it at all --
a bare value-position BLOCK leaks identically -- so the population is "a
value-position block or branch whose TAIL MINTS a fresh owned temp", and the
`if` / `match` spellings are two members of it rather than the subject. Worth
stating because the obvious reading of the first two rows is "branches leak",
which would send a fix to `compile_if` / `compile_match` and miss the block.

WHAT IS MISSING. The block/arm hands its tail out correctly -- the consumer is
supposed to take it over -- and these two consuming positions register no
owner. That is the same shape B-2026-08-28-44 fixed for `println` and a plain
call argument, whose answer was a merge-point owner
(`own_branch_merged_clone` / `branch_tail_owner_slots`) that a consuming
destination then takes over through the usual funnel. That machinery is keyed
on a CONTAINER-ELEMENT CLONE (`vec_elem_field_clone_slots`), not on a fresh
call temp, which is why it does not reach these. A METHOD RECEIVER is a
further position of the same kind and is not covered there either.

SEVERITY: one leak per evaluation, unbounded in a loop; no double free and no
wrong answer, so it is a leak-only class.
fix:
FIXED by 707912b. The row's measurements were right and its
localization was one level off. It read the leak as two consuming positions
that "register no owner" and pointed at B-2026-08-28-44's merge-point owner as
the machinery to extend. The consumers are fine. Every one of them already has
a gate asking exactly the right question -- is this value's buffer unowned by
anyone else -- and every one answers it with `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp`,
which matches `Call`/`MethodCall` and nothing else. A wrapper is neither, so no
gate ever fired. The unwrapped call is clean at all of them, which is what
localizes this to the predicate rather than to the frees: the machinery was
correct, it was just never reached through a wrapper. No merge-point owner was
needed, and adding one would have had to be paired with a takeover half at
every OWNING destination or it would have traded the leak for a double free.

The fix is one new predicate, `expr_is_fresh_owned_branch_tail`, chained with
`||` into the gates that hold it. It admits a value-position
Block/Seq/Unsafe/LabeledBlock/If/Match whose EVERY tail mints a fresh owned
temp, recursing through nested wrappers so a block inside an arm and an
`else if` chain are decided on the same terms as the shapes that spell them
flat. Kept SEPARATE from the general predicate, the choice
`expr_is_fresh_owned_array_temp` documents: ~50 sites ask that one, and a
wrapper is not universally a fresh owned temp in their sense.

SEVEN POSITIONS, not the two the row named. Boundary-sweeping the argument and
receiver surface found five more, each its own gate in codegen, each with a
clean unwrapped control proving the gate is there and only the wrapper missed
it:
  - a method receiver (`{ mk(n) }.contains(..)`, `.to_string()`, `.to_uppercase()`)
  - the len/is_empty fast path -- a SEPARATE receiver gate, which is why
    `{ mkv(n) }.len()` and `if c { mk(n) } else { mk(n+1) }.len()` were STILL
    leaking after the first four sites were fixed and re-measured
  - a by-value call argument, where the BLOCK arm already existed
    (B-2026-06-11-5, `take({ f"..." })`) and its own comment named the branching
    case as "a (safe) leak for a later slice"; this is that slice, and the
    aliased-place shape it worried about still declines
  - an f-string interpolation -- `f"[{if c { mk(n) } else { mk(n+1) }}]"` and
    `f"[{{ mk(n) }}]"`, a position the row did not list at all
  - a `for` iterable -- `for x in { mkv(n) }` loses the whole buffer per run
  - `free_fresh_owned_str_arg`, the shared borrow-consuming-operand chokepoint
    (a concat operand `{ mk(n) } + "!"`, a push argument, a map key)

MEASURED on the regression fixture: 437 B in 16 allocations under LSan pre-fix,
zero after. Under valgrind, 555 B in 20 blocks at -O0 and 378 B in 14 at -O2 --
with BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout before and after, so this is a leak-only class
exactly as the row said, and the interpreter (which does not leak) agrees with
the compiled output on every row.

FAIL-CLOSED ON EVERY TAIL, and the reason is sharper than "conservative by
design". A tail that hands out a BINDING rather than minting a temp must keep
leaking, because `let a = { loc }.contains("payload"); println(loc)` leaves
`loc` READABLE afterwards -- measured, it still prints correctly -- so the
wrapper disarms the binding's cleanup without ending its lifetime. Several of
these gates free IMMEDIATELY at the use site
(`free_str_vec_buffer_if_heap` at both method-receiver sites,
`free_fresh_owned_str_arg` at the operand chokepoint), so admitting such a tail
would DANGLE that later read: a use-after-free, strictly worse than the leak it
replaces. A minted temp cannot have a later reader, which is precisely what the
predicate tests for. ONE disqualifying tail therefore declines the whole
construct.

The remainders are split out rather than buried in this row: the binding-tail
class as B-2026-08-30-2, and an f-string arm tail -- a producer whose own disarm has
no counterpart at the merge, a different mechanism and a different fix -- as
B-2026-08-30-3.

Regression: `asan_branch_tail_owned_temp_frees_once` covers seven positions
across the three constructs, takes the ELSE arm in one row so the fixture does
not prove only the then-path, and runs the leaking shape three times in a loop
so "unbounded in a loop" is asserted rather than claimed. Its `f`-rows are the
tripwire and not decoration: a `let`, a `Vec.push` argument, a `return` and an
assignment all OWN the merged buffer, so each is a DOUBLE FREE if the widened
predicate fires where a destination has already taken the value over; two
discarded statements cover the fourth corner, where the statement frame owns it.
`asan_branch_tail_declined_shapes_do_not_double_free` pins the two declined
shapes at their leaking values under the leak-tolerant runner, which asserts the
thing that actually matters about them -- that the fix did not turn either into
a memory error.

NO CODEGEN E2E TWIN, deliberately. Output is byte-identical before and after, so
an output test would have passed pre-fix and asserted nothing. The neighbouring
B-2026-08-28-44 -- the same merge, one producer over -- has none for the same
reason.

title: A FRESH-TEMP ENUM SCRUTINEE'S OWN `Drop` BODY RUNS AT THE MATCH ON THE INTERPRETER AND AT THE END OF THE ENCLOSING SCOPE ON BOTH COMPILED BACKENDS -- `match mk() { E.A(r) => .. }` is interp `v7 dR7 dE s1 s2 s3` vs compiled `v7 dR7 s1 s2 s3 dE`; same count, different place
detail:
Measured on the B-2026-08-28-67 fix commit, interp / jit / build /
KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, with a HEAD build and fresh archives.

    struct R { id: i64 }  impl Drop for R { println(f"dR{self.id}") }
    enum E { A(R), B }    impl Drop for E { println("dE") }
    fn mk() -> E { E.A(R { id: 7 }) }

      match mk() { E.A(r) => { println(f"v{r.id}") } E.B => {} }
      println("s1"); println("s2"); println("s3")

        interp:            v7 dR7 dE s1 s2 s3
        jit / build / np:  v7 dR7 s1 s2 s3 dE

The PAYLOAD's body (`dR7`) fires at the match on every backend and the counts
all agree -- one each. What differs is the SCRUTINEE'S OWN body: the interpreter
runs it at the match, both compiled backends defer it to the end of the
enclosing scope. Adding statements after the match separates the two placements
unambiguously, which is what the `s1 s2 s3` tail is for.

INDEPENDENT OF WHAT THE ARM DOES. The same divergence appears with a consuming
arm (`let m = r;` -> interp `m7 dR7 dE post` vs compiled `m7 dR7 post dE`), so
this is about the temporary's own lifetime, not about the payload's ownership.

WHICH IS RIGHT, on the evidence available: the INTERPRETER. The scrutinee is a
temporary whose last use is the match, so its live range ends there, and
design.md's NLL rule puts the drop at the end of the live range rather than the
end of the scope. But B-2026-08-28-67's own history is the caution here -- its
row assumed the interpreter was defensible and the settled answer went the other
way -- so this needs the same treatment: pick one, state it against design.md,
and move the other backend. Do not just make them match.

PRE-EXISTING and NOT caused by B-2026-08-28-67's fix: measured byte-identical
with that fix stashed (interp `v7 dR7 dE`, compiled `v7 dR7 post dE`). It is
pinned on the interpreter side by that fix's `fresh-temp-scrutinee` fixture row,
which asserts the interpreter's current placement and says in its comment that
the compiled half is this row.

LOW: counts agree in every cell, so nothing leaks or double-frees; only the
placement of one body differs.

SOURCE NOTE: found while probing the boundary shapes of B-2026-08-28-67's gate
-- a fresh-temp scrutinee is the case where the arm stash has no disarm to pair
with, so it had to be measured before that fix could be trusted.
fix:
FIXED by 501b70d.

THE ROW ASKS "which is right" AND WARNS AGAINST ASSUMING. It is the INTERPRETER,
and unlike B-2026-08-28-67 -- whose row made the same guess and was overruled --
this one is settled by a sentence written for exactly this position rather than
by inference from a neighbouring rule. design.md § Temporary Lifetime Rules
carries a per-position table, and one of its rows is this construct:

    | Match-expression scrutinee | Through every arm body (the scrutinee is
      live across all arms; drops at match exit) | This section |

The same section's composition-with-NLL paragraph then forbids, by name, the
direction codegen had taken: "The position-specific live-range end is the LATEST
drop point for the temporary; NLL can shorten it. NLL never EXTENDS a
temporary's live range past the position-specific end -- that direction would
invalidate the lock-eagerness guarantee." Codegen extended it to the enclosing
block's exit, so `match pool.acquire() { .. }` held the lease until the function
returned. That is the precise footgun the table was written to close (§ Why an
explicit table cites `mu.lock().get(k).cloned()` as the canonical case), which
is why this is a spec-conformance fix and not merely a parity one.

WHERE IT WENT WRONG. `materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee` mints an alloca for
the temp and calls `track_user_drop_var`, which pushes onto
`scope_cleanup_actions.last_mut()` -- the enclosing frame. Its own doc says so
("registers the drop in the CURRENT scope frame ... so the EnumDrop fires at the
enclosing scope's exit"), correctly for the MEMORY channel it was written for.
The user-body channel needed a different answer and never got one:
`fire_due_user_drops`, the NLL placer, excludes enum user-drops explicitly ("Enum
user-drops (dual-registered with a complementary EnumDrop payload walk) ... stay
at scope exit -- a conservative residual"), and `drain_statement_temp_user_drops`
fires only a hard-coded allowlist of temp names that this one was not on. Two
mechanisms that place bodies early, and the fresh-temp scrutinee fell between
them.

THE FIX IS IN TWO HALVES, AND THE FIRST ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH -- measured, not
assumed. Admitting `__freshtemp_enum_scrut` to the statement-end drain closes
17 of the 25, because a `match` is nearly always the whole statement. The two it
does not close are the two where "statement end" and "match exit" are different
points:

    println(f"c{sink(match mk(2) { .. })}")     stmt-end `dR2 c2 dE`
                                               interp   `dR2 dE c2`
    let a = match mk(3) { .. } + match mk(4) { .. };
                                               stmt-end `dR3 dR4 dE dE a7`
                                               interp   `dR3 dE dR4 dE a7`

So the second half fires the body at the merge block of `compile_match` itself
and retires the action, with the statement-end entry kept as the fallback for
`if let` / `let...else` / `while let` (whose spec rows say "through the matching
arm body", which for a statement-position construct IS the statement's end).
Emitted after the phi rather than beside `position_at_end(merge_bb)` because a
PHI must lead its block; that is the only reason it sits at the two tail returns.

FIRING EXACTLY ONCE PER PATH IS STRUCTURAL, not a condition to maintain. An arm
that `return`s/`break`s emits its cleanup -- including this action, still
registered -- on its own edge and never reaches the merge block; an arm that
falls through reaches the merge block and fires there. The retirement runs after
every arm is compiled, so it cannot take the action away from a diverging arm
that already emitted it. `arm-returns-fires-on-that-edge` pins that path.

MEASURED across interp / jit / build / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 on a 32-shape matrix
(statement / nested-in-expression / two-per-statement / nested / value-position /
in-loop / nested-block / guard / consumed / read-through / never-mentioned /
if-let / if-let-miss / let-else / while-let / heap-payload bound + unbound /
no-own-drop / place-binding / other-arm / shared / struct / terminator arms):

    pre-fix                    7 AGREE / 25 DIVERGE

title: A PROJECTION-PLACE ENUM SCRUTINEE RUNS ITS PAYLOAD'S `Drop` BODY TWICE ON BOTH COMPILED BACKENDS, THE SECOND TIME ON THE ZEROED SLOT -- `match s.e { E.A(r) => .. }` prints `dR8:n8 dE dR0:` where one payload fire is due; the `t.0` spelling is the same bug and also loses `dE` on the interpreter
detail:
Measured on the B-2026-08-28-67 fix commit, interp / jit / build /
KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, with a HEAD build and fresh archives.

    struct R { id: i64, name: String }
    impl Drop for R { println(f"dR{self.id}:{self.name}") }
    enum E { A(R), B }    impl Drop for E { println("dE") }
    struct S { e: E }

      let s = S { e: E.A(R { id: 8, name: f"n{8}" }) };
      match s.e { E.A(r) => { println(f"v{r.id}") } E.B => {} }

        interp:            v8 dE dR8:n8
        jit / build / np:  v8 dR8:n8 dE dR0:          <- THREE bodies, two due

The compiled backends run `R`'s `Drop` body TWICE. The second fire observes a
ZEROED object -- `dR0:` is `self.id == 0` and `self.name` empty -- i.e. the
move-out already cap-zeroed the slot and the body runs on it anyway. The
interpreter runs it once, in the order B-2026-08-28-67 settled (own body, then
payload).

This is not merely a run-vs-build divergence, which is why it is filed as
`soundness` and not `run-vs-build`: a user `Drop` body that runs twice is wrong
on its own terms whatever the interpreter does. A body that decrements a
counter, releases a lease, or closes a handle does it twice; a body that reads
its own fields sees a zeroed object the second time.

THE TUPLE-ELEMENT SPELLING IS THE SAME BUG, and additionally loses a body on the
interpreter:

      let t = (E.A(R { id: 6 }), 1i64);
      match t.0 { E.A(r) => { println(f"v{r.id}") } E.B => {} }

        interp:            v6 dR6              <- `dE` missing entirely
        jit / build / np:  v6 dR6 dE dR0       <- same doubled payload body

Both are PROJECTION places (`s.e`, `t.0`), which is what unifies them: the
scrutinee is a view whose owner still walks, and the arm's own registration is
firing beside that walk instead of instead of it.

INDEPENDENT OF WHAT THE ARM DOES: a consuming arm (`let k = keep(r);`) gives
compiled `k8 dR8:n8 dE dR0:` -- the same doubled body.

NO ALLOCATOR ABORT observed: the binary exits 0 and glibc reports nothing, which
is consistent with the second fire's `String` free being cap-guarded (the name
prints empty). Whether it is also a double FREE under a sanitizer was NOT
measured -- the claim here is the doubled BODY, which is directly observable.

PRE-EXISTING and NOT caused by B-2026-08-28-67's fix: measured byte-identical
with that fix stashed. That fix's gate is conditioned on the scrutinee place
being an identifier or `self`, so projection places are outside it by
construction.

SOURCE NOTE: found while probing the boundary shapes of B-2026-08-28-67's gate,
in the same pass that turned up the fresh-temp placement row filed beside this
one.
fix:
HALF FIXED by af86dfd: every READ-THROUGH shape the row reports, on both
compiled backends and the interpreter. The MATERIALIZING-arm half the row's
"INDEPENDENT OF WHAT THE ARM DOES" paragraph claims is NOT fixed and is filed
as B-2026-08-29-33; see the correction at the end, because that paragraph is
also where the row's diagnosis goes wrong.

THE ROW'S MECHANISM IS RIGHT ("the arm's own registration is firing beside that
walk instead of instead of it") AND ITS IMPLIED REPAIR IS NOT AVAILABLE. The
natural reading -- retract the owner's payload walk, as B-2026-08-28-67 does for
an identifier scrutinee -- cannot be written: a struct's field-bodies walk is
ONE emitted function (`__karac_dropbodies_S`) running the enum's own body and
its payload's body together, so `suppress_struct_field_bodies_for_var` can only
take BOTH (losing `dE`) or neither. The identifier spelling has TWO separate
cleanup actions, `OwnWrapper` and `ContainerElemBodies`, and that -- not any
difference in semantics -- is the entire reason it can hand the payload to the
arm. The interpreter has the mirror-image limit: its tuple disarm
(`moved_out_tuple_elem_bodies`) is also whole-element, which is why `t.0` there
lost `dE` outright.

So the fix goes the other way: a projection place is a VIEW, and the arm is
classified as a BORROW (`scrutinee_is_readonly_owned_enum_projection` and its
`_block` sibling, raising `pattern_binding_is_borrow`). The owner is untouched
by the match and outlives it, so its walk is the payload's one owner. One flag
fixes both halves, because the whole suppression block -- including
`suppress_destructured_struct_field_enum_cleanup`, the memory half that did the
cap-zeroing the `dR0` reads back -- is gated on that flag being clear, and
`bind_pattern_values` skips the binding's own registration.

THE OWNERSHIP WITNESS IS A LIVE BODIES WALK ON THE CHAIN'S ROOT, asked of the
cleanup frames directly (`var_has_live_bodies_walk`), not inferred from the
place's shape. Standing the arm down when nothing else runs the body loses it
outright -- the failure `place_walk_is_retractable` already records from the
other side for a fresh-temp scrutinee. `OwnWrapper` deliberately does not count:
it is the root's own body, which says nothing about a nested payload. An
ESCAPING arm keeps today's transfer path, since a binding that outlives the
owner cannot be a view of it.

THE INTERPRETER HAD A DEFECT OF ITS OWN, not merely the compiled side's mirror,
and it is the shape B-2026-08-28-67 exists to prevent, reached by the one arm
that fix did not route through it. The tuple disarm asked
`pattern_consumes_user_drop_payload` directly instead of the shared
`match_disarms_payload_walk`, so a read-through arm -- which moves nothing out
and can never take over the enum's own body -- still silenced the whole element
walk. The `if let` site had separately hand-rolled the identifier/`self` place
test rather than calling `place_walk_is_retractable`, which is exactly how the
`t.0` spelling was left out of the read-through gate; both now route through one
function, and the `if let` tuple row was wrong in the OTHER direction there
(`v8 dR8 dE dR8`, two bodies where one is due, agreeing on all four surfaces so
no A/B gate could have reported it).

MEASURED interp / jit / build / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 byte-identical across 11
shapes, valgrind clean, each printing exactly what the IDENTIFIER spelling
prints for the same arm: struct field, tuple element, both never-mentioned,
a two-hop chain `w.s.e`, both `if let` spellings, a `self.e` projection under a
`ref self` method, a read-only guard, and the two no-own-`Drop` boundary rows.
The identifier spelling is the oracle throughout -- the place a value is reached
through must not change how many times its destructor runs.

THE ROW IS WRONG ABOUT THE no-own-`Drop` BOUNDARY BEING OUT OF SCOPE, which it
does not say outright but inherits from B-2026-08-28-67, whose gate requires the
enum to have its own `Drop`. That gate is right there and wrong here: with no
own body the two ORDERS coincide, but the payload's body was still doubled
(`v8 dR8 dR0` for `enum H { A(R), B }` with no `impl Drop`). Both no-own-`Drop`
rows are RED rows in the fixture, not boundary pins.

CORRECTION TO THE ROW: "INDEPENDENT OF WHAT THE ARM DOES" IS FALSE, and the
consuming measurement it cites is misread. `let k = keep(r);` gives compiled
`k8 dR8 dE dR0` -- but the INTERPRETER gives `k8 dR8 dE dR8` there, i.e. it runs
the same TWO bodies. So for a materializing arm both backends double; only the
zeroed second read is compiled-specific. The read-through case, which the row's
title and primary repro use, was the one where the interpreter was correct at
one body and the compiled backends doubled -- that asymmetry is the actual
defect, and it is what makes the read-through half `soundness` while the
materializing half is a design question about partial moves out of a projection.
Full 24-cell matrix (scrutinee x arm x own-`Drop`) in B-2026-08-29-33.

Fixtures: `codegen::e2e_readthrough_arm_over_a_projection_leaves_the_payload_
with_its_owner` (11 rows) and `interpreter::readthrough_arm_over_a_projection_
leaves_the_payload_with_its_owner` (8 rows), both RED-verified against the
unfixed tree -- 9 of the 11 compiled rows and 4 of the 8 interpreter rows fail
there. The struct-field interpreter rows and the `self.e` compiled row are
deliberate PARITY PINS, green before and after, so a later edit cannot reconcile
the family by moving the half that was already right.

FIXED by 4a8397f3. The remaining half A is FIXED, on all three backends in one commit, and the
mechanism is the one the row specified: give the arm's value an owner INSIDE
the arm, because the statement site structurally cannot reach it.

THREE PARTS.

  1. `compute_discarded_branch_spans` now records `let _ = <if with no else>`.
     This is the half the row's analysis did not have, and without it the fix
     covers only the BARE spelling. That pre-pass recorded a discarding
     position for a bare expression-statement and for a loop tail, never for a
     wildcard `let` -- so `own_value` stayed TRUE for `let _ = if ..`, the arm
     took the tail-SUPPRESSION path, and handed its value to a consumer that
     does not exist. The two spellings of one program therefore disagreed even
     once the arm-level owner worked: `if n == 1 { R { .. } };` ran the body
     and `let _ = if n == 1 { R { .. } };` did not.

     Recorded through a NARROW recorder (`record_discarded_else_less_if`), not
     `record_discarded_branch`, and the narrowness is the safety argument
     rather than caution. Every OTHER discarded branch under a wildcard `let`
     -- a `match`, an `if`/`else`, an `else if` chain -- is ALREADY owned by
     the statement site, which frees the merged phi. Recording those would give
     one value two owners: a double free, not a missing body.

  2. The arm-level owner's gate is widened past `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp`
     (`discarded_arm_owned_aggregate_tail`), which admits `Call`/`MethodCall`
     and nothing else, so a struct-LITERAL arm never reached it. It now also
     admits a struct/tuple literal via `discarded_owned_literal_tail` (the
     ALL-FRESH-fields form -- a field naming a live binding stays declined,
     because that binding keeps its own drop), a unit variant in either
     spelling, and a NESTED branch construct whose every tail mints.

  3. A BODIES/AGGREGATE leg beside the existing one
     (`track_discarded_arm_owned_aggregate`). This is why even the `mk(7)`
     spelling -- a Call, already admitted by the old gate -- ran no body:
     `materialize_owned_temp` owns exactly three kinds (a Vec/String buffer, a
     Map/Set handle, an RC box) and a plain user struct is none of them, nor
     does it have an `owned_temp_drops` entry, since `lowering.rs` seeds that
     table from container and shared types only. So it registered NOTHING. The
     new leg routes the tail through `track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg`, the
     same arg-position registrar the wildcard-let discard site uses, so the two
     spellings cannot answer differently. The two legs own DISJOINT kinds by
     construction -- the registrar returns immediately for a bare pointer and
     excludes the Vec struct type by name -- so no value is ever claimed twice.

INTERPRETER, same commit. Both declining gates (`discard_rhs_produces_owned_-
value`'s `If` arm and the bare-statement `If` arm) admit the no-`else` case on
the then-tail alone, keeping the `Identifier` exclusion -- which is doing MORE
work here than in the two-tail case: a tail naming a live enclosing local hands
out a binding that owns its own body, and codegen's arm-level owner declines
that shape for the same reason. `discard_producer_expr` peels the RHS through a
no-`else` `if` so the enum-payload walk asks about the CONSTRUCTION rather than
the `If` node -- without it `let _ = if c { E.A(mk(8)) };` ran the enum's own
body alone here while both compiled backends ran the payload's too.

MEASURED on all four surfaces (interp / jit / aot / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0), 25
shapes. The row's four spellings, `dR7` where all were silent:

    let _ = if n == 1 { R { .. } };   silent -> dR7   on all four
    let _ = if n == 1 { mk(7) };      silent -> dR7   on all four
    if n == 1 { R { .. } };           silent -> dR7   on all four
    if n == 1 { mk(7) };              silent -> dR7   on all four

plus the shapes the widened gate brings with it, each silent AND leaking
before: a block-wrapped RHS, a nested `if` tail, a nested `match` tail, a tuple
literal, an inline enum ctor (`dE dR8`, matching what the direct
`let _ = E.A(..)` spelling already did on every backend), a unit variant, and a
loop body (one body per iteration).

LEAK, `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0`, valgrind: each of the three row fixtures went from 1
leaked block (8-10 B) to 0. On a 20-iteration loop the per-evaluation leak
compounds: 770 B definitely lost in 20 blocks before, 0 after.

At the DEFAULT `-O2` the pre-fix program does not leak at all -- the discarded
allocation is dead and LLVM deletes the whole chain (measured: that same
20-iteration loop is 0/0 both before and after). That is a true fact about
`-O2`, not a vacuous fixture, and it is recorded on
`asan_no_else_if_arm_owns_the_value_it_mints` so the next reader does not try
to rescue the leak claim with an allocation floor -- the audit reads 22-23
allocations either way, because the surviving println/f-string machinery dwarfs
the one allocation at issue. At `-O2` that fixture gates the OTHER direction,
that the new owner does not double-free; at `-O0` it fails pre-fix with
`ERROR: LeakSanitizer` and passes after.

CONTROLS, all unchanged, each a shape where an over-eager owner is a DOUBLE
free rather than a leak: a tail naming a live local (bare `dR1`, wildcard-let
silent), an `if` WITH an `else` in both the literal and call spellings, an
`else if` chain, a struct literal whose FIELD names a live local, the branch
not taken, and a `.clone()` receiver.

TESTS: `codegen::e2e_no_else_if_arm_owns_the_value_it_mints` and
`interpreter::test_no_else_if_arm_owns_the_value_it_mints` carry the SAME 19
shapes in the same order, so the two backends cannot be fixed to different
answers; `memory_sanitizer::asan_no_else_if_arm_owns_the_value_it_mints` is the
memory leg. All three RED-verified against the stashed compiler (rebuilt each
time, per CLAUDE.md's stale-binary rule). Four pre-existing pins that held the
DEFECT flip with this: two in
`e2e_discarded_branch_frees_the_value_its_arm_hands_out`, row 3 of
`e2e_discarded_literal_statement_and_no_else_if`, and their two interpreter
twins.

TWO NEIGHBOURS FOUND AND LEFT ALONE, both pre-existing and both filed rather
than folded in: a discarded `shared` struct literal (B-2026-08-31-21) and an
own-`Drop` enum ctor under an `if` WITH an `else` (B-2026-08-31-22). The shared
one was deliberately REVERTED mid-fix after measuring: widening
`materialize_owned_temp` to the admitted literal DOES fix it on both compiled
backends (41 B leak to clean, `dS` starts printing), but the interpreter has no
shared arm in `run_discarded_value_user_drops` at all -- the DIRECT spellings
`let _ = S { .. };` and `S { .. };` are silent and leak 41 B on all three
backends today -- so landing it alone would have traded an agreed gap for a
run-vs-build divergence in one more shape, which is the exact trade this row's
own half A was held back to avoid.
title: A DISCARDED `if` WITH NO `else` RUNS NO `Drop` BODY AND LEAKS -- `let _ = if n == 1 { R { .. } };` is silent on all three backends where one body is due, because a no-`else` merge yields a const-0 placeholder and the arm's value never reaches either discard site; the BARE-STATEMENT STRUCT LITERAL half of this row is FIXED (2ac067e), as is that commit's other find -- the bare spelling of the no-`else` `if` was a live run-vs-build divergence at fd4e80f, not the agreed silence first recorded here
detail:
FOUND WHILE FIXING B-2026-08-29-25, as the boundary of what that row's gate
widening deliberately does NOT admit. Both shapes are AGREED across interp /
jit / aot, so no A/B parity gate can see either; each is pinned at its measured
value in that row's codegen and interpreter suites, so a fix surfaces as those
rows failing.

Fixture throughout:

    struct R { id: i64, name: String }
    impl Drop for R { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"dR{self.id}") } }
    fn mk(i: i64) -> R { return R { id: i, name: f"heap-{i}" }; }

  A. AN `if` WITH NO `else`. One body is due -- the taken branch mints an `R`
     and nothing takes it.

     let _ = if n == 1 { R { id: 7, .. } };     interp / jit / aot -> silent
     let _ = if n == 1 { mk(7) };               interp / jit / aot -> silent

     DECLINED ON PURPOSE by B-2026-08-29-25 rather than missed, and
     B-2026-08-29-5's fix independently records the same obstacle from the
     other side: `compile_if`'s merge yields a CONST-0 PLACEHOLDER when
     `else_val` is `None`, so the statement discard site never receives the
     arm's value at all. Freeing it needs a registration inside the ARM (which
     is what -5 added) or a conditional one at the statement; a wider gate
     cannot reach it. -5's arm-level owner is gated on
     `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp`, so it covers neither of these two: the
     struct-literal spelling is not a Call, and the `mk(7)` spelling is a Call
     but still runs no user `Drop` BODY, which that mechanism does not do.
     The `else`-carrying spelling of both lines is correct as of -25, which is
     what identifies the missing-`else` case specifically rather than `if`
     generally.

  B. A BARE-STATEMENT STRUCT LITERAL, and its block-wrapped sibling.

     R { id: 7, .. };                interp / jit / aot -> silent
     { R { id: 7, .. } };            interp / jit / aot -> silent
     let _ = R { id: 7, .. };        interp / jit / aot -> dR7   (correct)
     let _ = { R { id: 7, .. } };    interp / jit / aot -> dR7   (correct as
                                                         of B-2026-08-29-25)

     So the two STATEMENT FORMS disagree for a struct literal, in the
     direction opposite to the usual one: here the BARE form is silent and the
     `let _ =` form is right. The interpreter's bare-statement discard
     dispatch has no `StructLiteral` arm at all, and codegen's bare gate
     reaches a struct literal through neither `discarded_owned_temp_tail`
     (Call/MethodCall only) nor `discarded_match_value_tail` (branching
     constructs only). PRE-EXISTING and untouched by -25 -- measured identical
     before and after.

THEY LEAK, and that is the half a body-count fixture cannot see. At
`KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0`, with the `String`-carrying `R` above and the statement in
a `go()` helper (so the stale slot sits below the stack pointer when LSan
looks -- B-2026-08-29-5's fixture note):

    let _ = if n == 1 { R { id: 7, .. } };   6 bytes leaked in 1 allocation
    let _ = if n == 1 { mk(7) };             6 bytes leaked in 1 allocation
    R { id: 7, .. };                         6 bytes leaked in 1 allocation
    { R { id: 7, .. } };                     6 bytes leaked in 1 allocation

At the default `-O2` all four are CLEAN -- the allocation is dead and LLVM
deletes it -- which is the vacuous-pass shape the `-O0` leg exists for. Any
fixture filed for this row belongs on that leg.

SOURCE NOTE: found as boundary probes while fixing B-2026-08-29-25 -- A by
asking whether an `if` with no `else` shared the two-branch spelling's gap, B
by asking whether the bare and `let _ =` forms of a struct literal agreed once
the wrapper gap closed. The leak measurement came from re-running both probes
under `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0` after they read clean at `-O2`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
UPDATE 2026-08-29 (2ac067e): HALF B IS FIXED, and half A's BARE-STATEMENT
spelling was a DIVERGENCE rather than the agreed silence recorded above.

B (bare struct literal, plain and block-wrapped) -- FIXED. The bare-statement
discard arm now chains `discarded_owned_literal_tail`, the leg its `let _ =`
sibling has carried since B-2026-07-30-11, and the interpreter's dispatch
gains the matching `StructLiteral`/`Tuple` arm. B-2026-08-01-8's moved-place
retraction was widened to the bare spelling with it: admitting the tuple
without retracting doubles a body instead of supplying one, which the two
`(r, 20)` controls in both new row-tables hold.

The leak measured larger here than the 6 B recorded above, because the row's
`R` carries an f-string of the id while the fixture's `H` carries a
`seed()`-derived payload: `H { s: payload() };` stranded 36 B against a clean
`let _ = H { s: payload() };`. Pinned at `-O0` and `-O2` by
`asan_bare_literal_statement_discard_owns_its_heap`.

A (no-`else` `if`) -- STILL OPEN, and the analysis above is right about why: a
no-`else` merge yields a const-0 placeholder, so no widening of a STATEMENT
gate can reach the arm's value. What the row did not have is that the two
spellings did not behave alike at fd4e80f:

    let _ = if n == 1 { R { .. } };     interp / jit / aot -> silent   AGREED
    if n == 1 { R { .. } };             interp -> dR7, jit / aot -> silent
                                                                  DIVERGENT

The wildcard-let `If` arm added by fd4e80f requires BOTH tails (`_ => false`);
its statement-site sibling gated on liveness alone, and a no-`else` `if` hands
out no live binding, so that arm fired a body neither compiled backend can
emit. 2ac067e makes the statement-site arm require an `else` too, which
restores agreement -- an agreed gap beats a divergence, the same call this
file makes for `v.remove(i);`. Row 3 of both new row-tables is that regression
guard.

So what remains under this id is exactly half A, on all three backends
together: give the arm an owner (B-2026-08-29-5's second mechanism, widened
past `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp` to literals and given a bodies leg) and
mirror it in the interpreter, in ONE commit.

fix:
FIXED by 5d6a9a7e. The `let _ =` spelling now owns whatever its arm hands out, on all three
backends, and the row's five measured leaks are gone.

FOUR PARTS, and the row's own "may be one change or two" is answered: it was
four, because the populations are fixed by OPPOSITE means.

  1. A WILDCARD `let` NO LONGER MARKS ITS RHS AS AN ESCAPING POSITION
     (`note_escaping_stmt_sites`, both backends). This was the enclosing-local
     half and it is the part the row's "where to start" did not have.
     `StmtKind::Let` noted an escaping site regardless of the pattern, so a
     tail naming a local was marked moved-out, its conditional-move drop flag
     was cleared on the taken path (codegen) / `moved_out_user_drop_bindings`
     silenced it (interpreter), and NOTHING ran the body. The rule was already
     written down one arm over, for a discarded `if` in statement position:
     "its arm tails go nowhere, and marking them takes a program that runs one
     body today to zero". `let _ = ..` has no destination either.

  2. A WILDCARD `let` IS A RECORDED DISCARDING POSITION for every shape, not
     just the no-`else` `if` B-2026-08-29-30 admitted. See the CORRECTION
     below.

  3. A VALUE-POSITION BLOCK under a wildcard `let` is recorded by its own
     block span, so `compile_block_with_frame` can ask whether its tail has a
     consumer. Without it `let _ = { r };` still ran the tail suppression,
     zeroing the source's `cap` to hand the buffer to a consumer that does not
     exist: the body fired and freed nothing, stranding 9 B behind a
     correct-looking transcript.

  4. THE INTERPRETER'S DISCARD GATE stopped excluding a bare `Identifier` arm
     tail outright (`discard_arm_tail_is_ownable`). That exclusion is right for
     one population and wrong for the other, and `env.get` separates them
     exactly: a live ENCLOSING LOCAL keeps its own scope-exit body (firing here
     too would double it), while an arm's own PATTERN BINDING has already left
     scope and the arm's static retraction took its slot, so nothing owns it.
     It is the same liveness gate the BARE-STATEMENT arm already used, which is
     why the two statement forms now answer alike.

CORRECTION TO B-2026-08-29-30's OWN COMMENT, measured. That commit recorded
only the no-`else` `if` and wrote into `borrow_elision.rs` that recording a
`match` or an `if`/`else` there "would flip them from statement-owned to
arm-owned, giving one value two owners, which is a double free". THAT IS
FALSE for a branch: `compile_if` computes `discard_stmt_owns_value` as
`discarded_if_parts_qualify(..) && !own_value`, so clearing `own_value` is
precisely what ARMS the statement site rather than displacing it. The two are
complementary by construction. Measured across the whole matrix: every
all-mint row stayed at one body and valgrind-clean.

It IS true for a bare value-BLOCK, which has no `discard_stmt_owns_value` of
its own to stand down against — and that cost two rounds. Recording the block
span made it register a second owner beside the statement frame's and the body
ran TWICE (`dR7 dR7 end`), first for `{ match .. }`; guarding only on
`discarded_match_value_tail` then moved the doubling to `{ mk(7) }` one row
down. The guard is the statement site's FULL admission set. Both are pinned.

A FIFTH CHANGE, needed to avoid shipping a new divergence: `taken_branch_tail`,
the interpreter's record of WHICH ARM RAN. The discard gates are syntactic and
so had to judge every arm and take the conservative answer, which is wrong in
both directions for a MIXED branch -- `let _ = if c { r } else { mk(4) };` has
one arm handing out a live local and one minting. Requiring all arms ownable
loses the minted body; admitting on any arm doubles the local's. Compiled gets
this for free (an arm's owner is emitted into that arm's own basic block); the
interpreter evaluates only the taken arm, so writing that down as it goes IS
the proof of which path ran. Before this row BOTH backends printed `dR18` alone
for that program; parts 1-4 fixed compiled to `dR4 dR18` and this brings the
interpreter with it. That shape is B-2026-08-30-11's population.

MEASURED, all four surfaces (interp / jit / aot / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0). Every one
of the row's five rows went from silent-and-leaking to one body and clean:

    let _ = if n == 0 { r } else { mk(9) };        silent 9 B -> dR41, clean
    let _ = match n { 0 => r, _ => mk(9) };        silent 9 B -> dR41, clean
    let _ = { r };                                silent 9 B -> dR41, clean
    let _ = match o { Some(r) => { r } .. };       silent 3 B -> dR1,  clean
    let _ = match o { Some(r) => r, .. }           see below

LEAK, valgrind, and this fixture is a stronger gate than B-2026-08-29-30's: at
BOTH `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0` and the default `-O2`, a 20-iteration loop measures
760 B definitely lost in 20 blocks before and 0 after. The earlier row's
fixture was `-O0`-only because its discarded value was a pure temporary that
LLVM deleted at `-O2`; here the value starts as a real binding that is live
until the discard, so the allocation survives optimization.

ONE SHAPE REMAINS DIVERGENT AND IS FILED SEPARATELY (B-2026-08-31-28): a BARE
arm (no braces) handing out a HEAP-carrying `Option` payload runs the body on
the interpreter and on neither compiled backend. It is the boxed-Option-payload
channel, it is PRE-EXISTING -- the bare-STATEMENT spelling of the same program
diverged the same way before this row -- and it is narrowed by measurement: the
same bare arm over a USER enum, or over an `Option` whose payload carries no
heap, is correct on all three. Admitting it here is what FIXES the row's own
"row 2 DIVERGENT" (the heapless spelling, where compiled fired and the
interpreter did not); the residue is a strictly narrower intersection that
closing the codegen gap will fix in both statement forms at once.

TESTS: `codegen::e2e_wildcard_let_discard_owns_what_its_arm_hands_out` and
`interpreter::test_wildcard_let_discard_owns_what_its_arm_hands_out` carry the
SAME 11 shapes in the same order, each pinning the boxed-payload divergence on
its own side; `memory_sanitizer::asan_wildcard_let_discard_owns_what_its_arm_-
hands_out` is the memory leg. All three RED-verified against the stashed
compiler (rebuilt each time). SEVEN pre-existing pins that held the DEFECT flip
with this -- three rows of `e2e_discarded_let_wildcard_match_runs_its_drop_-
body_once`, two of `e2e_discarded_if_and_block_wrapped_match_run_their_drop_-
body_once`, one control in `e2e_no_else_if_arm_owns_the_value_it_mints`, and
their interpreter twins.

An EIGHTH pin flipped, found only by the full `--features llvm` suite and worth
its own paragraph: `asan_discarded_let_wildcard_match_frees_once`'s case 2 held
`end` alone for `let _ = match n { 0 => r, _ => .. };` over an ENCLOSING LOCAL,
under a doc paragraph reading "that cell still runs no body -- B-2026-08-29-5".
It was the last spelling of that discard still silent, and part 1 closed it.
ASAN is what makes the flip trustworthy rather than merely different: the
newly-running body is a SINGLE free, not a second one on a buffer the local
still owned, which is the exact failure a widening here can produce -- LSan
clean before and after. Re-measured after the flip, all FOUR spellings of the
same discard -- bare `if`, `let _ = if`, bare `match`, `let _ = match` -- print
`dR41 forty-one` on all four surfaces, so the statement forms have converged;
the bare-statement twin (`discarded_if_enclosing_local`, B-2026-08-29-5) sits a
few lines below in the same file as the comparison. Note the count above reads
SEVEN because the codegen and interpreter suites both passed post-fix: an ASAN
pin is invisible to them, which is the reason this row's gate list is the full
llvm suite and not the two behaviour suites.
title: THE `let _ =` SPELLING OF A DISCARDED BRANCH STILL STRANDS WHATEVER ITS ARM HANDS OUT -- B-2026-08-29-5 fixed the BARE-STATEMENT form, and the wildcard-let form of the same `if` / `match` leaks 9 B (enclosing local) or 3 B (bound payload) at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 and runs NO `Drop` body on any backend; one row of the population is additionally a live run-vs-build divergence
detail:
THE `let _ =` SPELLING OF THE POPULATION B-2026-08-29-5 FIXED. That row closed
the BARE-STATEMENT form -- `if n == 0 { r } else { .. };` and its `match` and
`if let` siblings no longer strand what the taken arm hands out. The
wildcard-let form of the same constructs was not covered and still leaks.

MEASURED at `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0`, `String`-carrying `R`, each statement inside a
`go()` helper (the stale-stack-slot precaution -5's fixture note records):

    let r = R { id: 41, name: f"forty-one" };
    let _ = if n == 0 { r } else { R { id: 9, .. } };     9 bytes leaked
    let _ = match n { 0 => r, _ => R { id: 9, .. } };     9 bytes leaked
    let _ = { r };                                       9 bytes leaked

    let o: Option[R] = Some(R { id: 1, name: f"one" });
    let _ = match o { Some(r) => { r } None => { .. } };  3 bytes leaked

    and the control, which -5 fixed and which stays clean:
    if n == 0 { r } else { R { id: 9, .. } };             CLEAN, prints dR41

At the default `-O2` every row above is clean (dead allocation, deleted), so
the `-O0` leg is the only one that sees this.

THE BODY IS MISSING TOO, and that half is what several existing fixtures
already pin. On all three backends each `let _ =` row above prints NOTHING
where one body is due: the binding is moved into the discarded construct, so
its scope-exit body does not run, and no discard site claims the value. Pinned
as `UNFIXED (B-2026-08-29-31)` in
`e2e_discarded_let_wildcard_match_runs_its_drop_body_once` (rows 1, 2 and 6),
`e2e_discarded_if_and_block_wrapped_match_run_their_drop_body_once`, and the
interpreter twins of both -- those rows flip when this is fixed.

ROW 2 OF THOSE TABLES IS ADDITIONALLY A LIVE RUN-VS-BUILD DIVERGENCE: for
`let _ = match o { Some(r) => r, None => .. };` (bare arm, no braces) compiled
prints `dR1` through the general match lowering's arm-scope drop while the
interpreter prints nothing. That asymmetry is why both backends' discard
predicates EXCLUDE a bare `Identifier` at an arm tail rather than admitting it:
admitting it on the interpreter fixes row 2 and breaks row 1, moving the
divergence instead of removing it (measured while fixing B-2026-08-29-20).

WHERE TO START. -5's mechanism 1 is the shape of the answer: an arm tail that
names an existing owner reaches `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg_ex`,
which HANDS the buffer from that owner to the construct's consumer, and a
discarded construct has no consumer. -5 gated that call on `owns_result` /
`branch_arm_value_discarded` at the bare-statement sites. The wildcard-let
statement is a third site that also has no consumer, and it does not currently
tell the arm so -- `branch_arm_value_discarded` is set from
`branch_value_is_owned(condition)`, which does not know the enclosing statement
is `let _ =`. Fixing the leak and running the body may be one change or two:
leaving the source armed restores the local's own scope-exit body, which is a
body in the right place for the enclosing-local rows but not for the
bound-payload ones, whose binding has already left scope.

SOURCE NOTE: found while re-basing B-2026-08-29-25 onto B-2026-08-29-5's fix
and re-measuring the pinned rows in that row's suites, then probing them under
`KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0`.

title: A DISCARDED BRANCH OR MATCH WHOSE ARMS ARE LITERALS OF A STRUCT WITH HEAP FIELDS BUT NO `impl Drop` LEAKS THEM -- `if c { P { a: payload(), b: 1 } } else { .. };` and `let _ = match .. { P { a: payload() } .. }` each strand 38 B, because the discard battery answers the BODIES question correctly (there is no body) and then returns before the memory one is ever asked
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while writing the ASAN fixture for B-2026-08-29-30's
literal half, as a row that stayed red after that fix. Measured
byte-identical at fd4e80f and at 2ac067e, so it is neither a regression from
the discard-gate widening nor something that widening reaches. Deliberately
kept OUT of `asan_bare_literal_statement_discard_owns_its_heap` -- a row that
cannot pass would only make that fixture red -- and its doc comment records
why.

MEASURED (KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, valgrind; `struct P { a: String, b: i64 }` with
NO `impl Drop` of its own, payload derived from `env.args().len()` so nothing
folds):

    if seed() > 0 { P { a: payload(), b: 1 } } else { P { a: payload(), b: 2 } };
                                                       38 B LEAKED
    let _ = match seed() { 1 => P { a: payload(), b: 1 }, _ => P { .. } };
                                                       38 B LEAKED

    CONTROL -- the same literal discarded DIRECTLY:     clean
    P { a: payload(), b: 1 };
    let _ = P { a: payload(), b: 1 };

THE CONTROL IS THE WHOLE DIAGNOSIS, and it is why this is not simply "the
branch gate is too narrow": the gate ADMITS these shapes, and the body
question is answered correctly for them. A directly-discarded literal routes
through `track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg`, which carries memory AND bodies. A
literal reached through a BRANCH routes through
`try_track_discarded_user_drop_temp` instead, which resolves the type name and
then asks `type_runs_user_drop` -- false for `P`, since neither it nor its
fields declare a `Drop` -- and RETURNS. There is indeed no body to run; the
memory registration is simply on the far side of that early return.

Note the `match` spelling is B-2026-08-29-20's shape. That row fixed its
BODIES half, and this is the memory remainder of the same cell rather than a
regression from it -- which is also why no body-count fixture has ever seen
it.

WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE: at that early return, fall through to the aggregate
registrar the direct-literal path already uses rather than declining outright.
The type name is resolved by that point, which is the hard part. Guard against
double-owning for a type that DOES declare `Drop`, whose wrapper already
carries both halves -- that is the double free this family trades against.
fix:
FIXED by 79458f1c. `try_track_discarded_user_drop_temp` now registers the
memory for a body-less aggregate a discarded branch mints, instead of
returning as soon as it establishes there is no body to run.

THE ROW'S DIAGNOSIS WAS EXACTLY RIGHT and the control was the whole of it: a
DIRECTLY-discarded literal routes through `track_inline_owned_aggregate_arg`,
which carries memory AND bodies; a literal reached through a BRANCH routes
here, which asks `type_runs_user_drop` -- false for a `P` that declares no
`Drop` on itself or any field -- and returns. Both of that routine's returns
sat ABOVE `track_struct_var`, the one memory registration the path makes, so
the answer to the bodies question silently decided the memory question too.
The fix answers "no bodies" and falls through, then stops short of the final
`track_user_drop_var`, which would hang a `karac_drop_<T>` wrapper that a type
with no `Drop` has no symbol for.

MEASURED (KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0, valgrind), all four spellings the row names plus
three the row did not, each 38 B before and clean after:

    if seed() > 0 { P { a: payload(), b: 1 } } else { .. };      38 B -> clean
    let _ = if seed() > 0 { P { .. } } else { .. };              38 B -> clean
    match seed() { 1 => { P { .. } } _ => { .. } };              38 B -> clean
    let _ = match seed() { 1 => { P { .. } } _ => { .. } };      38 B -> clean
    let _ = if .. { P { .. } } else if .. { P { .. } } else { }; 38 B -> clean
    let _ = if .. { match .. { .. => { P { .. } } } } else { };   38 B -> clean
    let _ = if seed() > 0 { mkp(1) } else { mkp(2) };            38 B -> clean

    CONTROL, clean before and after:  P { .. };   let _ = P { .. };

GUARDED, AND THE GUARD IS THE HALF WORTH READING. Registering unconditionally
turned working programs into `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`. A
field initialized from something that already has an owner ALIASES it, so the
literal's new owner frees the same pointer a second time. The guard admits
only values MINTED at the literal -- a call, a `.clone()`, literals,
interpolated strings, operator results -- and declines every identifier and
every place.

THE FIRST CUT OF THAT GUARD WAS WRONG, and the way it was wrong is the
methodological finding of this row. It declined only a projection ROOTED AT A
CALL TEMP, because a 37-case single-statement matrix measured `P { a: t.a }`
over a local as clean. That was a FALSE NEGATIVE: a local dies at its NLL last
use when nothing follows it, so the alias and the local's own cleanup never
coexist and the double free cannot appear. Add one more discard after it and
they do -- that two-statement program double-freed under the narrow guard,
where the same pair with NO registration merely leaked 38 B and reported zero
valgrind errors. Every fixture in this row therefore STACKS statements; a
one-statement fixture is structurally unable to see this class.

The declined kinds keep their pre-existing 38 B leak. That is a deliberate
trade and not an oversight: registering them is precisely what produced the
double free, and a leak is the better half of that pair.

TWO PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS FOUND AND FILED, both measured byte-identical at
`c4af3243` -- the commit BEFORE B-2026-08-29-31 taught this path to own an
arm's value at all -- so neither is a regression from that row or this one:

  * B-2026-08-31-34: `let w = V { v: mkv(1).v, b: 1 };` -- the `let`-BOUND
    spelling of an aliasing literal, no discard anywhere in it -- double-frees
    on AOT while the interpreter prints normally. Memory corruption AND a
    run-vs-build divergence. This is the defect the guard exists to avoid
    walking into, and it is why the fix cannot simply register everything.
  * B-2026-08-31-35: a discarded branch whose arm literal CONSUMES A LOCAL,
    whole or projected, runs that local's `Drop` body TWICE -- once at the
    discard and once at scope end. All three backends agree, so it is an
    agreed gap rather than a divergence, and the BOUND spelling of the same
    move is correct at one body, which localizes it to the discard.

TESTS: `memory_sanitizer::asan_discarded_branch_of_body_less_heap_literals_-
frees_once` is the gate and the only fixture that can see this row at all --
`P` has no body, so the leak changes no transcript and every body-count test
in the tree reads identically before and after. It RED-verifies (FAILED
pre-fix, ok post-fix) and measures 810 B in 20 blocks over a 20-iteration loop
before, clean after, at `KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0` AND at the default `-O2` the
harness actually builds at -- both stated because the sibling fixture for
B-2026-08-29-30 gates at `-O0` only, and reading that caveat across would
understate this one. `codegen::e2e_discarded_branch_of_body_less_heap_-
literals_keeps_one_owner` and its interpreter twin do NOT red-verify for this
row and are not claimed to: they are double-own regression guards, pinning
that a type WITH `Drop`, a type with a Drop-BEARING field, and the direct
discard spellings each stay at exactly one body, since a wrong fall-through
shows up as a doubled body long before it shows up as a double free. Both also
pin the two defects above as KNOWN, on both backends, so a one-sided fix of
either shows up here as a failure.

title: A MATERIALIZING ARM OVER A PROJECTION-PLACE ENUM SCRUTINEE RUNS THE PAYLOAD'S `Drop` BODY TWICE ON EVERY BACKEND -- `match s.e { E.A(r) => { let m = r; .. } }` is interp `m8 dR8 dE dR8` vs compiled `m8 dR8 dE dR0`, where the identifier spelling gives `m8 dR8 dE`
detail:
Measured on af86dfd (the B-2026-08-29-29 fix), interp / jit / build /
KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, with fresh archives and a HEAD build of BOTH bins.

B-2026-08-29-29 fixed every READ-THROUGH arm over a projection place. Its
"INDEPENDENT OF WHAT THE ARM DOES" paragraph claimed the materializing arm was
the same bug; it is not, and it is what is left.

    struct R { id: i64 }
    impl Drop for R { println(f"dR{self.id}") }
    enum E { A(R), B }    impl Drop for E { println("dE") }
    struct S { e: E }

FULL 24-CELL MATRIX -- scrutinee place x arm shape x whether `E` has its own
`Drop`. The IDENTIFIER column is the oracle: it agrees on all four surfaces in
every cell and is what B-2026-08-28-67 settled. `read` is `println(r.id)`,
`nomention` never names `r`, `letmove` is `let m = r;`, `keepfn` is
`let k = keep(r);` for `fn keep(x: R) -> R { x }`.

    own `Drop`   place   arm         interp                compiled
    ----------   -----   ---------   -------------------   -------------------
    yes          ident   read        v8 dE dR8             v8 dE dR8      AGREE
    yes          ident   nomention   x dE dR8              x dE dR8       AGREE
    yes          ident   letmove     m8 dR8 dE             m8 dR8 dE      AGREE
    yes          ident   keepfn      k8 dR8 dR8 dE         k8 dR8 dR8 dE  AGREE
    yes          field   read        v8 dE dR8             v8 dE dR8      AGREE
    yes          field   nomention   x dE dR8              x dE dR8       AGREE
    yes          field   letmove     m8 dR8 dE dR8         m8 dR8 dE dR0  DIVERGE
    yes          field   keepfn      k8 dR8 dE dR8         k8 dR8 dR8 dE dR0  DIVERGE
    yes          tuple   read        v8 dE dR8             v8 dE dR8      AGREE
    yes          tuple   nomention   x dE dR8              x dE dR8       AGREE
    yes          tuple   letmove     m8 dR8                m8 dR8 dE dR0  DIVERGE
    yes          tuple   keepfn      k8 dR8 dR8            k8 dR8 dR8 dE dR0  DIVERGE
    no           ident   read        v8 dR8                v8 dR8         AGREE
    no           ident   nomention   x dR8                 x dR8          AGREE
    no           ident   letmove     m8 dR8                m8 dR8         AGREE
    no           ident   keepfn      k8 dR8 dR8            k8 dR8 dR8     AGREE
    no           field   read        v8 dR8                v8 dR8         AGREE
    no           field   nomention   x dR8                 x dR8          AGREE
    no           field   letmove     m8 dR8 dR8            m8 dR8 dR0     DIVERGE
    no           field   keepfn      k8 dR8 dR8            k8 dR8 dR8 dR0 DIVERGE
    no           tuple   read        v8 dR8                v8 dR8         AGREE
    no           tuple   nomention   x dR8                 x dR8          AGREE
    no           tuple   letmove     m8 dR8                m8 dR8 dR0     DIVERGE
    no           tuple   keepfn      k8 dR8 dR8            k8 dR8 dR8 dR0 DIVERGE

THREE DISTINCT DEFECTS LIVE IN THE EIGHT DIVERGING CELLS, and conflating them is
how the parent row's diagnosis went wrong:

  (a) BOTH BACKENDS DOUBLE the payload body for a `field` materializing arm --
      interp `m8 dR8 dE dR8`, compiled `m8 dR8 dE dR0`. Same COUNT. The arm owns
      the payload and the owner's walk runs it too. The identifier spelling
      gives one body.
  (b) COMPILED reads the doubled body off a ZEROED slot (`dR0`) because the
      arm's move-out cap-zeroed the source; the interpreter reads the live one.
      That is the only compiled-specific part.
  (c) THE INTERPRETER LOSES `dE` for a `tuple` materializing arm (`m8 dR8`,
      where compiled has `dE`), because `moved_out_tuple_elem_bodies` retracts
      the WHOLE element walk rather than just the payload's body.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE, which is the whole reason this is a
separate row and not a follow-up commit. Making the arm the sole owner requires
retracting the OWNER's payload body while keeping the enum's own -- and neither
backend can express a payload-ONLY retraction. A struct's field-bodies walk is
one emitted function (`__karac_dropbodies_S`) running both bodies together, so
`suppress_struct_field_bodies_for_var` can only take both (losing `dE`) or
neither; the interpreter's tuple set has the mirror limit, which is defect (c)
above. The identifier spelling escapes this only because it happens to have TWO
cleanup actions, `OwnWrapper` and `ContainerElemBodies`.

THE OTHER DIRECTION -- borrow-classify the materializing arm too, as
B-2026-08-29-29 does for read-through ones -- WAS TRIED AND HELD BACK
DELIBERATELY. It would give `m8 dE dR8` (one body, the owner's) and
`k8 dR8 dE dR8`, both agreeing, and the escape guard already declines the
dangerous shapes. But `no_arm_payload_escapes` is a MATERIALIZATION test, not a
lifetime one: it cannot separate `let m = r;` (m dies at the arm's end -- safe)
from `v.push(r)` (the alias outlives the owner -- a use-after-free once the
owner's walk frees the buffer). Relaxing it needs a real "does anything derived
from this binding outlive the arm?" analysis, and getting that wrong fails in
the unsafe direction. NOT attempted here.

NO MEMORY ERROR in any of the 24 cells: valgrind clean throughout, including the
`String`-payload variants, so this is a doubled BODY and a lost `dE`, not a
double free. That is also why (b) is silent -- the second fire's `String` free
is cap-guarded, so it prints an empty name rather than aborting.

PROBABLY WANTS A DESIGN ANSWER FIRST. design.md Part 8 says "partial moves out
of a struct field are rejected if the struct has a `Drop` impl: the drop body
assumes all fields are present". A materializing arm over `s.e` is exactly such
a partial move, out from under a walk that assumes the payload is there -- so
REJECTING it may be the correct answer rather than deciding who runs the body.
The identifier spelling's behaviour is not evidence against that: there the
scrutinee IS the value being matched, and nothing outlives the move.

SOURCE NOTE: found while fixing B-2026-08-29-29; the matrix above is that
session's, re-measured at the fix commit.
fix:
FIXED by 9f3e2cb. All eight diverging cells, plus the four `if let` / `while let`
spellings the row's matrix did not cover.

THE ROW'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS WRONG AND I WROTE IT: "neither backend can express a
payload-ONLY retraction" is false. It is expressible, one granularity finer than
the mask that already existed, and the evidence was in the row's own paragraph —
a struct's field-bodies walk emits an enum field's OWN body and its PAYLOAD's
body as two SEPARATE calls (`E.drop` then `emit_enum_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn`,
B-2026-08-28-40). Dropping the second and keeping the first is a one-line gate
inside the emitter. What I had checked was the RETRACTION API — `suppress_struct_
field_bodies_for_var` takes a whole field — and concluded the emitted walk was
monolithic without reading it. The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: "the
mechanism cannot express X" is a claim about emitted code, and reading the
retraction helper is not reading the emitter.

WHAT THE FIX IS. `FieldSkipTree` gains `payload_here`, a set of ENUM fields whose
payload bodies are masked while their own body still runs; the tuple walker gains
the peer `payload_skip`, threaded into `emit_slot_drop_bodies_at_opt`. Both fold
into the walker's symbol name so a masked walker never aliases the full one.
`disarm_struct_field_enum_payload_bodies_at` / `disarm_tuple_elem_enum_payload_
bodies_at` record into per-variable maps and re-emit; `disarm_projection_enum_
payload_bodies` dispatches from the BODIES half of `suppress_destructured_struct_
field_enum_cleanup`, which until now did only the memory half. The interpreter
gets the twin pair of `(var, field)` / `(var, index)` sets and a one-shot
top-level mask (`pending_payload_masked_fields`, TAKEN not borrowed, so the
walker's recursion cannot inherit it through a field-name collision).

TWO PLACEMENT TRAPS, both measured, both fixed inside this commit.

  1. THE MASKED WALKER MUST BE SWAPPED IN PLACE, not retracted and
     re-registered. The existing retract-and-re-register pair is correct only
     when the caller runs in the frame the action lives in — true of the
     `let x = h.o` move-out sites it was written for, false of a match ARM,
     whose frame is inner. Re-registering from there moved the owner's walk into
     the arm and drained it at the ARM's end: measured `k8 dE dR8` where
     `k8 dR8 dE` is due, the owner's `dE` overtaking a body that belongs before
     it. `replace_user_drop_fn_for_var` mutates the action's `drop_fn` and
     leaves its frame and position alone.

  2. NO FALLBACK REGISTRATION when nothing matched. An absent action means the
     owner has no bodies walk here — a `ref self` receiver, whose CALLER owns
     it — and inventing one made the caller's struct fire INSIDE the callee:
     measured `dR8 dE n8 dE dR8`, `dE` twice. Nothing to hand over is not the
     same as something to add.

`Option`/`Result` PLACES STAY ON THE OLD WHOLE-ELEMENT PATH, and that is not a
narrowing but a correctness requirement. Their walk reaches them through
`run_discarded_value_user_drops` BEFORE the user-enum arm the payload mask
guards, so routing them through the finer mask half-masks them and the body
fires twice — caught by `test_tuple_elem_match_scrutinee_body_fires_at_arm_end`
and `test_result_struct_payload_field_freed_and_single_body`'s `local-match`.
They have no own `Drop` body to preserve, so the finer mask buys nothing there
anyway. The interpreter's struct-field arm stash is locked to whether the disarm
ACTUALLY RECORDED, rather than answering structurally like the tuple arm: that is
the other half of the same double (stash without retract), and it is why the
FieldAccess arm of `scrutinee_expr_is_consuming` reads a set instead of a shape.

A USE-AFTER-FREE CAME OUT OF THE PROBE, filed as B-2026-08-29-35 and fixed in
this commit. The three `let`-form legs (`if let` / `while let` / `let … else`)
never ran the projection-place suppressor at all, so `if let E.A(r) = s.e
{ let m = r; }` over a HEAP payload left the source struct populated while the
binding took the buffer and both freed it: no program output, valgrind reporting
an invalid read of a freed block, while the `match` spelling was clean. Adding
the call to all three legs fixes it, and because that function now carries the
bodies half too, the two move together — the B-2026-08-28-67 lockstep rule.

MEASURED interp / jit / build / KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 byte-identical across all 24
cells of the row's matrix, valgrind clean, every projection cell printing exactly
what the IDENTIFIER spelling prints for the same arm.

THE ROW'S "PROBABLY WANTS A DESIGN ANSWER FIRST" DID NOT HOLD UP either, and is
worth correcting rather than leaving as a standing suggestion. It proposed
REJECTING the partial move on design.md Part 8's rule ("partial moves out of a
struct field are rejected if the struct has a `Drop` impl"). That rule is about a
destructor whose body assumes all fields present — and the payload mask satisfies
exactly that premise: `E.drop` still runs, on an object whose payload the arm
took, which is the same state a bare `let m = r;` out of an identifier-place
enum has produced on every backend since B-2026-08-28-67. There is nothing here
the identifier spelling does not already do; the only thing that was wrong was
WHO ran the payload's body.

THE BORROW ROUTE THE ROW DESCRIBES IS STILL NOT TAKEN, and its objection stands
unchanged: `no_arm_payload_escapes` is a materialization test, not a lifetime
one. It is simply no longer needed — the arm owns the payload, as it should, and
the owner's walk stops running it.

TWO PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCES SURVIVE, both verified byte-identical before this
change and filed rather than left in this row: B-2026-08-29-36 (a two-hop chain
`w.s.e`, which needs the mask threaded through `FieldSkipTree::nested`) and
B-2026-08-29-37 (a `ref self` method whose match moves `self.e`'s payload out,
running `dE` twice compiled — the trap-2 shape, but present without it and
therefore something else's).

Fixtures: `codegen::e2e_materializing_arm_over_a_projection_owns_the_payload_
once` (12 rows, including the two use-after-free ones and an identifier-spelling
control every other row is measured against) and
`interpreter::materializing_arm_over_a_projection_owns_the_payload_once`
(8 rows, including the `Option`/`Result` carve-out pin), both RED-verified
against the unfixed tree.

title: A `Vector[bf16, N]` LANE OP ABORTS ISel ON arm64 AND wasm32 -- the vector legalizer SCALARIZES `<4 x bfloat> fadd` back into the unselectable scalar `bf16 fadd`, so the SIMD path keeps the disease B-2026-08-29-23 fixed for scalars. Non-monotonic: a one-op probe selects, a three-op one does not.
detail:
FOUND while fixing B-2026-08-29-23, which closed the same disease on the
SCALAR bf16 path. `Vector[bf16, N]` has it too, through a different set of
sites and needing a different fix, so it is filed rather than folded in.

REPRODUCED with llc-18 from x86_64 (the `-mtriple` override reproduces the
target's ISel exactly):

    fn main() {
        let a: Vector[bf16, 4] = Vector[bf16, 4](1.5bf16, 2.5bf16, 1.5bf16, 2.5bf16);
        let b: Vector[bf16, 4] = Vector[bf16, 4](0.5bf16, 0.5bf16, 0.5bf16, 0.5bf16);
        println(f"sum={(a + b).reduce_sum()} prod={(a * b).reduce_sum()}");
        println(f"min={a.reduce_min()} max={a.reduce_max()}");
        println(f"dot={a.dot(b)}");
    }

emits `= fadd <4 x bfloat>` and `= fmul <4 x bfloat>`, and then:

    aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu  LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: bf16 = fadd ...
    wasm32-unknown-wasi        LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: i32 = fp_to_bf16 ...

THE MECHANISM IS ONE STEP REMOVED FROM THE SCALAR BUG, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS
ITS OWN FIX. The IR contains no scalar bf16 node at all -- it is the AArch64
VECTOR legalizer that scalarizes `<N x bfloat>` lane ops down to scalar
`bf16` ones, which are then exactly the unselectable nodes B-2026-08-29-23
documents. So the vector form is broken for the scalar form's reason, but no
scalar-level check or fix reaches it. wasm32 fails one step earlier, on the
`fp_to_bf16` conversion node.

NOTE THE NON-MONOTONICITY: a SMALLER program can select fine. `a + b`
followed by a single `reduce_sum()` selects on aarch64; adding the second
arithmetic op and the reductions above makes it scalarize and die. So a
one-line probe is not evidence of health here, and whatever fixture this
gets must use the larger shape.

SCOPE. ~18 vector-typed `build_float_compare` / `build_float_neg` sites
across `expr_ops.rs` (the six SIMD lane comparisons), `method_call_vector.rs`
and `tensor.rs`, plus the vector arithmetic builders beside them
(`build_float_add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`/`rem` on `VectorValue`). The fix shape
is the scalar one lifted to vectors: widen `<N x bfloat>` to `<N x float>`,
operate, round back -- so it wants a vector sibling of
`build_float_cast_bf16_safe` rather than a reuse of it (that helper takes a
scalar `FloatValue`, which is why the scalar fix deliberately left these
sites alone rather than mis-routing them).

DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED BY `verify_no_native_bf16_ops`. That guard, added by
B-2026-08-29-23, rejects scalar native bf16 nodes on every host. Extending it
to `<N x bfloat>` would turn `Vector[bf16, N]` code that works on x86 today
into a hard compile error everywhere WITHOUT fixing it -- a worse trade than
the status quo. When this row is fixed, widen the guard in the same commit;
the guard's doc comment carries a pointer to this row so the two do not drift.

CONTEXT ON URGENCY: design.md ~13678 lists `f16` / `bf16` as permitted
`Vector[T, N]` element types "once they ship", so this is arguably a
not-yet-shipped surface. It is constructible and returns correct answers on
x86 today, though, which is enough to be a real arm64/wasm trap rather than a
purely hypothetical one.

CORRECTION (2026-08-29, on fixing) -- THREE OF THIS ROW'S OWN CLAIMS WERE WRONG.

1. "DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED BY `verify_no_native_bf16_ops`" was already half
   false when it was written, and the false half was a live regression. That
   guard's FIRST pass matches intrinsics BY NAME, and `llvm.sqrt.v4bf16`
   contains "bf16" -- so from the moment B-2026-08-29-23 landed, the nine vector
   transcendental/rounding methods were a HARD COMPILE ERROR on every host,
   x86 included. Verified by disabling the guard and rebuilding: they compile
   and return correct values without it (`sqrt`=4, `exp`=10.875, `floor`="4 4 4
   4"), and abort ISel with it on aarch64. So -23 converted "silently broken on
   arm64, works on x86" into "hard error everywhere" for that subset -- arguably
   the better failure mode, but a behavioural regression on x86 that neither
   -23's commit message nor this row acknowledged.

2. THE NON-MONOTONICITY IS REAL BUT THE BOUNDARY IS IN THE WRONG PLACE. This
   row said "`a + b` followed by a single `reduce_sum()` selects on aarch64".
   It does not -- it aborts at -O1 and above exactly like the larger shape. What
   DOES select is `a + b` followed by a lane READ, and the reason is not
   selectability: llc constant-folds the add away, so the emitted asm contains
   ZERO `fadd` and nothing ever reached ISel. That is the same vacuity trap
   this project keeps meeting in new costumes, so the rule is worth stating
   generally: a probe that comes back green must be checked for whether the
   operation SURVIVED into the asm before the green is believed.

3. "~18 vector-typed sites" over-counts by an order of magnitude, because it
   counted sites rather than boundaries. Two boundaries -- `compile_vector_binop`
   and `apply_vector_float_unary` -- dominate every one of them, and the
   `tensor.rs` / `kernel.rs` sites the row named turned out to be unreachable
   with a bf16 element (`Tensor[bf16, N]` does not typecheck; the `Vec[bf16]`
   iterator paths emit no vector bf16 op -- measured).

Also measured while verifying, and filed separately rather than folded in:
B-2026-08-29-42 (fixed here -- reduced-precision receivers called the f64 libm
symbol and got silent garbage), B-2026-08-29-40 and B-2026-08-29-41 (both open,
both interpreter-side rounding).
fix:
FIXED by e860b90. The fix is the scalar row's rule lifted to vectors,
plus a scalar hole that row left behind and this one uncovered.

VECTOR HALF. `widen_bf16_vector` / `narrow_bf16_vector` (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs)
widen `<N x bfloat>` to `<N x float>`, and are applied at two BOUNDARIES rather
than at each of the ~18 sites the row estimated:

  - `compile_vector_binop` -- operands widen, the op runs at `<N x float>`, and
    arithmetic rounds back. Comparisons do not round: their result is an
    `<N x i1>` mask, already a legal type.
  - `apply_vector_float_unary` -- the receiver widens ONCE for the whole body,
    so all nine transcendental / rounding methods, the `exp`/`ln` polynomials,
    and the `splat` closure (which derives its type from the receiver) follow
    automatically. Boundary widening is also more accurate than per-op would
    be: polynomial intermediates stay in f32 instead of rounding to bf16 after
    every step.

The widen/narrow pair is a STRUCTURAL MIRROR of the scalar `emit_bf16_to_f32` /
`emit_f32_to_bf16` -- same steps, same order, `<N x _>` types throughout --
rather than a lane loop over them (which would re-scalarize the vector) or an
independent implementation (which could round differently). That matters
